original_question: Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does the product ideal C2* o L_infinity have property (I), meaning that for every epsilon > 0 each finite-rank operator in C2* o L_infinity can be factorized almost isometrically with one factor having finite-dimensional range?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A Banach operator ideal (A, A) assigns to every pair of Banach spaces X, Y a linear subspace A(X,Y) of the bounded operators B(X,Y) together with a complete norm A(·) which dominates the operator norm and satisfies the usual ideal property A(SAT) ≤ ‖S‖·A(A)·‖T‖. The ideal is called maximal if A(X,Y) consists of all T ∈ B(X,Y) for which sup{A(QTI) : I : E → X finite-dimensional inclusion, Q : Y → F/N finite-codimensional quotient} is finite, with A(·) equal to this supremum, and injective if for every isometric embedding J : Y → Z one has A(JT) = A(T).

Let C2 denote the maximal injective Banach operator ideal of cotype 2 operators (operators T : X → Y such that Y has cotype 2 with respect to T in the usual sense, equipped with its natural cotype-2 constant). Let C2* denote its adjoint (dual) ideal in the sense of operator ideals. Let L_∞ denote the maximal Banach ideal of operators factoring through an L_∞-space, with its associated factorization norm.

For two Banach ideals (A, A) and (B, B), the product ideal A ∘ B is defined by T ∈ (A ∘ B)(X,Y) iff there exist a Banach space Z and operators B ∈ B(X,Z), A ∈ A(Z,Y) with T = AB, normed by (A ∘ B)(T) = inf A(A)·B(B) over all such factorizations.

A product ideal A ∘ B is said to have property (I) if for every ε > 0 and every finite-rank operator L ∈ (A ∘ B)(X,Y) there exists a factorization L = AB with A ∈ A, B ∈ B such that A(A)·B(B) ≤ (1+ε)·(A ∘ B)(L) and A has finite-dimensional range.

Problem. Does the product ideal C2* ∘ L_∞ have property (I)?
status_search_result: No source resolving this specific question about property (I) for C2* ∘ L_∞ was located. Related work on normed products of operator ideals exists, but no later paper or survey was found explicitly settling this problem in either direction.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), find more counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo channel and small perturbations of it, and determine whether the counterexamples support or refute the conjecture that multiplicativity holds throughout 1 ≤ p ≤ 2.
self_contained_problem:
For a quantum channel Φ (a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between matrix algebras) and a real number p ≥ 1, define the maximal output p-norm by
   ν_p(Φ) := sup_ρ ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,
where the supremum is taken over all density matrices ρ on the input space and ‖A‖_p = (Tr |A|^p)^{1/p}.

The maximal output p-norm multiplicativity conjecture asserts that for every pair of quantum channels Φ and Ω,
   ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω).

Two questions are posed:
(a) Exhibit pairs of quantum channels (Φ, Ω) for which ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) > ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω), beyond the Werner–Holevo channel example and small perturbations of it.
(b) Determine whether such counterexamples can occur in the regime 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, or whether multiplicativity in fact holds throughout 1 ≤ p ≤ 2.
status_search_result: The problem was resolved. Hayden (2007) constructed counterexamples for 1 < p < 2, Winter extended this to p = 2, and Hayden–Winter (arXiv:0807.4753, Comm. Math. Phys. 2008) produced counterexamples for all p > 1. Subsequently, Hastings (2008) gave counterexamples even at p = 1 (the minimum output entropy additivity conjecture). Thus multiplicativity fails throughout p > 1, refuting the suggested 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 multiplicativity.

context_brief: whether right-accessibility is needed in Corollary 2.6
original_question: Corollary 2.6 states that if (B, B) is a maximal Banach ideal, X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2, B*(X0, Y0) is not a subset of L2(X0, Y0), and B o L_infinity is right-accessible and has property (I), then the B-LRP is not satisfied. Can the hypothesis that B o L_infinity is right-accessible be dropped while keeping the same conclusion?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let (B, ‖·‖_B) be a maximal Banach operator ideal in the sense of Pietsch, with adjoint ideal B* and trace duality. Recall that an operator ideal A is called right-accessible if for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space F, every operator T ∈ L(E,F), and every ε>0, there exist a finite-dimensional Banach space E_0, an operator S ∈ L(E,E_0), and an operator T_0 ∈ A(E_0,F) such that T = T_0 ∘ S and ‖T_0‖_A · ‖S‖ ≤ (1+ε)·‖T‖_A. The composition ideal B ∘ L_∞ is the ideal of operators that factor through an L_∞-space followed by an operator from B. The ideal B ∘ L_∞ is said to have property (I) if its component on every pair of Banach spaces is closed in the operator norm topology. The B-local reformulation property (B-LRP) for a pair of Banach spaces (X_0, Y_0) is the statement that B(X_0, Y_0) coincides isometrically with the local hull obtained by testing on finite-dimensional subspaces.

Known fact. If (B, ‖·‖_B) is a maximal Banach ideal, X_0 and Y_0 are Banach spaces such that the dual X_0' and Y_0 are both of cotype 2, B*(X_0, Y_0) is not contained in the ideal L_2(X_0, Y_0) of 2-summing operators, and the composition ideal B ∘ L_∞ is right-accessible and has property (I), then the pair (X_0, Y_0) does not satisfy the B-LRP.

Question. Can the hypothesis that B ∘ L_∞ is right-accessible be removed while preserving the same conclusion? That is: assuming (B, ‖·‖_B) is a maximal Banach ideal, X_0' and Y_0 are of cotype 2, B*(X_0, Y_0) ⊄ L_2(X_0, Y_0), and B ∘ L_∞ has property (I), does it still follow that the B-LRP fails for (X_0, Y_0)?
status_search_result: A web search for the specific technical terms (B-LRP, right-accessible, maximal Banach ideal, property (I)) returned no relevant follow-up references that resolve whether the right-accessibility hypothesis can be dropped. No subsequent published work confirming or refuting the conjecture was located.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For which classes of quantum channels can maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω) be proved at p = 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_A)$ and $\Omega:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_B)$ be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving linear maps between matrix algebras on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces). For a real number $p\ge 1$, define the maximal output $p$-norm of a channel $\Phi$ by
\[
\nu_p(\Phi) \;=\; \sup_{\rho}\, \|\Phi(\rho)\|_p \;=\; \sup_{\rho}\,\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}\,|\Phi(\rho)|^p\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where the supremum is over all density operators $\rho$ on the input space, and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$ is the Schatten $p$-norm. The channel $\Phi\otimes\Omega$ acts on density operators of the bipartite system $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$.

The maximal output $p$-norm multiplicativity property at the value $p=2$ asserts
\[
\nu_2(\Phi\otimes\Omega) \;=\; \nu_2(\Phi)\,\nu_2(\Omega). \tag{$\ast$}
\]

Identify and characterize broad classes of pairs of quantum channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ for which the equality $(\ast)$ can be rigorously established, and provide proofs of multiplicativity at $p=2$ for as wide a class of channels as possible.
status_search_result: Multiplicativity at p=2 is known for several classes (e.g., entanglement-breaking channels, unital qubit channels, depolarizing channels, Hadamard channels, and Gaussian channels in appropriate settings), proved by King, Shor, and others. However, Hayden–Winter (arXiv:0707.3291) showed that the general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is false for all p>1, including p=2 in a neighborhood interpretation, and Hastings later disproved additivity. Thus multiplicativity at p=2 cannot hold for all channels, and the program of identifying the largest natural classes where it does hold is ongoing and partially resolved.

original_question: Does every subgroup H of an infinite-dimensional Lie group G admit a smooth manifold structure making H an initial Lie subgroup of G? Here this means that, for every k in N union {infinity}, H is C^k-initial in G in the sense that the inclusion map lambda: H -> G is C^k and every map f: X -> H from a C^k-manifold X is C^k whenever lambda o f is C^k, and moreover the induced tangent map L(lambda): L(H) -> L(G) is injective.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite-dimensional Lie group (a group equipped with a smooth manifold structure modeled on a locally convex topological vector space, such that multiplication and inversion are smooth), and write $L(G) = T_1 G$ for its Lie algebra. For $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, a subset $H \subseteq G$ endowed with a smooth manifold structure is called $C^k$-initial in $G$ if the inclusion $\lambda \colon H \to G$ is $C^k$ and, for every $C^k$-manifold $X$ and every map $f \colon X \to H$, the composition $\lambda \circ f$ being $C^k$ implies that $f$ itself is $C^k$. A subgroup $H \subseteq G$ is called an initial Lie subgroup of $G$ if it admits a smooth manifold structure making it a Lie group, making it $C^k$-initial in $G$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, and making the induced tangent map $L(\lambda) \colon L(H) \to L(G)$ injective.

Question: Does every subgroup $H$ of every infinite-dimensional Lie group $G$ admit such a smooth manifold structure making it an initial Lie subgroup of $G$?

Equivalently, decide whether the additive subgroup $\ell^\infty$ of bounded real sequences, viewed as a subgroup of the infinite-dimensional Lie group $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (with the product topology and the obvious smooth structure), can be given the structure of an initial Lie subgroup.
status_search_result: The problem (Neeb's "Initial Subgroup Problem") has been resolved in the negative: the additive subgroup $\ell^\infty \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ provides a counterexample, since for every $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ it fails to be a $C^k$-initial submanifold and hence is not an initial Lie subgroup.

This answers the Initial Subgroup Problem in the negative.", "claim": "The Initial Subgroup Problem is answered in the negative."}]

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find a proof of maximal output p-norm multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel that does not rely on unitary equivalence to channels with negative multipliers.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A qubit channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ : M₂(ℂ) → M₂(ℂ). For ρ ∈ M₂(ℂ), the maximal output p-norm of Φ (for p ≥ 1) is

  ν_p(Φ) := sup_{ρ ≥ 0, Tr ρ = 1} ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where ‖A‖_p = (Tr |A|^p)^{1/p}. The channel Φ is said to be multiplicative for p-norms if for every channel Ψ (acting on any finite-dimensional matrix algebra),

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ψ) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ψ).

The two-Pauli qubit channel is the channel

  Φ_{2P}(ρ) = (1 − x) ρ + (x/2) (σ_x ρ σ_x + σ_z ρ σ_z),  x ∈ [0,1],

where σ_x, σ_z are the Pauli matrices. In the Bloch representation it acts as a diagonal map (r_x, r_y, r_z) ↦ (λ_x r_x, λ_y r_y, λ_z r_z) with multipliers (λ_x, λ_y, λ_z) = (1 − x, 1 − 2x, 1 − x); for x > 1/2 the middle multiplier is negative. By a unitary rotation one can conjugate Φ_{2P} into a channel with all multipliers non-negative, and known proofs of p-norm multiplicativity for Φ_{2P} pass through such conjugation.

Problem. Produce a proof, valid for all p ∈ [1, ∞] (in particular for the relevant range establishing additivity-type results), that the two-Pauli qubit channel Φ_{2P} satisfies

  ν_p(Φ_{2P} ⊗ Ψ) = ν_p(Φ_{2P}) · ν_p(Ψ)

for every channel Ψ, without using unitary equivalence to a Pauli-diagonal channel whose Bloch multipliers are all non-negative.
status_search_result: The general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture for quantum channels was disproved (Hastings; Hayden–Winter) for sufficiently large p, but multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel is established via known King-style proofs that do invoke unitary equivalence to a channel with non-negative multipliers. No published work was located that provides a multiplicativity proof for the two-Pauli qubit channel avoiding this reduction, so the specific methodological question appears to remain unresolved, though we could not verify this conclusively.

context_brief: Subgroups of direct limit Lie groups
original_question: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence G1 subseteq G2 subseteq ... of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, must every subgroup H of G be an initial Lie subgroup of G? Equivalently, can H be equipped with the direct-limit Lie group structure coming from Hn := Gn intersection H so that the inclusion H -> G is strongly C^k-initial for every k in N union {infinity}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G_1 \subseteq G_2 \subseteq \cdots$ be an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional real Lie groups such that each inclusion map $G_n \hookrightarrow G_{n+1}$ is a smooth homomorphism, and let $G = \varinjlim G_n$ denote the corresponding direct limit Lie group (in the category of Lie groups modeled on locally convex spaces, with its natural direct-limit smooth structure).

Recall that a subgroup $H \subseteq G$ endowed with a Lie group structure is called an initial Lie subgroup of $G$ if the inclusion $\iota: H \to G$ is smooth and, for every smooth manifold $M$ and every map $f: M \to H$, $f$ is smooth whenever $\iota \circ f: M \to G$ is smooth. More strongly, the inclusion is called strongly $C^k$-initial (for $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$) if for every $C^k$-manifold $M$ and every map $f: M \to H$, $f$ is $C^k$ whenever $\iota \circ f: M \to G$ is $C^k$.

For an arbitrary subgroup $H \subseteq G$, set $H_n := G_n \cap H$ and equip $H_n$ with a finite-dimensional Lie group structure induced from $G_n$ and $H$, then equip $H$ with the direct-limit Lie group structure $H = \varinjlim H_n$.

Prove or disprove: with these structures, the inclusion $H \to G$ is strongly $C^k$-initial for every $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; in particular, every subgroup of $G$ is an initial Lie subgroup of $G$.
status_search_result: The question (posed as Problem VII.3 in a survey by Neeb on infinite-dimensional Lie groups) is answered affirmatively by Glöckner: every subgroup of a direct limit of finite-dimensional Lie groups admits a direct-limit Lie group structure making the inclusion strongly $C^k$-initial for all $k$, hence is an initial Lie subgroup.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Identify new classes of extreme completely positive trace-preserving maps for which one can prove minimal output entropy additivity, S_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S_min(Φ) + S_min(Ω), and/or maximal output p-norm multiplicativity, ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a completely positive trace-preserving (CPT) linear map between finite-dimensional matrix algebras. Recall that $\Phi$ is called extreme if it is an extreme point of the convex set of CPT maps from $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)$ to $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$; equivalently, by Choi's theorem, $\Phi$ has a Kraus representation $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{k=1}^{r} A_k\rho A_k^*$ such that the operators $\{A_j^*A_k\}_{j,k=1}^{r}$ are linearly independent.

Define the minimal output von Neumann entropy of $\Phi$ by
$$S_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}\, S(\Phi(\rho)),\qquad S(\sigma)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma),$$
the infimum being over density matrices on $\mathcal{H}_A$. For $1\le p\le\infty$ define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)=\sup_{\rho}\,\|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,\qquad \|\sigma\|_p=(\operatorname{Tr}|\sigma|^p)^{1/p}.$$

Identify new classes of extreme CPT maps $\Phi$ such that, for every CPT map $\Omega$ (in some natural class, e.g. all CPT maps, or all maps in the same class), one can prove either the additivity relation
$$S_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S_{\min}(\Phi)+S_{\min}(\Omega),$$
or the multiplicativity relation
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega)$$
for some $p>1$.
status_search_result: The general additivity conjecture for minimal output von Neumann entropy was disproved by Hastings (2009) via random channel constructions, with later analyses by Fukuda–King–Moser and Aubrun–Szarek. Multiplicativity of maximal output $p$-norms for $p>1$ was also disproved (Hayden–Winter). However, additivity/multiplicativity is still proved for specific classes of channels (entanglement-breaking, unital qubit, depolarizing, Hadamard, etc.), and the broader task of identifying new classes of extreme CPT maps for which these relations hold remains an active research direction with only partial results.

context_brief: Direct limits as topological groups with Lie algebra
original_question: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, is G a topological group with Lie algebra in the sense of Hofmann and Morris? That is, do the continuous one-parameter subgroups Hom_c(R, G) carry the vector-space and Lie-bracket operations specified by Definition 3.1, with addition given by the Trotter-type limit of (gamma(t/n) eta(t/n))^n and bracket given by the commutator limit, so that Hom_c(R, G) becomes a topological Lie algebra naturally identified with L(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G_1 \subseteq G_2 \subseteq \cdots$ be an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional real Lie groups such that each inclusion $G_n \hookrightarrow G_{n+1}$ is a smooth homomorphism, and let $G = \varinjlim G_n$ be the direct limit, equipped with the finest topology making all inclusions $G_n \to G$ continuous (so that $G$ is a topological group). Let $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ denote the set of continuous one-parameter subgroups of $G$, equipped with the compact-open topology, and let scalar multiplication be defined by $(s\cdot \gamma)(t) := \gamma(st)$.

The topological group $G$ is said to be a topological group with Lie algebra (in the sense of Hofmann–Morris) if:
(a) for all $\gamma, \eta \in \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$, the limit
$$(\gamma + \eta)(t) := \lim_{n \to \infty} \big(\gamma(t/n)\,\eta(t/n)\big)^n$$
exists for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and defines a continuous homomorphism $\mathbb{R} \to G$;
(b) with this addition and the scalar multiplication above, $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ is a topological vector space;
(c) there exists a continuous bilinear map $[\cdot,\cdot] : \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G) \times \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G) \to \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ given by a commutator limit, making $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ into a topological Lie algebra.

Question: Is every such direct limit $G = \varinjlim G_n$ a topological group with Lie algebra in this sense, with $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ naturally identified as a topological Lie algebra with the Lie algebra $L(G) = \varinjlim L(G_n)$ of $G$?
status_search_result: The question is answered affirmatively: every direct limit of finite-dimensional Lie groups along smooth inclusions is a topological group with Lie algebra in the Hofmann–Morris sense, and the natural map $L(G) \to \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R}, G)$ is a homeomorphism of topological Lie algebras.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For random sub-unitary channels, prove maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), at least at p = 2, or determine whether these channels yield additional counterexamples to multiplicativity.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map Φ: M_d(ℂ) → M_{d'}(ℂ), which can be represented in Kraus form Φ(ρ) = Σ_k A_k ρ A_k^*, with Σ_k A_k^* A_k = I_d. For p ≥ 1, the maximal output p-norm of Φ is defined by

  ν_p(Φ) := sup_{ρ ≥ 0, Tr ρ = 1} ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where ‖X‖_p = (Tr|X|^p)^{1/p} is the Schatten p-norm.

A channel Φ is called a "random sub-unitary channel" if it admits a Kraus representation of the form

  A_k = √{p_k} · U_k P_k,

where {p_k} is a probability distribution (p_k ≥ 0, Σ_k p_k = 1), each U_k is a unitary on ℂ^d, and each P_k is an orthogonal projection on ℂ^d, chosen so that the trace-preserving condition Σ_k p_k P_k U_k^* U_k P_k = Σ_k p_k P_k = I_d holds. (Equivalently, Φ(ρ) = Σ_k p_k U_k P_k ρ P_k U_k^* with Σ_k p_k P_k = I.)

Question. Let Φ be a random sub-unitary channel and let Ω be an arbitrary quantum channel. Prove or disprove the multiplicativity identity

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω),

at least in the case p = 2. If this identity fails, exhibit a pair (Φ, Ω) with Φ random sub-unitary for which strict inequality ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) > ν_p(Φ) ν_p(Ω) occurs.
status_search_result: While the general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been disproved for all p > 1 (Hayden–Winter, and for p > 2 by Winter), and weak multiplicativity results for random quantum channels are known (Montanaro and others), no source found directly settles the multiplicativity of ν_p at p = 2 specifically for the class of "random sub-unitary" channels with Kraus operators of the form √{p_k} U_k P_k. The status of this specific question appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

original_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $\sigma$-compact smooth manifold of dimension $n \geq 1$, and let $p \in M$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$ denote the group of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms of $M$, and let \[ \mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0} = \{\, \gamma \in \mathrm{Diff}_c(M) : \gamma(p) = p \text{ and } \det(d\gamma_p) > 0 \,\}. \] Fix a smooth chart $\varphi$ around $p$ with $\varphi(p) = 0$. For $\gamma \in \mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$, write $T_p^\infty(\gamma)$ for the formal power series at $0$ of $\varphi \circ \gamma \circ \varphi^{-1}$. Let $G_f^n(\mathbb{R})_0$ denote the group (under formal composition) of formal power series diffeomorphisms $f = (f_1, \ldots, f_n) \in \mathbb{R}[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]^n$ with $f(0) = 0$ and $\det(Df(0)) > 0$.

Question: Is the Taylor-series map
\[ T_p^\infty : \mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0} \longrightarrow G_f^n(\mathbb{R})_0 \]
a surjective homomorphism of (infinite-dimensional) Lie groups? Equivalently, is every formal diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with positive-determinant linear part realized as the Taylor expansion at $p$ of some compactly supported diffeomorphism of $M$ fixing $p$?
status_search_result: The problem (a Borel-type theorem for diffeomorphism groups, asserting surjectivity of the Taylor-series map onto formal diffeomorphisms with positive-determinant linear part) is established as a theorem; the surjectivity is proved by reducing to the case $M = \mathbb{R}^n$ via charts and applying the classical Borel theorem componentwise to construct a compactly supported smooth diffeomorphism with prescribed jet.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For any fixed pair of quantum channels Φ and Ω, does there exist a number p* > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds either for every p in an interval (p*,1) with p* < 1 or for every p in an interval (1,p*) with p* > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_A)$ and $\Omega:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_B)$ be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving linear maps between matrix algebras). For $p>0$, $p\neq 1$, the Rényi entropy of order $p$ of a density operator $\rho$ is
$$S^p(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^p),$$
and for $p=1$ it is the von Neumann entropy $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$. The minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy of a channel $\Phi$ is
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}S^p(\Phi(\rho)),$$
where the infimum is over input density operators (equivalently, pure states).

Decide the following statement: for every pair of quantum channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$, there exists $p^*>0$ such that either
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $p^*<1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(p^*,1)$, or
\item[(ii)] $p^*>1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(1,p^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
That is, prove this dichotomy holds for all channel pairs, or exhibit a counterexample.
category_tag: Quantum channels and Rényi entropy additivity
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be refuted. Hastings (2009) produced channels for which additivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy fails at $p=1$; subsequent analyses (Aubrun–Szarek–Werner; Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter; Collins–Fukuda–Nechita and others) show that the same random-subspace constructions yield violations of additivity of the minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy on intervals adjacent to $p=1$ (in particular for $p\in(1-p_0,1)$ with $p_0\approx 0.2855$). Combined with Hayden–Winter / Grudka–Horodecki / recent constructive results showing violations for all $p>1$, there exist fixed pairs $(\Phi,\Omega)$ for which additivity fails on every one-sided neighborhood of $p=1$, contradicting the conjectured dichotomy.

paper_title: A Collection of Problems on Spectrally Bounded Operators
original_question: Let A be a Banach algebra and let δ: A → A be a derivation. Suppose that for every x in A the commutator [x, δx] = xδx − δx x belongs to Z(A), where Z(A) denotes the centre modulo the radical, i.e. the preimage in A of the centre of A/rad(A). Must it follow that δ(A) is contained in rad(A)? Equivalently, under the same hypothesis, must δ be spectrally bounded?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra with Jacobson radical $\operatorname{rad}(A)$, and let $Z(A/\operatorname{rad}(A))$ denote the centre of the quotient Banach algebra $A/\operatorname{rad}(A)$. Define
$$Z(A) := \pi^{-1}\bigl(Z(A/\operatorname{rad}(A))\bigr),$$
where $\pi: A \to A/\operatorname{rad}(A)$ is the canonical quotient map (so $Z(A)$ is the centre modulo the radical).

Let $\delta: A \to A$ be a (not necessarily continuous) derivation, i.e. a linear map satisfying $\delta(xy) = \delta(x)y + x\delta(y)$ for all $x, y \in A$. Suppose that
$$[x, \delta x] := x\,\delta x - \delta x \cdot x \in Z(A) \qquad \text{for every } x \in A.$$

Question: Does it follow that $\delta(A) \subseteq \operatorname{rad}(A)$? Equivalently, under the same hypothesis, must $\delta$ be spectrally bounded (i.e. must there exist a constant $M \geq 0$ such that the spectral radius satisfies $r(\delta x) \leq M\, r(x)$ for all $x \in A$)?
status_search_result: The noncommutative Singer–Wermer conjecture, asking whether every (possibly discontinuous) derivation on a noncommutative Banach algebra maps into the Jacobson radical (under the centre-modulo-radical commutator hypothesis), remains open. The continuous case and the commutative case (the classical Singer–Wermer theorem, proved by Thomas in 1988) are known, and recent work has only addressed variants such as φ-derivations, skew derivations, and canonical test cases, without resolving the general conjecture.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For each fixed dimension bound d, does there exist a number p_d > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds uniformly for all channels Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'} with d' ≤ d either throughout p_d < p < 1 when p_d < 1 or throughout 1 < p < p_d when p_d > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let M_n denote the algebra of n×n complex matrices, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ: M_n → M_n. For p > 0 with p ≠ 1, the minimal output Rényi p-entropy of Φ is defined by
   S^p_min(Φ) = inf_ρ (1/(1−p)) log Tr[(Φ(ρ))^p],
where the infimum runs over all density matrices ρ ∈ M_n (positive semidefinite, trace one); equivalently, S^p_min(Φ) = inf_ρ S_p(Φ(ρ)), where S_p(σ) = (1−p)^{−1} log Tr(σ^p) is the Rényi p-entropy of σ.

For two channels Φ: M_n → M_n and Ω: M_m → M_m, the tensor product channel Φ ⊗ Ω: M_{nm} → M_{nm} is the standard one. Say that the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive if
   S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω).

Prove or disprove: For every positive integer d there exists a real number p_d > 0 such that one of the following holds:
 (i) p_d < 1, and for every pair of integers d', d'' ≤ d, every channel Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'}, every channel Ω: M_{d''} → M_{d''}, and every p with p_d < p < 1, the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive;
 (ii) p_d > 1, and for every pair of integers d', d'' ≤ d, every channel Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'}, every channel Ω: M_{d''} → M_{d''}, and every p with 1 < p < p_d, the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive.
status_search_result: Case (ii) of the conjecture (a neighborhood of 1 from above) has been refuted: counterexamples to additivity of minimum output Rényi p-entropy are now known for every p > 1 (Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter, 2008, and subsequent constructive work). For 0 < p < 1, counterexamples have been constructed for p in intervals (0, p₀) and (1 − p₀, 1) with p₀ ≈ 0.2855, ruling out a uniform p_d for sufficiently large dimensions. The von Neumann (p = 1) additivity itself was disproved by Hastings (2008). Thus a uniform dimension-dependent threshold p_d as conjectured does not survive on the p > 1 side, and is severely constrained on the p < 1 side; the precise dimension-by-dimension version stated remains not fully resolved in the literature.

paper_title: A Collection of Problems on Spectrally Bounded Operators
original_question: Let A and B be semisimple unital Banach algebras, and let T: A → B be a unital, surjective, invertibility-preserving linear map. Is T necessarily a Jordan epimorphism, meaning a surjective linear map that preserves the Jordan product x ◦ y = (xy + yx)/2?
status_search_result: Kaplansky's problem on whether unital surjective invertibility-preserving linear maps between semisimple unital Banach algebras must be Jordan epimorphisms remains open in general. Affirmative answers are known in important special cases, e.g., when the domain is a von Neumann algebra (Aupetit) and when the codomain is a C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state, but the general case (and even the C*-algebra case, sometimes called the Harris–Kadison conjecture) is still unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Rényi-additivity violations on both sides of p=1
original_question: Does there exist a single channel, or a pair of channels, that violates additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω) both at some p1 > 1 and at some p2 with 0 < p2 < 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. A quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map. For $p>0$, $p\neq 1$, the Rényi $p$-entropy of a state $\rho$ is
$$S^p(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\mathrm{Tr}(\rho^p),$$
and the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy of $\Phi$ is
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}S^p(\Phi(\rho)),$$
where the infimum is over input density operators on $\mathcal{H}_A$. One says that channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$ satisfy additivity at exponent $p$ when
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega).$$

Question: Do there exist a quantum channel $\Phi$ (or a pair of quantum channels $\Phi,\Omega$) and exponents $p_1>1$ and $0<p_2<1$ such that additivity of the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy fails simultaneously at $p=p_1$ and at $p=p_2$ for the same channel (or for the same pair of channels)?
status_search_result: Counterexamples to additivity of the minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy are now known separately for all $p>1$ (constructive examples, e.g., 2025 constructions extending earlier $p>2$ results) and for $p$ close to $0$ (Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter, 2008). However, web searches did not surface a result exhibiting a single channel or fixed pair of channels that simultaneously violates additivity at some $p_1>1$ and at some $p_2\in(0,1)$, so the specific question of joint violation by one channel/pair appears not to be definitively settled in the located literature.

paper_title: A Collection of Problems on Spectrally Bounded Operators
context_brief: Glimm ideal invariance under spectral isometries
original_question: If T is a unital spectral isometry from a unital C*-algebra onto another unital C*-algebra, must T leave every Glimm ideal invariant? In other words, does each Glimm ideal I in the domain necessarily satisfy that its image under T corresponds to an invariant Glimm ideal in the codomain?
self_contained_problem:
Let A and B be unital C*-algebras. For an element a in a unital C*-algebra, write sp(a) for its spectrum and r(a) = sup{|λ| : λ ∈ sp(a)} for its spectral radius. A linear map T : A → B is called a spectral isometry if r(T(a)) = r(a) for every a ∈ A; T is called unital if T(1_A) = 1_B.

Recall that for a unital C*-algebra A, the Glimm ideals of A are the closed two-sided ideals of A generated by the maximal ideals of the center Z(A); equivalently, they are the intersections of the primitive ideals of A lying over a single point of the maximal ideal space of Z(A). The set of Glimm ideals of A is in natural bijection with the maximal ideal space of Z(A).

Question: Suppose T : A → B is a surjective unital spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras. Must T leave every Glimm ideal of A invariant, in the sense that for each Glimm ideal G of A there is a Glimm ideal G' of B with T(G) = G' (equivalently, T induces a bijection between the Glimm ideals of A and those of B compatible with T)?

context_brief: First tensor-power failure of Rényi additivity
original_question: Find a quantum channel Φ, an integer m, and a real p > 0 such that minimal output Rényi entropy is additive for fewer than m tensor powers, S^p_min(Φ^{⊗n}) = n S^p_min(Φ) for n < m, but fails exactly at m copies in the sense S^p_min(Φ^{⊗m}) < m S^p_min(Φ).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a quantum channel, i.e. a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between matrix algebras. For a real number $p>0$, define the minimal output $p$-Rényi entropy of $\Phi$ by
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi) \;=\; \inf_{\rho}\, S_p\bigl(\Phi(\rho)\bigr), \qquad S_p(\sigma)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma^p),$$
where the infimum is over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$. For an integer $n\ge 1$ let $\Phi^{\otimes n}$ denote the $n$-fold tensor power of $\Phi$, acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A^{\otimes n})$. One always has $S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes n})\le n\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi)$.

Exhibit an explicit triple $(\Phi, m, p)$ consisting of a quantum channel $\Phi$, an integer $m\ge 2$, and a real number $p>0$ such that
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes n}) \;=\; n\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi) \quad \text{for every } 1\le n<m,$$
but
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes m}) \;<\; m\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi).$$
That is, additivity of the minimal output $p$-Rényi entropy holds for fewer than $m$ tensor copies and fails for the first time at exactly $m$ copies.
status_search_result: Many counterexamples to additivity of minimum output p-Rényi entropy are known (for p>2, p>1, p close to 0, and via random/antisymmetric constructions). However, none of the located references explicitly exhibit a channel where additivity holds for all n<m but breaks exactly at n=m for some finite m≥2; the question of a "first failure at exactly m copies" remains unresolved in the sources found.

original_question: Is every unital surjective spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras necessarily a Jordan isomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ and $B$ be unital C*-algebras. For an element $a$ in a unital Banach algebra, denote by $\sigma(a)$ its spectrum and by $r(a) = \sup\{|\lambda| : \lambda \in \sigma(a)\}$ its spectral radius. A linear map $T : A \to B$ is called a spectral isometry if $r(T(a)) = r(a)$ for every $a \in A$. A linear map $J : A \to B$ is called a Jordan isomorphism if it is a bijection satisfying $J(a^2) = J(a)^2$ for all $a \in A$ (equivalently, $J(ab + ba) = J(a)J(b) + J(b)J(a)$).

Question: Is every unital ($T(1_A) = 1_B$) surjective spectral isometry $T : A \to B$ between unital C*-algebras necessarily a Jordan isomorphism?
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: e.g. if a unital surjective spectral isometry maps projections to idempotents and the domain has real rank zero, then it is a Jordan isomorphism. No source found announces a full solution; the question continues to appear as an open problem in subsequent literature on spectrally bounded operators.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For all counterexamples to maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), must the counterexample channels have non-negative completely bounded (CB) entropy and/or zero coherent information?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the bounded operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$. For $p\ge 1$, define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)=\sup_{\rho}\,\|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,$$
where the supremum runs over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$. A pair $(\Phi,\Omega)$ of channels is said to be a counterexample to maximal output $p$-norm multiplicativity if
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)>\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega).$$

For a channel $\Phi$ with Stinespring isometry $V:\mathcal{H}_A\to\mathcal{H}_B\otimes\mathcal{H}_E$ and complementary channel $\Phi^c(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^\dagger)$, define:
- the coherent information $I_c(\rho,\Phi)=S(\Phi(\rho))-S(\Phi^c(\rho))$, where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy;
- the completely bounded (CB) entropy $S_{\mathrm{CB}}(\Phi)$, defined as the regularized minimum, over all input states $\rho_{RA}$ on an arbitrary reference system $R$ tensored with the input, of $S(\Phi^c(\rho_A))-S(\Phi(\rho_A))$ optimized in the CB sense (equivalently, $-\inf_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$ in the appropriate completely bounded regularization).

Question: For every $p>1$ and every pair of channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ that violates maximal output $p$-norm multiplicativity, must at least one of the following hold for the channels involved?
(a) The CB entropy is non-negative;
(b) The maximum coherent information $\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$ equals zero.

However, no source found explicitly addresses whether all known counterexamples necessarily exhibit non-negative CB entropy and/or zero coherent information; the specific entropy-signature question therefore appears not to have been settled in the literature returned by search.

original_question: Prove additivity of minimal output entropy for quantum channels, S_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S_min(Φ) + S_min(Ω), where S_min(Φ) is the infimum of S[Φ(γ)] over density matrices γ, or else find a counterexample to this additivity statement.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find pairs of quantum channels M and N that are mutually degradable, meaning that there exist channels X and Y for which X ∘ M equals the complementary channel N^C and Y ∘ N equals the complementary channel M^C; in particular, find nontrivial examples beyond the known case M = I, such as pairs where both channels have Choi rank d but are not individually degradable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$, $\mathcal{H}_B$, $\mathcal{H}_E$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. Recall that a quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map between spaces of trace-class operators. Every channel $M : B(\mathcal{H}_A) \to B(\mathcal{H}_B)$ admits a Stinespring isometry $V_M : \mathcal{H}_A \to \mathcal{H}_B \otimes \mathcal{H}_E$ such that $M(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_E(V_M \rho V_M^*)$; the complementary channel is defined by $M^C(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_B(V_M \rho V_M^*)$. The Choi rank of $M$ is the minimum dimension of $\mathcal{H}_E$ in any Stinespring dilation, equivalently the rank of the Choi matrix of $M$. A channel $M$ is called degradable if there exists a channel $D$ with $D \circ M = M^C$.

Two channels $M$ and $N$ (with appropriately compatible input/output spaces) are said to be mutually degradable if there exist channels $X$ and $Y$ such that
$$ X \circ M = N^C \quad \text{and} \quad Y \circ N = M^C. $$

Note that if $M = I$ is the identity channel, then $M^C$ is (up to isometry) the trace, so the conditions reduce trivially and any channel $N$ pairs with $I$. Exhibit nontrivial pairs $(M, N)$ of mutually degradable channels in which neither channel is the identity. In particular, construct a pair $(M, N)$ such that both $M$ and $N$ act on a $d$-dimensional input system, both have Choi rank equal to $d$, and neither $M$ nor $N$ is individually degradable; or prove that no such pair exists.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For the N-representability problem, where one seeks necessary and sufficient conditions for a p-particle reduced density matrix to come from an antisymmetric or symmetric N-particle density matrix, find a minimal complete set of local invariants for an antisymmetric or symmetric two-particle density matrix. The local invariants should be parameters invariant under transformations U ⊗ U ⊗ … ⊗ U and rich enough to express the two-particle N-representability conditions.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $U(\mathcal{H})$ denote its unitary group. For an integer $N\ge 2$, consider the $N$-fold tensor power $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}$, and let $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge N}\subset \mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee N}$) denote its totally antisymmetric (resp. totally symmetric) subspace. An $N$-fermion (resp. $N$-boson) density matrix is a positive semidefinite trace-one operator $\rho_{1,\dots,N}$ supported on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge N}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee N}$). For $1\le p\le N$, the $p$-particle reduced density matrix is
$$\rho_{1,\dots,p}\;=\;\mathrm{Tr}_{p+1,\dots,N}\,\rho_{1,\dots,N},$$
which acts on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge p}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee p}$).

Local unitary action. The unitary group $U(\mathcal{H})$ acts on operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes p}$ via the diagonal representation $U^{\otimes p}$, i.e. by
$$\rho \;\longmapsto\; U^{\otimes p}\,\rho\,(U^{\otimes p})^\dagger,\qquad U\in U(\mathcal{H}).$$
A local invariant of a $p$-particle density matrix is a function of $\rho_{1,\dots,p}$ that is constant on each orbit of this action. A set $\{I_\alpha\}$ of local invariants is called complete if it separates orbits, i.e. two $p$-particle density matrices have the same values of all $I_\alpha$ if and only if they lie in the same $U^{\otimes p}$-orbit. The set is called minimal if no proper subset is complete.

Problem. Take $p=2$. Exhibit, for both the antisymmetric case (operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge 2}$) and the symmetric case (operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\vee 2}$), a minimal complete set of local invariants of a two-particle density matrix under the action $\rho \mapsto (U\otimes U)\rho(U\otimes U)^\dagger$, $U\in U(\mathcal{H})$. The set should be expressive enough that the two-particle $N$-representability conditions (necessary and sufficient conditions on $\rho_{1,2}$ for the existence of an $N$-particle antisymmetric/symmetric density matrix $\rho_{1,\dots,N}$ with $\mathrm{Tr}_{3,\dots,N}\rho_{1,\dots,N}=\rho_{1,2}$) can be formulated in terms of these invariants.

The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let H^k_n(r) = (Delta^n(1-r) x Delta^k) union (Delta^n x A^k(r,1)) be the Hartogs figure introduced in the paper, and let X be a compact or disk-convex complex manifold or complex space in the class P^-_k, with the stronger subclass G_k when appropriate. Is it true in all dimensions that every meromorphic map from H^k_n(r) to X extends to Delta^(n+k) minus a singular set A of Hausdorff (2n-1)-dimensional measure zero, with the stronger topological restrictions predicted in the G_k case when A is nonempty? In particular, should the three-dimensional extension theorem stated as Theorem 3.2 remain valid for equidimensional meromorphic maps in every dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For positive integers $n,k$ and $0<r<1$, let $\Delta^m\subset\mathbb{C}^m$ denote the open unit polydisc, $\Delta^m(s)$ the polydisc of polyradius $s$, and $A^k(r,1)=\Delta^k\setminus\overline{\Delta^k(r)}$ the spherical shell. Define the Hartogs figure
$$H^k_n(r)=\bigl(\Delta^n(1-r)\times\Delta^k\bigr)\;\cup\;\bigl(\Delta^n\times A^k(r,1)\bigr)\subset\Delta^{n+k}.$$

Classes of target spaces. A complex manifold (or complex space) $X$ is said to belong to the class $\mathcal{P}^-_k$ if every meromorphic map from $H^k_n(r)$ into $X$ extends meromorphically to $\Delta^{n+k}$ minus a (possibly empty) analytic-type singular set; and to the (stronger) class $\mathcal{G}_k$ if, in addition, the existence of a non-removable singularity forces strong topological/complex-structural constraints on $X$ (e.g. existence of rational curves, non-Kähler structure, etc., as in known results for $k=1$). Assume $X$ is compact, or more generally disk-convex.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following:

(a) (General extension.) For every $n,k\ge 1$ and every compact or disk-convex complex manifold/space $X\in\mathcal{P}^-_k$, every meromorphic map $f:H^k_n(r)\dashrightarrow X$ extends to a meromorphic map on $\Delta^{n+k}\setminus A$, where $A$ is a closed subset of Hausdorff $(2n-1)$-dimensional measure zero.

(b) (Topological rigidity in $\mathcal{G}_k$.) If furthermore $X\in\mathcal{G}_k$ and the singular set $A$ in (a) is nonempty, then $X$ must satisfy very restrictive conditions on its topology and complex structure (to be made precise, paralleling the case $k=1$).

(c) (Equidimensional case.) In particular, the three-dimensional Hartogs-type extension theorem for equidimensional meromorphic maps holds in every dimension: every meromorphic map between equidimensional complex manifolds from $H^k_n(r)$ into a compact manifold of class $\mathcal{P}^-_k$ extends as in (a).

Math. 1992; Ann. of Math. 2004; results for q-complete and non-Kähler targets), but no source was found that directly settles the general higher-dimensional conjecture for the classes $\mathcal{P}^-_k$ and $\mathcal{G}_k$ as stated. The status appears to remain unresolved in full generality.

original_question: As a first step toward the general conjecture on extension from Hartogs figures, prove the case of meromorphic extension from the four-dimensional Hartogs figure H^2_2(r) to a target manifold in the class G_2.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc and, for $0<r<1$, let
$$H^{2}_{2}(r)\;=\;\bigl\{(z_1,z_2)\in\Delta^{2}\,:\,|z_1|>1-r\bigr\}\;\cup\;\bigl\{(z_1,z_2)\in\Delta^{2}\,:\,|z_2|<r\bigr\}\subset\mathbb C^{2}$$
be the (two‑complex‑dimensional, four‑real‑dimensional) Hartogs figure, with associated Hartogs hull (envelope of holomorphy) the bidisc $\Delta^{2}$.

Let $\mathcal G_{2}$ denote the class of complex manifolds $X$ characterised by the following Hartogs‑type extension property: every meromorphic map from a Hartogs figure of complex dimension $2$ into $X$ extends meromorphically to the corresponding bidisc, possibly after blow‑ups along an analytic subset of codimension at least $2$ in the target (the natural class of target manifolds where two‑dimensional meromorphic Hartogs extension is known to hold under additional disc‑convexity / Kähler‑type assumptions).

Prove the following base case of the general meromorphic‑extension‑from‑Hartogs‑figures conjecture: for every complex manifold $X\in\mathcal G_{2}$, every $0<r<1$, and every meromorphic map
$$f:H^{2}_{2}(r)\longrightarrow X,$$
there exists a meromorphic extension
$$\widetilde f:\Delta^{2}\longrightarrow X$$
with $\widetilde f|_{H^{2}_{2}(r)}=f$.

Related Hartogs‑type extension results for meromorphic mappings into compact Kähler, disc‑convex, and $q$-complete targets are known, but no source located clearly settles this precise formulation. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
original_question: For semi-algebraic sets, are the middle Betti numbers intrinsically harder to compute than the lowest Betti numbers, the highest Betti numbers, and the Euler-Poincare characteristic? More concretely, is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result or analogous explanation showing that middle Betti numbers carry the computationally difficult information, in the way they carry central information in some geometric settings such as smooth projective complex varieties?
self_contained_problem:
A semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb{R}^k$ is a finite Boolean combination of sets of the form $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^k : P(x) \ \square \ 0\}$ where $P \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$ and $\square \in \{=,>,<,\ge,\le\}$. For a semi-algebraic set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^k$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ denote its $i$-th Betti number, and let $\chi(S) = \sum_i (-1)^i b_i(S)$ denote its Euler–Poincaré characteristic. Algorithms are known that, given a description of $S$ (e.g. a quantifier-free formula in a fixed first-order language over the reals with polynomials of bounded degree), compute the lowest Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_\ell(S)$ for any constant $\ell$, the top Betti number $b_{\dim S}(S)$, and $\chi(S)$ with significantly better complexity bounds (e.g. singly exponential in $k$) than those known for the "middle" Betti numbers $b_i(S)$ with $i$ near $\dim S / 2$ (where only doubly exponential bounds are currently available).

Question: Is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result establishing that, for semi-algebraic sets, computing the middle Betti numbers is intrinsically harder than computing the lowest Betti numbers, the highest Betti number, or the Euler–Poincaré characteristic? Equivalently, exhibit a reduction or other rigorous separation explaining why middle Betti numbers concentrate the computationally difficult information, in analogy with their role of carrying essential geometric information for smooth projective complex varieties.
status_search_result: Partial hardness results exist (e.g. computing the $\ell$-th Betti number of semi-algebraic sets defined by quadratic inequalities is #P-hard for $\ell = O(\log k)$, and connectedness/Betti-number decision problems for complex varieties are PSPACE-hard), and algorithms compute lowest/top Betti numbers and the Euler characteristic faster than middle ones. However, no known complexity-theoretic separation rigorously establishes that the middle Betti numbers are intrinsically harder than the lowest/top Betti numbers or the Euler–Poincaré characteristic, so the question appears to remain open.

original_question: Generalize Corollary 3.2 to all dimensions. In other words, for a compact affine n-fold whose universal cover is viewed as a domain over C^n with locally biholomorphic projection, determine whether pseudoconcavity of the covering domain at a boundary point forces the compact manifold to contain the higher-dimensional analogue of a spherical shell.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$. Let $V$ be a compact complex affine $n$-fold, i.e. a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ equipped with a holomorphic affine structure (a maximal atlas of holomorphic charts into $\mathbb{C}^n$ whose transition maps are restrictions of complex affine transformations of $\mathbb{C}^n$). The developing map of this structure realizes the universal cover $\widetilde V$ as a Riemann domain $(\widetilde V,\widetilde\pi)$ over $\mathbb{C}^n$ with locally biholomorphic projection $\widetilde\pi:\widetilde V\to\mathbb{C}^n$. 

Recall that $(\widetilde V,\widetilde\pi)$ is said to be pseudoconcave at a boundary point $p\in\partial\widetilde V$ if there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$ in the natural completion such that, for every plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ defined on $U\cap\widetilde V$ and continuous up to $p$, one has $\varphi(p)\le\sup_{U\cap\widetilde V}\varphi$ (equivalently, the boundary is pseudoconcave in the sense of Andreotti). A compact complex manifold $V$ of dimension $n$ is said to contain a spherical shell (of dimension $n$) if there exists a holomorphic embedding of a neighborhood of the unit sphere $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ into $V$ which is not homologous to zero (equivalently, whose image does not bound in $V$).

Question: Suppose that $(\widetilde V,\widetilde\pi)$ is pseudoconcave at some boundary point. Does it follow that $V$ contains a spherical shell of dimension $n$?
status_search_result: Web searches for the higher-dimensional generalization of the pseudoconcavity/spherical-shell result for compact affine manifolds did not return any source explicitly resolving the n-dimensional case. No follow-up paper claiming a proof or counterexample was located, so the current status could not be verified.

original_question: Let X be a compact complex manifold carrying a plurinegative metric form, and let f: Delta^3 \ S -> X be a meromorphic map. Suppose A is the minimal closed subset of Delta^3 such that f extends meromorphically to Delta^3 \ A. Prove that each connected component of A is a complex curve.
self_contained_problem:

$$f : \Delta^3 \setminus S \longrightarrow X$$ 
be a meromorphic mapping. Let $A \subset \Delta^3$ be the (unique) minimal closed subset such that $f$ admits a meromorphic extension to $\Delta^3 \setminus A$.

paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
original_question: For general semi-algebraic sets, roadmap algorithms provide connectivity information by constructing a one-dimensional semi-algebraic subset that is nonempty and connected inside each connected component, but their known complexity has an O(k^2) exponent. Can the exponent O(k^2) in roadmap-based connectivity algorithms be improved to O(k), so that testing connectivity has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness? Such an improvement would also seek effective control of semi-algebraic connecting paths, including their length and semi-algebraic complexity, in terms of the input parameters.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{R}$ be a real closed field and let $S \subset \mathbf{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set defined by a quantifier-free first-order formula involving $s$ polynomials of degree at most $d$ in $k$ variables with coefficients in $\mathbf{R}$. A roadmap of $S$ is a one-dimensional semi-algebraic subset $M \subseteq S$ such that, for every connected component $C$ of $S$, the intersection $M \cap C$ is nonempty and semi-algebraically connected, and moreover $M$ meets every connected component of the intersection of $S$ with each hyperplane of a prescribed family. Such a roadmap allows one to decide whether two given points of $S$ lie in the same connected component, and hence to count and identify the semi-algebraically connected components of $S$.

Testing whether $S$ is empty can be performed in time $(s\,d)^{O(k)}$, i.e. with an exponent linear in $k$. The classical roadmap-based algorithms for connectivity over $S$ run in time $(s\,d)^{O(k^2)}$, with a quadratic exponent in $k$.

Question: Can one design an algorithm that, given the defining formula of an arbitrary semi-algebraic set $S \subseteq \mathbf{R}^k$, computes a roadmap of $S$ (and thus decides connectivity and lists connected components) in time $(s\,d)^{O(k)}$, achieving the same asymptotic exponent as the emptiness test? As a consequence, one would obtain bounds of the form $(s\,d)^{O(k)}$ on the semi-algebraic complexity (number of defining polynomials and their degrees) and the length of semi-algebraic paths connecting any two points lying in the same connected component of $S$.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made but the question is not fully resolved. Basu, Roy, Safey El Din, Schost and others introduced "baby-step/giant-step" and divide-and-conquer roadmap algorithms which lowered the exponent from $O(k^2)$ to $O(k^{3/2})$ and, in the smooth bounded real algebraic case, to nearly $O(k)$ (Safey El Din–Schost, JACM 2017). For general (possibly singular, unbounded) semi-algebraic sets, the best known general bound remains super-linear in $k$, so the full conjectured $(sd)^{O(k)}$ complexity for connectivity of arbitrary semi-algebraic sets is still open.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
context_brief: A-local reflexivity for maximal Banach ideals
original_question: Let (A, A) be an arbitrary maximal Banach ideal. Must the principle of A-local reflexivity always hold? Concretely, for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every finite-dimensional subspace F of Y', every operator T in L(E, Y''), and every epsilon > 0, does there always exist an operator S in L(E, Y) such that A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T), the pairing identity <Sx, y'> = <y', Tx> holds for all (x, y') in E x F, and j_Y Sx = Tx for every x in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y))? Equivalently, is there any maximal Banach ideal for which this A-LRP factorization property fails?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ be a maximal Banach operator ideal. Recall that an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ assigns to every pair of Banach spaces $X, Y$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y) \subseteq L(X,Y)$ together with an ideal norm $A(\cdot)$, and is called maximal if for every $T \in L(X,Y)$ one has $A(T) = \sup\{ A(Q_F T J_E) : E \subseteq X \text{ finite-dimensional}, F \subseteq Y \text{ finite-codimensional}\}$, where $J_E : E \hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion and $Q_F : Y \to Y/F$ is the quotient map (so $A$ is determined by its values on finite-rank operators between finite-dimensional spaces and extended by this supremum formula).

For a Banach space $Y$, let $j_Y : Y \hookrightarrow Y''$ denote the canonical embedding into the bidual.

Definition (principle of $A$-local reflexivity, $A$-LRP). The ideal $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ is said to satisfy the principle of $A$-local reflexivity if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F \subseteq Y'$, every operator $T \in L(E, Y'')$, and every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an operator $S \in L(E, Y)$ such that:
  (i) $A(S) \le (1 + \varepsilon)\, A(T)$;
  (ii) $\langle Sx, y' \rangle = \langle y', Tx \rangle$ for all $(x, y') \in E \times F$;
  (iii) $j_Y(Sx) = Tx$ for every $x \in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y))$.

Question. Does every maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ satisfy the principle of $A$-local reflexivity? Equivalently, does there exist a maximal Banach ideal for which the above factorization property fails?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the A-local reflexivity question for arbitrary maximal Banach ideals. The problem is closely tied to the long-standing question of whether every maximal Banach ideal is accessible, which remains open in the literature on operator ideals. paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two conditions equivalent: first, that (A, A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every operator T in L(E, Y), and every epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and an operator S in L(E, N) with T = J_N^Y S and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T); and second, that (A, A) satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle described in Definition 1.1?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A pair $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ is called a Banach operator ideal if $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq \mathfrak{L}$ is an operator ideal in the sense of Pietsch and $A$ is a complete ideal norm on $\mathfrak{A}$. For Banach spaces $E,F$, write $\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ for the component of the ideal and $A(\cdot)$ for its norm. The maximal hull $(\mathfrak{A}^{\max}, A^{\max})$ of $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is defined by
$$A^{\max}(T) := \sup\{ A(Q_L^F T J_M^E) : M\subseteq E\text{ finite-dimensional},\ L\subseteq F\text{ finite-codimensional}\},$$
where $J_M^E:M\hookrightarrow E$ is the inclusion and $Q_L^F:F\twoheadrightarrow F/L$ the quotient map; $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called maximal if $(\mathfrak{A},A)=(\mathfrak{A}^{\max},A^{\max})$.

For a Banach space $Y$ and a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$, let $J_N^Y:N\hookrightarrow Y$ be the canonical inclusion.

Right-accessibility. A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called right-accessible if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,Y)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$ and an operator $S\in\mathfrak{L}(E,N)$ such that
$$T = J_N^Y\, S \qquad\text{and}\qquad A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\, A(T).$$

The $A$-local reflexivity principle ($A$-LRP). A maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is said to satisfy the $A$-local reflexivity principle if for every Banach space $X$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq X^{**}$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subseteq X^*$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an operator $R:M\to X$ such that:
(a) $\langle R x^{**},\,x^*\rangle = \langle x^{**},\,x^*\rangle$ for all $x^{**}\in M$ and all $x^*\in F$;
(b) $R x^{**}=x^{**}$ for every $x^{**}\in M\cap X$ (under the canonical embedding $X\hookrightarrow X^{**}$);
(c) for every Banach space $Z$ and every $T\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,X^{**})$ with $T(Z)\subseteq M$, the operator $R\circ T\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,X)$ satisfies $A(R\circ T)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,A(T)$.

It is known that every right-accessible maximal Banach ideal satisfies the $A$-LRP.

Question.

Let $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(i) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible.
(ii) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the $A$-local reflexivity principle.

Status is therefore unverified.

original_question: Let (A_P, A_P) be Pisier's explicitly constructed maximal Banach ideal that is known not to be right-accessible. Does this specific ideal nevertheless satisfy the A_P-local reflexivity principle? That is, does the A-LRP from Definition 1.1 hold when A is specialized to A_P?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is a subclass $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ together with an ideal norm $\mathbf{A}$ such that, for every pair of Banach spaces $E,F$, the component $\mathfrak{A}(E,F):=\mathfrak{A}\cap\mathfrak{L}(E,F)$ is a Banach space under $\mathbf{A}$, satisfies the ideal property $\mathbf{A}(BTC)\le\|B\|\,\mathbf{A}(T)\,\|C\|$ for all composable bounded operators $B,C$ and all $T\in\mathfrak{A}$, and contains all finite rank operators with $\mathbf{A}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\,\|y\|$.

A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is called maximal if for every operator $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,F)$ one has $T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ with $\mathbf{A}(T)=\sup\mathbf{A}(Q_LTJ_M)$, where the supremum is over all finite-codimensional closed subspaces $L\subseteq F$ and finite-dimensional subspaces $M\subseteq E$, $J_M$ is the inclusion and $Q_L$ the quotient map.

The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is called right-accessible if for every operator $T:E\to F$ between Banach spaces with $E$ finite-dimensional, every $S\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional Banach space $G$, an operator $S_0\in\mathfrak{A}(E,G)$, and an operator $R\in\mathfrak{L}(G,F)$ with $\|R\|\le 1$ such that $S=R S_0$ and $\mathbf{A}(S_0)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(S)$.

For a Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ we say the $\mathfrak{A}$-local reflexivity principle ($\mathfrak{A}$-LRP) holds if for every Banach space $E$, every Banach space $F$, every $T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F^{**})$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq E$, every finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq F^{*}$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\widetilde T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ with $\mathbf{A}(\widetilde T)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(T)$ such that $\widetilde T x=Tx$ on the weak-$*$ closure-sense for $x\in M$ in the duality with $N$, i.e. $\langle \widetilde T x, y'\rangle=\langle Tx,y'\rangle$ for all $x\in M$ and $y'\in N$.

In 1993 G. Pisier constructed an explicit maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P)$ which is not right-accessible.

Question. Does the maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P)$ satisfy the $\mathfrak{A}_P$-LRP?

original_question: Does the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 admit an ideal norm? Equivalently, is the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 normed?
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Work in the category of operators between Banach spaces. For Banach spaces $E,F$ let $\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ denote the Banach space of all bounded linear operators from $E$ into $F$. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ (in the sense of Pietsch) assigns to every pair $(E,F)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(E,F)\subseteq \mathcal{L}(E,F)$ containing all finite-rank operators and stable under composition with bounded operators on either side. A quasi-norm $A$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ making $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ a quasi-Banach ideal is called an ideal quasi-norm; if it is a norm satisfying $A(SRT)\le \|S\|\,A(R)\,\|T\|$ and $A(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{K}})=1$, then $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is a Banach (or normed) operator ideal.

Given two quasi-Banach operator ideals $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ and $(\mathfrak{B},B)$, their product $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ consists of all operators $T\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ that admit a factorization $T=RS$ with $S\in\mathfrak{B}(E,G)$ and $R\in\mathfrak{A}(G,F)$ for some Banach space $G$. The natural quasi-norm on $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ is
$$ (A\circ B)(T) \;=\; \inf\{A(R)\,B(S) : T=RS\}, $$
which is in general only a quasi-norm. One says that the product ideal $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ is normed (admits an ideal norm) if there exists an ideal norm on it equivalent to $A\circ B$ turning it into a Banach operator ideal.

Let $\mathfrak{L}_1$ denote the Banach ideal of absolutely $1$-summing operators, $\mathfrak{L}_2$ the Banach ideal of absolutely $2$-summing operators, and $\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ the Banach ideal of all bounded linear operators. For a quasi-Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$, write $(\mathfrak{A}^{**},A^{**})$ for its bidual ideal in the sense of Pietsch.

Question. Set $\mathfrak{A} := (\mathfrak{L}_1\circ \mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}$. Does the product operator ideal
$$ \mathfrak{A}\circ \mathfrak{L}_2 \;=\; (\mathfrak{L}_1\circ \mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}\circ\mathfrak{L}_2 $$
admit an ideal norm; equivalently, is this product ideal normed?
status_search_result: A 2001 preprint by Oertel ("On normed products of operator ideals which contain L_2 as a factor") raises and studies precisely this type of question, and a 2007 note by the same author lists Problem 2.4 (the question above) as still open, noting that no known criteria suffice to establish such an ideal norm on a product of quasi-Banach ideals. No subsequent published resolution was located.

original_question: The paper lists several notions of disk-convexity: the original condition from Definition 6.1, a version using holomorphic maps from arbitrary bordered Riemann surfaces, a sequential compactness condition for analytic disks, and the analogous sequential condition for families of bordered Riemann surfaces. What is the precise relationship among these notions? Are they all equivalent, and if not, which implications between them are valid?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a complex manifold. Consider the following four candidate notions of "disk-convexity" for X:

(D1) (Disk-convexity via analytic disks.) For every compact subset K ⊂ X there exists a compact subset K' ⊂ X such that for every holomorphic map f: D̄ → X from the closed unit disk D̄ ⊂ ℂ with f(∂D) ⊂ K, one has f(D̄) ⊂ K'.

(D2) (Disk-convexity via bordered Riemann surfaces.) For every compact subset K ⊂ X there exists a compact subset K' ⊂ X such that for every compact bordered Riemann surface (Σ, ∂Σ) and every holomorphic map f: Σ → X with f(∂Σ) ⊂ K, one has f(Σ) ⊂ K'.

(D3) (Sequential disk-convexity for analytic disks.) For every sequence of holomorphic maps f_n: D̄ → X such that the restrictions f_n|_{∂D} converge uniformly on ∂D to a continuous map ∂D → X, the images f_n(D̄) are contained in a compact subset of X (and a subsequence converges in a suitable sense).

(D4) (Sequential disk-convexity for bordered Riemann surfaces.) The analogue of (D3) in which the closed disk D̄ is replaced by an arbitrary compact bordered Riemann surface Σ: for every sequence of holomorphic maps f_n: Σ_n → X (with Σ_n bordered Riemann surfaces of bounded topological type) whose boundary restrictions converge uniformly to a continuous map into X, the images f_n(Σ_n) lie in a compact subset of X.

Determine the precise logical relationship among (D1), (D2), (D3), (D4). Specifically: which of these conditions are equivalent for an arbitrary complex manifold X, and which strict implications hold between non-equivalent ones? Provide either proofs of all equivalences or counterexamples distinguishing the inequivalent notions.

If B ◦ L∞ has property (I), does it already follow that the B-LRP is not satisfied, even without assuming that B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible? In other words, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on B ◦ L∞ be removed from this implication?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Work in the category of Banach spaces and bounded linear operators. For Banach spaces $X,Y$, let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the Banach space of bounded linear operators $X\to Y$, and let $\mathcal{F}(X,Y)$ denote the finite-rank operators. A Banach (operator) ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ assigns to each pair $(X,Y)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ containing $\mathcal{F}(X,Y)$, equipped with a norm $\mathbf{B}$ such that $(\mathfrak{B}(X,Y),\mathbf{B})$ is a Banach space, $\mathbf{B}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\,\|y\|$, and the two-sided ideal property holds with respect to bounded operators. The adjoint ideal is $(\mathfrak{B}^*,\mathbf{B}^*)$, and $\mathfrak{B}$ is called maximal if it coincides isometrically with its bidual ideal in the sense of Pietsch. Let $\mathcal{L}_2$ denote the ideal of operators factoring through a Hilbert space (the $\gamma_2$-ideal), and $\mathcal{L}_\infty$ the maximal Banach ideal of $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-factorable operators. The composition ideal $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ is the Banach ideal whose component on $(X,Y)$ consists of operators that factor as $T=B\circ S$ with $S\in\mathcal{L}_\infty(X,Z)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{B}(Z,Y)$ for some Banach space $Z$, equipped with the natural infimum norm.

Recall that a Banach space $X$ has cotype $2$ if there exists $C>0$ such that $\big(\sum_i \|x_i\|^2\big)^{1/2}\le C\,\big(\mathbb{E}\|\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_i\|^2\big)^{1/2}$ for all finite families $(x_i)$ in $X$, where $(\varepsilon_i)$ are independent Rademacher variables. A Banach ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is right-accessible if for every finite-rank operator $L\in\mathcal{F}(M,Y)$ from a finite-dimensional space $M$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional space $N$, an operator $A\in\mathcal{L}(M,N)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{A}(N,Y)$ with $L=B\circ A$ and $\|A\|\,\mathbf{A}(B)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,\mathbf{A}(L)$. The ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to have property (I) if for all Banach spaces $X,Y$ the natural inclusion $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{A}^{**}(X,Y)$ is an isometric embedding into the maximal hull. The Banach ideal $\mathfrak{B}$ is said to satisfy the $\mathfrak{B}$-Limit Order Right Property ($\mathfrak{B}$-LRP) if a certain right-sided factorization/limit-order condition holds (the precise definition being the standard one used in the geometry of maximal Banach ideals).

Problem. Let $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be Banach spaces such that $X_0'$ and $Y_0$ are of cotype $2$ and $\mathfrak{B}^*(X_0,Y_0)\not\subseteq \mathcal{L}_2(X_0,Y_0)$. Suppose that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ has property (I). Does it follow that the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP fails, without assuming that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ is right-accessible? Equivalently, can the hypothesis of right-accessibility of $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ be removed from the known implication that, under the above hypotheses together with right-accessibility of $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$, the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP is not satisfied?
status_search_result: No follow-up resolution was located. The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on the geometry of operator ideals, and no subsequent published work could be verified to remove the right-accessibility hypothesis. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

context_brief: Bounding graph volume from image volume and differential lower bounds
original_question: Fix a compact complex manifold X, an integer k, a constant R > 0, and a constant C_1. Let J_R be the class of meromorphic maps f: Delta^k -> X such that the norm of the differential satisfies ||Df|| > R everywhere and the volume of the image f(Delta^k) is at most C_1. Prove that there is a constant C_2 = C_2(X, R, C_1) such that the volume of the graph Gamma_f is at most C_2 for every f in J_R.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold and fix an integer $k \geq 1$, a real number $R > 0$, and a constant $C_1 > 0$. Let $\Delta^k \subset \mathbb{C}^k$ denote the unit polydisk. Consider the class $\mathcal{J}_R$ of meromorphic mappings $f : \Delta^k \to X$ such that:

(a) at every point where $f$ is holomorphic, the operator norm of the differential satisfies $\|Df\| > R$;

(b) the volume of the image satisfies $\mathrm{Vol}(f(\Delta^k)) \leq C_1$,

where volumes are computed with respect to a fixed Hermitian metric on $X$ (and the standard Euclidean metric on $\Delta^k$ where applicable), and $f(\Delta^k)$ is counted with multiplicities as an analytic set.

For $f \in \mathcal{J}_R$, let $\Gamma_f \subset \Delta^k \times X$ denote the graph of $f$ (i.e., the closure of the graph of $f$ over its domain of holomorphy, which is an analytic subset of $\Delta^k \times X$).

Prove that there exists a constant $C_2 = C_2(X, R, C_1)$, depending only on $X$, $R$, and $C_1$, such that
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\Gamma_f) \leq C_2 \quad \text{for every } f \in \mathcal{J}_R.$$
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a specific resolution (proof or counterexample) of the stated graph-volume bound under the differential lower bound and image-volume hypotheses. Related work on extension and volume estimates for meromorphic mappings exists, but no source clearly confirming or refuting this exact statement was found.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line with initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x), where u_0 is almost periodic in x. McKean and Trubowitz proved that periodic initial data produce solutions that are almost periodic in time. Does the same conclusion hold for almost periodic initial data, and more fundamentally can one establish short-time existence and then understand the associated spectral theory of the Schrödinger operator H(t) = -d^2/dx^2 + u(x,t) for general almost periodic potentials well enough to analyze the KdV evolution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation
  u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t ∈ ℝ,
with initial condition u(x,0) = u_0(x), where u_0 : ℝ → ℝ is an almost periodic function (i.e., u_0 lies in the closure, in the uniform norm on ℝ, of the set of trigonometric polynomials Σ c_j e^{i ξ_j x}).

It is known (McKean–Trubowitz) that when u_0 is periodic, the resulting KdV solution exists globally and is almost periodic in time, with the spectrum of the Schrödinger operator H(t) = −d^2/dx^2 + u(·,t) being preserved under the flow.

Address the following for general almost periodic initial data u_0:

(a) Prove short-time existence of a classical solution u(x,t) of the above Cauchy problem in the class of functions that are almost periodic in x for each t in some interval (−T, T), T > 0.

(b) Develop the spectral theory of the family of Schrödinger operators H(t) = −d^2/dx^2 + u(·,t), acting on L^2(ℝ), for almost periodic potentials u(·,t), to a degree sufficient to track the KdV evolution (in particular, isospectrality of H(t)).

(c) Show that the resulting solution u(x,t) is almost periodic in t, thereby extending the McKean–Trubowitz periodic-in-time result from periodic to almost periodic initial data.
category_tag: KdV with almost periodic initial data
status_search_result: The problem (often called the Deift conjecture) has been settled in important cases but not in full generality. Damanik–Goldstein (2014) established short-time existence and uniqueness for quasi-periodic initial data with exponentially decaying Fourier coefficients, and global existence/uniqueness for small analytic quasi-periodic data with Diophantine frequency. Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic (Duke Math. J., 2018) proved almost periodicity in time of KdV solutions for a class of almost periodic initial data whose associated Schrödinger operators have absolutely continuous, not-too-thin spectrum, including all small analytic quasi-periodic data with Diophantine frequency. The full conjecture for general almost periodic initial data remains open.
