context_brief: Finite-volume extension from a punctured polydisk
original_question: Let f: Delta^*_k -> X be a meromorphic map from a punctured k-dimensional polydisk into a compact complex space X. If the volume of f(Delta^*_k) is finite, prove that f extends meromorphically across the puncture to the origin.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$ denote the open unit disk and let $\Delta_*^k = (\Delta \setminus \{0\}) \times \Delta^{k-1}$ denote the $k$-dimensional polydisk punctured along the divisor $\{z_1 = 0\}$ (more generally, any standard punctured polydisk obtained by removing a coordinate hypersurface, or the polydisk with the origin removed). Let $X$ be a compact complex space and let 
$$f : \Delta_*^k \longrightarrow X$$
be a meromorphic mapping. Recall that the volume of $f$ is defined, with respect to a fixed Hermitian metric $\omega_X$ on $X$, by 
$$\mathrm{Vol}\, f(\Delta_*^k) \;=\; \int_{\Delta_*^k} f^*\omega_X^{\,n},$$
where $n = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$ (or, more invariantly, the mass of the graph of $f$ in $\Delta_*^k \times X$ with respect to a product Hermitian metric).

Assume that $\mathrm{Vol}\, f(\Delta_*^k) < \infty$. Prove that $f$ extends to a meromorphic mapping $\tilde f : \Delta^k \to X$ across the puncture; that is, the indeterminacy/extension across the missing coordinate locus (in particular across $0 \in \Delta^k$) can be realized so that the graph of $f$ has analytic closure in $\Delta^k \times X$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not produce a definitive resolution of this finite-volume meromorphic extension problem from a punctured polydisk into an arbitrary compact complex space. Related extension theorems by Ivashkovich and others are known in the Kähler or disk-convex setting, and partial results exist for special targets, but no source clearly establishes (or refutes) the general statement, so its status is treated as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For random matrix ensembles with symmetry classes β=1 and β=4, prove bulk and edge universality for general potentials of the form Q(x)=N V(x), especially when the associated equilibrium measure is supported on several disjoint intervals, rather than only for the already understood polynomial-potential cases with one-cut support. More broadly, determine whether the newer methods developed for unitary ensembles can be adapted to these orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, and resolve the long-standing conjecture that Wigner matrices also exhibit bulk universality.
self_contained_problem:
Consider invariant random matrix ensembles on the spaces of N×N real symmetric (β=1), complex Hermitian (β=2), or quaternion self-dual (β=4) matrices, with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

  ∏_{i<j} |x_i − x_j|^β · exp(−∑_{k=1}^N Q(x_k)),

where Q(x) = N V(x) and V : ℝ → ℝ is a sufficiently regular (e.g. real-analytic or polynomial) confining potential. Let μ_V denote the associated equilibrium measure, i.e. the unique minimizer of

  I[μ] = ∫∫ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x) dμ(x)

over Borel probability measures on ℝ. Assume the support of μ_V consists of finitely many disjoint intervals (the multi-cut regime).

(a) For β = 1 and β = 4, prove bulk universality: after appropriate rescaling around any point in the interior of the support of μ_V, the local k-point correlation functions of the eigenvalues converge, as N → ∞, to the universal limits given by the standard β=1 and β=4 sine kernels (respectively the Pfaffian sine kernels of the GOE and GSE).

(b) For β = 1 and β = 4, prove edge universality: after appropriate rescaling around any soft edge of the support of μ_V, the local correlation functions converge to the universal β=1 and β=4 Airy (Pfaffian Airy) kernels.

(c) Determine whether the techniques developed for unitary (β=2) ensembles—in particular Riemann–Hilbert methods—can be adapted so as to establish (a) and (b) in this multi-cut, general-potential setting.

(d) (Wigner bulk universality.) Let H = (H_{ij}) be an N×N real symmetric or Hermitian Wigner matrix whose entries above the diagonal are i.i.d. (with appropriate symmetry) random variables of mean zero, variance 1/N, and suitable moment conditions. Prove that the bulk local eigenvalue statistics of H, in the limit N → ∞, coincide with those of the GOE (resp. GUE).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. Wigner bulk universality (part d) has been resolved by Erdős–Schlein–Yau and independently Tao–Vu (around 2010–2012). For invariant β=1, 4 ensembles, bulk and edge universality have been established for one-cut regular potentials of class C⁴ or analytic (Shcherbina; Bourgade–Erdős–Yau; Krishnapur–Rider–Virág; Deift–Gioev and others), and Laguerre-type analogues are known. The full multi-cut case for general (non-polynomial) potentials in β=1, 4 is partially understood but not completely resolved in the generality stated.

context_brief: Persistence of global spherical shells under deformation
original_question: Let X = {X_t} be a deformation of compact complex surfaces. If every nearby fiber X_t with t != 0 contains a global spherical shell, must the central fiber X_0 also contain a global spherical shell?
self_contained_problem:
A global spherical shell (GSS) in a compact complex surface $S$ is the image of a holomorphic embedding $\varphi : U \to S$ of an open neighborhood $U \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ of the standard sphere $S^3 = \{ z \in \mathbb{C}^2 : |z| = 1 \}$ such that $\varphi(S^3)$ does not disconnect $S$.

Let $\pi : \mathcal{X} \to \Delta$ be a deformation of compact complex surfaces over the unit disk $\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$, i.e. a proper smooth holomorphic submersion whose fibers $X_t = \pi^{-1}(t)$ are compact complex surfaces. Assume that for every $t \in \Delta \setminus \{0\}$, the fiber $X_t$ contains a global spherical shell.

Question: Must the central fiber $X_0$ also contain a global spherical shell?
category_tag: Complex surfaces and global spherical shells
status_search_result: The broader global spherical shell (GSS) conjecture for minimal class VII surfaces with positive second Betti number remained unresolved as of 2024 according to standard references on the Enriques–Kodaira classification. No source was found establishing that the property of containing a GSS is closed under deformation in general, so the specific persistence question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Extend the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems with oscillatory data of the form e^{i n φ(z)} r(z) as n→∞ to the case where the phase function φ is not analytic but has only finite smoothness. The goal is to recover asymptotic control of the associated equilibrium measure and contour deformations without the analyticity assumption that current theory relies on.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{C}$ be an oriented contour and consider a family of $2\times 2$ matrix-valued Riemann–Hilbert problems indexed by $n\in\mathbb{N}$: find $M_n:\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma\to GL_2(\mathbb{C})$ such that
\[ M_{n,+}(z) = M_{n,-}(z)\,J_n(z),\quad z\in\Sigma,\qquad M_n(z)\to I\ \text{as}\ z\to\infty, \]
where the jump matrix has the oscillatory form
\[ J_n(z) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \overline{r(z)}\,e^{-in\varphi(z)} \\ r(z)\,e^{in\varphi(z)} & 1+|r(z)|^2 \end{pmatrix} \]
(or a closely related factorized form), with reflection coefficient $r$ and real-valued phase $\varphi$.

The Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method provides, as $n\to\infty$, asymptotics for $M_n$ via:
(i) the construction of a $g$-function and an associated equilibrium measure determining the relevant signature regions of $\operatorname{Re}(i\varphi)$;
(ii) lensing/contour deformations of $\Sigma$ into steepest-descent contours where the off-diagonal entries decay; and
(iii) local parametrices at stationary/critical points matched to a global parametrix.

All standard implementations of this scheme assume that $\varphi$ is real-analytic in a neighborhood of $\Sigma$, so that the deformations and analytic continuations in (ii) are available.

Problem. Develop a version of the nonlinear steepest descent method that yields the same asymptotic control of $M_n$ — including a workable analogue of the equilibrium measure, the $g$-function transformations, the contour deformations, and the local parametrix construction — under the weaker hypothesis that the phase $\varphi$ has only a finite number of derivatives (i.e. $\varphi\in C^k$ for some finite $k$, with $r$ likewise of finite smoothness) rather than being analytic. In particular, identify the minimal smoothness on $\varphi$ and $r$ under which leading-order (and subleading) large-$n$ asymptotics for $M_n$ can be rigorously established.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on relaxing the analyticity hypothesis. Varzugin extended Deift–Zhou to a restricted class of non-analytic phases, and the $\bar\partial$-steepest descent method (McLaughlin–Miller and later authors) handles substantially broader non-analytic settings by replacing analytic continuation with $\bar\partial$-extensions. However, sharp characterizations of the minimal finite smoothness required for full asymptotic control remain incomplete, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Let F be a family of holomorphic or meromorphic maps from the unit polydisk Delta^(n+1) to a compact Kähler manifold X, or more generally to a target X in the class G_1. If F is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure H^1_n(r), must F be equicontinuous on the whole polydisk Delta^(n+1)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta\subset\mathbb{C}$ denote the open unit disk, and for an integer $n\ge 1$ let $\Delta^{n+1}$ denote the unit polydisk in $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$. For $0<r<1$, define the Hartogs figure
$$H^{1}_{n}(r)=\{(z,w)\in\Delta\times\Delta^{n}:\ |z|>1-r\}\;\cup\;\{(z,w)\in\Delta\times\Delta^{n}:\ \|w\|<r\}.$$
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold, or more generally a complex manifold belonging to the class $\mathcal{G}_{1}$ (the class of compact complex manifolds for which meromorphic maps from a Hartogs figure into $X$ extend meromorphically across the polydisk). Equip $X$ with a fixed Hermitian distance $d_X$, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of holomorphic (respectively meromorphic) mappings from $\Delta^{n+1}$ to $X$. The family $\mathcal{F}$ is said to be equicontinuous on a subset $U\subset\Delta^{n+1}$ if, with respect to a suitable distance on the graph space (or, in the meromorphic case, the Hausdorff distance on graphs), for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that $d_X(f(p),f(q))<\varepsilon$ for all $f\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $p,q\in U$ with $|p-q|<\delta$.

Question: If $\mathcal{F}$ is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure $H^{1}_{n}(r)$, must $\mathcal{F}$ be equicontinuous on the entire polydisk $\Delta^{n+1}$?
status_search_result: A web search for follow-up work on this equicontinuity-extension question (extending equicontinuity of families of holomorphic/meromorphic maps from a Hartogs figure to the full polydisk, in the setting of compact Kähler manifolds or the class $\mathcal{G}_1$) did not turn up an explicit resolution. Related Hartogs-type extension theorems for individual meromorphic maps are well known, but the family/equicontinuity version posed here was not found to be answered in the located sources.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory for the six Painlevé equations, analogous in spirit to the Bateman project or Abramowitz-Stegun for classical special functions. In particular, build dependable software and accompanying asymptotic and algebraic infrastructure for computing Painlevé transcendents, such as determining features like the pole locations in the complex plane for the Painlevé II solution asymptotic to the Airy function as x→+∞.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory of the six Painlevé equations P_I, P_II, P_III, P_IV, P_V, P_VI, comparable in scope and dependability to classical handbooks of special functions (such as the Bateman manuscript project or the Abramowitz–Stegun Handbook). The theory should provide:

1. A unified algebraic and analytic infrastructure (Hamiltonian forms, Bäcklund transformations, isomonodromic representations, connection formulas, Riemann–Hilbert problems, classical and rational solutions, parameter symmetries) sufficient to characterize and tabulate the Painlevé transcendents.
2. Reliable asymptotic expansions of solutions in all directions of the complex plane, including the connection problem relating asymptotic data at different critical points.
3. Robust numerical software that, given initial/asymptotic data identifying a particular Painlevé transcendent, computes its values throughout the complex plane to controlled accuracy and locates its singularities.

As a concrete benchmark within this program, consider the Hastings–McLeod-type setting for the second Painlevé equation
   u''(x) = 2 u(x)^3 + x u(x),
and let u(x) be the unique real solution satisfying u(x) ~ Ai(x) as x → +∞, where Ai is the Airy function. Determine, by means of the developed theory and software, the locations in the complex x-plane of the poles of this solution u(x) (each of which is a simple pole with residue ±1), including their distribution and asymptotic pattern.
status_search_result: The Painlevé Project was launched (NIST e-site, DLMF Chapter 32) and substantial progress has been made: numerical Riemann–Hilbert based algorithms (Olver, Bornemann, Trogdon) compute Painlevé transcendents reliably in the complex plane, and pole distributions for the Hastings–McLeod and tronquée solutions of P_II have been studied (Fornberg–Weideman, Costin–Huang–Tanveer, Bertola–Bothner). However, a complete, comprehensive Bateman/Abramowitz–Stegun-style infrastructure with universally validated software for all six Painlevé equations is still an ongoing community effort rather than a finished project.

original_question: For the Lie superalgebra osp(1|2), can one complete the final identification over the two independent parameters c0 + d0^2 and d0^2 and thereby derive a genuine super-triangle sum rule, expressed with the supertriangle Delta_S and parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, that plays the same role for osp(1|2) that the ordinary triangle sum rule plays for su(2) and su_q(2)?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let osp(1|2) denote the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra of rank one, with finite-dimensional irreducible representations labeled by a non-negative (half-)integer spin J of definite grade, having superdimension related to the usual su(2) branching osp(1|2) ⊃ su(2). For three such irreps with spins j1, j2, j3, define the supertriangle factor Δ_S(j1, j2, j3) (the osp(1|2) analogue of the triangle factor Δ(j1, j2, j3) of su(2)) and the parity-independent super 6-j symbol {j1 j2 j3 ; j4 j5 j6}^S, constructed from the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients of osp(1|2) by symmetrizing over the Z_2-grading so as to be insensitive to parity choices.

Recall that for su(2) (and likewise for the quantum deformation su_q(2)) the 6-j symbols satisfy a triangle sum rule of the form
   Σ_x (2x+1) (-1)^{2(a+b+x)} {a b x ; a b c} = (2a+1)(2b+1) Δ(a,b,c)·(triangle factor),
i.e. a closed identity in which the only spin-dependent quantity surviving the sum is the triangle Δ(a,b,c).

Problem. Working with the intrinsic-operator (tensor-operator) techniques for osp(1|2), reduce the candidate super-triangle sum rule for the parity-independent 6-j^S symbols to an identification problem in two independent parameters
   u = c0 + d0^2,    v = d0^2,

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Let M be a p×n data matrix with p,n→∞ and p/n→γ∈(0,∞), and let S=(1/n) M̂ M̂^T be the centered sample covariance matrix whose ordered eigenvalues are l_1≥⋯≥l_p. For real Gaussian spiked covariance models, where the population covariance has eigenvalues η_1≥⋯≥η_k>η_{k+1}=⋯=η_p=1, determine the asymptotic distributions of the leading sample eigenvalues and describe the phase transitions analogous to the complex case, despite the absence of a real analogue of the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber formula.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a real Gaussian spiked covariance model in the following setting. For each pair $(p,n)$ with $p,n\to\infty$ and $p/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, let $X$ be a $p\times n$ matrix whose columns are i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$, where the population covariance $\Sigma$ has ordered eigenvalues
$$\eta_1\ge\eta_2\ge\cdots\ge\eta_k>\eta_{k+1}=\cdots=\eta_p=1$$
for some fixed $k\ge 1$ and fixed spike values $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_k$. Let $\hat X$ denote the column-centered version of $X$ and define the sample covariance matrix
$$S=\tfrac{1}{n}\hat X\hat X^{T},$$
with ordered eigenvalues $\ell_1\ge\ell_2\ge\cdots\ge\ell_p$.

Determine, for each fixed $i\le k$, the limiting distribution (after suitable centering and scaling) of the leading sample eigenvalue $\ell_i$ as $p,n\to\infty$ with $p/n\to\gamma$. In particular, identify the critical threshold $\eta_c(\gamma)$ governing the phase transition between the regime in which $\ell_i$ converges to the bulk edge with Tracy–Widom-type fluctuations and the regime in which $\ell_i$ separates from the bulk with Gaussian-type fluctuations, and describe the limiting laws on each side of the transition. The problem is to obtain such a complete real-case analogue of the known results for the complex Gaussian spiked model, despite the lack of a real analogue of the Harish-Chandra–Itzykson–Zuber integral formula.
status_search_result: The problem of asymptotic distributions and phase transitions for the leading eigenvalues of real Gaussian spiked sample covariance matrices has been substantially resolved in subsequent work. Bai–Yao, Paul, and Benaych-Georges–Nadakuditi established Gaussian fluctuations for supercritical spikes, while Bloemendal–Virág ("Limits of spiked random matrices I/II") and Mo determined Tracy–Widom-type laws at and below the BBP threshold $1+\sqrt{\gamma}$ in the real case, providing real analogues of the complex results.

original_question: Let P_pi(lambda, kappa) denote the symmetric polynomials that appear in the closure relation for osp(1|2) iterated tensor operators, expanded in the binomial basis (c0 + d0^2)^([pi]-m) (d0^2)^m with coefficients x^pi_m(lambda, kappa). Consider the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ and its iterated tensor operators acting on irreducible representations. paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For general β-ensembles, equivalently log gases at inverse temperature β>0, use the stochastic Schrödinger operator H_β = d^2/dx^2 - x - √(2/β) dB(x)/dx on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0 to obtain structural information about the edge statistics of the ensemble. In particular, derive the Tracy-Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue in the case β=2 directly from H_β.
self_contained_problem:
For each inverse temperature parameter β>0, consider the log-gas (general β-ensemble) on the real line with joint density proportional to ∏_{i<j}|x_i−x_j|^β exp(−(β/4)∑_i x_i^2), and let λ_1(N;β) denote the largest particle in the N-particle ensemble (suitably centered and rescaled at the soft edge by 2√N + N^{−1/6}·).

Define the stochastic Airy (Schrödinger) operator
   H_β = −d^2/dx^2 + x + (2/√β) dB(x)/dx,
acting on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0, where dB/dx is standard one-dimensional white noise. Let Λ_1(β) ≤ Λ_2(β) ≤ … denote the (almost surely well-defined, discrete, simple) spectrum of H_β, and define the Tracy–Widom_β distribution by TW_β(t) = P(−Λ_1(β) ≤ t).

(a) Use the operator H_β to extract structural information about the edge statistics of the β-ensemble; in particular, show that the rescaled top eigenvalue of the β-ensemble converges in distribution to −Λ_1(β).

(b) In the case β=2, derive the classical Tracy–Widom GUE formula
   F_2(t) = exp(−∫_t^∞ (s−t) q(s)^2 ds),
where q solves the Painlevé II equation q''(s) = s q(s) + 2 q(s)^3 with q(s) ~ Ai(s) as s→∞, directly from the stochastic operator H_2 (rather than via determinantal/Hermitian-matrix kernel techniques).
status_search_result: Ramírez–Rider–Virág (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 2011) proved that the rescaled top eigenvalues of general β-ensembles converge to the low eigenvalues of the stochastic Airy operator H_β, and characterized the resulting Tracy–Widom_β laws via a one-dimensional diffusion (explosion probability). This resolves part (a) and gives a stochastic-operator characterization of TW_β for all β>0. However, a direct derivation of the classical Fredholm-determinant / Painlevé II Tracy–Widom formula F_2 specifically from H_2 (without invoking determinantal/Hermite kernel methods) does not appear to be established; subsequent works (e.g., right-tail asymptotics by Ramírez–Rider–Virág and tail analyses) give partial information but not the full explicit β=2 formula directly from H_β. The problem is therefore partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop theoretical and numerical methods that can determine where, and at what rate, the eigenvalues of important non-self-adjoint operators accumulate in the complex plane. A central example is the AKNS operator arising in the semiclassical focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation, where the spectrum off the real axis is discrete but the numerical range is open and the relevant spectral computation is unstable beyond all algebraic orders in the semiclassical parameter h.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the semiclassical regime
$$ i h\, \partial_t \psi + \tfrac{h^2}{2}\, \partial_x^2 \psi + |\psi|^2 \psi = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t\ge 0, $$
with small parameter $h>0$ and initial data $\psi(x,0)=A(x)\exp\!\big(\tfrac{i}{h} S(x)\big)$ for smooth real-valued functions $A,S$ with $A$ rapidly decaying. The associated AKNS (Zakharov–Shabat) scattering operator is the non-self-adjoint first-order system
$$ \mathcal{L}_h \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix} = \lambda \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal{L}_h := \begin{pmatrix} -i h\,\partial_x & i\, q(x) \\ i\,\overline{q(x)} & i h\,\partial_x \end{pmatrix}, $$
where $q(x) = A(x) e^{i S(x)/h}$. For generic such potentials the spectrum of $\mathcal{L}_h$ off the real axis consists of discrete eigenvalues $\{\lambda_j(h)\}\subset\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}$, while the numerical range of $\mathcal{L}_h$ is an open subset of the complex plane, and the standard numerical computation of these eigenvalues is unstable beyond all algebraic orders in $h$ (errors decay no faster than any power of $h$ but are dominated by exponentially small terms).

Develop theoretical and/or numerical methods to determine, in the limit $h\to 0^+$:

1. The asymptotic locus (curve, set, or measure) in $\mathbb{C}$ on which the eigenvalues $\lambda_j(h)$ of $\mathcal{L}_h$ accumulate, as a function of the data $(A,S)$.
2. The asymptotic rate (density) at which the eigenvalues populate this locus, including a quantitative description of the counting measure $\sum_j \delta_{\lambda_j(h)}$ as $h\to 0^+$.

The methods should be applicable to general (not necessarily analytic or exactly solvable) initial data $(A,S)$ and should overcome the instability of direct spectral computation for such non-self-adjoint operators.
status_search_result: The problem of locating and quantifying the accumulation of complex eigenvalues of the non-self-adjoint Zakharov–Shabat (AKNS) operator in the semiclassical focusing NLS limit remains an active area of research. Partial results exist for special classes of analytic potentials (e.g. WKB / Bohr–Sommerfeld-type quantization yielding accumulation along Stokes curves and "Y-shaped" sets, with $O(1/h)$ density), via works of Bronski, Klaus–Shaw, Fujiié–Kamvissis and others, but a general theory for arbitrary smooth data and stable numerical algorithms beyond all algebraic orders in $h$ has not been established.

original_question: If Q_pi(lambda; kappa) denotes the polynomial family arising from the low-rank closure relations and P_pi(lambda, kappa) denotes the family from the high-rank closure relations, does the identity Q_pi(lambda; kappa) = P_pi(lambda, kappa - lambda + pi) hold for every admissible lambda, kappa, and pi?

$$Q_\pi(\lambda;\kappa) \;=\; P_\pi(\lambda,\;\kappa-\lambda+\pi).$$

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Determine the long-time behavior of integrable systems when the initial data are non-generic and the associated Lax operator has singular spectral features not covered by the standard generic theory. In particular, for focusing nonlinear Schrödinger evolution, understand how spectra that accumulate on the real line at essentially arbitrary rates affect long-time asymptotics, and similarly clarify the situation for higher-order self-adjoint Lax operators such as those for the Boussinesq equation.
self_contained_problem:
Consider integrable nonlinear evolution equations whose Cauchy problems are solved via inverse scattering using a Lax pair, focusing on two cases.

(a) Focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Let q(x,t) satisfy
   i q_t + q_{xx} + 2|q|^2 q = 0,  x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
with initial data q(x,0) = q_0(x) decaying as |x| → ∞. The associated Lax operator is the Zakharov–Shabat operator
   L = i σ_3 ∂_x + ( 0, q_0(x); -\bar q_0(x), 0 ).
For "generic" initial data, the discrete spectrum of L consists of finitely many simple eigenvalues lying off the real axis, and the reflection coefficient is smooth on ℝ; in this case the long-time asymptotics of q(x,t) are known via nonlinear steepest descent. Consider instead non-generic initial data for which the spectrum exhibits singular features, in particular sequences of (possibly higher-order) eigenvalues accumulating on the real axis at arbitrary prescribed rates, and/or spectral singularities (poles of the scattering data on ℝ). Determine, as t → ∞, the leading-order asymptotic behavior of q(x,t) along all rays x/t = ξ ∈ ℝ in this non-generic regime, and identify how the rate of accumulation of eigenvalues on ℝ enters the asymptotic formulas and error terms.

(b) Boussinesq equation. Let u(x,t) satisfy the (good) Boussinesq equation
   u_{tt} = u_{xx} + (u^2)_{xx} + u_{xxxx},  x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
with general decaying initial data (u(x,0), u_t(x,0)). The associated Lax operator is a third-order self-adjoint differential operator
   L = ∂_x^3 + ∂_x q(x,t) + q(x,t) ∂_x + p(x,t),
whose spectral theory is significantly more involved than that of second-order operators, with continuous spectrum on ℝ and possible embedded singularities. Determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) for general (not merely Schwartz-class or generic) initial data.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Using ∂̄-steepest descent, long-time asymptotics for focusing NLS have been extended to non-generic initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces, including the presence of high-order discrete spectrum (e.g., arXiv:2104.07301). Long-time asymptotics for the Boussinesq equation with Schwartz-class data have been obtained via nonlinear steepest descent methods. However, the fully general non-generic regime—covering eigenvalue sequences accumulating on the real axis at arbitrary rates, general spectral singularities for NLS, and general (non-Schwartz) initial data for Boussinesq—has not been completely resolved, so the problem remains only partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Construct a microscopic mathematical model for parked-car spacing statistics on long streets that explains why empirical data exhibit random-matrix behavior and why two-way streets appear to show GUE statistics whereas left-side parking on one-way streets appears to show GOE statistics. The goal is an analogue, for parking, of the microscopic random-matrix explanation previously developed for the Cuernavaca bus problem.
self_contained_problem:
Empirical observations of parked-car positions along long urban streets indicate that, after appropriate normalization, the gaps between consecutive parked cars exhibit spacing statistics characteristic of random matrix ensembles: on two-way streets the empirical spacing distribution matches that of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE), while for left-side parking on one-way streets it matches that of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE).

Recall that for an N×N Hermitian matrix drawn from the GUE (respectively, real symmetric from the GOE), with eigenvalues λ_1 ≤ … ≤ λ_N rescaled so that the mean nearest-neighbor spacing in the bulk equals 1, the limiting nearest-neighbor spacing distribution p_β(s) (β=2 for GUE, β=1 for GOE) is well-approximated by the Wigner surmise p_β(s) = a_β s^β exp(−b_β s^2) with constants a_β, b_β fixed by normalization.

Recall also the Cuernavaca bus problem: for a bus line in Cuernavaca, Mexico, the spacings between consecutive buses passing a fixed checkpoint were observed to follow GUE statistics, and a microscopic stochastic model (in which independent drivers adjust their speeds to avoid being too close to the bus ahead, leading via a hard-core interaction to a determinantal point process with the sine-kernel correlations of GUE) was constructed which provably reproduces these statistics in an appropriate scaling limit.

Problem. Construct an analogous microscopic stochastic model for the positions of parked cars along a long street, based on plausible local rules describing how drivers choose parking spots given the positions of already-parked cars, with the following properties:

(a) The model is defined for both a "two-way street" variant and a "one-way street, left-side parking" variant, the only difference being the local rules / symmetry constraints reflecting the directional structure of the street.

(b) In an appropriate thermodynamic / large-street scaling limit, the rescaled point process of parked-car positions converges to a translation-invariant point process on ℝ whose nearest-neighbor spacing distribution coincides with the bulk GUE spacing distribution p_2(s) in the two-way case and with the bulk GOE spacing distribution p_1(s) in the one-way left-side case.

(c) The mechanism producing the change from β=2 to β=1 statistics is identified explicitly in terms of the symmetry of the underlying interaction (e.g. a time-reversal or reflection symmetry that is present in the one-way left-side rules but broken in the two-way rules).

Either exhibit such a model with proofs of the convergence claims in (b)–(c), or prove that no model in a specified natural class can reproduce both ensembles by symmetry breaking alone.

The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Can one explicitly compute, program, and publish tables of parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols for low spins (for example up to spin 20) from the general formulas cited by the paper, so that low-spin calculations can test candidate triangle-sum-rule identities and reveal patterns among the expansion coefficients x?
self_contained_problem:
In the Racah–Wigner calculus for the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra osp(1|2), one can define parity-independent 6-j symbols, denoted 6-j^S, that generalize the usual SU(2) (so(3)) 6-j symbols and satisfy super-analogues of the Racah triangular and orthogonality identities. General closed-form expressions for these 6-j^S symbols (as finite sums analogous to Racah's formula) are known.

The task is the following:

(a) Using such general formulas, compute explicitly the numerical values of all parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols
   { j1 j2 j3 ; j4 j5 j6 }^S
in which every entry j_i runs over the half-integer/integer spin values 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, …, up to some fixed bound J_max (for example J_max = 20), subject to the appropriate super-triangle conditions.

(b) Produce machine-readable tables of these values, in either exact closed form (rational multiples of square roots of rationals) or arbitrary-precision numerical form.

(c) Use these tables to test candidate "triangle-sum-rule" identities for 6-j^S symbols — i.e., linear or quadratic relations summed over one or more spins compatible with fixed triangles — and to identify, by inspection of the resulting data, structural patterns among the expansion coefficients x appearing in such conjectured identities.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Find a probabilistic operation X on an i.i.d. sequence (a_1,a_2,...) that plays a role for random-matrix statistics analogous to summation in the classical central limit theorem: after applying X to the first n inputs, the resulting random variables should converge, as n→∞, to the Gaudin distribution or to a Tracy-Widom distribution. In other words, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms.
self_contained_problem:
Background. In classical probability, the central limit theorem identifies summation as the canonical probabilistic operation that, applied to an i.i.d. sequence with finite variance, produces (after centering and scaling) Gaussian limits in the large-n limit. In random matrix theory, the Gaudin distribution governs spacings between consecutive eigenvalues in the bulk of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (or, more generally, of large Hermitian random matrices), and the Tracy–Widom distributions F_1, F_2, F_4 govern the fluctuations of the largest eigenvalue of GOE/GUE/GSE random matrices. Both Gaudin and Tracy–Widom limits are known to be universal: they arise in a wide variety of models (random matrices, longest increasing subsequences of random permutations, last-passage percolation, growth processes, etc.).

Problem. Exhibit a probabilistic operation X — a measurable map taking an i.i.d. sequence (a_1, a_2, …) of real-valued random variables (under some natural moment hypothesis, e.g. finite variance or finite fourth moment) and the integer n to a random variable X_n(a_1, …, a_n), or to a finite collection of such variables — with the following property: for every law of a_1 in the prescribed class, after suitable centering and scaling the random variables X_n(a_1, …, a_n) converge in distribution as n → ∞ to either the Gaudin spacing distribution or one of the Tracy–Widom distributions F_1, F_2, F_4. The operation X should be a genuine analogue of summation: it must be defined directly in probabilistic/combinatorial terms (without reference to a specific underlying random matrix model) and must produce the prescribed random-matrix limit universally over the class of input distributions. In other words, give a purely probabilistic characterization of random-matrix universality of Gaudin/Tracy–Widom type, parallel to the way summation characterizes Gaussian universality in the classical CLT.
status_search_result: The full problem of identifying a universal probabilistic operation X analogous to summation that produces Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits from arbitrary i.i.d. inputs is generally regarded as open. Important partial progress has been made: Baik–Suidan (2005) and Bodineau–Martin (2005) independently established GUE/Tracy–Widom universality for directed last-passage site percolation in thin rectangles under finite-moment assumptions, and a substantial subsequent literature (KPZ universality, invariance principles for last-passage percolation, etc.) has extended such results to wider classes. However, no fully general probabilistic operation X analogous to summation has been singled out that yields Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits universally on all i.i.d. inputs.

original_question: The paper restricts the parameters c0 and d0 to be real numbers throughout the osp(1|2) analysis. If one allows c0 and/or d0 to take imaginary values instead, does the obstruction to completing the osp(1|2) triangle-sum-rule derivation change, and can such an extension lead to a valid final solution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra osp(1|2) and its 6-j symbols. In the intrinsic-operator approach to deriving a super-triangle sum rule generalizing the classical su(2) triangle sum rule, one introduces two real parameters c₀ and d₀ that arise during the identification of expansion coefficients (typically through binomial expressions of the form (c₀ + d₀²)^{Ω−m}(d₀²)^m, where Ω and m are non-negative integers indexing the expansion). Under the assumption that c₀, d₀ ∈ ℝ, the identification of coefficients in the candidate super-triangle sum rule reaches an impasse and no closed-form solution is obtained.

Question: If the restriction c₀, d₀ ∈ ℝ is relaxed to allow c₀ and/or d₀ to be purely imaginary (or, more generally, complex), does the obstruction to completing the derivation of the osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule disappear? Specifically, does there exist an admissible choice of c₀, d₀ ∈ ℂ (with at least one of them non-real) for which the identification of all expansion coefficients can be carried out consistently, yielding a valid closed-form super-triangle sum rule for osp(1|2) 6-j symbols?
status_search_result: No follow-up work was located that addresses the proposed extension of c₀ and d₀ to imaginary or complex values in the osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule derivation. The original treatment leaves this as a speculative direction, and no resolution could be verified.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Given a tridiagonal TE1 random matrix, equivalently Toda lattice initial data whose diagonal entries are independent Gaussians and whose off-diagonal entries have the corresponding χ-distributions, determine the average time required for the Toda flow to diagonalize the matrix to a prescribed accuracy ε. Equivalently, estimate the average time until the interacting Toda particles become asymptotically free, which in the algorithmic formulation can be taken as the time when the last off-diagonal entry b_{n-1}(t) drops below ε.
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let T = (T_{ij}) be a random real symmetric tridiagonal n×n matrix sampled from the following ensemble (the tridiagonal β=1 / TE1 ensemble): the diagonal entries T_{ii} (1 ≤ i ≤ n) are independent Gaussian random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and the off-diagonal entries b_i := T_{i,i+1} = T_{i+1,i} (1 ≤ i ≤ n−1) are independent (and independent of the diagonal) with b_i distributed as (1/√2) χ_{n−i}, where χ_k denotes the chi distribution with k degrees of freedom.

Let X(t) be the solution of the Toda lattice flow with initial condition X(0) = T, i.e. X(t) is the symmetric tridiagonal n×n matrix evolving according to
   dX/dt = [B(X), X],
where B(X) is the skew-symmetric matrix obtained from X by taking its strictly lower-triangular part minus its strictly upper-triangular part. Let b_i(t) denote the (i, i+1) entry of X(t).

For ε > 0 (the prescribed accuracy), define the halting time
   τ_n(ε) := inf{ t ≥ 0 : b_{n−1}(t) < ε }.

Determine the asymptotic behavior, as n → ∞ (and as a function of ε), of the expected halting time E[τ_n(ε)]. Equivalently, determine the average time required for the Toda flow with TE1 initial data to drive its last off-diagonal entry below the threshold ε, i.e. for the interacting Toda particles to become asymptotically free to within accuracy ε.
status_search_result: Empirical and theoretical work by Pfrang–Deift–Menon and Deift–Trogdon established universality for the (suitably normalized) deflation/halting time of the Toda algorithm on Wigner-class random matrices, showing that the limiting distribution depends only on the algorithm and not on the underlying ensemble or matrix size. However, a full rigorous determination of the average halting time E[τ_n(ε)] as a function of n and ε for the TE1 ensemble is described in the literature as still far from resolved, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: For a non-commutative group G, determine the invariant ν(G), the minimal number of colors required to color G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic subset A that is symmetric in the group-theoretic sense A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. In particular, decide whether ν(F_2) is finite for the free group F_2 on two generators.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a group. A subset A ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that A = gA^{-1}g, where A^{-1} = {a^{-1} : a ∈ A}. For a positive integer r, an r-coloring of G is a map χ : G → {1, …, r}; a subset is monochromatic if χ is constant on it. Define the invariant

  ν(G) := min { r ∈ ℕ : there exists an r-coloring of G containing no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset },

with ν(G) := ∞ if no such r exists.

(a) For non-commutative groups G, determine ν(G).

(b) In particular, decide whether ν(F_2) is finite, where F_2 denotes the free group on two generators.
status_search_result: The problem, attributed to R. I. Grigorchuk, asks about the symmetric-coloring invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups, with the specific question of finiteness of ν(F_2). Status appears unresolved based on accessible sources.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop perturbation theory for infinite-dimensional integrable systems in settings where solitons are present and the perturbation no longer becomes asymptotically negligible. A central instance is the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an added perturbation term ε V(|u|)u, especially for solutions lying near k-soliton states with k≥2, together with a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics; related questions include the persistence of Toda shocks and rarefactions under perturbations and perturbations of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam problem.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the real line,

  i u_t + u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u + ε V(|u|) u = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t ≥ 0,

where ε > 0 is a small parameter and V: [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth real-valued function such that the perturbation does not become asymptotically negligible as t → ∞ (i.e. solitonic structures of the unperturbed equation persist and interact with the perturbation). Recall that the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS (ε = 0) is completely integrable via inverse scattering and admits k-soliton solutions for every integer k ≥ 1.

Develop a perturbation theory for this equation in the regime where the initial data lie in a neighborhood of a k-soliton solution (k ≥ 2) of the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS. Specifically:

(a) Construct, for sufficiently small ε, the global solution u(x,t) of the perturbed equation with initial data near a prescribed k-soliton.

(b) Provide a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics of u(x,t) as t → ∞, including the modulation of soliton parameters (positions, velocities, amplitudes, phases), the interaction between solitons induced by the perturbation, the radiation component, and explicit error estimates.

In parallel, address the analogous problems of: (i) the persistence (or breakdown) of Toda shock and Toda rarefaction wave solutions of the Toda lattice under small Hamiltonian perturbations, and (ii) the perturbation theory of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam problem, again with a description of long-time asymptotics in the presence of solitons.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Borghese–Jenkins–McLaughlin and Cuccagna–Jenkins, and more recent ∂̄-steepest descent analyses) has produced detailed long-time asymptotics for the unperturbed focusing NLS in soliton regions and partial results for certain perturbations and for the defocusing N-soliton case. However, a complete perturbation theory for the focusing cubic NLS near a k-soliton state (k ≥ 2) with non-negligible perturbation εV(|u|)u, together with the analogous Toda shock/rarefaction persistence and sine-Gordon/FPU problems, does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature; the program is still considered open in its general form.

context_brief: Large finite symmetric subsets in infinite groups
original_question: Given any infinite group G and any finite coloring of G, determine whether one must always be able to find a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrarily large finite cardinality.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be an infinite group. A subset A ⊂ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that gA⁻¹g = A, equivalently A = {gx⁻¹g : x ∈ A} for some g ∈ G. A finite coloring of G is a map χ : G → {1, 2, …, r} for some positive integer r, and a subset A ⊂ G is called monochromatic (with respect to χ) if χ is constant on A.

Decide whether the following statement is true: for every infinite group G, every positive integer r, and every coloring χ : G → {1, …, r}, and every positive integer n, there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G with |A| ≥ n.

In other words, must every finite coloring of an infinite group admit monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality?
status_search_result: Partial results are known: Protasov, Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets and others have established the existence of arbitrarily large monochromatic symmetric subsets for infinite abelian groups under finite colorings, and have studied related quantitative invariants ν(G) (minimal number of colors avoiding infinite monochromatic symmetric subsets), e.g. ν(Z^k) = k+1. The general question for all infinite (in particular nonabelian) groups appears to remain open in the form posed by Protasov; no full resolution was found in the search.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Create an effective perturbation theory for exactly solvable combinatorial models whose asymptotic random-matrix behavior is currently proved only for very rigid input distributions. For example, in last-passage percolation the exact analysis uses geometric or exponential waiting times; determine what happens under small perturbations of those distributions and prove whether the same random-matrix fluctuation laws persist.
self_contained_problem:
Consider last-passage percolation on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$: assign i.i.d. nonnegative random weights $\{w(i,j)\}_{(i,j)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2}$ with common distribution $\mu$, and define
$$L_\mu(N,N) = \max_{\pi}\sum_{(i,j)\in\pi} w(i,j),$$
where the maximum is over all up-right lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(N,N)$. When $\mu$ is the geometric distribution with parameter $q\in(0,1)$ (or, in a related model, the exponential distribution), it is known that
$$\frac{L_\mu(N,N) - c_1(\mu)\,N}{c_2(\mu)\,N^{1/3}} \xrightarrow{d} F_2 \qquad (N\to\infty),$$
where $F_2$ is the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution and $c_1(\mu),c_2(\mu)>0$ are explicit model-dependent constants.

Develop an effective perturbation theory for this exactly solvable model under perturbations of the input weight distribution. Specifically, prove or disprove the following: for every distribution $\nu$ in a suitable neighborhood of the geometric distribution $\mu_q$ (for example, distributions of the form $\nu_\epsilon = (1-\epsilon)\mu_q + \epsilon\rho$ for an arbitrary probability measure $\rho$ on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ with sufficient moments and $\epsilon$ small), there exist constants $c_1(\nu),c_2(\nu)>0$ such that
$$\frac{L_\nu(N,N) - c_1(\nu)\,N}{c_2(\nu)\,N^{1/3}} \xrightarrow{d} F_2.$$
Equivalently, establish quantitative stability of the $N^{1/3}$ scaling and the GUE Tracy–Widom limit law under small perturbations of the underlying i.i.d. weight distribution away from the integrable (geometric or exponential) case.
status_search_result: Full KPZ-class universality of one-point Tracy–Widom fluctuations for last-passage percolation with general i.i.d. weights remains an outstanding open problem. Partial progress exists: universality has been established in special regimes such as paths close to the axis (Bodineau–Martin 2005 and recent 2025 work), and for TASEP-type models with arbitrary particle density (Ferrari–Nejjar 2017), and there are recent extensions via KMT coupling toward the directed landscape. However, no general perturbation theory establishing Tracy–Widom limits for arbitrary small perturbations of the geometric/exponential distributions is currently available.

context_brief: Central sets in free Abelian groups
original_question: For the free Abelian groups Z^n with n > 3, compute the numbers χ(Z^n) and determine the structure of their central sets, where a central set E in a group G is one such that every r-coloring of G with r < ν(G) contains an infinite monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to some point x in E.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a group. For x in G, a subset S ⊂ G is called symmetric with respect to x if S = xS^{-1}x (equivalently, if for every s ∈ S the point xs^{-1} also lies in S; the point x is the centre of symmetry). Define ν(G) to be the smallest cardinal r such that there exists an r-coloring G = C_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_r with the property that no class C_i contains an infinite subset symmetric with respect to any point of G. A subset E ⊂ G is called central if for every cardinal r < ν(G) and every r-coloring of G there exists an infinite monochromatic subset that is symmetric with respect to some point x ∈ E. Define χ(G) to be the smallest cardinality of a central subset of G.

For the free Abelian groups G = Z^n with n > 3, compute the cardinal invariant χ(Z^n) and describe the structure of the central subsets of Z^n.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For integrable equations on a half-line, resolve the mismatch between the well-posed initial-boundary data and the additional dependent boundary quantities required by the Fokas method. In particular, for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on x≥0,t≥0 with smooth compactly supported initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x) and periodic boundary forcing u(0,t)=sin(ω t) with ω≠0, determine the long-time behavior of the solution and decide whether a fully explicit description is possible for general data.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the quarter-plane
  i u_t + u_{xx} - 2|u|^2 u = 0,   x ≥ 0,  t ≥ 0,
with initial data
  u(x, 0) = u_0(x),  x ≥ 0,
where u_0 is smooth and compactly supported, and with the time-periodic Dirichlet boundary condition
  u(0, t) = sin(ω t),  t ≥ 0,
for some fixed real ω ≠ 0.

The Fokas (unified transform) method represents the solution via a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem whose jump data depend on four spectral functions determined by both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary values at x = 0. Although the Dirichlet datum is prescribed, the corresponding Neumann datum u_x(0, t) is not free and must be determined consistently with the initial data and the boundary forcing (the "generalized Dirichlet-to-Neumann problem").

Determine the long-time behavior of u(x, t) as t → ∞ in different regions of the (x, t) quarter-plane (e.g., along rays x/t = const), and decide whether a fully explicit asymptotic description of u(x, t) can be obtained for general smooth compactly supported initial data u_0.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Boutet de Monvel–Its–Kotlyarov and by Lenells–Fokas (the "Unified Method II" series) treats NLS on the half-line with t-periodic boundary data, in particular single-exponential forcing a e^{2iωt}, and obtains long-time asymptotics and an asymptotically periodic Neumann value via Riemann–Hilbert analysis. The case of strictly real sinusoidal forcing sin(ωt) and the construction of fully explicit solutions for general smooth compactly supported initial data have been only partially resolved; rigorous treatments (e.g., for the linearized/inhomogeneous Schrödinger case) appeared as recently as 2023, indicating the original problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

context_brief: Odd-order groups and the ms invariant
original_question: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, determine whether the invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is always strictly greater than 1/r^2.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group. A subset X ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that gX^{-1}g = X (equivalently, X is invariant under the involution x ↦ gx^{-1}g for some g ∈ G). For an integer r ≥ 1, an r-coloring of G is a map χ : G → {1, 2, …, r}. Define

  ms(G, r) = (1/|G|) · min_{χ} max { |X| : X ⊆ G is symmetric and χ is constant on X },

where the minimum runs over all r-colorings χ of G; that is, ms(G, r) is the normalized guaranteed size of a largest monochromatic symmetric subset over all r-colorings of G.

Question: Is it true that for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1 one has

  ms(G, r) > 1/r^2 ?

Determine whether this strict inequality holds in full generality, or exhibit a finite group G of odd order and an integer r > 1 for which ms(G, r) ≤ 1/r^2.
category_tag: monochromatic symmetric subsets in colored groups
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of the question of whether ms(G, r) > 1/r^2 holds for every finite group G of odd order and every r > 1. Related literature on monochromatic symmetric subsets in colored groups (e.g., work by Protasov and collaborators, and subsequent studies on symmetric perfect colorings) addresses adjacent questions but no source clearly settles this specific inequality. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Extend the Riemann-Hilbert/steepest-descent method beyond the currently tractable 3×3 problems so that it applies to generic n×n Riemann-Hilbert problems arising in multi-matrix random matrix models and matrix models with an external field. Such an extension should also have consequences for multiple orthogonal polynomials, Padé-Hermite approximation, and irrationality problems for special real numbers.
status_search_result: The general program of extending nonlinear steepest descent to arbitrary n×n Riemann-Hilbert problems remains open. Significant partial progress has been made for specific 3×3 and 4×4 cases: e.g., steepest-descent analyses of 4×4 RH problems for biorthogonal polynomials in the two-matrix model (one-cut regular case) and Gaussian matrices with external source, and corresponding multi-sheeted-Riemann-surface global parametrix constructions. A fully general n×n framework with universal local parametrices and arithmetic applications has not been achieved.

context_brief: How small ms(G,r) can be for finite groups
original_question: Fix ε > 0 and an integer r > 1. Determine whether there exists a finite group G whose invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is smaller than ε.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists an element g ∈ G such that gS⁻¹g = S (equivalently, S is invariant under some involutive "central symmetry" x ↦ gx⁻¹g of G). For an integer r ≥ 1 and any coloring χ: G → {1, …, r}, define

  ms(χ) = max{ |S| : S ⊆ G is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to χ },

and set
  ms(G, r) = (1/|G|) · min_{χ: G → {1,…,r}} ms(χ).

Question: For every ε > 0 and every integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G with ms(G, r) < ε?
category_tag: Ramsey theory of symmetric subsets in groups
status_search_result: The question, attributed to Protasov and Banakh in surveys on symmetry and colorings of groups, is listed as an open problem in the Ramsey-type treatment of symmetric subsets of finite groups. Available sources (Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets and follow-up papers on monochromatic symmetric subsets of colored groups, and Protasov's surveys) discuss partial bounds for ms(G, r) but do not record a resolution. No definitive solution was located in the search.

original_question: For symmetric random band matrices whose bandwidth W ranges from 1 to N-1 in dimension N, determine the transition from Poisson bulk eigenvalue statistics to Gaudin-Mehta statistics and locate the sharp threshold. The conjecture highlighted in the source predicts a narrow transition region around W≈√N.
status_search_result: The conjectured sharp transition at $W \asymp \sqrt{N}$ for one-dimensional symmetric random band matrices remains open in full strength. Substantial partial progress has been made: delocalization has been proved for bandwidths well above $\sqrt{N}$ (work of Bourgade, Yang, Yau, Yin, Erdős–Riabov and others establishing GOE/GUE bulk statistics for sufficiently large $W$), and recent localization results push the localized/Poisson regime closer to $\sqrt{N}$ from below, but the optimal threshold $W \sim \sqrt{N}$ has not been reached from either side as of 2025–2026.

original_question: Determine whether there exists a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G, r), the largest guaranteed Haar measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of G, is strictly less than 1/r^2. In particular, compute the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2).
self_contained_problem:
For a topological group $G$ equipped with normalized Haar measure $\mu$, a measurable subset $A \subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g \in G$ such that $A = gA^{-1}g$ (equivalently, $A$ is invariant under the involution $x \mapsto gx^{-1}g$ for some $g \in G$). For a positive integer $r$, a measurable $r$-coloring of $G$ is a partition $G = C_1 \sqcup C_2 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup C_r$ into measurable sets. Define
$$\mathrm{ms}(G,r) = \inf_{\text{measurable } r\text{-colorings}} \; \max_{1 \le i \le r} \; \sup\{\mu(A) : A \subseteq C_i,\; A \text{ symmetric and measurable}\}.$$
Thus $\mathrm{ms}(G,r)$ is the largest value $c$ such that every measurable $r$-coloring of $G$ contains a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset of Haar measure at least $c$.

(a) Does there exist a connected compact group $G$ and a positive integer $r$ such that $\mathrm{ms}(G,r) < 1/r^2$?

(b) Determine the exact value of $\mathrm{ms}(SO(3), 2)$, where $SO(3)$ is the group of rotations of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its normalized Haar measure.
status_search_result: A web search for the invariant ms(G,r) on connected compact groups and the specific value ms(SO(3),2) did not return any source establishing a resolution. Related literature on monochrome symmetric subsets in colorings of groups (Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets and follow-ups) develops the framework but does not appear to determine ms(SO(3),2) or exhibit a connected compact group with ms(G,r) < 1/r^2. The current status could not be verified, so it is recorded as unknown.

original_question: For integers n > 1 and r > 1, determine whether ms(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2, where S^n is the n-dimensional sphere and I^+_2 denotes the orientation-preserving involutive isometries. Equivalently, decide whether every measurable r-coloring of S^n contains a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^n \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ denote the $n$-dimensional unit sphere, equipped with its normalized rotation-invariant Lebesgue measure $\mu$ (so $\mu(S^n)=1$). A subset $A \subseteq S^n$ is called axis-symmetric if there exists a line $\ell$ through the origin such that the orthogonal reflection of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that is the identity on $\ell$ and $-\mathrm{id}$ on $\ell^{\perp}$ (an orientation-preserving involutive isometry of $S^n$ when $n$ is odd, or, more generally, any involutive isometry of $S^n$ fixing some line through the center) maps $A$ onto itself. For an integer $r > 1$, a measurable $r$-coloring of $S^n$ is a partition $S^n = C_1 \sqcup C_2 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup C_r$ into measurable sets. Define
$$\mathrm{ms}(S^n, I^+_2, r) = \inf_{\{C_i\}} \; \sup_{1 \le i \le r} \; \sup\{\mu(A) : A \subseteq C_i \text{ is measurable and axis-symmetric}\},$$
where the outer infimum is over all measurable $r$-colorings of $S^n$.

Prove or disprove: for all integers $n > 1$ and $r > 1$,
$$\mathrm{ms}(S^n, I^+_2, r) = \frac{1}{r^2}.$$
Equivalently, decide whether for every integers $n,r>1$ and every measurable $r$-coloring of $S^n$, there exist a color class and a measurable axis-symmetric subset of that class of measure at least $1/r^2$.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any publication establishing or refuting the equality $\mathrm{ms}(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2$ for $n,r>1$. Related literature on chromatic numbers of spheres and symmetric monochromatic subsets exists, but no result directly resolving this specific question was located, so the status is unknown.

original_question: Classify the invariant ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n when n > 2. In particular, compute ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3, equivalently ms(S_4 × I, 2).
self_contained_problem:
For a compact set X ⊂ ℝⁿ of positive Lebesgue measure, call a measurable set B ⊂ ℝⁿ centrally symmetric if there exists a point c ∈ ℝⁿ (the center) such that B = 2c − B. For an integer r ≥ 2, an r-coloring of X is a partition X = A₁ ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ Aᵣ into Lebesgue-measurable pieces. Define

  ms(X, r) = inf over r-colorings (A₁,…,Aᵣ) of X of  max₁≤i≤r  sup{ λ(S) : S ⊂ Aᵢ measurable and centrally symmetric },

normalized by λ(X) (so 0 ≤ ms(X, r) ≤ 1), where λ denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ. Thus ms(X, r) is the largest m such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic centrally symmetric measurable subset of measure at least m·λ(X).

Problem.
(a) Classify (i.e., compute or give sharp formulas for) ms(X, r) for compact subsets X ⊂ ℝⁿ of positive Lebesgue measure when n > 2.
(b) In particular, compute ms(P, r) for every regular polyhedron P in ℝⁿ for all n > 2 and all r ≥ 2.
(c) Compute ms(T, 2), where T ⊂ ℝ³ is the regular tetrahedron (equivalently, ms(S₄ × I, 2), where S₄ × I denotes the prism over the regular tetrahedron viewed as a product space, with the same convention for centrally symmetric subsets).
status_search_result: The invariant ms(X, r) was introduced by Banakh, Verbitsky and Vorobets ("A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry"); the case of compact subsets of ℝⁿ for n > 2, including the regular tetrahedron T ⊂ ℝ³ with r = 2, is listed as an explicit open problem in the 2009 survey "Symmetry and colorings" and is still listed among open problems in the 2011 follow-up survey (arXiv:1111.1015). No subsequent paper resolving ms(T, 2) or classifying ms(X, r) for higher-dimensional regular polyhedra was located.

original_question: Compute the blurred interval invariants bms([n], r), at least for small n when r = 2, where bms([n], r) is the blurred analogue of the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in an r-coloring of the discrete interval [n].
self_contained_problem:
Let [n] = {1, 2, …, n} denote the discrete interval. A subset S ⊆ [n] is called symmetric if there exists a center c ∈ ½ℤ such that S = 2c − S, i.e. S is invariant under the reflection x ↦ 2c − x. Given an r-coloring χ : [n] → {1, …, r}, let

  ms(χ) = max { |S| : S ⊆ [n] is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to χ } / n,

and define the (normalized) interval invariant

  ms([n], r) = min { ms(χ) : χ is an r-coloring of [n] }.

Now consider the "blurred" variant. Fix an integer parameter (the blur radius) and call a subset S ⊆ [n] blurredly symmetric if S is contained in a small neighbourhood of a genuinely symmetric set, and call S blurredly monochromatic with respect to an r-coloring χ if its elements all receive colors from a single allowed cluster in the blurred sense (with the precise blurring relaxation as in the standard Banakh–Protasov setup). Define analogously

  bms([n], r) = min over r-colorings χ of ([n]) of (1/n) · max{ |S| : S ⊆ [n] is blurredly symmetric and blurredly monochromatic for χ }.

Problem. Determine the values of bms([n], 2), at least for small n. More generally, compute bms([n], r) for r = 2.
status_search_result: Searches surfaced the Banakh–Protasov survey on symmetry and colorings and the related Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets "Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry," along with subsequent work on monochromatic symmetric subsets, but no source providing computed values of the blurred invariant bms([n], r) (even for r = 2 and small n) was found. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Symmetric subsets in colored unit intervals
original_question: Compute the invariant ms([0, 1], r), the largest guaranteed Lebesgue measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of the unit interval [0, 1], at least in the case r = 2.
self_contained_problem:
For a measurable subset $B$ of the real line, call $B$ symmetric if there exists $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $B = 2c - B$ (i.e., $B$ is invariant under the reflection $x \mapsto 2c - x$). For a Lebesgue measurable set $A \subseteq [0,1]$, let
$$\mathrm{ms}(A) = \sup\{\lambda(B) : B \subseteq A,\ B \text{ Lebesgue measurable and symmetric}\},$$
where $\lambda$ denotes Lebesgue measure. For an integer $r \geq 1$, a measurable $r$-coloring of $[0,1]$ is a Lebesgue measurable map $\chi : [0,1] \to \{1,\dots,r\}$, with color classes $A_i = \chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i=1,\dots,r$. Define
$$\mathrm{ms}([0,1], r) = \inf_{\chi} \max_{1 \leq i \leq r} \mathrm{ms}(A_i),$$
the infimum being taken over all measurable $r$-colorings $\chi$ of $[0,1]$.

Determine the exact value of $\mathrm{ms}([0,1], r)$. In particular, compute $\mathrm{ms}([0,1], 2)$.
status_search_result: The invariant $\mathrm{ms}([0,1], r)$ was introduced and studied by Banakh, Verbitsky, and Vorobets in "A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry"; only lower and upper bounds for $\mathrm{ms}([0,1], 2)$ and asymptotics for large $r$ appear to be known. No source found gives an exact value of $\mathrm{ms}([0,1], r)$ for any $r \geq 2$, and the problem of computing it (even for $r=2$) is referenced as open in subsequent literature on symmetric monochromatic subsets.

paper_title: Vectored route-length minimization – a heuristic and an open conjecture
original_question: Given a finite partially connected network of N nodes embedded in a strictly Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, with a pre-specified source node S0 and sink node SN, does Vectored Route-length Minimization Search (VeRMinS) necessarily and sufficiently identify a route from S0 to SN whose total Euclidean route length is minimum? In VeRMinS, a connectivity matrix encodes the available edges, route vectors indicate which nodes lie on each source-to-sink route, an ideal route is the straight line from source to sink, a weight vector records each node's Euclidean distance from that ideal route with source and sink weights equal to zero, Euclidean-dominance filtering removes any route vector that differs from another only by including an extra intermediate node, and the selected route is the remaining route minimizing the route-vector/weight-vector product. Can this procedure be proved correct for every such finite Euclidean network, or can one construct a counterexample in which a shorter route exists but is not selected by VeRMinS?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite undirected graph with vertex set V = {S_0, S_1, ..., S_N} embedded in a Euclidean space R^d (d ≥ 1) so that each vertex S_i has a position x_i ∈ R^d, and each edge {S_i, S_j} ∈ E has length ‖x_i − x_j‖_2. Designate S_0 as a source and S_N as a sink. Define an admissible route from S_0 to S_N as a simple path in G starting at S_0 and ending at S_N; encode such a path as a 0/1 incidence vector P = (k_0, k_1, ..., k_N) over V, where k_j = 1 iff S_j lies on the path. Let the ideal route be the straight line segment L from x_0 to x_N in R^d, and define the weight vector W = (w_0, w_1, ..., w_N) by w_j = dist(x_j, L) (the Euclidean distance from S_j to L), with the convention w_0 = w_N = 0.

Define the following heuristic procedure (VeRMinS) to choose a route:
(1) Enumerate every simple path from S_0 to S_N as a vector P_t = (k_{t,0}, ..., k_{t,N}).
(2) Apply Euclidean-dominance filtering: discard any route vector P_t whenever there exists another route vector P_s such that P_t and P_s differ in exactly one coordinate j ∉ {0, N} with k_{t,j} = 1 and k_{s,j} = 0 (i.e., P_t is obtained from P_s by inserting one extra intermediate vertex while keeping all other vertices the same).
(3) Among the surviving route vectors, select the one minimizing the dot product P_t · W = Σ_j k_{t,j} w_j.

Question: Is it true that for every finite graph G with Euclidean vertex positions and every choice of source S_0 and sink S_N, the route selected by VeRMinS is necessarily and sufficiently a route of minimum total Euclidean length from S_0 to S_N? Equivalently, prove that VeRMinS always returns an actual shortest path, or exhibit a finite Euclidean network on which VeRMinS fails to identify a path of minimum total Euclidean length.
status_search_result: The conjecture was posed as an open problem in 2008, with the authors explicitly stating only a heuristic was provided. A web search reveals no subsequent published proof or counterexample, and no follow-up literature addressing the VeRMinS conjecture beyond the original posting. Its current status therefore could not be verified from available sources.

paper_title: An open question: Are topological arguments helpful in setting initial conditions for transport problems and quantization criteria/ quantum computing for Density Wave physics?
original_question: For charge-density-wave transport modeled by a generalized tunneling Hamiltonian in a driven sine-Gordon system, with tunneling between Gaussian wavefunctionals of a scalar quantum field, should the coefficients in the wavefunctionals and the coefficients in the driven sine-Gordon physical system be chosen by topological-charge arguments tied to Coleman's false-vacuum hypothesis, and can that topological choice help explain the observed current-versus-electric-field behavior as evidence for a first-order phase transition and quantum switching relevant to quantum computing via quantum-coherent phase evolution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional driven sine-Gordon model for charge-density-wave (CDW) transport, with Lagrangian density of the form

  L[φ] = (1/2)(∂_t φ)^2 − (1/2)v^2(∂_x φ)^2 − V_0[1 − cos(βφ)] + Jφ,

where φ(x,t) is a real scalar field, β, V_0, v are real parameters, and J is a driving term proportional to an applied electric field E. Model CDW tunneling between two metastable configurations of φ by a generalized tunneling Hamiltonian whose matrix elements are taken between Gaussian wavefunctionals

  Ψ_i[φ] = N_i exp{ −(1/2) ∫ dx dy [φ(x) − φ_i(x)] K_i(x,y) [φ(y) − φ_i(y)] },  i = 1,2,

centered on classical false- and true-vacuum field configurations φ_1, φ_2 of the tilted washboard potential, with positive-definite kernels K_i and normalization N_i.

Questions:

(a) Determine whether the parameters {φ_i, K_i, N_i} of the Gaussian wavefunctionals, together with the coefficients (β, V_0, v, J) of the driven sine-Gordon system, can be selected canonically by topological-charge arguments — i.e. by requiring that φ_1 and φ_2 lie in distinct topological sectors of the sine-Gordon vacuum manifold and that the tunneling amplitude correspond to a kink/anti-kink (false-vacuum decay) configuration in the sense of Coleman's bounce solution.

(b) Show whether such a topological-charge prescription forces the tunneling current I, computed from the resulting Hamiltonian as a function of the drive E, to exhibit a threshold-type, first-order-transition I–E characteristic with a sharp onset above a critical field E_T.

(c) Decide whether the resulting two-state tunneling dynamics admit a quantum-coherent phase evolution between the Gaussian wavefunctionals (a Josephson-like oscillation of the CDW phase φ) suitable as a qubit-like quantum switching mechanism, and quantify the decoherence conditions under which such coherent evolution persists.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual/physical question about whether topological-charge arguments à la Coleman's false-vacuum decay provide the correct way to fix wavefunctional and sine-Gordon coefficients for CDW tunneling. No subsequent work definitively resolving this specific prescription was identified; the status appears unresolved.

original_question: Determine how fast the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} converge to their common limit ms([0, 1], r).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A subset $S$ of an additively written set $\Omega$ (such as a finite arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ or the unit interval $[0,1]\subset\mathbb{R}$) is called centrally symmetric if there exists a center $c$ such that $S = c - S$, i.e., $S$ is invariant under the reflection $x\mapsto c-x$.

For an integer $r\ge 2$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let
$$
\mathrm{ms}([n],r)\;=\;\frac{1}{n}\,\max\Bigl\{\,m\;:\;\text{every coloring }\chi:\{1,\dots,n\}\to\{1,\dots,r\}\text{ admits a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset of cardinality }\ge m\,\Bigr\},
$$
and let
$$
\mathrm{bms}([n],r)\;=\;\frac{1}{n}\,\max\Bigl\{\,m\;:\;\text{every coloring }\chi:\{1,\dots,n\}\to\{1,\dots,r\}\text{ admits a monochromatic block-symmetric (interval-symmetric) subset of cardinality }\ge m\,\Bigr\},
$$
where a block-symmetric subset is a centrally symmetric subset that is the intersection of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with an interval symmetric about its midpoint.

For the continuous interval, define
$$
\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)\;=\;\sup\Bigl\{\,\mu\;:\;\text{every Lebesgue-measurable coloring }\chi:[0,1]\to\{1,\dots,r\}\text{ admits a monochromatic measurable centrally symmetric subset of Lebesgue measure }\ge \mu\,\Bigr\}.
$$

It is known that for each fixed $r\ge 2$ both sequences $\{\mathrm{ms}([n],r)\}_{n\ge 1}$ and $\{\mathrm{bms}([n],r)\}_{n\ge 1}$ converge to the common limit $\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)$ as $n\to\infty$.

Problem. For each fixed $r\ge 2$, determine the rate of convergence of the sequences $\{\mathrm{ms}([n],r)\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ and $\{\mathrm{bms}([n],r)\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ to their common limit $\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)$. In particular, find sharp upper and lower bounds for the differences
$$
\mathrm{ms}([n],r)-\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)\quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{bms}([n],r)-\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)
$$
as functions of $n$.
status_search_result: A search of subsequent surveys and follow-up work by Banakh and collaborators on symmetric monochromatic subsets (including the sequel "Symmetry and colorings: some results and open problems, II" from 2011) does not surface a published determination of the convergence rate of $\mathrm{ms}([n],r)$ and $\mathrm{bms}([n],r)$ to $\mathrm{ms}([0,1],r)$. The earlier "Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry" establishes asymptotics in $r$ and bounds for fixed small $r$ but not the $n$-rate. Status appears unresolved, but no definitive open-problem update was found.

original_question: For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k + 1, Matousek's theorem states that there is a constant c(p,q,k) such that every k-uniform hypergraph satisfying the (p,q)-property has transversal number at most c(p,q,k). Is it possible to choose this bound with asymptotic growth c(p,q,k) = O(p^k)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \ge 1$ be an integer. A hypergraph $H = (V, E)$ is called $k$-uniform if every edge $e \in E$ has exactly $k$ vertices. For an integer $p \ge q \ge k+1$, $H$ is said to satisfy the $(p,q)$-property if among every $p$ edges of $H$, some $q$ of them share a common vertex. The transversal number $\tau(H)$ is the minimum size of a set $T \subseteq V$ that meets every edge of $H$.

A theorem of Matoušek asserts that for every triple of integers $p \ge q \ge k+1$, there exists a finite constant $c(p,q,k)$ such that every $k$-uniform hypergraph with the $(p,q)$-property satisfies $\tau(H) \le c(p,q,k)$.

Question: Can $c(p,q,k)$ be chosen so that, for fixed $q$ and $k$, it grows at most polynomially of degree $k$ in $p$, i.e.,
$$ c(p,q,k) = O(p^k) \quad \text{as } p \to \infty? $$
The case of primary interest is $q = k+1$.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a result establishing $c(p,q,k) = O(p^k)$ for general $k$-uniform hypergraphs satisfying the $(p,q)$-property. Improved Hadwiger–Debrunner-type bounds (e.g., Keller–Smorodinsky–Tardos) tighten the geometric/convex setting, but the abstract combinatorial question for $k$-uniform hypergraphs—particularly $q=k+1$—does not appear to have been resolved.

original_question: Does the abrupt turn-on of the current-versus-electric-field curve imply a phase transition that could be exploited for quantum switching devices and ultra-fast data transitions, specifically if the Bogomolnyi inequality can be used to derive the identification α ≈ L⁻¹ ≡ ΔE_gap ≡ V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) and thereby connect 1+1-dimensional φ⁴ field theory to Gaussian wavefunctionals in the charge-density-wave setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional charge-density-wave (CDW) condensate modeled by a real scalar field φ(x,t) in 1+1 spacetime dimensions whose dynamics, after appropriate rescaling, is governed by a φ^4 (double-well) effective potential V_E(φ) with two distinct extrema φ_T (a "true" or false vacuum) and φ_F such that ΔE_gap := V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) > 0. Static finite-energy solutions interpolating between the two minima saturate the Bogomolnyi bound: for any field configuration with appropriate boundary conditions, the static energy obeys E[φ] ≥ |∫ dφ √(2 V_E(φ))|, with equality on BPS (kink/instanton) configurations satisfying dφ/dx = ±√(2 V_E(φ)). Let L denote the characteristic spatial width of such a soliton and let α denote the inverse correlation length governing the exponential turn-on of the tunneling/pinning current J as a function of applied electric field E in the CDW system, so that J(E) is sharply switched on at a threshold field E_T.

Question: Does the abrupt turn-on of the current–field characteristic J(E) at E_T correspond to a genuine phase transition of the underlying 1+1-dimensional φ^4 field theory? More precisely, can the Bogomolnyi (BPS) inequality applied to this φ^4 model be used to rigorously establish the identification
   α ≈ L^{-1} ≡ ΔE_gap ≡ V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T),
and to construct an exact bridge between the soliton sector of the 1+1-dimensional φ^4 field theory and a Gaussian wavefunctional description of the CDW ground state, thereby providing a field-theoretic mechanism for quantum switching and ultrafast transitions in CDW devices?
