paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: Does the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18) admit time-periodic solutions without restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type occupying a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The unknowns are the velocity field $v(t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the pressure $p(t,x) \in \mathbb{R}$, and the deviatoric extra-stress tensor $\sigma(t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_{\mathrm{sym}}$, governed by the system
$$\rho\bigl(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla) v\bigr) = -\nabla p + \operatorname{Div}\sigma + \rho f(t,x), \qquad \operatorname{div} v = 0,$$
together with the Jeffreys-type rheological relation
$$\sigma + \lambda\,\frac{\mathcal{D}\sigma}{\mathcal{D}t} = 2\eta\Bigl(E(v) + \kappa\,\frac{\mathcal{D} E(v)}{\mathcal{D}t}\Bigr),$$
where $E(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^\top)$ is the rate-of-strain tensor, $\rho>0$ is the density, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, $\lambda>0$ is the relaxation time, $\kappa\in(0,\lambda)$ is the retardation time, and $\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{D}t$ denotes a frame-indifferent objective time derivative (e.g. the upper- or lower-convected, Jaumann, or material derivative). The system is supplemented with the no-slip boundary condition $v\big|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ and a prescribed time-periodic body force $f(t+T,x) = f(t,x)$ of period $T>0$.

Question: Does this initial-boundary value problem admit, for every period $T>0$ and every choice of admissible coefficients $\rho,\eta,\lambda,\kappa$ and every sufficiently regular time-periodic external force $f$, at least one weak (or generalized) solution $(v,\sigma)$ that is time-periodic with period $T$, without any smallness restriction on the coefficients, on the external force, or on the initial data?
status_search_result: A review of mathematical results on Jeffreys-type viscoelastic motion lists the existence of time-periodic solutions without restrictions on coefficients, forcing, or initial data as an open problem. Available literature treats only restricted versions (small data, particular objective derivatives, simplified geometries, or related elastic-wave settings such as the 2024 work on time-periodic solutions of nonlinear elastic wave equations with viscoelastic terms). No source establishing the full unrestricted existence result for the Jeffreys system was found.

Equivalently, identify the weak-coupling asymptotic of the critical curve beyond the currently known bounds, using only the model data supported in the paper: α is the tail exponent in the renewal law K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), h_c(λ) is the localization-delocalization critical curve, and m_α depends only on α and not on the detailed law of the disorder sequence or on the full renewal distribution.
self_contained_problem:
Let $	au=(	au_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ with $	au_0=0$ and i.i.d. increments distributed according to a probability law $K$ on $\mathbb{N}$ satisfying the tail asymptotics
$$K(n) := \mathbb{P}(	au_1 = n) \;\sim\;  rac{C_K}{n^{1+\alpha}} \qquad (n	o\infty),$$
for a fixed exponent $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and a constant $C_K>0$. Let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables independent of $	au$, with mean $0$, variance $1$, and finite exponential moments $\mathbb{E}[e^{t\omega_1}]<\infty$ in a neighborhood of $0$.

For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (disorder strength) and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ (asymmetry bias), define the copolymer partition function

where $\Delta_n\in\{0,1\}$ encodes the standard copolymer interaction along the renewal $	au$. The quenched free energy
$$	extsf{F}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E} ig[\log Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h) ig]$$
exists and is non-negative. The critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda) \;=\; \inf\{\,h\ge 0 : 	extsf{F}(\lambda,h)=0\,\}.$$

original_question: In the corotational case D = D0 described by equation (3.2), are the global weak-solvability results claimed in reference [53] actually valid?

Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys (Oldroyd) type on a bounded domain (or the torus) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, governed by the system
$$\partial_t v + (v\cdot
abla) v - 
u\,\Delta v + 
abla p = \operatorname{div}\sigma, \qquad \operatorname{div} v = 0,$$
coupled with the corotational constitutive law for the extra stress $\sigma$:
$$\partial_t \sigma + (v\cdot
abla)\sigma + \sigma\,W(v) - W(v)\,\sigma + 	frac{1}{\lambda}\sigma = 	frac{2\mu_1}{\lambda}\,D(v),$$
where $D(v) = 	frac12(
abla v + (

abla v - (

original_question: In the same weak-coupling copolymer setting, prove the strict lower bound m_1/2 > 2/3 for the universal slope m_α of the critical curve h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ when α = 1/2.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting from $0$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables, independent of $S$, with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$, and finite exponential moments. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ and $h\in\mathbb{R}$, define the (quenched) copolymer Gibbs measure of length $N$ by the Radon–Nikodym derivative
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}(S)\;=\;\frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\exp\!\Big(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\Big),$$
with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(0)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$. The quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)\;=\;\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}\right]$$
exists and is non-negative; it satisfies $\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)\ge \lambda h$, and the (quenched) critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda)\;=\;\inf\{h\ge 0:\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=\lambda h\}.$$
More generally, replacing $S$ by a recurrent renewal process whose inter-arrival law has a regularly varying tail with exponent $1+\alpha$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, one has
$$\lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0}\frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}\;=\;m_\alpha\in(0,\infty),$$
a universal constant depending only on $\alpha$. It is known that $\tfrac{1}{1+\alpha}\le m_\alpha\le 1$; in particular $m_{1/2}\ge \tfrac{2}{3}$.

Problem. Prove the strict inequality
$$m_{1/2}\;>\;\tfrac{2}{3}.$$
status_search_result: The slope $m_\alpha$ of the copolymer critical curve at weak coupling is known to lie in $[1/(1+\alpha),1]$, and Caravenna–Giacomin (and subsequent work by Berger–Caravenna–Poisat–Sun–Zygouras, arXiv:1301.5308) established universality of $m_\alpha$ as the slope of a continuum copolymer model, refuting the Monthus-type conjecture $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$ in some regimes. However, no source located explicitly establishes the strict inequality $m_{1/2}>2/3$ for the simple-random-walk/$\alpha=1/2$ copolymer; the question appears to remain open, although it is closely related to disproving $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$ at $\alpha=1/2$. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: If one succeeds, even partially, in proving global existence for the Jeffreys-type evolutionary problem, can one then construct attractors, at least generalized ones, and/or inertial manifolds for that system?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys type occupying a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary. The motion is governed by the system
$$\rho\bigl(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v\bigr) = \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma - \nabla p + f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,v = 0,$$
where $v(t,x)$ is the velocity field, $p$ is the pressure, $f$ is a (time-independent) body force, and the deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma$ satisfies the Jeffreys constitutive relation
$$\sigma + \lambda_1\frac{D\sigma}{Dt} = 2\eta\!\left(\mathcal{E}(v) + \lambda_2\frac{D\mathcal{E}(v)}{Dt}\right),$$
with relaxation time $\lambda_1>0$, retardation time $\lambda_2\in(0,\lambda_1)$, viscosity $\eta>0$, strain-rate tensor $\mathcal{E}(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^\top)$, and $D/Dt$ an objective (e.g.\ Jaumann or upper/lower convected) derivative along trajectories. Equip the system with no-slip boundary condition $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ and prescribed initial data $v(0,\cdot)=v_0$, $\sigma(0,\cdot)=\sigma_0$.

Suppose one has any class of globally defined (possibly weak or generalized) solutions to this initial-boundary value problem. The problem is the following:

(a) Construct a (possibly generalized, e.g.\ trajectory) global attractor for the dynamical system associated with this class of global solutions, and establish its basic properties (compactness, invariance, attraction in a suitable topology, finite fractal/Hausdorff dimension when possible).

(b) Establish existence of a finite-dimensional inertial manifold — i.e.\ a finite-dimensional, positively invariant, Lipschitz (or smoother) submanifold of the phase space that exponentially attracts all trajectories — for this system, or prove that such a manifold cannot exist.

Give precise conditions on $\Omega$, $f$, the parameters $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, the choice of objective derivative, and the function space framework under which (a) and (b) hold.
status_search_result: Existence of minimal trajectory and global attractors for weak solutions of the autonomous Jeffreys-type viscoelastic motion equations has been established (e.g., Vorotnikov–Zvyagin), and uniform trajectory/global attractors have been proven in non-autonomous cases and for related Kelvin–Voigt and memory models. However, full results on inertial manifolds and finite-dimensional reduction for general Jeffreys-type systems do not appear to be available, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the universal weak-coupling slope m_α of the copolymer critical curve equals 1/(1+α)? Here m_α is defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ for small λ when the limit exists, and the question asks whether the lower-bound expression 1/(1+α) is ever the exact value of the slope for the original copolymer model.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the random copolymer model defined as follows. Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a simple random walk on ℤ, and let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be an i.i.d. sequence of centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, independent of S. For parameters λ ≥ 0 and h ≥ 0, define the polymer measure of length N by

  dP_{N,λ,h}^{ω}/dP(S) = (1/Z_{N,λ,h}^{ω}) · exp( -2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h) Δ_n ),

where Δ_n = 1 if (S_{n-1}, S_n) lies in the lower half-plane (i.e. max(S_{n-1}, S_n) ≤ 0) and Δ_n = 0 otherwise, and Z_{N,λ,h}^{ω} is the normalizing partition function.

The model exhibits a localization–delocalization phase transition along a critical curve h = h_c(λ), which for the simple random walk satisfies a polynomial tail exponent α = 1/2 of the underlying return-time distribution; more generally one considers an analogous model where the underlying renewal/return-time distribution has regularly varying tails with index 1+α for some α > 0. It is known that the limit

  m_α := lim_{λ ↓ 0} h_c(λ)/λ

exists (under suitable hypotheses), and satisfies the universal bounds

  1/(1+α) ≤ m_α ≤ 1   for every α > 0.

Question: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the equality m_α = 1/(1+α) holds, i.e., for which the lower bound is attained?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Bolthausen, den Hollander and Opoku proved that the lower bound is strict, i.e. m_α > 1/(1+α) for every α ∈ (0,∞), thereby ruling out Monthus' conjecture that the lower bound was sharp. The matching universal weak-coupling asymptotics m_α (and its value strictly above 1/(1+α)) were further established by Berger, Caravenna, Poisat, Sun and Zygouras, who proved the corresponding conjecture in Comm. Math. Phys. (2013).

context_brief: Generalization of Dirac-type boundary-value theory to arbitrary first-order elliptic operators.
original_question: For a smooth compact Riemannian manifold M with boundary Σ, Hermitian vector bundles E and F over M, and a general linear first-order elliptic differential operator A: C∞(M, E) → C∞(M, F), determine to what extent the structural properties known for Dirac-type operators continue to hold without assuming the Dirac or near-boundary product-form setting with fixed geometric data. In particular, after rewriting A near the boundary in product form A = J(x)(∂x + B(x)) plus lower-order terms, ask how far one can recover, for such arbitrary first-order elliptic operators, the same package of results emphasized for Dirac-type operators: a transparent and canonical Calderón projection, the Lagrangian property of the Cauchy data space, self-adjoint Fredholm extensions under regular pseudodifferential boundary conditions, the Cobordism Theorem, and continuous dependence of the associated data under variation of the operator, domain, and boundary geometry.
category_tag: Boundary value problems for first-order elliptic operators
status_search_result: Substantial portions of this program have been carried out by Bär–Ballmann (2012, 2016) for general first-order elliptic operators on manifolds with boundary, establishing maximal/minimal extensions, boundary regularity, Calderón projection, and Fredholm boundary conditions in considerable generality. original_question: The paper proves that for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0, where F is the quenched free energy and h_c is the critical curve. Can this smoothing estimate be strengthened by replacing the power δ^2 with a strictly larger exponent, i.e. by proving that the free energy vanishes faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized side?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\tau=(\tau_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}_0$ with $\tau_0=0$ and i.i.d. increments whose interarrival law satisfies
$$P(\tau_1=n)=\frac{L(n)}{n^{1+\alpha}},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
for some $\alpha\ge 0$ and a slowly varying function $L$. Let $(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables, independent of $\tau$, with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$, and $\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\omega_1}]<\infty$ for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $0$. For parameters $\lambda>0$ (disorder strength) and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ (pinning bias), define the disordered pinning partition function
$$Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}=\mathbb{E}_\tau\!\left[\exp\!\Big(\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\lambda\omega_n-\log\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\omega_1}]+h)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{n\in\tau\}}\Big)\right],$$
and the quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}_\omega\!\big[\log Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}\big]\ge 0.$$
The critical curve is $h_c(\lambda)=\sup\{h:\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h)=0\}$, finite for every $\lambda>0$.

Known smoothing bound. For every $\lambda>0$ there exists a constant $c(\lambda)<\infty$ such that
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le (1+\alpha)\,c(\lambda)\,\delta^{2}\qquad\text{for all }\delta>0.$$

Question. Can the exponent $2$ above be improved? Equivalently, does there exist (for some, or all, $\lambda>0$ and $\alpha>0$) an exponent $\gamma>2$ and a finite constant $C(\lambda)$ such that
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le C(\lambda)\,\delta^{\gamma}\qquad\text{for all }\delta\in(0,1)?$$
That is, can one prove that the quenched free energy vanishes strictly faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized phase?
status_search_result: The quadratic smoothing bound of Giacomin–Toninelli has been refined in several directions (sharp constants, weak-disorder asymptotics, more general disorder; e.g., Caravenna–den Hollander 2013, and subsequent work on disorder relevance), but no result is known to replace the exponent $2$ by a strictly larger one in the general disordered pinning model. In regimes of relevant disorder the quadratic behavior is believed to be sharp; in marginal/irrelevant regimes the question of strict improvement remains open according to the available literature.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
original_question: Are Dirac’s Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity, formulated using the original metric variables, and the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, which reparametrizes gravitational variables using lapse and shift functions together with the spatial three-metric, equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of the same theory despite the claim that the transformation from the four-metric variables to ADM variables is not canonical in the usual phase space?
self_contained_problem:
Consider General Relativity in the Hamiltonian framework on a globally hyperbolic spacetime with a 3+1 foliation. Two standard Hamiltonian formulations are:

(i) Dirac's formulation, which treats the ten components of the spacetime metric g_{μν} (μ,ν = 0,1,2,3) as the configuration variables, introduces conjugate momenta π^{μν} via Legendre transform of the Einstein–Hilbert Lagrangian density, and applies the Dirac procedure for constrained Hamiltonian systems on the resulting phase space.

(ii) The ADM formulation, which reparametrizes the metric components in terms of the lapse N, the shift N_i (i = 1,2,3), and the spatial three-metric γ_{ij}, takes (γ_{ij}, N, N_i) as configuration variables with their corresponding conjugate momenta, and again applies the Dirac procedure.

The change of variables (g_{μν}) ↔ (N, N_i, γ_{ij}), extended to the full phase spaces with their respective conjugate momenta, is known to fail to be a canonical transformation in the usual symplectic sense.

Question: Are formulations (i) and (ii) equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of General Relativity (i.e., do they yield the same constraint structure, gauge symmetry algebra, and physical observables) despite being related by this non-canonical change of phase-space variables? Provide a precise characterization of the relationship between the two formulations resolving this "non-canonicity puzzle".
status_search_result: Multiple subsequent works address this question. Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin (2008/2011, "The Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity: myths and reality") argue the two formulations are inequivalent because the change of variables is non-canonical and yields a different gauge symmetry. Others (e.g., Samanta, "Lagrangian symmetries of the ADM action", 2011; an extended-phase-space approach by Shestakova, 2011) maintain the formulations are physically equivalent and resolve the puzzle by reinterpreting the gauge sector. A "solution of the noncanonicity puzzle" via a new Hamiltonian formulation has been proposed (Phys. Lett. B, 2012). Consensus is not unanimous, but the puzzle is widely regarded as resolved at the level of physical content while inequivalence persists at the level of off-shell symmetries; we therefore mark it partially solved.

This asks whether the decay scale controlling correlation length or longest-excursion asymptotics vanishes at the same logarithmic rate as the free energy near criticality.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the disordered pinning model defined as follows. Let τ = (τ_n)_{n≥0} be a (recurrent) renewal process on ℕ with τ_0 = 0, and let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be an i.i.d. sequence of real random variables, independent of τ, with E[ω_1] = 0, E[ω_1^2] = 1, and finite exponential moments. For parameters λ ≥ 0 (disorder strength) and h ∈ ℝ (pinning bias), and integer N ≥ 1, define the partition function
   Z_{N,ω} := E[ exp( Σ_{n=1}^{N} (λ ω_n + h) 1_{n ∈ τ} ) 1_{N ∈ τ} ],
where E is expectation over τ. The quenched free energy is
   F(λ, h) := lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E[ log Z_{N,ω} ],
and the localized phase {(λ,h) : F(λ,h) > 0} is separated from the delocalized phase by the critical curve h_c(λ) = inf{h : F(λ,h) > 0}.

In the localized phase, define the auxiliary quantity
   μ(λ, h) := - lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[ (1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h))) / Z_{N,ω} ],
which controls exponential decay scales (e.g. for correlation functions or longest-excursion tails).

Question: Is it true that, as h ↘ h_c(λ) at fixed λ > 0,
   log μ(λ, h) ∼ log F(λ, h),
that is, log μ(λ,h) / log F(λ,h) → 1?

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
original_question: Are the Hamiltonian formulations of General Relativity associated with Dirac’s original metric-variable approach and the ADM lapse-shift-spatial-metric approach equivalent to original Einstein General Relativity as a Lagrangian theory, rather than being separate Hamiltonian models such as “ADM gravity” with no reference to Einstein General Relativity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Einstein's General Relativity formulated as a Lagrangian field theory via the Einstein–Hilbert action
\[ S_{EH}[g] = \frac{1}{16\pi G}\int R\,\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x, \]
with dynamical variable the spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ on a 4-manifold $M$, and gauge symmetry given by the group of spacetime diffeomorphisms $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$.

Two standard Hamiltonian (constrained) formulations of this theory are:

(a) Dirac's metric formulation: perform a 3+1 split of $M = \mathbb{R}\times\Sigma$, take as canonical variables the ten components of the spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ together with their conjugate momenta $\pi^{\mu\nu}$, and apply the Dirac–Bergmann algorithm for constrained Hamiltonian systems to identify the primary, secondary, first-class and second-class constraints, and to derive the generator of gauge transformations from the first-class constraints.

(b) The ADM formulation: change variables to the lapse $N$, the shift $N^i$, and the spatial 3-metric $h_{ij}$ on the slices $\Sigma$, with conjugate momenta $\pi^{ij}$ to $h_{ij}$ (the momenta conjugate to $N$ and $N^i$ being primary constraints), and again apply the constrained Hamiltonian analysis.

Question. Are the Hamiltonian theories obtained in (a) and (b) equivalent — both as constrained Hamiltonian systems with full four-dimensional diffeomorphism invariance and as dynamical theories — to the original Lagrangian Einstein General Relativity defined by $S_{EH}$? Equivalently: do (a) and (b) yield the same canonical theory of gravity (related by a canonical transformation in some appropriate, possibly extended, phase space) whose gauge group is $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ and whose solutions coincide with those of the Einstein equations, or must the ADM formulation be regarded as an inequivalent theory ("ADM gravity") whose constraint structure and gauge symmetries differ from those of Einstein General Relativity?
status_search_result: The question is actively debated. Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin (2011, "The Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity: myths and reality") argue that the Dirac and ADM Hamiltonian analyses are not equivalent: the change of variables from $(g_{\mu\nu},\pi^{\mu\nu})$ to ADM variables is not a canonical transformation, and only the Dirac analysis (without changes of variables) reproduces four-dimensional diffeomorphism invariance directly from the first-class constraints. Other authors maintain that within an extended phase-space formalism the ADM and metric Hamiltonian formulations are equivalent to each other and to Lagrangian Einstein gravity. Thus, the equivalence holds in some formulations (extended phase space) but is contested in the standard treatment; the issue is partially resolved but not closed in the literature.

original_question: Fix parameters (λ,h) in the interior of the delocalized region D, where D = {(λ,h) : F(λ,h)=0}. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the quenched polymer measure of the event that the polymer stays entirely in the favorable solvent during the whole terminal segment [εN, N] tends to 0 almost surely as N → ∞? In the paper's notation this is the question whether lim_{N→∞} P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN, N] ∩ N) = 0 almost surely, where Δ_n is the indicator that monomer n is below the interface, so Δ_n = 0 means that monomer n is not below the interface.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following random copolymer model at a selective interface. Let $\tau = \{\tau_j\}_{j\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}_0$ with $\tau_0 = 0$ and inter-arrival law $K(\cdot)$ satisfying $K(n) \sim c\, n^{-(1+\alpha)}$ for some $\alpha > 0$ (the renewal points represent the returns of a directed polymer to a horizontal interface). Independently of $\tau$, let $\xi = \{\xi_j\}_{j\ge 1}$ be i.i.d. Bernoulli$(1/2)$ random variables, and define
$$\Delta_n := \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} \xi_j\, \mathbf{1}_{(\tau_{j-1},\tau_j]}(n), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N},$$
so that $\Delta_n \in \{0,1\}$ is constant on each excursion of $\tau$ and indicates whether the $n$-th monomer lies below ($\Delta_n=1$) or not below ($\Delta_n=0$) the interface.

Let $\omega = \{\omega_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of real-valued random variables (the disorder) with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$ and finite exponential moments, defined on a probability space with measure $\mathbb{P}$. For parameters $\lambda \ge 0$ and $h \in \mathbb{R}$ and integer $N\ge 1$, define the quenched polymer measure
$$\frac{dP_{N,\omega}}{dP_0}(\tau,\xi) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z_{N,\omega}}\, \exp\!\Big(-2\lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N} (\omega_n + h)\, \Delta_n\Big)\, \mathbf{1}_{\{N\in\tau\}},$$
where $P_0$ is the law of $(\tau,\xi)$ and $Z_{N,\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. Let
$$F(\lambda,h) \;:=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\, \mathbb{E}\!\big[\log Z_{N,\omega}\big]$$
be the quenched free energy. Define the delocalized region $\mathcal{D} := \{(\lambda,h):\, F(\lambda,h)=0\}$.

Question: For $(\lambda,h)$ in the interior of $\mathcal{D}$, is it true that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty} P_{N,\omega}\!\big(\Delta_n = 0 \text{ for every } n \in [\varepsilon N, N]\cap \mathbb{N}\big) \;=\; 0 \qquad \mathbb{P}(d\omega)\text{-almost surely}?$$
status_search_result: Path properties of disordered copolymers in the interior of the delocalized region (in particular almost-sure statements like the one asked) are widely described in surveys as among the hardest unsolved problems for this model. Available results give annealed/in-probability statements and bounds of order $O(\log N)$ on the number of monomers in the unfavorable solvent, but a quenched almost-sure delocalization statement of this strong form does not appear to have been established.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Phase-space transformations versus Einstein gauge transformations
original_question: Is the group of transformations generated in Hamiltonian phase space the same as, or at least inclusive of, the gauge-transformation group of Einstein General Relativity, including the diffeomorphism-type transformations of all gravitational variables such as g_{0μ} and the ADM lapse and shift variables?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Einstein's General Relativity formulated on a four-dimensional spacetime with Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, decomposed in the Arnowitt–Deser–Misner (ADM) variables consisting of the spatial 3-metric $g_{ij}$ together with the lapse function $N$ and shift vector $N^i$ (which encode the components $g_{0\mu}$). Consider the Dirac–Bergmann constrained Hamiltonian formulation of this theory, in which one identifies primary and secondary first-class constraints on the phase space $(g_{ij},\pi^{ij},N,N^i,\pi_N,\pi_{N^i})$. Let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{ph}}$ be the group of canonical transformations of this phase space generated by suitable linear combinations of all first-class constraints (e.g., via the Castellani chain construction), and let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{GR}}$ denote the gauge group of Einstein's theory consisting of all spacetime diffeomorphism-induced transformations acting on every component of the metric, including $g_{0\mu}$ (equivalently the lapse $N$ and shift $N^i$).

Determine whether $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{ph}} = \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{GR}}$, or at least whether $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{ph}} \supseteq \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{GR}}$. In particular, decide whether the diffeomorphism transformations of $g_{0\mu}$ (and of $N$, $N^i$), which cannot be produced by acting with the secondary momentum/Hamiltonian constraints alone on the 3-metric sector, can be recovered as canonical transformations generated by an explicit combination of all first-class constraints in the Hamiltonian formulation, and provide a constructive prescription for the generator when this is the case.
category_tag: Constrained Hamiltonian gauge symmetries in General Relativity
status_search_result: The question has been substantially addressed in the constrained-dynamics literature: using the Castellani/Rosenfeld–Anderson–Bergmann chain procedure, one can construct an explicit generator (a tuned sum of primary and secondary first-class constraints) that produces gauge transformations of all metric components, including the lapse and shift. Pons, Salisbury, Shepley and others have shown that the Hamiltonian phase-space gauge group includes the projectable subgroup of spacetime diffeomorphisms, with generators depending explicitly on the lapse and shift, while full diffeomorphism invariance requires this projectability condition. Thus the inclusion $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{ph}}\supseteq\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{GR}}$ (in the projectable sense) is established constructively, but exact equality with the full diffeomorphism group remains subtle and is still actively discussed.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.
self_contained_problem:
Let P = {p_1, ..., p_n} be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment between p_i and p_j contains no other point of P. The point visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph G(P) on vertex set {v_1, ..., v_n} with v_i v_j an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Problem: Given as input a simple undirected graph G specified by its adjacency matrix, decide whether there exists a finite point set P in the plane such that G(P) is isomorphic to G. Determine the computational complexity (decidability, and complexity class) of this recognition problem.
status_search_result: Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015; DCG 2017) proved that point visibility graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals (∃ℝ-complete), placing it between NP and PSPACE; this resolves the complexity question up to ∃ℝ-completeness, but exact decidability/complexity classification (e.g., whether ∃ℝ = NP) remains open. Recognition for grid point visibility graphs is decidable iff the existential theory of the rationals is decidable, which is itself an open question.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
original_question: What principled rules should determine the construction of a generator of gauge transformations in the phase space of constrained gravitational theory, given that constraint-based generator algorithms can depend on the chosen Hamiltonian and parametrization and can give correct transformations only for certain gravitational variables or parametrizations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a constrained Hamiltonian system on a phase space $(\Gamma,\{\cdot,\cdot\})$ obtained from a singular Lagrangian field theory (in particular, general relativity in metric or tetrad-connection variables), with a set of primary and secondary constraints $\{\phi_a\}$, classified into first-class constraints $\{\gamma_\alpha\}$ generating gauge transformations and second-class constraints. A gauge generator is a phase-space functional of the form
$$G[\varepsilon] = \int d^3x\, \big(\varepsilon^\alpha(t,x)\,\gamma_\alpha + \dot\varepsilon^\alpha(t,x)\,C_\alpha + \cdots\big),$$
constructed as a linear combination of first-class constraints (and possibly their time derivatives) with smearing functions $\varepsilon^\alpha$, such that the canonical action of $G$ on phase-space variables reproduces the gauge transformations of the underlying Lagrangian theory (e.g., spacetime diffeomorphisms in general relativity).

Existing algorithms for constructing such a generator (for instance the Dirac procedure, and the Castellani-type chain procedure) depend on:
(i) the explicit form of the total Hamiltonian and the multiplier conventions chosen,
(ii) the parametrization of the canonical variables (e.g., ADM variables vs.\ tetrad/connection variables),
and they are known to reproduce the correct off-shell gauge transformations only for particular choices of variables or parametrizations; the algebra of constraints itself is not invariant under change of parametrization.

Problem. Formulate a set of principled, parametrization-independent rules — analogous in status to the Lagrangian "rules of procedure" — that uniquely determine a gauge generator $G$ on the phase space of a generally covariant constrained theory such that:

(a) the canonical transformation generated by $G$ coincides, on solutions and off-shell up to trivial gauge transformations, with the full local symmetry group of the underlying Lagrangian theory (for general relativity, the spacetime diffeomorphism group);
(b) the construction is invariant under canonical changes of parametrization of the gravitational variables and independent of the particular splitting of the Hamiltonian into "main" and "constraint" parts;
(c) the rules reduce to the known correct generators in cases where these have been independently verified.

Either provide such a set of rules together with a proof of (a)–(c), or prove that no such universal set of rules can exist for general relativity.
status_search_result: The question concerns a foundational/conceptual issue about canonical generators of gauge transformations in constrained Hamiltonian general relativity. While Castellani's algorithm and subsequent refinements provide gauge generators in specific parametrizations (ADM, tetrad, Ashtekar variables), no parametrization-independent universal "rule of procedure" with the requested status has been established; the literature (Pons, Salisbury, Shepley; Pitts; and others through the 2010s–2020s) continues to debate the correct construction and its parametrization dependence. The problem appears to remain open as a matter of principle.

original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Define two points p_i, p_j ∈ P to be mutually visible if the open line segment between p_i and p_j contains no other point of P (i.e., no third point of P lies on the segment p_i p_j). Associate to P the point visibility graph G(P) whose vertex set is P and whose edges are exactly the pairs {p_i, p_j} of mutually visible points.

Give a complete combinatorial characterization of the class of graphs G that arise in this way: namely, determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial (graph-theoretic) conditions on a finite simple graph G so that there exists a finite point set P ⊂ R^2 with G(P) isomorphic to G.
status_search_result: The general characterization of point visibility graphs remains an open problem. Partial progress is known: the recognition problem has been shown to be NP-hard and lies in PSPACE, and is complete for the existential theory of the reals. Complete characterizations have been obtained only for special subclasses (e.g., planar point visibility graphs), but no combinatorial characterization of the full class is known.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Whether to abandon ADM and other parametrizations
original_question: Should the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, or other Hamiltonian formulations based on parametrizations whose canonicity is unproved in the usual phase space, be abandoned or treated as independent models rather than as valid formulations of Einstein General Relativity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Einstein's General Relativity formulated on a globally hyperbolic 4-manifold M = R × Σ, with Lorentzian metric g_{μν} of signature (-,+,+,+) and Einstein–Hilbert action S[g] = (1/16πG) ∫ R √(-g) d^4x. The Arnowitt–Deser–Misner (ADM) parametrization replaces the ten components of g_{μν} by the lapse N, the shift N^i, and the spatial metric h_{ij} on Σ via
   g_{00} = -N^2 + h_{ij} N^i N^j,   g_{0i} = h_{ij} N^j,   g_{ij} = h_{ij},
and passes to a Hamiltonian formulation on the phase space coordinatized by (h_{ij}, π^{ij}, N, N^i, π_N, π_i) with the standard Poisson bracket structure. Other Hamiltonian formulations of General Relativity (for example, those based on alternative metric parametrizations or on tetrad/connection variables) likewise introduce new configuration variables in place of g_{μν}.

A change of variables from the canonical phase space variables associated with g_{μν} (and their conjugate momenta) to the variables of such an alternative Hamiltonian formulation is called canonical if it preserves the Poisson bracket structure on the full phase space.

Question: Suppose a Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity is obtained from a parametrization for which the transformation from the original metric phase-space variables to the new variables is not known to be a canonical transformation in the usual phase space. Must such a formulation (in particular the ADM formulation) be regarded as an autonomous dynamical model — distinct from Einstein General Relativity — rather than as an equivalent Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein's theory? Equivalently: does the lack of a verified canonicity of the parametrization force one to abandon the ADM Hamiltonian formulation (and analogous parametrization-based Hamiltonian formulations) as legitimate formulations of Einstein General Relativity?
status_search_result: The question is conceptual and concerns the interpretation of Hamiltonian formulations of General Relativity built on non-canonical parametrizations. There is an ongoing debate: Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin have argued that ADM should be considered a separate model, while others maintain ADM remains a valid formulation of Einstein gravity; the matter has not been definitively resolved by community consensus.

original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let P = {p_1, …, p_n} be a finite set of distinct points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment joining p_i and p_j contains no other point of P. The (point) visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph G(P) on vertex set {v_1, …, v_n} in which v_i v_j is an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Problem. Given a finite simple undirected graph G that is guaranteed to be the point visibility graph of some finite point set in the plane, give an algorithm that, on input G, outputs explicit coordinates of points q_1, …, q_n ∈ R^2 such that the visibility graph of Q = {q_1, …, q_n} is isomorphic to G.
status_search_result: The point visibility graph reconstruction problem remains open. Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015; DCG 2017) showed that point visibility graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals (∃R), which places recognition (and hence reconstruction with explicit real coordinates) in PSPACE but provides no polynomial-time algorithm. No algorithm producing a planar realization for an arbitrary point visibility graph is known, and the problem is considered a long-standing open problem in the area.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Extended phase space as an alternative Hamiltonian formalism
original_question: Does an extended phase-space Hamiltonian formalism, in which gauge degrees of freedom are treated on the same footing as physical degrees of freedom and missing velocities are introduced by differential gauge conditions, provide an alternative to both the original Dirac and ADM approaches while preserving equivalence with the Lagrangian equations and producing correct transformations for all phase variables?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a generally covariant gravitational theory described by a Lagrangian L(q, \dot q) where the configuration variables q = (q_phys, q_gauge) include both physical and gauge (lapse/shift-type) degrees of freedom, and where the standard Legendre transformation is singular because some velocities (those of the gauge variables) cannot be expressed through momenta. Two classical Hamiltonian treatments are known: (i) the Dirac constraint analysis, in which primary and secondary first-class constraints generate gauge transformations, and (ii) the ADM formulation, in which the metric is decomposed into lapse, shift, and spatial 3-metric, with lapse and shift treated as Lagrange multipliers.

Construct, as an alternative, an extended phase space formalism with the following properties:

1. Gauge variables q_gauge are placed on the same footing as physical variables q_phys; in particular, momenta conjugate to q_gauge are introduced.
2. The "missing velocities" \dot q_gauge are supplied by adjoining differential gauge-fixing conditions to the original Lagrangian (together with the corresponding Faddeev–Popov ghost sector), yielding a non-degenerate effective Lagrangian to which the standard Legendre transformation applies.
3. The resulting Hamiltonian equations of motion in the extended phase space are equivalent to the Euler–Lagrange equations of the original theory together with the chosen differential gauge conditions.
4. The full system possesses a global BRST symmetry, and the corresponding Noether BRST charge generates the correct BRST transformations on all extended phase space variables (including ghosts and gauge variables).

Prove that such a formalism exists for general relativity, establish the equivalence in (3) on the full extended phase space, and demonstrate the property in (4); alternatively, identify obstructions to any of these requirements.
status_search_result: The extended phase space approach (developed by Savchenko, Shestakova, and collaborators) has been constructed for general relativity and shown to yield Hamiltonian equations equivalent to the Lagrangian equations supplemented by differential gauge conditions, with a global BRST symmetry whose Noether charge generates correct transformations on all phase variables. However, its status as a fully accepted "alternative" to the Dirac/ADM approaches is debated: results depend on the choice of gauge condition (gauge-noninvariance of the resulting quantum theory) and the physical interpretation remains under discussion. Thus the construction itself exists (partially solved) while the broader equivalence/interpretation question is not settled.

original_question: Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear, in the standard convention; otherwise, two points see each other iff the open segment joining them contains no other point of P). The point visibility graph G of P has vertex set P, with two points joined by an edge precisely when they see each other. Let ω(G) denote the clique number and χ(G) the chromatic number of G.

Prove or disprove: every point visibility graph G with ω(G) ≤ 4 satisfies χ(G) ≤ 5.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been disproved. A construction of a point visibility graph with clique number 4 and chromatic number 6 was given by Pfender (arXiv:1610.00952, "On colouring point visibility graphs"), refuting the proposed bound χ ≤ 5 when ω ≤ 4. The broader question of whether χ is bounded by any function of ω for point visibility graphs remains open, with only super-polynomial lower bounds known.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Extending simple-model results to full gravity
original_question: Can the results of the extended phase-space approach, which have been demonstrated only for simple models with finitely many degrees of freedom, be reproduced for the full gravitational theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the extended phase-space approach to the Hamiltonian formulation of a generally covariant theory. In this approach, one starts from a Lagrangian invariant under reparametrizations (or, more generally, gauge transformations), adjoins gauge-fixing conditions written in differential form so as to introduce the missing velocities of the gauge variables, and thereby obtains an effective Lagrangian whose Legendre transform yields a Hamiltonian system on an extended phase space in which gauge degrees of freedom are treated on equal footing with physical ones. The resulting Hamiltonian dynamics is constraint-free, is equivalent to the original Lagrangian (Euler–Lagrange) dynamics together with the chosen gauge conditions, and admits canonical transformations relating different parametrizations of the configuration variables and different gauge choices.

For minisuperspace and other models with finitely many degrees of freedom (e.g., isotropic or spherically symmetric reductions of gravity coupled to matter), this construction has been carried out and shown to: (i) be equivalent to the Lagrangian formulation; (ii) yield a Schrödinger-type quantum equation upon canonical quantization; and (iii) be related across different gauges and parametrizations by canonical transformations on the extended phase space.

Problem. Carry out the analogous construction for the full theory of General Relativity, with infinitely many degrees of freedom, where the configuration variables are the components of a Lorentzian metric g_{μν} on a 4-manifold M, the action is the Einstein–Hilbert action S = (1/16πG) ∫_M R √(−g) d^4 x (possibly with matter), and the gauge group is the full diffeomorphism group of M. Specifically:

1. Construct an extended phase space for the full Einstein–Hilbert theory by adjoining four independent differential gauge-fixing conditions for the lapse and shift (or, more generally, for a chosen parametrization of g_{μν}) so that the resulting effective Lagrangian is non-degenerate in all metric components and yields a Hamiltonian system without first-class constraints, equivalent to the Einstein equations together with the gauge conditions.

2. Prove that Hamiltonian formulations of the full theory associated to different admissible parametrizations of the gravitational variables and different admissible differential gauge conditions are related by canonical transformations on this extended phase space.

3. Demonstrate that the resulting Hamiltonian dynamics and its canonical quantization reproduce, in the full field-theoretic setting, the structural features (gauge-invariance properties, equivalence with the Lagrangian formulation, Schrödinger-type quantum dynamics) established for finite-dimensional reductions.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has extended the extended phase-space approach beyond finite-dimensional minisuperspace models, including a generalized spherically-symmetric model (2013) and treatments of canonical transformations of gravitational variables in extended phase space for wide classes of parametrizations and gauges (2010–2011). A 2025 review still discusses features and perspectives of this quantization program. However, a complete construction reproducing all results for the full gravitational theory with infinitely many degrees of freedom does not appear to have been fully achieved; the program is best characterized as partially solved/ongoing.

original_question: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear is not required; instead use the standard convention that two points u,v ∈ P are mutually visible if the open segment uv contains no point of P). The visibility graph V(P) has vertex set P and edges between every pair of mutually visible points. For a graph G, let ω(G) denote the clique number and χ(G) the chromatic number.

Prove that there exists an absolute constant c such that every point visibility graph G = V(P) satisfying ω(G) = 5 satisfies χ(G) ≤ c.

(Equivalently, extend the known result that point visibility graphs with clique number at most 4 have bounded chromatic number to the case of clique number 5.)

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: In nuclear density functional theory, the Levy-Lieb energy is obtained by minimizing a density functional F[ρ] over neutron and proton densities whose integrals are fixed particle numbers N and Z, while the inner constrained search may still range over many-body density operators that are not eigenstates of the particle-number operators. A nuclear mass formula is concave when second differences of ground-state energies in the N,Z plane are positive definite. How can density functional and energy-density-functional theories, including formalisms with pairing correlations κ and particle-number fluctuation penalties, be adjusted so that the constrained minimization rigorously enforces concavity and cannot assign an ensemble density with average particle numbers N,Z an energy below the true N,Z ground-state energy?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a nuclear quantum many-body system characterized by neutron and proton number densities ρ_n(r), ρ_p(r) on R^3 with prescribed integrals
  ∫ ρ_n = N,   ∫ ρ_p = Z,   N, Z ∈ Z_{≥0}.
Let E(N,Z) denote the exact ground-state energy of the nuclear Hamiltonian in the (N,Z) particle-number sector, with associated ground-state density (ρ^{N,Z}_n, ρ^{N,Z}_p).

Levy–Lieb constrained-search functional. Define
  F[ρ_n, ρ_p] = inf { Tr(D H_int) : D is a (possibly mixed) many-body density operator on the full Fock space yielding densities ρ_n, ρ_p },
where H_int is the intrinsic nuclear Hamiltonian and D is allowed to be a statistical mixture that need not be an eigenstate of the neutron- and proton-number operators. In generalized energy-density-functional formalisms, F may also depend on a pairing tensor κ and on particle-number-fluctuation penalty terms.

Concavity. The mass surface (N,Z) ↦ E(N,Z) is said to be concave on its lattice domain if every second difference is positive, i.e. for every (N,Z) and every nonzero integer step (n,z),
  E(N+n, Z+z) + E(N−n, Z−z) − 2 E(N, Z) > 0.

The pathology. If F is defined by the broad constrained search above, then for any n, z one may form the ensemble
  D = (1/2)(|Ψ_{N+n,Z+z}⟩⟨Ψ_{N+n,Z+z}| + |Ψ_{N−n,Z−z}⟩⟨Ψ_{N−n,Z−z}|),
whose induced one-body density has integrals (N,Z) on average but whose energy is
  (1/2)(E(N+n,Z+z) + E(N−n,Z−z)).
Whenever the mass surface is non-concave at (N,Z) along (n,z), this ensemble energy lies strictly below E(N,Z); minimizing F over densities with fixed integrals (N,Z) then yields a value below the true ground-state energy.

Problem. Construct a precise modification of the density-functional / energy-density-functional formalism — possibly involving the admissible class of trial density operators D, the role of the pairing tensor κ, particle-number-projection or restoration procedures, and/or particle-number-fluctuation penalty functionals — such that:
  (a) the resulting constrained-search minimum F̃[ρ_n, ρ_p] satisfies F̃ ≥ E(N,Z) whenever ∫ρ_n = N, ∫ρ_p = Z;
  (b) the framework rigorously enforces (or is at least consistent with) concavity of the resulting mass surface;
  (c) the formalism reduces, in appropriate limits, to standard nuclear DFT/EDF with pairing.

Provide a mathematically rigorous prescription that achieves (a)–(c), or prove that no such prescription exists within a specified class of EDF theories.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the nuclear DFT literature concerning how to adjust constrained-search density functionals (with pairing and particle-number fluctuation terms) so that the minimization rigorously enforces concavity of the mass surface. Web searches on Levy–Lieb concavity in nuclear DFT and on subsequent reviews of nuclear density functional theory do not surface a rigorous resolution; the issue is still discussed as unresolved in surveys of nuclear DFT.

original_question: For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. Two points x, y in P are said to be mutually visible (with respect to P) if the open line segment between x and y contains no point of P. A subset S ⊆ P is called a visible clique if every pair of distinct points in S is mutually visible. A subset of P is called collinear if all its points lie on a single line.

The big-line-big-clique conjecture asserts: for all integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, there exists an integer h(k, ℓ) such that every set P of at least h(k, ℓ) points in the plane contains either ℓ collinear points or a visible clique of size k.

It is known that the conjecture holds whenever ℓ ≤ 3 (since in this case general-position point sets are forced) and whenever k ≤ 5 (using the existence of an empty convex pentagon in any sufficiently large planar point set with no ℓ collinear points).

Prove the conjecture in either of the following remaining cases:
(a) k = 6 (with ℓ ≥ 2 arbitrary), or
(b) ℓ = 4 (with k ≥ 2 arbitrary).

That is, show that there is an integer h such that any planar point set of at least h points contains 6 mutually visible points or ℓ collinear points (case a), respectively contains k mutually visible points or 4 collinear points (case b).
category_tag: discrete geometry / visibility in point sets
status_search_result: The big-line-big-clique conjecture of Kára, Pór, and Wood remains open for finite planar point sets. The case k ≤ 5 was settled by the empty-pentagon theorem, and ℓ ≤ 3 is trivial; the next cases k = 6 and ℓ = 4 are still listed as unsolved on the Open Problem Garden and on the Wikipedia page for the conjecture, with no resolution found in subsequent literature.

original_question: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. A finite set P of points is said to be in general position if no three points of P are collinear. Given such a set P, a blocking set for P is a finite set Q of points in the plane, disjoint from P, such that for every pair of distinct points p, p' in P the open segment pp' contains at least one point of Q. Let b(P) denote the minimum cardinality of a blocking set for P, and define
   b(n) = min { b(P) : P is a set of n points in the plane in general position }.

Prove that b(n)/n → ∞ as n → ∞.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: In a radial version of nuclear Kohn-Sham density functional theory, the physical density is a scalar radial profile ρ0(r), ordinary Slater determinants built from LS orbitals |nlmσ⟩ or jj orbitals |nljm⟩ in scalar mean fields u0(r) are not themselves scalar except at subshell closure, and the proposed kinetic functional FKS0[ρ0] minimizes the kinetic energy over scalar mixtures D′0 of such determinants that reproduce ρ0. How should the Kohn-Sham procedure be adapted in this radial setting, including the construction and properties of the redefined kinetic functional FKS0[ρ0] and the radial Kohn-Sham potential uKS0(r), so that self-consistent spherical orbitals reproduce ρ0 and can be related to or compared with existing spherical and deformed nuclear energy density functionals?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a self-bound, rotationally invariant fermionic many-body system (e.g., a nucleus) described in a radial setting in which the only physical density retained is the scalar radial profile $\rho_0(r)$, defined so that $\int_0^\infty 4\pi r^2 \rho_0(r)\,dr = N$ (the particle number). Single-particle states are taken either in the LS coupling form $|n l m \sigma\rangle$ or in the jj coupling form $|n l j m\rangle$, generated as eigenstates of a scalar (rotationally invariant) one-body mean-field Hamiltonian $h = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta + u_0(r)$. A general Slater determinant $D$ built from a finite set of such orbitals is, by Wigner–Eckart considerations, generally not a scalar (rotationally invariant) state, except when all occupied subshells are completely filled (subshell closure).

Let $\mathcal{S}_{\rho_0}$ denote the convex set of scalar (rotationally invariant) mixed states $D'_0$ of the form $D'_0 = \sum_k w_k |D_k\rangle\langle D_k|$, with $w_k \ge 0$, $\sum_k w_k = 1$, and each $D_k$ a Slater determinant constructed from such radial orbitals, such that the one-body density of $D'_0$ equals the prescribed $\rho_0(r)$. Define the radial Kohn–Sham kinetic functional
$$F_{KS,0}[\rho_0] \;=\; \inf_{D'_0 \in \mathcal{S}_{\rho_0}}\, \mathrm{Tr}\!\left( D'_0\, \hat T \right), \qquad \hat T = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\Delta_i.$$
Let $F_0[\rho_0]$ denote the exact (interacting) radial energy density functional of the system, and define a candidate radial Kohn–Sham potential by the radial functional derivative
$$r\, u_{KS,0}(r) \;=\; \frac{\delta\bigl(F_0 - F_{KS,0}\bigr)}{r\,\delta \rho_0(r)}.$$

Tasks:
(i) Establish whether $\mathcal{S}_{\rho_0}$ is non-empty for every admissible $\rho_0$ (a $v$-representability/$N$-representability question in the radial scalar setting), and prove existence/uniqueness properties (convexity, lower semicontinuity, differentiability) of $F_{KS,0}[\rho_0]$.
(ii) Derive the Euler–Lagrange equations characterizing the minimizer and show that there exists a self-consistent spherical orbital set, generated from the one-body Hamiltonian $-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta + u_{KS,0}(r)$, whose associated scalar mixed determinant reproduces the prescribed $\rho_0(r)$.
(iii) Formulate and justify a meaningful Hartree-type subtraction adapted to short-range, state-dependent nuclear effective interactions, and analyze the resulting simplified form of $u_{KS,0}(r)$.
(iv) Compare the resulting radial Kohn–Sham scheme with standard spherical and deformed nuclear energy density functionals, identifying precise mathematical relations or obstructions.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a largely open program for radial Kohn–Sham theory in the nuclear context. No subsequent work establishing a complete construction and analysis of $F_{KS,0}[\rho_0]$ and $u_{KS,0}(r)$ in this radial scalar setting appears to be available; the broader program of nuclear DFT foundations remains an active and unresolved area.

original_question: Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?
self_contained_problem:
An obstacle representation of a simple graph G = (V, E) consists of an injective placement P : V → ℝ² of the vertices as points in the plane together with a finite collection Q of pairwise disjoint connected polygonal regions in the plane (the obstacles), disjoint from P(V), such that for any two distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, the open straight-line segment connecting P(u) and P(v) is disjoint from every obstacle in Q if and only if uv ∈ E. The obstacle number obs(G) of G is the minimum cardinality of Q over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every graph G on n vertices satisfies obs(G) ≤ C·n? Equivalently, is the obstacle number of an n-vertex graph bounded above by a linear function of n?

No linear upper bound for general (polygonal) obstacles has been established.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: Let Φ be a simple intrinsic nuclear state, such as a Slater determinant or Hartree-Bogoliubov state, from which rotationally projected states ΦJMK are built by angular-momentum projection. Define an intrinsic-density functional FJMK[ρ] by minimizing the projected-state energy over simple intrinsic states Φ with intrinsic density ρ; this functional depends on the allowed class of Φ and, a priori, on the angular-momentum labels J, M, and K. Under what conditions can the intrinsic state or intrinsic density be practically independent of J, M, and K so that one density ρ is valid for many projected rotational states, and how does such an intrinsic-density functional relate to the traditional three-dimensional nuclear energy density functionals used for deformed nuclei?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a many-body nuclear Hamiltonian acting on the antisymmetric Hilbert space of A nucleons. Consider a class S of "simple" intrinsic states Φ (for instance, Slater determinants or Hartree–Bogoliubov quasiparticle vacua), each carrying a one-body density ρ_Φ(r) (the diagonal of the one-body density matrix in coordinate space).

For Φ ∈ S and angular-momentum quantum numbers (J, M, K) with |M|, |K| ≤ J, let P^J_{MK} denote the standard angular-momentum projection operator onto the (J, M, K) sector, and define the projected state Φ_{JMK} = P^J_{MK} Φ together with the projected energy
   E[Φ; J, M, K] = ⟨Φ_{JMK} | H | Φ_{JMK}⟩ / ⟨Φ_{JMK} | Φ_{JMK}⟩,
assumed nonzero.

Define an intrinsic-density functional by the constrained minimization
   F_{JMK}[ρ] = inf { E[Φ; J, M, K] : Φ ∈ S, ρ_Φ = ρ },
and the projected ground-state energy in the class S by
   E_{JMK} = inf_ρ F_{JMK}[ρ].

A priori, both the minimizing intrinsic state Φ* = Φ*(J, M, K) and the minimizing density ρ* = ρ*(J, M, K) depend on (J, M, K) as well as on the chosen class S.

Problem. Determine general conditions on the Hamiltonian H and the class S of simple intrinsic states under which there exists a single intrinsic state Φ* ∈ S (equivalently, a single intrinsic density ρ*) that is, to within a controlled accuracy, an optimizer of F_{JMK} simultaneously for a large family of triples (J, M, K), so that one universal intrinsic density ρ* serves as the input for the projected energies of many rotational states. In addition, characterize precisely the relationship between such a (J, M, K)-independent intrinsic-density functional ρ ↦ F[ρ] and the conventional three-dimensional energy density functionals used to describe deformed nuclei (i.e., functionals of a symmetry-broken intrinsic density whose stationary points are interpreted as approximations to laboratory-frame rotational band energies).
status_search_result: The question of when projection-based intrinsic density functionals can be made (J, M, K)-independent and how they relate to standard symmetry-breaking 3D nuclear EDFs is a well-known open conceptual problem in nuclear DFT. Subsequent literature on multi-reference EDF, projection methods, and the foundations of nuclear DFT continues to discuss it without providing a general resolution; spurious self-interaction and singularities in restoration procedures have been identified as obstructions, but no general theorem characterizing the desired (J, M, K)-independence has been established.

original_question: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. An obstacle representation of $G$ consists of a set $P$ of $|V|$ points in general position in the plane (one for each vertex) together with a finite collection $Q$ of pairwise disjoint closed connected subsets of the plane (called obstacles), each disjoint from $P$, such that for any two distinct vertices $u,v\in V$ the open straight-line segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle in $Q$ if and only if $\{u,v\}\in E$. The obstacle number $\mathrm{obs}(G)$ of $G$ is the minimum cardinality of $Q$ over all obstacle representations $(P,Q)$ of $G$.

Define $f(n)=\max\{\mathrm{obs}(G): G \text{ is a graph on } n \text{ vertices}\}$. It is known that $f(n)=\Omega(n/\log^2 n)$. Improve this lower bound; that is, determine an asymptotically larger lower bound for $f(n)$, ideally matching (up to logarithmic factors) the known upper bound $f(n)=O(n\log n)$.
status_search_result: The lower bound has been improved several times since the original O(n/log² n) bound. Mukkamala, Pach, and Pálvölgyi (2012) improved it to Ω(n/log n); Dujmović and Morin (2015) gave Ω(n/(log log n)²); and Balko, Ganian, Hliněný, Pach, and Valtr (2022) further improved bounds in restricted settings (Ω(n/log log n) for simple-polygon obstacles, Ω(n) for convex obstacles). Thus the problem has been partially solved—improvements exist—but a tight bound matching the O(n log n) upper bound is still not established.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: For electronic atoms or molecules with local Coulomb interactions, a theorem states that the square root of an eigenstate density ρ(r) obeys a one-body equation driven by a local potential usqr, with eigenvalue given by the difference between the A-particle energy and the ground-state energy of the system with one particle removed. Nuclear interactions can be strongly nonlocal, but nuclear density functional theory commonly uses local or quasi-local ingredients such as local Kohn-Sham, effective, optical, and Hartree potentials. Is there a generic approximate local potential usqr that drives √ρ and is valid for many nuclei, and if so how would it relate to nuclear density functional theory?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider an A-body quantum system with Hamiltonian
  H = Σ_{i=1}^{A} (-ℏ²/2m) Δ_i + Σ_{i<j} v_{ij},
where v_{ij} may be a (possibly strongly nonlocal) two-body interaction. For any normalized eigenstate Ψ of H with energy E_A, define the one-body density
  ρ(r) = A ∫ |Ψ(r, r_2, …, r_A)|² dr_2 ⋯ dr_A.

Background result (local case). When v_{ij} is local (e.g., the Coulomb repulsion in atoms and molecules), there exists a local one-body potential u_sqr(r) such that the function √ρ satisfies the one-body Schrödinger-type equation
  [ -(ℏ²/2m) Δ + u_sqr(r) ] √ρ(r) = ε √ρ(r),
with eigenvalue ε = E_A − E_{A−1}^{gs}, where E_{A−1}^{gs} is the ground-state energy of the (A−1)-particle system obtained by removing one particle. The locality of v_{ij} is used in the proof, so a direct extension to nonlocal interactions is not available.

Question. For nuclear systems, where the interaction v_{ij} is generally nonlocal but where commonly used effective ingredients (Kohn–Sham, effective two-body forces, optical potentials, Hartree potentials) are local or quasi-local up to reasonable approximations:

Does there exist a generic approximate local potential u_sqr(r), expressible in a closed functional form valid across a wide range of nuclei, such that √ρ approximately satisfies
  [ -(ℏ²/2m) Δ + u_sqr(r) ] √ρ(r) ≈ (E_A − E_{A−1}^{gs}) √ρ(r) ?
If such a u_sqr exists, exhibit it and determine its precise relationship (e.g., as a functional derivative or a definite combination of mean-field, exchange, and correlation contributions) to the local or quasi-local potentials of nuclear density functional theory.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this question was located in the literature. The underlying theorem (existence of a local potential driving √ρ) is well known in the local-interaction setting (Levy–Perdew–Sahni and related works), but a generic approximate local u_sqr applicable to nuclei with nonlocal interactions, together with a precise tie-in to nuclear DFT, does not appear to have been established.

original_question: For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with vertex set V(G). An obstacle representation of G consists of a set P of |V(G)| distinct points in the plane, in bijection with V(G), together with a finite set Q of pairwise disjoint simply connected closed regions (obstacles) in the plane whose interiors are disjoint from P, such that for any two vertices u, v of G, the open straight-line segment between the points representing u and v avoids every obstacle in Q if and only if uv is an edge of G. The obstacle number obs(G) of G is the minimum cardinality of Q over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

For each integer h > 1, determine

   f(h) := min { |V(G)| : G is a finite simple graph with obs(G) = h }.

That is, find the smallest number of vertices of any graph whose obstacle number equals exactly h.
status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as open. Subsequent research has obtained partial results: small graphs requiring 2 obstacles have been identified (e.g., a 10-vertex graph K*_{5,5} and an 8-vertex example needing two obstacles), and lower/upper bounds on obstacle numbers in general have been studied (Mukkamala et al.; Alpert–Koch–Laison; Balko et al.). However, no closed-form expression for the minimum vertex count f(h) for general h > 1 appears to have been established.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: In a finite harmonic-oscillator shell-model construction, the neutron and proton densities are represented by finite density-polynomial coefficients, the Levy-Lieb density constraints and normalization constraint become algebraic polynomial equations in configuration-mixing coefficients, and eliminating constrained variables and survivor coefficients yields an implicit polynomial relation R(η, Cn1, …, CnNn, Cp1, …, CpNp) = 0 linking the minimal energy η to density parameters. What practical algebraic strategies can handle the resulting large multivariate polynomials, compare distinct polynomial relations R obtained from different finite-basis choices, extrapolate when direct calculations become too cumbersome, and make rigorous polynomial density functionals useful in larger nuclear models?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite-dimensional harmonic-oscillator shell-model setting for a nucleus with $N_n$ neutron and $N_p$ proton single-particle orbitals. Let the one-body neutron and proton densities $ho_n(\mathbf{r})$ and $ho_p(\mathbf{r})$ be expanded in a finite polynomial basis with real coefficients $C_{n,1},\dots,C_{n,N_n}$ and $C_{p,1},\dots,C_{p,N_p}$ respectively. For an $A$-body Hamiltonian $H$, define the Levy–Lieb constrained-search energy
$$\eta(ho_n,ho_p)=\inf_{\Psi	o(ho_n,ho_p)}\langle\Psi|H|\Psiangle,$$
where $\Psi$ ranges over antisymmetric many-body states in the chosen finite shell-model space whose one-body densities reproduce $ho_n,ho_p$. Express $\Psi$ via configuration-mixing coefficients; then the density-matching constraints and normalization conditions become a system of polynomial equations in those coefficients. After eliminating the constrained and surviving mixing variables (e.g.\ by Gröbner-basis or resultant methods), one obtains an implicit polynomial relation
$$R(\eta,\,C_{n,1},\dots,C_{n,N_n},\,C_{p,1},\dots,C_{p,N_p})=0$$
that plays the role of a rigorous (implicit) density functional whose minimization over the $C$'s yields the ground-state energy.

Develop practical algebraic strategies that:
(i) make the elimination tractable for the very large multivariate polynomials arising when $N_n,N_p$ grow;
(ii) allow rigorous comparison between two such polynomial relations $R$ and $R'$ obtained from different finite-basis truncations of the same physical system;
(iii) provide controlled extrapolation procedures yielding approximations to $\eta$ when direct symbolic computation of $R=0$ is infeasible;
(iv) embed the resulting rigorous polynomial density functionals into larger nuclear-structure calculations.

Either produce such algorithms with provable correctness/complexity guarantees, or prove obstructions to their existence.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open challenge concerning the practical handling of implicit polynomial density functionals derived from Levy–Lieb constrained search in finite shell-model spaces. No subsequent work resolving this set of algebraic-strategy questions in nuclear density functional theory was located.

original_question: Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a simple graph. An obstacle representation of G consists of:
(i) an injection P: V → ℝ² mapping the vertices of G to distinct points in the plane in general position, and
(ii) a finite set Q of pairwise-disjoint closed polygonal regions ("obstacles") in the plane, disjoint from P(V),
such that for any two distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, the open straight-line segment between P(u) and P(v) avoids every obstacle in Q if and only if {u, v} ∈ E. The obstacle number of G, denoted obs(G), is the minimum cardinality |Q| over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

Question: Does every planar graph G satisfy obs(G) ≤ 1?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Planar graphs with obstacle number 2 have been exhibited: the 1-skeleton of the icosahedron was shown to have obstacle number 2, refuting the conjecture that every planar graph has obstacle number at most 1. Smaller examples (such as the gyroelongated 4-bipyramid, on 10 vertices) have since been found. A related question — whether the obstacle number of planar graphs is bounded by an absolute constant — remains open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: Can the algebraic polynomial construction of nuclear density functionals, which eliminates density constraints in a finite configuration-mixing model to obtain an implicit energy-density relation, also provide the Kohn-Sham potential associated with the density functional?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a finite configuration-mixing model for a self-bound many-fermion system (e.g., a nucleus) in which a family of trial states $\{|\Psi_\alpha\rangle\}$ parameterized by a finite set of collective coordinates $\alpha = (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ produces, for each $\alpha$, an energy
$$E(\alpha) = \langle \Psi_\alpha | \hat H | \Psi_\alpha \rangle$$
and a one-body density
$$\rho_\alpha(\mathbf{r}) = \langle \Psi_\alpha | \hat\rho(\mathbf{r}) | \Psi_\alpha \rangle.$$
Assume that one can algebraically eliminate the parameters $\alpha$ between $E(\alpha)$ and $\rho_\alpha$ by a polynomial construction, i.e. one can find a polynomial relation
$$P\big(E,\, \rho(\cdot)\big) = 0$$
that implicitly defines an energy density functional $E[\rho]$ free of any explicit constraint relating $\rho$ to $\alpha$.

Question. Within this purely algebraic (polynomial-elimination) framework, can one also extract the Kohn–Sham potential
$$v_{\text{KS}}[\rho](\mathbf{r}) = \frac{\delta E[\rho]}{\delta \rho(\mathbf{r})}$$
associated with the implicitly defined functional $E[\rho]$? That is, does the algebraic construction yield not only the functional but also a constructive procedure for the corresponding local single-particle potential entering the Kohn–Sham equations whose ground-state density reproduces $\rho$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive published resolution of whether the algebraic polynomial-elimination construction of nuclear energy density functionals also yields the corresponding Kohn–Sham potential. The question is described as having only preliminary results, and no later work explicitly settling it was located. General literature on inverse Kohn–Sham mappings and density-potential mappings exists but does not address this specific algebraic-polynomial setting.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \{s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n\}$ be a finite set of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $P = \{p_1, p_2, \dots, p_{2n}\}$ be the set of their endpoints. Two points $p_i, p_j \in P$ are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment joining $p_i$ and $p_j$ does not intersect any segment in $S$. The segment (endpoint) visibility graph of $S$ is the graph $G(S)$ on vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_{2n}\}$ (with $v_i$ corresponding to $p_i$) in which $v_i v_j$ is an edge if and only if either $p_i$ and $p_j$ are mutually visible, or $p_i$ and $p_j$ are the two endpoints of a common segment of $S$.

Problem: Design an algorithm that, given the adjacency matrix of an arbitrary finite simple graph $G$, decides whether there exists a set $S$ of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane such that $G \cong G(S)$. Equivalently, characterize the class of graphs that arise as segment endpoint visibility graphs of finite sets of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.
status_search_result: The recognition, characterization, and reconstruction problems for segment (endpoint) visibility graphs of disjoint line segments in the plane are reported as open in the computational-geometry literature. Only partial progress is known: a characterization exists for the subclass of segment visibility graphs without $K_5$ as a minor (Everett et al.), and it has been proven that every segment endpoint visibility graph is Hamiltonian (Hoffmann–Tóth). No general recognition algorithm or full characterization is known.
