paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let LENT_z be the operator ideal defined by the dyadic entropy-number condition (e_{2^k}(S)) ∈ z(N0). Determine whether LAPP_z is always contained in LENT_z for every shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. For an operator $S\colon X\to Y$ in $\mathcal{L}$, define:

- The $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-A\|:A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\},\qquad n=1,2,\dots$$
- The $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number
$$e_n(S):=\inf\Big\{\varepsilon>0:\exists\,y_1,\dots,y_{2^{n-1}}\in Y\ \text{with}\ S(B_X)\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{2^{n-1}}(y_j+\varepsilon B_Y)\Big\}.$$

A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ (the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$) that contains all eventually zero sequences and is solid in the usual sense. The sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if for every $(\xi_k)_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ the shifted sequence $(\xi_{k+1})_{k\ge 0}$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and conversely if a sequence and its left-shift coincide modulo membership conditions, the membership is preserved.

For a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the following classes of operators:
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}:=\{S\in\mathcal{L}:(a_{2^k}(S))_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\},$$
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z}:=\{S\in\mathcal{L}:(e_{2^k}(S))_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\}.$$
Both are operator ideals on the class of all Banach spaces.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$,
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}\ \subseteq\ \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z}.$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the listed Pietsch-style collection of open problems on traces and operator ideals (2023). Web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the inclusion $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\subseteq\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ for all shift-monotone sequence ideals. While classical inequalities relating entropy and approximation numbers (Carl, Triebel, Pietsch) are well known, no general resolution at the level of arbitrary shift-monotone sequence ideals appears in the indexed literature.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) for which the entropy-number ideal LENT_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of real (or complex) null sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if:
(i) it is solid: whenever $(a_k) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $(b_k) \in c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfies $|b_k| \le |a_k|$ for all $k$, then $(b_k) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(b_k)\| \le \|(a_k)\|$; and
(ii) it is invariant under the forward shift $S: (a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots) \mapsto (0, a_0, a_1, \dots)$ as well as under the backward shift $T: (a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots)\mapsto (a_1,a_2,\dots)$, both acting continuously on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

For an operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ between Banach spaces, the $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number $\varepsilon_n(T)$ is the infimum of all $\varepsilon>0$ such that the image of the unit ball of $X$ can be covered by $2^{n-1}$ closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ in $Y$. Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the entropy-number operator ideal
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z := \{\, T \in \mathcal{L} : (\varepsilon_n(T))_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\},$$
where $\mathcal{L}$ denotes the class of all bounded linear operators between arbitrary Banach spaces.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathcal{I}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ on the components $\mathcal{I}(X,X)$ (for every Banach space $X$) satisfying $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever the products make sense. The trace $\tau$ is called singular if it vanishes on every finite-rank operator.

Problem. Determine the shift-monotone sequence ideals $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for which the entropy-number operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ carries a non-vanishing singular trace.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. A web search did not reveal any subsequent work resolving the existence of non-vanishing singular traces on entropy-number ideals $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ for general shift-monotone sequence ideals $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. The status appears to remain open.

context_brief: Ample versus virtually ample versus weakly ample
original_question: What is the precise relationship among ample fields, virtually ample fields, and weakly ample fields? In particular, if a field K is called virtually ample when some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample when every K-curve C becomes infinite over some finite extension L/K, must every weakly ample field be virtually ample, and must every virtually ample field already be ample?
self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called ample (also known as large or anti-Mordellic) if every smooth $K$-curve $C$ with at least one $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points; equivalently, every geometrically integral $K$-variety with a smooth $K$-point has Zariski-dense $K$-rational points. Define two weakenings:

(i) $K$ is virtually ample if there exists a finite extension $L/K$ such that $L$ is ample.

(ii) $K$ is weakly ample if for every smooth geometrically integral $K$-curve $C$ there exists a finite extension $L/K$ (possibly depending on $C$) such that $C(L)$ is infinite.

Clearly every ample field is virtually ample, and every virtually ample field is weakly ample. Determine the precise relationship between these three classes by answering the following:

(a) Is every weakly ample field virtually ample?

(b) Is every virtually ample field already ample?
status_search_result: Part (b) has been answered negatively: Bary-Soroker, Fehm and Petersen, and subsequently Srinivasan ("A virtually ample field that is not ample", Israel J. Math., arXiv:1810.05184), constructed a virtually ample field that is not ample. Part (a) — whether every weakly ample field is virtually ample — does not appear to have a published resolution and seems to remain open.

original_question: Is every radically closed field ample, where radically closed means that the multiplicative group K^times of the field is divisible?
self_contained_problem:
Recall the following definitions.

(1) A field $K$ is called radically closed if its multiplicative group $K^{\times}$ is divisible; equivalently, for every $a \in K^{\times}$ and every positive integer $n$, the equation $x^{n}=a$ has a solution in $K$.

(2) A field $K$ is called ample (also large) if every smooth geometrically integral $K$-variety that has a $K$-rational point has a Zariski-dense set of $K$-rational points. Equivalently, every smooth $K$-curve with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

Question: Is every radically closed field ample?

original_question: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large families Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ LAPP_z(X,Y) is injective on Z.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under coordinatewise multiplication by bounded sequences (so that the usual ideal property holds). Such a sequence ideal is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ such that:

(a) the unit-vector basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ generates $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ in a suitable sense and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural pointwise order on nonnegative non-increasing sequences;

(b) shift-monotonicity holds: for every sequence $a=(a_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every $k\geq 0$, the shifted sequence $S_k a = (a_{n+k})$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|S_k a\|_z \le \|a\|_z$.

For parameters $0<r<\infty$ and a non-increasing weight $w=(w_n)\in c_0\setminus\ell_1$ with $w_0=1$, the Lorentz-type sequence ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is defined by
$$d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0) = \Big\{ a=(a_n) : \|a\|_{d_{r,w}} := \Big(\sum_{n=0}^\infty w_n\, a_n^{*\,r}\Big)^{1/r} <\infty \Big\},$$
where $(a_n^*)$ denotes the non-increasing rearrangement of $(|a_n|)$.

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$, the operator ideal of approximable operators of type $z$ is
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y) :=  ig\{ T\in \mathcal{L}(X,Y) : (a_n(T))_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)  ig\},$$
endowed with its natural quasi-norm, where $a_n(T)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number of $T$.

Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$. Determine large families $\mathcal{Z}$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals satisfying:

(i) every Lorentz-type ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ belongs to $\mathcal{Z}$;

(ii) the assignment $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \mapsto \mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ is injective on $\mathcal{Z}$, i.e. distinct members of $\mathcal{Z}$ give rise to distinct operator-ideal components $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2023 work on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. No subsequent literature appears to resolve the injectivity question for $z\mapsto \mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ on a family containing all Lorentz-type sequence ideals $d_{r,w}$, so it appears to remain open.

original_question: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X that have few approximable operators, in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than the cone c0*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences; ideally, make app(X) as small as possible.
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the cone of all nonincreasing null sequences of nonnegative real numbers, equipped with the dominance preorder $\sigma \preccurlyeq \tau$ meaning $\sigma_n \le \tau_n$ for all $n$. For a bounded linear operator $S$ between Banach spaces, let $a_n(S)$ denote its $n$-th approximation number, defined by
$$a_n(S) = \inf\{\|S - F\| : F \text{ has rank} < n\}.$$
For an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$, let $\mathcal{C}_0(X)$ denote the set of all bounded linear operators $S : X \to X$ whose approximation numbers form a null sequence, and define
$$\mathrm{app}(X) := \{(\sigma_n) \in c_0^*(\mathbb{N}) : \sigma_n \preccurlyeq a_n(S) \text{ for some } S \in \mathcal{C}_0(X)\}.$$
We say $X$ has *few approximable operators* if $\mathrm{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$.

Problem: Exhibit infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ that have few approximable operators, and make the set $\mathrm{app}(X)$ as small as possible.

original_question: Is every minimal field algebraically closed, where an infinite field K is called minimal when every subset A of K definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings is finite or cofinite?
self_contained_problem: Work in the first-order language of rings $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{ring}} = \{+,-,\cdot,0,1\}$. An infinite field $K$ is called minimal if every subset $A \subseteq K$ that is definable by a first-order $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{ring}}$-formula with parameters from $K$ is either finite or cofinite in $K$. Prove or disprove: every minimal field is algebraically closed.
status_search_result: Podewski's conjecture is known to hold in positive characteristic (Wagner) and for large fields (Koenigsmann), and has been reduced to a partially ordered case with the almost-linear subcase resolved. The characteristic zero case remains open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence and nevertheless have few approximable operators in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than c0*(N).
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $\mathcal{L}(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. Denote by $\mathrm{App}(X)$ the closed two-sided ideal of approximable operators on $X$, that is, the closure in the operator norm of the ideal of finite-rank operators on $X$. Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the operator ideal consisting of all bounded linear operators $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ whose sequence of approximation numbers $(a_n(T))_{n=1}^\infty$ tends to $0$, where 
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : F \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}.$$
One says that $X$ has few approximable operators if $\mathrm{App}(X)$ is strictly smaller than $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$ (i.e., there exists a bounded operator on $X$ whose approximation numbers tend to zero but which is not a norm limit of finite-rank operators).

Exhibit an example of an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ that simultaneously satisfies:
(i) $X$ contains an infinite unconditional basic sequence; and
(ii) $X$ has few approximable operators, i.e., $\mathrm{App}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals. Related constructions exist: Argyros and Deliyanni built spaces with few operators that fail to contain unconditional basic sequences, while Argyros's later "sequentially unconditional Banach space with few operators" (Proc. London Math. Soc., 2005) provides a space where every operator is a strictly singular perturbation of a multiple of the identity and which contains unconditional basic sequences. Whether that or a similar construction strictly separates $\mathrm{App}(X)$ from $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$ is not clearly settled by the sources retrieved, so the status with respect to the precise formulation is not definitively established.

context_brief: Non-ample fields satisfying the Debes-Deschamps conjecture
original_question: Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes-Deschamps conjecture holds?
self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called ample (or large) if every smooth $K$-curve with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points; equivalently, $K$ is existentially closed in the Laurent series field $K((t))$. A finite embedding problem over $K$ is a pair $(\alpha\colon \mathrm{Gal}(K)\twoheadrightarrow A,\ f\colon B\twoheadrightarrow A)$ consisting of a continuous surjection from the absolute Galois group of $K$ onto a finite group $A$ and a surjection of finite groups $f\colon B\to A$. The problem is split if $f$ admits a group-theoretic section. A regular solution of such an embedding problem is a Galois extension $F/K(z)$ (with $z$ transcendental over $K$) of group $B$, regular over $K$ (i.e.\ $F\cap \overline{K}=K$), together with an isomorphism $\mathrm{Gal}(F/K(z))\cong B$ compatible with $\alpha$ and $f$ via the canonical surjection $\mathrm{Gal}(K(z))\to \mathrm{Gal}(K)$. The Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture asserts that every finite split embedding problem over every field $K$ has a regular solution.

Question: Does there exist a non-ample field $K$ such that every finite split embedding problem over $K$ admits a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field $K$ for which the Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture holds?
status_search_result: The Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture is known to hold for ample (large) fields and over rational function fields of one variable over ample fields, but for non-ample fields it remains unproven and no example of a non-ample field satisfying the full conjecture appears in the literature. Surveys on the regular inverse Galois problem and embedding problems indicate the question remains open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let X_K be the C0-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of ℓ1 mentioned in Section 2.9, and let τ_Z be the continuous singular trace on N(2/3,Z) constructed in Theorem 2.26. Describe the restriction of τ_Z to the operator ideal N(2/3,X_K)(ℓ2).
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) For Banach spaces $E,F$ and $0<r\le 1$, an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ is called $r$-nuclear if it admits a representation $S=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} a_i\, x_i^*\otimes y_i$ with $x_i^*\in E^*$, $y_i\in F$, $\|x_i^*\|\le 1$, $\|y_i\|\le 1$, and $(a_i)\in\ell_r$. The class of all $r$-nuclear operators forms a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}_r$.

(b) Given a Banach space $Z$, the factor ideal $\mathcal{N}_r^{Z}$ consists of all operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ that admit a factorization $S=BTA$ with $A\in\mathcal{L}(E,Z)$, $T\in\mathcal{N}_r(Z,Z)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Z,F)$. We write $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)$ for this ideal and $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)(\ell_2)$ for its component on $\ell_2$, i.e. the operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$ admitting such a factorization through $Z$.

(c) A Banach space $Z$ is called $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial (in the sense relevant here) if every operator on $Z$ has the form $\lambda I_Z + K$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $K$ compact, equivalently if the Calkin algebra $\mathcal{L}(Z)/\mathcal{K}(Z)$ is one-dimensional. The Argyros–Haydon construction provides such a Banach space $X_K$ which is moreover a predual of $\ell_1$ and possesses a Schauder basis.

(d) Fix $r=2/3$ and an $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Banach space $Z$. For $S\in\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)(Z,Z)$, choose any factorization $S=\sum_{i} U_i T_i V_i$ with $T_i\in\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$ such that the canonical scalar $\varphi(U_iV_i)$ (the unique scalar $\lambda_i$ with $U_iV_i-\lambda_i I_Z$ compact, extracted via the trivial Calkin algebra of $Z$) is well defined. Then the formula
$$ \tau_Z(S)\;:=\;\sum_{i} \varphi(U_iV_i)\,\operatorname{tr}(T_i) $$
defines a continuous singular trace on the quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)$ (here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the standard nuclear trace on $\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$, which is well defined because $2/3\le 2/3$).

Problem. Take $Z=X_K$, the $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of $\ell_1$. Give an explicit description of the restriction of the trace $\tau_{X_K}$ to the ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2)$ of operators on $\ell_2$ that factor (in the sense above) through $X_K$ via a $2/3$-nuclear middle operator. In particular, identify this restriction in terms of standard traces (the operator trace, Dixmier-type singular traces, etc.) on the corresponding ideal in $\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem ("Problem 23") in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No subsequent paper resolving the description of $\tau_{X_K}$ restricted to $\mathcal{N}(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2)$ was located, so the problem appears still open.

original_question: Consider the family of elliptic one-variable germs f_{lambda,a}(z)=lambda z+z^2 g_a(z), where |lambda|=1 and lambda is not a root of unity. Find concrete families for which holomorphic linearizability is equivalent to lambda satisfying the Brjuno condition, and in particular determine whether every elliptic polynomial (or at least every elliptic cubic polynomial) is holomorphically linearizable exactly when its multiplier is a Brjuno number.
self_contained_problem:
A holomorphic germ at the origin in one complex variable is a power series f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + ⋯ converging in a neighborhood of 0, fixing 0 with multiplier f'(0) = λ. The germ is called elliptic if |λ| = 1 and λ is not a root of unity. The germ f is said to be holomorphically linearizable at 0 if there exists a local biholomorphism φ with φ(0) = 0 such that φ ∘ f ∘ φ^{-1}(z) = λz. Writing λ = e^{2π i θ} with θ ∈ ℝ ∖ ℚ, and letting p_n / q_n denote the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of θ, the number λ (equivalently θ) is said to satisfy the Brjuno condition if 
   ∑_{n ≥ 0} (log q_{n+1}) / q_n < ∞.

Consider parameterized families of elliptic germs of the form
   f_{λ, a}(z) = λ z + z^2 g_a(z),
where a ranges over a parameter space M and g_a is holomorphic near 0 with g_a(0) ≠ 0 (in particular, M may be a space of polynomials of fixed degree).

Problem.
(a) Exhibit explicit nontrivial families {f_{λ, a}}_{a ∈ M} of elliptic one-variable holomorphic germs such that, for every a ∈ M, f_{λ, a} is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if λ satisfies the Brjuno condition.

(b) In particular, decide whether the following statement is true: every elliptic polynomial f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + ⋯ + a_d z^d (with |λ| = 1, λ not a root of unity, a_d ≠ 0) is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if its multiplier λ is a Brjuno number.

(c) Decide the same question restricted to the cubic case: is every elliptic cubic polynomial f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 (with a_3 ≠ 0) holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if λ is a Brjuno number?
status_search_result: Yoccoz (1995) established that for the quadratic family z ↦ λz + z^2 the Brjuno condition is both necessary and sufficient for holomorphic linearizability; the analogous optimality (necessity of Brjuno) for general polynomial families of degree ≥ 3, including the elliptic cubic case, is widely cited as still open in surveys on small divisors in discrete local holomorphic dynamics. No solution for degree ≥ 3 polynomials was found in the search.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let LLEX_z = H ◦ LWEYL_z be the old-fashioned left-hand extension ideal built from operators factoring through Hilbert spaces. Determine whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞}, or even the smaller ideal LAPP_{1,∞}, fails to be contained in LLEX_{1,∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between (complex) Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ assigns to every pair of Banach spaces $X,Y$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ that is stable under composition with bounded operators on either side and contains the finite-rank operators. A quasi-Banach operator ideal is an operator ideal equipped with a complete quasi-norm respecting the ideal structure.

For a bounded sequence $(s_n)$ of non-negative reals, the Lorentz quasi-norm of type $(r,\infty)$ is
$$\|(s_n)\|_{r,\infty} := \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} s_n^*,$$
where $(s_n^*)$ is the non-increasing rearrangement. For an operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, denote by $a_n(T)$ the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:\ F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},$$
and by $x_n(T)$ the $n$-th Weyl number
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(T A):\ A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$

Define the following quasi-Banach operator ideals:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(a_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$, quasi-normed by $\|T\|_{\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}}=\|(a_n(T))\|_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(x_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{LAPP}_{r,\infty}$ and $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$: the "left-sided" versions, defined as the components $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ obtained by composing on the right with arbitrary bounded operators (equivalently, the largest ideals whose Hilbert-space components coincide with those of $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$ resp. $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$ via factorization through arbitrary Banach spaces on the left and $\ell_2$ on the right).
\item $\mathfrak{H}$: the ideal of operators that factor through some Hilbert space.
\item $\mathrm{LLEX}_{r,\infty} := \mathfrak{H}\circ\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$, the "left-hand extension" ideal.
\end{itemize}

Product ideals are defined componentwise via factorization: $T\in\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)$ iff $T=AB$ with $B\in\mathfrak{B}(X,Z)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,Y)$ for some Banach space $Z$.

Problem. Show that the operator ideal $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{2,\infty}\circ\mathrm{APP}_{2,\infty}$ is not contained in $\mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}$. More strongly, show that even
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}\ \not\subseteq\ \mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}.$$
Equivalently, exhibit Banach spaces $X,Y$ and an operator $T\in\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}(X,Y)$ that does not admit a factorization $T=A_2 A_1$ with $A_1\in\mathrm{LWEYL}_{1,\infty}$ and $A_2$ factoring through a Hilbert space.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. A web search did not return any subsequent paper resolving the inclusion question for LAPP_{1,∞} versus LLEX_{1,∞}, so the problem appears still open.

context_brief: Regularity of log r plus Brjuno
original_question: Let B(theta) be the Brjuno function and r(theta) the infimum of radii of convergence of linearizations for injective germs on the unit disk with multiplier e^{2 pi i theta}. Does the function log r(theta)+B(theta) extend from irrational theta to all theta in [0,1) as a 1/2-Holder continuous function?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$. For $\theta\in[0,1)$, let
$$r(\theta)=\inf\{\,r(f)\mid f\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C},0)\text{ is defined and injective on }\mathbb{D}\text{ with }f'(0)=e^{2\pi i\theta}\,\},$$
where $r(f)$ is the radius of convergence of the (formal) linearization of $f$ at $0$ (with the convention that $r(f)=0$ when $f$ is not linearizable). 

Let $B:[0,1)\to[0,+\infty]$ be the Brjuno function, defined for irrational $\theta$ by
$$B(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\beta_{n-1}(\theta)\log\frac{1}{\theta_n},$$
where $\theta_0=\theta$, $\theta_{n+1}=\{1/\theta_n\}$, $\beta_{-1}=1$, and $\beta_n=\theta_0\theta_1\cdots\theta_n$. The Brjuno numbers are precisely those $\theta$ for which $B(\theta)<\infty$, equivalently those for which $r(\theta)>0$.

The function $\theta\mapsto \log r(\theta)+B(\theta)$ is therefore well defined and finite on the set of Brjuno numbers in $[0,1)$. 

Question: Does $\log r(\theta)+B(\theta)$ extend from the set of Brjuno numbers in $[0,1)$ to a $\tfrac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous function on all of $[0,1)$?
status_search_result: Buff and Chéritat (2006) proved that for quadratic polynomials the analogous function $\log r(\alpha)+Y(\alpha)$ extends continuously to $\mathbb{R}$, but no $1/2$-Hölder continuous extension is known. For the general univalent-germ setting with $r(\theta)$ defined by an infimum over all injective germs on the unit disk, the $1/2$-Hölder regularity question appears to remain open; it is consistent with conjectural "universality up to a 1/2-Hölder function" suggested by Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz, but no proof is recorded in the literature found.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find operator ideals, different from the examples furnished by Theorems 2.26 and 2.27, that support non-vanishing traces.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y) \subseteq \mathfrak{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathfrak{A}$;
(ii) for all Banach spaces $W,X,Y,Z$ and all $B\in\mathfrak{L}(W,X)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$, $C\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,Z)$, the composition $CAB$ lies in $\mathfrak{A}(W,Z)$.

A trace on $\mathfrak{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X : \mathfrak{A}(X,X) \to \mathbb{C}$, defined for every Banach space $X$, satisfying:
(a) $\tau_X(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes x^*\otimes x) = \langle x, x^*\rangle$ for all rank-one operators on $X$ (equivalently, $\tau$ extends the standard trace on finite-rank operators);
(b) the trace property: $\tau_Y(AB) = \tau_X(BA)$ whenever $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,X)$ (or, more generally, whenever both compositions lie in the relevant ideal components).

A trace $\tau$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to be non-vanishing if $\tau$ is not identically zero on $\mathfrak{A}$.

It is known that non-vanishing traces exist on certain operator ideals, e.g. on the ideal of nuclear operators (where the spectral / Grothendieck–Lidskii trace need not vanish), and on certain ideals constructed via specific shift-invariant sequence space methods.

Problem. Exhibit operator ideals defined on the class of all Banach spaces, distinct from the previously known examples (the nuclear-type ideals and ideals built from the standard sequence-ideal/shift-invariant-functional construction), that support a non-vanishing trace in the sense above.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. Web searches do not reveal subsequent work exhibiting genuinely new operator ideals (beyond the nuclear-type and sequence-ideal-based constructions) supporting non-vanishing traces. Construction of non-vanishing traces on Banach-space operator ideals remains a notably difficult area, and the problem appears to still be open.

original_question: For elliptic non-linearizable one-variable germs (Cremer points), are the pair of invariants consisting of (i) the multiplier and (ii) the homeomorphism class of the germ of the stable set at the origin a complete set of topological invariants for topological local conjugacy?
self_contained_problem:
Let f: (ℂ,0) → (ℂ,0) be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, written near 0 as f(z) = λz + O(z²), with multiplier λ = f'(0). Assume that 0 is a Cremer point of f, meaning that |λ| = 1, λ is not a root of unity, and f is not holomorphically (equivalently, formally) linearizable at 0; in particular, f is not holomorphically conjugate to the rotation z ↦ λz on any neighborhood of 0.

For such a germ, define the stable set at 0 by
   K(f) = { z ∈ U : f^n(z) is defined and remains in U for all n ≥ 0 },
where U is a sufficiently small neighborhood of 0; the germ at 0 of K(f) is independent of the choice of U.

Two germs f, g ∈ End(ℂ,0) are said to be topologically locally conjugate if there exists a germ of a homeomorphism h: (ℂ,0) → (ℂ,0) such that h ∘ f = g ∘ h as germs at 0.

Question: Is it true that for any two holomorphic germs f, g ∈ End(ℂ,0) with Cremer points at 0, f and g are topologically locally conjugate if and only if
  (i) their multipliers f'(0) and g'(0) coincide, and
  (ii) the germs at 0 of their stable sets K(f) and K(g) are homeomorphic?

In other words, do the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the germ of the stable set form a complete set of topological invariants for local topological conjugacy in the Cremer case?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this question. Topological classification at Cremer fixed points remains poorly understood; even basic structural questions about hedgehogs and stable sets at Cremer points are still under active investigation (e.g., recent work on hedgehogs for neutral dissipative germs), and no source claims that the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the stable set form a complete set of topological invariants. The question is best classified as open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: For every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), determine whether there always exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that the reiteration identity (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z holds.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_x$ making it a quasi-Banach space, and satisfying the usual ideal property (it contains all finitely supported sequences and is closed under coordinate-wise multiplication by bounded sequences with $\|(\lambda_n a_n)\|_x\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\,\|(a_n)\|_x$). It is called shift-monotone if the forward and backward shift operators act boundedly on it and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural shift partial order (equivalently, $\|(a_{n+1})\|_x\le\|(a_n)\|_x$).
 
A quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}=(\mathfrak A(E,F),\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A})$ assigns to each pair of Banach spaces $(E,F)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak A(E,F)$ of bounded operators, complete under a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A}$ dominating the operator norm, with the usual ideal axioms (containing finite-rank operators and being closed under composition with bounded operators on either side).
 
For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, define the approximation procedure $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{x}$ as the class of all bounded operators $T:E\to F$ between Banach spaces such that there exists a sequence $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ of operators with $T_n\in\mathfrak A(E,F)$ for all $n$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A}<\infty$, and the sequence of approximation-type numbers $(\|T-T_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the natural quasi-norm
$$\|T\|_{\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x}:=\inf\big\{\max(\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A},\,\|(\|T-T_n\|)_n\|_x)\big\},$$
the infimum running over all such sequences $(T_n)$. Then $\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x$ is again a quasi-Banach operator ideal.
 
Problem. Prove or disprove: for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak A$ and every pair $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, $y(\mathbb{N}_0)$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the reiteration identity
$$\big(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x\big)^{\mathrm{APP}}_y \;=\; \mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$$
holds (with equivalent quasi-norms).
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly listed open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. No web evidence was found indicating that a resolution of this generalized reiteration identity for approximation procedures has been published; it appears to remain open.

original_question: Given two one-variable germs tangent to the identity (multiplier 1), provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that determines whether they are holomorphically locally conjugated.
self_contained_problem:
A germ of one-variable holomorphic diffeomorphism tangent to the identity is an equivalence class, under agreement near the origin, of holomorphic maps $f:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ whose Taylor expansion at $0$ has the form $f(z)=z+a_{k+1}z^{k+1}+a_{k+2}z^{k+2}+\cdots$ with $k\ge 1$ (so $f'(0)=1$). Two such germs $f$ and $g$ are said to be holomorphically locally conjugate if there exists a germ of biholomorphism $h:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$ as germs at $0$.

The Écalle–Voronin theorem provides a complete set of analytic invariants (the multiplicity $k+1$, the residual constant, and the horn-map data) classifying such germs up to holomorphic local conjugacy. However, these invariants are functional moduli, defined via Fatou coordinates, and are not given by a finite computation in the Taylor coefficients.

Problem: Provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that, given two convergent power series $f(z)=z+\sum_{n\ge k+1}a_n z^n$ and $g(z)=z+\sum_{n\ge k+1}b_n z^n$ representing germs tangent to the identity (specified by an algorithm producing their Taylor coefficients to arbitrary order, together with explicit bounds expressing convergence), decides in finite time whether $f$ and $g$ are holomorphically locally conjugate.
status_search_result: The classification of one-variable parabolic germs up to holomorphic local conjugacy is given by the Écalle–Voronin functional moduli (multiplicity, residual constant, and horn maps). While numerical schemes (e.g., resurgent/Borel-summation methods, parabolic renormalization) can compute these invariants as convergent series, we found no published work providing a finite, effective decision procedure that takes two tangent-to-identity germs as input and decides holomorphic local conjugacy. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find a shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) for which the two equivalent quasi-norms on LAPP_z discussed in Theorem 1.4, namely ‖·|LAPP_z‖ and |||·|LAPP_z|||, are genuinely different on at least one operator S ∈ LAPP_z(X,Y).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of eventually zero scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A quasi-normed sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded sequences containing $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\,|z\|$ that makes it complete (or at least quasi-normed) and that satisfies the ideal property: for every $\xi=(\xi_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every bounded sequence $(\lambda_n)$, the pointwise product $(\lambda_n\xi_n)$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(\lambda_n\xi_n)\,|z\|\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\cdot\|\xi\,|z\|$.

For $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$ let $\sigma_k:\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}\to\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ denote the right-shift defined by $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=\xi_{n-k}$ for $n\ge k$ and $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=0$ for $n<k$. The ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if $\sigma_k$ maps $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ into itself for every $k\ge 0$ and the operator quasi-norms $c_k:=\|\sigma_k:z\to z\|$ satisfy $c_k\to 0$ as well as $c_0=1$ (more precisely, the standard shift-monotonicity assumption $\|\sigma_k\xi\,|z\|\le c_k\|\xi\,|z\|$ with $c_k\downarrow 0$ as $k\to\infty$ -- equivalently, the canonical embedding $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\hookrightarrow c_0$ is bounded and shifts contract suitably).

Approximation numbers. For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $S:X\to Y$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L:X\to Y \text{ linear, } \mathrm{rank}\,L<n\}, \qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.$$
Set $\alpha_n(S):=a_{n+1}(S)$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, so that $\alpha_0(S)=\|S\|\ge \alpha_1(S)\ge \alpha_2(S)\ge\cdots$.

The approximation operator ideal associated with $z$. Define
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y):=\{S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y): (\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\}$$
and equip it with the quasi-norm
$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|:=\bigl\|(\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|.$$
A second quasi-norm is defined by means of finite-rank approximations: with $\mathcal{F}_{<n}(X,Y)$ the set of bounded linear operators of rank strictly less than $n$,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\bigl\|(\beta_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|, \quad \text{where } \beta_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\text{ attains a rank-}n\text{ optimal-type form}\},$$
the second quantity being the natural "ideal-internal" quasi-norm obtained by replacing the scalar infimum defining $\alpha_n$ with the $z$-quasi-norm of the residual sequences; equivalently,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\inf\bigl\{\bigl\|(\|S-L_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|: L_n\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $\|\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|$ and $|||\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||$ are equivalent quasi-norms on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for every quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

Problem. Exhibit a quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, Banach spaces $X,Y$, and an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for which the two quasi-norms are not equal, that is,
$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|\;\neq\;|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||.$$
Equivalently, determine whether the two equivalent quasi-norms can fail to coincide, and produce an explicit example if so.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific problem about producing a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for which the two equivalent quasi-norms on the approximation-type operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ differ on some operator. The problem is listed among open problems in the literature on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces, with no follow-up solution found.

original_question: Given two one-variable parabolic germs (multiplier a root of unity), provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that determines whether they are holomorphically locally conjugated.
self_contained_problem:
A one-variable parabolic germ is a germ at $0\in\mathbb{C}$ of a holomorphic map $f:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ of the form $f(z)=\lambda z + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + \cdots$, where the multiplier $\lambda=f'(0)$ is a root of unity. Two such germs $f$ and $g$ are said to be holomorphically locally conjugate if there exists a germ of a biholomorphism $h:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ such that $h\circ f = g\circ h$ as germs at $0$.

The Écalle–Voronin theory provides a complete set of analytic invariants (the formal invariants together with the Écalle–Voronin moduli) classifying parabolic germs up to holomorphic local conjugacy, but these moduli are functional in nature and not directly amenable to comparison from finite data such as Taylor coefficients.

Problem. Provide an effective and implementable decision procedure which, given as input the (truncated, computable) Taylor expansions of two one-variable parabolic germs $f$ and $g$ at $0$ whose multipliers are roots of unity, decides in finitely many steps whether $f$ and $g$ are holomorphically locally conjugate.
status_search_result: No published source presents an effective/implementable algorithm deciding holomorphic local conjugacy of parabolic germs from Taylor data. The classification via Écalle–Voronin moduli is well-known, but turning it into a finite decision procedure is not addressed in the literature found. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
context_brief: Distance complexity in discrete time-tree graphs
original_question: A discrete time-tree is a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on a fixed labeled leaf set in which every node is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time and each child has smaller time than its parent. The paper studies graph families on such trees, including DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, and RNNIu, where two trees are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by one allowed local move such as changing the length of one event interval by 1, swapping the ranks of two nodes that bound a unit-length interval, or performing a nearest-neighbor interchange move on a unit-length interval, with graph-specific restrictions. Given two discrete time-trees in one of these graph families, what is the computational complexity of computing their graph distance, meaning the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform one tree into the other?
status_search_result: The complexity of computing the RNNI distance has been resolved: Collienne and Gavryushkin (published 2021) gave an O(n^2)-time algorithm (FINDPATH) for computing shortest paths in the RNNI graph, and the same approach extends to RNNIu. However, related variants remain hard: with rank moves only (RNNI(0)) the problem is NP-hard, and the complexity for the full DtTm and DtTum graphs (which include integer length moves on event intervals) does not appear to have been settled. Thus the original problem is partially solved.

context_brief: Asymptotic attraction rate in higher dimensions
original_question: Let f in End(C^n,O) be non-invertible and dominant, let c(f^k) be the order of the k-th iterate, and let c_infinity(f)=lim_{k->+infinity} c(f^k)^{1/k}. Must c_infinity(f) always be an algebraic integer of degree at most n? Equivalently, do there always exist integers a_0,...,a_{n-1} such that c_infinity^n + a_{n-1} c_infinity^{n-1} + ... + a_0 = 0, and does there always exist delta in (0,1] with delta c_infinity^k <= c(f^k) <= c_infinity^k for all k >= 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, and assume $f$ is non-invertible (i.e.\ its differential at $O$ is not invertible) and dominant (i.e.\ its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically). Denote by $\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n,O}$ the maximal ideal of the local ring of holomorphic germs at $O$, and for any holomorphic germ $g:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ define the order
$$c(g)=\min\{\,k\geq 0 : g^*\mathfrak{m}\not\subset\mathfrak{m}^{k+1}\,\}=\sup\{\,k\geq 0 : g^*\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}^{k}\,\}.$$
For the iterates $f^k=f\circ\cdots\circ f$ ($k$ times) one has the submultiplicativity $c(f^{k+l})\geq c(f^k)\,c(f^l)$, which guarantees that the asymptotic attraction rate
$$c_\infty(f)=\lim_{k\to+\infty} c(f^k)^{1/k}\in[1,+\infty)$$
exists.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(a) The number $c_\infty(f)$ is an algebraic integer of degree at most $n$; that is, there exist integers $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1}\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$c_\infty(f)^n + a_{n-1}\,c_\infty(f)^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1\,c_\infty(f)+a_0 = 0.$$

(b) There exists a constant $\delta\in(0,1]$ (depending on $f$) such that
$$\delta\,c_\infty(f)^k \leq c(f^k) \leq c_\infty(f)^k\qquad\text{for every integer } k\geq 1.$$
status_search_result: For $n=2$, work of Favre–Jonsson on eigenvaluations established that $c_\infty(f)$ is a quadratic integer and the two-sided estimate holds. In higher dimensions $n\geq 3$, only partial generalizations are known (e.g., for monomial or rigid germs, by Favre, Jonsson, Ruggiero and collaborators), and the general algebraicity and lower-bound questions appear to remain open.

paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
context_brief: Split theorem for ranked and timed tree graphs
original_question: Consider any of the discrete time-tree graph families DtT, DtTu, RNNI, or RNNIu on a fixed leaf set. Suppose two trees T and R share a split, meaning that each tree has an edge whose removal induces the same bipartition of the leaves. Must every shortest path from T to R in the chosen graph stay entirely within trees that continue to display that shared split?
self_contained_problem:
Let L be a fixed finite leaf set with |L| = n. A discrete time-tree on L is a rooted phylogenetic tree with leaves bijectively labelled by L, in which each internal node is assigned an integer "time" (rank) such that times strictly increase along every path from a leaf to the root. Consider the following four graphs whose vertices are such trees:

• DtT: discrete time-trees on L, where each internal node carries a positive integer time and ties between non-adjacent nodes are allowed.
• DtTu: the analogue of DtT in which all leaves are required to have time 0 ("ultrametric"/coalescent-style).
• RNNI: ranked nearest-neighbour-interchange graph, whose vertices are discrete time-trees in which the n−1 internal nodes have distinct ranks 1,…,n−1.
• RNNIu: the ultrametric variant of RNNI.

In each of these graphs, edges are given by the natural local moves: an NNI-style move that exchanges two subtrees adjacent to an interval between consecutive-rank internal nodes, and a "rank move" that swaps the ranks of two internal nodes whose ranks differ by one (plus, in DtT/DtTu, moves that change an integer time by one, when permitted). Distance d(T,R) is the length of a shortest path in the graph.

Given a tree T on L and an internal edge e of T, removing e disconnects T into two components and induces a bipartition (split) of L. Two trees T and R are said to share a split σ if each of them has an internal edge inducing the bipartition σ.

Question. Let G be any one of DtT, DtTu, RNNI, RNNIu. Suppose T and R are two vertices of G that share a split σ. Must every shortest path from T to R in G consist entirely of trees that also display σ?
status_search_result: A counterexample to the conjectured Split Theorem in the RNNI graph was found by Collienne (reported on the bioAI lab page describing Collienne's RNNI geometry paper). Thus the strong split-preservation statement is false in RNNI; a weaker version remains plausible but is not established.

original_question: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^n,O), does the integer sequence {c(f^k)}_{k in N} satisfy, at least for all sufficiently large k, a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon (\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, and define its order at the origin by
$$c(f)=\min\bigl\{\,\mathrm{ord}_O(f_j) \,:\, j=1,\dots,n\,\bigr\},$$
where $\mathrm{ord}_O(f_j)$ is the lowest degree of a non-zero homogeneous term in the Taylor expansion of $f_j$ at $O$. Assume that $f$ is dominant (i.e.\ its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically) and non-invertible (i.e.\ $c(f)\ge 2$). For each positive integer $k$ let $f^k=f\circ\cdots\circ f$ denote the $k$-fold iterate, and consider the integer sequence $\{c(f^k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $K\ge 1$, an integer $r\ge 1$, and integers $a_1,\dots,a_r$ such that
$$c(f^{k+r}) = a_1\,c(f^{k+r-1}) + a_2\,c(f^{k+r-2}) + \cdots + a_r\,c(f^{k})$$
holds for all $k\ge K$? In other words, must the sequence $\{c(f^k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ eventually satisfy a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source establishing or refuting the existence of an eventual linear integer recurrence for the order sequence $\{c(f^k)\}$ of iterates of a non-invertible dominant holomorphic germ in $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$. No follow-up work resolving this question was located, but absence of evidence is not evidence of resolution; the status is therefore recorded as unknown.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
context_brief: BRAVO for critically loaded finite-buffer GI/G/1/K queues
original_question: Consider a finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue with one server, renewal arrivals, independent and identically distributed service times, K-1 waiting places, and loss of customers who arrive when the system is full. In the critically loaded case λ = μ, where c_a^2 and c_s^2 denote the squared coefficients of variation of the inter-arrival and service times, does the queue exhibit the BRAVO effect (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs), and in particular, for light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, is the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* equal to (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (one server in service plus K−1 waiting positions). Customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2 := Var(inter-arrival)/(mean inter-arrival)^2. Service times are i.i.d., independent of arrivals, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. A customer who arrives to find the system full (K customers present) is lost; otherwise the customer joins the queue and is eventually served in FCFS order. Let D(t) denote the number of customers that have departed (completed service and left) by time t in stationarity, and define the long-run departure-process variability parameter
   γ*(K) := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / (μ t),
assumed to exist.

Assume the system is critically loaded, i.e. λ = μ, and assume that both the inter-arrival and the service time distributions are light-tailed (have finite moment generating functions in a neighborhood of zero).

Question. Does the BRAVO ("Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs") effect hold for this GI/G/1/K queue, and in particular is it true that
   γ*(K) = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)   as K → ∞ ?
status_search_result: The conjecture, posed for the critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue with light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, appears still open. paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: For the critically loaded finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue in Conjecture 1, what are the weakest distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service times under which the asymptotic formula γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) should hold? More specifically, if requiring light tails in the sense of an exponential moment is stronger than necessary, is there a sharper minimal condition, and is the existence of 2+ε moments sufficient or not?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (the GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ, variance σ_a², and squared coefficient of variation c_a² = λ²σ_a²; service times are i.i.d. with mean 1/μ, variance σ_s², and squared coefficient of variation c_s² = μ²σ_s²; arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost. Assume the system is critically loaded, i.e. ρ = λ/μ = 1. Let D(t) denote the number of departures (served customers) in [0, t], and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K = lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized variability parameter γ_K* = V_K / μ. It has been conjectured that, under suitable distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions,

   γ_K* = (1/3)(c_a² + c_s²) + O(1/K)   as K → ∞.

The original conjecture is stated under the assumption that both the inter-arrival and service distributions possess a finite exponential moment (i.e., are light-tailed). The problem is the following:

(a) Determine the weakest distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions under which the asymptotic formula above holds.

(b) In particular, decide whether the existence of 2+ε moments (for some ε > 0) on both inter-arrival and service time distributions is sufficient for the formula to hold, or whether some strictly stronger condition (weaker than an exponential moment but stronger than 2+ε moments) is necessary.
status_search_result: The conjectured 1/3 asymptotic variance formula for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues (BRAVO effect) is known and has been studied in several follow-up works (e.g., Hanbali–Mandjes–Nazarathy–Whitt on heavy-traffic GI/GI/1 departure variance, and recent 2024 work on phase transitions and generalized BRAVO). However, no source located in the search states a sharp minimal moment condition on the inter-arrival and service time distributions under which the (1/3)(c_a² + c_s²) + O(1/K) formula holds; the question of the minimal condition (and whether 2+ε moments suffice) appears to remain open.

original_question: Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n,O) with first nonzero homogeneous term H. If the postcritical set of f is a topological cone near the origin, under what conditions is f topologically locally conjugated to H, and specifically does this always hold when H is non-degenerate?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, written as the formal series $f = H + \text{(higher order terms)}$, where $H$ is the first non-zero homogeneous term in the expansion of $f$ (so $\deg H \geq 2$). Assume $f$ is superattracting at $O$, meaning $df_O = 0$. The critical set $C(f)$ is the analytic set $\{z : \det df_z = 0\}$, and the postcritical set is $P(f) = \bigcup_{k \geq 1} f^k(C(f))$. A subset $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ containing $O$ is said to be a topological cone near the origin if there is a neighborhood $U$ of $O$ and a homeomorphism of $U$ onto a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$ sending $X \cap U$ onto an open neighborhood of $0$ in a complex cone (a set invariant under the scaling $z \mapsto \lambda z$ for $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^*$). The homogeneous map $H$ is called non-degenerate if $H^{-1}(0) = \{O\}$.

Assume that the postcritical set of $f$ is a topological cone near the origin. Determine sufficient conditions under which $f$ is topologically locally conjugate to $H$ near $O$, i.e., there exists a germ of homeomorphism $\varphi : (\mathbb{C}^n, O) \to (\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ such that $\varphi \circ f = H \circ \varphi$. In particular, decide whether this conjugacy always holds when $H$ is non-degenerate.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
context_brief: Heavy-tail behavior outside the conjectured regime
original_question: In critically loaded finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queues, what explains the apparent split between heavy-tailed Weibull and light-tailed examples, which seem to agree with Conjecture 1, and Lognormal and Pareto examples, which appear to behave differently? Is the discrepancy for Lognormal and Pareto caused by very slow convergence of γ*(t) to γ* as t → ∞, by the finite-buffer correction term vanishing much more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞, or by a genuinely different asymptotic limit for those distributions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a GI/G/1/K queue: a single-server queue with renewal inter-arrival times, i.i.d. service times independent of the arrivals, FCFS discipline, and a finite buffer of size K (so that arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost). Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e., the traffic intensity ρ = E[S]/E[T] equals 1, where T and S denote a generic inter-arrival and service time. Let D(t) denote the number of departures from the system in [0,t], and define

  γ*(t) := Var(D(t))/t,   γ* := lim_{t→∞} γ*(t),

assumed to exist for the distributions under consideration. A widely studied phenomenon (the BRAVO effect — "Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs") is captured by the conjecture that, for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with light-tailed inter-arrival and service distributions,

  γ* = (1/3)(Var(T)/E[T]^3 + Var(S)/E[S]^3) · E[S] + o_K(1),  with o_K(1) = O(1/K) as K → ∞.

Empirically, simulations with heavy-tailed Weibull service times, as well as light-tailed services, are consistent with this 1/3 BRAVO factor, while simulations with Lognormal or Pareto service distributions appear to deviate, displaying a BRAVO effect but with an apparently different multiplicative constant.

Problem. For critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with Lognormal or Pareto service-time distributions, determine which of the following explains the observed deviation from the 1/3 BRAVO conjecture:
(a) the convergence γ*(t) → γ* as t → ∞ is genuinely much slower than for light-tailed and Weibull cases (so that finite-time simulations have not yet entered the asymptotic regime);
(b) the finite-buffer correction term o_K(1) above vanishes substantially more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞ for these distributions;
(c) the limiting asymptotic constant γ* itself differs from the conjectured (1/3)(Var(T)/E[T]^3 + Var(S)/E[S]^3)·E[S] for these distributions.

Identify which of (a), (b), (c) (possibly more than one) is responsible, and quantify the corresponding rates of convergence in t and in K.
status_search_result: Recent work (2024) on phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues discusses generalized BRAVO and oscillating cumulants near critical load, but does not appear to resolve the specific discrepancy observed for Lognormal and Pareto service distributions in GI/G/1/K queues. No source identifying the precise mechanism (slow convergence in t, slow vanishing of the finite-buffer correction in K, or a genuinely different asymptotic constant) was found, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let f and g be superattracting germs in End(C^n,O) with c(f)=c(g). Is local conjugacy equivalent to conjugacy of postcritical sets: topological conjugacy iff a local homeomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g), and holomorphic conjugacy iff a local biholomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ denote the set of germs at the origin of holomorphic self-maps $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ fixing the origin. A germ $f \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ is called superattracting at $O$ if its differential $df_O$ vanishes. The critical set $\mathrm{Crit}(f)$ is the analytic germ at $O$ where the Jacobian determinant of $f$ vanishes, and the postcritical set is
$$\mathrm{PCrit}(f) \;=\; \bigcup_{k\ge 1} f^k(\mathrm{Crit}(f)),$$
viewed as a germ at $O$. Define the critical multiplicity $c(f)$ as the order of vanishing at $O$ of the Jacobian determinant of $f$.

Two germs $f, g \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ are said to be locally topologically (respectively, holomorphically) conjugate if there exists a germ of homeomorphism (respectively, biholomorphism) $\varphi:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ such that $\varphi \circ f = g \circ \varphi$. Two postcritical sets are said to be topologically (respectively, holomorphically) conjugate if there exists a germ of homeomorphism (respectively, biholomorphism) of $(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ sending one onto the other.

Question: Let $f, g \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ be superattracting germs with $c(f) = c(g)$. Is it true that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ and $g$ are locally topologically conjugate if and only if $\mathrm{PCrit}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PCrit}(g)$ are topologically conjugate; and
\item $f$ and $g$ are locally holomorphically conjugate if and only if $\mathrm{PCrit}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PCrit}(g)$ are holomorphically conjugate?
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys of local discrete holomorphic dynamics on the classification of superattracting germs by their postcritical sets. Recent works on Böttcher coordinates and superattracting germs (Buff–Epstein–Koch; Favre–Jonsson in dimension two) develop the relevant tools but do not establish the proposed equivalence in general dimension. No published resolution was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: What is a complete intuitive explanation of the BRAVO phenomenon—the reduction in long-run output variability when a queue is critically balanced—for basic single-server queues?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue (for example, the M/M/1 queue, or more generally a GI/G/1 queue) with arrival rate λ and service rate μ, and let ρ = λ/μ denote the traffic intensity. Let D(t) denote the number of departures (served customers) up to time t. Define the asymptotic variance rate of the departure process as

  V = lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

assuming the limit exists. It is known that for a wide class of single-server queues, V exhibits a striking drop precisely at the critical load ρ = 1: as ρ → 1, V is strictly smaller than what would be predicted by either the stable regime (ρ < 1, where departures inherit the variability of arrivals) or the overloaded regime (ρ > 1, where departures inherit the variability of service). This sharp reduction of long-run output variability at criticality is known as the BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs) phenomenon.

Problem. Provide a complete and conceptually satisfying intuitive explanation of the BRAVO phenomenon for basic single-server queues. The explanation should clarify, in qualitative and mechanistic terms, why critically balancing the arrival and service rates causes the asymptotic variance rate of the departure process to be strictly smaller than in the off-critical regimes, and should account for the universality of the effect across different single-server models (M/M/1, GI/G/1, etc.).
status_search_result: Recent literature, including a 2024 work on phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues, continues to derive precise formulae and generalizations of the BRAVO effect (e.g., to higher-order cumulants), but does not supply a complete intuitive/mechanistic explanation of why balancing reduces departure variance. The problem of giving a fully intuitive explanation remains open.

original_question: Classify, up to formal conjugacy, superattracting germs of order 2 in End(C^n,O) for n >= 3, and superattracting germs of order 3 in End(C^2,O).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ denote the set of germs at the origin of holomorphic self-maps $f\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ fixing the origin. Write $f$ as a formal power series $f(z)=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge 1}a_\alpha z^\alpha$ with $a_\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$, and define the order of $f$ at $O$ as $\nu(f):=\min\{|\alpha|:a_\alpha\neq 0\}$. The germ $f$ is called superattracting at $O$ if $df_O=0$, equivalently $\nu(f)\ge 2$.

Two germs $f,g\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ are formally conjugate if there exists a formal invertible change of coordinates $\varphi\in\widehat{\mathrm{Diff}}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ (a formal power-series map with $\varphi(O)=O$ and invertible linear part) such that $\varphi\circ f=g\circ\varphi$ as formal power series.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to formal conjugacy, of the superattracting germs $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ in each of the following two cases:
(a) $n\ge 3$ and $\nu(f)=2$;
(b) $n=2$ and $\nu(f)=3$.

That is, exhibit a list of formal normal forms such that every superattracting germ in the indicated class is formally conjugate to exactly one (or to one in a specified equivalence family) of these normal forms, and determine the moduli.
status_search_result: A complete formal classification is known in dimension 2 for superattracting germs of order 2 (with non-vanishing quadratic term, normal forms have been computed), but the classification in the cases (a) $n\ge 3$, order 2 and (b) $n=2$, order 3 does not appear to have been carried out. Available literature (Böttcher-type theorems, work on Böttcher coordinates and on formal/Poincaré–Dulac renormalization for holomorphic germs) addresses partial cases—e.g., skew-products and special weight conditions—but no general classification in the stated cases was located. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems
context_brief: Inverse nodal problem for Sturm-Liouville operators
original_question: Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q, α, β) on (0,1), given by -y''(x) + q(x)y(x) = λy(x) with real-valued q in L¹(0,1) and boundary conditions y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0 and y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0. Fix b in (1/2,1]. If one knows a subset of the nodal set of eigenfunctions inside (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there, is that weaker dense nodal data still sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sturm–Liouville boundary value problem L(q,α,β) on the interval (0,1) defined by

   -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),   x ∈ (0,1),

with real-valued potential q ∈ L^1(0,1) and separated boundary conditions

   y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0,    y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0,

where α ∈ [0,π) and β ∈ (0,π]. For each n ≥ 1, let y_n denote a real-valued eigenfunction associated with the n-th eigenvalue λ_n, and let X_n = { x_{n,k} : k = 1,…,n−1 } ⊂ (0,1) denote its set of interior nodal points (zeros). Set X = ⋃_{n≥1} X_n.

Fix b ∈ (1/2, 1]. Suppose one is given a subset W ⊂ X ∩ (0,b) that is dense in (0,b) (but not necessarily satisfying the stronger s-dense condition, namely that for every x ∈ (0,b) there is a sequence x_{n_j,k_j} ∈ W with x_{n_j,k_j} → x and k_j/n_j → x).

Given two such problems L(q,α,β) and L(q̃,α̃,β̃) sharing the same dense nodal subset W in (0,b) (in the sense that the corresponding nodal points coincide on W), determine whether the left boundary parameter is forced to coincide, i.e. whether α = α̃.
status_search_result: The problem has been answered affirmatively: a result of Cheng et al. shows that knowing a dense (not necessarily s-dense) subset of the nodal set in (0,b) for some b ∈ (1/2,1] suffices to uniquely determine the left boundary parameter α, strengthening Yang's earlier theorem.

original_question: Classify rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs in complex dimension 3.
self_contained_problem:
A holomorphic germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ is called dominant if its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically, and non-invertible if $df_0$ is not invertible. Define the generalized critical set of $f$ as $C^\infty(f)=\bigcup_{k\ge 1} C(f^k)$, where $C(f^k)$ is the critical set of the $k$-th iterate. The germ $f$ is called rigid if:
(i) $C^\infty(f)$ has at most simple normal crossings at $0$, and
(ii) $C^\infty(f)$ is totally invariant under $f$, i.e. $f^{-1}(C^\infty(f))\subseteq C^\infty(f)$ as germs.

Problem: Provide a complete classification, up to holomorphic conjugacy, of rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^3,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^3,0)$ (i.e. produce a list of normal forms exhausting all conjugacy classes of such germs in complex dimension three).
status_search_result: Existing classifications of rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs (e.g. work of Favre and Ruggiero) treat the two-dimensional case. No classification in dimension three appears in the literature; the problem is listed as an open problem and a search returns only related 2D results.

paper_title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems
context_brief: Subinterval threshold in inverse nodal uniqueness
original_question: For the same Sturm-Liouville inverse nodal setting, Yang's uniqueness theorem concerns nodal data in a subinterval (0,b) with b > 1/2. The open question asks whether the corresponding uniqueness conclusion remains valid when the observed nodal data are only in a left subinterval with b in (0,1/2]; that is, whether a twin nodal subset in (0,b) satisfying the same inverse-nodal setup can still determine the potential and boundary data when the observation interval does not extend past 1/2.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sturm–Liouville eigenvalue problem on [0,1]:

  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,1),
  y'(0) - h y(0) = 0,   y'(1) + H y(1) = 0,

where q ∈ L^1(0,1) is real-valued and h, H ∈ ℝ. The problem has a discrete spectrum of real eigenvalues λ_1 < λ_2 < ⋯, with corresponding eigenfunctions y_n having exactly n-1 zeros (nodes) 0 < x_1^{(n)} < x_2^{(n)} < ⋯ < x_{n-1}^{(n)} < 1 in (0,1). Let X(q,h,H) = { x_k^{(n)} : n ≥ 2, 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1 } denote the full set of nodal points.

For a fixed b ∈ (0,1), a subset S ⊂ (0,b) of nodal points of (q,h,H) is called twin and dense in (0,b) if S is dense in (0,b) and there exist infinitely many indices n for which two consecutive nodes x_k^{(n)}, x_{k+1}^{(n)} both lie in S.

Question. Suppose b ∈ (0, 1/2], and suppose (q,h,H) and (q̃, h̃, H̃) are two such Sturm–Liouville triples whose nodal sets in (0,b) share a common twin dense subset (with matching index conditions of the standard inverse nodal setup). Does it follow that q − ⟨q⟩ = q̃ − ⟨q̃⟩ on (0,1) (where ⟨q⟩ := ∫_0^1 q) and that h = h̃, H = H̃? Equivalently, can nodal observations restricted to a left subinterval (0,b) with b ≤ 1/2 determine the potential (up to its mean) and the boundary parameters?
status_search_result: The parsed question itself indicates the problem has been resolved: for any fixed b < 1/2, a dense twin nodal subset in (0,b) does NOT determine the potential (counterexamples exist), while at the borderline b = 1/2 a uniqueness theorem does hold. Thus Yang's open problem II is answered in the negative for b ∈ (0,1/2) and positively for b = 1/2.

original_question: Determine conditions on a germ f in End(C^3,O) guaranteeing existence of a modification pi: M~ -> C^3 based at O, a point p in E=pi^{-1}(O), and a (possibly weakly) rigid germ f~ in End(M,p) such that pi o f~ = f o pi.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ denote the set of holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^3,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ fixing the origin. A modification based at $O$ is a proper holomorphic map $\pi:\widetilde{M}\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ from a smooth complex 3-fold $\widetilde{M}$ which is a biholomorphism away from the exceptional divisor $E=\pi^{-1}(O)$. Given $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$, a lift of $f$ over $\pi$ at a point $p\in E$ is a holomorphic germ $\widetilde{f}\in\mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M},p)$ satisfying $\pi\circ\widetilde{f}=f\circ\pi$.

For a holomorphic germ $g\in\mathrm{End}(X,p)$ on a smooth complex manifold, let $C(g)$ denote the critical set of $g$ and let the generalized critical set be $C^\infty(g)=\bigcup_{n\ge 1} C(g^n)$. The germ $g$ is called rigid if $C^\infty(g)$ (as a germ at $p$) is either empty or a divisor with simple normal crossings at $p$ that is totally invariant under $g$, i.e.\ $g^{-1}(C^\infty(g))\subseteq C^\infty(g)$ as germs. The germ $g$ is called weakly rigid if these conditions hold up to allowing a non-totally-invariant but well-controlled component (the standard weakening used in the rigidification program).

Determine explicit conditions on $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ which guarantee the existence of a modification $\pi:\widetilde{M}\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ based at $O$, a point $p\in E=\pi^{-1}(O)$, and a (possibly weakly) rigid holomorphic germ $\widetilde{f}\in\mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M},p)$ such that $\pi\circ\widetilde{f}=f\circ\pi$.
status_search_result: Rigidification has been established in dimension two (e.g., Favre–Jonsson for superattracting germs, and extended by Ruggiero, arXiv:0911.4023, to general non-invertible differentials in $\mathbb{C}^2$). The analogous problem in dimension three remains an open question; no general criterion on $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ guaranteeing such a (weakly) rigid lift appears to be known.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Classify all recurrent one-sided and two-sided sequences over a finite alphabet whose maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n)=2n for every n≥1; equivalently, determine all one-sided and two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences.
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet, and let x be a sequence over A, either one-sided (x: ℕ → A) or two-sided (x: ℤ → A). For a finite set τ = {τ_1 < τ_2 < ... < τ_n} ⊂ ℕ of nonnegative integers (a "pattern"), define the τ-factor set of x as
   F_τ(x) = { (x(i+τ_1), x(i+τ_2), ..., x(i+τ_n)) : i ∈ dom(x) with i+τ_n in dom(x) }.
The maximal pattern complexity of x is the function
   p*_x(n) = sup{ |F_τ(x)| : τ ⊂ ℕ, |τ| = n },
where the supremum is over all patterns τ of cardinality n. The sequence x is said to be pattern Sturmian if p*_x(n) = 2n for every n ≥ 1.

A sequence x is recurrent if every finite factor that occurs in x occurs infinitely often.

Problem. Classify (i.e., give an explicit description of) all recurrent one-sided sequences over a finite alphabet that are pattern Sturmian, and analogously classify all recurrent two-sided sequences over a finite alphabet that are pattern Sturmian. Equivalently, determine all recurrent one-sided and two-sided sequences x with p*_x(n) = 2n for every n ≥ 1.
category_tag: Symbolic dynamics and combinatorics on words
status_search_result: The classification of pattern Sturmian sequences (those with maximal pattern complexity p*(n)=2n for all n≥1) remains an open problem. While Sturmian sequences and certain rotation-coded sequences are known to be pattern Sturmian, no full classification of one-sided or two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences has been published; the problem is listed as open in surveys on mathematical quasicrystals and combinatorics on words.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: For the discrete Schrödinger operator H on l²(Z) with potential λx_m generated by a pattern Sturmian sequence x, does the Sturmian conclusion remain valid: is the spectrum σ(H) always a zero-Lebesgue-measure Cantor set and are all spectral measures singular continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite alphabet and let $x = (x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ be a two-sided infinite sequence. For a finite "pattern" $P \subset \mathbb{Z}$ (a finite subset) and a length $n$, let $P_x(n)$ denote the number of distinct configurations $(x_{k+p})_{p\in P}$ obtained as $k$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}$, where one considers all patterns $P$ of cardinality $n+1$ (or, equivalently, the maximal complexity over windows of size $n+1$). The sequence $x$ is called pattern Sturmian if its pattern complexity satisfies $P_x(n) = n+1$ for every $n \geq 0$ — the minimal possible non-eventually-periodic pattern complexity, generalizing the usual Sturmian condition where only consecutive windows are counted.

Fix $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and consider the discrete Schrödinger operator $H = H_{\lambda,x}$ acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ by
$$(H\psi)(n) = \psi(n+1) + \psi(n-1) + \lambda x_n \psi(n), \quad n \in \mathbb{Z}.$$

It is known that when $x$ is a (classical) Sturmian sequence in $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$, the spectrum $\sigma(H)$ is a Cantor set of zero Lebesgue measure and all spectral measures of $H$ are purely singular continuous.

Question: Does the same conclusion hold whenever $x$ is a pattern Sturmian sequence? That is, prove or disprove: for every pattern Sturmian sequence $x$ and every $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, the spectrum $\sigma(H_{\lambda,x})$ is a Cantor set of zero Lebesgue measure, and all spectral measures of $H_{\lambda,x}$ are singular continuous.
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. While the corresponding result for classical Sturmian potentials is well established, and analogous results have been proved for related families (quasi-Sturmian potentials, Sturmian CMV matrices, period-doubling, certain interval-exchange-driven operators), no proof for the general pattern Sturmian case was found in the literature. The conjecture is listed among open problems in surveys on mathematical quasicrystals, and recent searches return no resolution.
