original_question: For a finite group G of odd order, is the maximal symmetry number always strictly larger than 1/r^2 for every r > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group. For each g ∈ G define the central symmetry s_g : G → G by s_g(x) = g x^{-1} g. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if s_g(S) = S for some g ∈ G. For an integer r ≥ 1, an r-coloring of G is any map χ : G → {1, …, r}; a subset S ⊆ G is monochromatic with respect to χ if χ is constant on S. Define the maximal symmetry number

  ms_r(G) = (1/|G|) · min_{χ : G → {1,…,r}} max{ |S| : S ⊆ G is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to χ }.

(Equivalently, ms_r(G)·|G| is the largest integer m such that every r-coloring of G admits a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality at least m.)

Question: Is it true that for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1 one has

  ms_r(G) > 1/r^2 ?
status_search_result: The bound ms_r(G) > 1/r^2 is established for finite Abelian groups of odd order in the survey where the question is posed. A web search did not turn up subsequent work resolving the question for arbitrary (non-Abelian) finite groups of odd order, so the current status appears unverified from accessible sources.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In heterogeneous computing applications that are decomposed into tasks and subtasks, what methods can support the feedback communications required among subtasks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing system consisting of a set M = {m_1, ..., m_k} of machines with differing architectures and performance characteristics, together with an interconnection network providing communication between machines. An application is modeled as a directed acyclic task graph G = (T, E), where each task t ∈ T may be further decomposed into a set of communicating subtasks S(t) = {s_{t,1}, ..., s_{t,n_t}}. The subtasks of a task have data dependencies among them but may be assigned to different machines in M for concurrent execution. During execution, subtasks may need to exchange not only forward data dependencies but also feedback communications, i.e., information that flows from a subtask back to one or more subtasks that have already begun or completed execution, in order to influence subsequent computation (for example, iterative refinement, dynamic parameter updates, or convergence signals).

Develop and characterize methods (including programming-model constructs, runtime mechanisms, scheduling policies, and synchronization protocols) that support such feedback communications among subtasks assigned to distinct machines in a heterogeneous system, in a way that:
(i) preserves the data dependencies imposed by G,
(ii) permits subtasks executing on different machines to send and receive feedback messages while running, and
(iii) admits a performance model under which the resulting execution time can be analyzed.

Formally describe at least one such method and prove (or argue) its correctness with respect to (i)–(iii).
status_search_result: The question is a broad open problem about supporting feedback communication among subtasks in heterogeneous computing systems. It is a methodological/research-direction question rather than a precise mathematical conjecture, and no single definitive resolution is available; various partial approaches (message-passing runtimes, dataflow models, iterative task graphs) address aspects of it, but no canonical solution is established.

context_brief: How small finite-group symmetry numbers can be
original_question: Given ε > 0 and an integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G whose maximal symmetry number ms_r(G) is smaller than ε?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that S = gS^{-1}g, where S^{-1} = {s^{-1} : s ∈ S}. (Equivalently, S is symmetric if it is invariant under some involutive map of the form x ↦ gx^{-1}g.) For an integer r ≥ 2 and an r-coloring χ : G → {1, …, r}, let

  ν(χ) = max { |S|/|G| : S ⊆ G is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to χ }.

Define the maximal symmetry number of G with r colors by

  ms_r(G) = min { ν(χ) : χ is an r-coloring of G },

so that ms_r(G) is the largest real number c such that every r-coloring of G admits a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality at least c·|G|.

Question: Given any real number ε > 0 and any integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G with

  ms_r(G) < ε ?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the question of whether ms_r(G) can be made arbitrarily small over finite groups G for each fixed r > 1. The question is posed as an open problem in the survey on symmetry and colorings by Banakh; no follow-up announcing a solution was located.

original_question: Does there exist a connected compact group G for which ms_r(G) < 1/r^2 for some integer r? In particular, what are the exact values of ms_2(SO(3)) and of ms_2(S^3), where S^3 is the multiplicative group of unit quaternions?

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: For heterogeneous computing suites, what hierarchical scheduling techniques can make it possible to scale the suite up to very large sizes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) suite, defined as a distributed collection of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed communication links, on which a stream of tasks (each with possibly different machine-dependent execution times and inter-task communication requirements) must be mapped to machines and ordered in time so as to optimize a global performance objective (for example, minimizing makespan or maximizing throughput). A scheduler is called hierarchical if it decomposes the mapping/scheduling decision across multiple levels (for instance, a top-level scheduler that assigns tasks or task groups to clusters or sub-suites, and lower-level schedulers that assign tasks to individual machines within each cluster), with limited information exchange between levels.

Problem: Design and analyze hierarchical scheduling techniques for heterogeneous computing suites that allow the suite to scale to very large sizes (in number of machines, tasks, and degree of heterogeneity) while maintaining good global scheduling performance. Specifically, identify hierarchical decomposition strategies, level-to-level information abstractions, and per-level scheduling policies whose combined time and communication complexity grows sub-linearly (or otherwise scalably) in the size of the suite, and quantify the loss in global scheduling quality (relative to an idealized centralized scheduler) introduced by the hierarchy as a function of the suite size and heterogeneity parameters.
status_search_result: Hierarchical scheduling for large-scale heterogeneous computing remains an active research topic. Numerous papers continue to propose hierarchical and multi-level schedulers for heterogeneous clusters, grids, clouds, and HPC/AI systems, but no canonical, fully scalable solution with provable optimality guarantees has been established. The question is therefore best regarded as still open in its general form.

context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of infinite groups
original_question: Let G be an infinite group, and let MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be the cardinal symmetry numbers defined using central symmetries and the cardinal-valued measures card and card^+. Must both MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be infinite for every finite number of colors r? Equivalently, does every finite coloring of an infinite group contain monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite size?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite group. For each element $c\in G$ define the central symmetry $s_c\colon G\to G$ by $s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c$, and let $\mathcal S=\{s_c:c\in G\}$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called symmetric if $s_c(A)=A$ for some $c\in G$ (equivalently, $A=cA^{-1}c$ for some $c\in G$).

For a positive integer $r$, define the cardinal symmetry numbers
$$MS_r(G)=\min_{\chi}\;\max_{i=1,\dots,r}\;\sup\bigl\{|A|:A\subseteq\chi^{-1}(i)\text{ is symmetric}\bigr\},$$
$$MS_r^{+}(G)=\min_{\chi}\;\max_{i=1,\dots,r}\;\sup\bigl\{|A|^{+}:A\subseteq\chi^{-1}(i)\text{ is symmetric}\bigr\},$$
where $\chi$ ranges over all colorings $\chi\colon G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$, $|A|$ denotes the cardinality of $A$, and $|A|^{+}$ denotes its successor cardinal (so $MS_r^{+}$ takes the supremum over a strict-inequality variant).

Question: Is it true that for every infinite group $G$ and every positive integer $r$, both $MS_r(G)$ and $MS_r^{+}(G)$ are infinite cardinals? Equivalently, is it true that for every finite coloring of any infinite group $G$ there exist monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality?
category_tag: Ramsey theory of symmetric subsets in groups
status_search_result: Web searches surface related work by Banakh, Protasov, Verbitsky and Vorobets on monochromatic symmetric subsets and on the cardinal invariant ν(G), and partial results for abelian groups and ℤ^k (e.g. ν(ℤ^m)=m+1). However, no source found explicitly resolves the question of whether MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) are infinite for every infinite group G and every finite r. The problem appears to remain open in full generality.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In heterogeneous computing environments where centralized control is inadequate, what distributed mapping heuristics can replace centralized ones while still producing effective task-to-machine mappings?
self_contained_problem: Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment consisting of a finite set M = {m_1, ..., m_p} of machines with differing computational capabilities, and a finite collection T = {t_1, ..., t_n} of tasks (possibly partitioned into subtasks with precedence constraints described by a directed acyclic graph). For each task t_i and machine m_j, an estimated execution time E(i,j) is given, together with inter-machine communication costs C(j,k) for transferring data between machines. A mapping is a pair (μ, σ) where μ : T → M assigns each task to a machine and σ specifies, for each machine m_j, a total order on μ^{-1}(m_j); the makespan of (μ, σ) is the completion time of the last task respecting the precedence constraints, execution times, and communication costs. A mapping heuristic is centralized if a single designated machine has global knowledge of T, M, E, C, and the current system state and computes (μ, σ); it is distributed if the decisions defining (μ, σ) are produced by an algorithm in which each machine acts based only on local information and message exchanges with a bounded neighborhood, with no node holding global state.\n\nProblem. Design distributed mapping heuristics for the above HC scheduling model that can replace centralized heuristics in settings where centralized control is infeasible (e.g., scalability, fault-tolerance, or partial-information constraints), while still producing mappings whose makespan is competitive with that produced by standard centralized heuristics. Specifically, identify a family of distributed heuristics together with a precise performance guarantee (e.g., a worst-case or expected approximation ratio relative to an optimal or to a fixed centralized baseline) that holds across a meaningful class of HC instances.
status_search_result: The question is a broad research direction on distributed mapping heuristics for heterogeneous computing rather than a sharply formulated conjecture. While many distributed scheduling and mapping heuristics have been proposed in the literature on heterogeneous and grid/cloud computing since the early 2000s, no single result definitively settles the general question of replacing centralized mapping heuristics with distributed ones at comparable performance across all HC settings. Status is therefore best regarded as unknown/ongoing.

context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of special linear groups
original_question: Let G = SL(K), where K is an infinite field. Is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(G) equal to |G|^+ for every finite number of colors r?
self_contained_problem:
For a group $G$ and a positive integer $r$, define the cardinal symmetry number $MS_r^+(G)$ as the smallest cardinal $\kappa$ such that for every coloring $\chi:G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset $S\subseteq G$ with $|S|\geq\lambda$ for every cardinal $\lambda<\kappa$; here a subset $S\subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g\in G$ with $gS^{-1}g=S$ (equivalently, $S$ is invariant under the involution $x\mapsto gx^{-1}g$ for some $g\in G$).

Let $K$ be an infinite field and let $G=\mathrm{SL}(K)=\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\mathrm{SL}_n(K)$ be the special linear group over $K$ (the direct limit of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_n(K)$ under the standard embeddings). 

Is it true that $MS_r^+(G)=|G|^+$ for every finite cardinal $r$? In other words, for every finite coloring of $\mathrm{SL}(K)$ with $r$ colors, must there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality $|G|$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search for the cardinal symmetry number $MS_r^+$ of the special linear group $\mathrm{SL}(K)$ and related monochromatic symmetric subset problems did not return any results indicating that the case of arbitrary finite $r$ has been resolved beyond the known $r=2$ case. No follow-up paper resolving the question was identified, so the status is unclear.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: Given that most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, how should heterogeneous computing mapping procedures incorporate multi-tasking, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage multi-tasking together with other quality-of-service requirements?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) system consisting of a set of machines M = {m_1, ..., m_p} with differing architectures and computational capabilities, on which a dynamically arriving set of tasks T = {t_1, t_2, ...} must be executed. Each machine m_j runs an operating system that supports preemptive multi-tasking, so that several tasks assigned to m_j may share its processor time according to a time-sharing policy. Each task t_i has an estimated execution time e_{ij} on machine m_j, plus quality-of-service (QoS) requirements such as deadlines, priorities, throughput, security level, or fault tolerance level.

Design and analyze a mapping procedure (i.e., a matching-and-scheduling algorithm) M: T -> M together with a per-machine time-allocation policy A_j that, for each machine m_j, partitions its processor time among the tasks currently assigned to it, with the following objectives:

1. The mapping M explicitly accounts for the fact that each machine can execute multiple tasks concurrently via multi-tasking, rather than assuming exclusive use of a processor.
2. The time-allocation policies A_j allocate processor time among co-located tasks in a way that respects all per-task QoS requirements simultaneously.
3. The combined scheme leverages multi-tasking (e.g., to overlap I/O with computation, to satisfy mixed-priority workloads, or to improve responsiveness) while still optimizing a global system performance metric such as makespan, weighted QoS satisfaction, or robustness.

Provide a formal model for this problem, define an appropriate optimality (or approximation) criterion, and either give an algorithm achieving that criterion with provable guarantees or prove hardness/impossibility results characterizing the trade-offs between multi-tasking benefits and QoS guarantees in heterogeneous computing environments.
status_search_result: Incorporating multi-tasking into heterogeneous computing mapping procedures while honoring multiple QoS requirements is described as an ongoing research area, with no single agreed-upon optimal framework. Subsequent literature on HC scheduling, QoS-aware mapping, and time-sharing on heterogeneous resources continues to address subproblems but does not provide a comprehensive solution to this general formulation, so the problem is best regarded as open.

context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of the free group F2
original_question: For the free group F_2 on two generators, is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite number of colors r?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g \in G$ such that $S = gS^{-1}g$, i.e., $S$ is invariant under the involution $x \mapsto gx^{-1}g$ for some $g \in G$. For a cardinal $r$, an $r$-coloring of $G$ is a function $\chi : G \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$. Define the cardinal symmetry number
$$MS_r^+(G) = \min_{\chi} \sup\{|S| : S \subseteq G \text{ is symmetric, infinite, and monochromatic with respect to } \chi\}^+,$$
where the minimum runs over all $r$-colorings $\chi : G \to r$, and the operation $\kappa \mapsto \kappa^+$ denotes the successor cardinal of the supremum of cardinalities of monochromatic symmetric subsets. Equivalently, $MS_r^+(G) > \kappa$ means that for every $r$-coloring of $G$ there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality $\geq \kappa$.

Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators. It is known that $MS_2^+(F_2)$ is uncountable, i.e., for every $2$-coloring of $F_2$ there is an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.

Question: Is $MS_r^+(F_2)$ uncountable for every finite cardinal $r$? That is, is it true that for every finite number $r$ of colors and every $r$-coloring of $F_2$, there exists an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset?
category_tag: Ramsey theory of symmetric subsets in groups
status_search_result: A web search did not return direct evidence that this problem about the cardinal symmetry number $MS_r^+(F_2)$ for the free group on two generators with arbitrary finite number of colors $r$ has been resolved. Related work by Banakh, Protasov, Verbitsky, and Vorobets on Ramsey-type symmetry invariants exists, but no source explicitly confirming a resolution for all finite $r$ was found.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In multi-user, distributed, peer-to-peer heterogeneous computing environments where users execute tasks on other machines, how should the inherent security issues be addressed?
self_contained_problem: Consider a multi-user, distributed, peer-to-peer heterogeneous computing environment, modeled as a set of machines M = {m_1, ..., m_n} with varying computational capabilities, interconnected by communication links of varying bandwidth and latency, and a set of users U = {u_1, ..., u_k} who submit tasks that may be assigned to and executed on machines owned or used by other users. In such an environment, identify and formally address the security issues that arise from allowing users to execute tasks on machines they do not own or control. Specifically, propose a security framework (with precise definitions of trust assumptions, adversary model, and security guarantees) that ensures: (i) confidentiality and integrity of a task's code and data while executing on a remote host; (ii) protection of the host machine from malicious or faulty submitted tasks; (iii) authentication and access control among peers; and (iv) safe inter-task communication. Prove that the proposed framework achieves the stated guarantees against the specified adversary model.
status_search_result: The question is broad and open-ended rather than a precise mathematical conjecture. Security for distributed peer-to-peer heterogeneous computing has been studied extensively (trusted execution, secure multiparty computation, sandboxing, attestation), but no single closed-form solution is generally accepted as resolving all aspects, and the original posing is a research direction rather than a settled problem.

context_brief: Dimension symmetry in the hyperbolic plane
original_question: Let H^2 be the hyperbolic plane with the family of central symmetries s_c that reflect points through a midpoint c, and let mds_r(H^2) be the corresponding dimension symmetry number based on asymptotic dimension. Is mds_r(H^2) ≥ 0 for every r ≥ 2? Equivalently, does every r-coloring of H^2 contain an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^2$ denote the hyperbolic plane (the Lobachevsky plane), endowed with its standard hyperbolic metric and Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For each point $c \in \mathbb{H}^2$ let $s_c : \mathbb{H}^2 \to \mathbb{H}^2$ be the central symmetry through $c$, i.e., the unique isometry that fixes $c$ and reverses every geodesic through $c$. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{H}^2$ is called centrally symmetric if there exists a point $c$ such that $s_c(A) = A$. A Borel $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{H}^2$ is a partition $\mathbb{H}^2 = C_1 \sqcup C_2 \sqcup \dots \sqcup C_r$ into $r$ Borel pieces. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{H}^2$ is unbounded if its hyperbolic diameter is infinite (equivalently, its asymptotic dimension satisfies $\operatorname{asdim}(A) \geq 0$ in the convention that the empty set and bounded sets have asymptotic dimension $-\infty$, while unbounded sets have $\operatorname{asdim} \geq 0$).

Question: For every integer $r \geq 2$, does every Borel $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{H}^2$ contain a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset that is unbounded?
category_tag: Euclidean Ramsey theory in hyperbolic geometry
status_search_result: A published result ("Symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings of the Lobachevsky plane", DMTCS) establishes that for each partition of the Lobachevsky (hyperbolic) plane into finitely many Borel pieces, one of the cells contains an unbounded centrally symmetric subset. This affirmatively answers the question for all r ≥ 2.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Sharp observability constants for the constant-coefficient heat equation
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the linear heat equation φ_t − Δφ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T). There exist constants γ > 0 and C > 0 such that the weighted observability inequality ∫_0^T∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^T∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt holds for every solution, and the analogous inequality also makes sense on the infinite time interval because the L²-norm of solutions decays exponentially. Determine the best possible constant γ in these observability inequalities, in particular in the infinite-time version ∫_0^∞∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^∞∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt, and decide whether the lower bound γ ≥ sup_{B(x_0,p)⊂Ω\ω} p^2/4 is sharp, especially in radially symmetric geometries.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset. For $T \in (0,\infty]$, consider the linear heat equation
$$\varphi_t - \Delta \varphi = 0 \text{ in } \Omega \times (0,T), \qquad \varphi = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega \times (0,T), \qquad \varphi(\cdot,0)=\varphi_0 \in L^2(\Omega).$$
It is known that there exist constants $\gamma > 0$ and $C = C(\gamma) > 0$ such that
$$\int_0^T \!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt \;\le\; C \int_0^T\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt$$
for every solution $\varphi$, and (using exponential decay of the $L^2$-norm) the same form of inequality makes sense for $T = \infty$:
$$\int_0^\infty \!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt \;\le\; C \int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt. \qquad (\star)$$
Define
$$\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega) := \inf\{\gamma > 0 : (\star) \text{ holds for some } C > 0\}.$$
A simple test using radial Gaussian-like solutions concentrated in a ball $B(x_0,\rho) \subset \Omega \setminus \overline{\omega}$ yields the lower bound
$$\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega) \;\ge\; \sup\bigl\{\rho^2/4 : B(x_0,\rho) \subset \Omega\setminus\overline{\omega}\bigr\}.$$
Determine $\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega)$ explicitly (the best possible $\gamma$ in the observability inequalities, especially in the infinite-time version), and decide whether the above lower bound is sharp, in particular for radially symmetric geometries (e.g., $\Omega$ a ball and $\omega$ an annular neighborhood of $\partial\Omega$).
status_search_result: Ervedoza and Zuazua (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2011, "Sharp observability estimates for heat equations") obtained sharp upper bounds on the best constant γ via a transmutation method from observability of the wave equation. Their estimates are proved sharp in one space dimension (for an interval of length L controlled at the boundary, the threshold is γ = L²/2) and in radially symmetric multi-dimensional configurations, matching the geometric lower bound sup ρ²/4. The general (non-radial) multi-dimensional case of identifying the exact best constant remains open.

original_question: Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, µ, S), a number of colors r, and a threshold λ in the measure range, calculate the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X), meaning the smallest size of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic S'-symmetric measurable set of measure at least λ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $S$ be a family of measurable involutive bijections $s : X \to X$ (so $s\circ s = \mathrm{id}_X$ and $s$ preserves $\mu$). The triple $X = (X,\mu,S)$ is called a symmetry measure space. For a subfamily $S' \subset S$, a measurable subset $A \subset X$ is called $S'$-symmetric if there exists $s \in S'$ with $s(A) = A$.

Fix an integer $r \ge 2$ (the number of colors) and a real number $\lambda$ in the range of $\mu$. A measurable $r$-coloring of $X$ is a partition $X = C_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup C_r$ into measurable sets. A subfamily $S' \subset S$ is called an $(r,\lambda)$-centerpole if, for every measurable $r$-coloring $X = C_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup C_r$, there exist an index $i \in \{1,\dots,r\}$ and a measurable subset $A \subset C_i$ with $\mu(A) \ge \lambda$ such that $A$ is $S'$-symmetric.

Define the $(r,\lambda)$-centerpole number
$$c_r^{\lambda}(X) = \min\{|S'| : S' \subset S \text{ is an } (r,\lambda)\text{-centerpole}\}.$$

Problem: For a given symmetry measure space $X = (X,\mu,S)$, compute (or give exact formulas/asymptotics for) the centerpole numbers $c_r^{\lambda}(X)$ as functions of $r$ and $\lambda$.
category_tag: centerpole numbers in symmetry measure spaces
status_search_result: The general problem of computing $(r,\lambda)$-centerpole numbers for arbitrary symmetry measure spaces is a broad open problem; only partial results and special cases (e.g., for compact topological groups, Euclidean spaces, finite cyclic groups) have appeared in the literature on symmetry and Ramsey-type problems by Banakh and collaborators. No general solution has been verified.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Observability for heat equations with bounded potential
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the heat equation with bounded potential φ_t − Δφ + a(x,t)φ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, where a ∈ L^∞(Ω × (0,T)). Existing observability estimates involve a factor of the form exp(C‖a‖_∞^{2/3}). Determine whether one can improve this dependence to exp(C‖a‖_∞^{1/2}), or otherwise obtain a sharper observability inequality with weaker growth in ‖a‖_∞, for example by proving suitable Carleman inequalities in spaces of the form L^p(0,T;L^q(Ω)) rather than only in L²(Ω × (0,T)).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset, let $T > 0$, and let $a \in L^\infty(\Omega \times (0,T))$. Consider the linear heat equation with bounded potential
$$\varphi_t - \Delta \varphi + a(x,t)\varphi = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,T),$$
$$\varphi = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega \times (0,T), \qquad \varphi(\cdot,0) = \varphi_0 \in L^2(\Omega).$$
By known global Carleman estimates, there exists a constant $C = C(\Omega,\omega,T) > 0$ such that the observability inequality
$$\|\varphi(\cdot,T)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 \le \exp\!\bigl(C\,(1+\|a\|_\infty^{2/3})\bigr)\int_0^T\!\!\int_\omega |\varphi(x,t)|^2\,dx\,dt$$
holds for every solution $\varphi$ of the above system.

Question: Can the exponent $2/3$ in the factor $\exp(C\|a\|_\infty^{2/3})$ be improved? In particular, does an observability inequality of the same form hold with $\exp(C\|a\|_\infty^{1/2})$ in place of $\exp(C\|a\|_\infty^{2/3})$? More generally, can one establish a sharper observability inequality with weaker growth of the constant in $\|a\|_\infty$, for instance through Carleman inequalities formulated in mixed Lebesgue spaces $L^p(0,T;L^q(\Omega))$ rather than only in $L^2(\Omega \times (0,T))$?
category_tag: Observability and Carleman estimates for heat equations
status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) confirms that for general bounded potentials, the best known exponent in the observability constant for the scalar heat equation remains 2/3, and optimality of this exponent for scalar parabolic equations is explicitly stated as still open. Improvements to exp(C(‖∇V‖^{1/2}+‖∂_t V‖^{1/3})) are known under additional Lipschitz regularity, but no improvement to exp(C‖a‖_∞^{1/2}) for merely L^∞ potentials has been established.

context_brief: Comparing Euclidean and lattice centerpole numbers
original_question: For Euclidean space R^n and the integer lattice Z^n, both equipped with central symmetries and asymptotic dimension, is it always true that c_r^0(R^n) = c_r^0(Z^n) for every r ≤ n? Here c_r^0 is the minimum number of centers needed to force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset in every r-coloring.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A symmetry measure space is a triple (X, μ, 𝒮) where X is a set, μ is a σ-additive measure with a distinguished σ-ideal of "bounded" sets (so that "unbounded subset" makes sense), and 𝒮 is a family of involutions s : X → X (called central symmetries), each having a unique fixed point c(s) ∈ X called its center. A subset A ⊂ X is called 𝒮'-symmetric (for 𝒮' ⊂ 𝒮) if there exists s ∈ 𝒮' with s(A) = A.

For a positive integer r, define the centerpole number
   c_r^0(X) := min { |𝒮'| : 𝒮' ⊂ 𝒮 and for every r-coloring χ : X → {1, …, r} there exists an unbounded monochromatic 𝒮'-symmetric subset A ⊂ X }.

Consider the two symmetry measure spaces:
 (i) X = ℝ^n with Lebesgue measure, bounded sets in the usual sense, and 𝒮 the family of all central symmetries x ↦ 2c − x for c ∈ ℝ^n;
 (ii) X = ℤ^n with counting measure, bounded sets being finite sets, and 𝒮 the family of central symmetries x ↦ 2c − x for c ∈ (½ℤ)^n that preserve ℤ^n (equivalently those induced from ℝ^n that map ℤ^n to itself).

Question. Is it true that for every positive integer n and every integer r with 1 ≤ r ≤ n one has
   c_r^0(ℝ^n) = c_r^0(ℤ^n) ?

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Growth thresholds for null-controllability of semilinear heat equations
original_question: Consider the semilinear heat equation u_t − Δu + f(u) = v1_ω in a bounded smooth domain Ω, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T), control region ω ⊂ Ω open and nonempty, and a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity f satisfying f(0)=0 together with the local well-posedness assumptions used in the chapter. The chapter proves null-controllability when f grows strictly slower than |s|(log|s|)^{3/2} at infinity and gives counterexamples when f grows like |s|(log|s|)^p with p>2. Determine whether the system is null-controllable in the intermediate range C_1|s|(log|s|)^{3/2} ≤ |f(s)| ≤ C_2|s|(log|s|)^2 as |s|→∞, or more generally relax the known sufficient growth conditions for null-controllability, especially for nonlinearities growing slower than |s|(log|s|)^2 or such that 1/√|F(s)| is not integrable at infinity, where F(s)=∫_0^s f(σ)dσ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset, and let $T>0$. Consider the semilinear heat equation with internal control
$$
\begin{cases}
u_t - \Delta u + f(u) = v\,\mathbf{1}_\omega & \text{in } \Omega \times (0,T),\\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega \times (0,T),\\
u(\cdot,0) = u_0 & \text{in } \Omega,
\end{cases}
$$
where $u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$, $v \in L^2(\omega \times (0,T))$ is the control, and $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is locally Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$ and is such that the Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the standard energy class. Define $F(s)=\int_0^s f(\sigma)\,d\sigma$. The system is said to be null-controllable at time $T$ if for every $u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$ there exists a control $v$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(\cdot,T)\equiv 0$ in $\Omega$.

It is known that null-controllability holds whenever $|f(s)|/(|s|(\log|s|)^{3/2}) \to 0$ as $|s|\to\infty$, and that there exist nonlinearities with $|f(s)| \sim |s|(\log|s|)^p$ for some $p>2$ for which null-controllability fails (in fact, blow-up cannot be prevented by any control).

Question: Determine whether null-controllability holds in the intermediate growth range
$$
C_1 |s|(\log|s|)^{3/2} \le |f(s)| \le C_2 |s|(\log|s|)^2 \quad \text{as } |s|\to\infty,
$$
for constants $C_1,C_2>0$. More generally, identify the optimal growth condition on $f$ ensuring null-controllability; in particular, decide whether null-controllability holds whenever $1/\sqrt{|F(s)|}$ is not integrable at infinity, or whenever $f$ grows strictly slower than $|s|(\log|s|)^2$ at infinity.
status_search_result: A web search indicates that the positive null-controllability result up to growth $|s|(\log|s|)^{3/2}$ (Fernández-Cara–Zuazua, 2000) and the negative result for growth $|s|(\log|s|)^p$ with $p>2$ remain the standard thresholds in the literature. No publication was found that closes the gap in the intermediate range $(\log|s|)^{3/2} \le |f(s)|/|s| \le (\log|s|)^2$, and recent works on null-controllability of semilinear heat equations still cite these as the best known bounds. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

context_brief: Structure of minimal 4-centerpole sets in R4
original_question: Call a subset C ⊂ R^4 4-centerpole when the central symmetries with centers in C force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset under every 4-coloring. Is every 12-element 4-centerpole subset of R^4 affinely equivalent to the sandwich Ξ^3_1, the 12-point subset of Z^4 whose slices {-1} × 2^3_{<1}, {0} × 2^3_{<3}, and {1} × 2^3_{>1} have 1, 7, and 4 points, respectively?
self_contained_problem:
For a point $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$, let $s_c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the central symmetry $s_c(x)=2c-x$. A subset $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called symmetric if $s_c(S)=S$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For an integer $r\ge 1$, a subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $r$-centerpole if for every coloring $\chi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ there exist a color class and an unbounded subset of that color class which is symmetric with respect to some center $c\in C$ (equivalently, the family of central symmetries $\{s_c:c\in C\}$ forces an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset under every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Define the "$3$-sandwich" $\Xi^3_1\subset\mathbb{Z}^4$ as the following $12$-point set, described by its three slices in the first coordinate. Writing $2^3=\{0,1\}^3$ and letting $|x|=x_1+x_2+x_3$ for $x\in 2^3$, set
$$2^3_{=k}=\{x\in 2^3:|x|=k\},\quad 2^3_{<k}=\{x\in 2^3:|x|<k\},\quad 2^3_{>k}=\{x\in 2^3:|x|>k\}.$$
Then
$$\Xi^3_1=\big(\{-1\}\times 2^3_{=1}\big)\cup\big(\{0\}\times 2^3_{<3}\big)\cup\big(\{1\}\times 2^3_{>1}\big),$$
so the slices over $-1$, $0$, $1$ contain $1$, $7$, and $4$ points respectively (here the slice over $-1$ is interpreted as a single chosen point of $2^3_{=1}$, giving the total $1+7+4=12$).

Two subsets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ are affinely equivalent if there is an invertible affine map $f:\mathbb{R}^4\to\mathbb{R}^4$ with $f(A)=B$.

Question: Is every $12$-element $4$-centerpole subset of $\mathbb{R}^4$ affinely equivalent to $\Xi^3_1$?

The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Failure of null-controllability on general conical domains
original_question: For the heat equation on an unbounded conical domain Ω, with control acting on the boundary or on a bounded region as in the half-line and half-space problems discussed in the chapter, decide whether the negative null-controllability result proved for the half-line and extended to the half-space remains true in every conical domain. The main obstacle identified in the chapter is that, although similarity variables still apply in conical domains, the existing method does not extend because the traces of the normal derivatives of the relevant eigenfunctions on ∂Ω are not orthogonal.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be an unbounded conical domain, i.e., a domain such that $\lambda x \in \Omega$ for every $x \in \Omega$ and every $\lambda > 0$, with sufficiently regular boundary $\partial\Omega$. Consider the heat equation
$$\partial_t u - \Delta u = 0 \text{ in } \Omega \times (0,T), \qquad u(0,\cdot) = u_0 \in L^2(\Omega),$$
controlled either by a Dirichlet boundary control $v \in L^2(\partial\Omega \times (0,T))$ acting on $\partial\Omega$ (with $u = v$ on $\partial\Omega \times (0,T)$) or by an internal control supported in a bounded subset $\omega \subset \Omega$ (with $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega \times (0,T)$ and a forcing $v \mathbf{1}_\omega$ in the equation).

The system is said to be null-controllable in time $T > 0$ if for every initial datum $u_0$ (in a suitable class, e.g., smooth and compactly supported) there exists an admissible control $v$ such that $u(T,\cdot) \equiv 0$ in $\Omega$.

It is known that on the half-line $\Omega = (0,\infty)$, and more generally on the half-space $\Omega = \mathbb{R}^N_+$, the system is not null-controllable: there exists a nonzero smooth, compactly supported initial datum that cannot be driven to zero in any finite time by such controls. The proof relies on similarity variables together with the orthogonality of the traces of the normal derivatives of certain eigenfunctions on the boundary.

The similarity variable transformation extends to any conical $\Omega$, but the orthogonality property of the traces of normal derivatives of the eigenfunctions on $\partial\Omega$ is in general not available.

Question: Does the negative null-controllability result above (failure of null-controllability for some smooth, compactly supported initial datum, in any positive time, by either Dirichlet boundary control on $\partial\Omega$ or internal control on a bounded set) extend to every unbounded conical domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$?
category_tag: Null-controllability of the heat equation on unbounded domains
status_search_result: Web searches for null-controllability of the heat equation on unbounded conical domains return work on half-lines, half-spaces, and unbounded domains with finite-measure or thick control regions (Micu–Zuazua; Egidi–Veselić et al.), but no source clearly establishes or refutes the negative null-controllability result for general unbounded conical domains. The specific extension from the half-space to arbitrary conical domains does not appear to have been settled in the literature accessible via search.

original_question: Determine the (5,0)-centerpole number c_5^0(R^5) for Euclidean 5-space, that is, the smallest number of centers needed to force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset in every 5-coloring of R^5. The known bounds are 18 ≤ c_5^0(R^5) ≤ c_5^0(Z^5) ≤ 25.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}^5$ denote Euclidean 5-space. For a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5$ and a point $s \in \mathbb{R}^5$, say that $A$ is symmetric with respect to the center $s$ if $A = 2s - A := \{2s - a : a \in A\}$. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5$ is called unbounded if it is not contained in any ball of finite radius.

Given a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^5$ of centers and an integer $r \geq 1$, say that $S$ forces unbounded monochromatic symmetry for $r$ colors if, for every coloring $\chi : \mathbb{R}^5 \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$, there exists some center $s \in S$ and some unbounded subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5$ that is symmetric with respect to $s$ and on which $\chi$ is constant.

Define the $(5,0)$-centerpole number
$$c_5^{0}(\mathbb{R}^5) = \min\{\,|S| : S \subset \mathbb{R}^5 \text{ forces unbounded monochromatic symmetry for } 5 \text{ colors}\,\}.$$

It is known that
$$18 \le c_5^{0}(\mathbb{R}^5) \le c_5^{0}(\mathbb{Z}^5) \le 25,$$
where $c_5^{0}(\mathbb{Z}^5)$ is defined analogously with $\mathbb{R}^5$ replaced by the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^5$ (and centers $s$ taken in $\mathbb{Z}^5$, with symmetry $A = 2s - A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^5$).

Determine the exact value of $c_5^{0}(\mathbb{R}^5)$.
category_tag: Centerpole numbers and symmetric Ramsey theory

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Variable-coefficient and semilinear half-line heat equations
original_question: Consider the one-dimensional variable-coefficient heat equation on the half-line p(x)u_t − (a(x)u_x)_x = 0 for x>0 and t>0, with boundary control u(0,t)=v(t) and initial datum u(x,0)=u_0(x), where a and p are positive, bounded, smooth functions. Determine whether the lack of null-controllability proved in the chapter for the constant-coefficient half-line heat equation extends to this more general variable-coefficient setting. More generally, determine whether the same negative phenomenon persists for equations whose coefficients depend on both x and t, for equations with lower-order potentials, or for semilinear variants on the half-line.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional heat equation on the half-line with variable coefficients
\[
p(x)\,u_t - (a(x)\,u_x)_x = 0, \qquad x>0,\; t>0,
\]
with boundary control and initial condition
\[
u(0,t)=v(t),\qquad u(x,0)=u_0(x),
\]
where $a,p:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ are smooth, bounded, and uniformly positive. The system is said to be null-controllable at time $T>0$ if for every $u_0$ in a suitable function space (e.g., $L^2(0,\infty)$) there exists a control $v\in L^2(0,T)$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(\cdot,T)\equiv 0$.

It is known that for the constant-coefficient case $a\equiv p\equiv 1$ the system is not null-controllable at any time $T>0$.

(a) Determine whether this lack of null-controllability persists for all admissible smooth, bounded, uniformly positive coefficients $a(x)$ and $p(x)$.

(b) More generally, determine whether the same negative result holds when the coefficients $a$, $p$ depend on both $x$ and $t$, when a bounded lower-order potential term $c(x,t)u$ is added to the equation, and when a semilinear term $f(u)$ (with $f$ globally Lipschitz, $f(0)=0$) is added on the half-line.
category_tag: Null-controllability of heat equations on unbounded domains
status_search_result: The lack of null-controllability for the constant-coefficient heat equation on the half-line has been reproved by elementary/Fokas-method techniques (Kalimeris–Özsarı, 2020), and recent works treat null-controllability of 1D heat equations with variable coefficients (including with internal point masses) on bounded intervals via backstepping or spectral methods. However, a comprehensive extension of the half-line negative result to fully general variable-coefficient (in $x$ and $t$), lower-order potential, and semilinear settings does not appear to be settled in the literature; the question as posed remains, in its full generality, open.

context_brief: Asymptotic growth of diagonal centerpole numbers
original_question: What is the growth rate of the sequence {c_r^0(R^r)}_{r=1}^∞? Is it exponential or polynomial in r?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer r, consider the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^r$ together with the operation of inversion at a point $c\in\mathbb{R}^r$, namely $x\mapsto 2c-x$. A subset $S\subset\mathbb{R}^r$ is called symmetric with center $c$ if $S=2c-S$. 

Call a subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^r$ a diagonal $r$-centerpole for $\mathbb{R}^r$ if:
(i) $C$ is contained in the diagonal $\Delta=\{(t,t,\dots,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^r$, and
(ii) for every coloring $\chi:\mathbb{R}^r\to\{1,2,\dots,r\}$ of $\mathbb{R}^r$ into $r$ colors, there exists a point $c\in C$ and an unbounded monochromatic subset $S\subset\mathbb{R}^r$ that is symmetric with center $c$ (that is, $\chi$ is constant on $S$ and $S=2c-S$).

Define the diagonal centerpole number 
$$c^0_r(\mathbb{R}^r)\;=\;\min\bigl\{|C|:C\text{ is a diagonal }r\text{-centerpole for }\mathbb{R}^r\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $c^0_r(\mathbb{R}^r)$ admits an upper bound that grows exponentially in $r$ and a lower bound that grows polynomially in $r$. Determine the true asymptotic growth rate of the sequence $\bigl(c^0_r(\mathbb{R}^r)\bigr)_{r=1}^{\infty}$: is it polynomial or exponential in $r$?

Related work by Banakh and collaborators on centerpole sets for colorings of abelian groups establishes only the exponential upper / polynomial lower bound gap; no source confirming the problem has been settled was found.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: For a general control system Σ = (M, U, F) on a manifold M and a closed target set A ⊆ M, what sufficient conditions guarantee the existence of feedback laws that locally asymptotically stabilize A? In particular, when can one certify that A can be rendered invariant, that there exists a dynamical system for which A is at least a local attractor, and that these sufficient conditions are constructive enough to lead to actual controller design rather than only existence statements? A further part of the problem is to identify appropriate canonical classes of control systems in which such constructive sufficient conditions might be formulated.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction asking for constructive sufficient conditions for feedback stabilization of closed sets in fully general control systems on manifolds. While many partial results exist for specific subclasses (e.g. control-affine systems on R^n via control-Lyapunov functions and Sontag-type formulas, homogeneous systems, and CLSS frameworks), no general constructive theory covering arbitrary Σ = (M, U, F) and arbitrary closed targets A is known. The problem appears to remain open in its full generality.

original_question: For Euclidean spaces R^n equipped with central symmetries, calculate or estimate the centerpole numbers c_r^λ(R^n) for various choices of the number of colors r, the threshold λ, and the dimension n.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ be an integer. Equip $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the family of all central symmetries $s_c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$, $s_c(x)=2c-x$, for $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a subset $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and a point $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$, write $A_c=A\cap s_c(A)$ for the largest subset of $A$ that is centrally symmetric about $c$.

Fix nonnegative integers $r$ (the number of colors) and a cardinal/real threshold $\lambda$ (the size threshold). A subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called an $(r,\lambda)$-centerpole set if for every coloring $\chi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ there exist a center $c\in C$ and a color $i\in\{1,\dots,r\}$ such that the monochromatic set $\chi^{-1}(i)_c=\chi^{-1}(i)\cap s_c(\chi^{-1}(i))$ has cardinality (or measure/dimension, in the prescribed sense) at least $\lambda$. The centerpole number $c^{\lambda}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is defined as the smallest cardinality of an $(r,\lambda)$-centerpole subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

It is known that for finite nonnegative $r,\lambda,n$ with $r+\lambda\le n+1$,
$$c^{0}_{r}(\mathbb{R}^n)\;\le\;c^{\lambda}_{r}(\mathbb{R}^n)\;<\;2^{n}.$$

Problem. Compute, or give sharp lower and upper bounds for, the centerpole numbers $c^{\lambda}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for various choices of the parameters $r$, $\lambda$, and $n$.

Available references give only the bounds $c^0_r(\mathbb{R}^n)\le c^\lambda_r(\mathbb{R}^n)<2^n$ when $r+\lambda\le n+1$, with no general formula known. No subsequent work resolving the general computation was located.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: Can one develop computationally tractable topological and numerical tools that decide, a priori, whether a given stabilization problem admits a solution, with checks that are easier than brute-force numerical experimentation and that still provide certificates of accuracy when the control law or vector field data are noisy, approximate, or experimentally obtained? Computational homology and topological data analysis are proposed as possible ingredients in such certified decision procedures.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold (possibly with boundary), let $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ be a control set, and consider a control system $\dot x = f(x,u)$ where $f: M 	imes U 	o TM$ is a continuous vector field, with a designated equilibrium point $x^\star \in M$ (so that $f(x^\star,u^\star)=0$ for some $u^\star \in U$). A continuous feedback stabilizer is a continuous map $k: M 	o U$ with $k(x^\star)=u^\star$ such that $x^\star$ is a (locally or globally) asymptotically stable equilibrium of the closed-loop vector field $X_k(x):=f(x,k(x))$.

Develop a computationally tractable decision procedure with the following properties:

(a) Given as input a finite description of $(M,f,x^\star)$ — for instance, a sampled or approximate representation of $f$ corrupted by bounded noise $\|f-	ilde f\|_\infty \le \varepsilon$ — the procedure outputs one of the verdicts "stabilizable", "not stabilizable", or "inconclusive".

(b) The verdict "stabilizable" or "not stabilizable" comes with a mathematical certificate: a finite combinatorial / numerical object (for example, a persistent homology barcode, an index-pair computation in computational homology, a Conley index, or a sum-of-squares Lyapunov certificate) whose validity can be checked rigorously and which, together with the bound $\varepsilon$ on the data error, implies the stated conclusion for the true system $f$.

(c) The worst-case computational cost of the procedure is strictly lower than that of exhaustively simulating closed-loop trajectories on a fine grid of initial conditions and feedback laws.

Concretely: identify computable necessary conditions and computable sufficient conditions for the existence of a continuous (or, more generally, discontinuous but robust) feedback stabilizer of $x^\star$, expressible in terms of topological invariants of $M$, of the image of $f$, or of associated index pairs, such that the conditions (i) can be evaluated from finitely sampled, noisy data with explicit error bounds, and (ii) together yield a certified decision algorithm satisfying (a)–(c). Does such a procedure exist, and if so, what is its complexity?

original_question: Given an (Abelian) group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its dimension symmetry numbers mds_r(G).
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group (in particular one may take $G$ Abelian). Equip $G$ with the family $S$ of central symmetries, namely the involutions $s_g\colon G\to G$ defined by $s_g(x)=gx^{-1}g$ for $g\in G$. Let $\operatorname{asdim}$ denote the asymptotic dimension function defined on subsets of $G$ (with respect to the canonical group coarse structure): for $A\subseteq G$, $\operatorname{asdim}(A)$ is the smallest integer $n\ge 0$ such that for every $R>0$ there exists a uniformly bounded cover of $A$ of $R$-multiplicity at most $n+1$, and $\operatorname{asdim}(A)=\infty$ otherwise.

For a real number $r\ge 0$ and an integer $k\ge 1$ (a "symmetry number" parameter), define the dimension symmetry number
$$\mathrm{mds}_r(G)\;=\;\sup\bigl\{\operatorname{asdim}(A): A\subseteq G\text{ such that for every finite }F\subseteq A\text{ there exists a central symmetry }s\in S\text{ with }|s(F)\cap A|\ge r|F|\bigr\},$$
i.e. the maximal asymptotic dimension of a subset $A\subseteq G$ which is "$r$-symmetric" with respect to the family $S$ of central symmetries (the maximal symmetry number $\mathrm{ms}_r$ of the symmetry measure space $(G,\operatorname{asdim},S)$).

Problem: For an arbitrary (Abelian) group $G$, compute or give nontrivial estimates for the dimension symmetry numbers $\mathrm{mds}_r(G)$ as functions of $r$.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: Which new topological invariants, short of a complete conjugacy classification, can still capture qualitative behavior relevant to stability and stabilization of dynamical and control systems on manifolds? In particular, can one choose the homotopy appearing in the cited asymptotic-stabilization obstruction result so that the entire homotopy is itself asymptotically stabilizing, and can an analogous invariant-based program be extended beyond autonomous dynamical systems to general input-output systems in a compositional way?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $\mathcal{X}(M)$ denote the space of continuous vector fields on $M$, equipped with the compact-open topology. Given $X \in \mathcal{X}(M)$ and a compact subset $A \subset M$, we say that $A$ is asymptotically stable for $X$ if (i) $A$ is Lyapunov stable (every neighborhood $U$ of $A$ admits a neighborhood $V \subset U$ of $A$ whose forward trajectories under $X$ remain in $U$), and (ii) $A$ is locally attracting (some neighborhood of $A$ has all forward trajectories converging to $A$). The vector field $X$ is said to asymptotically stabilize $A$ when $A$ is asymptotically stable for $X$.

Suppose the following obstruction-type result holds: if $X_0, X_1 \in \mathcal{X}(M)$ each asymptotically stabilize a common compact set $A$, then under appropriate topological conditions there exists a continuous homotopy $\{X_s\}_{s\in[0,1]} \subset \mathcal{X}(M)$ joining $X_0$ to $X_1$.

Question. Can such a homotopy $\{X_s\}_{s\in[0,1]}$ always be chosen so that, for every $s \in [0,1]$, the vector field $X_s$ also asymptotically stabilizes $A$? That is, can the connecting path be taken to lie entirely inside the subspace of vector fields that asymptotically stabilize $A$?

Companion question. Formulate, and determine the existence of, an analogous theory of topological invariants — capturing qualitative behavior relevant to stability and stabilization (short of full conjugacy classification) — that extends in a compositional manner from autonomous dynamical systems on manifolds to general input-output control systems (i.e., systems with inputs and outputs that can be interconnected by series, parallel, and feedback composition), so that the invariants are well-defined on input-output systems and respect these composition operations.
status_search_result: Searches indicate the question of whether the homotopy connecting two asymptotically stabilizing vector fields can itself remain asymptotically stabilizing throughout is an active follow-up question discussed in the literature on obstructions to asymptotic stabilization, with no published resolution found. The compositional extension of invariant-based qualitative theory to general input-output systems is similarly stated as an open direction. No source claims a complete solution.

original_question: Given a group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its centerpole numbers c_r^λ(G).
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group, equipped with the family $S$ of central symmetries, where for each $g\in G$ the central symmetry centered at $g$ is the involution $s_g:G\to G$ defined by $s_g(x)=gx^{-1}g$. Let $\operatorname{asdim}$ denote the asymptotic-dimension type ideal of "small" subsets of $G$ (the family of subsets $A\subseteq G$ of asymptotic dimension less than that of $G$, or, in the finite case, the ideal of proper subsets); together $(G,\operatorname{asdim},S)$ forms what is called a symmetry measure space.

For a cardinal $\lambda$ and an integer $r\geq 2$, define the centerpole number $c_r^\lambda(G)$ as the smallest cardinality of a subset $C\subseteq G$ (a "centerpole") with the following property: for every coloring $\chi:G\to \lambda$ of $G$ into $\lambda$ colors such that no color class lies in $\operatorname{asdim}$ (i.e., every color class is "large"), there exist $r$ distinct color classes $A_1,\dots,A_r$ and an element $c\in C$ such that $s_c(A_i)\cap A_j$ is large for all $1\le i,j\le r$ — equivalently, $C$ meets the "center" of every $\lambda$-coloring of $G$ whose monochromatic classes are all large in the sense of $\operatorname{asdim}$.

Problem: Given a group $G$, compute or estimate the centerpole numbers $c_r^\lambda(G)$ for all integers $r\geq 2$ and cardinals $\lambda\geq 2$.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: How can one identify a nonlinear system, or at least an appropriate global equivalence class of nonlinear systems, from data at a global scale rather than only along finite trajectories or in local neighborhoods? In particular, how can one detect unstable equilibria and build a theory combining topological methods, topological data analysis, and modern high-dimensional probability, while also clarifying how approaches such as neural networks, Gaussian processes, and Koopman-operator methods can be developed into a global identification framework?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time nonlinear dynamical system on a smooth manifold M of the form x_{k+1} = f(x_k) + w_k, where f : M -> M is an unknown smooth map and {w_k} is a noise process, observed through samples y_k = h(x_k) + v_k for some (possibly known) observation map h. Existing identification theory typically reconstructs f either (a) along finite trajectories of bounded length, with statistical guarantees that depend on a single initialization, or (b) in a local neighborhood of a stable equilibrium or invariant set where linearization is informative.

Develop a theory of *global* nonlinear system identification with the following components:

1. Define a precise notion of global equivalence class [f] of nonlinear systems (for instance via topological conjugacy of flows, equivalence of Morse decompositions, or equality of Koopman operator spectral data on a fixed function space) such that two maps f, g lie in the same class iff their long-term qualitative dynamics on M agree.

2. Given a data set D = {(x_k, x_{k+1})} (or {y_k}) drawn from possibly multiple initial conditions and possibly off-trajectory queries, give a statistical estimator [\hat f] of the equivalence class [f], together with finite-sample, high-dimensional concentration guarantees of the form
   P( d([\hat f], [f]) > \varepsilon ) \le \delta(n, \varepsilon, M, f),
   where d is a metric on equivalence classes (e.g. interleaving distance of associated persistence modules, or a metric on Koopman spectra).

3. Provide identifiability conditions on the sampling distribution and on f under which all equilibria of f - including unstable equilibria, periodic orbits, and other invariant sets of arbitrary Morse index - can be recovered consistently from D, and prove matching impossibility results when these conditions fail.

4. Show how the framework specializes to and unifies the following classes of estimators: (i) neural-network parameterizations \hat f_\theta trained by empirical risk minimization, (ii) Gaussian process regression with kernels on M, and (iii) finite-dimensional approximations of the Koopman operator (e.g. EDMD), giving in each case explicit conditions under which the estimator recovers the global equivalence class rather than only a local model.

5. Integrate tools from topological data analysis (persistent homology of sublevel sets, Conley index, Morse theory) with modern high-dimensional probability (concentration on manifolds, empirical process theory in non-Donsker regimes) to establish the guarantees in (2)-(3).

The problem is to produce such a framework with proven theorems, or to establish fundamental obstructions that prevent it.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open research direction in nonlinear system identification. While there is active work on Koopman-based identification, neural ODEs, Gaussian-process system ID, and topological data analysis for dynamics, no comprehensive global identification framework with the requested topological + high-dimensional-probability guarantees and recovery of unstable equilibria has been established.

context_brief: Centerpole finiteness for the free group F2
original_question: Does the free group F_2 have finite centerpole numbers c_r^0(F_2) for every integer r?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group. For a subset $A\subseteq G$ and a point $c\in G$, the reflection of $A$ with respect to $c$ is the set $cA^{-1}c=\{ca^{-1}c:a\in A\}$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called symmetric with respect to $c$ if $A=cA^{-1}c$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is unbounded if it is infinite (equivalently, not contained in any finite subset).

For a positive integer $r$, a subset $C\subseteq G$ is called an $r$-centerpole in $G$ if for every coloring $\chi:G\to\{1,2,\dots,r\}$ there exists an infinite monochromatic subset $A\subseteq G$ that is symmetric with respect to some point $c\in C$. Define
$$c^{0}_{r}(G)=\min\{|C|:C\subseteq G\text{ is an }r\text{-centerpole in }G\},$$
allowing the value $\infty$ if no finite $r$-centerpole exists.

Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators. Question: is $c^{0}_{r}(F_2)$ finite for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$?
status_search_result: Centerpole numbers were introduced by Banakh and Protasov / Banakh and Chervak in the context of colorings of groups, with most known results concerning abelian groups. Available sources note that very little is known about centerpole numbers of non-commutative groups, in particular the free group $F_2$. No published resolution of the finiteness question for $c^0_r(F_2)$ was located.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: How can one formulate a principled theory of topological obstructions to stabilization that is invariant under feedback reparametrization rather than depending on a particular parametrization of the control system? More concretely, the open problem is to replace obstruction results that rely on a chosen control-system presentation with feedback-invariant statements depending only on genuinely intrinsic data, such as the underlying manifold M and the target set to be stabilized, while still retaining useful system-specific conclusions when necessary.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $S \subset M$ be a closed (compact) target submanifold to be locally asymptotically stabilized by a control system on $M$. A control system on $M$ may be presented in many forms (for instance, as a parametrized family of vector fields $\dot{x} = f(x,u)$ with $u$ ranging in a control set $U$, or as an affine distribution, etc.); two presentations are said to be feedback equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a (state-dependent) reparametrization of the control inputs together with a diffeomorphism of $M$. A statement about the system is called feedback invariant if it depends only on the equivalence class under feedback equivalence, i.e., only on intrinsic geometric data attached to $(M, S)$ and the control-affine structure, not on a particular choice of parametrization.

Many known topological obstructions to the existence of a continuous (or smooth) stabilizing feedback for $S \subset M$ are stated in terms of a specific parametrization of the control system and are therefore not manifestly feedback invariant.

Problem: Develop a principled theory of topological obstructions to local asymptotic stabilization of a target set $S$ in a manifold $M$ that is fully invariant under feedback reparametrization. Concretely, reformulate the existing obstruction results so that all hypotheses and conclusions are expressed solely in terms of feedback-invariant data (intrinsic to $M$, $S$, and the equivalence class of the control system), while still being strong enough to recover the system-specific conclusions of the parametrization-dependent theory in the cases where such conclusions are needed.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the recent monograph on topological obstructions to stability and stabilization (2023). Subsequent literature (e.g., 2025 surveys and follow-ups on the dynamics of control) continues to discuss the lack of feedback-invariant formulations of obstruction results without reporting a complete resolution. No source found establishes a fully feedback-invariant general theory replacing parametrization-dependent obstructions.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: What is the most meaningful way to extend obstruction-theoretic stability and stabilization results from deterministic systems on manifolds to stochastic systems with disturbances? Existing noise-aware results often focus on moments, but the open problem is to build a genuinely satisfactory stochastic analogue of the deterministic topological theory.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth (finite-dimensional, paracompact, connected) manifold and consider a control system on $M$ of the form
$$\dot x(t) = f(x(t),u(t)), \qquad x(t)\in M,\ u(t)\in U,$$
where $f$ is smooth in $x$ and $U$ is a set of admissible control values. For such deterministic systems there is a well-developed obstruction-theoretic theory of (global) stability and stabilization: given a target equilibrium $x^\star\in M$, topological invariants of $M$ (such as the Euler characteristic, characteristic classes of associated vector bundles, and homotopy-theoretic obstructions to the existence of nowhere-vanishing or transverse sections) provide obstructions to the existence of a continuous feedback $u=k(x)$ that renders $x^\star$ globally asymptotically stable, and more generally classify when stabilizing feedbacks exist up to homotopy.

Now consider a stochastic perturbation of such a system, modelled e.g. by an Itô stochastic differential equation
$$dx(t) = f(x(t),u(t))\,dt + \sigma(x(t),u(t))\,dW(t)$$
on $M$, where $W$ is a standard Brownian motion and $\sigma$ is a smooth noise coefficient (so that disturbances are genuinely incorporated, not merely averaged out into moment bounds).

Problem. Formulate a notion of "stochastic global asymptotic stabilizability" of an equilibrium (or invariant set) $x^\star$ of such a controlled stochastic system on $M$, together with associated topological obstructions, that constitutes a genuine analogue of the deterministic obstruction-theoretic theory, in the following sense:

(a) When $\sigma\equiv 0$, the notion and the obstructions reduce exactly to the deterministic ones.

(b) The obstructions are topological invariants of $M$ (and of any associated bundles entering the problem), independent of the particular drift, diffusion, and feedback chosen.

(c) The theory is not merely a statement about moments of $x(t)$ but captures pathwise/almost-sure or distributional stabilization in a way that yields necessary topological conditions on $M$ analogous to (and ideally strictly refining) the deterministic ones.

Construct such a theory, or prove that no theory satisfying (a)–(c) can exist beyond what is already implied by the deterministic obstructions.
status_search_result: No literature was located that develops a genuinely topological/obstruction-theoretic analogue of deterministic global stabilizability theory for stochastic control systems on manifolds. Existing stochastic stabilization results focus on Lyapunov/moment criteria rather than on topological obstructions, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in a graph G. For integers q >= 1, r >= 1, and 1 <= k <= qr, is the maximum number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices attained by the disjoint union of q copies of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,r}? Equivalently, does Theta(k, qr, r) = phi(k, qK_{r,r}) hold for every k = 1, ..., qr, where Theta(k, n, r) is the maximum of phi(k, G) over simple r-regular graphs G on 2n vertices?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\phi(k,G)$ denote the number of matchings of size $k$ in $G$ (i.e., the number of sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges of $G$). For positive integers $n$ and $r$ with $r \le n$, let $\mathcal{G}(2n,r)$ denote the set of all simple $r$-regular graphs on $2n$ vertices, and define
$$\Theta(k,n,r) := \max\{\phi(k,G) : G \in \mathcal{G}(2n,r)\}.$$
Let $K_{r,r}$ denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of size $r$, and for a positive integer $q$ let $qK_{r,r}$ denote the disjoint union of $q$ copies of $K_{r,r}$ (a simple $r$-regular graph on $2qr$ vertices).

Prove or disprove: for every choice of integers $q \ge 1$, $r \ge 1$, and $1 \le k \le qr$,
$$\Theta(k, qr, r) = \phi(k, qK_{r,r}).$$
Equivalently, the disjoint union of $q$ copies of $K_{r,r}$ maximizes the number of $k$-matchings among all simple $r$-regular graphs on $2qr$ vertices, for every $k$.

The conjecture is therefore established asymptotically but is not known in full generality for all $q,r,k$.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: What additional theory and invariants can handle stabilization problems in which the relevant attractor or target set has Euler characteristic zero, a regime that includes many abundant examples such as odd-dimensional manifolds, Lie groups, and periodic orbits? These cases are especially difficult, so the problem is to develop methods that improve on the current reliance on retraction theory or otherwise yield a finer classification of zero-Euler-characteristic situations.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a research direction: zero Euler characteristic targets (odd-dimensional manifolds, Lie groups, periodic orbits) are widely recognized as a regime where retraction-theoretic obstructions to feedback stabilization are silent. While partial advances exist (e.g. Coron's results on stabilization of driftless systems on Lie groups via time-varying feedback, and obstructions from homotopy of vector fields), no general theory of invariants providing a fine classification in this regime has been established. The overall problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in G, and let lambda(k, n, r) be the minimum of phi(k, G) over all r-regular bipartite multigraphs G on 2n vertices. For a multigraph $G$, let $\phi(k,G)$ denote the number of $k$-matchings in $G$, that is, the number of sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. Let $\mathcal{G}_{bi,mult}(2n,r)$ denote the set of $r$-regular bipartite multigraphs on $2n$ vertices (with vertex bipartition into two parts of size $n$), and define

paper_title: Solving Open Problems in Right Alternative Rings with Z-Module Reasoning
original_question: Let R be a right alternative ring, meaning a possibly nonassociative ring in which x(yy) = xyy for all x and y. If the associator is defined by (x, y, z) = (xy)z - x(yz), is it always true that for every x, y in R one has ((x, x, y)(x, x, y))x((x, x, y)(x, x, y)) = 0? Equivalently, must (x, x, y)^2 x (x, x, y)^2 vanish identically in every right alternative ring?
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a right alternative ring; that is, $R$ is a (not necessarily associative) ring satisfying the identity $x(yy) = (xy)y$ for all $x, y \in R$. Define the associator of three elements by
$$(x, y, z) := (xy)z - x(yz).$$
Prove or disprove: for all $x, y \in R$,
$$(x, x, y)^2 \, x \, (x, x, y)^2 = 0,$$
where $(x,x,y)^2$ denotes $(x,x,y)\cdot(x,x,y)$ and the whole expression is the product $\big((x,x,y)(x,x,y)\big)\,x\,\big((x,x,y)(x,x,y)\big)$ (with some fixed association, e.g. left-to-right).
status_search_result: The identity $(x,x,y)^2 x (x,x,y)^2 = 0$ in right alternative rings was established by automated theorem proving (Z-module reasoning / ZMR system) work of Stevens and others, confirming the conjecture as a theorem. It is no longer an open problem.

original_question: Let omega(k, n, r) be the minimum number of k-matchings among r-regular r-colorable multigraphs on 2n vertices. For each fixed r >= 3, does the perfect-matching minimum omega(n, n, r) grow exponentially in n?
self_contained_problem:
For integers $r\ge 1$ and $n\ge 1$, let $\mathcal{G}_{co,mult}(2n,r)$ denote the class of $r$-regular multigraphs (loops and parallel edges allowed) on $2n$ labeled vertices that are $r$-edge-colorable, i.e., whose edges can be partitioned into $r$ perfect matchings. For a graph $G\in\mathcal{G}_{co,mult}(2n,r)$ and an integer $k$ with $0\le k\le n$, let $\phi(k,G)$ denote the number of $k$-matchings in $G$ (sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges). Define
$$\omega(k,n,r) := \min\{\phi(k,G) : G\in\mathcal{G}_{co,mult}(2n,r)\}.$$
In particular, $\omega(n,n,r)$ is the minimum number of perfect matchings in any $r$-regular $r$-edge-colorable multigraph on $2n$ vertices.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$, the sequence $\omega(n,n,r)$ grows exponentially in $n$; that is, there exist constants $c_r>1$ and $C_r>0$ such that $\omega(n,n,r)\ge C_r\, c_r^{\,n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
status_search_result: The case $r=3$ follows from the Lovász–Plummer conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs, proved by Esperet, Kardoš, King, Král' and Norine (2011), since every $3$-edge-colorable cubic multigraph is bridgeless. The bipartite/$r$-edge-colorable case for general $r$ follows from Schrijver's lower bound on permanents of doubly stochastic matrices. The general (nonbipartite) case for $r\ge 4$ does not appear to have a published resolution beyond these reductions; the conjecture is therefore at least partially established.

paper_title: Solving Open Problems in Right Alternative Rings with Z-Module Reasoning
context_brief: Generalized open problem in right alternative rings
original_question: Let R be a right alternative ring, meaning a possibly nonassociative ring in which x(yy) = xyy for all x and y, and let the associator be (x, y, z) = (xy)z - x(yz). For a positive integer n, does the identity (x, x, y)^2 x^n (x, x, y)^2 = 0 hold for all x, y in R, where x^n denotes the n-fold power of x used in the paper's generalized conjecture? In other words, must the element (x, x, y)^2 annihilate x^n on both sides in this specific pattern for every positive integer n?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be a right alternative ring, that is, a (not necessarily associative) ring satisfying the identity x(yy) = (xy)y for all x, y ∈ R. For x, y, z ∈ R define the associator (x, y, z) = (xy)z − x(yz). For a positive integer n, let x^n denote the right-normed power defined recursively by x^1 = x and x^{k+1} = x^k · x.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer n and for all x, y ∈ R,
   (x, x, y)^2 · x^n · (x, x, y)^2 = 0,
where (x, x, y)^2 means the square (x, x, y)·(x, x, y) of the associator.
status_search_result: The generalized identity (x,x,y)^2 x^n (x,x,y)^2 = 0 in right alternative rings has been established (a computer-assisted proof of this identity for every positive integer n is reported in the literature on automated reasoning for nonassociative rings).

original_question: Let G be an infinite r-regular graph, and let h_G(p) denote its p-matching entropy, defined from finite graph approximations G_k by h_G(p) = limsup_{k->infty} log(phi(m_k, G_k)) / |V_k| when 2m_k / |V_k| -> p. If h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) is the corresponding entropy for a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, is it always true that h_G(p) <= h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) for every p in [0, 1]?
self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be an infinite r-regular graph with a countable vertex set. For a finite graph H, let φ(m,H) denote the number of matchings of size m in H (a matching being a set of pairwise non-incident edges). 

Approximate G by an exhaustion: a sequence of finite induced subgraphs G_k=(V_k,E_k) with |V_k|→∞ and V_k↑V. For p∈[0,1], define the p-matching entropy of G by
   h_G(p) = limsup_{k→∞} (1/|V_k|) log φ(m_k, G_k),
where the limsup is taken over all sequences (m_k) of nonnegative integers satisfying 2m_k/|V_k|→p.

Let K_{r,r} denote the complete bipartite graph with r+r vertices, and let ∞·K_{r,r} denote the disjoint union of countably many copies of K_{r,r}. Define h_{∞·K_{r,r}}(p) analogously.

Question: Is it true that for every infinite r-regular graph G and every p∈[0,1],
   h_G(p) ≤ h_{∞·K_{r,r}}(p) ?
status_search_result: The asymptotic form of the upper matching conjecture was established by Ilinca and Kahn, who proved the corresponding asymptotic inequality on matching entropies for r-regular graphs. The finite (non-asymptotic) Upper Matching Conjecture of Friedland, Krop, and Markström was subsequently proved for all sufficiently large d-regular graphs by Davies, Jenssen, Perkins, and Roberts (J. Combin. Theory B, 2021), which in particular implies the asymptotic entropy inequality. Thus the asymptotic upper matching conjecture is regarded as solved.
