paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
context_brief: Inflection points on projectively flat surfaces
original_question: Estimate the minimum possible number of inflection points of a closed curve lying on a Riemann surface equipped with a projectively flat connection.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a Riemann surface (a connected smooth 2-manifold equipped with a complex structure) endowed with a projectively flat affine connection $
abla$; that is, a torsion-free affine connection on $T\Sigma$ whose projective equivalence class is locally trivial, so that locally there exist coordinates in which the geodesics of $
abla$ are straight lines (up to reparametrization). Given a smooth immersed closed curve $\gamma : S^1 	o \Sigma$, an inflection point of $\gamma$ is a point at which the velocity vector $\dot\gamma$ and the acceleration $
abla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma$ are linearly dependent (equivalently, a point where $\gamma$ has contact of order $\geq 2$ with a $
abla$-geodesic). 

Determine sharp lower bounds for the number of inflection points of a closed curve $\gamma$ on $(\Sigma,
abla)$, possibly depending on the topology of $\Sigma$, the homotopy/homology class of $\gamma$, or the projective monodromy of $
abla$. In particular, give an estimate for the minimum possible number of inflection points among all smooth closed curves on a Riemann surface equipped with a projectively flat connection.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the problem of estimating the minimum number of inflection points of a closed curve on a Riemann surface with a projectively flat connection. While there is a classical line of work on inflections of curves (Möbius's theorem, four-vertex-type results, and generalizations to projective/affine connections), no source examined here states a complete sharp answer to this specific problem, so its current status is taken to be unknown.

original_question: Is there a universal constant C such that every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} satisfies H[\hat{f}^2] <= C * I[f], where H[\hat{f}^2] is the spectral entropy and I[f] is the total influence?
self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier–Walsh expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat{f}(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i,$$
where $\widehat{f}(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)$. Parseval's identity gives $\sum_S \widehat{f}(S)^2=1$, so $\{\widehat{f}(S)^2\}_{S\subseteq[n]}$ is a probability distribution on the subsets of $[n]$. Define the spectral entropy
$$H[\widehat{f}^{\,2}]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \widehat{f}(S)^2 \log_2\!\left(\frac{1}{\widehat{f}(S)^2}\right),$$
with the convention $0\log(1/0)=0$. The total influence is
$$I[f]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} |S|\,\widehat{f}(S)^2,$$
equivalently $I[f]=\sum_{i=1}^n \Pr_x[f(x)\neq f(x^{\oplus i})]$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ flips the $i$-th coordinate of $x$.

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$, independent of $n$, such that for every $n\geq 1$ and every Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
$$H[\widehat{f}^{\,2}]\;\leq\; C\cdot I[f]\;?$$
status_search_result: The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture of Friedgut–Kalai remains open. Recent work (Combinatorica, 2025; arXiv:2312.08271) provides the strongest known partial bound, showing $H[\widehat{f}^{\,2}] = O(I(f) + \sum_k I_k(f)\log(1/I_k(f)))$, but a full linear bound by $C\cdot I[f]$ for a universal constant $C$ has not been established. Related results (composition theorems, lower bounds on constants for the min-entropy variant) confirm the conjecture is still actively studied and unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
original_question: For a closed curve on a Riemann surface with a projectively flat connection, estimate the number of affine vertices. Under the additional assumption that the inflection points are isolated, what relationship holds between the number of affine vertices and the number of inflection points?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a Riemann surface equipped with a projectively flat connection $\nabla$ (that is, a torsion-free affine connection whose unparametrized geodesics define a flat projective structure on $\Sigma$). Let $\gamma:S^1\to\Sigma$ be an immersed closed curve.

A point $p=\gamma(t)$ is called an inflection point of $\gamma$ if the velocity vector $\dot\gamma(t)$ and the acceleration $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma(t)$ are linearly dependent (equivalently, if $\gamma$ has higher-order contact with a $\nabla$-geodesic at $p$). At a non-inflection point one may, using the projectively flat structure, define a notion of osculating conic; an affine vertex of $\gamma$ is a point at which the osculating conic has contact of order at least five with $\gamma$ (equivalently, a critical point of the projective/affine curvature function defined off the inflection locus).

Assume that the set of inflection points of $\gamma$ is isolated, and let $V(\gamma)$ denote the number of affine vertices of $\gamma$ and $I(\gamma)$ the number of inflection points.

Establish a sharp lower bound for $V(\gamma)$ in terms of topological and geometric invariants of $(\Sigma,\nabla,\gamma)$, and determine the precise relationship (for instance, an inequality of the form $V(\gamma)\ge f(I(\gamma))$ or a parity/congruence relation) between $V(\gamma)$ and $I(\gamma)$ that holds for every such curve.
status_search_result: A web search did not return any specific result establishing a sharp count of affine vertices versus inflection points for closed curves on Riemann surfaces with a projectively flat connection. While there is a substantial body of work on four-vertex-type theorems and on projective/affine structures on surfaces, no definitive resolution of this particular estimation problem could be located, so its current status is unclear.

context_brief: Noise stability of majority among LTFs
original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is a linear threshold function on an odd number n of variables, must it satisfy Stab_rho[f] >= Stab_rho[Maj_n] for every rho in [0,1]?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be an odd positive integer. For a Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1} and a parameter ρ ∈ [0,1], the noise stability of f at ρ is defined as
   Stab_ρ[f] = E[f(x) f(y)],
where x is uniformly distributed on {-1,1}^n and y ∈ {-1,1}^n is the ρ-correlated copy of x (each coordinate y_i independently equals x_i with probability (1+ρ)/2 and -x_i with probability (1-ρ)/2).

A linear threshold function (LTF) on {-1,1}^n is a function of the form f(x) = sign(a_0 + a_1 x_1 + ⋯ + a_n x_n) for some real coefficients a_0, a_1, …, a_n (with the convention that sign(0) is fixed to be either +1 or -1). The majority function on n (odd) variables is Maj_n(x) = sign(x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_n).

Question: Is it true that for every odd n and every linear threshold function f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1}, one has
   Stab_ρ[f] ≥ Stab_ρ[Maj_n]   for all ρ ∈ [0,1]?
status_search_result: The "Majority is Least Stable" conjecture has been disproved. Counterexamples were given by Jain (2017) for n = 5, with further counterexamples by Gopi and by Heilman–Kane. Subsequent work (Biswas–Sarkar, 2022) confirmed that the statement holds only for n = 1 and n = 3 and fails for every odd n ≥ 5.

context_brief: Global existence for affine curve flow
original_question: Prove the existence of a solution defined for all time for the evolution equation of curves in the affine plane given by ∂x/∂u = (1 + k p)x″, where u is a time parameter, x″ is the affine normal, k is the affine curvature, and p is the affine support function of the curve x.
self_contained_problem: Let $x(s,u)$ be a smooth one-parameter family of strictly convex closed curves in the affine plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ (equipped with the standard area form), parametrized in the spatial variable by affine arc length $s$ so that $\det(x_s, x_{ss}) = 1$. Denote by $x'' := x_{ss}$ the affine normal vector, by $k := \det(x_{ss}, x_{sss})$ the affine curvature, and by $p := -\det(x, x_s)$ the affine support function of the curve (so that $x = -p\, x'' + p'\, T$ in a suitable affine frame, where $T = x_s$). Consider the geometric evolution equation\n$$\frac{\partial x}{\partial u} = (1 + k p)\, x'',$$\nwhere $u \in [0, U)$ is the time parameter. Starting from any smooth strictly convex closed initial curve $x(\cdot, 0)$, prove that the solution $x(\cdot, u)$ of this evolution equation exists for all time $u \in [0, \infty)$.
status_search_result: A direct web search for this specific evolution equation $\partial x/\partial u = (1+kp)x''$ on affine plane curves did not surface a paper establishing time-global existence. Related affine and centro-affine curve flows (affine curve shortening, centro-affine normal flows) have well-developed long-time existence theories, but the specific flow stated here was not found to be resolved in the accessible literature; status is therefore inconclusive.

context_brief: Optimality of majority for correlation distillation
original_question: Fix r in N, odd n, and 0 < epsilon < 1/2. For f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, let P(f) be the probability that r independent epsilon-noisy copies of a uniform x all give the same output under f. Among odd functions f, is P(f) always maximized by a majority function Maj_k on some odd number k of inputs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $n$ be an odd positive integer, and fix $\epsilon \in (0, 1/2)$. For $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$, an $\epsilon$-noisy copy $y$ of $x$ is the random vector obtained by independently, for each coordinate $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, setting $y_i = x_i$ with probability $1-\epsilon$ and $y_i = -x_i$ with probability $\epsilon$. For a function $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$, define
$$P(f) \;=\; \Pr\!\left[f(y^{(1)}) = f(y^{(2)}) = \cdots = f(y^{(r)})\right],$$
where $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$ is chosen uniformly at random and, conditional on $x$, the vectors $y^{(1)},\dots,y^{(r)}$ are independent $\epsilon$-noisy copies of $x$. A function $f$ is called odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for every $x$. For each odd $k \le n$, let $\mathrm{Maj}_k : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be the function that depends only on the first $k$ coordinates and outputs the sign of their sum.

Question: Is it true that, for every choice of $r$, odd $n$, and $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, the maximum of $P(f)$ over all odd functions $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ is attained by $\mathrm{Maj}_k$ for some odd $k \le n$?
status_search_result: The question concerns whether majority functions maximize the r-wise agreement probability under noise among odd Boolean functions (a non-interactive correlation distillation question). Surveys and follow-up work on noise stability and NICD (e.g., Li–Médard 2018) discuss this and related conjectures; majority is known to be optimal in certain asymptotic regimes, but whether some majority always maximizes the r-wise moment for general parameters appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
context_brief: Stein property of tangent bundles of Hessian manifolds
original_question: Let M be a Hessian manifold with Hessian metric g, and suppose that the Riemannian manifold (M, g) is complete. Is the tangent bundle of M, equipped with its natural complex structure, a Stein manifold? In particular, if Ω is a convex domain in ℝⁿ containing no complete straight lines and Γ is a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group of Ω acting freely and properly discontinuously on Ω, is the tangent bundle over the quotient Ω/Γ a Stein manifold?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A Hessian manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a flat affine connection $
abla$ and a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, locally around every point, there exist affine coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$ (i.e. coordinates in which the Christoffel symbols of $
abla$ vanish) and a smooth real-valued function $\varphi$ with
$$g_{ij} \;=\;  rac{\partial^2 \varphi}{\partial x^i \partial x^j}.$$
Given such a Hessian structure, the tangent bundle $TM$ carries a canonical complex structure: in any affine local chart $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ on $M$ with fiber coordinates $(y^1,\dots,y^n)$ (so that a tangent vector at $x$ is $\sum_i y^i\,\partial/\partial x^i$), the functions
$$z^j \;=\; x^j + \sqrt{-1}\,y^j, \qquad j=1,\dots,n,$$
serve as holomorphic coordinates on $TM$, and the resulting complex structure is independent of the choice of affine chart. With respect to this complex structure, the metric on $TM$ obtained from $g$ via the local Kähler potential $\varphi(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ (extended to $TM$ in the obvious way) is Kähler.

A complex manifold $X$ is called a Stein manifold if it is holomorphically convex and holomorphic functions separate points of $X$.

Problem. 
(a) Let $(M,g)$ be a Hessian manifold and assume that the Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is complete. Endow $TM$ with the canonical complex structure described above. Is $TM$ necessarily a Stein manifold?

(b) Specifically, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex domain that contains no complete affine line, and let $\Gamma$ be a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group of $\Omega$ acting freely and properly discontinuously on $\Omega$, so that the quotient $M=\Omega/\Gamma$ inherits a Hessian structure. Is the tangent bundle $T(\Omega/\Gamma)$, with its canonical complex structure, a Stein manifold?
status_search_result: Web searches yielded general references on Hessian manifolds (Shima) and the canonical Kähler/complex structure on their tangent bundles, including recent works (e.g. a 2025 preprint on Born structures on the tangent bundle of a Hessian manifold and a 2025 preprint on topology and geometry of Hessian manifolds), but no source was found that explicitly settles whether the tangent bundle of an arbitrary complete Hessian manifold (or of $\Omega/\Gamma$ for $\Omega$ a convex domain without complete lines) is Stein. The status appears to be unresolved in the sources located.

original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is the intersection of k linear threshold functions, must its noise sensitivity satisfy NS_delta[f] <= O(sqrt(log k)) * sqrt(delta)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n,k\ge 1$. For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and a noise rate $\delta\in[0,1/2]$, define the noise sensitivity
$$\mathrm{NS}_\delta[f] \;=\; \Pr_{x,y}[f(x)\ne f(y)],$$
where $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is uniformly random and $y\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is obtained from $x$ by independently flipping each coordinate with probability $\delta$.

A linear threshold function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is a function of the form $\mathrm{sgn}(w_0+\sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i)$ for some real numbers $w_0,w_1,\dots,w_n$. Say that $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is the intersection of $k$ linear threshold functions if there exist linear threshold functions $g_1,\dots,g_k$ such that $f(x)=1$ iff $g_i(x)=1$ for all $i$, and $f(x)=-1$ otherwise.

Prove or disprove: there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n,k\ge 1$, every $\delta\in[0,1/2]$, and every $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ that is the intersection of $k$ linear threshold functions,
$$\mathrm{NS}_\delta[f] \;\le\; C\sqrt{\log k}\cdot\sqrt{\delta}.$$
status_search_result: Nazarov established the analogous bound in the Gaussian setting. Harsha–Klivans–Meka proved a weaker bound of the form $\log(k)^{O(1)}\delta^{1/6}$ for intersections of sufficiently regular halfspaces on the Boolean cube. Kane (2014) proved the optimal average-sensitivity bound $O(\sqrt{n\log k})$ for intersections of $k$ halfspaces on $\{-1,1\}^n$, which corresponds to the conjectured noise-sensitivity bound at $\delta=\Theta(1/n)$. The full Boolean-cube noise-sensitivity bound $\mathrm{NS}_\delta[f]\le O(\sqrt{\log k}\,\sqrt{\delta})$ for arbitrary $\delta$ does not appear to have been established in this generality; it remains a partially resolved conjecture.

paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
original_question: Study the stability of Hessian metrics under small deformations of affine structures. More precisely, if M is a compact Hessian manifold and one deforms M in the sense of affine-structure deformation, does every sufficiently small deformation of M again admit a Hessian metric?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold equipped with a Hessian structure $(D, g)$, that is, $D$ is a flat torsion-free affine connection on $M$ and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$ which is locally of the form $g = D^2 u$ for some smooth function $u$ (equivalently, in any local affine coordinate system $(x^1, \dots, x^n)$ adapted to $D$, the components of $g$ satisfy $g_{ij} = \partial^2 u/\partial x^i \partial x^j$). Such a pair $(D,g)$ is called a Hessian metric, and $(M, D, g)$ a compact Hessian manifold.

Consider deformations of $M$ in the sense of deformations of the underlying flat affine structure $D$: a smooth family $\{D_t\}_{t \in (-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)}$ of flat torsion-free affine connections on $M$ with $D_0 = D$.

Question: Does there exist $\delta > 0$ such that for every $t$ with $|t| < \delta$, the affine manifold $(M, D_t)$ admits a Hessian metric $g_t$ (i.e., a Riemannian metric locally expressible as $D_t^2 u_t$ for some smooth function $u_t$)?
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of the stability question for Hessian metrics under deformations of affine structures on a compact Hessian manifold. Recent works on Hessian manifolds (e.g., topology and curvature studies, affine Hermitian–Einstein theory) discuss related structural and topological constraints, but no clear theorem affirming or refuting general stability under small deformations of the affine connection was found.

original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be unbiased. For a random restriction z in {-1,0,1}^n where each coordinate is independently +1 or -1 with probability p/2 each and 0 with probability 1-p, with p < 1/2 and n odd, is E_z[|f(z)|] maximized when f is the majority function, identifying f with its multilinear expansion?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be an odd positive integer and let f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1} be an unbiased Boolean function (i.e., E[f(x)] = 0 when x is uniform on {-1,1}^n). Identify f with its multilinear polynomial extension, so that f is defined on all of [-1,1]^n by its (unique) multilinear expansion

  f(x) = Σ_{S ⊆ [n]} f̂(S) ∏_{i ∈ S} x_i.

Fix a parameter p ∈ (0, 1/2). Let z ∈ {-1, 0, 1}^n be a random vector whose coordinates are independent, with each coordinate equal to +1 with probability p/2, equal to -1 with probability p/2, and equal to 0 with probability 1 - p.

Let Maj_n : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1} denote the majority function, Maj_n(x) = sign(Σ_i x_i).

Question: Is it true that, among all unbiased f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1}, the quantity

  E_z [ |f(z)| ]

(where f(z) is computed via the multilinear extension) is maximized by f = Maj_n?

paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
context_brief: New examples of compact Hessian manifolds
original_question: Construct examples of compact Hessian manifolds other than direct products of hyperbolic compact Hessian manifolds and flat compact Hessian manifolds. In particular, beyond the known example of a compact Hessian manifold with a nontrivial fiber bundle structure whose base is hyperbolic and whose fiber is flat, can one construct an example having no fiber bundle structure, perhaps by using deformation theory of affine structures?
self_contained_problem:
A Hessian manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a flat affine connection $\nabla$ together with a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, locally on every affine coordinate chart $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ for $\nabla$, there exists a smooth function $\varphi$ with $g_{ij}=\partial^2\varphi/\partial x^i\partial x^j$. A compact Hessian manifold $(M,\nabla,g)$ is called flat if $g$ is a flat Riemannian metric, and is called hyperbolic if its universal cover, realized as an open convex domain in affine space via the developing map, is a regular convex cone (equivalently, the Koszul form is negative definite, giving a complete Hessian metric of negative Ricci-type curvature in the Koszul sense).

Two basic constructions give compact Hessian manifolds: direct products of hyperbolic compact Hessian manifolds with flat compact Hessian manifolds, and total spaces of certain non-trivial fiber bundles built in analogy with Kuga fiber varieties, whose base is a hyperbolic compact Hessian manifold and whose fiber is a flat compact Hessian manifold.

Problem: Construct a compact Hessian manifold $(M,\nabla,g)$ that is not isomorphic, as a Hessian manifold, to any direct product of a hyperbolic compact Hessian manifold and a flat compact Hessian manifold, and that, in addition, admits no smooth fiber bundle structure $F\to M\to B$ in which $B$ is a hyperbolic compact Hessian manifold and $F$ is a flat compact Hessian manifold compatible with the Hessian structure. In particular, produce such an example via the deformation theory of flat affine structures: starting from a known compact Hessian manifold, deform its affine structure within the moduli of flat affine structures so that the deformed structure still admits a Hessian metric but the resulting compact Hessian manifold has neither a product nor such a fiber-bundle decomposition.
status_search_result: Recent work (2025) discusses topology and geometry of Hessian manifolds and constructs new families of compact Hessian manifolds of Koszul type with negative scalar curvature, but it is not clear from available sources whether a compact Hessian manifold has been produced that is provably neither a product of hyperbolic and flat factors nor a hyperbolic-base/flat-fiber bundle, particularly via deformation of affine structures. The problem appears to remain open or its status is not clearly documented.

original_question: Let A subseteq F2^n. If one must remove epsilon * 2^n elements from A to make it triangle-free, meaning there do not exist x, y, x+y in A, must the probability over uniform independent x,y in F2^n satisfy Pr[x,y,x+y in A] >= poly(epsilon)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is said to be triangle-free if there do not exist $x, y \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that $x \in A$, $y \in A$, and $x+y \in A$. For $\epsilon > 0$, suppose $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has the property that any triangle-free subset $A' \subseteq A$ satisfies $|A \setminus A'| \geq \epsilon \cdot 2^n$ (i.e.\ one must delete at least $\epsilon \cdot 2^n$ elements from $A$ to make it triangle-free). Determine whether there exist absolute constants $C, c > 0$ (independent of $n$ and $A$) such that
$$\Pr_{x,y}\bigl[\,x \in A,\ y \in A,\ x+y \in A\,\bigr] \;\geq\; c\,\epsilon^{C},$$
where $x, y$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. That is, does the arithmetic triangle removal lemma in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ admit a polynomial bound?
status_search_result: Green asked whether the arithmetic triangle removal lemma in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ admits a polynomial bound. Fox and Lovász (Sauermann) established a tight polynomial bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces over finite fields, determining the best-possible exponent for every prime $p$ (for $p=2$ the exponent constants are explicit), thereby resolving the polynomial-bound question affirmatively.

paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
original_question: Probability density functions are usually written as f(x; θ), where x lies in the sample space and θ is a parameter, and Amari and others introduced a natural Hessian metric on the parameter space. Find and study an appropriate geometry on the product of the sample space and the parameter space, taking into account that the resulting geometry may depend on the choice of a statistically meaningful θ-coordinate system.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a sample space (a measurable space, typically an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with a reference measure) and let $\Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ be an open parameter domain. Let $\{f(x;	heta) : 	heta \in \Theta\}$ be a smooth statistical model of probability density functions on $X$, so that for each $	heta \in \Theta$, $f(\cdot;	heta) \geq 0$ and $\int_X f(x;	heta)\,dx = 1$. Recall that the Fisher information matrix
$$g_{ij}(	heta) = \int_X  rac{\partial \log f(x;	heta)}{\partial 	heta^i} rac{\partial \log f(x;	heta)}{\partial 	heta^j} f(x;	heta)\,dx$$
defines a Riemannian metric on $\Theta$. For an exponential family $f(x;	heta) = \exp(	heta^i T_i(x) - \psi(	heta))$, this metric is Hessian: $g_{ij}(	heta) = \partial_i\partial_j \psi(	heta)$, giving $\Theta$ the structure of a Hessian manifold (in the sense of Shima and Amari).

Problem. Construct and study a natural geometric structure (e.g., a Riemannian, Hessian, affine, or statistical manifold structure, possibly with a dual pair of affine connections) on the product space $X 	imes \Theta$ that:
(i) restricts on each fiber $\{x\} 	imes \Theta$ to (or is compatible with) the Hessian/Fisher metric on the parameter space;
(ii) incorporates the sample variable $x$ in a statistically meaningful way through $f(x;	heta)$ and its derivatives;
(iii) transforms in a controlled manner under reparametrizations $	heta \mapsto 	ilde	heta(	heta)$ corresponding to statistically meaningful coordinate changes (such as those preserving the dually flat / exponential or mixture structure).

Identify the dependence of the resulting geometry on the choice of $	heta$-coordinate system, and investigate its curvature, geodesics, and divergence-theoretic properties.
status_search_result: The problem is open-ended and programmatic, asking to construct an appropriate geometry on the sample-parameter product space. No definitive resolution was located via search; partial related work exists in information geometry and Hessian geometry, but the question as posed does not appear to have an accepted final answer.

original_question: Fix a constant alpha > 0. If A subseteq F2^n has density at least alpha, must A + A contain a subspace of codimension O(sqrt(n))?
self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. For a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$, define its density to be $|A|/2^n$ and its sumset by $A+A = \{a+a' : a, a' \in A\}$. Fix a constant $\alpha > 0$ (independent of $n$). Is it true that for every $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density at least $\alpha$, the sumset $A+A$ contains an affine (equivalently, linear) subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of codimension $O(\sqrt{n})$, where the implied constant may depend on $\alpha$ but not on $n$?
status_search_result: The problem of whether sumsets of positive-density subsets of F_2^n must contain subspaces of codimension O(√n) is a well-known question due to Green. Sanders proved subspaces of codimension o(n) (and codimension 1 near density 1/2), and subsequent work has improved bounds, but no result attaining the conjectured √n codimension for arbitrary constant density is known; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: On Some Open Problems of Mahmoudi and Renshaw
original_question: Does there exist a monoid S and a cyclic right S-act A that does not admit a (P)-cover, where a cyclic right S-act is an act generated by one element (equivalently of the form S/ρ for a right congruence ρ), and a (P)-cover means a cover by an S-act satisfying condition (P): whenever as = a't, there exist a'', u, v with a = a''u, a' = a''v, and us = vt?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a monoid. A right $S$-act is a set $A$ equipped with a right action $A \times S \to A$, $(a,s) \mapsto as$, satisfying $a1 = a$ and $a(st) = (as)t$. A right $S$-act $A$ is called cyclic if it is generated by a single element; equivalently, $A \cong S/\rho$ for some right congruence $\rho$ on $S$ (where $S/\rho$ denotes the set of $\rho$-classes with right $S$-action $[x]_\rho \cdot s = [xs]_\rho$).

A right $S$-act $B$ is said to satisfy condition (P) if, whenever $bs = b's$' with $b,b' \in B$ and $s,s' \in S$, there exist $b'' \in B$ and $u,v \in S$ such that $b = b''u$, $b' = b''v$, and $us = vt$. (Here we read the relation as: for any $b,b' \in B$ and $s,t \in S$ with $bs = b't$, there exist $b'' \in B$ and $u,v \in S$ with $b = b''u$, $b' = b''v$, $us = vt$.)

A (P)-cover of a right $S$-act $A$ is an $S$-epimorphism $f : B \to A$ where $B$ satisfies condition (P) and $f$ is a "cover" in the categorical sense (no proper subact of $B$ maps onto $A$ via $f$).

Question: Does there exist a monoid $S$ and a cyclic right $S$-act $A$ such that $A$ admits no (P)-cover?
status_search_result: The problem (Open Problem 1 of Mahmoudi–Renshaw) was answered affirmatively: by taking $S$ to be a free monoid and $\rho$ a right congruence whose 1-class has more than one element in a suitable sense, the cyclic right $S$-act $S/\rho$ has no (P)-cover. Thus the existence of such a monoid and cyclic act is established.

context_brief: Influence lower bounds for bounded low-degree functions
original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,1] has degree at most k, must there exist a coordinate i in [n] with influence Inf_i[f] >= (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?
self_contained_problem:
For a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, write its (unique) multilinear Fourier expansion as $f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\hat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$. The degree of $f$ is $\deg(f)=\max\{|S|:\hat f(S)\neq 0\}$. The variance is $\mathrm{Var}[f]=\sum_{S\neq\emptyset}\hat f(S)^2$ (with respect to the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}^n$). For each coordinate $i\in[n]$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ is 
$$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;=\; \mathbb{E}_{x}\!\left[\Big(\tfrac{f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i})}{2}\Big)^2\right] \;=\; \sum_{S\ni i}\hat f(S)^2,$$
where $x^{\oplus i}$ denotes $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\ge 1$, every integer $k\ge 1$, and every function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ with $\deg(f)\le k$, there is a coordinate $i\in[n]$ satisfying
$$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \left(\frac{\mathrm{Var}[f]}{k}\right)^{C}.$$
status_search_result: This is the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture (2008). It remains open in general. Partial progress includes a proof for Boolean-valued functions, a proof for completely bounded block-multilinear forms (Bansal–Sinha–de Wolf, 2022), and a proof under random restrictions (ECCC TR24-035, 2024). A blog post by Aaronson (2019) and subsequent works confirm the conjecture is still open in full generality.

paper_title: On Some Open Problems of Mahmoudi and Renshaw
original_question: Are strongly flat covers of cyclic right S-acts unique? Here a strongly flat cover means a cover C → A in which C is a strongly flat right S-act; in the paper, strongly flat acts are recalled as acts satisfying the interpolation conditions (P) and (E).
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a monoid (a semigroup with identity 1). A right S-act is a nonempty set A equipped with a right action A × S → A, (a,s) ↦ as, satisfying a·1 = a and (as)t = a(st). A right S-act C is called strongly flat if it satisfies the following two interpolation conditions:
 (P) For all c, c' ∈ C and s, s' ∈ S, if cs = c's' then there exist c'' ∈ C and u, v ∈ S such that c = c''u, c' = c''v, and us = vs'.
 (E) For all c ∈ C and s, s' ∈ S, if cs = cs' then there exist c'' ∈ C and u ∈ S such that c = c''u and us = us'.

Given a right S-act A, a cover of A is an S-homomorphism f : C → A such that:
 (i) f is surjective;
 (ii) for any S-homomorphism g : C' → A from a strongly flat right S-act C' to A, there exists an S-homomorphism h : C' → C with f∘h = g (existence relative to the class of strongly flat acts);
 (iii) any S-endomorphism h : C → C with f∘h = f is an automorphism (the minimality/coessential condition).

A strongly flat cover of A is a cover f : C → A in which C is strongly flat. Two covers f : C → A and f' : C' → A are considered the same if there is an S-isomorphism h : C → C' with f'∘h = f.

Question: Are strongly flat covers of cyclic right S-acts (i.e. acts of the form S/ρ for a right congruence ρ on S) unique up to isomorphism over A? More precisely, decide whether for every monoid S and every right congruence ρ on S, any two strongly flat covers of S/ρ must be isomorphic, or exhibit a monoid S and cyclic right S-act for which uniqueness fails.
status_search_result: The question, originally posed as Open Problem 5 of Mahmoudi–Renshaw, has been answered in the negative: there exists a monoid S and a cyclic right S-act S/ρ whose strongly flat covers are not unique; in fact one can construct cyclic acts with arbitrarily many non-isomorphic strongly flat covers (and (P)-covers).

original_question: Fix a possibly infinite collection of affine constraints {(M_1,sigma_1),(M_2,sigma_2),...} over F2. For each n, let P_n be the property that a function f : F2^n -> {0,1} is (M_i,sigma_i)-free for every i. Must there exist a one-sided-error constant-query property-testing algorithm for P_n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ denote the field with two elements. For a matrix $M \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m \times k}$ and a vector $\sigma \in \{0,1\}^k$, say that a function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ is $(M,\sigma)$-free if there do not exist vectors $x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(k)} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that $M\,(x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(k)})^\top = 0$ (as a system over $\mathbb{F}_2$) and $f(x^{(j)}) = \sigma_j$ for every $j \in \{1,\dots,k\}$.

Fix a (possibly infinite) collection $\mathcal{C} = \{(M_1,\sigma_1),(M_2,\sigma_2),\dots\}$ of such affine constraints, where $M_i \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m_i \times k_i}$ and $\sigma_i \in \{0,1\}^{k_i}$. For each $n \geq 1$, let $P_n$ be the property of functions $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ that $f$ is $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free for every $i$.

The distance between $f,g:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ is $\Pr_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n}[f(x) \neq g(x)]$, and the distance from $f$ to $P_n$ is the infimum of distances from $f$ to functions satisfying $P_n$.

A one-sided-error, constant-query property tester for $\{P_n\}$ is a randomized algorithm that, given query access to $f$ and a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, makes at most $q(\varepsilon)$ queries (independent of $n$) to $f$, accepts with probability $1$ if $f \in P_n$, and rejects with probability at least $2/3$ if $f$ has distance at least $\varepsilon$ from $P_n$.

Question: Does such a one-sided-error, constant-query property tester exist for every choice of $\mathcal{C}$?
status_search_result: The conjecture that every (possibly infinite) collection of affine constraints over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defines a property that is testable with one-sided error and constant query complexity was established as a theorem by Bhattacharyya, Fischer, Hatami, Hatami, and Lovett ("Every locally characterized affine-invariant property is testable", 2012, arXiv:1212.3849), building on earlier work on testing low-complexity affine-invariant properties. Subspace-hereditary / locally characterized affine-invariant properties — which include $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-freeness families — admit one-sided constant-query testers.

paper_title: On Some Open Problems of Mahmoudi and Renshaw
context_brief: Cyclic acts over infinite inverse semigroups
original_question: If S is an infinite inverse semigroup, must every cyclic right S-act S/ρ admit a (P)-cover? Here an inverse semigroup is a semigroup that is regular and whose idempotents commute, a cyclic right S-act is an act generated by one element, and a (P)-cover is a cover by an act satisfying condition (P).
self_contained_problem:
Setup and definitions:
- A semigroup S is called an inverse semigroup if it is regular (for every a ∈ S there exists x ∈ S with axa = a) and its idempotents commute (ef = fe for all idempotents e, f ∈ S).
- A right S-act is a set A together with a right action A × S → A, (a, s) ↦ as, satisfying (as)t = a(st) for all a ∈ A, s, t ∈ S (and a·1 = a if S is a monoid).
- A right S-act is cyclic if it is generated by a single element; equivalently, it has the form S/ρ for some right congruence ρ on S (with the natural right action). If S is a semigroup without identity, S/ρ is taken in the appropriate sense for acts.
- A right S-act B is said to satisfy condition (P) if, whenever bs = b's' with b, b' ∈ B and s, s' ∈ S, there exist b'' ∈ B and u, v ∈ S such that b = b''u, b' = b''v, and us = vs'.
- An epimorphism f: B → A of right S-acts is called coessential if no proper subact of B is mapped onto A by f. A (P)-cover of a right S-act A is a coessential epimorphism f: B → A from a right S-act B satisfying condition (P), such that for any right S-act C satisfying (P) and any homomorphism g: C → B with f∘g surjective, g itself is surjective (i.e., f is a cover in the sense of Enochs/Mahmoudi–Renshaw with respect to the class of (P)-acts).

Question: Let S be an infinite inverse semigroup. Does every cyclic right S-act S/ρ admit a (P)-cover?
status_search_result: Search results indicate the problem (posed by Mahmoudi–Renshaw) has attracted follow-up work providing partial answers (e.g., sufficient conditions on inverse monoids ensuring all cyclic acts have a (P)-cover, and examples), but no source clearly establishes a full resolution for arbitrary infinite inverse semigroups. The general status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Fix 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1. If A,B subseteq R^n have Gaussian measures mu and nu respectively and A is centrally symmetric, A = -A, what is the minimum possible value of Pr[x in A, y in B] when (x,y) are rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors?
self_contained_problem:
Let $0 \le \rho, \mu, \nu \le 1$ and $n \ge 1$. Let $(X,Y)$ be a pair of $\rho$-correlated standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$; that is, $X$ and $Y$ are each distributed as $N(0, I_n)$ and their joint distribution is the centered Gaussian on $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathbb{E}[X_i Y_j] = \rho\,\delta_{ij}$. For a Borel set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, let $\gamma_n(S) := \Pr[X \in S]$ denote its standard Gaussian measure.

Determine
$$ \inf\bigl\{\, \Pr[X \in A,\ Y \in B] \,:\, A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ Borel},\ \gamma_n(A) = \mu,\ \gamma_n(B) = \nu,\ A = -A \,\bigr\}, $$
where the infimum is over all such pairs $(A,B)$ with $A$ centrally symmetric (i.e., $A = -A$). Identify the extremal sets achieving this infimum (or show that no minimizer exists), and give a closed-form expression for the value of the infimum as a function of $\rho$, $\mu$, $\nu$, and $n$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the minimum joint probability $\Pr[X\in A, Y\in B]$ over centrally symmetric $A$ and arbitrary $B$ of fixed Gaussian measures, for $\rho$-correlated Gaussian vectors, is a noise-stability problem related to the symmetric Gaussian noise-stability conjecture. Partial progress exists: in dimension one the centered interval (or its complement) is extremal at small $\rho$, and in higher dimensions the analogous ball statement is known to fail in general (Heilman, "Low Correlation Noise Stability of Symmetric Sets", J. Theoret. Probab. 2020). The general extremal problem in arbitrary dimension appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
context_brief: Learning a polytope from random samples
original_question: Given only random samples from an unknown polytope in R^n, can the polytope be learned efficiently? More specifically, although the volume of a polytope can be computed efficiently when one has membership-oracle access, is there a polynomial-time procedure that reconstructs or approximately learns the polytope from random sample points alone?
self_contained_problem: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be an unknown convex polytope (for instance, with at most $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ vertices or facets), and suppose we are given access only to independent samples drawn uniformly at random from $P$. Design a polynomial-time algorithm that, with high probability, outputs a description of a convex polytope $\widehat{P}$ (e.g. by its vertices or facets) such that $\widehat{P}$ is close to $P$ in a natural metric (e.g. the symmetric-difference volume, $\mathrm{vol}(P \triangle \widehat{P}) \le \varepsilon \cdot \mathrm{vol}(P)$), using a number of samples and running time polynomial in $n$ and $1/\varepsilon$. Equivalently: is there an efficient (polynomial-time in the dimension) procedure for PAC-learning an arbitrary polytope from uniform random samples drawn from its interior?
status_search_result: The polytope learning problem—efficiently reconstructing a polytope from uniform random samples—remains an open problem in algorithmic convex geometry. Information-theoretically, poly(n) samples suffice for polytopes with poly(n) vertices, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known. The problem is featured as an active open question in Simons Institute talks and related literature on algorithmic polytope reconstruction.

context_brief: Gaussian simplex partitions and noise stability
original_question: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, and for -1 <= rho <= 0 does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?
self_contained_problem:
Equip $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard Gaussian probability measure $\gamma_n$ of density $(2\pi)^{-n/2}e^{-\|x\|^2/2}$. For $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $(X,Y)$ be a pair of jointly Gaussian random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_iY_j]=\rho\,\delta_{ij}$. For a measurable partition $\mathcal{A}=(A_1,\dots,A_q)$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$, define the noise stability at correlation $\rho$ by
$$\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(\mathcal{A})=\sum_{i=1}^q\Pr[X\in A_i,\;Y\in A_i].$$
Fix integers $3\le q\le n+1$. The standard simplex partition is defined as follows: let $a_1,\dots,a_q\in\mathbb{R}^n$ be the vertices of a regular simplex centered at the origin (so $\sum_i a_i=0$ and $\langle a_i,a_j\rangle$ depends only on whether $i=j$); set
$$S_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,a_i\rangle=\max_{1\le j\le q}\langle x,a_j\rangle\},\quad i=1,\dots,q.$$
Then $(S_1,\dots,S_q)$ partitions $\mathbb{R}^n$ into $q$ pieces, each of Gaussian measure $1/q$.

Prove or disprove the following:
(a) For every $\rho\in[0,1]$, among all measurable partitions $\mathcal{A}=(A_1,\dots,A_q)$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\gamma_n(A_i)=1/q$ for all $i$, the quantity $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(\mathcal{A})$ is maximized by the standard simplex partition.
(b) For every $\rho\in[-1,0]$, among all such equal-Gaussian-measure partitions into $q$ parts, $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(\mathcal{A})$ is minimized by the standard simplex partition.
status_search_result: The conjecture (the Standard Simplex Conjecture) is generally still open in the stated equal-measure form. Heilman (2014) proved the conjecture in the case q=3, n≥2, for sufficiently small positive ρ (i.e., 0<ρ<ρ_0(q,n)). Heilman–Mossel–Nayar (2016) showed that if the parts are required to have prescribed but unequal measures, the standard simplex is not optimal; this does not contradict the equal-measure version. No proof for general q, n, and all ρ has been published.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every convex body K in R^n admits an ellipsoid E with the following approximate sandwiching property: at least half the volume of E lies inside K, and at least half the volume of K lies inside the dilated ellipsoid C log n · E?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let K ⊂ ℝⁿ be a convex body (a compact convex set with non-empty interior). For an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝⁿ centered at some point and a scalar t > 0, write tE for the dilation of E by factor t about its center. Determine whether the following holds:

There exists an absolute constant C > 0 (independent of n and K) such that for every n ≥ 2 and every convex body K ⊂ ℝⁿ, one can find an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝⁿ satisfying simultaneously
  (i) vol(E ∩ K) ≥ (1/2) · vol(E),
  (ii) vol(K ∩ (C log n) · E) ≥ (1/2) · vol(K),
where vol denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ.

Prove or disprove the existence of such a constant C.
status_search_result: The conjectured approximate ellipsoidal sandwiching with a C·log n factor follows from (and is now far surpassed by) the resolution of Bourgain's slicing/hyperplane conjecture by Klartag and Lehec (using a key bound of Guan), announced in December 2024, and the subsequent thin-shell bound of Klartag–Lehec (2025). For an isotropic convex body the inertia ellipsoid gives the sandwiching with an absolute constant (in particular better than C log n) once the thin-shell/isotropic-constant bounds are constants. Hence the stated conjecture is affirmatively resolved.

original_question: For every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the sum of the absolute values of the linear Fourier coefficients bounded by sqrt(deg(f))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let its Fourier expansion be
\[ f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}}\widehat{f}(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i, \]
with Fourier coefficients $\widehat{f}(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)$. Write $\widehat{f}(i):=\widehat{f}(\{i\})$ for the linear (degree-1) Fourier coefficients, and define the degree of $f$ by
\[ \deg(f)=\max\{|S|:\widehat{f}(S)\neq 0\}. \]
Prove or disprove: for every $n\geq 1$ and every Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
\[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{f}(i)\;\leq\;\sqrt{\deg(f)}. \]
status_search_result: The inequality is a weak form of a conjecture attributed to Gopalan and Servedio relating the sum of linear Fourier coefficients of a Boolean function to its degree (the stronger form replaces sqrt(deg(f)) with the corresponding sum for the majority function on deg(f) bits, which is asymptotically ~sqrt(2 deg(f)/π)). Subsequent works (e.g., the 2016 note "On the Sum of Linear Coefficients of a Boolean Valued Function") still treat the statement as an open conjecture and provide reformulations rather than a proof.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: If X is drawn from an isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, must the variance of the squared Euclidean norm ||X||^2 always be at most Cn for some absolute constant C? Equivalently, must isotropic logconcave measures have most of their mass concentrated in a thin Euclidean shell of constant-width scale after normalization?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let f: R^n → [0,∞) be a log-concave probability density (i.e., f = e^{-V} for some convex V: R^n → (-∞,∞]) that is isotropic, meaning that if X is a random vector with density f then E[X] = 0 and the covariance matrix of X equals the n×n identity, E[X X^T] = I_n. Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant C > 0, independent of n and f, such that for every such X,

  Var(‖X‖_2^2) ≤ C n,

where ‖·‖_2 denotes the Euclidean norm on R^n. Equivalently, show that every isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^n concentrates most of its mass in a Euclidean shell of constant width about the sphere of radius √n.
status_search_result: Recent work by Klartag and Lehec (2024–2025), building on a parallel-coupling/stochastic-localization technique introduced by Guan in the resolution of Bourgain's slicing conjecture, established the thin-shell conjecture: for isotropic log-concave X in R^n one has Var(‖X‖^2) ≤ C n with an absolute constant C. The result is reported in expository accounts and the 2025 preprint "Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling" (arXiv:2507.15495).

original_question: Fix d in N and epsilon in (0,1). What is the least k = k(d,epsilon) such that every degree-d polynomial threshold event over a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X approximates the corresponding event under a standard Gaussian vector Z within additive error epsilon; that is, |Pr[p(X) >= 0] - Pr[p(Z) >= 0]| <= epsilon for every degree-d polynomial p : R^n -> R?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer d ≥ 1 and a real number ε ∈ (0,1). Call a random vector X = (X_1,…,X_n) ∈ R^n a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal vector if (i) each coordinate X_i has the standard one-dimensional Gaussian distribution N(0,1) and (ii) for every choice of indices i_1 < i_2 < … < i_k, the random variables X_{i_1}, …, X_{i_k} are mutually independent (and hence jointly distributed as N(0,I_k)). Let Z ∼ N(0,I_n) denote a standard n-dimensional Gaussian vector.

Determine the least positive integer k = k(d,ε), depending only on d and ε (and not on the dimension n), such that the following holds: for every n ≥ 1, every degree-d polynomial p : R^n → R, and every k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X in R^n,
   | Pr[ p(X) ≥ 0 ] − Pr[ p(Z) ≥ 0 ] | ≤ ε.
status_search_result: Upper bounds are known: Kane (2011) showed that k = O_d(ε^{-4d} · 7^d)-wise independence among standard Gaussian marginals suffices to ε-fool every degree-d polynomial threshold function, and subsequent work (e.g., Kane's "local hyperconcentration" approach and later PRG constructions) has improved the dependence on ε for various regimes. However, the exact least value of k(d,ε), and even the tight asymptotic dependence on d and ε, does not appear to be settled in the literature.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: For every logconcave density f on R^n with covariance matrix A_f, is the isoperimetric coefficient Φ_f always bounded below by c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)) for some absolute constant c, where λ_1(A_f) is the largest eigenvalue of A_f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ be a logconcave probability density (i.e., $\log f$ is concave on its support and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f = 1$). Let $A_f$ denote the covariance matrix of $f$, and let $\lambda_1(A_f)$ denote its largest eigenvalue (equivalently, the operator norm of $A_f$). Define the isoperimetric coefficient
$$\Phi_f \;=\; \inf_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{\int_{\partial S} f\,d\sigma}{\min\!\big(\int_S f,\; 1-\int_S f\big)},$$
where the infimum is taken over all sufficiently regular subsets $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\int_{\partial S} f\,d\sigma$ denotes the surface integral of $f$ over the boundary of $S$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ (independent of $n$ and $f$) such that for every $n\ge 1$ and every logconcave probability density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\Phi_f \;\geq\; \frac{c}{\sqrt{\lambda_1(A_f)}}\,?$$
status_search_result: The KLS isoperimetric conjecture in its full form remains open. Significant progress: Chen (2021) gave a quasi-polynomial bound; Klartag and Lehec (2022) established the conjecture up to a polylogarithmic factor in the dimension. Subsequent work (Guan, Klartag, Lehec, 2024–2025) resolved the related Bourgain slicing problem and the thin-shell conjecture, yielding further improvements, but the sharp constant version of KLS is not yet proven.

original_question: For each constant delta > 0, do s^{-O(1)}-biased densities delta-fool all size-s DNF formulas; equivalently, if f : {0,1}^n -> {-1,1} is computable by a size-s DNF and phi is an s^{-O(1)}-biased density on {0,1}^n, must |E_{x~{0,1}^n}[f(x)] - E_{y~phi}[f(y)]| <= delta?
self_contained_problem:
Let n, s be positive integers. A DNF formula of size s on variables x_1,...,x_n is a Boolean function expressible as the OR of at most s ANDs (terms) of literals over x_1,...,x_n; we view such an f as a function {0,1}^n -> {-1,1}. A density on {0,1}^n is a function phi : {0,1}^n -> R_{>=0} with E_{x ~ U}[phi(x)] = 1, where U is the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n; the associated probability distribution assigns to y the weight phi(y)/2^n. For epsilon >= 0, phi is called epsilon-biased if for every nonempty S subseteq {1,...,n}, |E_{x ~ U}[phi(x) * chi_S(x)]| <= epsilon, where chi_S(x) = prod_{i in S}(-1)^{x_i}. Equivalently, the corresponding distribution agrees with U up to additive error epsilon on every nontrivial parity.

Question: Is the following statement true? For every constant delta > 0 there exists a constant c = c(delta) > 0 such that for every n and every s, every s^{-c}-biased density phi on {0,1}^n delta-fools every size-s DNF formula f : {0,1}^n -> {-1,1}, in the sense that
  | E_{x ~ U}[f(x)] - E_{y ~ phi}[f(y)] | <= delta,
where E_{y ~ phi}[f(y)] := E_{x ~ U}[phi(x) f(x)].
status_search_result: Whether small-bias (poly(1/s))-biased distributions fool size-s DNF formulas to constant error remains a well-known open problem in pseudorandomness. Known positive results show that polylogarithmic independence (Bazzi, Razborov) fools DNFs, and Lee–Viola established limitations for sums of small-bias distributions against read-once CNFs, but no construction or refutation is known for the general small-bias-fools-DNFs question. No source found resolving the question as stated.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every isotropic logconcave density f on R^n satisfies f(0) ≤ C^n? In the equivalent convex-body form highlighted in the paper, does every isotropic convex body in R^n have volume at least c^n for some absolute constant c?
self_contained_problem:
A probability density $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ is called log-concave if $\log f$ is concave on its support (with the convention $\log 0=-\infty$). Such a density is called isotropic if its barycenter is the origin, i.e. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x\, f(x)\,dx = 0$, and its covariance matrix is the identity, i.e. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x_i x_j f(x)\,dx = \delta_{ij}$ for all $1\le i,j\le n$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$) such that for every dimension $n\ge 1$ and every isotropic log-concave probability density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$f(0) \le C^n\,?$$

Equivalently (in the convex-body form): a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of unit volume with barycenter at the origin is called isotropic if there is a constant $L_K>0$ with $\int_K \langle x,\theta\rangle^2\, dx = L_K^2$ for every unit vector $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every isotropic convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (so with unit volume) satisfies, after suitable normalization, a uniform bound $L_K\le C$ for an absolute constant $C$ — equivalently, that the isotropic constant $L_K$ is bounded above by a universal constant independent of the dimension $n$?
status_search_result: Bourgain's slicing/hyperplane conjecture has been resolved. Building on a small-ball estimate of Qingyang Guan (2024), Bo'az Klartag and Joseph Lehec announced a proof in December 2024 (arXiv:2501.06854, "The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates") establishing that the isotropic constant of log-concave probability densities in R^n is bounded by an absolute constant independent of dimension, equivalently $f(0) \le C^n$ for isotropic log-concave $f$.

context_brief: PTF sparsity for inner product mod 2
original_question: Does every polynomial threshold function representation of the inner product mod 2 function IP_{2n} : F2^{2n} -> {-1,1} require at least 3^n monomials?
self_contained_problem:
A polynomial threshold function (PTF) representation of a Boolean function f : {0,1}^m → {−1, +1} is a real multilinear polynomial p(x_1, …, x_m) such that f(x) = sign(p(x)) for every x ∈ {0,1}^m. The sparsity of such a representation is the number of monomials with nonzero coefficient appearing in p. 

For a positive integer n, define the inner product mod 2 function on 2n bits, IP_{2n} : {0,1}^{2n} → {−1, +1}, by
    IP_{2n}(x_1, …, x_n, y_1, …, y_n) = (−1)^{x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + ⋯ + x_n y_n},
where the exponent is computed modulo 2.

Prove or disprove: every PTF representation of IP_{2n} has sparsity at least 3^n. Equivalently, does there exist a multilinear real polynomial p in 2n variables with strictly fewer than 3^n nonzero monomials such that sign(p(x, y)) = IP_{2n}(x, y) for all (x, y) ∈ {0,1}^{2n}?
status_search_result: A web search on PTF sparsity lower bounds for the inner product mod 2 function did not surface a definitive resolution of the 3^n sparsity lower bound conjecture. Related work studies sparse PTF representations and complexity-theoretic implications, but no source clearly establishes or refutes the specific 3^n monomial lower bound for IP_{2n}.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Let f be a logconcave density on R^n, and let P be any partition of R^n into convex parts. Is there an absolute constant C such that the sum over parts P of σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) is always at most Cσ_f^2, where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f in any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest directional variance of the restriction of f to the part P?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f$ be a logconcave probability density on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (i.e., $f = e^{-\varphi}$ for some convex $\varphi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$, with $\int f = 1$). For a Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive $f$-measure, define
\[ \pi_f(S) = \int_S f(x)\,dx, \qquad \sigma_f(S)^2 = \sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,\|u\|=1}\;\frac{1}{\pi_f(S)}\int_S \langle u, x - \mu_S\rangle^2 f(x)\,dx, \]
where $\mu_S = \frac{1}{\pi_f(S)}\int_S x\, f(x)\,dx$. Set $\sigma_f^2 = \sigma_f(\mathbb{R}^n)^2$, the largest variance of $f$ along any unit direction.

A partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called convex if every part $P\in\mathcal{P}$ is a convex set.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$, $f$, and $\mathcal{P}$) such that for every logconcave density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and every convex partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$,
\[ \sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}} \sigma_f(P)^2\,\pi_f(P) \;\le\; C\,\sigma_f^2 \;? \]
status_search_result: The conjecture concerns averaging directional variances over convex partitions of a logconcave density and is closely related to the KLS (Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits) program. While the KLS hyperplane conjecture itself has seen major progress (Eldan's stochastic localization, Lee–Vempala $O(n^{1/4})$ Cheeger bound, Klartag–Lehec polylogarithmic bounds), no source found directly confirms a resolution of this specific localization-partition variance inequality. Its status appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

context_brief: Monotone functions close to low-degree juntas
original_question: Fix any epsilon > 0. Is every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} epsilon-close to a junta whose size is polynomial in deg(f)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Identify $\{-1,1\}^n$ with the uniform probability space, and define the distance between two Boolean functions $f,g$ as $\Pr_{x}[f(x)\neq g(x)]$. We say $f$ is $\varepsilon$-close to $g$ if this distance is at most $\varepsilon$. A function $h:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is called a $k$-junta if it depends on at most $k$ of its $n$ input coordinates. The Fourier (real multilinear) expansion of $f$ is $f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\hat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and the degree $\deg(f)$ is the largest $|S|$ with $\hat f(S)\neq 0$. The function $f$ is monotone if $f(x)\le f(y)$ whenever $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i$.

Question: Is it true that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a function $J_\varepsilon:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $J_\varepsilon(d)=\mathrm{poly}(d)$ such that, for every $n$ and every monotone $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, the function $f$ is $\varepsilon$-close to a $J_\varepsilon(\deg(f))$-junta?
status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved in the negative by Daniel Kane in 2012, who constructed monotone Boolean functions of low degree that are not $\varepsilon$-close to any junta of size polynomial in the degree.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Can an intersection of two halfspaces be PAC-learned in polynomial time? More generally, is there a polynomial-time PAC-learning algorithm for this class that avoids the current gap between efficiently learning a single halfspace and the still-open two-halfspace case?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix the input space $\mathbb{R}^n$. A halfspace is a function $h_{w,\theta}:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{0,1\}$ of the form $h_{w,\theta}(x)=\mathbf{1}[\langle w,x\rangle\ge\theta]$ for some $w\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$. The concept class $\mathcal{C}_2^{(n)}$ of intersections of two halfspaces consists of all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{0,1\}$ of the form $f(x)=h_1(x)\wedge h_2(x)$, where $h_1,h_2$ are halfspaces.

Recall the (distribution-free) PAC model: an algorithm $A$ PAC-learns $\mathcal{C}_2=\{\mathcal{C}_2^{(n)}\}_{n\ge 1}$ if for every $n$, every target $f\in\mathcal{C}_2^{(n)}$, every distribution $D$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and every $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$, given access to labeled samples $(x,f(x))$ with $x\sim D$, $A$ outputs with probability at least $1-\delta$ a hypothesis $\hat f$ satisfying $\Pr_{x\sim D}[\hat f(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon$. The algorithm is efficient if its running time (and sample complexity) is polynomial in $n$, $1/\varepsilon$, $1/\delta$, and the bit-complexity of the target.

Question. Does there exist an efficient (polynomial-time) PAC-learning algorithm for the class $\mathcal{C}_2$ of intersections of two halfspaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in this distribution-free setting?
status_search_result: The distribution-free PAC-learnability of intersections of two halfspaces in polynomial time remains a major open problem. Cryptographic hardness results (Klivans–Sherstov) show that learning intersections of n^ε halfspaces is at least as hard as Õ(n^1.5)-uSVP, but no such hardness is known for just two halfspaces. The best general algorithms remain quasi-polynomial, and recent progress (e.g., COLT 2025 on factorizable distributions and margin halfspaces) addresses only restricted distributional settings, leaving the general problem open.

original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is monotone, must its total influence satisfy I[f] < o(sens[f])?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. For $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $x^{(i)}$ denote $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Define the sensitivity of $f$ at $x$ by
$$s(f,x)=\#\{i\in\{1,\dots,n\}: f(x)\ne f(x^{(i)})\},$$
the maximum sensitivity by $\mathrm{sens}[f]=\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n} s(f,x)$, and the total influence by
$$I[f]=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\{-1,1\}^n}[s(f,x)],$$
where $x$ is uniformly distributed on $\{-1,1\}^n$. The function $f$ is called monotone if $f(x)\le f(y)$ whenever $x\le y$ coordinatewise (using the order $-1<1$).

Question: Is it the case that for every monotone $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
$$I[f] = o(\mathrm{sens}[f])$$
as $n\to\infty$? Equivalently, must the total influence of a monotone Boolean function be asymptotically negligible compared to its maximum sensitivity?
status_search_result: This is a conjecture attributed to Servedio. The best known lower-bound separation, due to O'Donnell–Servedio, exhibits a monotone function with average sensitivity $\Omega(\mathrm{sens}[f]^{0.61})$, while the best known upper bound is roughly $I[f] \le \sqrt{2/\pi}\,\mathrm{sens}[f](1+o(1))$. No proof of $I[f]=o(\mathrm{sens}[f])$ is known, and the conjecture remains open.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Is there a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming, meaning an algorithm whose running time can be bounded polynomially in the dimension and combinatorial input size without dependence on numerical accuracy parameters arising from repeated rescaling?
self_contained_problem:
A linear program is the optimization problem of maximizing (or minimizing) a linear functional $c^	op x$ over $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ subject to finitely many linear inequality constraints $Ax \le b$, where $A \in \mathbb{Q}^{m	imes n}$, $b \in \mathbb{Q}^m$, and $c \in \mathbb{Q}^n$.

An algorithm for linear programming is called strongly polynomial if:
(i) it uses only the basic arithmetic operations $+,-,	imes,\div$ and comparisons on the input numbers,
(ii) the total number of such operations performed is bounded by a polynomial in the dimensions $m$ and $n$ (i.e., independent of the bit-sizes of the entries of $A$, $b$, $c$), and
(iii) on a Turing machine model, the bit-size of every intermediate number computed is bounded by a polynomial in the total bit-size of the input.

Question: Does there exist a strongly polynomial algorithm that solves every linear program (deciding feasibility, detecting unboundedness, and otherwise outputting an optimal vertex solution)?
status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem, listed by Smale as Problem 9 on his list of mathematical problems for the 21st century. As of recent surveys and results (e.g., progress on combinatorial LP, Tardos's strongly polynomial algorithm for combinatorial LP, and recent work on Markov decision processes and special LP classes), no strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming is known, and the problem remains open.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: For either hit-and-run or the ball walk on a convex body, is there a single deterministic starting point that is as effective as a warm start for mixing? For example, if one starts the walk at the centroid, does it converge at the same asymptotic rate as when started from a random warm-start distribution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body (a compact convex set with nonempty interior), and let $\pi_K$ denote the uniform distribution on $K$. Two Markov chains on $K$ with stationary distribution $\pi_K$ are considered:

(i) The ball walk with radius $\delta>0$: from a current point $x \in K$, pick $y$ uniformly at random in the Euclidean ball $B(x,\delta)$; move to $y$ if $y \in K$, otherwise stay at $x$.

(ii) Hit-and-run: from a current point $x$ in the interior of $K$, pick a uniformly random direction $u \in S^{n-1}$, and move to a point sampled from the one-dimensional restriction of $\pi_K$ to the chord $K \cap \{x + tu : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

A starting distribution $\mu_0$ on $K$ is called an $M$-warm start (with respect to $\pi_K$) if $d\mu_0/d\pi_K \le M$ almost everywhere; the mixing time from $\mu_0$ is the number of steps required to bring the law of the chain within total variation distance $1/4$ of $\pi_K$.

Question: Does there exist a single deterministic point $x_0 \in K$ (computable from $K$, e.g., the centroid $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(K)} \int_K x\, dx$) such that, when started at the Dirac mass $\delta_{x_0}$, either the ball walk (with appropriately chosen $\delta$) or hit-and-run achieves a mixing time matching, up to constants, the mixing time achievable from an $O(1)$-warm start? Equivalently: is the asymptotic convergence rate of one of these walks started at the centroid the same as that obtained from a random warm start?
category_tag: Mixing time of random walks on convex bodies
status_search_result: Lovász and Vempala showed that hit-and-run mixes in polynomial time from any interior starting point ("Hit-and-Run from a Corner"), but the bounds incur extra factors depending on the distance to the boundary, so they do not match the warm-start mixing rate. We did not find a published result establishing that starting at the centroid gives the same asymptotic mixing rate as a warm start for either the ball walk or hit-and-run; the problem appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive recent statement was found, so the status is uncertain.

original_question: Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are degree-at-most-2 polynomials and the indicator of the all-ones vector, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1,1}, can be written as AND(x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ and consider the vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Define the function $\mathrm{AND} : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{-1, 1\}$ by
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \begin{cases} -1 & \text{if } x = (1,1,\dots,1), \\ 1 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$
Suppose $q_1, q_2, \dots, q_m : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$ are polynomials of degree at most $2$ (in the ring $\mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i)$), and suppose there exist real coefficients $c_1, c_2, \dots, c_m \in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i \, (-1)^{q_i(x)} \qquad \text{for all } x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n.$$
Determine the best (largest) lower bound, as a function of $n$, on the number $m$ of quadratic phase functions required for such a representation.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Can the reflection walk based on a separation oracle be analyzed sharply enough to show that it needs only O*(nD) oracle calls for a convex body of diameter D, or even O*(n) oracle calls for isotropic bodies?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body of diameter $D$ that is accessible only through a separation oracle: given a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the oracle either declares $x \in K$ or returns a hyperplane separating $x$ from $K$. Consider the reflection walk on $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined as follows. At a current point $x \in K$, sample a random direction $u$ uniformly from the unit sphere and a random step length, producing a tentative move along the line $\ell$ through $x$ in direction $u$. If the resulting trajectory stays in $K$, accept the new point. Otherwise, query the separation oracle at the first point outside $K$; the returned half-space defines a hyperplane off which the trajectory is reflected, and the process continues (querying the oracle each time the reflected trajectory exits $K$) until a point inside $K$ is reached. The cost of one Markov-chain step is measured by the number of separation-oracle calls it makes.

Standard analysis shows that sampling a near-uniform point from $K$ via this walk uses $\widetilde{O}(n^2 D^2)$ oracle calls in the worst case. 

(a) Prove or disprove: the reflection walk produces a near-uniform sample from $K$ using only $\widetilde{O}(n D)$ separation-oracle calls in total (independent of the number of Markov-chain steps).

(b) Prove or disprove: when $K$ is in isotropic position, the reflection walk produces a near-uniform sample using only $\widetilde{O}(n)$ separation-oracle calls.

Here $\widetilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides factors polylogarithmic in $n$, $D$, and $1/\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon$ is the desired total-variation distance to the uniform distribution on $K$.

context_brief: Singular continuous spectrum under rank-one perturbation
original_question: Let A be a self-adjoint cyclic operator on a Hilbert space, let φ be a cyclic vector for A, and let A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ be a rank-one perturbation with spectral measure mu_alpha taken with respect to φ. Characterize the singular continuous part of mu_alpha in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure mu.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space and let $A$ be a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal{H}$ with a cyclic vector $\varphi$, meaning that the closed linear span of $\{(A-z)^{-1}\varphi : z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}\}$ equals $\mathcal{H}$. Let $\mu$ denote the spectral measure of $A$ associated with $\varphi$, i.e., the unique Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$\langle \varphi, f(A)\varphi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$$
for every bounded Borel function $f$. By the Lebesgue decomposition, write $\mu = \mu_{ac} + \mu_{sc} + \mu_{pp}$ into its absolutely continuous, singular continuous, and pure point parts with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.

For each real parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, define the rank-one perturbation
$$A_\alpha = A + \alpha\,\langle\,\cdot\,,\varphi\rangle\,\varphi.$$
Then $\varphi$ is also cyclic for $A_\alpha$; let $\mu_\alpha$ denote the spectral measure of $A_\alpha$ with respect to $\varphi$, and decompose $\mu_\alpha = \mu_{\alpha,ac} + \mu_{\alpha,sc} + \mu_{\alpha,pp}$.

It is known that:
(i) $\mu_{\alpha,ac}$ is supported on (and characterized by) the essential support of $\mu_{ac}$ (independence of $\alpha$ for the a.c. part, by the Kato–Rosenblum theorem and Aronszajn–Donoghue theory);
(ii) the pure point part $\mu_{\alpha,pp}$ is characterized by the Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem in terms of the boundary behavior of the Borel transform $F(z) = \int (t-z)^{-1}\,d\mu(t)$.

Problem. Give an analogous characterization of the singular continuous part $\mu_{\alpha,sc}$ of $\mu_\alpha$ in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure $\mu$ (equivalently, in terms of the boundary behavior of its Borel transform $F$), valid for every (or for almost every, or for a generic) coupling $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$.
status_search_result: The literature (Simon–Wolff, del Rio–Jitomirskaya–Last–Simon, Aronszajn–Donoghue) gives complete characterizations of the absolutely continuous and pure point parts of the perturbed spectral measure under rank-one perturbations, and provides genericity/abundance results for singular continuous spectrum (e.g. dense G_δ sets of couplings for which it occurs). However, no intrinsic characterization of the singular continuous part of μ_α purely in terms of μ appears in the literature; this is generally regarded as an open problem in rank-one perturbation theory.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Which broader classes of distributions or geometric spaces admit efficient random-walk sampling algorithms? In particular, can one give a sufficient condition, phrased in terms of isoperimetry together with a suitable local regularity property of the target density, that guarantees efficient sampling, and can such a framework cover manifolds of nonnegative curvature?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a complete connected Riemannian manifold equipped with a probability density $f:M\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ (with respect to the Riemannian volume measure). For a Markov chain on $M$ with stationary distribution proportional to $f$, define the mixing time $\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)$ as the smallest $t$ such that the total variation distance between the distribution at step $t$ (from any starting point in a set of large measure) and the target is at most $\varepsilon$. Call a sampling algorithm "efficient" if $\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\dim M$, $\log(1/\varepsilon)$, and natural geometric/analytic parameters of $(M,f)$.

Recall that $(M,f)$ satisfies an isoperimetric inequality with constant $\psi>0$ if for every measurable $S\subseteq M$,
$$\int_{\partial S} f \;\ge\; \psi\,\min\bigl(\mu_f(S),\,1-\mu_f(S)\bigr),$$
where $\mu_f$ is the probability measure with density $f$.

Problem. Identify a broad class of pairs $(M,f)$ that admit efficient random-walk sampling. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a sufficient condition, expressed as the conjunction of (i) an isoperimetric inequality for $\mu_f$ and (ii) a local regularity property of $f$ (for instance, a quantitative bound on how fast $f$ varies over balls of a controlled radius), under which there exists a Markov chain whose mixing time is polynomial in the dimension and the relevant parameters, and prove that this condition implies efficient sampling.

(b) Apply such a framework to Riemannian manifolds of nonnegative sectional (or Ricci) curvature, for which isoperimetric inequalities are known, and determine for which such manifolds $M$ and target densities $f$ an efficient sampling process can be defined.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Mangoubi–Smith (2018) proved rapid mixing of geodesic walks on manifolds with positive sectional curvature bounded above and below, with mixing time independent of dimension. Goyal–Shetty (2019) gave a polynomial-time random-walk-based sampling and optimization algorithm on convex sets in Riemannian manifolds of non-negative curvature. Recent work (e.g. Riemannian proximal samplers, 2025) further develops high-accuracy sampling on manifolds. A fully general sufficient condition combining isoperimetry with a local regularity property covering all such settings has not been definitively established, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

original_question: Fix an interval I contained in R and a subset B contained in R. Can one construct a family of measures {mu_beta} such that for every subset J of I the singular part of mu_beta gives J positive mass exactly for parameters beta in B, while the absolutely continuous part of mu_beta gives J positive mass for every beta in R?
self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed interval and let $B \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed subset. For each $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$, let $\mu_\beta$ be a finite positive Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and write its Lebesgue decomposition (with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$) as
$$\mu_\beta = (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}} + (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}},$$
where $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}}$ is the absolutely continuous part and $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the singular part.

Does there exist a family $\{\mu_\beta\}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}}$ of such measures with the following property: for every Borel subset $J \subset I$,
$$(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}(J) > 0 \iff \beta \in B,$$
while at the same time
$$(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}}(J) > 0 \quad \text{for every } \beta \in \mathbb{R}?$$

Determine whether such a family can be constructed for arbitrary $I$ and $B$, or characterize the pairs $(I,B)$ for which it exists.
status_search_result: A search returns related work on families of spectral measures with mixed types and constructions producing dense absolutely continuous and dense singular spectrum, but no source was found that resolves the precise question of prescribing the singular part to charge every subset of $I$ exactly for $\beta\in B$ while the absolutely continuous part charges every subset for all $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$. Status appears unverified.
