status_search_result: This is a longstanding open program in nuclear theory. TDHFB solvers for drip-line nuclei have been developed in restricted geometries, but a general framework with correct continuum asymptotics for medium/heavy nuclei, treatment of reactions with more than three outgoing fragments, and a TDDFT prescription for exclusive cross sections free of spurious cross-channel correlations remains unresolved as of recent reviews.

original_question: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, and assume the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Under this atoroidal hypothesis, is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N rigid when the tachyon masses are fixed?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. An anti-de Sitter (AdS) 3-manifold is a Lorentzian 3-manifold of constant sectional curvature −1. A tachyon singularity along a smooth space-like curve is a cone-type Lorentzian singularity modeled, in suitable local coordinates, on the quotient of a wedge of AdS_3 by a space-like rotation; the "tachyon mass" is the cone angle parameter measuring the rotational defect transverse to the singular curve.

Let N be a closed 3-manifold equipped with an AdS structure that has tachyon singularities along a link L ⊂ N (the singular locus is a disjoint union of finitely many simple closed space-like curves), with prescribed tachyon masses m_1, …, m_k along the components of L. Assume that the complement N ∖ L is atoroidal, i.e. every embedded incompressible torus in N ∖ L is boundary-parallel.

Question. Under the above atoroidal hypothesis, is the AdS structure on N rigid relative to the tachyon masses? Equivalently, is every continuous deformation of the singular AdS structure on N that preserves the tachyon masses (m_1, …, m_k) trivial up to isotopy?

paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
original_question: How can a quasiparticle random phase approximation be developed that simultaneously includes pairing correlations, explicit continuum states, shape deformation, and full self-consistency of all residual fields for nuclei near the drip line? The challenge is to formulate linear response on top of time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov theory even though, in the quasiparticle representation, the relevant phase space becomes effectively infinite when continuum orbitals are treated explicitly, and then to build numerical methods and algorithms suitable for large-scale parallel computation and for eventual application to both finite nuclei and inhomogeneous nuclear matter.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a quasiparticle random phase approximation (QRPA) for atomic nuclei near the drip lines that simultaneously incorporates: (i) pairing correlations on top of a Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (HFB) ground state, (ii) an explicit treatment of single-particle continuum states, (iii) intrinsic shape (axial and/or triaxial) deformation, and (iv) full self-consistency of all residual fields, namely the residual particle–hole, particle–particle, and rearrangement interactions derived from the same effective Hamiltonian/energy density functional used to obtain the HFB ground state.

The formal task is to formulate the linear response of the time-dependent HFB equations under an external perturbing field in such a way that the formally infinite quasiparticle phase space arising when continuum orbitals are kept explicitly is handled rigorously (e.g., via Green's function / response-function techniques in coordinate space, exact boundary conditions for the outgoing continuum, or controlled discretization). The construction must be applicable both to finite deformed nuclei and to inhomogeneous nuclear matter (e.g., neutron-star inner crust pasta phases).

The accompanying computational task is to design numerical methods and algorithms for solving the resulting large-scale QRPA problem that are suitable for massively parallel computation, and to demonstrate convergence and full self-consistency of the residual interaction with the underlying HFB mean field and pairing field.

Question: Construct such a fully self-consistent deformed continuum QRPA framework, including its mathematical formulation, its numerical/algorithmic realization, and a demonstration of its applicability to drip-line nuclei and to inhomogeneous nuclear matter.

Fully self-consistent Skyrme-QRPA frameworks exist on a canonical HFB basis for spherical systems. However, a fully self-consistent continuum HFB+QRPA in deformed nuclei with massively parallel implementation and applicability to inhomogeneous nuclear matter has not been fully achieved, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Let N be a closed 3-manifold carrying a nonsingular anti-de Sitter structure, and let Σ be a link in N. Do there exist nearby anti-de Sitter structures with tachyon singularities along Σ, and if so, what topological or geometric conditions on the pair (N, Σ) are necessary for such deformations to exist?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a closed 3-manifold equipped with a nonsingular anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure, i.e. a $(G,X)$-structure modeled on the Lorentzian symmetric space $\mathrm{AdS}^3 = \widetilde{\mathrm{PSL}}_2(\mathbb{R})$ of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Let $\Sigma \subset N$ be a link. An AdS structure on $N$ with a tachyon singularity of mass $m>0$ along $\Sigma$ is, by definition, a smooth AdS structure on $N \setminus \Sigma$ whose geodesic completion is homeomorphic to $N$, such that the metric near each component of $\Sigma$ is locally modeled on the Lorentzian cone manifold obtained from $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ by a Lorentzian holonomy fixing a spacelike geodesic, with rotation parameter (mass) $m$ along that geodesic; equivalently, the singular locus is a spacelike geodesic and a meridian linking $\Sigma$ has hyperbolic holonomy with translation length $m$.

Question: Given the pair $(N,\Sigma)$ as above, do there exist AdS structures on $N$ with tachyon singularities along $\Sigma$ that are arbitrarily close (in the deformation space of $(G,X)$-structures on $N$) to the given nonsingular AdS structure? What topological conditions on the pair $(N,\Sigma)$ are necessary or sufficient for the existence of such deformations? What geometric conditions (e.g. on the homotopy class or on the geometry of $\Sigma$ inside $N$) are necessary or sufficient?
category_tag: anti-de Sitter structures with cone/tachyon singularities
status_search_result: The question asks for a general criterion (topological/geometric conditions on $(N,\Sigma)$) under which a nonsingular AdS structure on a closed 3-manifold can be deformed to nearby AdS structures with tachyon singularities along a prescribed link. Existing work establishes such deformations in specific examples (e.g. unit tangent bundles of $(2,m,m)$ triangle orbifolds for $m\ge 5$, via geometric transitions through half-pipe geometry from hyperbolic cone structures), but no general necessary/sufficient conditions on $(N,\Sigma)$ have been found in the literature surveyed. The problem appears to remain open in full generality.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: What physical process produces the prompt high-energy emission in gamma-ray bursts, specifically what mechanism generates its nonthermal component, and does the prompt-emission spectrum also contain a photospheric thermal component? The unresolved alternatives named in the source are synchrotron radiation, jitter radiation, and synchrotron self-Compton emission for the nonthermal part, together with the separate possibility that thermal photospheric emission is present in the same prompt signal.
self_contained_problem:
Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) exhibit a prompt high-energy emission phase whose spectrum is typically well fit by a smoothly broken power law with a non-thermal appearance, but whose underlying radiative origin remains uncertain. Determine the physical radiation process that produces the prompt high-energy emission in GRBs. Specifically:

(a) Identify which mechanism is responsible for the non-thermal component of the prompt spectrum among the following candidates:
 (i) optically thin synchrotron radiation by relativistic electrons in a tangled or ordered magnetic field within the relativistic jet,
 (ii) jitter radiation, i.e. radiation by relativistic electrons traversing small-scale, randomly oriented magnetic field fluctuations whose coherence length is much smaller than the electron Larmor radius, or
 (iii) synchrotron self-Compton emission, in which synchrotron photons are inverse-Compton scattered by the same population of relativistic electrons.

(b) Determine whether the prompt emission spectrum also contains a photospheric thermal component, namely (quasi-)blackbody radiation released at the Thomson photosphere of the relativistic outflow, in addition to the non-thermal component identified in (a).

Provide a definitive identification of the dominant non-thermal mechanism and decide the presence (or absence) of a thermal photospheric contribution in the prompt emission of GRBs.
status_search_result: Recent reviews and 2024–2026 observational studies indicate the question is still open and actively debated. Time-resolved spectroscopy of bright GRBs (e.g. GRB 230307A, GRB 240825A) provides growing evidence for hybrid models combining a photospheric thermal component with a non-thermal component, and for transitions between photosphere-dominated and synchrotron-dominated regimes, but no consensus on whether the non-thermal part is synchrotron, jitter, or SSC has been reached.

original_question: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l and ρ_r be quasi-Fuchsian representations of π1(S) into PSL2(C). Does there exist a (ρ_l, ρ_r)-equivariant space-like embedding of the universal cover of S into the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C, and if such an embedding exists, can one choose one of constant curvature?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\widetilde{S}$ denote its universal cover. Let $\rho_l, \rho_r : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ be two quasi-Fuchsian representations. 

Let $X_{\mathbb{C}}$ denote the complex anti-de Sitter space, defined as $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ equipped with its bi-invariant complex pseudo-Riemannian metric coming from (a complex multiple of) the Killing form, on which $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ acts isometrically by left and right multiplication: $(g_l, g_r)\cdot x = g_l \, x \, g_r^{-1}$. A smooth embedding $f : \widetilde{S} \to X_{\mathbb{C}}$ is called $(\rho_l, \rho_r)$-equivariant if 
$$ f(\gamma \cdot p) = \rho_l(\gamma) \, f(p) \, \rho_r(\gamma)^{-1} \quad \text{for all } \gamma \in \pi_1(S), \ p \in \widetilde{S},$$
and is called space-like if the pullback by $f$ of the (real part of the) ambient pseudo-Riemannian metric is a Riemannian metric on $\widetilde{S}$.

(a) Does there always exist a $(\rho_l, \rho_r)$-equivariant space-like embedding $f : \widetilde{S} \to X_{\mathbb{C}}$?

(b) When such an embedding exists, can it be chosen so that the induced metric on $\widetilde{S}$ has constant curvature?

The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: If highly relativistic, Poynting-flux-dominated jets dissipate magnetic energy directly into radiation, by what specific physical process does that magnetic dissipation accelerate particles and produce nonthermal emission, and how should that process be evaluated relative to alternative particle-acceleration channels operating in jets, including mechanisms driven by cross-flow velocity shear?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a highly relativistic astrophysical outflow (a "jet") whose energy is carried predominantly in electromagnetic (Poynting) flux rather than in bulk kinetic energy of matter, as is thought to be the case in some models of gamma-ray burst (GRB) jets and active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets. Suppose that, somewhere along the flow, magnetic energy is dissipated and converted directly into radiation, producing the observed nonthermal (e.g., power-law) photon spectrum.

(a) Identify and characterize the specific physical mechanism(s) by which the dissipation of magnetic energy in such a Poynting-flux-dominated relativistic flow accelerates charged particles to a nonthermal energy distribution capable of producing the observed radiation. The description should specify the microphysical process (e.g., the relevant electromagnetic field structures, the acceleration channel, and the resulting particle spectrum), as well as the macroscopic conditions in the flow under which the mechanism operates efficiently.

(b) Compare this magnetic-dissipation acceleration channel quantitatively with alternative particle-acceleration mechanisms that may operate in relativistic jets, in particular mechanisms that extract energy from cross-flow velocity shear (shear acceleration at the jet boundary). The comparison should address relative efficiency, characteristic acceleration timescales, the resulting particle energy spectra, the maximum attainable Lorentz factors, and the regimes (in jet magnetization, Lorentz factor, and geometry) in which each mechanism dominates.
status_search_result: Recent reviews and simulation studies (2020–2025) continue to investigate magnetic reconnection as the leading channel for converting Poynting flux into nonthermal particles in relativistic jets, with active work on power-law spectra, 3D effects, and competing shear-driven acceleration. The microphysical details, efficiency, and relative weight of magnetic-reconnection vs. shear acceleration in GRB/AGN jets remain unresolved, indicating the problem is still open.

context_brief: Proper domains for quasi-Fuchsian pairs in X_C
original_question: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l and ρ_r be quasi-Fuchsian representations of π1(S) into PSL2(C). Does there exist a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which the subgroup (ρ_l, ρ_r)(π1(S)) of PSL2(C) × PSL2(C) acts properly discontinuously, and if so, what is the topology of the quotient of that domain?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\pi_1(S)$ denote its fundamental group. A representation $\rho:\pi_1(S)\to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ is called quasi-Fuchsian if it is faithful, discrete, and its limit set in $\partial\mathbb{H}^3=\mathbb{CP}^1$ is a Jordan curve.

Consider the complex anti-de Sitter space
$$X_{\mathbb{C}} \;=\; \bigl(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\bigr)\big/\Delta,$$
where $\Delta$ denotes the diagonal subgroup, equipped with the natural left action of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ (the complexification of the standard model of three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space).

Given two quasi-Fuchsian representations $\rho_l,\rho_r:\pi_1(S)\to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$, form the homomorphism
$$(\rho_l,\rho_r):\pi_1(S)\longrightarrow \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}),\qquad \gamma\mapsto(\rho_l(\gamma),\rho_r(\gamma)).$$

(a) Does there exist an open subset $\Omega\subseteq X_{\mathbb{C}}$, invariant under $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\pi_1(S))$, on which this group acts properly discontinuously, and which is maximal among such subsets (with respect to inclusion)?

(b) If such a maximal domain $\Omega$ exists, determine the topology (in particular the homeomorphism or diffeomorphism type) of the quotient manifold $\Omega/(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\pi_1(S))$.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: Can internal magnetic-energy dissipation, by itself, efficiently accelerate a relativistic jet through the magnetic-pressure gradient it creates along the flow when the problem is modeled without the strong simplifications used in existing approximate treatments, using instead more realistic resistive relativistic-magnetohydrodynamic calculations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic astrophysical jet modeled within the framework of resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), in which the plasma is described by the relativistic continuity, energy-momentum, and Maxwell equations together with a generalized Ohm's law that includes a finite electrical resistivity (so that the ideal-MHD frozen-in condition is relaxed and magnetic reconnection/dissipation can occur). Suppose the jet is initially Poynting-flux-dominated, i.e. its energy flux is carried predominantly by the electromagnetic field rather than by particle rest-mass and enthalpy.

Internal dissipation of magnetic energy along the flow generates a gradient in magnetic pressure that can do work on the plasma and accelerate it. The question is to determine, without invoking simplifying assumptions such as prescribed dissipation profiles, idealized geometry, or neglect of dynamical back-reaction, whether internal magnetic-energy dissipation alone — that is, in the absence of any acceleration that would occur in the corresponding non-dissipative ideal-MHD configuration — can, through the magnetic-pressure gradient it produces along the flow, efficiently accelerate the jet to high Lorentz factors (Γ ≫ 1) characteristic of relativistic astrophysical jets.

Formulate and answer this question by means of self-consistent resistive relativistic MHD calculations: quantify the asymptotic Lorentz factor, the magnetization parameter σ = b²/(4πρc²) (where b² is the comoving magnetic-field energy density and ρ the rest-mass density), and the conversion efficiency of Poynting flux into kinetic flux as functions of the resistivity prescription, the initial magnetization, and the jet geometry, and decide under what (if any) conditions dissipation-driven acceleration alone is efficient.
status_search_result: Recent resistive relativistic MHD simulations and semianalytic studies (2023–2025) have begun to address this question directly. Findings indicate that Ohmic dissipation can modify jet structure (enhanced collimation, stronger toroidal fields) but tends to weaken thermal acceleration and in some regimes even decelerates the outflow, while in other configurations magnetic dissipation contributes to acceleration through localized dissipation regions. A complete, parameter-space-spanning answer to whether dissipation alone can efficiently accelerate Poynting-dominated jets to high Lorentz factors under fully realistic RRMHD conditions has not yet been settled, so the problem is best regarded as partially resolved.

context_brief: Proper actions on X_C for 3-manifold groups
original_question: Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold and let ρ_l, ρ_r be convex cocompact representations of π1(M) into PSL2(C). Is there a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which (ρ_l, ρ_r)(π1(M)) acts properly discontinuously, what is the topology of the quotient, and how can one read properness or non-properness of this action geometrically?

(b) When such a maximal domain $\Omega$ exists, describe the topology of the quotient $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\Gamma)\backslash \Omega$.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: How is strong dissipation actually achieved in initially Poynting-flux-dominated relativistic outflows, and does efficient dissipation in relativistic jet sources require a configuration analogous to the one invoked for the pulsar-wind “σ problem,” where the outstanding issue is how magnetic energy is converted efficiently in the first place?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic outflow that is initially Poynting-flux dominated, i.e. whose energy flux is carried predominantly by an ordered electromagnetic field rather than by the bulk kinetic energy of matter. Define the magnetization parameter σ as the ratio of Poynting flux to matter (rest-mass plus kinetic) energy flux at a given location along the flow; an initially Poynting-flux-dominated outflow has σ ≫ 1 at its base. Observations of relativistic jet sources (e.g. those associated with active galactic nuclei and gamma-ray bursts) indicate that, by the time the flow reaches the dissipation/emission region, a substantial fraction of the electromagnetic energy must have been converted into kinetic energy of the bulk flow and/or into the energy of nonthermal radiating particles, so that σ has decreased to values of order unity or below.

(a) Identify a physically consistent mechanism by which strong dissipation of magnetic energy can be achieved in an initially Poynting-flux-dominated relativistic outflow, specifying the geometry of the magnetic field, the role of current sheets and/or current-driven (e.g. kink) instabilities, the role of magnetic reconnection, and the resulting partition of dissipated energy between bulk acceleration and nonthermal particle acceleration.

(b) Determine whether efficient magnetic-energy conversion in such relativistic jets necessarily requires a configuration analogous to the striped-wind/current-sheet structure invoked for the pulsar-wind "σ problem" (in which a small-scale alternating magnetic field component dissipates via reconnection in the equatorial current sheet), or whether other field configurations (e.g. globally helical fields with no small-scale stripes) can yield comparable dissipation efficiencies under realistic conditions.
status_search_result: The pulsar-wind σ problem and the analogous question of efficient magnetic dissipation in Poynting-flux-dominated relativistic jets remain active research questions. Although various mechanisms (reconnection in striped current sheets, kink instabilities, turbulence-enhanced dissipation, PIC-simulation evidence for reconnection beyond the light cylinder) have been proposed, no single mechanism has been universally established as the resolution. Papers from 2013 through 2024 continue to propose partial solutions and refinements rather than a definitive answer.

original_question: For the q-Eulerian numbers of type B defined by B_n(t, q) = Σ_{k=0}^n B_{n,k}(q)t^k, is the symmetric identity proposed in Conjecture 1.8 true: for natural numbers a and b, with α = a + b + 1, does (α choose a)_q + Σ_k (α choose k)_q 2^(α-k) B_{k,b}(q) equal (α choose b)_q + Σ_k (α choose k)_q 2^(α-k) B_{k,a}(q)?

   (m choose j)_q = [m]_q! / ([j]_q! [m−j]_q!).

original_question: What produces gamma-ray-burst afterglow emission: how many distinct outflow components contribute at a given stage of the afterglow evolution, and what are the relative contributions of synchrotron emission and inverse-Compton emission in each observed spectral regime?

Consider the broadband (radio through very-high-energy gamma-ray) afterglow emission that follows a gamma-ray burst (GRB), modeled as arising from one or more relativistic outflow components (e.g., a forward shock driven into the circumburst medium, a reverse shock propagating into the ejecta, a long-lived central-engine outflow, a structured jet with a narrow core and wider wings, or a cocoon component) whose shocked electrons radiate via synchrotron emission and synchrotron self-Compton (and external inverse-Compton) emission. For a generic GRB afterglow, address the following:

(a) Determine, as a function of observer time t after the burst trigger, the number N(t) of physically distinct outflow components that contribute non-negligibly to the observed afterglow flux, and characterize how N(t) depends on the burst's energetics, ejecta Lorentz factor distribution, jet structure, and the density profile of the circumburst medium.

(b) For each component identified in (a), and in each of the standard synchrotron spectral regimes delimited by the self-absorption frequency ν_a, the injection frequency ν_m, and the cooling frequency ν_c, compute the fractional contribution of synchrotron radiation versus inverse-Compton (IC) radiation to the observed specific flux F_ν(t), expressed in terms of the microphysical shock parameters (ε_e, ε_B, p), the bulk Lorentz factor, the Compton Y-parameter, and the Klein–Nishina suppression factor.

Provide a predictive framework that, given the observable multiwavelength light curves and spectra, uniquely identifies the number of components and the synchrotron/IC partition in each spectral regime.
status_search_result: The decomposition of GRB afterglow emission into distinct outflow components and the relative role of synchrotron versus inverse-Compton processes remain active research questions. paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: For a partition λ of n, with hook lengths h_u, arms a_u, legs ℓ_u, and multiplicities k_j(λ) = #{i : λ_i = j}, is it true that the four partition sums in Conjecture 2.1 are all equal: Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ, a_u=0} (h_u+t)/h_u, Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{j≥1} binom(k_j+t, k_j), Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (h_u^2+t)/h_u^2, and Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ, ℓ_u=0} (h_u+t)/h_u?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let t be an indeterminate. For a partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ … ) of n, write λ ⊢ n. Identify λ with its Young diagram, the set of cells u = (i, j) with 1 ≤ j ≤ λ_i. For a cell u ∈ λ, define:
• the arm a_u = λ_i − j (the number of cells strictly to the right of u in its row);
• the leg ℓ_u = λ'_j − i, where λ' is the conjugate partition (the number of cells strictly below u in its column);
• the hook length h_u = a_u + ℓ_u + 1.
For each integer j ≥ 1, let k_j(λ) = #{ i : λ_i = j } be the multiplicity of j as a part of λ, and write k_j = k_j(λ). For a nonnegative integer m and an indeterminate t, let \binom{m+t}{m} = (t+1)(t+2)⋯(t+m)/m! (with value 1 when m = 0).

Define the four polynomials in t:
S_1(n; t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} ∏_{u ∈ λ : a_u = 0} (h_u + t)/h_u,
S_2(n; t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} ∏_{j ≥ 1} \binom{k_j(λ) + t}{k_j(λ)},
S_3(n; t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} ∏_{u ∈ λ} (h_u^2 + t)/h_u^2,
S_4(n; t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} ∏_{u ∈ λ : ℓ_u = 0} (h_u + t)/h_u.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer n and as polynomial identities in t,
S_1(n; t) = S_2(n; t) = S_3(n; t) = S_4(n; t).
status_search_result: The equality S_1 = S_4 follows from conjugation of partitions, which interchanges arms and legs. The identity S_3 corresponds to the Nekrasov–Okounkov hook-length formula (with a shift), proved by Han. The equality involving the arm-zero/leg-zero refined product was conjectured by Amdeberhan and proved by Heim, Neuhauser and Rupp (Archiv der Mathematik, 2019; arXiv:1810.02226). The general family of Amdeberhan's hook-length conjectures, including the equality with the multiplicity sum S_2, was established by Chenglang Yang, "Hook-Lengths, Symplectic/Orthogonal Contents and Amdeberhan's Conjectures" (arXiv:2404.01973; Proc. London Math. Soc., 2025).

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: Is the proposed photon-breeding mechanism in active-galactic-nucleus jets actually viable as a way to convert a significant fraction of jet kinetic energy into high-energy radiation once the model is tested with more elaborate numerical simulations that include the dynamical response of the ambient medium and the character of the ambient medium's assumed magnetization?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic jet emanating from an active galactic nucleus, propagating through an ambient medium that is assumed to be magnetized. In the photon-breeding scenario, high-energy photons produced inside the jet escape into the ambient medium, where they Compton-scatter off ambient particles; the scattered photons can re-enter the jet, undergo photon-photon collisions to create electron-positron pairs, and these new pairs are then accelerated by the jet bulk flow and produce further high-energy photons. Under suitable conditions this feedback loop is supercritical and exponentially amplifies the high-energy photon population at the expense of the jet's bulk kinetic energy.

Determine, by means of self-consistent numerical simulations that explicitly include (i) the dynamical back-reaction and response of the ambient medium to the energy and momentum deposited by the breeding photons and pairs, and (ii) realistic assumptions about the strength and topology of the ambient magnetization, whether the photon-breeding mechanism remains viable as a process that converts a significant (order-unity) fraction of the jet's kinetic luminosity into high-energy electromagnetic radiation. In particular, identify the range of jet Lorentz factors, jet radii, ambient densities, and ambient magnetic-field configurations for which the supercritical breeding regime is realized and the radiative efficiency is large.
status_search_result: Searches return the original photon-breeding proposals and follow-up studies establishing the mechanism in idealized cylindrical, homogeneous, non-radiating jet setups, but no published work appears to have carried out the more elaborate self-consistent simulations including ambient-medium back-reaction and realistic magnetization that would settle viability. The question therefore appears to remain open.

P_n(t) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \; \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{h_u^2 + t}{h_u^2}.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: If long/soft gamma-ray-burst jets are accelerated magnetically and later undergo rarefaction acceleration after leaving the progenitor star, how can that scenario explain reports of very early jet breaks in afterglow light curves, and do such very early jet breaks actually occur in real bursts?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a model of long/soft gamma-ray-burst (GRB) outflows in which the relativistic jet is accelerated primarily by magnetic forces while propagating through the progenitor star, and then undergoes additional ("rarefaction") acceleration once the jet exits the stellar envelope into a much lower-density medium. In the standard afterglow framework, a "jet break" is an achromatic steepening of the afterglow light curve that occurs at the observer time t_j when the bulk Lorentz factor Γ of the decelerating blast wave drops below 1/θ_j, where θ_j is the half-opening angle of the jet; this break time is related to the isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy E_iso, the ambient density n, and θ_j by approximately t_j ∝ (E_iso/n)^{1/3} θ_j^{8/3} (1+z) for a uniform conical jet in a constant-density medium.

(a) Within the magnetic-acceleration-plus-rarefaction-acceleration scenario described above, derive whether and under what choices of model parameters (initial magnetization, opening angle at breakout, post-breakout acceleration efficiency, ambient density profile) the predicted afterglow light curve can exhibit a jet break at very early observer times (e.g., t_j ≲ a few hundred seconds to ~10^3 s after the prompt emission).

(b) Determine whether such very early achromatic jet breaks are actually present in observed GRB afterglow datasets, by specifying the observational criteria (achromaticity across X-ray, optical, and radio bands; post-break temporal slope; consistency of inferred θ_j) that must be met, and assessing whether any reported early breaks satisfy these criteria.
status_search_result: The question concerns whether magnetically accelerated GRB jets with post-breakout rarefaction acceleration can produce very early afterglow jet breaks, and whether such breaks are real. The literature on GRB jet breaks (e.g., Swift-era studies) shows continuing debate: many "early breaks" lack achromaticity and may instead reflect energy injection or structured jets, and magnetic acceleration models continue to be developed without a definitive resolution. No conclusive consensus answer was located.

original_question: For the same hook polynomial P_n(t) = Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (h_u^2 + t)/h_u^2, is P_n(t) unimodal for every n?
self_contained_problem:
For a partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$ (written $\lambda \vdash n$), the Young diagram of $\lambda$ is the set of unit cells $u$ arranged in left-justified rows whose lengths are the parts of $\lambda$. For each cell $u$ in the Young diagram, the hook length $h_u$ is the number of cells directly to the right of $u$ in the same row, plus the number of cells directly below $u$ in the same column, plus $1$ (for $u$ itself).

Define the polynomial
$$P_n(t) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n}\; \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{h_u^{2} + t}{h_u^{2}} \;\in\; \mathbb{Q}[t].$$

A polynomial $a_0 + a_1 t + a_2 t^2 + \cdots + a_d t^d$ with real coefficients is called unimodal if there exists an index $k$ such that $a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_k \ge a_{k+1} \ge \cdots \ge a_d$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial $P_n(t)$ is unimodal.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: In low/hard accretion states of galactic black-hole binaries, is jet dominance really caused by the formation of a large-scale poloidal magnetic-field configuration, and if so what detailed physical process forms that field while remaining consistent with spectral models that infer a relatively weak magnetic field in the X-ray emission region of the hard state and a comparatively strong field in the soft state?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a galactic black-hole X-ray binary, modeled as a stellar-mass black hole accreting from a companion star via an accretion disk, which is observed to undergo transitions between two canonical spectral states: (i) a low/hard state, characterized by a hard power-law X-ray spectrum and the presence of a steady, powerful relativistic jet, and (ii) a soft (high/soft) state, characterized by a thermal-dominant disk spectrum and strong suppression or absence of the steady jet. Spectral modeling of the X-ray emission region indicates that the hard state is compatible with a comparatively weak magnetic field in the X-ray-emitting region while the soft state is compatible with a comparatively strong field there.

Address the following questions:

1. Is the dominance of a relativistic jet during the low/hard state caused by the formation of a large-scale, ordered poloidal magnetic-field configuration threading the inner accretion flow and/or the black hole?

2. If so, identify the detailed physical mechanism (e.g., advection of external flux by a hot, geometrically thick inner flow; magnetic flux trapping; dynamo action; disk-wind-mediated transport; or another process) by which such a large-scale poloidal field is generated and maintained in the hard state but not in the soft state.

3. Show that the proposed mechanism is quantitatively consistent with the spectral constraints, namely a relatively weak magnetic field in the X-ray emission region during the hard state and a relatively strong field there during the soft state, while still permitting (in the hard state) a poloidal flux configuration sufficient to power the observed jet via, e.g., a Blandford–Znajek or Blandford–Payne type mechanism.
status_search_result: The mechanism producing large-scale poloidal magnetic flux in the inner regions of black-hole X-ray binary accretion flows, and its connection to state transitions and jet launching, remains an active area of research. Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD) models and flux-advection scenarios have made progress, but the detailed origin of the field, its state dependence, and reconciliation with X-ray spectral magnetic-field constraints are not settled.

paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
original_question: What is the precise nature of the accretion–outflow connection in relativistic jet sources, to what extent is the outflow controlled by properties of the central compact object rather than only by the accretion flow, and what role does black-hole spin play in driving outflows in X-ray binaries and, by analogy, in active galactic nuclei?
self_contained_problem:
Consider relativistic jet sources, namely astrophysical systems in which a central compact object (a black hole or a neutron star) accretes matter from a surrounding accretion flow and launches a collimated, relativistic outflow (a "jet"). Such sources include Galactic X-ray binaries (XRBs), in which the compact object accretes from a stellar companion, and active galactic nuclei (AGNs), in which a supermassive black hole accretes at the center of a galaxy.

Address the following questions:

(a) Characterize precisely the accretion–outflow connection in relativistic jet sources: namely, give a quantitative relationship between the properties of the accretion flow (e.g. mass accretion rate, spectral state, disk geometry, magnetic flux threading the disk) and the properties of the launched outflow (e.g. jet power, Lorentz factor, mass-loading, collimation, duty cycle).

(b) Determine to what extent the outflow is controlled by intrinsic properties of the central compact object — in particular its mass, spin, magnetic field, and the presence or absence of a horizon — as opposed to being determined solely by the accretion flow. Formulate a criterion that disentangles these two contributions.

(c) Specifically, quantify the role of black-hole spin $a_* = cJ/(GM^2)$ in driving outflows from stellar-mass black hole XRBs. Compare systematically with neutron-star XRBs (which by definition have no event horizon and a different spin/magnetic-field structure) so as to isolate the effect of the spin and/or horizon. Then, using the observed scaling analogies between XRBs and AGNs, decide whether the conclusions reached for stellar-mass systems can be extended to extragalactic jets.

Provide either theoretical predictions, observational diagnostics, or a combination thereof that resolves (a)–(c).
status_search_result: The disk–jet connection and the role of black-hole spin in launching relativistic jets remain active areas of investigation. Recent work (e.g. a 2025 Nature Astronomy study) finds that the fastest jets propagate along the black-hole spin axis, supporting the Blandford–Znajek picture, but no clear correlation between measured spin values and jet speeds has yet been established, and the relative contributions of spin versus accretion-flow properties (and the XRB→AGN extrapolation) are not settled.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
context_brief: Threshold branch points and cluster states
original_question: In continuum shell-model descriptions of nuclei as open quantum systems, a nucleus is coupled to scattering and decay channels through an energy-dependent effective Hamiltonian, and particle-emission thresholds appear as branch points of the scattering matrix. Is the formation of cluster states near decay thresholds, such as α-cluster states near α-emission thresholds or correlated two-neutron halo states near two-neutron emission thresholds, directly controlled by the branch point singularity of the relevant reaction channel, and what mechanism connects the threshold singularity to the channel-aligned cluster structure?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite many-body fermionic quantum system (a nucleus) modeled as an open quantum system, in which bound states, resonances, and scattering states are treated on equal footing through an energy-dependent, non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian H_eff(E) acting on the internal (bound-state-like) subspace, obtained by projection from a full Hamiltonian that couples the internal subspace to a set of decay/scattering channels c=1,...,N_c with thresholds E_c (continuum shell-model / Gamow shell-model framework). The associated multichannel scattering matrix S(E) is a meromorphic function on a multi-sheeted Riemann surface whose branch points lie at the channel thresholds E_c, since the channel momenta k_c(E) = √(2μ_c(E−E_c))/ℏ are square-root branch functions of E at E=E_c.

A "cluster state" associated to channel c is an internal eigenstate of H_eff(E) whose intrinsic structure, near E≈E_c, is dominated by the channel wave function of c (e.g., an α+core configuration for an α-emission channel, or a correlated dineutron-plus-core configuration for a two-neutron emission channel).

Problem. Establish (or refute) the following statements, and identify the precise mathematical mechanism if they hold:

(a) The square-root branch-point singularity of S(E) at a channel threshold E_c forces, through the energy dependence of the coupling term W(E) = ∑_c |Φ_c⟩ ⟨Φ_c| in H_eff(E), an alignment of one or more internal eigenstates of H_eff(E) with the channel wave function of c as E → E_c, so that the corresponding eigenstate acquires the cluster structure of channel c.

(b) Quantify this alignment: derive, in terms of the threshold branch-point and the channel coupling strength, the rate at which the overlap between the relevant eigenstate of H_eff(E) and the channel state of c approaches unity as E → E_c, and determine the conditions on the channel (s-wave vs. higher partial waves, charged vs. neutral, one-body vs. many-body break-up) under which this near-threshold cluster alignment is generic.

(c) Conclude whether the ubiquitous appearance of cluster states immediately below or above their respective particle-emission thresholds (such as a 0⁺ state just above an α+core threshold, or a halo ground state just below a two-neutron threshold) is a direct, model-independent consequence of the branch-point singularity at that threshold.
category_tag: Open quantum systems and threshold singularities
status_search_result: Subsequent work in the continuum/Gamow shell-model framework has provided substantial evidence and partial mechanisms linking near-threshold clustering to the branch-point singularity at the particle-emission threshold. Studies analyze exceptional points and continuum-coupling correlation energy near thresholds, showing that the branch point at a channel opening induces non-local correlations and channel-aligned cluster structure. However, a fully model-independent, quantitative theorem connecting the threshold branch-point singularity to the universal emergence of cluster states across all channel types remains unresolved.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is the generating function Σ_{n≥0} z^n/n! Σ_{π∈Inv(S_n)} tr(π)^k equal to ᵃB_k(z) e^{z + z^2/2}, where ᵃB_k(z) denotes the Bell polynomial appearing in Conjecture 4.1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters and let $\mathrm{Inv}(S_n) = \{\pi \in S_n : \pi^2 = e\}$ be the set of involutions in $S_n$. For $\pi \in S_n$, let $\mathrm{tr}(\pi)$ denote the number of fixed points of $\pi$ (equivalently, the trace of the permutation matrix of $\pi$).

For an integer $k \ge 0$, let $B_k(z)$ denote the $k$-th (exponential) Bell polynomial, also known as the Touchard polynomial, characterized by the operator identity
$$\left(z\frac{d}{dz}\right)^k e^{z} = B_k(z)\, e^{z},$$
equivalently $B_k(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} S(k,j)\, z^{j}$, where $S(k,j)$ are the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

Decide whether, for every integer $k \ge 0$, the following identity of formal power series in $z$ holds:
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{z^{n}}{n!} \sum_{\pi \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n)} \mathrm{tr}(\pi)^{k} \;=\; B_k(z)\, e^{\,z + z^{2}/2}.$$
status_search_result: A direct identity of this type follows from differentiating the classical bivariate exponential generating function $\sum_{n\ge 0}\frac{z^n}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Inv}(S_n)} x^{\mathrm{tr}(\pi)} = e^{xz + z^2/2}$ via the operator $(x\partial_x)^k$ at $x=1$, but no specific reference confirming or refuting the exact form of the conjecture (with the particular Bell polynomial $\bar B_k$ used in the source) was located in the search. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
context_brief: States most affected by continuum coupling
original_question: In nuclear open quantum systems, how can one identify and predict which bound or unbound interacting-shell-model eigenstates are most strongly reorganized by coupling to scattering-continuum reaction channels, rather than assuming that continuum coupling produces a uniform instability of all states near a particle-emission threshold?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a nucleus described as an open quantum system in which valence nucleons occupy a single-particle space consisting of bound shell-model orbitals together with scattering states forming a continuum of reaction channels (e.g., one-nucleon and cluster decay channels above the corresponding particle-emission thresholds). Let H_0 be the standard interacting shell-model (ISM) Hamiltonian on the bound (Hermitian) configuration space, with eigenstates {|i⟩} and energies {E_i}. Let H be the corresponding open-quantum-system Hamiltonian (e.g., a Gamow shell model or continuum shell model Hamiltonian) acting on the enlarged Hilbert space that includes the scattering continuum, and let E_corr(i) denote the continuum-coupling correlation energy of the state derived from |i⟩, defined as the shift of its real part of energy due to the coupling to the continuum.

Formulate criteria, expressible in terms of the unperturbed ISM eigenstates {|i⟩}, their quantum numbers, the structure of the relevant decay channels, and the angular momentum / Coulomb barrier of the channel, that identify which ISM eigenstates are strongly reorganized by the continuum coupling (large |E_corr(i)| and large rearrangement of the wave function) versus those that are essentially unaffected, in the regime where excitation energies lie near a particle-emission threshold.

In particular, justify or refute the following picture: continuum coupling does not produce a uniform instability of all ISM eigenstates near a particle-emission threshold; instead, for each susceptible ISM wave function the near-threshold rearrangement is concentrated in a single dominant pair of unperturbed ISM states, and one should be able to predict a priori which pairs (i,j) of ISM states are the susceptible ones from the overlap of |i⟩ and |j⟩ with the channel wave functions of the open decay channels.
category_tag: Open quantum systems in nuclear shell model
status_search_result: Subsequent Gamow shell model studies (notably a 2024 study of continuum-coupling correlation energy near particle emission thresholds in 7Li and 7Be) have made substantial progress: they confirm that the correlation energy is state- and system-dependent, peaks at threshold for ℓ=0 neutron channels (shifted above threshold for protons due to Coulomb barrier), grows with valence nucleon number, is enhanced in even-even isotopes, and is largest for cluster decay channels. However, a fully general predictive criterion identifying a priori which ISM eigenstates and which pairs are most susceptible across arbitrary nuclei has not been established, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is the generating function Σ_{n≥0} x^n/n! Σ_{π∈S_n, E(π)=0} 2^{κ(π)} B̄_{κ(π)}(z) equal to e^{2zx/(1-x)}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ elements. For a permutation $\pi \in S_n$, write its disjoint cycle decomposition and let:
- $E(\pi)$ be the number of cycles of even length in $\pi$;
- $\kappa(\pi)$ be the total number of cycles of $\pi$.

For an integer $k \geq 0$, let $\bar{B}_k(z)$ denote the (single-variable) Bell polynomial defined by the exponential generating function
$$\sum_{k\geq 0} \bar{B}_k(z)\,\frac{t^k}{k!} \;=\; e^{\,z(e^t-1)},$$
so $\bar{B}_k(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} S(k,j)\, z^j$, where $S(k,j)$ are the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

Decide whether the following identity of formal power series in $\mathbb{Q}[z][[x]]$ holds:
$$\sum_{n\geq 0} \frac{x^n}{n!} \sum_{\substack{\pi\in S_n \\ E(\pi)=0}} 2^{\kappa(\pi)}\, \bar{B}_{\kappa(\pi)}(z) \;=\; \exp\!\left(\frac{2zx}{1-x}\right).$$
That is, prove or disprove this equality, where the inner sum on the left ranges over all permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ all of whose cycles have odd length.
status_search_result: A web search for the specific identity relating odd-cycle permutations weighted by Bell polynomials and the generating function exp(2zx/(1-x)) did not return any direct proof or disproof. Standard references on Bell polynomials and cycle index polynomials of symmetric groups appear, but none address this particular weighted identity. Status could not be verified.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: For many-body nuclear systems whose energies lie in a narrow window around a reaction threshold, which structural properties are universal consequences of threshold physics, and which properties depend on the chosen nuclear Hamiltonian, effective interaction, or model realization?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a many-body quantum system described in the projected (Feshbach) framework as follows. Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{Q} \oplus \mathcal{P}$ be a decomposition of the Hilbert space into a closed (bound) subspace $\mathcal{Q}$ and an open (scattering) subspace $\mathcal{P}$ representing decay channels with thresholds $E_c$, $c=1,\dots,N$. The dynamics in $\mathcal{Q}$ are governed by an energy-dependent effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian
$$\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{eff}}(E) = H_{QQ} + W(E), \qquad W(E) = H_{QP}\,G_P^{(+)}(E)\,H_{PQ},$$
where $H_{QQ}$ is the Hermitian internal Hamiltonian on $\mathcal{Q}$, $H_{QP}, H_{PQ}$ are the couplings between subspaces, and $G_P^{(+)}(E)$ is the outgoing-wave Green's function on $\mathcal{P}$. The complex eigenvalues $\mathcal{E}_k(E)$ of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{eff}}(E)$ describe resonances; coalescences of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{eff}}(E)$ are called exceptional points.

Fix a reaction threshold $E_c$ and let $I_\delta = (E_c - \delta, E_c + \delta)$ be a narrow energy window around it.

Problem. Determine which structural and statistical properties of the spectrum and eigenstates of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{eff}}(E)$ for $E \in I_\delta$ — for example, level clustering and avoided crossings near the threshold, the formation of one collective ``superradiant'' broad state and $N-1$ trapped narrow states upon channel opening, the statistics of widths $\Gamma_k = -2\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal{E}_k$, the alignment of internal eigenstates with channel states, and threshold cusps in cross sections — are universal in the sense that they hold for every choice of $H_{QQ}$ and of the coupling $W(E)$ (subject only to unitarity, analyticity, and the threshold branch-point structure of $G_P^{(+)}$), and which properties (such as the precise locations of exceptional points in the spectrum of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{eff}}(E)$) genuinely depend on the specific realization of $H_{QQ}$, $W(E)$, and $E$. Provide a precise characterization separating the universal (threshold-induced) features from the model-dependent features.
category_tag: Open quantum systems near reaction thresholds
status_search_result: The question of separating universal threshold-induced features of the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian from model-dependent ones in nuclear open quantum systems remains an active research topic. While qualitative universal phenomena (superradiance/trapping, threshold cusps, collectivization of widths) are well-established for generic random or schematic couplings, a complete rigorous classification distinguishing universal threshold consequences from Hamiltonian-dependent features (notably exceptional-point locations) has not been established, and the problem is still discussed as open in subsequent reviews on near-threshold physics and continuum shell models.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: When neighboring nuclei with different proton and neutron numbers are interconnected through continuum reaction channels, what determines the size and internal organization of the resulting correlated domains, or clusters, of quantum states, and how do those features depend on the binding energies of the participating states?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a family of atomic nuclei labeled by their proton number Z and neutron number N. Model each nucleus as an open quantum many-body system whose discrete many-body eigenstates are coupled to a common continuum of reaction channels (decay channels into lighter fragments plus emitted particles). Through these shared continuum channels, many-body states belonging to neighboring nuclei (with different (Z,N)) become dynamically coupled, and one may define an equivalence-like notion of "correlated domains" (clusters) of quantum states: maximal collections of many-body eigenstates—possibly drawn from several neighboring nuclei—that are mutually coupled with non-negligible strength via the continuum.

Formally, for each nucleus (Z,N) let {|ψ_i^{(Z,N)}⟩} denote its set of resonant many-body states with complex energies E_i = ε_i − iΓ_i/2 and binding energies B_i. Let the effective continuum-mediated coupling between two such states |ψ_i^{(Z,N)}⟩ and |ψ_j^{(Z',N')}⟩ be V_{ij} = Σ_c (⟨ψ_i| H_{QP} |c⟩⟨c| H_{QP} |ψ_j⟩)/(E − E_c^+), summed over the open reaction channels c. Build a graph whose vertices are the many-body states of all nuclei and whose edges connect pairs (i,j) with |V_{ij}| above a fixed threshold; a "cluster" is a connected component of this graph.

Determine:
(a) the typical size (number of states, and the spread in (Z,N)) of such clusters;
(b) the internal organization of a cluster (e.g., distribution of couplings, hierarchy of states, statistical level/width correlations within it); and
(c) how (a) and (b) depend on the binding energies B_i of the participating states, in particular as one approaches the particle drip lines where B_i → 0.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the theory of nuclear open quantum systems: little is known about basic features such as a typical cluster size or its dependence on binding properties. Subsequent literature on continuum shell models and Gamow shell models continues to investigate continuum couplings between neighboring nuclei, but no general quantitative theory of such correlated-domain sizes and their binding-energy dependence appears to be established.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
context_brief: Combinatorial proof in gauge-theory partition formulas
original_question: Find a combinatorial proof of Corollary 5.2, which gives a closed formula for (1/n!) Σ_{λ⊢n} f_λ^2 Σ_{u∈λ} ∏_{j=0}^{r-1} (h_u^2 - j^2).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ … ≥ 0) of a positive integer n (written λ ⊢ n), the Young diagram of λ is the set of cells {(i,j) : 1 ≤ j ≤ λ_i}. For a cell u = (i,j) ∈ λ, the hook length h_u is

  h_u = λ_i − j + λ'_j − i + 1,

where λ' denotes the conjugate partition. Let f_λ denote the number of standard Young tableaux of shape λ; equivalently, by the hook length formula, f_λ = n! / ∏_{u∈λ} h_u.

Fix a nonnegative integer r. It is known (and provable algebraically using symmetric function identities) that the quantity

  S_r(n) := (1/n!) ∑_{λ ⊢ n} f_λ^2 ∑_{u ∈ λ} ∏_{j=0}^{r−1} (h_u^2 − j^2)

is given by an explicit closed-form polynomial expression in n (independent of any particular partition).

Problem. Provide a purely combinatorial (preferably bijective) proof of this closed-form evaluation of S_r(n). That is, give a combinatorial interpretation of the weighted sum on the left-hand side and a bijective argument that establishes its closed-form value, without recourse to the algebraic machinery of symmetric functions or character theory.
status_search_result: A web search located the original problem (a request for a combinatorial proof of a hook-length identity of Stanley type) and several related works on hook-length and hook-content identities, including bijective proofs of nearby identities (e.g., the n^2-difference between sums of squares of hooks and contents). However, no source explicitly announcing a combinatorial/bijective proof of this particular closed-form identity was found, so its current status could not be confirmed.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: For neutron-rich isotopic chains such as oxygen and fluorine, how can one distinguish a shift in the neutron drip line caused by continuum-coupling-induced effective many-body interactions from an explanation based on explicitly introduced effective three-body interactions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider neutron-rich isotopic chains, in particular the oxygen (Z=8) and fluorine (Z=9) chains, and the location of the neutron drip line along these chains. Two competing theoretical mechanisms have been proposed to explain why the neutron drip line shifts to substantially heavier isotopes when going from oxygen to fluorine:

(a) Continuum-coupling mechanism. In an open quantum system description of the nucleus, the Hilbert space is partitioned into an internal (bound) subspace and an external (scattering) subspace. Even when the underlying nucleon–nucleon interaction is purely two-body in the full space, projecting onto the internal subspace and integrating out the coupling to the continuum induces effective many-body (in particular effective three-body and higher) interactions among the valence nucleons. These continuum-induced many-body terms have been argued to account for the observed shift of the neutron drip line between oxygen and fluorine.

(b) Bare three-nucleon force mechanism. Alternatively, one may work in a closed-system framework and explicitly include a genuine three-nucleon interaction (for example, of chiral effective field theory origin) in the nuclear Hamiltonian. This bare three-body force has also been shown to reproduce the same shift of the neutron drip line.

Problem. Devise observable, model-independent criteria — based on measurable quantities such as binding energies, separation energies, spectroscopic factors, decay widths, reaction cross sections, or correlations near threshold — that allow one to discriminate between scenario (a) and scenario (b) as the dominant origin of the drip-line shift between the oxygen and fluorine isotopic chains. Equivalently, determine whether the two scenarios are physically distinguishable, or whether they are unitarily/effectively equivalent descriptions of the same low-energy physics.
category_tag: Nuclear open quantum systems and drip-line mechanisms
status_search_result: The literature shows that both continuum-coupling-induced effective many-body interactions and explicit chiral three-nucleon forces independently reproduce the observed drip-line shift between oxygen and fluorine, and recent works (e.g., Hagen et al., PRL 108, 242501 (2012); subsequent dripline studies through ~2020s) emphasize the interplay of continuum effects and 3N forces rather than a clean experimental separation. No observable criterion has been established that uniquely distinguishes the two mechanisms; the question is generally regarded as still open.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: For symplectic contents c_sp(u), is the generating function Σ_{n≥0} x^n Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_sp(u))/h(u) equal to the infinite product stated in Conjecture 6.2(a)?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots)$ of $n$, identify $\lambda$ with its Young diagram, and for a cell $u=(i,j)\in\lambda$ define:
- the hook length $h(u)=\lambda_i-j+\lambda'_j-i+1$, where $\lambda'$ denotes the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content
$$c_{sp}(u)=\begin{cases} j-i, & \text{if } j>i,\\ i+j-1, & \text{if } j\le i.\end{cases}$$

Let $t$ be a formal parameter and $q$ a formal variable. Prove or disprove that
$$\sum_{n\ge 0} q^{n}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{u\in\lambda}\frac{t+c_{sp}(u)}{h(u)}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{8n})^{\binom{t+1}{2}}}{(1-q^{8n-2})^{\binom{t+1}{2}-1}}\cdot\left(\frac{1-q^{4n-1}}{1-q^{4n-3}}\right)^{t}\cdot\left(\frac{1-q^{8n-4}}{1-q^{8n-6}}\right)^{\binom{t}{2}-1},$$
as an identity of formal power series in $q$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}[t]$.
status_search_result: Amdeberhan's symplectic content conjecture (the identity above) was established in full generality by Chenglang Yang in "Hook-Lengths, Symplectic/Orthogonal Contents and Amdeberhan's Conjectures" (arXiv:2404.01973, 2024), published in Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (2025), where it appears as Theorem 1.1 and is proved using vertex operator and symplectic Schur function techniques. Earlier special cases were proved by Amdeberhan, Andrews, and Ballantine, and by Han–Xiong.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: How can the organization of interacting-shell-model eigenfunctions near a particle-emission threshold be made quantitatively predictive, especially for the ground state of 11Li where low-lying two-neutron and one-neutron emission thresholds are separated by less than 30 keV and may determine the relative weights of configurations associated with the two-neutron continuum of 9Li and with unbound 10Li channels?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an interacting shell-model (ISM) description of a weakly bound nuclear system in which single-particle states couple to one or more particle-emission continua, so that the many-body Hamiltonian becomes non-Hermitian and its eigenfunctions develop branch-point singularities at particle-emission thresholds. In such a description the ground state of the halo nucleus 11Li lies extremely close to two distinct decay thresholds: the two-neutron emission threshold corresponding to the channel [9Li(3/2−)]⊗[n^2(0+)] (with two neutrons in the continuum of 9Li) and the one-neutron emission threshold corresponding to channels associated with the unbound subsystem 10Li, in particular {[9Li(1/2−)]⊗[n(1/2−)]}_{1+}⊗[n(1/2−)], {[9Li(1/2−)]⊗[n(1/2+)]}_{1−}⊗[n(1/2+)], and {[9Li(3/2−)]⊗[n(1/2−)]}_{2+}⊗[n(1/2−)]. Empirically these two thresholds are separated by less than 30 keV.

Develop a quantitatively predictive theoretical framework that:

(i) Describes how ISM eigenfunctions reorganize as a function of the energy separation between two (or more) nearby particle-emission thresholds (branch points of the resolvent), including the limit of approximate degeneracy.

(ii) Yields, for the 11Li ground state, the relative spectroscopic weights of the configurations associated with the 9Li two-neutron continuum versus the 10Li one-neutron continuum channels listed above, as a function of the positions of these thresholds.

(iii) Predicts observable consequences (such as the spatial structure of the two-neutron halo and pairing correlations) of the near-degeneracy of the two thresholds.

The problem is to construct such a framework and to obtain quantitative predictions for the configuration mixing in the 11Li ground state under the empirical near-degeneracy of its one- and two-neutron emission thresholds.
status_search_result: The problem of quantitatively predicting the organization of interacting shell-model eigenfunctions near multiple nearly-degenerate particle-emission thresholds, and in particular fixing the configuration mixing in the 11Li ground state from first principles, remains an active research area without a definitive quantitative resolution. Continuum shell-model and Gamow shell-model calculations have made progress on 11Li halo structure, but a fully predictive theory of the threshold-driven reorganization in this regime is not established.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: How can low-energy exceptional points in nuclear open quantum systems, understood as double poles of the scattering matrix that arise from the interplay of Hermitian and non-Hermitian continuum coupling above threshold, be located or tested experimentally through reaction studies, for example through characteristic structures in elastic scattering phase shifts?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open quantum system describing a nucleus coupled to scattering continua above particle-emission thresholds. The dynamics is governed by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian obtained by projecting the full Hermitian many-body problem onto a finite set of bound configurations after eliminating continuum channels; equivalently, one studies the analytic continuation of the multichannel scattering matrix S(E) into the complex energy plane.

An exceptional point is a value of an external (or internal) control parameter at which two eigenvalues of the effective Hamiltonian, together with their eigenvectors, coalesce, producing a non-diagonalizable Jordan block. Equivalently, it corresponds to a double pole of S(E) on the second Riemann sheet, arising from the interplay between Hermitian (real) and non-Hermitian (continuum-induced, energy-dependent) couplings between resonant states.

Problem. Devise an experimentally realizable nuclear reaction protocol that locates and verifies the existence of such low-energy exceptional points. In particular:

(a) Identify model-independent observable signatures distinguishing a double pole from two nearby simple poles in elastic-scattering cross sections and phase shifts. Show, for instance, under what general conditions the elastic phase shift δ_ℓ(E) in a relevant partial wave exhibits a single jump of 2π (rather than two separate jumps of π) as the energy crosses the exceptional-point region, and under what conditions the corresponding cross section displays a characteristic split-peak structure.

(b) Specify how a continuous external parameter (e.g. the strength of continuum coupling, an applied field, or a target/projectile choice that tunes thresholds) may be varied to drive the system through the exceptional point, and characterize the universal scaling of resonance widths and energies near coalescence.

(c) Provide a quantitative criterion that uses the measured phase shifts and/or cross sections to test, simultaneously, the underlying effective nucleon–nucleon interaction and the configuration mixing of the open-quantum-system description.
category_tag: non-Hermitian exceptional points in nuclear scattering
status_search_result: Theoretical signatures (single 2π phase-shift jump, split-peak cross sections) have been characterized within the Gamow shell model and complex-scaling frameworks, and recent work (e.g., Gamow shell model description of an exceptional point in 7Li, and complex-scaling studies of resonant/scattering-state coalescence) provides concrete predictions for nuclear reactions such as 4He(3H,3H)4He. However, an unambiguous, controlled experimental confirmation of a low-energy nuclear exceptional point through reaction studies has not been firmly established, so the original program is partially advanced rather than fully solved.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: At the specialization t = 0, are the symplectic and orthogonal content generating functions equal, and do they both reduce to ∏_{j≥1} 1/(1 + x^{4j-2}) as claimed in Conjecture 6.2(c)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda \vdash n$ denote a partition of $n$, drawn as a Young diagram with cells $u = (i,j)$ (row $i$, column $j$, $1$-indexed). For a cell $u = (i,j) \in \lambda$ define:
- the hook length $h(u) = \lambda_i - j + \lambda'_j - i + 1$, where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content
$$c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j + 2, & i < j, \\ \lambda_i + \lambda_i - 2i + 2, & i = j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j - 2, & i > j; \end{cases}$$
- the orthogonal content
$$c_{\mathrm{O}}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j, & i \le j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j, & i > j. \end{cases}$$
(Here $\lambda_i$ is set to $0$ for $i$ exceeding the length of $\lambda$, and similarly for $\lambda'$.)

$$\sum_{n \ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u)}{h(u)} \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{\mathrm{O}}(u)}{h(u)} \;=\; \prod_{j \ge 1} \frac{1}{1 + x^{4j-2}}.$$

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: What sequence of theoretical developments is needed to build a unified theory of nuclear structure and nuclear reactions that treats bound states, resonances, and scattering states symmetrically, rather than keeping the discrete shell-model spectrum and scattering continuum artificially separated?
self_contained_problem:
In nuclear many-body theory, a nucleus is modeled as a system of A nucleons interacting through a (generally non-local) effective Hamiltonian H. The traditional shell model represents H in a basis of square-integrable single-particle orbitals, producing only a discrete spectrum of bound states; nuclear reactions, by contrast, are described in terms of scattering states belonging to the continuous spectrum of H, while narrow resonances appear as poles of the S-matrix (equivalently, as Gamow / Berggren states with complex energies E = E_r − iΓ/2). These two descriptions are usually developed separately, so bound states, resonances, and non-resonant scattering states are not treated on the same footing.

The Berggren completeness relation expresses the identity on a suitable single-particle Hilbert space as
   1 = Σ_{n∈b∪d} |u_n⟩⟨ũ_n| + ∫_{L+} dk |u(k)⟩⟨ũ(k)|,
where b is the set of bound poles, d a finite set of decaying (Gamow) poles enclosed between the real axis and a contour L+ in the fourth quadrant of the complex momentum plane, and ũ denotes the biorthogonal partner. The Gamow Shell Model (GSM) is the A-body second-quantized theory built on antisymmetrized products of such Berggren single-particle states.

Problem. Formulate, within the GSM framework (or a mathematically equivalent open-quantum-system formalism), a unified A-body theory of nuclear structure and reactions with the following properties:

(i) The Hilbert space carries a Berggren-type completeness relation at the A-body level so that bound states, resonances (as generalized eigenvectors with complex eigenvalues), and non-resonant scattering states all appear as elements of a single resolution of the identity.

(ii) The A-body Hamiltonian H, including realistic two- and three-nucleon interactions, admits a well-defined (possibly non-Hermitian, complex-symmetric) representation in this basis whose discrete and continuous parts are computed simultaneously, with controlled truncations and convergence as the contour L+ and the model space are refined.

(iii) Reaction observables (elastic, inelastic, transfer, and radiative capture cross sections, e.g.\ for ^{12}C(α,γ)^{16}O) and structure observables (binding energies, spectra, electromagnetic moments, decay widths, e.g.\ along the isotopic chain ^{9}Li→^{12}Li and for the Hoyle resonance in ^{12}C) are obtained from the same eigenvectors of H.

Identify the sequence of theoretical and mathematical developments—e.g.\ construction of the A-body Berggren basis, treatment of center-of-mass spuriosity, inclusion of antisymmetrized channel projectors for clustered configurations, derivation of effective interactions in continuum-coupled spaces, and proofs of completeness/convergence—needed to establish such a unified framework, and prove that the resulting formalism reproduces standard bound-state shell-model results in the limit of vanishing coupling to the continuum and standard reaction theory in the asymptotic-channel limit.
category_tag: Nuclear open quantum systems / Gamow shell model
status_search_result: The question of building a fully unified theory of nuclear structure and reactions through the Gamow Shell Model and related continuum shell models remains an active research program. Substantial partial progress has been made (e.g., GSM in the coupled-channel representation, no-core Gamow shell model, ab initio calculations including continuum couplings), but a complete unified framework treating bound states, resonances and scattering symmetrically for general A-body systems with realistic interactions has not been achieved as of 2026.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: How can the Gamow Shell Model be supplied with effective interactions that are accurate and systematic enough to study long isotopic or isotonic chains continuously from the valley of stability to the particle drip lines?
self_contained_problem:
The Gamow Shell Model (GSM) is a configuration-interaction approach to the nuclear many-body problem in which the single-particle basis is the Berggren ensemble: a complete set obtained by analytic continuation of the one-body Schrödinger equation into the complex-momentum plane, consisting of bound states, narrow resonant (Gamow) states with complex energies E = E_r - iΓ/2, and a contour of non-resonant scattering states. The A-nucleon Hamiltonian is written in this basis as H = T + V, where T is the kinetic-energy operator (with center-of-mass corrections) and V is a two-body (and possibly three-body) interaction acting in the truncated valence space above an inert core.

Develop a procedure to construct effective two-body (and, where relevant, three-body) interactions V_eff for use in the Gamow Shell Model with the following properties:

1. Systematic derivation: V_eff is obtained from an underlying realistic nucleon-nucleon (and three-nucleon) interaction by a well-defined many-body renormalization or similarity transformation adapted to the Berggren basis (so that coupling to the continuum, including resonant and scattering single-particle states, is treated consistently).

2. Mass-range stability: the same prescription, with smoothly varying parameters or with no refitting per nucleus, yields binding energies, spectra, decay widths, and reaction observables across long isotopic chains (fixed proton number Z, varying neutron number N) and isotonic chains (fixed N, varying Z), continuously from nuclei near the valley of β-stability to nuclei at and beyond the particle drip lines.

3. Quantitative accuracy: the resulting GSM calculations reproduce, within controlled and quantifiable error, experimentally known low-lying energy levels, widths of unbound states, and one- and two-nucleon separation energies along these chains.

Construct such an effective interaction (or prove obstructions to its construction) and demonstrate the above three properties.
status_search_result: The construction of accurate, systematic effective interactions enabling Gamow Shell Model calculations across long isotopic/isotonic chains from stability to the drip lines remains an active research program. Recent works (e.g., realistic GSM with Vlowk/IM-SRG-type interactions, Density Matrix Renormalization Group GSM, and Coupled-Cluster GSM) have made progress on light and medium-mass nuclei, but no universally validated effective interaction covering long chains up to the drip lines has been established.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
original_question: How can the Gamow Shell Model, which has mostly been applied to nuclear-structure calculations, be fully extended to reaction problems using a coupled-channel scattering formulation while preserving its treatment of bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continua?
self_contained_problem:
The Gamow Shell Model (GSM) is a configuration-interaction many-body framework formulated in a Rigged Hilbert Space that uses a single-particle Berggren basis (a complete set consisting of bound states, narrow decaying resonances, and complex-energy non-resonant scattering states on a contour in the complex momentum plane). In this basis, GSM provides a unified description of bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continua of an A-nucleon system, and it has been used extensively for nuclear-structure calculations of weakly bound and unbound nuclei.

Develop a fully consistent extension of the Gamow Shell Model to nuclear reaction problems by means of a coupled-channel formulation of the scattering problem. Concretely:

1. Define reaction channels (c) as antisymmetrized products of internal target/projectile states (eigenstates of GSM cluster sub-Hamiltonians) with relative-motion functions in suitably chosen relative (e.g., Cluster Orbital Shell Model) coordinates, so that the total A-body wave function admits a Resonating-Group-Method-type decomposition Ψ = Σ_c A{ φ_c(ξ) ⊗ u_c(r) }.

2. Derive, from a microscopic GSM Hamiltonian H acting on the Berggren-based A-body Hilbert space, the resulting non-local coupled-channel integro-differential equations for the radial channel functions u_c(r), including channel–channel coupling kernels, exchange (non-orthogonality) terms, and Coulomb asymptotics where applicable.

3. Impose Berggren/outgoing-wave boundary conditions consistent with the Rigged Hilbert Space formulation so that bound states, resonances, and the multi-channel scattering continuum are treated on equal footing, and the resulting S-matrix is unitary in the appropriate sense.

4. Demonstrate that the construction preserves the GSM treatment of many-body continuum coupling (no loss of completeness, antisymmetrization respected, internal structure of clusters described in the same Berggren basis) and yields cross sections for elastic scattering, inelastic scattering, transfer, and radiative capture reactions involving weakly bound or unbound nuclei.

Provide such a formulation, prove (or argue) its internal consistency and completeness, and exhibit a computational scheme by which the coupled-channel GSM equations can be solved.
status_search_result: A coupled-channel Gamow Shell Model (GSM-CC) has been developed using Cluster Orbital Shell Model coordinates and the Resonating Group Method, and has been applied successfully to elastic/inelastic scattering, proton and neutron radiative capture (e.g., 7Be(p,γ)8B, 7Li(n,γ)8Li), and transfer reactions such as 40Ca(d,p). Thus the program of extending GSM to reactions via a coupled-channel formulation has been substantially realized, though refinements (more channels, heavier systems, three-body breakup) remain active research.

Write λ' for the conjugate partition of λ, and identify λ with its Young diagram, regarded as the set of cells u = (i,j) with 1 ≤ j ≤ λ_i. Let f_λ denote the number of standard Young tableaux of shape λ (equivalently, the dimension of the irreducible S_n-representation indexed by λ).

For a cell u = (i,j) ∈ λ define the symplectic content
  c_sp(u) = λ_i + λ_j − i − j + 2,        if i ≤ j,
  c_sp(u) = −(λ'_i + λ'_j − i − j + 2),  if i > j.

Set δ_n = (−1)^{C(n,2)}, where C(n,2) = n(n−1)/2.

Prove or disprove the identity
  δ_n · ∑_{λ ⊢ n} f_λ^2 ∏_{u ∈ λ} c_sp(u)^2  =  n! · ∑_{λ ⊢ n} f_λ ∏_{u ∈ λ} c_sp(u)
for every positive integer n.
