original_question: A semi-dispersive billiard table is one whose boundary has dispersive inward-convex components together with neutral components such as line segments. Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a compact connected planar region whose boundary $\partial Y$ is a finite union of smooth curves meeting at finitely many corner points. Assume each smooth boundary component is either:

(i) a "dispersive" component, meaning a smooth curve that is strictly convex inward (i.e., its curvature, taken with respect to the inward normal pointing into $Y$, is strictly negative everywhere, so the boundary bulges into the table), or

(ii) a "neutral" component, meaning a straight line segment (zero curvature).

Consider the billiard flow on $Y$: a point particle moves with unit speed inside $Y$ along straight lines and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting $\partial Y$. The phase space is the unit tangent bundle of $Y$, equipped with the natural invariant Liouville measure $\mu$.

Call $Y$ a semi-dispersive billiard table if its boundary consists only of components of types (i) and (ii), with at least one component of type (i). Call the billiard flow on $Y$ hyperbolic if its Lyapunov exponents are nonzero almost everywhere with respect to $\mu$ (i.e., the flow is non-uniformly hyperbolic in the sense of Pesin theory).

Question: Is the billiard flow on every semi-dispersive billiard table $Y$ (in the above sense) hyperbolic?
status_search_result: Hyperbolicity and ergodicity of semi-dispersive billiards is a longstanding research area (Sinai, Bunimovich, Krámli–Simányi–Szász, Chernov–Dolgopyat). While hyperbolicity is established in many particular semi-dispersive systems (hard-ball gases, Lorentz gas, stadia, falling balls), the general question of whether every planar semi-dispersive billiard table (dispersive arcs together with neutral segments) is hyperbolic does not appear to have a complete proof in the literature, and surveys treat full hyperbolicity in this generality as still open.

original_question: For a hyperbolic billiard table Y, let f_Y(n) be the number of periodic points whose period is at most n. Does the exponential growth rate h = lim_{n -> infinity} log f_Y(n) / n exist?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y$ be a hyperbolic billiard table (a planar billiard whose associated billiard map is uniformly hyperbolic, so that the set of periodic orbits of any given period is finite). For each positive integer $n$, let $f_Y(n)$ denote the number of periodic points of the billiard map on $Y$ whose period is at most $n$. Determine whether the limit
$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$
exists.
status_search_result: The existence of the exponential growth rate of periodic points for general hyperbolic billiards is listed among open problems in surveys on billiard dynamics. While analogous results are known for smooth uniformly hyperbolic (Anosov) systems, billiards have singularities that obstruct direct application, and recent literature still treats this as an open question.

original_question: If the limit h = lim_{n -> infinity} log f_Y(n) / n exists for a hyperbolic billiard table Y, must this finite positive number coincide with the topological entropy of the billiard map?
self_contained_problem: Let $Y$ be a hyperbolic billiard table (a planar billiard whose associated billiard map $T_Y$ on the phase space of unit tangent vectors at the boundary is nonuniformly hyperbolic, e.g., a dispersing Sinai billiard, a Bunimovich stadium, or another hyperbolic billiard). Assume that for every positive integer $n$ the set of periodic points of $T_Y$ of period at most $n$ is finite, and let $f_Y(n)$ denote its cardinality. Suppose that the limit\n$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$\nexists and satisfies $0 < h < \infty$. Must $h$ equal the topological entropy of the billiard map $T_Y$?
status_search_result: For uniformly hyperbolic systems, the exponential growth rate of periodic points equals the topological entropy (classical results of Bowen, Katok). For general (nonuniformly) hyperbolic billiards the equality of the periodic-orbit growth rate and topological entropy is not established in full generality; recent work (e.g., on Sinai billiards and on generic convex billiards) addresses positivity and lower bounds for entropy, but a complete answer to whether the limit, when it exists, must coincide with topological entropy for arbitrary hyperbolic billiards has not been confirmed in the sources found.

original_question: Let T(n) denote the moduli space of n-gons of a fixed combinatorial type, let E(n) be the subset consisting of ergodic n-gons, and let lambda be the corresponding Lebesgue measure. Does lambda(E(n)) > 0 hold?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a combinatorial type of simple planar polygon with $n \geq 3$ vertices (i.e., a cyclic ordering of the vertices and the resulting edge structure), and let $T(n)$ denote the moduli space of all simple Euclidean $n$-gons of this combinatorial type, parametrized in the natural way (for example, by the locations of the vertices, modulo Euclidean similarities), so that $T(n)$ is an open subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Let $\lambda$ denote Lebesgue measure on $T(n)$. For each polygon $P \in T(n)$, consider the billiard flow on $P$: the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of $P$ with elastic reflection at the boundary, preserving Liouville measure. Call $P$ ergodic if this billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure, and let $E(n) \subset T(n)$ denote the set of ergodic $n$-gons. It is known (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie) that $E(n)$ is residual in $T(n)$ in the sense of Baire category. Determine whether
\[
\lambda(E(n)) > 0.
\]
status_search_result: The question of whether almost every polygon (with respect to Lebesgue measure on the moduli space of n-gons) has ergodic billiard flow is widely cited as an open problem. The known result of Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie establishes only Baire-genericity of E(n), and recent surveys and papers on polygonal billiards (e.g., on weak mixing in rational billiards, 2024) still describe positive-measure ergodicity as unresolved. No proof of λ(E(n)) > 0 appears in the literature.

original_question: Does there exist an irrational polygon whose billiard flow is not ergodic?
self_contained_problem: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a simply connected polygon. The billiard flow on $P$ is the dynamical system on the unit tangent bundle of $P$ defined by straight-line motion in the interior with elastic reflection at the boundary (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), with the flow undefined at trajectories hitting a vertex. This flow preserves Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue measure on $P$ with the uniform probability measure on directions). The polygon $P$ is called rational if every interior angle is a rational multiple of $\pi$, and irrational otherwise.\n\nProblem: Exhibit an irrational polygon $P$ whose billiard flow is not ergodic with respect to Liouville measure, or prove that no such polygon exists.
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Surveys of polygonal billiards (e.g., Schwartz's ICM survey, Masur–Tabachnikov's handbook chapter) describe the ergodicity question for irrational polygons as wide open. Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie (1986) showed ergodicity holds on a dense $G_\delta$ set of polygons, but no example of a non-ergodic irrational polygon is known, nor is a proof that all irrational polygons are ergodic.

original_question: Let P be an irrational n-gon with phase space Phi, and for each side a_i let Phi_i be the set of phase points whose base points lie on a_i. If M is an invariant subset of Phi with positive measure and Phi_i is contained in M for some side index i, must M equal the whole phase space Phi?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a polygon in the plane with $n$ sides $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$. Consider the billiard flow on $P$: a point particle moves with unit speed inside $P$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) off the boundary. The phase space $\Phi$ consists of all unit tangent vectors based at points of the boundary $\partial P = \bigcup_{i=1}^n a_i$ that point into $P$ (with the standard identification at reflections), and is equipped with the natural invariant Liouville measure preserved by the billiard flow. For each $1 \le i \le n$, let
\[
\Phi_i = \{(x,v) \in \Phi : x \in a_i\},
\]
so that $\Phi = \bigsqcup_{i=1}^n \Phi_i$ is a disjoint decomposition.

Call $P$ an irrational $n$-gon if at least one of its interior angles is an irrational multiple of $\pi$.

Question: Suppose $P$ is an irrational $n$-gon, and let $M \subset \Phi$ be a measurable set that is invariant under the billiard flow and has positive Liouville measure. If $\Phi_i \subset M$ for some $1 \le i \le n$, must it follow that $M = \Phi$?
status_search_result: The statement is posed as an open problem/conjecture in surveys on polygonal billiard dynamics. The corresponding statement is known to hold for rational polygons, but the irrational case appears to remain open as of recent surveys on open problems in billiards.

original_question: Does every polygon admit at least one periodic billiard orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a polygon in the Euclidean plane (a simply connected compact region whose boundary is a finite union of straight line segments). A billiard trajectory in P is the path of a point particle moving in straight lines inside P at unit speed and reflecting elastically off the boundary according to the law of equal angles, with the convention that trajectories meeting a vertex of P are undefined. Such a trajectory is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial direction.

Question: Does every polygon P admit at least one periodic billiard trajectory?

For obtuse triangles, Schwartz (2008) established existence when the largest angle is at most 100°, and Garber–Marinov–Moore–Tokarsky (2018) extended this to 112.3°. The case of arbitrary obtuse triangles, and hence the general polygon case, remains unresolved as of 2024.

original_question: For an irrational polygon P, let f_P(l) be the number of periodic bands of length at most l. Find efficient upper and lower bounds for the growth of f_P(l).
self_contained_problem:
Consider a simple polygon P in the Euclidean plane and the billiard flow inside P (a point particle moves with unit speed along straight lines and reflects off the boundary according to the law of equal angles, with reflections at vertices left undefined). Call P irrational if at least one of its interior angles is not a rational multiple of π.

A periodic billiard trajectory in P is a closed orbit of the billiard flow. A periodic band (or periodic strip) is a maximal open family of parallel periodic billiard trajectories of the same combinatorial type; all trajectories in a periodic band have the same length, which we call the length of the band. For l > 0, define
   f_P(l) = #{ periodic bands in P of length at most l }.

Problem. For an arbitrary irrational polygon P, establish efficient upper and lower bounds on the growth of the counting function f_P(l) as l → ∞. In particular, determine asymptotic or explicit functions g(l) and G(l) such that g(l) ≤ f_P(l) ≤ G(l) for all sufficiently large l, and identify the optimal such bounds.
status_search_result: The problem of finding efficient upper and lower bounds on the number of periodic bands (or periodic trajectories) in irrational polygons appears to remain open. While Masur established quadratic bounds for rational polygons, and partial results exist for irrational cases—Hooper constructed irrational polygons with growth like R log^k R, and Scheglov gave a sub-exponential upper bound for almost every triangle—no general efficient bounds are known for arbitrary irrational polygons. It is listed among standing open problems in polygonal billiards.

original_question: For a rational polygon P, the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P) are defined by inequalities c_*(P) l^2 <= f_P(l) <= c^*(P) l^2 for all sufficiently large l. Find efficient estimates for these quadratic constants.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a rational polygon, that is, a polygon in the Euclidean plane all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. A billiard trajectory in $P$ is the path of a point mass moving in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting off the sides according to the law of equal angles (with trajectories meeting a vertex left undefined). A periodic billiard orbit is a closed billiard trajectory; its length is the Euclidean length of one period.

For $\ell > 0$, let $f_P(\ell)$ denote the number of (geometrically distinct) periodic billiard orbits in $P$ of length at most $\ell$. It is known that there exist constants $0 < c_*(P) \le c^*(P) < \infty$ such that
$$c_*(P)\,\ell^2 \;\le\; f_P(\ell) \;\le\; c^*(P)\,\ell^2$$
for all sufficiently large $\ell$. The numbers $c_*(P)$ and $c^*(P)$ are called the quadratic constants of $P$.

Problem: Provide efficient (effective and quantitatively sharp) estimates for the quadratic constants $c_*(P)$ and $c^*(P)$ in terms of the geometry of $P$.
status_search_result: The problem of efficiently estimating the quadratic constants for counting periodic billiard orbits in rational polygons remains open. Existence of the bounds is due to Masur (with ineffective constants) and effective constants were later obtained by Vorobets, but sharp/efficient estimates in terms of polygon geometry are still being sought, and the equality $c_*(P)=c^*(P)$ (existence of a quadratic limit) is itself unresolved beyond Veech/lattice cases.

original_question: For a rational polygon P, if f_P(l) / l^2 converges then P is said to have quadratic asymptotics. Does every rational polygon have quadratic asymptotics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a rational polygon, that is, a polygon in the Euclidean plane all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. For $\ell > 0$, let $f_P(\ell)$ denote the number of (cylinders of) periodic billiard trajectories in $P$ of length at most $\ell$. By results of Masur and Boshernitzan, there exist constants $0 < c_*(P) \le c^*(P) < \infty$ such that
$$ c_*(P)\,\ell^2 \le f_P(\ell) \le c^*(P)\,\ell^2 $$
for all sufficiently large $\ell$. The polygon $P$ is said to have quadratic asymptotics if the limit
$$ c(P) := \lim_{\ell \to \infty} \frac{f_P(\ell)}{\ell^2} $$
exists, equivalently if $c_*(P) = c^*(P)$.

Question: Does every rational polygon $P$ have quadratic asymptotics?
status_search_result: Quadratic asymptotics is known for lattice (Veech) polygons and for certain classes accessible via Teichmüller flow techniques (e.g., results of Eskin–Mirzakhani–Mohammadi extensions), but the general question for arbitrary rational polygons is reported as a major open problem in survey literature, with no published proof or counterexample found.

original_question: A billiard table Omega is called secure if every pair of points x, y in Omega can be blocked by finitely many points z_1, ..., z_n in Omega \ {x, y}, meaning every billiard orbit from x to y passes through one of those blocking points. Characterize the secure polygons, and in particular find a criterion that decides security for rational polygons.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygonal billiard table. A billiard orbit from $x \in \Omega$ to $y \in \Omega$ is a continuous broken-line trajectory in $\Omega$ starting at $x$ and ending at $y$, whose interior segments hit only the (open) edges of $\partial\Omega$ (avoiding the vertices) and reflect there according to the law of equal angles. Let $\Gamma(x,y)$ denote the set of all billiard orbits from $x$ to $y$.

A pair $\{x,y\}$ with $x,y \in \Omega$ is called secure if there exists a finite set $\{z_1, \dots, z_n\} \subset \Omega \setminus \{x,y\}$ such that every $\gamma \in \Gamma(x,y)$ passes through some $z_i$. The polygon $\Omega$ is called secure if every pair of points $x,y \in \Omega$ is secure.

The polygon $\Omega$ is called rational if all of its interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$.

Problem: Characterize the secure polygons. In particular, give a criterion that decides whether a given rational polygon is secure.
status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Known partial results include: among regular polygons, only the square, equilateral triangle, and regular hexagon have the finite blocking (security) property; among Veech surfaces, only torus branched covers are secure; and a lattice polygon is secure iff it is arithmetic. A standing conjecture asserts that a polygon is secure iff it is "almost integrable" (in particular rational), but no full characterization—nor a complete criterion for arbitrary rational polygons—has been established.

original_question: Does there exist an integer d >= 3 such that for every polygon the full billiard complexity has a cubic lower bound and also an upper bound by a polynomial of degree d?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a (simple) polygon, and consider the billiard flow inside $P$: a point particle moves in straight lines and reflects off the boundary $\partial P$ according to the law of equal angles, with the trajectory undefined if it hits a vertex. Code each trajectory by the cyclic sequence of sides of $P$ that it strikes. The full billiard complexity $p(n)$ of $P$ is defined as the number of distinct words of length $n$ over the alphabet of sides of $P$ that arise as factors of some such bi-infinite billiard coding (equivalently, the number of equivalence classes of orbit segments crossing exactly $n$ sides, where two segments are equivalent if and only if they hit the same ordered sequence of sides).

Prove or disprove the following conjecture: there exists an integer $d \geq 3$ such that for every polygon $P$, there exist constants $c_1(P), c_2(P) > 0$ and $n_0(P)$ with
$$ c_1(P)\, n^3 \;\leq\; p(n) \;\leq\; c_2(P)\, n^d \qquad \text{for all } n \geq n_0(P). $$
status_search_result: Recent work has established cubic complexity asymptotics in special cases (rational polygons, regular N-gons, tiling polygons) and stretched-exponential or polynomial bounds for almost every triangle, but a uniform polynomial upper bound of fixed degree d valid for all polygons (together with the cubic lower bound) does not appear to be established. The conjecture appears to remain open in full generality.

original_question: An almost integrable polygon is one that is tiled under reflections by one of the integrable polygons. Is a polygon secure exactly when it is almost integrable?
self_contained_problem:
Consider polygonal billiards in the Euclidean plane. A polygon is called integrable if it is one of the following: the equilateral triangle, the right isosceles triangle, the 30-60-90 triangle, or any rectangle. A polygon P is called almost integrable if the group generated by reflections in the sides of one of the integrable polygons Q tiles the plane in such a way that P is a union of tiles in this tiling (equivalently, P is tiled under reflections by Q).

For two points x, y in the interior of a polygon P, a billiard trajectory from x to y is a polygonal path inside P from x to y whose reflections at the boundary obey the law of equal angles (and which avoids the corners). A finite set B ⊂ P \ {x, y} is said to block all billiard trajectories from x to y if every billiard trajectory from x to y passes through some point of B. The polygon P is called secure (or has finite blocking property) if for every pair of points x, y in the interior of P there exists such a finite blocking set B.

Question: Is it true that a polygon P is secure if and only if P is almost integrable?
status_search_result: The conjecture that a polygon is secure if and only if it is almost integrable is a well-known conjecture of Gutkin. Searches show it is still discussed as an open problem; partial results are known (e.g., almost integrable polygons are secure, and in the rational case implications have been established), but the full equivalence has not been settled.

original_question: For a compact smooth Riemannian manifold, is security equivalent to flatness? In other words, is every secure compact smooth Riemannian manifold flat, and every flat one secure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold. For points $x,y\in M$, let $\Gamma(x,y)$ denote the set of geodesic segments in $M$ from $x$ to $y$. A finite set $B\subset M\setminus\{x,y\}$ is said to block $\Gamma(x,y)$ if every geodesic segment in $\Gamma(x,y)$ contains at least one point of $B$. The pair $(x,y)$ is called secure if there exists a finite blocking set for $\Gamma(x,y)$, and the manifold $(M,g)$ is called secure if every pair $(x,y)\in M\times M$ is secure.

It is known that every compact flat Riemannian manifold is secure. Prove or disprove the following: a compact smooth Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is secure if and only if it is flat (i.e., has identically zero sectional curvature).
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. The "flat implies secure" direction is known. The converse has been established in several special cases: Bangert and Gutkin (2008) proved that secure 2-dimensional Riemannian tori are flat, and Burns–Gutkin and Lafont–Schmidt verified the conjecture for compact Riemannian manifolds with nonpositive sectional curvature. The general case of arbitrary compact smooth Riemannian manifolds is still unresolved.

original_question: Does the nonlinear Schrodinger equation posed on a tree graph admit a rigorous well-posedness theory comparable to the star-graph case, beyond the currently available partial results based on dispersive estimates?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a metric tree graph: a connected metric graph with no cycles, consisting of a finite or countable family of edges (each identified isometrically with an interval of $\mathbb{R}$, finite or half-infinite) joined at vertices. On each edge, equip the function space with the Lebesgue measure inherited from the edge parametrization, and define
$$L^2(\mathcal{T}) = \bigoplus_{e \in E(\mathcal{T})} L^2(e), \qquad H^1(\mathcal{T}) = \{u \in C(\mathcal{T}) : u|_e \in H^1(e) \text{ for all } e\}.$$
Let $-\Delta_{\mathcal{T}}$ be a self-adjoint realization of the Laplacian on $\mathcal{T}$ (for instance the Kirchhoff Laplacian, defined on functions $u$ that are continuous at every vertex $v$ and satisfy $\sum_{e \succ v} \partial_e u(v) = 0$, where the sum runs over edges incident to $v$ and the derivatives are taken in the outgoing direction).

Consider the Cauchy problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathcal{T}$:
$$ i\,\partial_t u(t,x) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{T}} u(t,x) + \lambda \, |u(t,x)|^{2\sigma} u(t,x), \quad x \in \mathcal{T},\ t \in \mathbb{R},$$
$$ u(0,\cdot) = u_0 \in H^1(\mathcal{T}), $$
with $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ and power $\sigma > 0$.

Question: Establish a rigorous well-posedness theory for this Cauchy problem on a general metric tree graph $\mathcal{T}$ analogous to the one available on the star graph (a single vertex with finitely many half-infinite edges). Specifically, prove local well-posedness in the energy space $H^1(\mathcal{T})$, conservation of mass and energy, and global well-posedness in the subcritical regime (e.g., $0 < \sigma < 2$ in the focusing case under suitable mass thresholds, and all $\sigma > 0$ in the defocusing case), together with the appropriate Strichartz-type dispersive estimates for the linear propagator $e^{it\Delta_{\mathcal{T}}}$ on the tree.
status_search_result: Local and global well-posedness for the NLS in the energy space $H^1$ on general (compact or non-compact) metric graphs, including trees, with Kirchhoff-type vertex conditions has been established by standard semigroup/energy methods and is now part of the literature on NLS on metric graphs (e.g., works of Adami–Cacciapuoti–Finco–Noja and subsequent authors). Sharp Strichartz-type dispersive estimates and a low-regularity well-posedness theory on general tree graphs comparable in detail to the Euclidean or star-graph theory are only partially available, with progress in special tree geometries.

original_question: When a nonlinear Schrodinger equation is posed on a system of thin tubes or guides connected at junctions and the transversal tube size shrinks to zero, does the limiting dynamics converge to an NLS on a metric graph, and if so which vertex boundary conditions appear in the limit? How do those limiting boundary conditions depend on the specific shrinking procedure for the tubes, guides, and junction size, and on whether the thin-tube boundary condition is Neumann or Dirichlet?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega_\varepsilon \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be a tubular neighborhood (a "fat graph") of a finite metric graph $\mathcal{G}=(V,E)$ with edges of fixed lengths, obtained by thickening each edge into a tube of transversal diameter of order $\varepsilon$ and gluing these tubes at junction regions of size of order $\varepsilon^\alpha$ for some $\alpha>0$. On $\Omega_\varepsilon$ consider the cubic (or, more generally, power) nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\partial_t \psi_\varepsilon = -\Delta \psi_\varepsilon + \kappa |\psi_\varepsilon|^{2\sigma}\psi_\varepsilon \quad \text{on } \Omega_\varepsilon, $$
with $\psi_\varepsilon(0,\cdot)=\psi_{0,\varepsilon}$ and either homogeneous Neumann or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega_\varepsilon$. Suitably renormalized after projection onto the transverse ground state, study the limit $\varepsilon\to 0^+$ of $\psi_\varepsilon$ and answer the following:

(a) Does $\psi_\varepsilon$ converge (in an appropriate topology, e.g., uniformly on compact time intervals in a suitable space) to a function $\psi$ that solves a nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\partial_x^2 \psi + \kappa' |\psi|^{2\sigma}\psi $$
on each edge of the metric graph $\mathcal{G}$, coupled by self-adjoint vertex (matching) boundary conditions at every vertex $v\in V$ of the form
$$ A_v \psi(v) + B_v \psi'(v) = 0, $$
where $\psi(v)$ and $\psi'(v)$ collect the limiting boundary values and outgoing derivatives of $\psi$ at $v$ along the incident edges, and $(A_v,B_v)$ parametrizes a self-adjoint extension?

(b) Determine, in terms of the geometry of the shrinking procedure (relative scaling of tube diameter and junction size, i.e., the parameter $\alpha$, and the shape of the junction regions), which family of vertex conditions $(A_v,B_v)$ arises in the limit.

(c) Determine how this family of limiting vertex conditions depends on whether Neumann or Dirichlet conditions are imposed on $\partial\Omega_\varepsilon$ in the prelimit problem.

status_search_result: Partial progress exists. For the linear case, norm-resolvent convergence of Schrödinger operators on shrinking fat graphs to operators on metric graphs with various self-adjoint vertex conditions is established (e.g., Cacciapuoti–Exner, Berkolaiko–Latushkin–Sukhtaiev). For NLS, rigorous results are limited: a strong-confinement / thin-waveguide limit in a single 2D tube has been derived (Cacciapuoti–Finco–Noja, Ann. Henri Poincaré 2017), and numerical/asymptotic studies of solitons in shrinking tubular networks (Uzdin et al.) suggest Kirchhoff-type vertex conditions in some regimes. The general nonlinear question on networks with junctions, the dependence of limiting vertex conditions on the scaling and on Neumann vs. Dirichlet wall conditions, is not fully settled.

original_question: Can one rigorously derive a quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrodinger equation on a graph-like structure such as a Y-junction from a many-body Bose-Einstein-condensate model, for example by starting from an N-body theory on the graph and taking the N to infinity limit with suitable scalings, while correctly determining the vertex boundary condition in the limit? The boundary-condition issue is already open even for the simplest graph with two edges, namely a line with a defect.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (for concreteness, take either (i) the real line $\mathbb{R}$ viewed as two half-lines joined at a single vertex $v=0$ ("line with a defect"), or (ii) the Y-junction consisting of three half-lines $[0,\infty)$ joined at a common vertex $v$). On $\mathcal{G}$ consider an $N$-body bosonic Hamiltonian acting on the symmetric tensor power of $L^2(\mathcal{G})$, of the form
$$ H_N \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^N \bigl(-\Delta_{\mathcal{G},i} + V_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)\bigr) \;+\; \sum_{1\le i<j\le N} N^{2}\, v\bigl(N(x_i-x_j)\bigr), $$
where $-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ equipped with a chosen self-adjoint vertex condition at $v$ (e.g.\ Kirchhoff, $\delta$-type, or more general) and $v\ge 0$ is a sufficiently regular pair-interaction potential of scattering length $a$. Let $\psi_{N,0}$ be a sequence of $N$-body bosonic states that exhibit complete Bose–Einstein condensation onto a one-particle wave function $\varphi_0\in L^2(\mathcal{G})$, and let $\psi_{N,t} = e^{-itH_N}\psi_{N,0}$.

Prove or disprove: in the limit $N\to\infty$ with the Gross–Pitaevskii scaling above, the reduced one-particle density matrices of $\psi_{N,t}$ converge to $|\varphi_t\rangle\langle\varphi_t|$, where $\varphi_t:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{C}$ solves a quasi–one-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger / Gross–Pitaevskii equation
$$ i\partial_t \varphi_t \;=\; -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\varphi_t \;+\; V_{\mathrm{ext}}\varphi_t \;+\; 8\pi a\,|\varphi_t|^2 \varphi_t \quad\text{on each edge of }\mathcal{G}, $$
supplemented by an effective self-adjoint vertex condition at $v$ that is to be identified explicitly from the microscopic data $(H_N, v, \text{vertex condition of }-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}})$. In particular, identify the correct effective vertex/boundary condition obtained in the limit, already in the simplest case of the line with a single defect (two edges meeting at one vertex).
category_tag: NLS on metric graphs from many-body limits
status_search_result: No published rigorous derivation of a (quasi-)1D Gross–Pitaevskii / NLS equation on a metric graph from an $N$-body bosonic dynamics with explicit identification of the limiting vertex condition appears to exist. Rigorous mean-field/Gross–Pitaevskii derivations are well established on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and tori, and there is an active literature on NLS on metric graphs with prescribed vertex conditions, but the bridge between the two—including the simplest case of a line with a defect—does not appear to have been resolved.

original_question: On graphs more complicated than a star graph, such as trees or graphs with loops, can one build an orbital-stability or orbital-instability theory for nonlinear standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation when explicit formulas for the standing waves are unavailable? In particular, can one effectively count negative eigenvalues of the linearized operator and verify the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition in these less explicit graph geometries?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_{\mathcal G}\psi - |\psi|^{p-1}\psi $$
posed on a metric graph $\mathcal G$, where $\Delta_{\mathcal G}$ denotes the Laplacian acting on functions $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathbb C$ defined edge-wise, with Kirchhoff (or other natural self-adjoint) vertex conditions. A standing wave is a solution of the form $\psi(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\phi_\omega(x)$ with $\omega>0$ and $\phi_\omega$ a real-valued bound state satisfying
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal G}\phi_\omega + \omega\phi_\omega - |\phi_\omega|^{p-1}\phi_\omega = 0. $$
Linearizing the equation about $\phi_\omega$ produces self-adjoint operators $L_1, L_2$ on $L^2(\mathcal G)$ with
$$ L_1 = -\Delta_{\mathcal G} + \omega - p\,\phi_\omega^{p-1}, \qquad L_2 = -\Delta_{\mathcal G} + \omega - \phi_\omega^{p-1}. $$
The classical Grillakis–Shatah–Strauss framework reduces the orbital (in)stability of $\phi_\omega$ to:
(i) counting the number $n(L_1)$ of negative eigenvalues of $L_1$, and
(ii) verifying the Vakhitov–Kolokolov slope condition, namely the sign of $\frac{d}{d\omega}\|\phi_\omega\|_{L^2(\mathcal G)}^2$.

Suppose $\mathcal G$ is a metric graph more complicated than a star graph — for instance a tree with several internal vertices, or a graph containing one or more loops — and suppose that no explicit closed-form expression for the bound state $\phi_\omega$ is available.

Develop a general method that, in this setting, allows one to:
(a) determine $n(L_1)$ for the standing wave $\phi_\omega$ on $\mathcal G$, and
(b) determine the sign of $\frac{d}{d\omega}\|\phi_\omega\|_{L^2(\mathcal G)}^2$,
and thereby establish orbital stability or orbital instability of $\phi_\omega$ on such graphs without relying on explicit formulas for the standing wave.
category_tag: NLS standing waves on metric graphs
status_search_result: Since 2013, substantial progress has been made on orbital stability of NLS standing waves on metric graphs beyond the star case, including results on tadpole graphs, dumbbell graphs, periodic graphs, and trees, often via variational/ground-state arguments or via spectral/Morse-index techniques that bypass explicit formulas. However, no single general method covering arbitrary trees and graphs with loops with non-explicit profiles has been established; the program remains active and only partially resolved.

original_question: For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on nontrivial graphs, how can one construct and identify branches of nonlinear stationary or bound states that do not bifurcate from any linear eigenstate? The paper notes that standard bifurcation theory can produce branches with a linear counterpart near the linear ground state, but it leaves open how to obtain excited states or other bound states without a linear counterpart.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (a finite or infinite graph whose edges are identified with intervals of $\mathbb{R}$, possibly including half-lines), equipped with the Lebesgue measure on each edge and Kirchhoff (or other self-adjoint) vertex conditions at the vertices. Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi - |\psi|^{p-1}\psi, \qquad p>1, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ denotes the self-adjoint Laplacian on $L^2(\mathcal{G})$ associated with the chosen vertex conditions. A nonlinear bound state of frequency $\omega>0$ is a solution of the form $\psi(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\varphi(x)$ with $\varphi\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ satisfying the stationary equation
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\varphi + \omega\varphi = |\varphi|^{p-1}\varphi $$
together with the vertex conditions. A branch of nonlinear bound states $\{\varphi_\omega\}$ is said to have a linear counterpart if $\|\varphi_\omega\|_{H^1}\to 0$ as $\omega$ approaches some eigenvalue $-\omega_0$ of $-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$, in which case the branch bifurcates from the corresponding linear eigenfunction.

Develop a general method, applicable to nontrivial metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$ (for instance star graphs, tadpole graphs, and graphs with loops), that constructs and identifies branches of nonlinear bound states which do not have a linear counterpart in the above sense — in particular, branches of nonlinear excited states known to exist on star graphs — characterizing the topological or geometric features of $\mathcal{G}$ responsible for their existence and providing criteria to detect such branches.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Several works after 2013 have produced branches of nonlinear bound states on metric graphs that do not bifurcate from linear eigenfunctions, most notably topology-induced bifurcations on the tadpole graph and bifurcations from edges of the essential/continuous spectrum or from resonances. These give partial answers in specific graph geometries, but a general theory covering arbitrary nontrivial graphs and all excited-state branches without linear counterpart is not established.

context_brief: Asymptotic stability of graph standing waves
original_question: Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs asymptotically stable in the following sense: every solution that starts near a standing wave in the energy norm eventually decomposes into a possibly different nearby standing wave, a dispersive term evolving under the linear graph Hamiltonian, and a remainder that decays to zero in L2 as time goes to infinity? More concretely, can one control the spectrum and time evolution of the non-selfadjoint linearized Hamiltonian J L on graphs, together with the decay of nonlinear remainders, well enough to prove such relaxation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (a connected metric space obtained by identifying endpoints of finitely many edges, each isometric to an interval of $\mathbb{R}$, possibly with half-lines). Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathcal{G}$,
$$ i\partial_t u(t,x) = H u(t,x) - |u(t,x)|^{2p} u(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R}, $$
where $H = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the self-adjoint Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ associated to a chosen set of vertex conditions (e.g. Kirchhoff or $\delta$-type), and $p>0$ is subcritical. A standing wave is a solution of the form $u_\omega(t,x) = e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega(x)$, where $\Phi_\omega\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ solves $H\Phi_\omega - |\Phi_\omega|^{2p}\Phi_\omega = -\omega \Phi_\omega$. Linearizing around $\Phi_\omega$ yields a (non-self-adjoint, non-skew-adjoint) Hamiltonian operator $JL$ acting on real-vector-valued perturbations.

Question: Are such standing waves asymptotically stable in the following sense? For every initial datum $u_0\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ sufficiently close, in the energy norm, to $\Phi_\omega$, does the corresponding solution $u(t)$ admit, for $t\to\infty$, a decomposition
$$ u(t,x) = e^{i\theta(t)}\Phi_{\omega_\infty}(x) + e^{-itH}\psi_\infty(x) + r(t,x), $$
with $\omega_\infty$ near $\omega$, a dispersive component $e^{-itH}\psi_\infty$ evolving under the linear graph Hamiltonian, and a remainder satisfying $\|r(t)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{G})}\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$?

Equivalently: can one establish sufficiently sharp spectral and dispersive estimates for the non-self-adjoint linearized Hamiltonian $JL$ on $\mathcal{G}$, and control the nonlinear remainder, to prove this asymptotic relaxation onto a nearby standing wave?
category_tag: Asymptotic stability of NLS standing waves on metric graphs
status_search_result: The general problem of asymptotic stability of NLS standing waves on metric graphs appears to remain open. Recent literature (through 2025–2026) on NLS on graphs focuses primarily on existence and orbital (Lyapunov) stability of ground states, including stability transitions on general metric graphs. Asymptotic stability results in the soliton-resolution sense are available only in restricted models with concentrated nonlinearities (point interactions on the line or in 3D), not for general metric graphs with extended nonlinearities, where dispersive estimates for the linearized non-self-adjoint operator $JL$ are not yet established.

original_question: For the scattering of fast solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on star graphs, do multisoliton solutions exist, and what is the dynamical outcome when several solitons collide at the same vertex?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on a star graph $\mathcal{G}$ consisting of $N\geq 2$ semi-infinite half-lines (edges) $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ joined at a single vertex $v$. On each edge identified with $[0,\infty)$, the wavefunction $\psi_j(t,x)$ satisfies
$$ i\partial_t \psi_j = -\partial_x^2 \psi_j - |\psi_j|^2 \psi_j, \qquad x>0,\; j=1,\ldots,N, $$
with Kirchhoff (or, more generally, $\delta$-type) coupling at the vertex:
$$ \psi_1(t,0)=\cdots=\psi_N(t,0), \qquad \sum_{j=1}^N \partial_x \psi_j(t,0) = \alpha\,\psi_1(t,0), $$
for some fixed $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$.

A "fast soliton" on edge $e_j$ is an incoming profile of the form $\psi_j(0,x)=e^{i v x}\,\mathrm{sech}(x-x_0)$ with $|v|$ large and $x_0\ll 0$ (so it travels toward the vertex). Existing results describe the scattering of a single fast soliton arriving at $v$ and produce reflected/transmitted solitonic components on the outgoing edges.

Question: 
(a) Do there exist genuine multisoliton solutions of this cubic NLS on the star graph $\mathcal{G}$ (i.e., solutions that, in suitable asymptotic regimes, decompose into several spatially separated soliton-like profiles propagating on the edges)?

(b) If several fast solitons are launched simultaneously on (possibly different) edges so that they all reach the vertex $v$ at the same time, what is the dynamical outcome of the collision at $v$? In particular, characterize the asymptotic state for $t\to+\infty$ in terms of reflected/transmitted soliton components, radiation, and any nonlinear interaction at the vertex.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: A 2013 survey on the NLS equation on graphs explicitly states that nothing is known about multisoliton existence or multi-soliton vertex collisions on star graphs in the cubic NLS scattering setting. Subsequent work has produced integrable matrix-NLS models on star graphs admitting multi-soliton solutions under special vertex conditions, but for the standard cubic NLS with Kirchhoff/δ coupling no general result on multisolitons or simultaneous vertex collisions appears in the literature, so the question remains open.

original_question: Can one develop a rigorous theory of soliton scattering for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs with nontrivial topology, especially trees, beyond the already treated star-graph and similar simple cases? In particular, how do network topology and the availability of Strichartz estimates affect the propagation and scattering of solitons on such graphs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph: a connected graph whose edges are identified with intervals (finite or semi-infinite) glued at vertices. On each edge parametrize a coordinate $x$, and consider a complex-valued function $\psi(t,x)$ defined on $\mathcal{G}	imes\mathbb{R}$ which on each edge satisfies the cubic (focusing) nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t\psi = -\partial_x^2\psi - |\psi|^2\psi, $$
supplemented at every vertex $v$ by Kirchhoff (or more general self-adjoint) matching conditions: $\psi$ is continuous at $v$ and $\sum_{e
i v}\partial_x\psi_e(v)=0$, where the sum is over edges incident to $v$ taken with the outgoing orientation.

A soliton on a single edge (line) is the family $\phi_{c,v,x_0,\gamma}(t,x)=\sqrt{2}c\,\operatorname{sech}(c(x-vt-x_0))\,e^{i(vx/2-(v^2/4-c^2)t+\gamma)}$ with amplitude $c>0$, velocity $v$, position $x_0$, phase $\gamma$. For the star graph (one vertex, $N\ge 3$ semi-infinite edges) it is known that a fast incoming soliton on one edge splits at the vertex into transmitted and reflected wave packets that retain a soliton-like profile on a long time scale, with reflection/transmission coefficients matching those of the underlying linear Schrödinger problem; a key analytic ingredient is the validity of Strichartz estimates for the linear propagator on the graph.

Problem. Develop a rigorous theory of soliton scattering for the above cubic NLS on metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$ with nontrivial topology beyond the star graph. Specifically:
(a) For an arbitrary finite tree graph $\mathcal{G}$ (with semi-infinite leaves) equipped with Kirchhoff vertex conditions, prove that an incoming high-velocity soliton entering along one semi-infinite edge propagates through the tree, splitting at each interior vertex, and that on each outgoing edge the resulting wave is, up to errors that vanish as the velocity tends to infinity, a sum of solitons whose parameters and reflection/transmission amplitudes are determined recursively by the linear scattering matrices at each vertex.
(b) Identify the precise class of metric graphs and vertex couplings for which the linear Schrödinger group $e^{it H_{\mathcal{G}}}$ satisfies Strichartz estimates of the form $\|e^{itH_{\mathcal{G}}}f\|_{L^q_t L^r_x(\mathcal{G})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^2(\mathcal{G})}$ for admissible Strichartz pairs $(q,r)$, and use these to obtain the corresponding nonlinear scattering result.
(c) Quantify the influence of the topology of $\mathcal{G}$ (presence of loops, cycles, branching structure) on the persistence, decay, or trapping of solitons.
status_search_result: The literature confirms that scattering of fast solitons for cubic NLS has been treated rigorously on the star graph and a few similar simple geometries, while extension to graphs with nontrivial topology, in particular general trees, remains open. Recent work continues to study NLS on graphs (looping-edge graphs, general networks), but a rigorous soliton-scattering theory on general trees and the complete characterization of metric graphs admitting Strichartz estimates are still active research problems.

context_brief: Longer validity timescale for outgoing solitons
original_question: After a soliton scatters at a graph vertex, can the time interval on which the outgoing waves are accurately approximated by solitary waves be extended beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity scale proved in the paper? How does that longer-timescale question depend on the initial data and on the external potential?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph $\mathcal{G}$ consisting of $N$ half-lines joined at a single vertex, with a Kirchhoff-type (or more general self-adjoint) coupling at the vertex and an external potential $V$ on the edges:
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\Delta\psi + V\psi - |\psi|^2\psi, \qquad \psi(t,\cdot)\in L^2(\mathcal{G}). $$
Let $\phi_v(x-vt)$ denote a standing soliton of the underlying line equation boosted to velocity $v$, and consider an initial datum given by such a fast solitary wave $\psi_0$ supported on one incoming edge and traveling toward the vertex with large velocity $v$. After scattering at the vertex, the solution decomposes into outgoing components on the various edges. It is known that there is a time interval of order $\log v / v$ (logarithmic in the velocity) on which each outgoing component is approximated, in $H^1$, by a solitary wave whose amplitude is determined by the linear scattering coefficients at the vertex.

Question: Can the timescale on which this solitary-wave approximation of the outgoing components remains accurate be extended beyond the $\log v / v$ scale? Specifically, determine whether (and under which assumptions on the initial datum $\psi_0$ and on the external potential $V$) the validity time of the outgoing-soliton approximation can be improved to a longer (e.g.\ polynomial in $v$, or velocity-independent) timescale, and characterize how the maximal such timescale depends on $\psi_0$ and $V$.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger solitons on metric graphs
status_search_result: Existing results on fast soliton scattering at the vertex of a star graph (Adami–Cacciapuoti–Finco–Noja and follow-ups) establish the solitary-wave approximation of outgoing waves only on a timescale logarithmic in the incoming velocity. No subsequent work was found that extends this approximation timescale on metric graphs; the question of longer-time validity and its dependence on initial data and external potential appears to remain open.

original_question: For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on graphs whose nonlinearity is close to the integrable cubic case but not exactly cubic, are the outgoing waves produced by vertex scattering still close to solitons over timescales comparable to those proved in the integrable cubic setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph with at least one semi-infinite edge, and consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\partial_x^2 \psi + f(|\psi|^2)\psi $$
on each edge of $\mathcal{G}$, with Kirchhoff (or otherwise self-adjoint) coupling conditions at every vertex. In the integrable case $f(s)=-s$ (cubic focusing NLS on the line), it is known that a fast soliton incoming along a semi-infinite edge of $\mathcal{G}$ scatters at the vertex and produces, on each outgoing edge, a wave that remains close in $H^1$ to a (rescaled) soliton over a timescale $T_v$ depending logarithmically (or polynomially) on the soliton velocity $v$.

Now suppose the nonlinearity $f$ is a smooth perturbation of the cubic one,
$$ f(s) = -s + \varepsilon\, g(s), $$
with $g$ smooth and bounded on compact sets, and $\varepsilon>0$ small. Prove or disprove the following: there exist $\varepsilon_0>0$ and a timescale $T_v'$ comparable to $T_v$ such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_0)$ and every sufficiently fast incoming soliton, the outgoing waves on each semi-infinite edge of $\mathcal{G}$ remain close in $H^1$ to solitons (of the unperturbed cubic NLS, with appropriately determined parameters) up to time $T_v'$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys on NLS on graphs continue to discuss soliton scattering at vertices in the integrable cubic case and list extensions to non-integrable or near-integrable nonlinearities as outstanding problems. No published result establishing soliton-closeness of outgoing waves on graphs for near-integrable nonlinearities over the relevant timescales was found.

original_question: What rigorous mechanisms describe the capture of solitons by graph defects or junctions and the generation of new solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs, particularly in dynamical regimes that are neither close to a standing wave nor in the fast-soliton scattering regime?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph consisting of a finite number of edges (half-lines or finite segments) joined at one or more vertices, equipped with a self-adjoint realization $H$ of the Laplacian $-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ (e.g., Kirchhoff or $\delta$-type coupling at the vertices). Consider the cubic (or, more generally, focusing power-type) nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathcal{G}$,
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi(t,x) = H\psi(t,x) - |\psi(t,x)|^{2\sigma}\psi(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R}, $$
with initial datum $\psi(0,\cdot)=\psi_0\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$. On each edge identified with $\mathbb{R}^+$, recall that the free NLS on the line admits soliton solutions of the form $\phi_{c,v}(t,x)=e^{i(vx/2-(v^2/4-c)t)}\,\eta_c(x-vt-x_0)$, where $\eta_c$ is the ground-state profile with parameter $c>0$ and $v\in\mathbb{R}$ is the velocity.

Two regimes are well studied: (i) the "near standing wave" regime, in which $\psi$ stays close to a stationary nonlinear bound state of $H$, and (ii) the "fast-soliton scattering" regime, in which a soliton of large velocity $v\gg 1$ impinges on a vertex and the scattering through the junction can be approximated by the linear scattering matrix of $H$.

Problem: For initial data consisting of one or several solitons incident on a vertex of $\mathcal{G}$ in dynamical regimes that are neither close to a standing wave nor in the fast-soliton scattering limit, provide a rigorous mathematical description of:
(a) the mechanism by which a soliton can be trapped (captured) at a vertex or graph defect, producing a long-lived localized state at the vertex; and
(b) the mechanism by which new solitons, carrying nontrivial mass and momentum, can be generated and emitted along the outgoing edges from such an interaction.

Specifically, identify quantitative conditions on $\mathcal{G}$, $H$, the nonlinearity exponent $\sigma$, and the parameters $(c,v)$ of the incoming soliton(s) under which capture and/or generation occur, and prove asymptotic decomposition theorems of the form
$$ \psi(t,\cdot) = \sum_{j} \phi_{c_j,v_j}(t,\cdot) + \chi(t,\cdot) + r(t,\cdot), \qquad \|r(t)\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})}\to 0, $$
where $\chi$ is a localized state attached to the vertex and the $\phi_{c_j,v_j}$ are outgoing solitons.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and research on NLS on metric graphs (e.g., the Royal Society survey on NLS on graphs and 2025 work on looping-edge graphs) continue to focus on standing waves, well-posedness, and fast-soliton scattering at junctions. original_question: Consider the single-input time-optimal control system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q) on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic pair of C-infinity vector fields, the control u is any measurable function with |u| <= 1, and trajectories are required to connect fixed endpoints in minimum time. Must every time-optimal trajectory for such a generic 3-dimensional system be piecewise smooth, meaning smooth except at finitely many switching points where the optimal control changes its regime?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a 3-dimensional smooth manifold and consider single-input control-affine systems of the form
$$\dot q = f(q) + u\, g(q), \qquad q \in M, \quad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$ and admissible controls $u(\cdot)$ are measurable functions with values in $[-1,1]$. Given two points $q_0, q_1 \in M$, a trajectory connecting $q_0$ to $q_1$ is called time-optimal if it minimizes the transfer time among all admissible trajectories with the same endpoints.

A trajectory is called piecewise smooth if it is smooth except at finitely many switching points where the optimal control changes regime.

Question: Is it true that for a generic pair $(f,g)$ of smooth vector fields on $M$ (in the sense of Whitney $C^\infty$ topology), every time-optimal trajectory of the above system is piecewise smooth?
status_search_result: Searches indicate the regularity of time-optimal trajectories for generic single-input control-affine systems in dimension 3 is an active research topic, with partial results by Agrachev, Biolo and collaborators establishing local piecewise-smooth structure under specific Lie-bracket nondegeneracy conditions (e.g., the 3D case with 2D control, and local regularity results). No source was found asserting a complete proof for the global generic 3D single-input case, consistent with the problem being stated as open in dimension 3.

original_question: For the same generic 3-dimensional single-input time-optimal problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, define sw(q) to be the least integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory contained in a sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = infinity if arbitrarily small neighborhoods of q contain time-optimal trajectories with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth $3$-dimensional manifold and let $f, g$ be smooth vector fields on $M$. Consider the single-input time-optimal control problem
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where one seeks measurable controls $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$ steering a given initial point to a given final point in minimum time $T$. A time-optimal trajectory is called bang-bang if its associated control takes values in $\{-1,+1\}$ almost everywhere; a switching point of such a trajectory is a point at which the control changes sign. Assume that the pair $(f,g)$ is generic (i.e. belongs to an open dense subset of the space of pairs of smooth vector fields on $M$ in the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology).

For each $q \in M$, define $\mathrm{sw}(q)$ to be the smallest non-negative integer $k$ such that there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $q$ for which every time-optimal trajectory entirely contained in $U$ has at most $k$ switching points; set $\mathrm{sw}(q) = \infty$ if every neighborhood of $q$ contains a time-optimal trajectory with infinitely many switching points.

Question: Is $\mathrm{sw}(q) < \infty$ for every $q \in M$?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Agrachev and collaborators (e.g., on the 3D case with 2D control, 2016) explicitly notes that, even in related settings, no global finite bound on the number of switchings is known on certain "bad" lower-dimensional subsets. No publication found establishes finiteness of sw(q) at every point q for the generic single-input 3D time-optimal problem; the question appears to remain open.

original_question: In the generic 3-dimensional time-optimal control problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, is every individual time-optimal trajectory forced to have only finitely many switching points, even if one does not assume a uniform neighborhood-wise bound on the number of switchings?
self_contained_problem:
Consider control-affine systems on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ of the form
$$\dot q = f(q) + u\, g(q), \qquad |u| \le 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$. A trajectory is called time-optimal if it minimizes the time to steer between its endpoints among all admissible trajectories. A switching point of an admissible trajectory associated with a measurable control $u(\cdot)$ is a point in time at which $u$ fails to be locally constant (equivalently, in the bang-bang setting, where the control jumps between $+1$ and $-1$).

For a generic pair $(f,g)$ — that is, for $(f,g)$ in a residual subset of the space of pairs of smooth vector fields on $M$ in the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology — is it true that every individual time-optimal trajectory has only finitely many switching points?

(Here one does not assume any uniform a priori bound on the number of switchings in a neighborhood; the question concerns finiteness per trajectory only.)
status_search_result: Searches return work on the closely related 3D/2D-control case (Agrachev–Biolo, 2016) and earlier regularity results for generic single-input 3D systems (Sigalotti and others), where local bounds on switchings near generic points are obtained, but no result asserting per-trajectory finiteness of switching points for generic single-input 3D time-optimal trajectories. The question of finiteness for each individual time-optimal trajectory under generic assumptions appears to remain unresolved.

original_question: In higher-dimensional single-input time-optimal control systems q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, there are examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose qualitative structure survives small perturbations of the system. Are such extremals actually time-optimal?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-input affine control system on a smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $n \geq 3$:
$$\dot q = f(q) + u\, g(q), \qquad |u(t)| \leq 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$. For fixed initial and terminal states, a time-optimal trajectory is an admissible trajectory steering the initial to the terminal state in minimum time. By Pontryagin's Maximum Principle, every time-optimal trajectory is the projection of an extremal, i.e.\ a curve $(q(t),p(t))$ in $T^*M$ satisfying the Hamiltonian system associated with the maximized Hamiltonian $H(q,p,u) = \langle p, f(q)\rangle + u\,\langle p, g(q)\rangle$, and the optimal control satisfies $u(t) = \mathrm{sgn}\,\langle p(t), g(q(t))\rangle$ at points where the switching function $\varphi(t) := \langle p(t), g(q(t))\rangle$ is nonzero.

A switching point is an instant $t$ at which $\varphi(t)=0$ and the control changes sign. There exist constructed examples of extremals of such systems whose switching points accumulate (chattering / Fuller-type extremals) and whose qualitative structure is stable under small smooth perturbations of the vector fields $f$ and $g$.

Question: For such structurally stable chattering extremals, are the corresponding trajectories actually time-optimal (at least locally) between their endpoints?
status_search_result: The literature on chattering (Fuller-type) extremals in higher-dimensional single-input affine control systems describes structurally stable examples (Kupka, Zelikin–Borisov) but does not establish their time-optimality. Recent surveys and works on optimal synthesis with chattering arcs continue to treat the optimality of such extremals as an unresolved problem; no proof of optimality (or of non-optimality) for the structurally stable chattering extremals appears to be available.

original_question: Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields, not necessarily generic, in the single-input time-optimal system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, must there exist a time-optimal trajectory connecting the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a real analytic manifold and let $f, g$ be real analytic vector fields on $M$ (not assumed to satisfy any genericity condition). Consider the single-input control-affine time-optimal control system
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
with measurable controls $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. A trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ is called time-optimal if it minimizes the transfer time among all admissible trajectories joining $q(0)$ to $q(T)$. A switching point of an admissible trajectory associated with a control $u$ is a point $q(t)$ such that $u$ is not constant on any neighborhood of $t$.

Question: Suppose two points $q_0, q_1 \in M$ are connected by some time-optimal trajectory of the system. Must there exist a time-optimal trajectory from $q_0$ to $q_1$ whose set of switching points is at most countable?
status_search_result: The general question—whether for arbitrary (non-generic) real analytic single-input control-affine systems any reachable pair of points can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory with at most countably many switching points—appears to remain open. Available results (Agrachev–Biolo and others) establish countability/finiteness of switchings only locally, in low dimensions, or under nondegeneracy/genericity hypotheses on iterated Lie brackets, not in the full generality posed here.

original_question: For the same real analytic single-input time-optimal control setting, can one always choose a time-optimal trajectory between two time-optimally connected points whose set of switching points avoids having positive measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a real analytic manifold and let $f, g$ be real analytic vector fields on $M$. Consider the single-input control-affine system
$$\dot{x}(t) = f(x(t)) + u(t)\, g(x(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
with measurable controls $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. Given two points $x_0, x_1 \in M$ that are connected by some time-optimal trajectory of this system, a switching point of an admissible control $u$ is a point $t \in [0,T]$ such that $u$ is not constantly equal to $+1$ or $-1$ on any neighborhood of $t$.

Question: Is it always possible to choose a time-optimal trajectory from $x_0$ to $x_1$ whose associated optimal control has a switching set of Lebesgue measure zero in $[0,T]$? Equivalently, can one always avoid time-optimal controls whose set of switching points has positive Lebesgue measure?
status_search_result: Search results discuss regularity of time-optimal trajectories for real analytic single-input systems (bang-bang, finitely many switchings under bracket nondegeneracy, regular synthesis in low dimensions), but no source found that directly resolves whether, in full generality, one can always select a time-optimal trajectory whose switching set has measure zero. The status appears unresolved in the literature available.

original_question: Let gamma_0 and gamma_1 be smooth admissible paths of a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M with gamma_0(0) = gamma_1(0) = q_0 and with initial tangent vectors at q_0 that are not collinear. Does there always exist an admissible path connecting gamma_0(1) to gamma_1(1) whose length is strictly smaller than the length of the broken path obtained by concatenating gamma_0 and gamma_1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure, that is, a smooth bracket-generating distribution $\mathcal{D}\subset TM$ together with a smoothly varying inner product on $\mathcal{D}$. An absolutely continuous path $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ is called admissible (horizontal) if $\dot\gamma(t)\in\mathcal{D}_{\gamma(t)}$ for almost every $t$, and its length is $\ell(\gamma)=\int_0^1\|\dot\gamma(t)\|\,dt$.

Let $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to M$ be two smooth admissible paths with common starting point $\gamma_0(0)=\gamma_1(0)=q_0$, and assume that their initial velocities are linearly independent: $\dot\gamma_0(0)\wedge\dot\gamma_1(0)\neq 0$. Consider the broken (corner) path obtained by concatenating $\bar\gamma_0$ (the reversal of $\gamma_0$) with $\gamma_1$, going from $\gamma_0(1)$ through $q_0$ to $\gamma_1(1)$, of total length $\ell(\gamma_0)+\ell(\gamma_1)$.

Question: does there always exist an admissible path joining $\gamma_0(1)$ to $\gamma_1(1)$ whose length is strictly less than $\ell(\gamma_0)+\ell(\gamma_1)$?
status_search_result: Hakavuori and Le Donne (Inventiones Math., 2016, "Non-minimality of corners in subriemannian geometry") proved that admissible curves with a corner are never length minimizing in any sub-Riemannian manifold. This affirmatively resolves the question: a strictly shorter admissible path between the endpoints always exists, so the problem is solved.

original_question: Fix a point q_0 in a sub-Riemannian manifold and consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H^1 admissible paths starting at q_0 to M, sending each path to its endpoint at time 1. Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or equivalently, is it impossible for singular curves issuing from q_0 to fill the whole manifold M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\Delta,g)$ be a sub-Riemannian manifold, where $M$ is a smooth connected manifold, $\Delta\subset TM$ is a smooth bracket-generating distribution, and $g$ is a smooth metric on $\Delta$. Fix a base point $q_0\in M$ and let
$$\Omega_{q_0} = \{\gamma\in H^1([0,1],M) : \dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}\text{ for a.e. }t,\ \gamma(0)=q_0\}$$
be the Hilbert manifold of horizontal (admissible) paths starting at $q_0$. Define the endpoint map
$$\mathrm{End}_{q_0}:\Omega_{q_0}\to M,\qquad \mathrm{End}_{q_0}(\gamma)=\gamma(1).$$
A horizontal path $\gamma\in\Omega_{q_0}$ is called singular (or abnormal) if it is a critical point of $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}$, i.e.\ the differential $d\mathrm{End}_{q_0}(\gamma)$ is not surjective. A point $q\in M$ is a regular value of $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}$ if every $\gamma\in\mathrm{End}_{q_0}^{-1}(q)$ is a regular point.

Question: Must the endpoint map $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}$ always admit at least one regular value in $M$? Equivalently, is it impossible that the singular horizontal curves issuing from $q_0$ fill the whole manifold $M$?
status_search_result: This is a form of the Sard conjecture in sub-Riemannian geometry: the set of endpoints of singular horizontal curves from a fixed point should have measure zero (in particular cannot fill M). It has been established in important special cases — e.g. on Martinet surfaces (Belotto da Silva–Rifford, 2018) and the strong Sard conjecture for analytic rank-two distributions on 3-manifolds (Belotto da Silva–Figalli–Parusiński–Rifford, Inventiones 2022, showing the singular reachable set has Hausdorff dimension ≤ 1) — but the general conjecture remains open.

original_question: In a sub-Riemannian manifold, optimal singular curves starting from a fixed point q_0 are known to fill a nowhere dense subset of the manifold. Can the set filled by such optimal singular curves nevertheless have positive measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\Delta,g)$ be a sub-Riemannian manifold, where $M$ is a smooth connected manifold, $\Delta\subset TM$ is a totally nonholonomic (bracket-generating) smooth distribution, and $g$ is a smooth metric on $\Delta$. A horizontal curve is an absolutely continuous curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ with $\dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ for almost every $t$; its length is $\int_0^1\sqrt{g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)}\,dt$. A horizontal curve is called singular if it is a critical point of the endpoint map $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}:\gamma\mapsto\gamma(1)$, defined on the Hilbert manifold of horizontal curves starting from a fixed point $q_0\in M$. A singular horizontal curve is called optimal (length-minimizing) if it minimizes sub-Riemannian length among horizontal curves with the same endpoints. 

It is known that the set 
$$ S(q_0)\;=\;\bigcup\{\gamma([0,1]) : \gamma \text{ is an optimal singular horizontal curve with }\gamma(0)=q_0\}$$
is a nowhere dense subset of $M$. 

Question: Can $S(q_0)$ have positive Lebesgue measure in $M$ for some choice of sub-Riemannian structure $(M,\Delta,g)$ and base point $q_0$?
status_search_result: The question is a form of the minimizing Sard conjecture in sub-Riemannian geometry. It remains open in full generality. Significant progress has been made: the Strong Sard Conjecture has been proved for analytic sub-Riemannian structures of rank 2 in dimension 3 (Belotto da Silva–Figalli–Parusiński–Rifford, Inventiones 2022), where the set of endpoints of singular minimizers from a point has Hausdorff dimension at most 1 and hence measure zero. The conjecture is also verified for certain Carnot groups (filiform; rank 2 step 4; rank 3 step 3). The general case is still listed as a major open problem.

original_question: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional Martinet distribution, consider a sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q_0 and a point where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve. What is the C^1-classification, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of R^3, of the germ of the sphere at such a point?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a 3-dimensional smooth manifold and let $D \subset TM$ be a rank-2 distribution which is of Martinet type, i.e. there exists a smooth 1-form $\omega$ with $D = \ker\omega$ such that the Martinet surface 
$$\Sigma = \{q \in M : \omega \wedge d\omega = 0\}$$
is a smooth 2-dimensional submanifold of $M$, and at each point of $\Sigma$ the distribution $D$ is transverse to $\Sigma$. Equip $D$ with a smooth Riemannian metric $g$, so that $(M, D, g)$ is a sub-Riemannian structure of Martinet type. For a base point $q_0 \in M$ and $r > 0$, define the sub-Riemannian sphere
$$S(q_0, r) = \{ q \in M : d_{SR}(q_0, q) = r \},$$
where $d_{SR}$ is the sub-Riemannian distance. A horizontal curve $\gamma : [0,T] \to M$ tangent to $D$ is called a singular (abnormal) curve if it is a critical point of the endpoint map restricted to horizontal curves with fixed initial point; in the Martinet case the singular curves through $q_0$ are the integral curves of $D \cap T\Sigma$ contained in $\Sigma$, and such a singular curve is called optimal if it is locally length-minimizing for $g$.

Consider the class of generic sub-Riemannian metrics $g$ on a Martinet distribution. Let $r>0$ be small enough that $S(q_0,r)$ meets an optimal singular curve issuing from $q_0$, and let $\bar q$ be a point of intersection of $S(q_0,r)$ with this optimal singular curve.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to germs of $C^1$-diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^3$, of the germ of the sub-Riemannian sphere $S(q_0,r)$ at the point $\bar q$.

paper_title: Open problems in hot QCD
context_brief: Systematic treatment of multi-loop thermal sum-integrals
original_question: Can one develop a systematic, preferably computer-algebraic, method for evaluating the multi-loop thermal sum-integrals that arise in perturbative finite-temperature QCD and related finite-temperature field theories, instead of continuing to solve the needed master sum-integrals one case at a time? Such a method would need to work in the presence of discretized Matsubara frequencies and the additional temperature scale, reuse more of the analytic machinery that is successful at zero temperature than integration-by-parts relations alone, and provide a reusable way to separate ultraviolet and infrared divergent pieces so that higher-order perturbative computations can be streamlined.
self_contained_problem:
In thermal quantum field theory in the imaginary-time (Matsubara) formalism, loop integrals are replaced by "sum-integrals" of the form

    ∑∫_P f(P) := T ∑_{p_0} ∫ d^{d-1}p/(2π)^{d-1} f(p_0, p),

where p_0 ranges over discrete Matsubara frequencies (p_0 = 2π n T for bosons, p_0 = (2n+1)π T for fermions, n ∈ ℤ), T > 0 is the temperature, and dimensional regularization is used in the spatial directions. In perturbative finite-temperature QCD and related field theories, higher-order computations require evaluation of multi-loop master sum-integrals that depend on the additional scale T and that mix ultraviolet and infrared divergent regions in a nontrivial way.

Develop a systematic, computer-algebraic algorithm for the evaluation of arbitrary multi-loop thermal sum-integrals with the following properties:

1. It handles the discretized Matsubara frequencies and the temperature scale T together with the continuous spatial loop momenta in a uniform framework.
2. It goes beyond purely integration-by-parts (IBP) reductions on Matsubara summands by incorporating additional analytic techniques known to be effective for zero-temperature multi-loop integrals (e.g., differential equations, dimensional shifts, Mellin–Barnes representations, sector decomposition, symbolic summation, etc.).
3. It produces a reusable, automated procedure for separating ultraviolet and infrared divergent contributions of any given sum-integral, so that the divergent parts can be isolated algorithmically rather than case by case.
4. It reduces the evaluation of any multi-loop master sum-integral occurring in higher-order thermal perturbation theory to a finite, mechanizable set of operations, as opposed to the case-by-case treatments currently used beyond two loops.

Construct such an algorithm and prove its correctness and termination, or else establish a precise obstruction showing that no such uniform algorithmic treatment is possible.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: thermal IBP reductions via Laporta-style algorithms, tensor-reduction by dimension shifts at finite T, symbolic-summation techniques, and numerical packages such as pySecDec adapted to Matsubara sums have all been developed. However, no fully general, uniform computer-algebraic framework for arbitrary multi-loop master sum-integrals (with automated UV/IR subtraction) exists; computations beyond two loops still proceed largely case-by-case for nontrivial cases. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved / still open in full generality.

original_question: For the Engel distribution, namely a rank-2 distribution on R^4 with n_3(q) = 3 and n_4(q) = 4, sub-Riemannian spheres are 3-dimensional hypersurfaces and every point lies on a unique singular curve whose small segments are optimal. What is the corresponding local classification of sphere singularities at points where such optimal singular curves meet the sphere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta$ be a smooth Engel distribution on $\mathbb{R}^4$, that is, a rank-2 distribution such that, denoting $\Delta^1=\Delta$ and $\Delta^{k+1}=\Delta^k+[\Delta,\Delta^k]$, one has $\dim\Delta^2(q)=3$ and $\dim\Delta^3(q)=4$ for every $q\in\mathbb{R}^4$. Equip $\Delta$ with a smooth sub-Riemannian metric $g$, and define the sub-Riemannian distance $d(q_0,q)$ as the infimum of the $g$-lengths of horizontal (i.e. tangent to $\Delta$) Lipschitz curves joining $q_0$ to $q$. For small $r>0$, the sub-Riemannian sphere $S_r(q_0)=\{q:d(q_0,q)=r\}$ is a 3-dimensional hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

It is known that through every point $q_0$ there passes a unique (up to reparametrization) singular (abnormal) horizontal curve $\gamma$, and that sufficiently short subarcs of $\gamma$ are length-minimizing. Hence $\gamma$ meets each small sphere $S_r(q_0)$ at distinguished points.

Problem: provide a complete local classification, up to smooth diffeomorphism of $(\mathbb{R}^4,q_0)$, of the singularities of $S_r(q_0)$ at the points where the optimal singular curve $\gamma$ through $q_0$ meets the sphere $S_r(q_0)$. Equivalently, describe all possible local diffeomorphism types of the germ $(S_r(q_0),p)$ at such intersection points $p=\gamma(\pm r)$.
status_search_result: For the flat (Carnot) sub-Riemannian Engel structure, the sphere has been studied and its abnormal "poles" are known to be non-subanalytic singular points; partial descriptions of the asymptotics of the front near these poles have been obtained in recent work on the Engel group sphere and on Legendre singularities of sub-Riemannian geodesics. However, a full local diffeomorphism classification of sphere singularities at points where optimal singular curves meet the sphere, in the general Engel case, does not appear to have been established.
