paper_title: Open problems in hot QCD
context_brief: General-N evaluation of the residual sum-integrals
original_question: Can the four convergent three-loop sum-integral contributions B^I_N, B^II_N, B^III_N, and B^IV_N that remain after the subtraction procedure be evaluated analytically for general integer N, rather than only by numerical approximation at specific fixed values such as N = 2 and N = 3? In concrete terms, the open problem is to turn the one-dimensional integral representations obtained after the subtraction and coordinate-space transformations into general-N formulas or a comparably systematic evaluation procedure that avoids case-by-case numerical treatment.
self_contained_problem:
Consider thermal field theory at temperature $T$ in the imaginary-time (Matsubara) formalism, where bosonic sum-integrals are defined by
$$\sumint_P f(P) \;=\; T\sum_{p_0\in 2\pi T\mathbb{Z}} \int\!\frac{d^{d-1}\mathbf p}{(2\pi)^{d-1}}\, f(p_0,\mathbf p),$$
with Euclidean four-momentum $P=(p_0,\mathbf p)$ and $P^2=p_0^2+\mathbf p^2$. In the evaluation of three-loop massless bosonic vacuum sum-integrals contributing to the next-to-next-to-leading-order Debye screening mass of hot QCD, after applying a standard ultraviolet/infrared subtraction procedure and a coordinate-space transformation, four convergent residual contributions, denoted
$$B^{\mathrm{I}}_N,\quad B^{\mathrm{II}}_N,\quad B^{\mathrm{III}}_N,\quad B^{\mathrm{IV}}_N,$$
parametrized by a positive integer $N$ (an exponent appearing on certain bosonic propagators), can be reduced to one-dimensional integrals over the positive real axis whose integrands are products of polylogarithms, ordinary logarithms, and hyperbolic functions of a single variable.

Problem. Find closed-form analytic expressions, valid for arbitrary integer $N\ge 1$, for the four families
$$B^{\mathrm{I}}_N,\ B^{\mathrm{II}}_N,\ B^{\mathrm{III}}_N,\ B^{\mathrm{IV}}_N,$$
or equivalently provide a systematic evaluation procedure that produces such expressions as explicit functions of $N$ (rather than a case-by-case numerical evaluation at fixed values such as $N=2$ and $N=3$).
status_search_result: Subsequent work on three-loop sum-integrals for the Debye mass in hot QCD (e.g. Ghişoiu–Schröder 2012 and follow-ups on tensor sum-integral techniques) reports analytic evaluation of divergent parts and numerical evaluation of finite parts at fixed N, but no explicit general-N closed-form evaluation of the four residual families B^I–IV_N appears to have been reported. The status thus appears unresolved, though no definitive negative result was found.

original_question: Consider a generic pair of smooth vector fields f_0 and f_1 near a point q_0 in R^2 such that f_0(q_0) and f_1(q_0) are collinear, n_2(q_0) = 1, and n_3(q_0) = 2, and define the almost-Riemannian distance S_{q_0}(q) as the minimum time needed to reach q from q_0 along trajectories of q˙ = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q) under the unit-norm constraint on the two control components stated in the paper. What is the C^1-classification of the germ of the distance function S_{q_0} for such generic pairs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f_0$ and $f_1$ be smooth vector fields on a neighborhood of a point $q_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Consider the control system
$$\dot q = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q), \qquad u_0^2 + u_1^2 \le 1,$$
and define the associated almost-Riemannian distance from $q_0$ by
$$S_{q_0}(q) = \inf\{\, T \ge 0 : \exists\, \text{admissible controls } (u_0,u_1) \text{ with } u_0^2+u_1^2 \le 1 \text{ steering } q_0 \text{ to } q \text{ in time } T\,\}.$$
For each $q$ near $q_0$, let $\Delta(q)=\mathrm{span}\{f_0(q),f_1(q)\}$, and let $\Delta^k(q)$ denote the $k$-th step of the flag obtained by iterated Lie brackets of $f_0,f_1$. Set
$$n_k(q)=\dim\Delta^k(q).$$
Assume that at $q_0$ the vectors $f_0(q_0)$ and $f_1(q_0)$ are collinear and that
$$n_2(q_0)=1,\qquad n_3(q_0)=2$$
(so $q_0$ is a tangency-type singular point where the distribution is one-dimensional, the first bracket does not generate, but the second bracket does).

Provide a $C^1$-classification of the germs at $q_0$ of the distance function $S_{q_0}$ for generic pairs $(f_0,f_1)$ satisfying the conditions $n_2(q_0)=1$ and $n_3(q_0)=2$. That is, exhibit a list of model germs such that, for an open dense set of pairs $(f_0,f_1)$ in the appropriate $C^\infty$ topology, the germ of $S_{q_0}$ is $C^1$-equivalent to one of these models, and prove that distinct models are not $C^1$-equivalent.

The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Let Delta be a vector distribution on a manifold M, and call it singular transitive when any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves of Delta. Does singular transitivity force the symmetry group of Delta, meaning the diffeomorphisms Phi of M with Phi_* Delta = Delta, to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $\Delta \subset TM$ be a smooth vector distribution on $M$ (a smooth subbundle, or more generally a smooth submodule of the tangent sheaf). A singular curve of $\Delta$ is, in the sense of sub-Riemannian/control geometry, an absolutely continuous horizontal curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ (i.e. $\dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ a.e.) which is a critical point of the endpoint map among horizontal curves with fixed endpoints. Call $\Delta$ singular transitive if any two points of $M$ can be joined by a concatenation of finitely many singular curves of $\Delta$. The symmetry group of $\Delta$ is
$$\mathrm{Sym}(\Delta)=\{\Phi\in\mathrm{Diff}(M):\Phi_*\Delta=\Delta\}.$$
Question: Does singular transitivity of $\Delta$ imply that $\mathrm{Sym}(\Delta)$ carries the structure of a finite-dimensional Lie group (acting smoothly on $M$)?
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. It is posed as a natural open question about symmetry groups of singular-transitive distributions, and no published proof or counterexample establishing finite-dimensionality (or its failure) under singular transitivity was located.

original_question: For each n, let mu(n) be the smallest integer m such that an m-times traversed plane convex curve admits arbitrarily small perturbations that become nondegenerate closed curves in R^n, where nondegeneracy means that the velocity, curvature, torsion, and higher Frenet data never degenerate. What is mu(n) for dimensions n > 3?
self_contained_problem:
A smooth closed curve $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is called nondegenerate (locally convex) if for every $t\in S^1$ the derivatives $\gamma'(t),\gamma''(t),\dots,\gamma^{(n)}(t)$ are linearly independent in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (equivalently, the Frenet frame is well defined and all generalized curvatures are nowhere vanishing). 

Given a strictly convex closed curve $c$ in a plane $\mathbb{R}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and an integer $m\geq 1$, let $c^{(m)}$ denote the curve obtained by traversing $c$ exactly $m$ times. Define $\mu(n)$ to be the smallest positive integer $m$ with the following property: for every strictly convex closed plane curve $c$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a smooth closed curve $\tilde\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$ that is nondegenerate in the above sense and is $\varepsilon$-close (in the $C^0$, or equivalently $C^k$ for any fixed $k$) to $c^{(m)}$.

It is known that $\mu(2)=1$ and $\mu(3)=2$. Determine $\mu(n)$ for every integer $n>3$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining μ(n) for n > 3 is described as an important open problem. Related work on spaces of nondegenerate (locally convex) closed curves in R^n and S^n (e.g., stratification by itineraries and combinatorialization of spaces of nondegenerate spherical curves) indicates that the homotopy type / structural questions about such spaces remain largely open in dimensions n ≥ 4, and no explicit value of μ(n) for n > 3 appears in the literature surveyed.

original_question: For regular closed curves in R^n equipped with their orthonormal Frenet frames in O(n), is the length of the Frenet frame always strictly greater than mu(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) embedded in O(n), where mu(n) is the minimum multiplicity needed for a plane convex curve to admit a regular perturbation in R^n?
self_contained_problem:
Equip $\mathbb{R}^n$ with its standard inner product and let $O(n)$ denote the orthogonal group with the bi-invariant Riemannian metric induced by the Frobenius inner product on $n\times n$ matrices. For a smooth regular closed curve $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$ that is sufficiently generic so that its orthonormal Frenet frame $F_\gamma:S^1\to O(n)$ is well-defined and smooth, let $L(F_\gamma)$ denote the length of $F_\gamma$ in $O(n)$ with respect to this metric. Let $\ell_n$ denote the length of the standard closed geodesic obtained from the embedding $SO(2)\hookrightarrow O(n)$ that acts as a rotation in the first two coordinates and trivially elsewhere.

Define $\mu(n)$ to be the smallest positive integer $m$ with the following property: every smooth regular closed plane convex curve, viewed as a curve in $\mathbb{R}^n$ via the inclusion $\mathbb{R}^2\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a smooth regular perturbation in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose Frenet frame has total turning multiplicity $m$ relative to the natural $SO(2)$ direction.

Determine $\mu(n)$ for all $n>3$, and decide whether the strict inequality
$$L(F_\gamma) > \mu(n)\cdot \ell_n$$
holds for every smooth regular closed curve $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ admitting a Frenet frame.
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as an open question concerning the determination of μ(n) for n > 3 and the corresponding length lower bound for Frenet frames. A general web search returns only standard expository material on Frenet–Serret frames and yields no source claiming a resolution, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation on the torus with periodic boundary conditions, viewed as a control system on the space V of divergence-free H^1 vector fields, where the forcing eta(t, .) is constrained to lie in a finite-dimensional subspace E of the space of divergence-free fields supported in a fixed open subset D of the torus, and E is required not to depend on the viscosity nu. Is the system approximately controllable in any time under such a localized degenerate forcing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d/(2\pi\mathbb{Z})^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be the flat torus, and let
$$V = \{u \in H^1(\mathbb{T}^d;\mathbb{R}^d) : \mathrm{div}\, u = 0,\ \int_{\mathbb{T}^d} u\,dx = 0\}.$$
Consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes system with periodic boundary conditions
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot
abla)u - 
u\,\Delta u + 
abla p = \eta(t,x), \qquad \mathrm{div}\, u = 0,$$
with viscosity $
u > 0$, viewed as a control system on $V$ with control $\eta(t,\cdot)$. Fix a nonempty open subset $D \subset \mathbb{T}^d$ and let
$$V_D = \overline{\{u \in V : \mathrm{supp}\, u \subset D\}}$$
(closure in $V$). Restrict the control to take values in a finite-dimensional subspace $E \subset V_D$ that does not depend on $
u$, so that for almost every $t$, $\eta(t,\cdot) \in E$.

The system is said to be approximately controllable in time $T>0$ if for every initial state $u_0 \in V$, every target $u_1 \in V$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a control $\eta \in L^2(0,T;E)$ such that the corresponding solution $u$ satisfies $\|u(T,\cdot) - u_1\|_{L^2} < \varepsilon$.

Question: Does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $E \subset V_D$, independent of $
u$, such that the Navier-Stokes system above is approximately controllable in any time $T>0$ by controls valued in $E$?  Equivalently, prove or disprove the existence and give an effective construction of such a subspace $E$.
status_search_result: The question of approximate controllability of the periodic Navier-Stokes system by a localized, finite-dimensional, viscosity-independent forcing supported in a fixed open subset of the torus is, to our knowledge, still open. The Agrachev-Sarychev program and subsequent works (including Shirikyan and others) established approximate controllability and controllability in finite-dimensional projections by low-mode (Fourier) forcing on the torus, but these forcings are global Fourier modes, not localized in physical space; combining localization in space with a finite-dimensional, viscosity-independent control space remains a recognized open problem.

original_question: In the same Navier-Stokes control setting on the torus, with forcing constrained to a finite-dimensional subspace E of divergence-free vector fields supported in a fixed open set D and chosen independently of the viscosity nu, is the system controllable in finite-dimensional projections in any time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes system on the two-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/2\pi\mathbb{Z}^2$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = h(t,x) + \eta(t,x), \qquad \mathrm{div}\,u = 0, \qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,$$
where $\nu>0$ is the viscosity, $h$ is a fixed external force, $u_0 \in V$, and $V$ denotes the space of divergence-free, mean-zero vector fields on $\mathbb{T}^2$ of class $H^1$. Fix a non-empty open set $D\subset \mathbb{T}^2$ and let
$$V_D = \overline{\{u\in V : \mathrm{supp}\,u \subset D\}}.$$
The control $\eta$ is required to take values in a finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset V_D$ that is chosen independently of $\nu$.

The system is said to be controllable in finite-dimensional projections in time $T>0$ if for every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subset V$, every $u_0\in V$, and every $\hat u\in V$ there exists a control $\eta\in L^2([0,T];E)$ such that the corresponding solution $u$ satisfies $\mathsf{P}_F u(T,\cdot) = \mathsf{P}_F \hat u$, where $\mathsf{P}_F$ is the orthogonal projection onto $F$.

Question: Does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset V_D$, independent of the viscosity $\nu$, such that the system above is controllable in finite-dimensional projections in every time $T>0$? If so, give an explicit construction of such $E$.
status_search_result: The combined requirements—forcing localized in a fixed open subdomain and taking values in a finite-dimensional subspace independent of viscosity, yielding controllability in finite-dimensional projections—do not appear to have been resolved. Agrachev–Sarychev-type results yield finite-dimensional but non-localized controls, while the recent work of Nersesyan–Rissel (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 2025) achieves physically localized controls of degenerate but not finite-dimensional structure, and explicitly contrasts the two settings, indicating the simultaneous problem remains open.

original_question: Let S be a numerical semigroup, meaning a cofinite submonoid of the nonnegative integers N, and let F(S) denote its Frobenius number, the greatest integer not belonging to S. Find a formula for F(S) in terms of a minimal system of generators of S when the embedding dimension e(S) is at least 3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A numerical semigroup is a submonoid $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ (containing $0$ and closed under addition) such that $\mathbb{N} \setminus S$ is finite. Every numerical semigroup $S \neq \mathbb{N}$ admits a unique minimal system of generators $\{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_e\}$ with $\gcd(n_1, \dots, n_e) = 1$; the integer $e = e(S)$ is called the embedding dimension of $S$. The Frobenius number of $S$ is defined as
$$F(S) = \max(\mathbb{Z} \setminus S),$$
i.e., the largest integer that does not belong to $S$.

For $e = 2$, with minimal generators $n_1 < n_2$, one has the classical formula $F(S) = n_1 n_2 - n_1 - n_2$.

Problem: For numerical semigroups $S$ with embedding dimension $e(S) \geq 3$, give a general closed-form formula expressing $F(S)$ as a function of a minimal system of generators $\{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_e\}$ of $S$.
status_search_result: The problem of finding a general closed-form formula for the Frobenius number of a numerical semigroup with embedding dimension at least 3 is a long-standing open problem. F. Curtis (1990) proved that the Frobenius number cannot be expressed as a finite-arithmetic-step closed formula (in particular as a polynomial) in the generators when e ≥ 3, and Ramírez Alfonsín showed that the corresponding decision problem is NP-hard. Partial results exist for special families (e.g., arithmetic, almost arithmetic, geometric, or symmetric/pseudo-symmetric semigroups, and the e=3 case has explicit semi-algorithmic descriptions), but no general formula is known.

original_question: Let S be a numerical semigroup and let H(S) = N \ S be its set of gaps. Determine the genus g(S) = |H(S)| from a minimal system of generators of S when the embedding dimension e(S) is at least 3.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that contains $0$, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. The set $H(S) = \mathbb{N} \setminus S$ is called the set of gaps of $S$, and its cardinality $g(S) = |H(S)|$ is called the genus of $S$. Every numerical semigroup $S \neq \mathbb{N}$ admits a unique minimal system of generators $\{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_e\}$, that is, $S = \{a_1 n_1 + \cdots + a_e n_e : a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$ and no $n_i$ is a non-negative integer combination of the others; the integer $e = e(S)$ is called the embedding dimension of $S$.

Provide an explicit closed-form formula that, given a minimal system of generators $\{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_e\}$ with $\gcd(n_1,\dots,n_e) = 1$ and $e = e(S) \geq 3$, computes the genus $g(S)$ of the numerical semigroup $S$ they generate.
status_search_result: The Frobenius/genus problem was solved by Sylvester for embedding dimension 2. For embedding dimension at least 3, no general closed-form formula for the genus is known; only formulas for special families (e.g., some cases by Tripathi) and algorithmic methods exist. The problem is widely cited as open.

original_question: Determine the type t(S) of a numerical semigroup S from other standard invariants, especially the multiplicity m(S), embedding dimension e(S), genus g(S), or Frobenius number F(S).
status_search_result: The general problem of determining the type of a numerical semigroup from its multiplicity, embedding dimension, genus, and/or Frobenius number remains open. original_question: For each genus g, let n_g be the number of numerical semigroups of genus g. Determine whether n_g > n_{g+1} fails never, equivalently whether there are always more numerical semigroups of genus g + 1 than of genus g, in the Fibonacci-like growth problem discussed by Bras-Amoros.

   n_{g+1} ≥ n_g,

original_question: For a modular numerical semigroup S(a, b, 1), find formulas for the Frobenius number F(S(a, b, 1)), multiplicity m(S(a, b, 1)), type t(S(a, b, 1)), and embedding dimension e(S(a, b, 1)) in terms of the parameters a and b.
self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. Consider the modular Diophantine inequality
$$a x \bmod b \;\le\; x,$$
and let
$$S(a,b,1) \;=\; \{\, x \in \mathbb{N} : a x \bmod b \le x \,\}.$$
It is known that $S(a,b,1)$ is a numerical semigroup, i.e. a submonoid of $(\mathbb{N},+)$ whose complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S(a,b,1)$ is finite. For a numerical semigroup $S$ define:

- the Frobenius number $F(S) = \max(\mathbb{Z}\setminus S)$;
- the multiplicity $m(S) = \min(S\setminus\{0\})$;
- the embedding dimension $e(S)$, the cardinality of the (unique) minimal system of generators of $S$;
- the type $t(S) = \#\{\, z \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus S : z + s \in S \text{ for all } s \in S\setminus\{0\}\,\}$ (the number of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of $S$).

Find closed-form expressions, in terms of the parameters $a$ and $b$ only, for
$$F(S(a,b,1)),\qquad m(S(a,b,1)),\qquad t(S(a,b,1)),\qquad e(S(a,b,1)).$$
status_search_result: The problem of giving closed-form formulas for the Frobenius number, multiplicity, type, and embedding dimension of the modular numerical semigroup S(a,b,1) in terms of a and b appears to remain open. While algorithms (of Euclidean-like complexity) exist for computing F(S(a,b,1)), and the genus has been given a formula, the literature on proportionally modular numerical semigroups still lists the question of closed formulas for these invariants as unsolved.

original_question: Determine whether Wilf's conjecture e(S)g(S) <= (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1) holds for every modular numerical semigroup.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}_0$. For such an $S$, define:
- the Frobenius number $F(S) = \max(\mathbb{N}_0 \setminus S)$,
- the genus $g(S) = |\mathbb{N}_0 \setminus S|$,
- the embedding dimension $e(S)$, the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of $S$.

Given positive integers $a < b$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$, the modular numerical semigroup associated with the pair $(a,b)$ is
$$S(a,b) \;=\; \{\, x \in \mathbb{N}_0 : ax \bmod b \le x \,\},$$
where $ax \bmod b$ denotes the remainder of $ax$ upon division by $b$. A numerical semigroup is called modular if it equals $S(a,b)$ for some such pair.

Wilf's conjecture asserts that for every numerical semigroup $S$,
$$e(S)\, g(S) \;\le\; (e(S)-1)\,(F(S)+1).$$

Question: Does Wilf's conjecture hold for every modular numerical semigroup?
status_search_result: Wilf's conjecture is a long-standing open problem in the theory of numerical semigroups. It is known to hold in many special cases (e.g., embedding dimension ≤ 3, large embedding dimension, conductor ≤ 3·multiplicity, genus ≤ 66), but the case of modular numerical semigroups is explicitly listed as not known. Recent surveys and problem lists from 2024–2025 still treat Wilf's conjecture as open in general, with no specific resolution for the modular subclass found.

paper_title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions
original_question: Beyond the class-group modules that arise in classical Iwasawa theory, which other Λ-modules have Property F, and what general hypotheses guarantee that a submodule of a free Λ-module has Property F? The question asks for intrinsic structural criteria, not just isolated examples, so that one can recognize when a projective-limit Λ-module has the same rigidity and decomposition behavior that the paper proves for the standard Iwasawa modules.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $K_\infty/K$ be a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of a number field $K$ with Galois group $\Gamma\cong\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}_p[[\Gamma]]$ denote the associated Iwasawa algebra (a complete regular local Noetherian ring isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$). A finitely generated $\Lambda$-module $M$ is said to have Property F if it is a submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module of finite rank and, in addition, satisfies the following rigidity condition: for every height-one prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $\Lambda$, the localization $M_\mathfrak{p}$ is a reflexive $\Lambda_\mathfrak{p}$-module, and $M$ admits a canonical decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{\chi}M(\chi)$ into isotypic components under any continuous action of a finite group commuting with $\Gamma$, with each component itself embedding as a submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module.

The standard Iwasawa class-group modules (e.g.\ the projective limits of $p$-parts of class groups along $K_\infty/K$, suitably modified) are known to enjoy Property F.

Problem. Provide intrinsic structural criteria — formulated purely in terms of $\Lambda$-module-theoretic invariants such as Fitting ideals, characteristic ideals, depth, or behavior under localization at height-one primes — that are necessary and sufficient (or at least sufficient under natural hypotheses) for a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module $M$ that arises as a projective limit of finite $p$-groups along $K_\infty/K$ to have Property F. Equivalently, identify general conditions on a submodule $M\subset\Lambda^n$ guaranteeing Property F, and exhibit further natural classes of $\Lambda$-modules (beyond the classical Iwasawa class-group modules) that satisfy Property F.
status_search_result: Property F is a structural property of Iwasawa Λ-modules introduced in seminar notes on open questions in Iwasawa theory; it is explicitly stated there as an open problem to find further examples and general conditions guaranteeing the property. Web searches return no follow-up paper providing such intrinsic criteria, and related work (e.g. on T and T* components of Λ-modules and on completely faithful Iwasawa modules) does not resolve it. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Given a proportionally modular numerical semigroup by its minimal generators, find formulas for its Frobenius number, genus, and type directly from that minimal generating system.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. The elements of $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ are called the gaps of $S$; the largest gap is the Frobenius number $F(S)$, and the number of gaps is the genus $g(S)$. The type $t(S)$ is the cardinality of the set $\{x\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus S : x+s\in S\text{ for every }s\in S\setminus\{0\}\}$ (the pseudo-Frobenius numbers). Every numerical semigroup admits a unique finite minimal system of generators.

For positive integers $a,b,c,d$ with $a/b<c/d$, set $I=[a/b,c/d]$ and define
$$S(I)\;=\;\mathbb{N}\cap\bigsqcup_{n\ge 0} nI\;=\;\{x\in\mathbb{N}:\exists n\in\mathbb{N},\ na/b\le x\le nc/d\}.$$
Then $S(I)$ is a numerical semigroup, and a numerical semigroup is called proportionally modular if it equals $S(I)$ for some such interval $I$.

Problem. Provide explicit closed-form formulas, depending only on the unique minimal system of generators $\{n_1<n_2<\cdots<n_e\}$ of a proportionally modular numerical semigroup $S$, that compute each of the following invariants of $S$:
(i) the Frobenius number $F(S)$,
(ii) the genus $g(S)$,
(iii) the type $t(S)$.
status_search_result: The general Frobenius problem (formulas for the Frobenius number and genus from minimal generators) is known to be open for embedding dimension at least 3, and no closed-form formulas in terms of minimal generators are reported for the proportionally modular family in the literature surveyed. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the Iwasawa module A′ built from the p-parts of the ideal class groups of the p-integers in the cyclotomic tower of a Galois number field K, is the T-torsion subgroup A′[T] always finite? Equivalently, does the generalized Gross-Kuz'min conjecture hold outside the special cases proved here, so that the T-primary obstruction in the p-unit class-group module is never infinite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime number, let $K$ be a Galois number field, and let $K_\infty/K$ be the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, with $K_n$ the unique subfield of $K_\infty$ with $[K_n:K]=p^n$. For each $n$, let $S_n$ denote the set of primes of $K_n$ lying above $p$, and let $\mathrm{Cl}'(K_n)$ be the ideal class group of the ring of $S_n$-integers (the $p$-integers) of $K_n$. Define
$$A'(K_n) := \mathrm{Cl}'(K_n)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}_p,$$
the $p$-part of the $p$-integer class group, and form the projective limit
$$A' := \varprojlim_{n} A'(K_n)$$
with respect to the norm maps. Then $A'$ is a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[[T]] \cong \mathbb{Z}_p[[\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty/K)]]$, where $T = \gamma - 1$ for a topological generator $\gamma$ of $\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty/K)$. Let
$$A'[T] := \{x\in A' : Tx = 0\}$$
denote the $T$-torsion submodule.

Question: Is $A'[T]$ finite for every Galois number field $K$ and every prime $p$? Equivalently, does the generalized Gross–Kuz'min conjecture hold for all such $K$ and $p$?
status_search_result: The generalized Gross–Kuz'min conjecture is known in several cases (notably for abelian and CM number fields) but remains open in general. It continues to be invoked as a hypothesis in recent Iwasawa-theoretic work, including the conditional proof of the Strong Brumer–Stark Conjecture, indicating that no general proof is known as of 2026.

original_question: Find an algorithm that decides whether a given numerical semigroup is of the form P(a, b, c, d) union {0}, where P(a, b, c, d) is the set of solutions of a contracted proportionally modular Diophantine inequality ax mod b <= cx - d with nonnegative integers a, b, c, d and b != 0 != c.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$.

For nonnegative integers $a,b,c,d$ with $b \neq 0$ and $c \neq 0$, define
$$P(a,b,c,d) \;=\; \{\, x \in \mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\} : (a x \bmod b) \le c x - d \,\},$$
where $a x \bmod b$ denotes the remainder of $ax$ modulo $b$ in $\{0,1,\dots,b-1\}$. The set
$$S(a,b,c,d) \;=\; P(a,b,c,d) \cup \{0\}$$
is a numerical semigroup, called the numerical semigroup of solutions of a contracted proportionally modular Diophantine inequality.

Problem. Provide an algorithm that, given a numerical semigroup $S$ (specified, for instance, by its finite system of generators or by its Apéry set with respect to its multiplicity), decides in finite time whether there exist nonnegative integers $a,b,c,d$ with $b \neq 0$ and $c \neq 0$ such that
$$S \;=\; S(a,b,c,d).$$

original_question: For an arbitrary number field K and a fixed prime p, does the Leopoldt defect D(K) vanish? In concrete terms, is the p-adic closure of the global unit group always as large as Leopoldt predicted, so that no unexpected p-adic rank defect occurs in the unit embedding?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n = r_1 + 2r_2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, where $r_1$ is the number of real embeddings and $r_2$ the number of pairs of complex embeddings, and let $p$ be a fixed rational prime. Let $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ denote the group of global units of $K$, and let $E := \mathcal{O}_K^\times / (\text{torsion})$, so by Dirichlet's unit theorem $E$ is a free abelian group of rank $r := r_1 + r_2 - 1$.

For each prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $K$ above $p$, let $K_\mathfrak{p}$ denote the completion and $U_\mathfrak{p} \subset \mathcal{O}_{K_\mathfrak{p}}^\times$ the group of principal local units (i.e., those congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak{p}$). Set 
$$U := \prod_{\mathfrak{p} \mid p} U_\mathfrak{p},$$
which is a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module. The diagonal embedding $\mathcal{O}_K^\times \hookrightarrow U$ induces a homomorphism $\iota_p : E \otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathbb{Z}_p \to U$. Define the closure $\overline{E} \subset U$ to be the topological closure of the image of $E$ under this embedding, and define the Leopoldt defect
$$D(K) := \mathrm{rk}_\mathbb{Z}(E) - \mathrm{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(\overline{E}) = r - \mathrm{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(\overline{E}).$$
Equivalently, $D(K)$ equals the dimension of the kernel of $\iota_p$ as a $\mathbb{Q}_p$-vector space.

Prove or disprove: for every number field $K$ and every prime $p$, one has $D(K) = 0$.
status_search_result: Leopoldt's conjecture is known to hold for fields abelian over $\mathbb{Q}$ or over an imaginary quadratic field (Ax–Brumer, 1967, via Baker's theorem on linear forms in $p$-adic logarithms), and Mihăilescu has announced a proof for CM number fields. For general number fields, however, the conjecture remains open as of 2026; recent works (e.g., Allen–Calegari–Gee–Newton on potential automorphy and Leopoldt, and ongoing efforts via representation-theoretic and unit-theoretic methods) continue to attack it without a complete resolution.

original_question: Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be written as quotients S / p = {x in N | px in S} of numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 3 by a positive integer, and determine whether every numerical semigroup arises in this way.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset S of the non-negative integers N that is closed under addition, contains 0, and has finite complement in N. Its embedding dimension is the cardinality of its (unique) minimal system of generators. For a numerical semigroup S and a positive integer p, the quotient S/p is defined as
   S/p = { x ∈ N : p·x ∈ S },
which is again a numerical semigroup.

(a) Give an explicit characterization of those numerical semigroups T for which there exist a numerical semigroup S of embedding dimension 3 and a positive integer p such that T = S/p.

(b) Decide whether every numerical semigroup arises in this form, i.e. whether for every numerical semigroup T there exist a numerical semigroup S of embedding dimension 3 and a positive integer p with T = S/p.

A construction (for each k ≥ 2) produces numerical semigroups of embedding dimension k+1 that cannot be written as a k-quotient; in particular, taking k = 3 yields explicit numerical semigroups that are not quotients of any embedding-dimension-3 numerical semigroup. However, an explicit characterization (part (a)) of which numerical semigroups do arise as such quotients does not appear to be available, so the characterization problem remains open.

original_question: Let K/Q be a Galois extension containing the p-th roots of unity, let H be the maximal unramified p-abelian extension of the cyclotomic Zp-extension K∞, and let HE′ be the subextension cut out by adjoining p-power roots of global units. Must the index [H : HE′] always be finite? This is the general Greenberg conjecture in the paper's formulation, and it asks whether the unramified Iwasawa module is always controlled up to finite index by the unit-generated extension.
self_contained_problem:
Fix an odd prime $p$. Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension containing the $p$-th roots of unity, and let $K_\infty = \bigcup_n K_n$ denote its cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, with $K_n$ the $n$-th layer. Let $H/K_\infty$ be the maximal unramified abelian pro-$p$ extension. For each $n$, let $E_n = \mathcal{O}(K_n)^\times$ be the global units of $K_n$, and define
$$\Omega_E \;=\; \bigcup_{n\ge 0} K_n\bigl(E_n^{1/p^n}\bigr),$$
the field obtained by adjoining all $p^n$-th roots of global units at every level. Set
$$H_{E'} \;=\; H \cap \Omega_E.$$
Prove or disprove: the index $[H : H_{E'}]$ is finite for every such $K$.
status_search_result: Greenberg's generalized conjecture (asserting pseudo-nullity of the unramified Iwasawa module over the compositum of all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions, equivalent in the formulation given to finiteness of $[H:H_{E'}]$) remains open in general. Only special cases and conditional results are known, e.g. for imaginary $\lambda$-regular fields and various families of small-degree number fields. Active research continues, including a 2025 preprint addressing certain families.

original_question: If a numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjecture, determine whether its half S/2 = {x in N | 2x in S} must also satisfy Wilf's conjecture.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset S of the nonnegative integers N that contains 0, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in N. For such an S, let:
- m(S) = min(S \ {0}) be the multiplicity,
- F(S) = max(N \ S) be the Frobenius number (assume S ≠ N),
- n(S) = #{ s ∈ S : s < F(S) },
- e(S) = the embedding dimension, i.e. the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S.

Wilf's conjecture asserts that for every numerical semigroup S ≠ N,
  F(S) + 1 ≤ e(S) · n(S).
Define the half of S by
  S/2 = { x ∈ N : 2x ∈ S }.
It is known that S/2 is again a numerical semigroup.

Question: If a numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjecture, must its half S/2 also satisfy Wilf's conjecture?

original_question: For a CM Galois extension K containing the p-th roots of unity, is the minus-part T-torsion in the p-unit class-group module trivial; that is, does (A′)^−[T] = {1} hold? This is the classical Gross conjecture in the paper's formulation, expressing that the minus-part p-unit class module has no nontrivial T-torsion.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $K$ be a CM number field containing the $p$-th roots of unity, with maximal totally real subfield $K^+$. Let $j$ denote the complex conjugation, which acts on $G = \mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$-modules; for a $\mathbb{Z}_p[j]$-module $M$ on which $2$ is invertible, write $M^- = \{m \in M : j(m) = -m\}$ for the minus part.

Fix a finite set $T$ of primes of $K^+$ containing all $p$-adic primes and all archimedean primes, and let $T$ also denote the corresponding set of primes of $K$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,T}$ be the ring of $T$-integers of $K$ and let $A'_K$ denote the $p$-part of the $T$-class group of $K$ (the ideal class group of $\mathcal{O}_{K,T}$, tensored with $\mathbb{Z}_p$).

Let $K_\infty/K$ be the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, with intermediate fields $K_n$, and define
$$A' := \varprojlim_n A'_{K_n},$$
a module over $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[[\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty/K)]]$. Let $T \subset \Lambda$ also denote (by abuse of notation) the augmentation-type element such that $M[T]$ denotes the $T$-torsion submodule, equivalently the submodule of $\Gamma$-coinvariants viewed as a torsion piece, i.e., $(A')^-[T] = \{x \in (A')^- : Tx = 0\}$.

Question: Is it true that
$$(A')^-[T] = \{1\}\,?$$

Equivalently, does the minus part of the inverse limit of $p$-parts of $T$-class groups along the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-tower of $K$ have no nontrivial $T$-torsion?
status_search_result: The statement is the minus part of the Gross–Kuz'min conjecture for CM fields. It is known in several special cases (e.g., for abelian CM extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ in which $p$ splits completely, via Greenberg's use of the Brumer–Baker theorem) and further partial results exist for CM fields, but the conjecture is not known in full generality and remains an active research topic.

original_question: For a numerical semigroup S, determine the smallest possible number of irreducible numerical semigroups whose intersection equals S, and decide whether there is a universal constant N such that every numerical semigroup is an intersection of at most N irreducible numerical semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset S of the non-negative integers N that is closed under addition, contains 0, and whose complement N\S (the set of gaps) is finite. The Frobenius number F(S) is the largest gap of S. A numerical semigroup S is called irreducible if it cannot be written as the intersection of two numerical semigroups properly containing it; equivalently, S is maximal (with respect to inclusion) among all numerical semigroups with Frobenius number F(S).

It is known that every numerical semigroup S can be written as a finite intersection S = S_1 ∩ S_2 ∩ ⋯ ∩ S_n of irreducible numerical semigroups. Define the minimum decomposition length λ(S) to be the smallest n for which such a decomposition exists.

(a) For an arbitrary numerical semigroup S, determine λ(S) (i.e., the smallest possible number of irreducible numerical semigroups whose intersection is S).

(b) Decide whether there exists a universal positive integer N such that λ(S) ≤ N for every numerical semigroup S; equivalently, decide whether the function S ↦ λ(S) is bounded over all numerical semigroups.
status_search_result: Part (b) has been resolved negatively: recent work has shown that the minimum decomposition length of a numerical semigroup into irreducibles is unbounded, so no universal N exists. Part (a)—computing the exact minimum decomposition length for an arbitrary numerical semigroup—remains an active research problem, with explicit results known only for restricted families (e.g., multiplicity at most 6, ordinary semigroups), and the related conjecture that the set of decomposition lengths forms an interval is still only partially proved.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
context_brief: Universal critical slope in weak coupling
original_question: Consider the general copolymer model near a selective interface in which the renewal inter-arrival law satisfies K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α) and α lies in (0,1). In the weak-coupling regime the critical curve satisfies h_c(λ) ~ m_αλ as λ ↓ 0, where m_α is universal in the sense that it depends only on α and not on the detailed disorder law or on the finer details of K(·). Determine the value of m_α, or equivalently determine the correct weak-coupling slope of the critical curve.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\tau = \{\tau_0, \tau_1, \tau_2, \dots\}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}_0$ with $\tau_0 = 0$ and i.i.d. inter-arrival increments distributed according to a probability law $K$ on $\mathbb{N}$ satisfying
$$K(n) \;\sim\; \frac{C_K}{n^{1+\alpha}} \qquad \text{as } n \to \infty,$$
for some constant $C_K > 0$ and some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $\omega = (\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. centered real random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, independent of $\tau$. For parameters $\lambda \ge 0$ (coupling strength) and $h \ge 0$ (asymmetry), define the copolymer partition function
$$Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h} \;=\; \mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\lambda \omega_n - h)\, \Delta_n\right) \mathbf{1}_{\{N \in \tau\}}\right],$$
where $\Delta_n \in \{0,1\}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. fair Bernoulli signs (independent of $\tau$ and $\omega$), interpreted as the sign of the polymer between successive returns to the interface (so $\Delta_n$ is constant between renewal epochs and equal to a fresh fair coin between them). The quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}[\log Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}]$$
exists and is non-negative; the critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda) \;=\; \inf\{h \ge 0 : \mathrm{f}(\lambda,h) = 0\}.$$

Known facts. For each $\alpha \in (0,1)$ the limit
$$m_\alpha \;=\; \lim_{\lambda \downarrow 0}\frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}$$
exists in $(0,\infty)$ and depends only on $\alpha$ (not on the law of $\omega$ nor on the finer details of $K$ beyond the exponent $\alpha$). It is also known that $m_\alpha$ admits a representation as the critical slope of a continuum copolymer model built on the $\alpha$-stable regenerative set.

Problem. Determine the exact value of $m_\alpha$ as a function of $\alpha \in (0,1)$ (equivalently, give an explicit formula or characterization for the universal weak-coupling slope of the copolymer critical curve).
status_search_result: Universality and existence of the weak-coupling slope $m_\alpha$ was established by Caravenna–Giacomin–Toninelli (2010) and Berger–Caravenna–Poisat–Sun–Zygouras (2014), who proved that $h_c(\lambda)/\lambda$ converges as $\lambda\downarrow 0$ to a constant $m_\alpha$ depending only on $\alpha\in(0,1)$, identified with the critical slope of a continuum copolymer model on the $\alpha$-stable regenerative set. However, the explicit value of $m_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in(0,1)$ is, to current knowledge, not known: the problem has been reduced to a continuum model whose critical slope itself remains to be computed. The case $\alpha=0$ has been treated separately by Berger–Giacomin–Lacoin (2018). No source establishing an exact formula for $m_\alpha$ on $(0,1)$ was found.

original_question: Determine whether every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. Given positive integers $a$ and $b$, the modular numerical semigroup $S(a,b)$ is defined as
$$S(a,b) = \{ x \in \mathbb{N} : a x \bmod b \le x \}.$$
More generally, for positive integers $a,b,c$, the proportionally modular numerical semigroup $S(a,b,c)$ is
$$S(a,b,c) = \{ x \in \mathbb{N} : a x \bmod b \le c x \}.$$
A numerical semigroup $S$ is said to admit a Toms decomposition if it can be expressed as a finite intersection
$$S = \bigcap_{i=1}^{n} S(a_i, b_i, c_i)$$
of proportionally modular numerical semigroups. The Frobenius number of $S$ is $F(S) = \max(\mathbb{N}\setminus S)$, and $S$ is called contracted if $\frac{F(S)+1}{2} \notin S$ (equivalently, $S$ contains no element strictly between $F(S)/2$ and $F(S)$ other than as required, in the sense used for contracted semigroups). 

Question: Is it true that every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition?
status_search_result: The conjecture that every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition (i.e., can be written as a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups) appears in problem lists on numerical semigroups and remains an open conjecture. Algorithms exist to test whether a given numerical semigroup admits such a decomposition, but no general proof or counterexample for the contracted modular case has been published.

self_contained_problem:

Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, with law $\mathbf{P}$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of standard Gaussian random variables (the disorder) with law $\mathbb{P}$, independent of $S$. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ and $h\ge 0$ and length $N\in\mathbb{N}$, define the polymer measure
$$\frac{d\mathbf{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{d\mathbf{P}}(S)=\frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\exp\!\left(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\right),$$

$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$$
exists, is non-negative, and is non-increasing in $h$. The (quenched) critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda)=\inf\{h\ge 0:\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=0\},\qquad \lambda>0,$$

$$m_{1/2}:=\lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0}\frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}$$
exists and satisfies $m_{1/2}\in[2/3,1]$.

$$m_{1/2}>\frac{2}{3}.$$

original_question: Decide whether every system of proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities is equivalent to a system in which all proportions are equal to 1; equivalently, determine whether every numerical semigroup that admits a Toms decomposition can be expressed as an intersection of modular numerical semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
A proportionally modular Diophantine inequality is an expression of the form a x mod b ≤ c x, where a, b, c are positive integers; the set S(a,b,c) = { x ∈ ℕ : a x mod b ≤ c x } is a numerical semigroup, called a proportionally modular numerical semigroup. When c = 1 the inequality is called modular, and the corresponding semigroup S(a,b,1) is called a modular numerical semigroup. A numerical semigroup S is said to admit a Toms decomposition if there exist positive integers q_1,…,q_n, m_1,…,m_n, and L with gcd(q_i, m_i) = gcd(L, m_i) = gcd(L, q_i) = 1 for every i, such that S can be written as a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups arising from this data; equivalently, S is a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups.

Question: Is every finite system of proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities equivalent (i.e., defining the same numerical semigroup as the intersection of solution sets) to a finite system of modular Diophantine inequalities (those with proportion c = 1)? Equivalently, can every numerical semigroup that admits a Toms decomposition be expressed as an intersection of finitely many modular numerical semigroups?

Web search did not surface any subsequent paper announcing a resolution (positive or negative) of the equivalence between systems of proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities and systems with all proportions equal to one. Status appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive confirmation was found.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
original_question: Does there exist some α > 0 for which the weak-coupling critical slope satisfies m_α = 1/(1+α)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of standard Gaussian random variables, independent of $S$. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (coupling) and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ (bias), and for each $N\in\mathbb{N}$, define the copolymer Gibbs measure with quenched disorder $\omega$ by

$$\frac{d\mathbf{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{d\mathbf{P}}(S)=\frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\exp\!\Big(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\Big),$$

with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(S_n)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$ when $S_n=0$, where $\mathbf{P}$ is the law of $S$ and $Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. The quenched free energy is

$$\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\big[\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}\big]\ge 0,$$

and the model exhibits a localization/delocalization transition along a critical curve $h_c(\lambda)=\inf\{h\ge 0:\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)=0\}$, which is known to satisfy $h_c(\lambda)/\lambda\to m\in[1/2,1]$ as $\lambda\downarrow 0$ for some constant $m$ (the weak-coupling critical slope).

More generally, replace the simple random walk by a discrete renewal process whose inter-arrival law has a regularly varying tail with index $1+\alpha$ for $\alpha\in(0,1)$ (so that the return-time distribution satisfies $\mathbf{P}(\tau_1=n)=n^{-(1+\alpha)}L(n)$ for a slowly varying $L$), and define analogously the copolymer free energy and critical curve. It is known that
$$\lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0}\frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}=:m_\alpha\in\Big[\frac{1}{1+\alpha},\,1\Big].$$

Question: Does there exist some $\alpha\in(0,1)$ for which 
$$m_\alpha=\frac{1}{1+\alpha}\,?$$
status_search_result: The weak-coupling slope $m_\alpha$ has been shown by Berger–Caravenna–Poisat–Sun–Zygouras (2014) to coincide with the critical point of a universal continuum copolymer model indexed by an $\alpha$-stable regenerative set, confirming earlier conjectures of Bolthausen–den Hollander–Opoku. However, the explicit value of $m_\alpha$ remains unknown, and there is no published proof that $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$ for any $\alpha\in(0,1)$ nor a proof of strict inequality $m_\alpha>1/(1+\alpha)$ for all $\alpha$. The question therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: Find simple sufficient conditions on a subset X of the positive integers N that guarantee that X is the set of fundamental gaps FG(S) of some numerical semigroup S.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and whose complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ is finite. The elements of $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ are called the gaps of $S$. A positive integer $n$ is a fundamental gap of $S$ if $n \notin S$ but $kn \in S$ for every integer $k \geq 2$; the set of fundamental gaps is denoted $\mathrm{FG}(S)$.

Equivalently, ordering the positive integers by divisibility ($a \preceq b$ iff $a \mid b$), the fundamental gaps are the maximal elements of the set of gaps of $S$. The set $\mathrm{FG}(S)$ uniquely determines $S$, since
$$ S = \mathbb{N} \setminus \{ d \in \mathbb{N} : d \mid x \text{ for some } x \in \mathrm{FG}(S)\}. $$

Problem. Find simple, easily checkable sufficient conditions on a finite subset $X \subseteq \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$ which guarantee the existence of a numerical semigroup $S$ such that $X = \mathrm{FG}(S)$.
status_search_result: A search reveals continued research on fundamental gaps of numerical semigroups (e.g., explicit descriptions for two-generator semigroups, bounds in terms of the Frobenius number, and a 2025 study of numerical semigroups with a fixed fundamental gap), but no simple general sufficient-condition characterization for an arbitrary subset $X \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ to be the fundamental-gap set of some numerical semigroup appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
original_question: For the general copolymer model, the free energy near criticality is known to satisfy F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0 under the stated disorder assumptions. Can this smoothing bound be improved by replacing the exponent 2 with a larger exponent?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the general copolymer model defined as follows. Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a recurrent random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, whose return time to $0$ has a distribution with polynomial tail of exponent $1+\alpha$ for some $\alpha\in(0,1]$ (i.e., $P(\tau_1=n)=n^{-(1+\alpha)}L(n)$ for a slowly varying $L$). Let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of centered, unit-variance random variables with finite exponential moments of all orders, independent of $S$. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ and $h\in\mathbb{R}$, define the quenched partition function
$$Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)=E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\right)\right],$$
with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(S_n)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$ if $S_n=0$. The quenched free energy is
$$F(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\log Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)\right]\ge 0,$$
and the critical curve is $h_c(\lambda)=\inf\{h\ge 0:F(\lambda,h)=0\}$.

It is known that for every $\lambda>0$ there exists a finite constant $c(\lambda)$ such that
$$F(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le (1+\alpha)\,c(\lambda)\,\delta^{2}\qquad\text{for every }\delta>0. \qquad (\star)$$

Question: Can the smoothing bound $(\star)$ be improved by replacing the exponent $2$ with a strictly larger exponent? More precisely, does there exist $\gamma>2$ such that for every $\lambda>0$ one has $F(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le C(\lambda)\,\delta^{\gamma}$ for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Caravenna and den Hollander (2013) sharpened the constant in the smoothing inequality and established asymptotic optimality of the constant in the weak-coupling regime, but kept the quadratic exponent. For the special boundary case $\alpha=0$, Berger–Giacomin–Lacoin (2018) proved the free energy vanishes faster than any power; however, for the general copolymer model with $\alpha\in(0,1]$, no improvement of the exponent $2$ in the smoothing bound appears to have been established, and the question seems to remain open.

original_question: For a given numerical semigroup S, let T range over all numerical semigroups with S = T/2. Find a formula, depending only on S, for the minimum Frobenius number among those doubles T.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ (the gaps of $S$). The Frobenius number $F(S)$ is the largest gap of $S$ (with $F(\mathbb{N})=-1$ by convention).

For numerical semigroups $S$ and $T$, define the quotient
$$T/2 \;=\; \{\, n\in\mathbb{N}\ :\ 2n\in T\,\}.$$
This $T/2$ is again a numerical semigroup. When $T/2=S$, we say that $T$ is a double of $S$. For every numerical semigroup $S$ the set
$$\mathcal{D}(S)\;=\;\{\,T\subseteq\mathbb{N}\ :\ T \text{ is a numerical semigroup with } T/2=S\,\}$$
is nonempty and finite.

Problem. Find a closed-form expression, depending only on invariants of $S$, for
$$\min\{\,F(T)\ :\ T\in\mathcal{D}(S)\,\},$$
the minimum Frobenius number among all doubles of $S$.
status_search_result: A related problem—the minimum genus among doubles of a numerical semigroup $S$—was solved by Strazzanti (arXiv:1512.00638), who proved that for $d$-folds the minimum genus equals $g(S)+\lceil (d-1)F(S)/2\rceil$. However, that work treats only the genus and does not provide a formula for the minimum Frobenius number among doubles. No source located in the search gives such a closed-form formula for $\min\{F(T):T/2=S\}$, so the status of this specific question appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
context_brief: Dependence of critical behavior on α and λ
original_question: How does the critical behavior of the copolymer model depend on the tail exponent α and possibly also on the coupling parameter λ? In particular, determine whether the near-critical behavior is α-dependent, λ-dependent, both, or neither.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the random copolymer model at a selective interface defined as follows. Let $\tau=\{\tau_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}$ with $\tau_0=0$ and inter-arrival law $P(\tau_1=n)=L(n)\,n^{-(1+\alpha)}$ for some slowly varying function $L$ and exponent $\alpha>0$. Let $\omega=\{\omega_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments (the disorder, or charge sequence). For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (coupling strength) and $h\ge 0$ (asymmetry bias), define the polymer measure of length $N$ by
$$\frac{dP_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}}{dP}(\tau) = \frac{1}{Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}}\exp\Big(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\Delta_n\Big)\mathbf{1}_{\{N\in\tau\}},$$
where $\Delta_n\in\{-1,+1\}$ is the sign of the excursion of the underlying walk between consecutive renewal points (interpreted via the standard copolymer construction), and $Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}$ is the partition function. The quenched free energy
$$\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}$$
exists, equals zero in the delocalized phase, and is positive in the localized phase, giving a critical curve $h_c(\lambda)$. Let $\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)$ vanish like $(h_c(\lambda)-h)^{\nu(\alpha,\lambda)}$ (in a suitable sense) as $h\uparrow h_c(\lambda)$, with possible logarithmic corrections.

Determine the dependence of the near-critical behavior of $\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)$ on the tail exponent $\alpha$ and on the coupling parameter $\lambda$. In particular, decide which of the following holds: the critical exponent and near-critical asymptotics are (i) $\alpha$-dependent only, (ii) $\lambda$-dependent only, (iii) dependent on both $\alpha$ and $\lambda$, or (iv) universal (independent of both). Provide the corresponding critical exponent(s) and any logarithmic corrections.
status_search_result: The question of how the near-critical behavior of the random copolymer free energy depends on the tail exponent α (and on the coupling λ) remains largely open. Substantial progress exists for the marginal case α=0 (Berger–Giacomin–Lacoin, 2018, showing infinite-order Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless-type singularity), and various bounds on the slope of the critical curve and on h_c are known for α>0, but a complete determination of the critical exponent and its α/λ dependence is not established.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
context_brief: Inverse correlation length versus free energy
original_question: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) denote the inverse correlation length defined through the exponential decay rate appearing in the model's excursion and correlation estimates. As h approaches the critical point h_c(λ) from below, is log μ(λ,h) asymptotic to log F(λ,h), where F(λ,h) is the free energy?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the copolymer model at a selective interface defined as follows. Let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be a sequence of i.i.d. centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, with law P. For parameters λ ≥ 0 and h ≥ 0 and an integer N ≥ 1, let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} denote a simple random walk on ℤ starting at 0 with law 𝐏, and define the (quenched) partition function

  Z_{N,ω} = 𝐄[ exp( -2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n + h) Δ_n ) ],

where Δ_n = 1 if S_n ≤ 0 (or, more precisely, if the bond (S_{n-1}, S_n) lies in the lower half-plane) and Δ_n = 0 otherwise. The free energy is

  F(λ, h) = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E log Z_{N,ω},

and the inverse correlation length is

  μ(λ, h) = − lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[ (1 + e^{−2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n + h)}) / Z_{N,ω} ].

Both limits exist (P-a.s. and in L¹) for λ > 0, h ≥ 0. There exists a critical curve h_c(λ) > 0 such that F(λ, h) > 0 for h < h_c(λ) (localized phase) and F(λ, h) = 0 for h ≥ h_c(λ) (delocalized phase); similarly μ(λ, h) > 0 in the localized phase and vanishes at h_c(λ).

Question: Fix λ > 0. Is it true that

  log μ(λ, h) ∼ log F(λ, h)   as h ↑ h_c(λ)  ?

That is, does the ratio log μ(λ, h) / log F(λ, h) tend to 1 as h approaches the critical point from below?
status_search_result: The question of comparing the asymptotic behavior of log μ(λ,h) and log F(λ,h) as h approaches the copolymer critical point appears to remain open. Available literature on the copolymer model (e.g., variational characterizations of the free energy, weak-coupling critical curves) addresses the free energy and the critical curve but does not establish such an asymptotic equivalence, and disorder-relevance heuristics suggest the equivalence likely fails. No published proof or disproof was located.

original_question: Let V_T be the Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition. Determine whether V_T is the least Frobenius variety containing all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 2.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a cofinite submonoid S of (N, +) containing 0. The embedding dimension of S is the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators. A nonempty family F of numerical semigroups is called a Frobenius variety if (i) S ∩ T ∈ F whenever S, T ∈ F, and (ii) for every S ∈ F with S ≠ N there exists T ∈ F such that T ⊋ S and T \ S = {F(S)}, where F(S) = max(N \ S) is the Frobenius number of S.

A numerical semigroup S is said to admit a Toms decomposition if there exist numerical semigroups S_1, …, S_n, each of embedding dimension two, such that S = S_1 ∩ … ∩ S_n. Let V_T denote the family of all numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition; it is known that V_T is a Frobenius variety, and that every numerical semigroup of embedding dimension two belongs to V_T.

Question: Is V_T the least Frobenius variety (with respect to inclusion) that contains every numerical semigroup of embedding dimension two? Equivalently, does every Frobenius variety containing all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension two contain V_T?

If (λ,h) lies in the interior of the delocalized region D, is it true that for every ε > 0 the quenched probability P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n in [εN, N] ∩ ℕ) converges to 0 almost surely with respect to the disorder as N → ∞?

Let $S=(S_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $S_0=0$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. For real parameters $\lambda\geq 0$ and $h\geq 0$ and an integer $N\geq 1$, define the quenched copolymer Gibbs measure on random walk paths of length $N$ by
$$\frac{dP_{N,\omega}}{dP}(S) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z_{N,\omega}}\exp\!\left(-2\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\Delta_n\right),$$
where $\Delta_n:=\tfrac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{sign}(S_n))$ is the indicator that the walk lies (weakly) below the interface at step $n$, and $Z_{N,\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. The quenched free energy
$$\textsf{f}(\lambda,h):=\lim_{N\to\infty}\tfrac{1}{N}\log Z_{N,\omega}$$
exists and is $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. constant. The delocalized region is
$$\mathcal{D}:=\{(\lambda,h):\textsf{f}(\lambda,h)=\lambda h\},$$
and $\mathring{\mathcal{D}}$ denotes its interior in $[0,\infty)^2$.

Question: Is it true that for every $(\lambda,h)\in\mathring{\mathcal{D}}$ and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,

context_brief: Level growth in infinite Frobenius varieties
original_question: For an infinite Frobenius variety V, let G(V) be the directed tree whose vertices are semigroups in V and whose levels are measured by distance from the root N. Determine whether, for every n, the (n + 1)-st level of G(V) contains more vertices than the n-th level.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A numerical semigroup is a submonoid $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ (containing $0$, closed under addition) whose complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ is finite. A (Frobenius) variety is a nonempty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups such that:
(i) if $S, T \in \mathcal{V}$ then $S \cap T \in \mathcal{V}$, and
(ii) if $S \in \mathcal{V}$ and $S \neq \mathbb{N}$, then $S \cup \{F(S)\} \in \mathcal{V}$, where $F(S) = \max(\mathbb{N}\setminus S)$ is the Frobenius number of $S$.

The variety $\mathcal{V}$ is called infinite if it contains infinitely many numerical semigroups.

Associated with $\mathcal{V}$ is a rooted directed tree $G(\mathcal{V})$: the vertex set is $\mathcal{V}$, the root is $\mathbb{N}$, and there is a directed edge from $S$ to $T$ whenever $T = S \cup \{F(S)\}$ (so $T$ is the parent of $S$). For $n \geq 0$, the $n$-th level of $G(\mathcal{V})$ is the set of vertices at directed distance $n$ from the root $\mathbb{N}$, and let $\ell_n(\mathcal{V})$ denote its cardinality.

Question: Is it true that for every infinite Frobenius variety $\mathcal{V}$ and every integer $n \geq 0$,
$$\ell_{n+1}(\mathcal{V}) > \ell_n(\mathcal{V})?$$
status_search_result: The analogous level-growth question for the full tree of numerical semigroups (the finite-Frobenius-variety case being trivial) is a longstanding open problem. Recent work on infinite chains in the semigroup tree (e.g., arXiv:2308.09500) and on Frobenius restricted/R-varieties (Semigroup Forum, 2018) treats related structural questions but does not resolve the strict-growth conjecture for arbitrary infinite Frobenius varieties. No source found establishing or refuting it.

paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
original_question: Can more precise measurements of the branching ratio for the purely leptonic decay B+ → τ+ντ resolve the tension between the experimental average (1.64 ± 0.34) × 10−4 and indirect CKM global-fit determinations, where CKMfitter places the indirect determination 2.6 standard deviations from the experimental value and UTfit places it 3.2 standard deviations away?
self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the purely leptonic decay of the charged B meson, B+ → τ+ ν_τ, has a branching ratio that can be predicted from the CKM matrix element |V_ub|, the B-meson decay constant f_B, the B-meson mass and lifetime, and the τ mass via the formula

  BR(B+ → τ+ ν_τ) = (G_F^2 m_B m_τ^2 / 8π) (1 − m_τ^2/m_B^2)^2 f_B^2 |V_ub|^2 τ_B.

A global unitarity-triangle fit (using inputs such as |V_ub| from semileptonic decays, ε_K, Δm_d, Δm_s, sin 2β, and the angles α and γ) yields an indirect Standard-Model prediction for this branching ratio. The current experimental world average is

  BR_exp(B+ → τ+ ν_τ) = (1.64 ± 0.34) × 10^{−4},

while the indirect global-fit determinations differ from this experimental value by 2.6σ (CKMfitter) and 3.2σ (UTfit).

Question: Determine whether sufficiently precise future experimental measurements of BR(B+ → τ+ ν_τ), combined with improved theoretical inputs (in particular f_B and |V_ub|), can resolve this tension within the Standard Model, or whether the discrepancy persists and signals new physics beyond the Standard Model (for example, a charged-Higgs contribution that modifies the leptonic decay amplitude).
status_search_result: The tension has substantially evolved since the question was posed. Updated Belle and BaBar measurements using hadronic and semileptonic tagging have lowered the experimental world average of BR(B+ → τ+ ν_τ) toward the Standard-Model expectation, and current CKMfitter/UTfit global fits report a much reduced discrepancy (typically below 2σ). The question is therefore partially resolved: no significant tension currently persists, but the precision is still limited and Belle II (with ~5% target precision) and FCC-ee projections are required to make a definitive statement.

original_question: Characterize those Frobenius varieties whose associated trees satisfy the Bras-Amoros-type growth property that each level has more vertices than the preceding level.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A numerical semigroup is a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement $\mathbb{N}_0\setminus S$. The cardinality $g(S)=|\mathbb{N}_0\setminus S|$ is the genus of $S$, and the largest integer not in $S$ is the Frobenius number $F(S)$.

A nonempty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups is called a Frobenius variety if:
(i) $S,T\in\mathcal{V}\Rightarrow S\cap T\in\mathcal{V}$, and
(ii) for every $S\in\mathcal{V}$ with $S\neq\mathbb{N}_0$, one has $S\cup\{F(S)\}\in\mathcal{V}$.

For a Frobenius variety $\mathcal{V}$, the associated tree $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{V})$ has the elements of $\mathcal{V}$ as vertices, with $\mathbb{N}_0$ as the root, and an edge between $S$ and $S\cup\{F(S)\}$ whenever $S\in\mathcal{V}\setminus\{\mathbb{N}_0\}$. The level of a vertex $S\in\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{V})$ equals its genus $g(S)$, and the $n$-th level set is
$$\mathcal{V}_n=\{S\in\mathcal{V}:g(S)=n\}.$$

Say that $\mathcal{V}$ has the Bras-Amorós growth property if
$$|\mathcal{V}_{n+1}|>|\mathcal{V}_n|\qquad\text{for every }n\geq 0,$$
the analogue, restricted to $\mathcal{V}$, of the Bras-Amorós conjecture concerning the strict growth of the number of numerical semigroups by genus.

Problem. Give an explicit characterization of the Frobenius varieties $\mathcal{V}$ for which $|\mathcal{V}_{n+1}|>|\mathcal{V}_n|$ holds for all $n\geq 0$.
status_search_result: The Bras-Amorós conjecture about strict growth of the count of numerical semigroups by genus is widely cited as still open. Subsequent literature on Frobenius varieties, pseudo-varieties, and Frobenius-restricted varieties studies their tree structure but does not give a general characterization of those Frobenius varieties whose level sequences are strictly increasing. No source found resolving this generalized question.

paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
original_question: Using purely leptonic B+ → ℓ+νℓ decays, where ℓ is a charged lepton and charged-Higgs effects in two-Higgs-doublet or supersymmetric scenarios can modify the Standard Model branching ratio through the parameters tanβ and charged-Higgs mass MH, how much of the tanβ–MH parameter plane can future SuperB measurements of B+ → τ+ντ and B+ → μ+νμ exclude with 75 ab−1 of data?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the purely leptonic decays B+ → ℓ+ν_ℓ (ℓ ∈ {μ, τ}) of a charged B meson. In the Standard Model the branching ratio is

  BR_SM(B+ → ℓ+ν_ℓ) = (G_F^2 m_B m_ℓ^2 / 8π) (1 − m_ℓ^2/m_B^2)^2 f_B^2 |V_ub|^2 τ_B,

where G_F is the Fermi constant, m_B and m_ℓ are the meson and lepton masses, f_B is the B-meson decay constant, V_ub is the relevant CKM element, and τ_B is the B+ lifetime.

In a type-II two-Higgs-doublet model (or in supersymmetric extensions sharing the same tree-level structure), exchange of a charged Higgs boson modifies this rate by a multiplicative factor depending on tan β (the ratio of the two Higgs vacuum expectation values) and the charged-Higgs mass M_H:

  BR(B+ → ℓ+ν_ℓ) = BR_SM · r_H,  with  r_H = (1 − tan^2 β · m_B^2 / M_H^2)^2.

Suppose a future high-luminosity B-factory program collects an integrated luminosity of 75 ab^(-1) and measures the branching ratios of B+ → τ+ν_τ and B+ → μ+ν_μ with their projected statistical and systematic uncertainties using both hadronic and semileptonic tagging methods. Determine, as a quantitative region in the (tan β, M_H) plane, the portion of parameter space that can be excluded at 95% confidence level by combining these two measurements assuming agreement with the Standard Model expectation, and identify the resulting lower bound on M_H as a function of tan β (and equivalently the upper bound on tan β / M_H).

Belle II is now the operating successor, with a target of about 50 ab^(-1); current Belle II analyses of B+ → τ+ν_τ and B+ → μ+ν_μ continue to constrain the (tan β, M_H) plane but the specific 75 ab^(-1) SuperB exclusion remains an unrealized projection rather than a settled mathematical theorem.

original_question: Characterize those Frobenius varieties V for which every S in V satisfies the generalized Wilf inequality e_V(S)g(S) <= (e_V(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where e_V(S) denotes the cardinality of the unique minimal V-system of generators of S.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a cofinite submonoid S of (N, +) (with 0 ∈ S). For such an S, let g(S) = #(N \ S) be its genus, F(S) = max(Z \ S) its Frobenius number, and e(S) the cardinality of its (unique) minimal system of generators (the embedding dimension). Wilf's classical conjecture asserts e(S) g(S) ≤ (e(S) − 1)(F(S) + 1) for every numerical semigroup S.

A Frobenius variety V is a nonempty family of numerical semigroups satisfying:
(i) if S, T ∈ V, then S ∩ T ∈ V;
(ii) if S ∈ V and S ≠ N, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ V.
Within such a variety, every S ∈ V admits a unique minimal V-system of generators, whose cardinality is denoted e_V(S).

Problem: Characterize all Frobenius varieties V with the property that, for every S ∈ V,
   e_V(S) · g(S) ≤ (e_V(S) − 1) · (F(S) + 1).
status_search_result: Wilf's classical conjecture for numerical semigroups remains open in general, with only partial results (e.g., symmetric, pseudo-symmetric semigroups, low embedding dimension, and recently preservation under gluing). The generalization to Frobenius varieties asks for a full characterization, and no such characterization appears in the literature; the question is still open.

original_question: Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the symmetric numerical semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ (whose elements are called the gaps of $S$). The largest gap of $S$ is its Frobenius number $F(S)$. A numerical semigroup $S \neq \mathbb{N}$ is called symmetric if for every integer $z$ exactly one of $z \in S$ or $F(S) - z \in S$ holds; equivalently, $S$ is irreducible with $F(S)$ odd.

A nonempty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups is called a Frobenius variety if it satisfies:
(i) if $S, T \in \mathcal{V}$, then $S \cap T \in \mathcal{V}$;
(ii) if $S \in \mathcal{V}$ and $S \neq \mathbb{N}$, then $S \cup \{F(S)\} \in \mathcal{V}$.

The intersection of an arbitrary family of Frobenius varieties is a Frobenius variety, so for any family $\mathcal{F}$ of numerical semigroups there is a smallest Frobenius variety containing $\mathcal{F}$, called the Frobenius variety generated by $\mathcal{F}$.

Problem: Explicitly describe the Frobenius variety generated by the family of all symmetric numerical semigroups; that is, characterize the numerical semigroups belonging to this variety.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as a research question in the numerical semigroups community. Related works on Frobenius pseudo-varieties, modular Frobenius pseudo-varieties, and Frobenius restricted (R-)varieties have appeared, but no source clearly identifies an explicit characterization of the Frobenius variety generated solely by the symmetric numerical semigroups, so the current status is unclear.

paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
original_question: Which SuperB detector configuration best improves searches for leptonic B+ → ℓ+νℓ decays by increasing signal efficiency and suppressing background, considering the reduced boost from βγ = 0.56 to 0.28, a forward particle-identification device for K/π separation in the 17°–25° polar-angle region, and a backward electromagnetic calorimeter veto in the 152°–167° polar-angle region?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a high-luminosity e+e- collider experiment operating at the Υ(4S) resonance, designed to study the rare leptonic decay B+ → ℓ+ν_ℓ (ℓ = e, μ, τ). The baseline detector is similar to a BaBar-style geometry but with the center-of-mass boost reduced from βγ = 0.56 to βγ = 0.28, which enlarges the geometric acceptance. Two optional sub-detectors are under consideration:

(i) a forward particle-identification device (Fwd-PID) covering the polar-angle range 17°–25°, providing K/π separation that improves tag-side kaon identification;
(ii) a backward electromagnetic calorimeter (Bwd-EMC) covering the polar-angle range 152°–167°, providing additional photon/energy veto capability.

Empirically determined per-component effects on the analysis of B+ → ℓ+ν_ℓ are:
- Reduced boost (βγ = 0.28 vs 0.56): signal efficiency multiplied by 1.07; background multiplied by 0.94.
- Fwd-PID inclusion: signal efficiency multiplied by 1.025; background multiplied by 1.025.
- Bwd-EMC inclusion: signal efficiency unchanged; background multiplied by 0.90.

Assuming the three modifications act independently and that the figure of merit for sensitivity to a rare branching fraction is S/√B (where S is signal yield ∝ signal efficiency and B is background yield), determine which of the eight possible configurations (each option on/off) maximizes S/√B, and compute the resulting multiplicative improvement factor relative to the baseline (βγ = 0.56, no Fwd-PID, no Bwd-EMC).
status_search_result: The question concerns a then-future SuperB detector-optimization study. The SuperB project at Tor Vergata was cancelled in late 2012 before construction, so the specific configuration was never finalized in operation. No definitive published "best configuration" answer based on the full optimization is identified; the listed per-component impacts (≈7% signal gain from boost, ≈2.5% from Fwd-PID, ≈10% background reduction from Bwd-EMC) are the partial findings reported. original_question: Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ (the gaps of $S$). The largest gap is called the Frobenius number $F(S)$. A numerical semigroup $S$ is pseudo-symmetric if $F(S)$ is even and, for every integer $x \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{F(S)/2\}$, one has $x \in S$ if and only if $F(S) - x \notin S$.

A Frobenius variety is a non-empty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups satisfying:
(i) if $S, T \in \mathcal{V}$, then $S \cap T \in \mathcal{V}$; and
(ii) if $S \in \mathcal{V}$ and $S \neq \mathbb{N}$, then $S \cup \{F(S)\} \in \mathcal{V}$.

The intersection of any family of Frobenius varieties is again a Frobenius variety, so given any set $\mathcal{F}$ of numerical semigroups there is a smallest Frobenius variety $\mathrm{Var}(\mathcal{F})$ containing $\mathcal{F}$, called the Frobenius variety generated by $\mathcal{F}$.

Problem: Give an explicit description (intrinsic membership characterization) of the Frobenius variety generated by the family of all pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups.
