context_brief: best constant in one-dimensional star-discrepancy lower bounds
original_question: Let c be the largest constant such that every one-dimensional sequence (x_n)_{n>=0} in [0,1) satisfies the star-discrepancy lower bound D_N^* >= c log N / N for infinitely many N. Can one improve the currently known bounds 0.06015... <= c <= 0.222...?
self_contained_problem:
For a sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 0}$ of points in $[0,1)$, define the star-discrepancy of its first $N$ terms by
$$D_N^*((x_n)) \;=\; \sup_{0<\alpha\le 1} \left| \frac{\#\{0\le n<N : x_n<\alpha\}}{N} - \alpha \right|.$$
Let $c$ be the largest real constant such that, for every sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in $[0,1)$, the inequality
$$D_N^*((x_n)) \;\ge\; c\,\frac{\log N}{N}$$
holds for infinitely many positive integers $N$. It is known that $0.06015\ldots \le c \le 0.222\ldots$. Improve either the lower bound or the upper bound (and ideally determine the exact value of $c$).
status_search_result: The problem of determining the best constant $c$ in the one-dimensional star-discrepancy lower bound $D_N^* \ge c\log N/N$ remains open. The known bounds (Larcher–type lower bound around $0.06$ and Ostromoukhov-type upper bound around $0.2223$) have not been substantially improved; recent work on greedy and low-discrepancy constructions still operates within this gap.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: How can the BBGKY hierarchy for a time-dependent many-fermion system be truncated by reconstructing the next-higher reduced density matrix as a practical functional of lower-order reduced density matrices, especially by approximating the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3) in terms of the one-body reduced density matrix γ and the two-body reduced density matrix Γ, so that one- and two-body observables can be propagated without solving the full hierarchy?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a non-relativistic quantum system of N identical fermions evolving under a Hamiltonian of the form H = sum_i h(i) + (1/2) sum_{i != j} v(i,j), where h is a one-body operator and v is a two-body interaction. For a (possibly mixed) time-dependent N-body state with density operator D(t), define the p-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by

  Γ^(p)(x_1,...,x_p; x'_1,...,x'_p; t) = (N!/(N-p)!) Tr_{p+1,...,N} D(t),

and write γ = Γ^(1) and Γ = Γ^(2). The exact equations of motion form the BBGKY hierarchy, in which the time evolution of Γ^(p) couples to Γ^(p+1); in particular,

  i ∂_t Γ = [h(1)+h(2)+v(1,2), Γ] + Tr_3 [v(1,3)+v(2,3), Γ^(3)].

Problem. Construct an explicit, practical, antisymmetry-preserving and Hermiticity-preserving closure functional

  Γ^(3)[γ, Γ]

that reconstructs the three-body RDM as a functional of γ and Γ alone, such that the resulting closed coupled system of evolution equations for (γ(t), Γ(t)):
  (i) preserves N-representability of γ and Γ along the flow,
  (ii) conserves total energy, total particle number, and is time-reversible,
  (iii) reduces to the known exact limits (e.g., uncorrelated/Hartree–Fock, weak-coupling perturbative, and small-correlation regimes),
  (iv) yields propagated one- and two-body observables that approximate those of the exact N-body dynamics with controlled error,
without requiring solution of the full hierarchy.

Does such a functional Γ^(3)[γ, Γ] exist, and if so, give an explicit construction; otherwise, characterize the obstructions to its existence.
status_search_result: The problem of finding a practical, exact functional reconstruction of Γ^(3) in terms of γ and Γ remains open. Existing approaches (TDDM antisymmetrized-product closures, cumulant reconstructions in TD2RDM, and energy-conserving/time-reversible truncations proposed since 2016) provide approximations but no general scheme satisfying all desired properties (N-representability, conservation laws, controlled accuracy). Recent works (2020–2025) continue to propose new closures, indicating the question is still actively investigated.

context_brief: lower bounds for two-dimensional digital base-2 sequences
original_question: Can one show that every two-dimensional digital sequence in base 2 satisfies the lower discrepancy bound D_N >= c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N, or at least prove this for a substantial class such as NUT sequences or finite-row sequences?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For an infinite sequence $\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_2,\ldots$ in the unit square $[0,1)^2$, let
$$D_N(\mathbf{x}) \;=\; \sup_{B}\left|\frac{\#\{1\le n\le N:\mathbf{x}_n\in B\}}{N} - \lambda(B)\right|,$$
where the supremum runs over all axis-aligned boxes $B=[0,a_1)\times[0,a_2)\subset[0,1)^2$ and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure. This is the star discrepancy of the first $N$ terms.

A two-dimensional digital sequence in base $2$ is constructed as follows. Choose two infinite matrices $C^{(1)},C^{(2)}\in\mathbb{F}_2^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$ (called generating matrices). For an integer $n\ge 0$ with binary expansion $n=\sum_{r\ge 0} a_r(n)\,2^r$, $a_r(n)\in\{0,1\}$, define the $j$-th coordinate of the $n$-th term by
$$x_n^{(j)} \;=\; \sum_{i\ge 1} \frac{y_{n,i}^{(j)}}{2^{i}}, \qquad y_{n,i}^{(j)} \;=\; \sum_{r\ge 0} C^{(j)}_{i,r+1}\, a_r(n) \pmod 2,$$
provided each coordinate is well defined (all column sums are finite). The sequence $(\mathbf{x}_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in $[0,1)^2$ thus produced is called a two-dimensional digital sequence in base $2$.

Two important subclasses are:
\begin{itemize}
\item NUT (non-singular upper triangular) digital sequences: each $C^{(j)}$ is upper triangular with non-zero diagonal entries.
\item Finite-row digital sequences: every row of each $C^{(j)}$ has only finitely many non-zero entries.
\end{itemize}

It is known that any such sequence can satisfy $D_N \le c'(\log N)^2/N$ for all $N\ge 2$, and a corresponding lower bound of order $(\log N)^2/N$ infinitely often is conjectured but not proved.

Problem. Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every two-dimensional digital sequence $(\mathbf{x}_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in base $2$ one has
$$D_N(\mathbf{x}) \;\ge\; c\,\frac{(\log N)^2}{N} \qquad \text{for infinitely many } N\in\mathbb{N}.$$
Or, failing the general statement, establish the same lower bound for the restricted class of NUT digital sequences, or for the class of finite-row digital sequences in base $2$.

The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: lower bounds for the two-dimensional Halton sequence
original_question: Can one obtain a better lower bound for the discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence, and ideally determine whether its true order is (log N)^2 / N or not?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer N ≥ 1 and a finite sequence of points x_1, …, x_N in the unit square [0,1)^2, define the star discrepancy
  D*_N = sup_{B} | #{1 ≤ n ≤ N : x_n ∈ B}/N − λ(B) |,
where the supremum is taken over all axis-aligned boxes B = [0,a_1) × [0,a_2) ⊂ [0,1)^2 and λ denotes the Lebesgue measure.

The two-dimensional Halton sequence (with bases 2 and 3) is the sequence (x_n)_{n ≥ 1} ⊂ [0,1)^2 defined by x_n = (φ_2(n), φ_3(n)), where for a prime p the radical-inverse function φ_p is given by
  φ_p(n) = Σ_{k ≥ 0} a_k p^{−k−1}   when   n = Σ_{k ≥ 0} a_k p^k,   a_k ∈ {0,1,…,p−1}.

It is known that the star discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence satisfies D*_N = O((log N)^2 / N).

Problem: Prove an improved lower bound for the star discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence. In particular, decide whether
  limsup_{N → ∞}  N · D*_N / (log N)^2  >  0,
i.e. whether the true order of magnitude of the star discrepancy of this sequence is exactly (log N)^2 / N.
status_search_result: M. B. Levin proved exact lower bounds for the star discrepancy of Halton's sequence, establishing in particular that limsup N (log N)^{-s} D*_N > 0 for the s-dimensional Halton sequence. For s = 2 this matches the known O((log N)^2/N) upper bound, so the true order of the discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence is (log N)^2/N. A survey of Levin's proofs (Kritzer, 2017) confirms these as exact lower discrepancy bounds. The problem therefore appears to be solved.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: How can closure approximations for time-dependent one- and two-body reduced density matrices be designed so that the propagated density matrices remain positive semidefinite and also satisfy fermionic occupation constraints, meaning natural orbital occupation numbers stay between zero and one, while avoiding unphysical negative local densities or divergent densities during electron dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-electron quantum system whose state is described by a sequence of reduced density matrices (RDMs). For p = 1, 2, the p-body reduced density matrix γ_p(t) is the trace over N − p particles of the full N-fermion density operator, regarded as a self-adjoint operator on the antisymmetric p-particle Hilbert space. The exact time evolution of {γ_p}_{p=1,...,N} is governed by the BBGKY hierarchy

  i ∂_t γ_p(t) = [H_p, γ_p(t)] + Tr_{p+1}[V_{p,p+1}, γ_{p+1}(t)],

which couples γ_p to γ_{p+1}. A "closure" at the two-body level is any prescription γ_3 ≈ Φ[γ_1, γ_2] that produces a closed system of evolution equations for (γ_1(t), γ_2(t)).

Required physical constraints to be preserved for all t ≥ 0 along the closed evolution:

(i) Positive semidefiniteness: γ_1(t) ⪰ 0 and γ_2(t) ⪰ 0 as operators.
(ii) Fermionic occupation bounds: every eigenvalue n_i(t) of γ_1(t) (the natural occupation number) satisfies 0 ≤ n_i(t) ≤ 1.
(iii) Physical local densities: the diagonal ρ(x,t) := γ_1(x,x;t) remains nonnegative and finite (no negative or divergent local densities) throughout the dynamics.
(iv) Consistency between γ_1 and γ_2: γ_1(t) = (N − 1)^{-1} Tr_2 γ_2(t) and the appropriate trace normalization is preserved.

Problem. Construct a nontrivial closure functional Φ[γ_1, γ_2] (going beyond the trivial mean-field/Hartree–Fock factorization) such that the resulting closed evolution equations for (γ_1(t), γ_2(t)) provably preserve conditions (i)–(iv) for arbitrary admissible initial data and for general one- and two-body Hamiltonian terms describing electron dynamics. Equivalently, identify structural conditions on Φ that are sufficient to guarantee these preservation properties, or prove that no such closure exists within a specified class.
status_search_result: No closure approximation for the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy at the 1- and 2-RDM level is known to provably preserve positive semidefiniteness together with the fermionic occupation-number bounds 0 ≤ n_i ≤ 1 and nonnegative local densities throughout electron dynamics. Recent literature on N-representability and 2-RDM methods (variational SDP-based ground-state methods, machine-learning approaches, and contracted Schrödinger-equation methods) addresses related representability constraints but does not provide a general dynamical closure with these guarantees, indicating the problem remains open.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Mechanism of divergence under conserved global quantities
original_question: Why can sophisticated truncation approximations for the coupled BBGKY equations, including approximations motivated by Green's-function expansions, fail to obey fundamental physical constraints and lead to divergence of reduced-density-matrix dynamics even when the total particle number and total energy are conserved?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a nonrelativistic many-body quantum system of N identical fermions (or bosons) governed by a Hamiltonian H = T + V, where T is a one-body kinetic operator and V is a two-body interaction. Define the reduced p-particle density matrices (p-RDM) ρ_p(t) by partial trace of the full density operator ρ(t) = e^{-iHt/ħ} ρ(0) e^{iHt/ħ} over N − p particles. The time-dependent BBGKY-type hierarchy for the {ρ_p} couples ρ_p to ρ_{p+1}, and any practical numerical scheme must close this hierarchy by approximating ρ_{p+1} as a functional of {ρ_1, …, ρ_p}. Standard closures include cluster (cumulant) expansions and closures motivated by nonequilibrium Green's-function (Φ-derivable / conserving) approximations such as Hartree–Fock, second Born, GW, and T-matrix approximations.

Empirically, when one integrates the resulting truncated equations of motion forward in time, the dynamics may exhibit unphysical behavior including loss of N-representability of ρ_1 (eigenvalues escaping the interval [0,1] for fermions), violation of positivity or trace conditions on ρ_p, and finite-time blow-up of matrix elements, despite the fact that the truncated equations exactly preserve the total particle number Tr ρ_1(t) = N and the total energy E(t) = Tr(T ρ_1(t)) + (1/2) Tr(V ρ_2(t)).

Problem. Identify and rigorously characterize the mathematical mechanism by which truncated BBGKY closures — in particular those derived from Green's-function-based conserving approximations — can produce solutions that violate N-representability and/or diverge in finite time, even when the closure manifestly conserves total particle number and total energy. Specifically:

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient structural conditions on a closure functional ρ_{p+1} = F[ρ_1,…,ρ_p] under which the resulting truncated hierarchy preserves the cone of N-representable reduced density matrices for all t ≥ 0.

(b) Show whether any closure that is conserving (in the Baym–Kadanoff sense) and that exactly conserves N and E necessarily preserves N-representability, or exhibit an explicit obstruction proving it need not.

(c) Explain why the divergence observed in numerical simulations is independent of the initial state (provided ρ(0) is a valid N-representable density matrix) and must be attributed to the structure of the approximated equations themselves.
status_search_result: The question of how to truncate the BBGKY / time-dependent reduced-density-matrix hierarchy in a way that simultaneously conserves particle number and energy and preserves N-representability remains an active and unresolved problem in nonequilibrium many-body theory. Subsequent work by Lackner, Brezinová, Kreibich, Stefanucci, Bonitz, and others has identified purity/contraction violations and finite-time instabilities in standard cumulant and Green's-function-based closures, and has proposed partial remedies (e.g., purification schemes, contraction-consistent closures), but no general structural characterization that rules out divergence under conservation of N and E has been established.

original_question: In a two-queue polling system with cyclic service, where arrivals to both queues are independent Poisson processes, service times and switch-over times are independent, and the first queue uses gated service while the second queue uses 1-limited service, determine the joint probability generating function of the steady-state queue-length vector at polling instants. Equivalently, determine the joint queue-length PGFs F1(z1, z2) and F2(z1, z2) for this G/1-L polling system.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a polling system with a single server and two queues $Q_1, Q_2$ operating in continuous time. Customers arrive at $Q_i$ according to a Poisson process with rate $\lambda_i > 0$, $i = 1, 2$, and the two arrival processes are independent. Service times at $Q_i$ are i.i.d. with distribution $B_i$ (Laplace–Stieltjes transform $\beta_i$ and finite mean), independent across queues and of the arrival processes. The server visits the queues in cyclic order $Q_1, Q_2, Q_1, Q_2, \ldots$ . Between a visit to $Q_i$ and the next visit to $Q_{i+1 \bmod 2}$, the server incurs an i.i.d. switch-over time with distribution $S_i$ (LST $\sigma_i$, finite mean), independent of everything else.

The service disciplines are mixed:
- $Q_1$ uses the gated discipline: upon arrival of the server at $Q_1$, exactly those customers present at that polling instant are served, while customers arriving during the visit are deferred to the next cycle.
- $Q_2$ uses the 1-limited discipline: at each visit to $Q_2$, the server serves exactly one customer if $Q_2$ is non-empty, and otherwise leaves immediately.

Assume the system is stable. Let $(X_1^{(i)}, X_2^{(i)})$ denote the steady-state vector of queue lengths at the polling instant of $Q_i$ ($i = 1, 2$), and define the joint probability generating functions
$$F_i(z_1, z_2) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[ z_1^{X_1^{(i)}} z_2^{X_2^{(i)}} \right], \qquad |z_1|, |z_2| \le 1, \quad i = 1, 2.$$

Determine $F_1(z_1, z_2)$ and $F_2(z_1, z_2)$ in closed form (or as the explicit solution of a tractable functional/boundary value problem) for this two-queue gated/1-limited polling system with general service and switch-over time distributions.
status_search_result: The problem is identified as an open problem in the polling-systems literature: while the joint queue-length PGF is known for two queues both under 1-limited (via boundary-value-problem techniques) and for branching-type disciplines (gated, exhaustive), the mixed gated/1-limited case does not satisfy the branching property and has not been resolved. No published solution was located in the search.

context_brief: Renewal arrivals with large deterministic switch-overs
original_question: Consider a cyclic polling system with a fixed cyclic order of N queues and general renewal arrival processes at the queues. When the switch-over times are deterministic and all deterministic switch-over times grow without bound while their ratios remain fixed, provide a rigorous proof that the system converges to a deterministic cyclic system.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a cyclic polling system with $N \geq 2$ queues $Q_1, \dots, Q_N$ served by a single server that visits the queues in the fixed cyclic order $Q_1 \to Q_2 \to \cdots \to Q_N \to Q_1 \to \cdots$. Customers arrive at $Q_i$ according to an independent renewal process with finite mean inter-arrival time $1/\lambda_i$ and a generally distributed service requirement with finite mean. The server uses a fixed work-conserving service discipline (e.g. exhaustive or gated) at each queue. Between completing service at $Q_i$ and starting service at $Q_{i+1}$, the server incurs a deterministic switch-over time $s_i > 0$. Assume the system is stable, i.e. $\rho := \sum_{i=1}^N \lambda_i \mathbb{E}[B_i] < 1$, where $B_i$ is the service time at $Q_i$.

Fix positive constants $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_N$ with $\sum_i \alpha_i = 1$, and consider the family of systems indexed by $S > 0$ in which the switch-over times are $s_i = s_i(S) = \alpha_i S$. Let the corresponding stationary cycle behavior (e.g. the joint distribution of cycle lengths, visit times, and queue lengths at polling instants, suitably normalized by $S$) be denoted $\mathcal{P}(S)$.

Prove rigorously that as $S \to \infty$, $\mathcal{P}(S)$ converges (in an appropriate distributional sense) to the behavior of the corresponding "deterministic cyclic system" — namely the limiting cyclic system in which inter-arrival times act as their means and all randomness in the polling dynamics vanishes, yielding a deterministic periodic schedule of visit times, cycle lengths, and workload trajectories determined solely by the means $1/\lambda_i$, $\mathbb{E}[B_i]$, and the ratios $\alpha_i$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem (a conjecture asking for a rigorous proof) in the polling systems literature. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent paper providing a rigorous proof of this convergence result for general renewal arrivals as deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: Can a variational or related time-propagation method impose positive semidefiniteness on the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3), and on the resulting one- and two-body reduced density matrices γ and Γ, despite the fact that approximate truncation can break the trace relations connecting these density matrices?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of N identical fermions evolving under a time-dependent many-body Hamiltonian. For each time t, let Γ^{(p)}(t) denote the p-body reduced density matrix (p-RDM), defined as the partial trace over N−p particles of the full N-body density operator, with normalization Tr Γ^{(p)} = N!/(N−p)!. Write γ := Γ^{(1)} and Γ := Γ^{(2)}. The time evolutions of γ, Γ, and Γ^{(3)} are linked by the BBGKY-type hierarchy, in which the equation of motion for Γ^{(p)} depends on Γ^{(p+1)}. Truncating this hierarchy at the three-body level requires approximating Γ^{(3)} as a functional of γ and Γ; such approximations generically break the exact contraction (trace) identities

  Tr_{p+1} Γ^{(p+1)} = (N−p) Γ^{(p)},

so that even if the approximate Γ^{(3)} is positive semidefinite, the propagated γ and Γ need not be.

Problem. Devise a variational (or otherwise constrained) time-propagation scheme for the truncated BBGKY hierarchy at the three-body level which, for all t ≥ 0, maintains simultaneously:

 (i) Γ^{(3)}(t) ⪰ 0,
 (ii) Γ(t) ⪰ 0, and
 (iii) γ(t) ⪰ 0,

despite the fact that the contraction identities relating Γ^{(3)}, Γ, and γ may fail under the chosen truncation. Equivalently, determine whether positive semidefiniteness of all three reduced density matrices can be enforced as a dynamical constraint along the evolution, and exhibit such a method, or prove that no such scheme can exist within a specified class of approximations.
category_tag: Reduced density matrices and BBGKY hierarchy
status_search_result: Subsequent work on time-dependent 2RDM methods has addressed the positive-semidefiniteness/N-representability issue partially via purification schemes (e.g., projective purification of correlated RDMs and TD2RDM stabilization), which restore N-representability of the 2RDM in many regimes. However, a fully variational time-propagation method that simultaneously enforces positive semidefiniteness of Γ^{(3)}, Γ, and γ under generic three-body truncations does not appear to be definitively established; the issue remains an active research direction.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: How should the residual three-body correlation term Δ(3) in the cluster or cumulant expansion of the three-body reduced density matrix be approximated, beyond the three-body collision-integral-free, three-body noninteracting, and Wang-Cassing-style truncations, to obtain a more reliable BBGKY closure?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of identical fermions described by the time-dependent reduced density matrices (RDMs) γ^{(k)} of order k = 1, 2, 3, …, satisfying the BBGKY hierarchy. Introduce the cumulant (cluster) expansion of the two- and three-body RDMs:

  Γ^{(2)} = A[γ ⊗ γ] + Δ^{(2)},
  Γ^{(3)} = S[γ ⊗ γ ⊗ γ] + A[γ ⊗ Δ^{(2)}] + Δ^{(3)},

where A and S denote the appropriate antisymmetrization/symmetrization operators acting on tensor products, Δ^{(2)} is the genuine two-body correlation function, and Δ^{(3)} is the residual (irreducible) three-body correlation function.

To close the BBGKY hierarchy at the level of γ and Δ^{(2)}, one must specify Δ^{(3)} as a functional of the lower-order objects (γ, Δ^{(2)}). Three standard truncations are:

 (i) the three-body collision-integral-free closure, in which the contribution of Δ^{(3)} to the equation of motion of Γ^{(2)} is set to zero;
 (ii) the three-body noninteracting closure, in which Δ^{(3)} ≡ 0;
 (iii) the Wang–Cassing-style closure, in which Δ^{(3)} is approximated by a specific antisymmetrized product structure built from γ and Δ^{(2)}.

Problem. Construct an approximation Δ^{(3)} ≈ F[γ, Δ^{(2)}] which goes beyond (i)–(iii), is consistent with the symmetry, trace, hermiticity, and contraction (sum-rule) properties required of a three-body cumulant, preserves conservation of energy, momentum, particle number, and (where applicable) total spin under the resulting closed equations of motion for (γ, Δ^{(2)}), and yields a more reliable closure of the BBGKY hierarchy than (i)–(iii) for time-dependent fermionic many-body dynamics.
status_search_result: The general problem of approximating the irreducible three-body cumulant Δ^{(3)} in time-dependent reduced-density-matrix theory is a long-standing challenge in many-body physics. Various proposals (e.g., reconstruction functionals via Green's-function/RDM connections, Nakatsuji–Yasuda and Mazziotti reconstructions in contracted Schrödinger equation theory) exist, but no universally accepted, conservation-preserving and reliable closure is known. The question is regarded as open.

original_question: Let A be a nonnegative primitive tensor of order m and dimension n, where primitiveness means that there exists a positive integer r such that T_A^r(x) > 0 for every nonnegative nonzero vector x, and let γ(A) be the least such r. The general upper bound proved for primitive tensors is γ(A) <= (n - 1)^2 + 1. Characterize the tensors A for which the primitive degree attains this maximal value γ(A) = (n - 1)^2 + 1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $m \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be integers, and let $A = (a_{i_1 i_2 \cdots i_m})$ be a nonnegative tensor of order $m$ and dimension $n$, i.e. $a_{i_1 \cdots i_m} \ge 0$ for all indices $i_j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$. For a vector $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)^	op \in \mathbb{R}^n$, define the map $T_A : \mathbb{R}^n 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ by
$$ igl(T_A(x) igr)_i \;=\; \sum_{i_2,\dots,i_m=1}^n a_{i\,i_2\cdots i_m}\, x_{i_2}\, x_{i_3}\cdots x_{i_m}, \qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
and let $T_A^r$ denote the $r$-fold composition of $T_A$ with itself. The tensor $A$ is called primitive if there exists a positive integer $r$ such that $T_A^r(x) > 0$ (componentwise) for every nonnegative nonzero vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. The smallest such $r$ is called the primitive degree of $A$ and is denoted by $\gamma(A)$. It is known that for every nonnegative primitive tensor of order $m$ and dimension $n$,
$$\gamma(A) \;\le\; (n-1)^2 + 1.$$
Problem: Give a characterization of all nonnegative primitive tensors $A$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ that attain this bound, i.e. for which $\gamma(A) = (n-1)^2 + 1$.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Extension beyond the Hubbard-model test case
original_question: Do the instability, density-divergence, and fermionic-constraint-violation phenomena observed for BBGKY truncations in a finite Hubbard model persist in small molecules and more complex correlated-electron systems, and how can the proposed partial remedies be validated in those settings?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of N interacting fermions evolving under a (possibly time-dependent) Hamiltonian, and let ρ_p(t) denote the p-body reduced density matrix at time t. The exact dynamics is governed by the BBGKY hierarchy, in which the time evolution of ρ_p couples to ρ_{p+1}. A standard truncation closes the hierarchy at second order by approximating ρ_3 as a functional of ρ_1 and ρ_2 (e.g., via cluster-expansion-type ansätze that preserve particle number and total energy), yielding coupled equations of motion for ρ_1(t) and ρ_2(t).

When this truncated scheme is applied to the few-site Hubbard model (a finite lattice with on-site Coulomb repulsion U and nearest-neighbor hopping), three pathologies have been documented:
(i) numerical/dynamical instability of the propagation;
(ii) divergence of local densities at finite times;
(iii) violation of the N-representability/fermionic constraints, namely the requirement that ρ_2 (and the contracted ρ_1) remain Hermitian, antisymmetric, positive semidefinite, and satisfy the correct partial-trace and eigenvalue bounds (0 ≤ eigenvalues of ρ_1 ≤ 1).

Several partial remedies have been proposed, including purification/positivity-restoration projections of ρ_2 during propagation and modified closure functionals designed to enforce contraction consistency.

Question: Do the three pathologies (i)–(iii) above persist when the same BBGKY truncation schemes are applied to genuine small-molecule electronic systems (i.e., ab initio Hamiltonians for atoms and small molecules with realistic Coulomb interactions and basis sets) and to other complex correlated-electron systems beyond the Hubbard test case? Furthermore, can the proposed partial remedies be rigorously validated as cures (or systematic mitigations) of these pathologies in those more general settings?
category_tag: BBGKY hierarchy and reduced density matrices
status_search_result: The phenomena (instability, density divergence, and N-representability violations) are documented for BBGKY truncations in finite Hubbard test systems, and preliminary indications suggest similar issues arise in small molecules. Subsequent literature continues to investigate positivity-preserving and contraction-consistent closures for the time-dependent two-body reduced density matrix, but no comprehensive validation establishing that the proposed partial remedies cure these pathologies across small molecules and general correlated-electron systems has been found. The question therefore appears still open.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: BBGKY closures tied to approximate wave functions
original_question: What relationship between BBGKY reduced-density-matrix equations and approximate wave functions can be used to build time-dependent truncations whose natural orbital occupation numbers remain physical, as happens in time-dependent Hartree-Fock where a corresponding wave function exists?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-fermion quantum system with antisymmetric, normalized time-dependent wave function Ψ(t) ∈ ⋀^N H, where H is a one-particle Hilbert space, evolving under a Hamiltonian of the form H = ∑_i h(i) + ∑_{i<j} v(i,j). For each k = 1, …, N define the k-particle reduced density matrix (k-RDM) by

  γ_k(t; x_1,…,x_k; x'_1,…,x'_k) = (N choose k) ∫ Ψ(t; x_1,…,x_k, y_{k+1},…,y_N) Ψ*(t; x'_1,…,x'_k, y_{k+1},…,y_N) dy_{k+1}…dy_N.

These satisfy the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy

  i ∂_t γ_k = [H_k, γ_k] + Tr_{k+1}[ V_{k,k+1}, γ_{k+1} ],   k = 1, …, N,

where H_k is the k-particle part of H and V_{k,k+1} couples particles 1,…,k to particle k+1.

A truncation of the hierarchy at level k consists of replacing γ_{k+1} on the right-hand side of the k-th equation by a functional Φ_k(γ_1,…,γ_k) (a closure), producing a closed evolution for (γ_1,…,γ_k). The eigenvalues of γ_1, called natural occupation numbers, are required by N-representability to lie in [0,1]; a truncation is said to preserve physicality of natural occupation numbers if, along its evolution, the eigenvalues of γ_1(t) remain in [0,1] for all t ≥ 0.

In the special case of time-dependent Hartree–Fock (the truncation γ_2 = γ_1 ∧ γ_1), there always exists a Slater-determinant wave function whose 1-RDM equals γ_1(t), and consequently the natural occupation numbers are automatically physical.

Problem. Identify and characterize a precise relationship between truncated BBGKY equations and (approximate) N-particle wave functions that yields, beyond the Hartree–Fock level, time-dependent truncation schemes Φ_k for which the evolved 1-RDM γ_1(t) corresponds (exactly or via an explicit construction) to some antisymmetric wave function and whose natural occupation numbers therefore remain in [0,1] for all times.
status_search_result: The question concerns constructing wave-function-consistent truncations of the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy that preserve physical natural occupation numbers. This is recognized as an outstanding open problem in time-dependent reduced-density-matrix theory; later work on TD-RDM and TD-density-matrix functional methods (e.g., contracted Schrödinger equations, purification schemes) addresses N-representability violations heuristically, but no general construction tying truncated BBGKY equations to an underlying approximate wave function (beyond TDHF) appears to have been established. No definitive solution was found in the search.

original_question: For a nonnegative primitive tensor A of order m and dimension n, define the majorization matrix M(A) by M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij...j}. For each j in [n], call A j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n], and let γ_j(A) be the least such k. Must the set of j-primitive degrees {γ_1(A), γ_2(A), ..., γ_n(A)} always be a consecutive interval of integers [a, b] for some positive integers a < b?

The product of two such tensors is defined coordinatewise so that powers $A^k$ are again nonnegative tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$ (using the standard tensor product that yields, for each $k\ge 1$, an $m$th-order $n$-dimensional tensor $A^k$). The majorization matrix $M(A)$ of $A$ is the $n\times n$ matrix with entries
\[ M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij j\cdots j}, \qquad i,j\in[n]. \]
The tensor $A$ is called primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that every entry of $M(A^k)$ is positive; the least such $k$ is the primitive degree $\gamma(A)$. For a fixed $j\in[n]$, $A$ is called $j$-primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $(M(A^k))_{uj}>0$ for all $u\in[n]$, and the least such $k$ is denoted $\gamma_j(A)$.

\[ \{\gamma_1(A),\gamma_2(A),\dots,\gamma_n(A)\} = \{a,a+1,\dots,b\}, \]
i.e. the set of $j$-primitive degrees is always a consecutive interval of integers?

original_question: Let A be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n. Define the majorization matrix by M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij...j}. For a fixed j in [n], call A j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n]. Call A irreducible if there is no nonempty proper subset I of {1, ..., n} such that a_{i_1...i_m} = 0 whenever i_1 is in I and i_2, ..., i_m are all outside I. Is it true that A is primitive if and only if A is irreducible and there exists some j in [n] for which A is j-primitive?
self_contained_problem:
Let $m \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be integers, and let $[n] = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. A tensor of order $m$ and dimension $n$ is an array $A = (a_{i_1 i_2 \cdots i_m})$ with entries indexed by $i_1, \ldots, i_m \in [n]$. Such a tensor is called nonnegative if all entries $a_{i_1 \cdots i_m}$ are nonnegative real numbers.

For a nonnegative tensor $A$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$, define the majorization matrix $M(A)$ to be the $n \times n$ matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is
$$M(A)_{ij} = a_{i j j \cdots j}, \qquad i, j \in [n].$$

The tensor product $A^k$ is defined recursively so that $A^k$ is again a nonnegative tensor of order $m$ and dimension $n$ via the standard tensor product associated with the Perron–Frobenius theory of nonnegative tensors: the entries of $A^k$ are the iterated polynomial expressions in the entries of $A$ obtained from $k$-fold composition (equivalently, from the map $x \mapsto Ax^{m-1}$).

The tensor $A$ is said to be primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that every entry of $A^k$ is strictly positive. For a fixed $j \in [n]$, the tensor $A$ is said to be $j$-primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that
$$\bigl(M(A^k)\bigr)_{u j} > 0 \quad \text{for every } u \in [n].$$

The tensor $A$ is said to be reducible if there exists a nonempty proper subset $I \subsetneq [n]$ such that
$$a_{i_1 i_2 \cdots i_m} = 0 \quad \text{whenever } i_1 \in I \text{ and } i_2, \ldots, i_m \in [n] \setminus I.$$
Otherwise $A$ is called irreducible.

Prove or disprove: a nonnegative tensor $A$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ is primitive if and only if $A$ is irreducible and there exists some $j \in [n]$ such that $A$ is $j$-primitive.

Related work on primitive tensors and primitive degree (e.g., the directed-hypergraph characterization of primitivity and the proof of Shao's conjecture on the primitive degree bound) exists, but no clear proof or counterexample of this specific equivalence was located.

original_question: How can time-dependent density-functional or reduced-density-matrix approximations incorporate nonlocality, memory dependence, time-dependent phases in functional terms, and energy conservation, instead of relying on adiabatic ground-state extensions that can produce pathologies such as time-independent occupation numbers?

status_search_result: The construction of nonadiabatic, memory-dependent, energy-conserving exchange–correlation functionals for time-dependent DFT and TDRDMFT is a long-standing open problem. context_brief: Extremal j-primitive degree for nonprimitive tensors
original_question: Fix integers m >= 3 and n >= 2. Let A be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n, and let M(A) denote its majorization matrix, defined by M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij...j}. For a fixed j in [n], call A j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n], and let γ_j(A) be the least such k. Among tensors A that are j-primitive for at least one j but are not primitive tensors, define r(m, n) to be the maximum possible value of γ_j(A). Determine r(m, n), and characterize the tensors that attain this extremal value.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $m \ge 3$ and $n \ge 2$. A tensor $A = (a_{i_1 i_2 \ldots i_m})$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ has entries indexed by $i_1, \ldots, i_m \in [n] := \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, and is called nonnegative if all entries are $\ge 0$. For two order-$m$ dimension-$n$ tensors $A$ and $B$, their product $A B$ is the order-$m$ dimension-$n$ tensor whose $(i, i_2, \ldots, i_m)$ entry is
$$ (AB)_{i\, i_2 \cdots i_m} \;=\; \sum_{j_2,\ldots,j_m \in [n]} a_{i\, j_2 \cdots j_m}\, b_{j_2\, i_2 \cdots i_m} \cdot \mathbf{1}[j_3=\cdots=j_m]\text{ along the standard tensor product convention,} $$
so that powers $A^k$ are defined recursively by $A^1 = A$ and $A^{k+1} = A \cdot A^k$ in the standard way used for nonnegative tensors. The majorization matrix $M(A)$ of $A$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with entries
$$ (M(A))_{ij} \;=\; a_{i\, j\, j\, \cdots\, j}, \qquad i,j \in [n]. $$
The tensor $A$ is called primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that every entry of $M(A^k)$ is positive. For a fixed $j \in [n]$, $A$ is called $j$-primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $(M(A^k))_{u\, j} > 0$ for every $u \in [n]$; the smallest such $k$ is the $j$-primitive degree $\gamma_j(A)$.

Define
$$ r(m, n) \;=\; \max\bigl\{\, \gamma_j(A) \,:\, A \text{ is a nonnegative order-}m\text{ dimension-}n\text{ tensor},\ A \text{ is not primitive},\ \exists\, j \in [n] \text{ with } A \text{ being } j\text{-primitive} \,\bigr\}. $$

Determine $r(m, n)$ in closed form, and characterize all tensors that attain this maximum.
status_search_result: Web searches for the $j$-primitive degree of nonnegative tensors and the quantity $r(m,n)$ did not surface a paper that determines $r(m,n)$ in general or characterizes the extremal tensors. Related results establish the sharp bound $(n-1)^2+1$ for the primitive degree of primitive tensors, but the analogous extremal problem in the $j$-primitive (non-primitive) setting does not appear to have a published resolution. Status is therefore taken as unknown.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Reliability of propagating only the second BBGKY equation
original_question: Is it possible to make propagation based only on the second BBGKY equation for the two-body reduced density matrix into a generally reliable approach, given that approximate closures can produce large total-energy fluctuations and can still diverge even when compatibility between the first and second hierarchy equations is no longer the immediate issue?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite, non-relativistic many-fermion quantum system whose state is described by a time-dependent density matrix on Fock space. For each integer $p\ge 1$, let $ho_p(t)$ denote the $p$-body reduced density matrix obtained by partial trace, normalized so that $\mathrm{Tr}\,ho_p =  inom{N}{p}$ where $N$ is the particle number. With a Hamiltonian containing one-body kinetic terms and a two-body interaction, the time-dependent reduced density matrices satisfy the BBGKY hierarchy
$$ i\hbar\,\partial_t ho_p(t) = [H_p,ho_p(t)] + \mathrm{Tr}_{p+1} igl[V_{p,p+1},ho_{p+1}(t) igr], $$
which couples $ho_p$ to $ho_{p+1}$. A "second-equation propagation scheme" consists of choosing a closure functional $ho_3[ho_1,ho_2]$ (e.g. cumulant expansions, the 3b-NIA approximation, or weak-coupling/WC truncations) and then evolving only $ho_2(t)$ via
$$ i\hbar\,\partial_t ho_2(t) = [H_2,ho_2(t)] + \mathrm{Tr}_{3} igl[V_{2,3},\,ho_3[ho_1(t),ho_2(t)] igr], $$
with $ho_1(t)$ obtained by contraction from $ho_2(t)$.

It is known that for typical closures (i) the total energy $E(t)=\mathrm{Tr}(Hho(t))$, while formally conserved, can in numerical simulations exhibit large fluctuations in time, and (ii) the propagated $ho_2(t)$ may fail to remain positive semidefinite or representable, leading to divergences in finite time, even in regimes where the compatibility relation $ho_1 = 	frac{1}{N-1}\mathrm{Tr}_2 ho_2$ between the first and second hierarchy levels is not violated.

Problem. Determine whether there exists a closure $ho_3[ho_1,ho_2]$ such that the resulting second-equation propagation scheme is generally reliable, in the sense that for a broad class of finite fermionic systems and initial data the propagated $ho_2(t)$ (a) remains positive semidefinite and $N$-representable for all $t\ge 0$, (b) conserves total energy with bounded long-time fluctuations, and (c) does not diverge in finite time. Equivalently, either construct such a closure together with a proof of these properties, or prove that no closure depending only on $ho_1$ and $ho_2$ can simultaneously satisfy (a)–(c) uniformly.
status_search_result: No published resolution was identified. The reliability of two-body BBGKY truncation schemes for time-dependent reduced density matrices remains an active research problem in many-body quantum dynamics, with ongoing work on cumulant closures, N-representability constraints, and energy conservation, but no general construction or impossibility result is known.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of type t is unimodal, without imposing any restriction on codimension or socle degree. In particular, the paper highlights the unresolved special case of proving that every type-2 pure O-sequence is unimodal in arbitrary codimension.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_r]$. A monomial order ideal is a finite, nonempty collection $X$ of monomials in $R$ that is closed under taking divisors: whenever $m \in X$ and $m'$ divides $m$, also $m' \in X$. original_question: Let A be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n. Call A strongly primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that A^k is a positive tensor, meaning every entry of A^k is positive, and let η(A) be the least such k. Can one develop and study the associated notions of strongly primitive degree, strongly exponent set, and j-strongly primitive tensors?
self_contained_problem:
For an order-$m$, dimension-$n$ tensor $A=(a_{i_1 i_2\cdots i_m})$ with $1\le i_j\le n$, define the tensor product $A\cdot B$ and the powers $A^k$ via the standard multilinear (Shao-type) product on nonnegative tensors, so that $A^k$ is again a nonnegative tensor of the same order and dimension. Call $A$ nonnegative if every entry is $\ge 0$, and call $A$ positive (write $A>0$) if every entry is $>0$.

Say that a nonnegative tensor $A$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ is strongly primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $A^k>0$. When $A$ is strongly primitive, define the strongly primitive degree
$$\eta(A)\;=\;\min\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\,:\,A^k>0\}.$$
Define the strongly exponent set of order $m$ and dimension $n$ as
$$E_s(m,n)\;=\;\{\eta(A)\,:\,A\text{ is a strongly primitive nonnegative tensor of order }m\text{ and dimension }n\}.$$
For an integer $j\ge 1$, call a nonnegative tensor $A$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ $j$-strongly primitive if $A$ is strongly primitive and exactly $j$ entries of $A^{\eta(A)-1}$ are zero (equivalently, $A^{\eta(A)-1}$ has exactly $j$ zero entries while $A^{\eta(A)}>0$).

Develop the theory of these notions. In particular:
(a) Determine sharp upper and lower bounds for $\eta(A)$ in terms of $m$ and $n$ over all strongly primitive tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$.
(b) Determine the strongly exponent set $E_s(m,n)$, including possible gaps.
(c) For each $j\ge 1$, characterize the structure of $j$-strongly primitive tensors and compute the maximum value of $\eta(A)$ over $j$-strongly primitive tensors of given order and dimension.
status_search_result: A web search shows extensive literature on the (ordinary) primitive degree, exponent set, and j-primitive nonnegative tensors, including bounds such as γ(A) ≤ (n−1)²+1 and characterizations via directed hypergraphs. However, the strongly primitive variant (using the noncommutative tensor product power A^k rather than the majorization/k-th power) is much less developed, and no complete determination of the strongly exponent set or full theory of j-strongly primitive tensors was found. Status appears to be largely open / not fully resolved.

original_question: When can a non-trivial virtual knot arise as the connected sum of two trivial virtual knots? Equivalently, for long virtual knots whose closure is the unknot, classify which non-isotopic long virtual knots can close to the same trivial compact knot and thereby explain when different connected-sum choices for closed virtual knots can produce a non-trivial result.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle). Two virtual knot diagrams are equivalent if they are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies, the three classical Reidemeister moves, the three virtual Reidemeister moves, and the mixed (semi-virtual) move. A virtual knot is an equivalence class of virtual knot diagrams. The unknot is the equivalence class of the diagram with no crossings.

A long virtual knot diagram is a virtual knot diagram in which one strand is cut at a generic point to produce two free ends going to infinity (a 1-1 tangle in the plane); equivalence of long virtual knot diagrams is generated by all the moves above performed away from the two ends. The closure of a long virtual knot is the (closed) virtual knot obtained by reconnecting the two ends in the plane.

The connected sum of two closed virtual knots K_1 and K_2 is defined by cutting each at a chosen arc and splicing them; in general this operation depends on the chosen arcs. For long virtual knots, concatenation gives a well-defined (but in general non-commutative) connected sum.

Problems.
(a) Classify all non-trivial virtual knots K that arise as a connected sum K = K_1 # K_2 in which both K_1 and K_2 are equivalent to the unknot.
(b) Classify all long virtual knots whose closure is equivalent to the (closed) unknot, up to equivalence of long virtual knots, and use this classification to describe precisely which choices of cutting arcs in two unknotted closed virtual knots can yield a non-trivial closed virtual connected sum.
status_search_result: The phenomenon that a non-trivial virtual knot (e.g., the Kishino knot) can be a connected sum of two unknotted virtual knots is well known, and many invariants (surface bracket, biquandle, parity, arrow polynomials) detect specific examples of non-triviality. However, no general classification of such virtual knots, nor of the long virtual knots whose closure is the unknot, appears in the literature; the question is listed among unsolved problems in virtual knot theory and remains open.

original_question: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is unimodal.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_r]$. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite, nonempty collection of monomials in $R$ such that whenever $M \in X$ and $N$ divides $M$, then $N \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is called pure if all of its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same degree. The pure $O$-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ counts the monomials of degree $i$ in $X$ and $e$ is the common degree of the maximal monomials. Equivalently, pure $O$-sequences coincide with the Hilbert functions of Artinian level monomial $k$-algebras. The codimension of $h$ is $h_1$, and the type of $h$ is $h_e$ (the number of maximal monomials, equivalently the socle dimension of the corresponding level algebra). The sequence $h$ is unimodal if there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

Problem. For each fixed integer $r \ge 1$, determine the largest integer $t = t(r)$ with the property that every pure $O$-sequence of codimension $r$ and type $t$ is unimodal.

Partial results are known: pure $O$-sequences of codimension $\le 2$ are always unimodal; in codimension 3, type 2 is unimodal (over any field), and Boyle (Illinois J. Math., 2014) proved unimodality for type 3 in three variables. Non-unimodal examples in codimension 3 are known starting at relatively large types (e.g., type 14), but the precise threshold is not established. No general formula or value for $t(r)$ for $r \ge 3$ has been determined.

original_question: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest socle degree e such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let k be a field and let R = k[x_1,...,x_r] be the polynomial ring in r variables. A finite, nonempty set X of monomials in R is called an order ideal (or a pure order ideal if all maximal monomials of X under divisibility have the same total degree) if, whenever m ∈ X and m' divides m, then m' ∈ X. For a pure order ideal X whose maximal monomials all have degree e, define h_i = #{m ∈ X : deg(m) = i} for i = 0,1,...,e. The resulting integer vector h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) = (1, h_1, ..., h_e) is called a pure O-sequence of codimension r (assuming h_1 = r) and socle degree e.

A finite sequence (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) of positive integers is said to be unimodal if there exists an index j with h_0 ≤ h_1 ≤ ... ≤ h_j ≥ h_{j+1} ≥ ... ≥ h_e.

Problem. For each fixed integer r ≥ 1, determine the largest integer e = e(r) (or show that no such largest value exists) such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal. Equivalently, characterize, as a function of the codimension r, the threshold socle degree above which non-unimodal pure O-sequences first appear.
status_search_result: The problem of determining, for each fixed codimension r, the largest socle degree e for which all pure O-sequences of codimension r and socle degree e are unimodal appears to remain open. Known partial results include: pure O-sequences of codimension ≤ 3 are unimodal in many cases (e.g., type 2 in codimension 3 via the Weak Lefschetz Property), while non-unimodal examples exist in higher codimensions (Stanley's example, and a known non-unimodal pure O-sequence in three variables is restricted to certain socle degrees). No general formula determining the threshold e(r) has been established.

original_question: Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots, and determine richer algebraic structures that can detect flat virtual-knot phenomena beyond mod 2 linking numbers despite the fact that the flat biquandle algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations.
self_contained_problem:
A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (the three classical Reidemeister moves, the three purely virtual moves, and the mixed semivirtual move). A flat virtual knot (equivalently, a virtual string) is the equivalence class of a virtual knot diagram in which the over/under information at every classical crossing is forgotten, so that classical crossings are simply transverse double points; the equivalence relation is generated by the corresponding flat versions of the generalized Reidemeister moves.

The flat biquandle algebra is the unital associative algebra generated by two invertible elements A and B subject to the relations obtained from the flat Reidemeister moves; it is known to be isomorphic to the Weyl algebra (the algebra generated by x, y with [x, y] = 1 over a field of characteristic zero), and consequently it admits no nontrivial finite-dimensional representations.

To date, the principal nontrivial combinatorial invariant of flat virtual knots is the mod 2 linking number (and small refinements thereof).

Problem: Construct new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots that distinguish pairs of flat virtual knots not separated by mod 2 linking numbers, and identify richer algebraic structures (beyond the flat biquandle / Weyl algebra) capable of detecting flat virtual-knot phenomena despite the absence of nontrivial finite-dimensional representations of the Weyl algebra.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as part of a list of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory. Subsequent work has produced partial advances—e.g., semiquandle counting invariants, chord-index based invariants, and polynomial invariants from affine flat biquandles—but flat virtual knots remain difficult to classify and the search for richer algebraic invariants beyond the Weyl-algebra setting continues. No source indicates the problem has been fully resolved.

original_question: For the flat hierarchy in which flat crossings are labeled by elements of an ordinal alpha and a flat third Reidemeister move allows a strand with two labels a to slide across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b, classify the resulting diagrams and determine how this hierarchy generalizes ordinary flat virtual-knot theory.
self_contained_problem:
Fix an ordinal $\alpha$. Define the *flat $\alpha$-hierarchy of diagrams* as follows. A diagram is a 4-valent planar graph (with the usual virtual-crossing convention) whose classical-type crossings are flat (i.e. unsigned, with no over/under information) and each such flat crossing carries a label drawn from $\alpha$. Two diagrams are considered equivalent if they are related by a finite sequence of the following local moves, performed in any region of the plane:

(i) Planar isotopy and the standard detour move for virtual crossings (so virtual crossings behave as in flat virtual knot theory).

(ii) A flat first Reidemeister move that adds or removes a flat kink with an arbitrary label from $\alpha$.

(iii) A flat second Reidemeister move that creates or destroys a bigon whose two flat crossings carry the same label.

(iv) A *labeled flat third Reidemeister move*: a strand both of whose crossings on the boundary of a triangular region are labeled by the same element $a \in \alpha$ may be slid across a flat crossing labeled $b \in \alpha$ to the opposite side of that crossing if and only if $a > b$ in $\alpha$.

When $\alpha = 1$ this reduces to ordinary flat virtual knot theory (virtual strings).

Problem: Classify the equivalence classes of diagrams under these moves for an arbitrary ordinal $\alpha$, and describe in what precise sense the resulting theory generalizes flat virtual knot theory (e.g., construct complete or computable invariants distinguishing the classes, identify nontrivial elements arising at each level $a \in \alpha$, and determine the relationship between the hierarchies for $\alpha < \alpha'$).

Even the base case (ordinary flat virtual knots / virtual strings) is known to be difficult and is not fully classified, and no complete classification of the hierarchy for general ordinals appears in the literature.

original_question: Clarify the relationship between flat virtual-knot theories and theories of doodles, including doodles with virtual crossings, and determine the resulting structures for cobordism, associated groups, and free-abelian cobordism classes of immersed surfaces without triple points.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A flat virtual knot/link diagram is a 4-valent planar diagram whose crossings are of two kinds: flat (unoriented, undecorated) crossings and virtual crossings (drawn with a small circle). Two diagrams are equivalent as flat virtual links if they are related by a finite sequence of: (i) the flat Reidemeister moves on flat crossings, (ii) the virtual Reidemeister moves on virtual crossings, and (iii) the mixed "detour" move that allows an arc passing only through virtual crossings to be replaced by any other such arc with the same endpoints. (Crucially, the detour move is allowed for virtual crossings relative to flat crossings, but not vice versa.)

(b) A doodle is a finite collection of closed curves immersed in the 2-sphere (or in a closed oriented surface) having only transverse double points and no triple points, considered up to ambient isotopy and the doodle Reidemeister moves that exclude any move creating or destroying a triple point. One may also enlarge this category to "virtual doodles" by allowing, in addition to ordinary double points, virtual crossings subject to the virtual Reidemeister moves and the detour move.

(c) A cobordism between two doodles D_0 and D_1 is a compact immersed surface S in (surface)×[0,1] whose boundary is D_0⊔D_1, whose singular set consists only of double-point curves (i.e. S has no triple points and no branch points). Doodle cobordism is an equivalence relation, and the set of cobordism classes of doodles forms an abelian group under disjoint union; this group is conjectured/observed to be free abelian.

Problem. Develop a precise dictionary between the theory of flat virtual knots and links and the theory of (possibly virtual) doodles. Specifically:

1. Construct a well-defined map (or pair of mutually inverse maps) between equivalence classes of flat virtual links and equivalence classes of (virtual) doodles, and determine its kernel and image.

2. Define cobordism in both categories so that the dictionary of (1) descends to a homomorphism between the corresponding cobordism groups, and identify this homomorphism.

3. Determine the structure of the free-abelian cobordism group of doodles whose cobordisms are immersed surfaces without triple points: produce an explicit set of free generators (e.g. in terms of double-point–count invariants or homotopy classes of immersions), and compute the analogous group for virtual doodles.

4. For each of the categories above (flat virtual links, doodles, virtual doodles), describe the naturally associated group invariant (the analogue of the knot group / fundamental group of the complement / quandle-type group), and exhibit how these groups correspond under the dictionary of (1).

original_question: Do the two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed links - homeomorphism and virtual equivalence via generalized Kirby moves - actually coincide? More generally, give a geometric-topological interpretation of virtual 3-manifolds, and determine whether the alternative construction obtained by doing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization yields the same theory.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A classical closed orientable 3-manifold can be presented by integral Dehn surgery on a framed link in S^3, and two such links present homeomorphic 3-manifolds if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of Kirby moves (handle slides and stabilizations). A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose crossings are labeled as classical (over/under) or virtual, considered up to the classical Reidemeister moves and the virtual Reidemeister moves. By extending the Kirby calculus to framed virtual link diagrams via "generalized Kirby moves," one obtains an equivalence relation on framed virtual links; the equivalence classes are called virtual 3-manifolds. Every classical framed link is in particular a virtual one, so this gives an equivalence relation on classical (ordinary) 3-manifolds (two ordinary 3-manifolds are virtually equivalent if their framed-link presentations are related through the virtual Kirby calculus).

Alternatively, for each closed orientable surface Σ_g one may consider framed links in the thickened surface Σ_g × ℝ and perform Dehn surgery on them; identifying surfaces and links under stabilization (adding a handle to Σ_g together with the corresponding inclusion of links) produces another candidate notion of "virtual 3-manifold."

Problems.
(a) Do the two equivalence relations on ordinary closed orientable 3-manifolds — homeomorphism, and virtual equivalence via generalized Kirby moves — coincide? Equivalently, if two framed links K, L ⊂ S^3 are equivalent via the virtual Kirby calculus, must they be equivalent via the classical Kirby calculus?

(b) Give a geometric-topological interpretation of the equivalence classes of framed virtual links under the virtual Kirby calculus: that is, identify what kind of geometric object a "virtual 3-manifold" is.

(c) Does the theory of virtual 3-manifolds defined via surgery on framed links in thickened surfaces Σ_g × ℝ, taken up to surface stabilization, coincide with the theory defined by virtual Kirby calculus on framed virtual link diagrams?
status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published resolution. The notion of virtual 3-manifolds via virtual Kirby calculus is established in work of Dye and Kauffman, and a thickened-surface/stabilization viewpoint is well known in virtual knot theory, but no source found explicitly proves that virtual Kirby equivalence of classical links implies classical Kirby equivalence, gives a definitive geometric-topological interpretation of virtual 3-manifolds, or proves equivalence of the two constructions. Status appears to remain open, but this could not be conclusively verified.

original_question: Determine the smallest number n of variables for which there exists a nonunimodal pure f-vector, equivalently a nonunimodal f-vector of a pure simplicial complex. The paper notes this after recalling Stanley's original nonunimodal example and later bounds for special cases.
self_contained_problem:
A simplicial complex Δ on vertex set {1,2,…,n} is called pure if all of its facets (inclusion-maximal faces) have the same dimension. Its f-vector is f(Δ)=(f_{-1},f_0,f_1,…,f_{d}), where f_i is the number of i-dimensional faces of Δ and d=dim Δ. A finite sequence (a_0,a_1,…,a_d) of nonnegative integers is called unimodal if there exists an index j with a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_j ≥ a_{j+1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_d, and nonunimodal otherwise.

Determine the smallest positive integer n such that there exists a pure simplicial complex on n vertices whose f-vector (f_0,f_1,…,f_d) is nonunimodal.
status_search_result: No source establishes the exact minimum number of vertices needed for a nonunimodal pure f-vector. Known partial results give a sharp lower bound of n=328 in the Cohen–Macaulay socle-degree-5 case (Tahat) and examples with n as low as 39 in higher socle degree, but the general pure case remains unresolved in the literature found.

original_question: Decide whether every matroid f-vector is unimodal or even log-concave, and whether every matroid h-vector has the analogous property. The paper records that representable matroids were known to satisfy these properties, but leaves the general case open.
self_contained_problem:
Let M be a matroid on a finite ground set E with rank function r, and let Δ(M) denote its independence complex, i.e. the simplicial complex whose faces are the independent sets of M. Write f(M) = (f_{-1}, f_0, f_1, …, f_{r-1}) for the f-vector of Δ(M), where f_{i-1} is the number of independent sets of M of cardinality i, and write h(M) = (h_0, h_1, …, h_r) for the h-vector of Δ(M), defined by the identity
   Σ_{i=0}^{r} f_{i-1} (t-1)^{r-i} = Σ_{i=0}^{r} h_i t^{r-i}.

A finite sequence (a_0, a_1, …, a_d) of nonnegative real numbers is called:
 • unimodal if there exists an index k with a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ … ≤ a_k ≥ a_{k+1} ≥ … ≥ a_d;
 • log-concave if a_i^2 ≥ a_{i-1} a_{i+1} for every 1 ≤ i ≤ d-1.

Decide each of the following statements, for every matroid M:
 (a) The f-vector f(M) is unimodal.
 (b) The f-vector f(M) is log-concave.
 (c) The h-vector h(M) is unimodal.
 (d) The h-vector h(M) is log-concave.
status_search_result: The f-vector questions (a) and (b) are fully resolved: Adiprasito–Huh–Katz (2018) proved the Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture, and the ultra-log-concavity of the independent-set numbers (Mason's strong conjecture) was proved independently by Anari–Liu–Oveis Gharan–Vinzant and by Brändén–Huh, establishing log-concavity (hence unimodality) of f(M) for every matroid. For h-vectors, Dawson's log-concavity conjecture for matroid h-vectors has been announced/established in recent work (Ardila; Berget–Spink–Tseng give a proof of log-concavity of the h-vector of the independence complex), implying unimodality, though full unimodality/log-concavity claims for all matroid h-vectors are more recent and the literature should be consulted for the precise current status.

original_question: Develop effective invariants and, if possible, a classification theory for welded knots. In particular, determine whether Satoh's map from welded knots or links to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space is faithful, and determine whether a welded knot with trivial fundamental group must itself be trivial as a welded knot.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A welded knot diagram is a generic immersion of a circle in the plane whose double points are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or welded (virtual) crossings. Two welded knot diagrams are equivalent if they are related by a finite sequence of the classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3, the virtual Reidemeister moves V1, V2, V3, the mixed move M (a classical strand passes through a welded crossing), and the over-commute (forbidden-overpass, F1) move in which an over-strand may slide past a virtual crossing. (The under-commute move F2 is NOT allowed.) A welded knot is an equivalence class of welded knot diagrams under these moves; welded links are defined analogously with several components.

The welded knot group of a welded knot K is the group with Wirtinger presentation read off from any of its diagrams (one generator per arc, one relation per classical crossing); this is a welded invariant.

Satoh's Tube map Tube assigns to every welded knot K an ambient isotopy class Tube(K) of an oriented embedded ribbon torus in S^4, by "inflating" each arc of a diagram into an annulus and resolving classical and welded crossings as ribbon singularities in 4-space. The map is well defined on welded equivalence classes, surjects onto ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus knots, and induces an isomorphism between the welded knot group of K and the fundamental group π_1(S^4 ∖ Tube(K)).

Problems. Provide answers to each of the following.

(a) Construct effective invariants of welded knots that, ideally, suffice to classify them up to welded equivalence.

(b) Decide whether the Tube map
      Tube : { welded knots } / (welded equivalence)  →  { ribbon torus knots in S^4 } / (ambient isotopy)
(and its analogue for welded links) is injective.

(c) Decide whether every welded knot K with trivial welded knot group (i.e. π_1 isomorphic to Z) is welded-equivalent to the unknot.
category_tag: welded knots and ribbon torus knots
status_search_result: Recent work shows Satoh's Tube map is not injective: there exist non-trivial welded knots and links mapped to the same ribbon torus knot, and Y-type local moves on welded links have been identified as part of the kernel, though the kernel of Tube is not yet completely understood. It is also known that having welded knot group Z does not force a welded knot to be trivial; non-trivial welded knots with trivial group exist. The broader problem of constructing a complete set of invariants and a full classification of welded knots remains open.

context_brief: Long virtual and long flat knots
original_question: Strengthen the invariant theory for long virtual knots and long flat virtual knots, especially by combining the long-knot approach of [160] with biquandle constructions, by extracting useful classical-knot invariants from that framework, and by seeking a full classification of long flat knots using the descending-diagram construction D(F) associated to a long flat virtual knot F.
self_contained_problem:
A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (drawn with a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (the classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3 together with the virtual moves V1, V2, V3 and the mixed move M). A long virtual knot is the analogous object for a properly embedded oriented arc with a generic projection to the plane (one input and one output strand at infinity), again considered up to generalized Reidemeister moves performed in a compact region. A long flat virtual knot is obtained by forgetting the over/under information at every classical crossing, so that classical crossings are replaced by transverse double points and one works modulo the flat versions of R2, R3 and the virtual/mixed moves.

A biquandle is a set X equipped with two binary operations (a,b) ↦ a^b and (a,b) ↦ a_b satisfying the axioms ensuring invariance under the classical and virtual Reidemeister moves: each map x ↦ x^y and x ↦ x_y is a bijection, the "sideways" map S(a,b) = (b^a, a_b) is invertible, and the operations satisfy the exchange laws making the biquandle coloring of any virtual knot diagram well defined.

For a long flat virtual knot F, one may form its descending diagram D(F): traverse the long arc from input to output and at each double point encountered for the first time declare the strand to pass over the strand met later, producing a long virtual (non-flat) knot D(F).

Solve the following research program:

(a) Construct a strengthened invariant theory for long virtual knots that unifies the long-knot invariant framework (in which a long virtual knot is encoded by the algebraic word read along its strand, modulo relations corresponding to long-knot Reidemeister moves) with the biquandle coloring construction, and produce invariants of long virtual knots strictly stronger than those obtained from either framework alone.

(b) From this combined framework, extract new invariants of classical knots (long classical knots, viewed as long virtual knots whose diagrams have no virtual crossings) that are not equivalent to previously known classical invariants, or prove that no such new classical invariants arise.

(c) Using the descending-diagram assignment F ↦ D(F), give a complete classification of long flat virtual knots: namely, decide whether two long flat virtual knots F1 and F2 are equivalent if and only if D(F1) and D(F2) are equivalent as long virtual knots, and if not, determine the precise equivalence relation on long virtual knots induced by this assignment so as to obtain a full set of invariants classifying long flat virtual knots.
status_search_result: The problem is a research program combining long virtual knot invariants, biquandle constructions, and the descending-diagram approach for long flat knots. No published work appears to fully classify long flat virtual knots or to establish the requested unified invariant framework; work on biquandle invariants and flat virtual knots continues but the classification problem for long flat virtual knots remains an acknowledged open problem.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? More generally, for each fixed codimension, which socle types force unimodality of all pure O-sequences in that codimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite, nonempty set of monomials of $R$ such that whenever $M \in X$ and $N$ is a monomial dividing $M$, also $N \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is called pure of type $t$ if the set of maximal monomials of $X$ (those not properly dividing any other element of $X$) has cardinality $t$ and all of these maximal monomials have the same degree. The pure O-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ is the number of monomials of $X$ of degree $i$ and $e$ is the common degree of the maximal monomials; equivalently, pure O-sequences are exactly the Hilbert functions of monomial Artinian level algebras. The codimension of $h$ is $r$ (the number of variables actually appearing). A finite sequence $(h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ of nonnegative integers is unimodal if there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

(a) Prove or disprove: every pure O-sequence of type $2$ is unimodal, in arbitrary codimension $r$.

(b) More generally, for each fixed codimension $r$, determine the set of socle types $t$ such that every pure O-sequence of codimension $r$ and type $t$ is unimodal.
status_search_result: The unimodality of all pure O-sequences of type 2 is established for codimensions r = 2, 3, and 4, but for arbitrary codimension (in particular r ≥ 5) the question appears to remain open. The general question of which (codimension, type) pairs force unimodality is still only partially understood: known positive cases include (r,1) for all r and (3,2), (3,3), (4,2), while non-unimodal examples exist for (r,t) with r ≥ 4 and certain t. Related log-concavity problems also remain open in case (3,2).

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Does the Interval Conjecture Property for pure O-sequences hold in important unresolved cases such as codimension three, and more broadly what is the exact scope of the Interval Property for pure O-sequences, pure f-vectors, and related classes of sequences?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$. A finite, nonempty set $X$ of monomials in $R$ is called an order ideal (or "downset") if, whenever $m \in X$ and $m'$ divides $m$, then $m' \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is pure if all its maximal monomials (under divisibility) have the same degree. The pure O-sequence of $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ counts the number of monomials of degree $i$ in $X$ and $e$ is the common degree of the maximal monomials. A vector $(h_0,\dots,h_e)$ of nonnegative integers is called a pure O-sequence if it arises in this way for some pure order ideal; its codimension is $h_1$ (which equals the number of variables actually used).

Interval Property (IP). A class $\mathcal{C}$ of integer sequences is said to satisfy the Interval Property if, whenever $(h_0,\dots,h_e) \in \mathcal{C}$ and $(h_0,\dots,h_{i-1},h_i+\alpha,h_{i+1},\dots,h_e) \in \mathcal{C}$ for some index $i$ and some positive integer $\alpha$, then for every integer $\beta$ with $0 \le \beta \le \alpha$ the sequence
$$(h_0,\dots,h_{i-1},h_i+\beta,h_{i+1},\dots,h_e)$$
also belongs to $\mathcal{C}$.

Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences (ICP). The class of pure O-sequences satisfies the Interval Property.

Pure $f$-vectors. The pure $f$-vector of a pure simplicial complex $\Delta$ on a finite vertex set is $(f_{-1},f_0,\dots,f_{d-1})$, where $f_i$ is the number of $i$-dimensional faces of $\Delta$ and all facets have the same dimension $d-1$. A vector is called a pure $f$-vector if it arises as the $f$-vector of some pure simplicial complex.

Problem. Resolve the following:

(a) Does the Interval Property hold for the class of pure O-sequences in codimension three (i.e., when $h_1 = 3$)?

(b) Does the Interval Property hold for the class of pure O-sequences in arbitrary codimension?

(c) Does the Interval Property hold for the class of pure $f$-vectors?

(d) Determine the precise scope of the Interval Property: identify natural classes of integer sequences arising in combinatorial commutative algebra and enumerative combinatorics for which the Interval Property holds, and exhibit natural classes for which it fails.
status_search_result: The Interval Conjecture for pure O-sequences (ICP) is widely cited as open in most cases, including codimension three. Subsequent work (e.g., by Boij–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Zanello and others) has established partial structural results such as unimodality for codimension 3, type 2 pure O-sequences via the Weak Lefschetz Property, but no full proof of the ICP in codimension three appears in the literature. The Interval Property for pure $f$-vectors is also reported as wide open with little progress, and the precise scope of the Interval Property remains unclarified.
