paper_title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions
context_brief: Monotone functions close to low-degree juntas
original_question: Fix any epsilon > 0. Is every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} epsilon-close to a junta whose number of relevant coordinates is bounded by a polynomial in deg(f)?
self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its (unique) multilinear Fourier expansion $f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\hat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and define its degree $\deg(f)$ to be the largest $|S|$ with $\hat f(S)\neq 0$. Call $f$ monotone if $f(x)\le f(y)$ whenever $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i$. For an integer $k\ge 0$, a $k$-junta is a Boolean function depending on at most $k$ of its input coordinates. For $\varepsilon>0$, two functions $f,g:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ are $\varepsilon$-close if $\Pr_{x}[f(x)\neq g(x)]\le\varepsilon$, where $x$ is drawn uniformly from $\{-1,1\}^n$.

Question: Does there exist, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a polynomial $p_\varepsilon$ such that every monotone Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ (for every $n$) is $\varepsilon$-close to some $p_\varepsilon(\deg(f))$-junta?
status_search_result: Daniel Kane (2012/2013) resolved this in the negative by constructing, for every depth $d$, a monotone Boolean function computable by a depth-$d$ decision tree (hence of degree $\le d$) that disagrees with every $k$-junta on a constant fraction of inputs for $k=\exp(o(\sqrt d))$. This rules out a poly(deg) bound and even a quasi-polynomial bound.

original_question: Given marginal distributions F1, ..., Fn, characterize the aggregation set D_n by deciding which target distributions G can occur as the law of some sum S = X1 + ··· + Xn with Xi ∼ Fi. Equivalently, for a specified distribution G, determine whether there exists S ∈ D_n such that S has distribution G.
self_contained_problem:
Let $F_1, \ldots, F_n$ be given univariate cumulative distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$. Define the aggregation set
$$D_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n) = \{\, \text{law}(X_1 + \cdots + X_n) \;:\; X_i \sim F_i \text{ for } i=1,\ldots,n,\ (X_1,\ldots,X_n)\text{ is some joint distribution with these marginals}\,\}.$$
That is, $D_n$ is the set of all distributions of $S = X_1 + \cdots + X_n$ obtainable by varying the dependence structure (copula) among $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ while keeping the marginal laws $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ fixed.

Provide a characterization of the set $D_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$. Equivalently, given a target distribution $G$ on $\mathbb{R}$, give necessary and sufficient conditions (in terms of $G$ and $F_1,\ldots,F_n$) under which there exist random variables $X_1 \sim F_1, \ldots, X_n \sim F_n$ on a common probability space such that $X_1 + \cdots + X_n \sim G$. In particular, treat the case of simple families of marginals (for example, identical marginals, uniform marginals, or other tractable parametric families).
category_tag: aggregation sets / dependence with given marginals
status_search_result: A full characterization of the aggregation set $D_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ for general marginals remains open. Partial results exist: Wang and Wang (2016) studied aggregation sets via lower-convex sets, and Mao, Wang, and others (2019) obtained analytical results for the case of standard uniform marginals. For heterogeneous or general marginals, an explicit analytical characterization is still considered very difficult and is an active research direction.

original_question: Develop algorithms that determine whether specified distributions are jointly mixable, or that solve the minimax assignment problem of arranging workers so as to minimize the maximum row sum in the production model. In particular, under what conditions do the swapping algorithms proposed for this purpose converge?
self_contained_problem:
Background. Given univariate distribution functions $F_1,\ldots,F_n$, the tuple $(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ is called jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ defined on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim F_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$, such that the sum $X_1+\cdots+X_n$ is almost surely constant. When $F_1=\cdots=F_n=F$, $F$ is said to be $n$-completely mixable.

The Rearrangement (swapping) Algorithm operates on an $N\times n$ matrix $A=(a_{i,j})$ whose $j$-th column consists of $N$ equiprobable quantiles of $F_j$. At each step one chooses a column $j$ and rearranges its entries so as to be oppositely ordered to the row sums of the remaining $n-1$ columns; this is iterated over columns until a stopping criterion is met. The algorithm is used both to numerically detect joint mixability (by trying to drive $\max_i\sum_j a_{i,j} - \min_i\sum_j a_{i,j}$ to zero) and, more generally, to address the minimax assignment problem of permuting entries within each column of a given non-negative matrix $A=(a_{i,j})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ so as to minimize $\max_{1\le i\le N}\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,\sigma_j(i)}$, where each $\sigma_j$ is a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

Problem. 
(a) Design algorithms that, given $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ (or given quantile matrices approximating them), decide whether $(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ is jointly mixable, and that compute (or approximate) the minimum of $\max_{1\le i\le N}\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,\sigma_j(i)}$ over all column-permutations $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n)$ of a given matrix $A$.
(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the input distributions $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ (respectively on the matrix $A$) under which the Rearrangement (swapping) Algorithm converges to a globally optimal arrangement, and quantify its rate of convergence.
status_search_result: The convergence behavior of the Rearrangement/swapping Algorithm for detecting joint mixability and solving the minimax assignment problem remains incompletely understood. Subsequent literature (e.g., Puccetti–Wang and follow-ups) has produced partial results, numerical evidence, and special-case guarantees, but no general necessary and sufficient convergence conditions are known; moreover, the general minimax column-rearrangement problem is known to be NP-complete, indicating that fully efficient algorithms are unlikely.

original_question: Extend mixability to higher-dimensional marginal constraints: when some fixed bivariate or higher-dimensional marginal distributions are prescribed, determine whether a joint mix exists and develop numerical algorithms to decide existence or construct one.
self_contained_problem:
A tuple of univariate cumulative distribution functions $(F_1, \dots, F_n)$ is said to be jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$, defined on a common probability space, with $X_i \sim F_i$ for each $i$, such that the sum $X_1 + \cdots + X_n$ is almost surely equal to a constant. Such a random vector $(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ is called a joint mix.

Now consider the following extension. Let $n \ge 3$ and partition the index set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ into (possibly overlapping) subsets $S_1,\dots,S_m \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, each of cardinality at least $2$. For each $k \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, prescribe a multivariate distribution $H_k$ on $\mathbb{R}^{|S_k|}$. Say that a joint mix compatible with these higher-dimensional marginal constraints exists if there is a random vector $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ such that:
(i) for every $k$, the subvector $(X_i)_{i \in S_k}$ has joint distribution $H_k$; and
(ii) $X_1 + \cdots + X_n$ is almost surely constant.

Solve the following:

(a) Characterize, in terms of the prescribed multivariate marginals $\{H_k\}$, when a joint mix compatible with these constraints exists.

(b) In the special case where $m \ge 2$ subsets $S_k$ are pairs (so each $H_k$ is a bivariate distribution) with consistent univariate marginals, give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of such a joint mix.

(c) Develop an effective numerical algorithm that, given the prescribed multivariate marginals $\{H_k\}$ (or sufficiently regular approximations thereof), decides whether a joint mix compatible with the constraints exists and, when it does, constructs one.
category_tag: Joint mixability with multivariate marginal constraints
status_search_result: The question of mixability under higher-dimensional (bivariate or higher) marginal constraints is listed among the current open questions in complete mixability. While necessary and sufficient conditions for joint mixability are known for several classes of univariate marginals (uniform, monotone densities, unimodal-symmetric densities, elliptical with shared characteristic generator), justifying existence of a joint mix with prescribed multivariate margins remains unresolved, and no general numerical algorithm appears to be available.

original_question: Generalize the definition of mixability by replacing the summation X1 + ··· + Xn with other multivariate functions, and determine what corresponding notions of complete or joint mixability are mathematically useful and how they can be characterized.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be an atomless probability space and let $F_1,\dots,F_n$ be univariate cumulative distribution functions. The classical notions of mixability are defined via the aggregation map $(X_1,\dots,X_n)\mapsto X_1+\cdots+X_n$:

- The tuple $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ is called jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_i\sim F_i$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) on $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ such that $X_1+\cdots+X_n$ is almost surely constant.
- A distribution $F$ is called $n$-completely mixable if $(F,\dots,F)$ ($n$ copies) is jointly mixable.

Now let $\psi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be a fixed measurable function (an "aggregation function"), and define $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ to be $\psi$-jointly mixable if there exist $X_i\sim F_i$ such that $\psi(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ is almost surely constant, with the analogous definition of $\psi$-complete mixability.

Problem. Develop a theory of $\psi$-mixability for aggregation functions $\psi$ other than the summation $\psi(x_1,\dots,x_n)=x_1+\cdots+x_n$. Specifically:

1. Identify natural classes of multivariate functions $\psi$ (e.g. symmetric, monotone, continuous, associative, or homogeneous aggregation functions, including means, maxima, products, and copula-based aggregations) for which the resulting notion of $\psi$-(complete or joint) mixability yields a mathematically useful and nontrivial theory.
2. For such $\psi$, give characterizations (necessary and/or sufficient conditions on $F_1,\dots,F_n$) of when $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ is $\psi$-jointly mixable, paralleling the known moment, support, and mean-type conditions in the additive case.
3. Determine which structural properties of additive mixability (such as the relation to variance reduction, optimal couplings, and the dual representation via the convex order) extend to general $\psi$, and which fail.
status_search_result: Surveys on complete and joint mixability list the extension to general aggregation functions replacing summation as an open research direction. While complete characterizations exist for $n\le 2$ in the additive case, no general theory of $\psi$-mixability for arbitrary multivariate aggregation $\psi$ has been established; only partial results exist for special $\psi$ (e.g. via convex/concave orderings).

original_question: How does the algebraic structure of the underlying semigroup G affect complete and joint mixability defined on G? In particular, which properties of G help or obstruct the existence, uniqueness, or characterization of mixes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(G,+)$ be a (topological) abelian semigroup equipped with a $\sigma$-algebra making $+$ measurable. For an integer $n\ge 2$ and probability measures $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n$ on $G$, the tuple $(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n)$ is called jointly mixable on $G$ if there exist $G$-valued random variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$, defined on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim\mu_i$ for each $i$, such that the sum $X_1+\cdots+X_n$ is almost surely constant (equal to some fixed $c\in G$). A probability measure $\mu$ on $G$ is called $n$-completely mixable if $(\mu,\dots,\mu)$ ($n$ copies) is jointly mixable on $G$.

Investigate how the algebraic structure of the underlying semigroup $G$ governs joint and complete mixability. Specifically, address the following:

(a) Identify algebraic properties of $G$ (e.g., cancellativity, existence of identity, existence of inverses making $G$ a group, divisibility, torsion, being finite/finitely generated, ordering, presence of idempotents) that ensure the existence of jointly mixable or completely mixable tuples for natural classes of marginals.

(b) Identify algebraic properties of $G$ that obstruct mixability — for example, properties that force the constant sum $c$ (the "center") to be unique, or that prevent any nontrivial $\mu$ from being $n$-completely mixable.

(c) Provide characterizations of which probability measures on $G$ are $n$-completely mixable, and which $n$-tuples are jointly mixable, in terms of the algebraic structure of $G$, including the question of uniqueness of the achievable center $c$.
category_tag: Joint and complete mixability on semigroups
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction for further research on the influence of semigroup structure on mixability. A targeted web search did not surface a subsequent work providing a general characterization of how semigroup algebraic structure affects existence, uniqueness, or characterization of complete and joint mixability; results in the literature typically remain in specific settings (e.g., $\mathbb{R}^d$ or finite groups). Status appears still open.

original_question: Let L be a finite field of characteristic p with |L| > 2, and let s be an invertible exponent, meaning gcd(s, |L|-1) = 1, for the power permutation x -> x^s on L. If s is congruent to 1 modulo p - 1, must the exponent be singular, that is, must there exist some a in L^x such that the Weil sum W_{L,s}(a) = sum_{x in L} mu(x^s - ax) is equal to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ with $|L|=q>2$, and let $\mu\colon L\to\mathbb{C}^\times$ be the canonical additive character of $L$, that is, $\mu(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,\mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p)$. For an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s,q-1)=1$ (so that $x\mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $L$), define the Weil sum
$$W_{L,s}(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(x^s-ax),\qquad a\in L.$$
The exponent $s$ is called singular if there exists $a\in L^\times$ such that $W_{L,s}(a)=0$.

Prove or disprove: if $|L|>2$ and $s\equiv 1\pmod{p-1}$ (with $\gcd(s,q-1)=1$), then $s$ is singular.
status_search_result: The Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture (1976) remains open in general. Partial results are known: it has been verified for Niho exponents and in various special cases (e.g., certain characteristic-3 settings). Recent work (e.g., Katz–Langevin–Nguyen, 2020–2021) provides new proofs in restricted families but does not establish the full conjecture.

original_question: In the special case of the Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture where the field characteristic is p in {2, 3} and the exponent is s = q - 2, prove that the exponent is singular without using the theory of elliptic curves; equivalently, show by a different method that there exists a nonzero a in L such that W_{L,q-2}(a) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime, let L be a finite field of characteristic p with q = |L| elements, and let ψ : L → ℂ^× denote the canonical additive character of L, given by ψ(x) = exp(2πi · Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p), where Tr_{L/F_p} is the absolute trace.

For an integer s with gcd(s, q − 1) = 1 (so that x ↦ x^s is a permutation of L) and for a ∈ L, define the Walsh (Weil) transform
    W_{L,s}(a) = ∑_{x ∈ L} ψ(x^s − a x).
The exponent s is called singular (over L) if there exists a ∈ L with a ≠ 0 such that W_{L,s}(a) = 0; otherwise s is called nonsingular. The Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture asserts that whenever q > 2 and s is an invertible exponent satisfying s ≡ 1 (mod p − 1), then s is singular.

Problem. Suppose p ∈ {2, 3}, L = F_q is a finite field of characteristic p with q > 2, and s = q − 2 (so that s is the inverse exponent, i.e. x^s = x^{−1} for x ≠ 0, and s ≡ 1 (mod p − 1) in both cases). Prove, without invoking the theory of elliptic curves over finite fields, that s = q − 2 is singular over L: that is, exhibit by an alternative method a nonzero element a ∈ L such that
    W_{L,q−2}(a) = ∑_{x ∈ L} ψ(x^{q−2} − a x) = 0.
status_search_result: Recent literature on Helleseth's vanishing conjecture (e.g., work by Katz, Langevin, Aubry, Feng, and Nguyen on Weil sums and Niho exponents) establishes the conjecture in various cases, including for the inverse exponent s = q − 2 via reductions to point-counting on elliptic curves in characteristics 2 and 3. I did not find a published proof in the case p ∈ {2, 3}, s = q − 2 that avoids the use of elliptic curves, so the specific challenge of providing an elliptic-curve-free proof appears to remain open.

original_question: Let L be a finite field of characteristic p such that the extension degree [L : F_p] is a power of two. For every invertible exponent s on L, is it impossible for the reduced Fourier spectrum of the power permutation x -> x^s to have exactly three distinct values? The paper notes that this is already proved for p = 2 and p = 3, so the open case is p > 3.
self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime and let L be a finite field of characteristic p such that the degree [L : F_p] is a power of two, where F_p denotes the prime field with p elements. Let q = |L|. An integer s with 1 ≤ s ≤ q-1 is called an invertible exponent on L if gcd(s, q-1) = 1, so that the map x ↦ x^s is a permutation of L. Fix a nontrivial additive character ψ: L → C^× (for example, ψ(x) = exp(2πi · Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p)). For an invertible exponent s, define the Weil/Fourier sum
    W_s(a,b) = Σ_{x ∈ L} ψ(a x^s + b x),    a, b ∈ L,
and let the reduced Fourier spectrum of the power permutation x ↦ x^s be the set of distinct values
    Spec(s) = { W_s(a,b) : a ∈ L^×, b ∈ L }  (equivalently, the set of nontrivial values arising from this family).

Prove or disprove: for every prime p and every finite field L with [L : F_p] a power of two, and for every invertible exponent s on L, the set Spec(s) does not consist of exactly three distinct values. (The cases p = 2 and p = 3 are known; the question concerns p > 3.)
status_search_result: Helleseth's 1976 three-valued cross-correlation conjecture is resolved for p = 2 (Katz) and p = 3, but remains open for primes p > 3 according to recent surveys on cross-correlation of m-sequences and Weil sums of binomials.

original_question: For a power permutation f(x) = x^s on a finite field L with s congruent to 1 modulo p - 1, Aubry and Langevin proved that some Fourier coefficient is divisible by 3. Can one prove an analogous forced divisibility statement for some prime l different from the characteristic p; that is, under comparable hypotheses, must there exist a nonzero Fourier coefficient divisible by a prime l != p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $L = \mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of order $q = p^n > 2$ and characteristic $p$, and fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi: L \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ (e.g. $\psi(x) = \exp(2\pi i\, \mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p)$). For a function $f: L \to L$, define its Walsh–Fourier transform by
$$\widehat{f}(a) = \sum_{x \in L} \psi(a f(x)) \qquad (a \in L).$$
A power map $f(x) = x^s$ (with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$, so that $f$ is a permutation of $L$) is called a power permutation of exponent $s$.

It is known that whenever $s \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$, there exists $a \in L^\times$ such that $\widehat{f}(a) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ (the Fourier values being algebraic integers in a cyclotomic ring, where divisibility by $3$ is interpreted via any prime above $3$).

Problem: Determine whether an analogous forced-divisibility phenomenon holds for some prime $\ell \neq p$ in place of $3$. Precisely, find conditions on the exponent $s$ (comparable to the congruence $s \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$) and a prime $\ell \neq p$ such that for every finite field $L$ of characteristic $p$ satisfying these conditions, there must exist $a \in L^\times$ with $\widehat{f}(a) \equiv 0 \pmod{\ell}$ in the ring of algebraic integers, where $f(x) = x^s$.

status_search_result: A web search surfaces the original problem list and related work by Aubry, Langevin, Feng, and Katz on divisibility properties of Fourier spectra of power permutations and Helleseth-type conjectures, but no source establishing or refuting an analogous forced-divisibility result for a prime $\ell \neq p$ under comparable hypotheses. The status appears to remain open, but this could not be conclusively verified.

original_question: Suppose x -> x^s is a four-valued power permutation over a finite field. Find an analogue of Katz's three-valued theorem, which for three-valued power permutations forces singularity, the congruence s equiv 1 modulo p - 1, and integrality of the spectrum. In other words, determine what comparable structural constraints must hold in the four-valued case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and $q = p^n$. For an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$, the map $\chi_s : \mathbb{F}_q \to \mathbb{F}_q$, $x \mapsto x^s$, is a permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ called a power permutation. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi : \mathbb{F}_q \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ (e.g. $\psi(x) = e^{2\pi i \operatorname{Tr}(x)/p}$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ denotes the absolute trace). The Walsh (or Weil) spectrum of $\chi_s$ is the multiset
$$\mathrm{Spec}(s) = \Big\{\, W_s(a) := \sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_q} \psi(x^s - a x) \;:\; a \in \mathbb{F}_q^\times \,\Big\}.$$
The exponent $s$ is called $k$-valued if $\mathrm{Spec}(s)$ takes exactly $k$ distinct values, and $s$ is called singular if its $p$-adic digit expansion involves fewer than $n$ nonzero digits (equivalently, $s$ is not a "generic" exponent in the sense of Katz).

A theorem of Katz (2012) asserts: if $\chi_s$ is a three-valued power permutation, then
(i) $s$ is singular,
(ii) $s \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$, and
(iii) the spectrum $\{0, A, B\}$ of $\chi_s$ is contained in $\mathbb{Z}$.

Problem. Establish a structural analogue of this theorem for four-valued power permutations: namely, determine which of the conclusions (singularity of $s$, the congruence $s \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$, and integrality/rationality of the spectrum), or suitable modifications thereof, must necessarily hold whenever $\chi_s : x \mapsto x^s$ is a power permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ whose Walsh spectrum takes exactly four distinct values.
category_tag: Power permutations and Walsh spectra over finite fields
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published analogue of Katz's three-valued theorem for four-valued power permutations. Related work on permutation polynomials and Walsh/cross-correlation spectra exists, but no source clearly establishes the requested structural constraints (singularity, congruence mod p−1, and integrality of the four-valued spectrum). The problem appears to remain unresolved, but the search evidence is inconclusive.

original_question: Let F(x) = mu(x^s) for an exponent s whose nonzero spectral values are A_1, ..., A_n. Determine for which exponents s the product of the nonzero spectral values, product_i A_i, is divisible by q = |L|.
self_contained_problem:
Let $L=\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of order $q$, where $q$ is a prime power, and let $\mu:L\to\mathbb{C}^\times$ be the canonical additive character $\mu(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,\mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p)$, where $p$ is the characteristic of $L$. Fix an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s,q-1)=1$, so that $x\mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $L$. Define
$$F(x)=\mu(x^s)\qquad(x\in L),$$
and consider the Fourier transform (Weil sum)
$$\widehat{F}(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(x^s-ax),\qquad a\in L.$$
The Fourier (Walsh) spectrum of $F$ is the multiset $\{\widehat{F}(a):a\in L\}$. Let $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_n$ denote the distinct nonzero values appearing in this spectrum. 

Determine all exponents $s$ (subject to $\gcd(s,q-1)=1$) for which the product
$$\prod_{i=1}^{n}A_i$$
is divisible by $q$ (in the ring of algebraic integers $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_p]$).

original_question: Let s be an invertible exponent over a finite field L of odd characteristic, and call s nice when the differential multiplicity N(1, v) takes at most three values as v ranges over L. Numerical experiments in the paper found that all nice exponents s not equivalent to 1 over prime fields of characteristic p < 5000 come from the paradigmatic examples s = 3 and s = q - 2. Is that always the case over all finite fields of odd characteristic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L = \mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of odd characteristic, and let $s$ be an integer with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$, so that the map $x \mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $L$. For $u, v \in L$, define
$$N(u, v) = \#\{x \in L : (x+u)^s - x^s = v\}.$$
Call $s$ a nice exponent over $L$ if the set $\{N(1, v) : v \in L\}$ has cardinality at most $3$. Two exponents $s, s'$ are called equivalent (written $s \approx s'$) if $s' \equiv p^i s \pmod{q-1}$ or $s s' \equiv p^i \pmod{q-1}$ for some $i \geq 0$, where $p$ is the characteristic of $L$.

Two known families of nice exponents are:
(i) $s = 3$ over any finite field of odd characteristic;
(ii) $s = q - 2$ (the inversion exponent) over any finite field of odd characteristic.

Prove or disprove: every nice exponent $s$ over a finite field $L$ of odd characteristic that is not equivalent to $1$ is equivalent to either $3$ or $q-2$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as Problem 6.7 in a 2014/2015 survey of open problems on Fourier spectra of power permutations over finite fields. Numerical experiments verified the classification only for prime fields of characteristic p < 5000. No subsequent work found in the search resolves the problem in general; the question of whether the only nice exponents (up to equivalence) over all finite fields of odd characteristic are s = 3 and s = q-2 appears to remain open.

self_contained_problem:

$$N(a, v) = \#\{x \in L : (x+a)^s - x^s = v\}.$$

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: For a feedback-controlled dynamical system, how large can the performance gain be when the controller has access to a specified amount of information about the system state? Equivalently, what quantitative upper bounds relate available information to achievable improvements in performance measures such as extracted work, efficiency, power output, or flux?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a dynamical system whose state evolves stochastically (classically or quantum-mechanically) in contact with one or several thermal reservoirs, driven by an external protocol and subject to feedback control. At specified times the controller performs a measurement of the system, obtaining an outcome that is correlated with the system's microstate. The mutual information between the measurement outcome and the system state quantifies the amount of information acquired by the controller, and on the basis of this outcome the controller chooses a subsequent driving protocol from a prescribed family.

Let one of the following be a chosen performance functional:
- the average work W extracted from the system over a cycle,
- the thermodynamic efficiency η = W/Q_h of a cyclic engine operating between two reservoirs at temperatures T_c < T_h,
- the average power output P = W/τ over a cycle of duration τ, or
- a steady-state average flux J of particles, charge, or energy across the system.

Let I denote a precisely defined measure of the information available to the controller about the system (for example, the mutual information between measurement outcomes and the system state, or, more generally, an information-theoretic quantity such as the QC-mutual information that may include quantum correlations).

Problem. Determine sharp, achievable upper bounds on the performance gain due to feedback as a function of I. Concretely:

(a) For each choice of performance functional above, find a tight inequality of the form
        Φ_feedback − Φ_no-feedback ≤ B(I, system parameters),
valid over all admissible measurement-and-feedback protocols, where Φ denotes the chosen performance functional and B is an explicit function expressing the maximal improvement allowed by access to information content I.

(b) Identify the protocols (measurements and feedback rules) that saturate each such bound, or prove that the bound cannot be saturated and exhibit the optimal achievable constant.

(c) Show that each such bound is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics when the thermodynamic cost of measurement and memory erasure performed by the controller is included.
status_search_result: For the case of average extracted work and efficiency, achievable upper bounds in terms of mutual (QC-)information have been established (Sagawa–Ueda 2008 and subsequent generalizations), giving a generalized second law W_ext ≤ −ΔF + k_B T · I and a universally valid framework that includes measurement/erasure costs. However, sharp, universally valid bounds for other performance measures (finite-time power, steady-state currents/fluxes in nonequilibrium settings) and identification of optimal protocols saturating them remain only partially understood and continue to be actively investigated.

original_question: Let s be an invertible exponent over a finite field of odd characteristic, with s not equivalent to 1. Must 2 always occur as a differential multiplicity of s; equivalently, must there always exist some field element v for which the system x + y = 1 and x^s + y^s = v has exactly two solutions in L^2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $L=\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$ for some integer $n\ge 1$, and let $L^{*}=L\setminus\{0\}$. For a positive integer $s$, the map $f:L\to L$ given by $f(x)=x^{s}$ is called a power permutation of $L$ if it is a bijection (equivalently, $\gcd(s,p^{n}-1)=1$); in this case $s$ is called an invertible exponent over $L$. Two exponents $s$ and $t$ are said to be equivalent (written $s\approx t$) if $t\equiv p^{i}s\pmod{p^{n}-1}$ for some $i\ge 0$, or if $st\equiv p^{i}\pmod{p^{n}-1}$ for some $i\ge 0$ (so that $f(x)=x^{s}$ and $g(x)=x^{t}$ have the same differential properties up to Frobenius and inversion).

For each $u,v\in L$, define
$$N(u,v)=\#\{(x,y)\in L^{2}:\ x+y=u,\ x^{s}+y^{s}=v\}.$$
A positive integer $m$ is called a differential multiplicity of $s$ if there exist $u\in L^{*}$ and $v\in L$ such that $N(u,v)=m$. Equivalently (by the substitution $x\to ux,\ y\to uy$), $m$ is a differential multiplicity of $s$ if and only if there exists $v\in L$ for which the system
$$x+y=1,\qquad x^{s}+y^{s}=v$$
has exactly $m$ solutions $(x,y)\in L^{2}$.

Question: Suppose $s$ is an invertible exponent over $L=\mathbb{F}_{p^{n}}$ (with $p$ odd) and $s\not\approx 1$. Must $2$ always be a differential multiplicity of $s$? That is, must there always exist some $v\in L$ such that the system $x+y=1,\ x^{s}+y^{s}=v$ has exactly two solutions in $L^{2}$?

status_search_result: The "optimist" conjecture asserting that 2 is always a differential multiplicity of any non-trivial invertible exponent in odd characteristic appears to remain open. Recent literature on differential spectra of power permutations over odd-characteristic finite fields (e.g., work on Niho exponents and on specific families such as $x^{p^{n}-3}$) treats individual exponent classes but does not establish the general statement. No source located resolves the conjecture in full generality.

original_question: Let {gamma_k}_{k>=0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that f(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function. For parameters p with -p not in N, define the generalized Bessel-type function F_p(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/(k! Gamma(k+p+1)). Characterize exactly which nonnegative sequences {gamma_k} make F_p belong to the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions.
self_contained_problem:
The Laguerre–Pólya class $\mathcal{L\!-\!P}$ consists of those real entire functions $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ which are uniform limits, on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$, of real polynomials all of whose zeros are real. Equivalently, $\varphi\in\mathcal{L\!-\!P}$ if and only if it admits a Hadamard-type representation
$$\varphi(x)=c\,x^{m}e^{-\alpha x^{2}+\beta x}\prod_{k\ge 1}\Bigl(1-\tfrac{x}{x_{k}}\Bigr)e^{x/x_{k}},$$
with $c,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $x_{k}\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, and $\sum_{k}x_{k}^{-2}<\infty$.

Let $\{\gamma_{k}\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that
$$f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_{k}\,\frac{x^{k}}{k!}$$
defines an entire function. For a parameter $p\in\mathbb{C}$ with $-p\notin\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$, define the associated generalized Bessel-type function
$$F_{p}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\gamma_{k}\,x^{k}}{k!\,\Gamma(k+p+1)}.$$

Problem. Give a complete characterization of all nonnegative sequences $\{\gamma_{k}\}_{k\ge 0}$ (with $f$ entire) for which $F_{p}\in\mathcal{L\!-\!P}$ for every parameter $p$ with $-p\notin\mathbb{N}$ (equivalently, determine the precise necessary and sufficient conditions on $\{\gamma_{k}\}$).
status_search_result: No published characterization addressing this specific problem was located. The problem is posed as an open question concerning when the generalized Bessel-type series associated to a nonnegative coefficient sequence belongs to the Laguerre–Pólya class, and no resolution appears in the available literature.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: How can one formulate the thermodynamics of feedback-controlled systems in a way that explicitly accounts for the thermodynamic consequences of information transfer between the system and the controller, so that quantities such as entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency are treated within a consistent thermodynamic framework?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical or quantum thermodynamic system in contact with one or more heat reservoirs, together with an external controller (a "demon") that performs measurements on the system and applies a feedback protocol whose form depends on the measurement outcomes. Let the joint dynamics of system and controller be specified, with the controller possessing a memory register that stores measurement outcomes and is reset between protocol runs.

Develop a consistent thermodynamic framework for such feedback-controlled systems that explicitly incorporates the thermodynamic role of information transfer between the system and the controller. Concretely, the framework should:

1. Define the relevant information-theoretic quantities (e.g., the mutual information acquired by measurement and any QC-mutual or transfer-entropy-type generalizations) entering the thermodynamic balance.

2. Derive a generalized second law of the form
   ⟨ΔS_sys⟩ + ⟨ΔS_bath⟩ ≥ −I,
   (and the corresponding bound on extractable work ⟨W_ext⟩ ≤ −ΔF + k_B T · I) that holds for arbitrary feedback protocols, where I is the chosen information measure.

3. Establish a fluctuation theorem (Jarzynski/Crooks-type identity) for trajectories that incorporates the information exchanged between system and controller.

4. Account for the thermodynamic cost of the controller's measurement and memory erasure (Landauer's principle), so that the total entropy balance over system + controller + reservoirs is consistent with the ordinary second law.

5. Define and bound the efficiency of feedback-driven heat engines (e.g., Maxwell-demon-type cycles) in terms of the information acquired, identifying when and how the conventional Carnot bound is modified.

The problem is to construct such a framework in full generality (covering classical stochastic, classical Hamiltonian, and quantum settings, with discrete or continuous measurements and feedback) and to identify the tightest universal information-thermodynamic inequalities governing entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency.
status_search_result: A substantial information-thermodynamics framework has been developed since 2008. Sagawa and Ueda derived generalized second laws and Jarzynski-type fluctuation theorems incorporating mutual information for both classical and quantum feedback control, establishing bounds on extractable work and efficiency that account for measurement and erasure costs. Subsequent work (fluctuation theorems with information exchange, transfer-entropy bounds, experimental verification via the Maxwell-demon photon experiment, and recent results on universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics, e.g. 2023–2024) has extended and refined these results. The core programme is thus largely realized, although fully general formulations (continuous measurement, strong coupling, non-Markovian and fully quantum regimes) remain active research areas, so the broader programme is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: For correlated repeated actuation of a feedback controller, what is the precise relationship between the entropy-reduction results derived from the viewpoint of the controlled system and Zurek's algorithmic-complexity analysis of the combined system-plus-controller, especially regarding the minimum energetic cost of erasing the controller's stored measurement record and the resulting thermodynamic limits on the system's entropy reduction?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled thermodynamic system in which a controller repeatedly performs measurements on the system and applies actuations conditioned on those measurement outcomes, with successive actuations allowed to be correlated (i.e., the controller's memory retains a record of past measurement outcomes that influences subsequent actuations). Two complementary frameworks describe the thermodynamics of such a setup:

(A) A "system" viewpoint, in which one bounds the entropy reduction of the controlled system in terms of the mutual information between system and controller and derives generalized second-law inequalities involving the work extracted, the free-energy change, and the information acquired by the controller.

(B) An "algorithmic" viewpoint based on Kolmogorov complexity, in which the physical entropy of the joint system-plus-controller is taken to be the sum of the statistical (Shannon/Boltzmann) entropy of the system conditioned on the controller's record and the algorithmic complexity K(r) of the binary string r stored in the controller's memory. In this viewpoint, Landauer's principle implies that the minimum energetic cost of erasing the record r is k_B T ln 2 · K(r), and this cost in turn imposes a thermodynamic upper bound on the achievable reduction of the system's entropy under correlated repeated actuation.

Problem. Establish the precise quantitative relationship between frameworks (A) and (B) for correlated repeated actuation. Specifically:

(i) Derive an exact identity (or, failing that, matching upper and lower bounds) connecting the maximal system entropy reduction obtainable in framework (A) to the algorithmic-complexity-based bound k_B T ln 2 · K(r) on the erasure cost in framework (B), in the regime where the controller's stored record r exhibits non-trivial temporal correlations across repeated actuations.

(ii) Identify the conditions under which the two frameworks give equivalent thermodynamic limits, and characterize the gap (if any) when they differ, in terms of the statistical properties of the measurement record and the protocol used by the controller.

(iii) Show how the minimum energetic erasure cost k_B T ln 2 · K(r) translates into the maximum entropy reduction of the controlled system, and compare this maximum with the bounds obtained from mutual-information-based generalized second laws.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: Can the entropy-reduction results obtained for correlated repeated feedback actuation be applied or extended to derive quantitative bounds for additional performance measures of feedback-controlled systems, in particular the maximum attainable flux or the maximum attainable power?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled stochastic system in contact with a thermal reservoir at temperature T, whose dynamics are repeatedly modulated by a controller that performs successive measurements on the system and applies control protocols based on the measurement outcomes. Let the sequence of measurement outcomes be {m_1, m_2, …, m_N}, generally correlated across time, and let H({m_i}) denote the Shannon entropy of this sequence. Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, the entropy reduction of the system due to feedback obeys quantitative bounds expressed in terms of the mutual information (or Shannon entropy) of the correlated measurement record, and the minimum energetic cost of erasing the controller's memory imposes a corresponding limit on the maximum extractable work.

Question: Develop quantitative thermodynamic bounds, derived from (or extending) the entropy-reduction results for correlated repeated feedback actuation, on the following performance measures of such feedback-controlled systems:

(a) the maximum attainable steady-state probability flux J (e.g., the average net particle or charge current that the feedback can sustain across the system per unit time), and

(b) the maximum attainable power P (e.g., the rate of work extraction, or the rate of free-energy production, achievable by the feedback protocol).

Specifically, express upper bounds on J and P in terms of the temperature T, the rate of information acquisition by the controller (the entropy rate of the correlated measurement sequence), and the relevant timescales of the controlled dynamics, and determine the conditions under which these bounds are saturated.
status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem regarding the extension of entropy-reduction bounds for correlated repeated feedback to performance measures such as flux and power. While the field of stochastic thermodynamics with feedback has developed substantially, with various information-theoretic bounds (e.g., generalized Jarzynski/Sagawa–Ueda relations, thermodynamic uncertainty relations) emerging, it is not clear from the search whether the specific question of tight bounds on maximum attainable flux and power in correlated repeated feedback systems—as posed here—has been definitively resolved. Status remains unclear from available sources.

original_question: When a feedback controller acts continuously, meaning that its actuation period is shorter than every characteristic time scale of the system dynamics, how can the results obtained for discrete repeated feedback actuation be extended to this continuous-time limit despite the nontrivial relation between discrete entropy and differential entropy?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic dynamical system whose state $X_t$ evolves in continuous time (e.g., according to a Langevin or Markovian stochastic differential equation), together with a feedback controller that, at each actuation step, performs a measurement of the system, gains an amount of information characterized by a mutual information $I_n$ between the measurement outcome and the system state, and applies a control action that influences subsequent dynamics. For the discrete repeated feedback setting, suppose one has established a generalized second law of thermodynamics of the form
$$\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle \;\le\; -\Delta F + k_B T \sum_{n} I_n,$$
where $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle$ is the average extracted work, $\Delta F$ is the free-energy change, $T$ is the bath temperature, and $I_n$ are the (discrete) Shannon mutual informations gathered at each of the discrete actuation times $t_n = n\,\Delta t$.

Now define the continuous-actuation limit as $\Delta t \to 0$, in which the controller's actuation period is shorter than every characteristic time scale of the system dynamics. In this limit, discrete Shannon entropies of the measured and controlled variables generically diverge, and the appropriate information measures become differential entropies (or mutual informations between continuous-time processes), whose relationship to the discrete Shannon entropies is nontrivial (e.g., $H(X_\varepsilon) = h(X) - \log\varepsilon + o(1)$ for an $\varepsilon$-quantization of a continuous random variable $X$ with differential entropy $h(X)$).

Problem: Formulate and prove a generalized second law for the continuous-actuation limit of feedback-controlled stochastic systems that:

(a) extends the discrete inequality above to a well-defined bound involving an information-theoretic functional of the joint continuous-time process of measurements and system trajectories;
(b) yields a finite, physically meaningful information term as $\Delta t \to 0$, despite the divergence of the individual discrete mutual informations $I_n$ and the nontrivial relation between Shannon and differential entropies; and
(c) reduces to the discrete result in the limit of large actuation period.

Equivalently, identify the correct continuous-time information-theoretic quantity (such as a transfer-entropy rate or mutual-information rate between the measurement record and the controlled trajectory) that bounds the extractable work in continuous feedback control, and rigorously establish the corresponding inequality.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has made substantial progress on this question. Continuous-time generalizations of the second law of feedback-controlled systems have been formulated using information rates (notably transfer entropy and mutual information rates), and the thermodynamics of continuous, non-Markovian feedback control has been developed and experimentally tested with levitated microparticles (Debiossac et al., Nature Communications 2020). Recent works (e.g., 2025 entropic-balance and quantum-classical transfer-entropy results) further refine these inequalities. Nevertheless, a fully general framework matching the discrete results in the strict continuous-actuation limit for arbitrary feedback protocols remains an active research direction, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Let p(x)=sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j be a polynomial with a_j>=0. Find conditions on p(x) that make the sequence {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} a multiplier sequence, and find conditions on p(x) that make {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that its diagonal operator does not increase the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial.
self_contained_problem:
Recall that a sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\geq 0}$ is called a multiplier sequence if the diagonal linear operator $T$ defined on real polynomials by $T[x^k]=\gamma_k x^k$ has the property that whenever a real polynomial $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^m c_k x^k$ has only real zeros, then $T[f](x)=\sum_{k=0}^m \gamma_k c_k x^k$ also has only real zeros. The sequence is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if for every real polynomial $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^m c_k x^k$ one has $Z_c(T[f]) \leq Z_c(f)$, where $Z_c(g)$ denotes the number of nonreal zeros of $g$ counted with multiplicity.

Let $p(x)=\sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j$ be a polynomial with real coefficients satisfying $a_j\geq 0$ for all $0\leq j\leq n$. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficients of $p(x)$ such that:
(a) the sequence $\{p(k)/k!\}_{k\geq 0}$ is a multiplier sequence;
(b) the sequence $\{p(k)/k!\}_{k\geq 0}$ is a complex zero decreasing sequence.
status_search_result: The full characterization of complex zero decreasing sequences remains a long-standing open problem in the theory of linear operators preserving real-rootedness, and the specific subproblem of characterizing polynomials $p$ with nonnegative coefficients such that $\{p(k)/k!\}$ is a multiplier sequence or CZDS is posed as an open problem in surveys by Craven–Csordas and related literature. No published full solution was located.

original_question: Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that the diagonal operator T[x^k]=((1+k+k^2)/k!)x^k never increases the number of nonreal zeros of a real polynomial?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the set of polynomials with real coefficients, and for $p\in\mathcal{P}$ let $Z_c(p)$ denote the number of nonreal zeros of $p$, counted with multiplicities. A sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ of real numbers is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if the diagonal linear operator $T:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal{P}$ defined on the monomial basis by
$$T[x^k] = \gamma_k\, x^k,\qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots,$$
and extended linearly, satisfies
$$Z_c(T[p]) \le Z_c(p) \quad \text{for every } p\in\mathcal{P}.$$
Determine whether the sequence
$$\gamma_k = \frac{1+k+k^2}{k!}, \qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots,$$
is a CZDS.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on complex zero decreasing sequences, where a complete characterization of CZDS remains unresolved. No published resolution of this specific test case was found; standard CZDS classifications (e.g., those interpolated by real polynomials in the Laguerre-Pólya class) do not directly settle this rational-times-reciprocal-factorial sequence.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, can the general thermodynamic results of [13] be applied to determine the maximum entropy reduction these ratchets can achieve and to establish a full thermodynamic description of such systems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet: a Brownian particle in contact with a thermal bath at temperature $T$ moves in one dimension under a spatially periodic, asymmetric potential $V(x)$ that can be switched on and off in time. A controller observes the position of the particle (either continuously or at discrete sampling times) and, based on the measurement outcomes, decides whether to keep the potential on or off, with the aim of rectifying thermal fluctuations into directed motion.

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics for feedback-controlled systems, the second law must be modified to incorporate the information acquired by the controller: for a feedback protocol acting on a stochastic system, one has a generalized inequality of the form
$$\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T\, I,$$
where $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle$ is the mean work extracted, $\Delta F$ is the free-energy change, and $I$ is an information-theoretic quantity (a mutual information / entropy reduction) characterizing the controller's measurements and actions. Equivalently, the entropy production of the controlled system is bounded below by $-I$, so $I$ plays the role of a maximum attainable "entropy reduction" induced by the feedback protocol.

Problem. Apply this general thermodynamic framework explicitly to the feedback flashing ratchet:
(a) Define the appropriate information quantity $I$ for an arbitrary measurement-and-switching protocol (continuous or discrete-time) acting on a flashing ratchet, taking into account the non-Markovian sequence of control actions generated by the controller.
(b) Determine the maximum entropy reduction $I_{\max}$ achievable by any such feedback protocol on the flashing ratchet, and exhibit (or bound) protocols saturating it.
(c) Use the result to give a complete thermodynamic description of feedback flashing ratchets, including tight upper bounds on extracted work, output power, and efficiency in terms of $I$, and identify the protocols that saturate these bounds.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has substantially developed the thermodynamic and information-theoretic description of feedback flashing ratchets. In particular, "Information in feedback ratchets" (Phys. Rev. E 108, 034112, 2023) computes the entropy reduction from the non-Markovian sequence of control actions and provides bounds (including a quasi-Markovian limit) on the entropy reduction, and a 2024 work gives a Markovian description of a class of feedback-controlled systems applied to the feedback flashing ratchet. These results realize much of the program (information quantity, bounds, role in the second law), although a fully tight characterization of the maximum attainable entropy reduction over all protocols is still being refined, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: The known bounds for feedback flashing ratchets express flux improvement and power improvement in terms of the information used per actuation. How can these bounds be reformulated in terms of the total non-redundant information acquired per unit time, so that the ratchet results can be related directly to the entropy-reduction and thermodynamic framework developed for general feedback-controlled systems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet: a Brownian particle (or ensemble of particles) moves in one dimension in an asymmetric periodic potential V(x) that can be switched on or off by a controller. The controller measures the particle positions at discrete actuation times and, based on these measurements, decides whether the potential is on or off, producing a directed mean flux ⟨J⟩ and extractable mechanical power ⟨P⟩ when an external load is applied.

For such systems there exist known bounds on the flux improvement Δ⟨J⟩ and on the power improvement Δ⟨P⟩ over the corresponding open-loop ratchet, expressed in terms of the Shannon information I_act used by the controller per actuation event (i.e., the mutual information between the measurement outcome and the chosen action at a single actuation step).

Separately, in the general thermodynamic framework of feedback-controlled systems, the relevant quantity is the rate Ï of non-redundant information acquired per unit time, defined as the entropy-reduction rate of the (generally non-Markovian) sequence of control actions, that is
   Ï = lim_{N→∞} (1/(NÏ„)) [ H(A_1,…,A_N) − redundant correlations ],
where A_k are the successive control actions, Ï„ is the actuation period, and only genuinely new information beyond what is already implied by previous actions is counted.

Problem. Reformulate the known per-actuation bounds on Δ⟨J⟩ and Δ⟨P⟩ for a feedback flashing ratchet as bounds expressed in terms of the non-redundant information rate Ï (information per unit time) rather than the per-actuation information I_act. In particular, derive explicit inequalities of the form
   Δ⟨J⟩ ≤ F_J(Ï),    Δ⟨P⟩ ≤ F_P(Ï),
that remain valid when successive measurements are correlated, and that connect directly to the entropy-reduction / second-law inequality for general feedback-controlled systems.
status_search_result: A 2023 study (Phys. Rev. E 108, 034112, "Information in feedback ratchets") explicitly addresses the entropy reduction of the non-Markovian sequence of control actions in feedback flashing ratchets, accounts for redundancies between successive measurements, and provides bounds on entropy reduction (and consequently on flux/power gains) per unit time using quasi-Markovian limits. This represents substantial progress toward the requested reformulation, though general closed-form bounds in terms of the non-redundant information rate appear to remain only partially established.

original_question: Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence and whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. Equivalently for the first part, decide whether the entire function phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to the Laguerre-Polya class with nonnegative coefficients.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

The Laguerre–Pólya class, denoted LP, is the set of entire functions that are uniform limits, on compact subsets of the complex plane, of sequences of real polynomials all of whose zeros are real. The subclass LP^+ consists of those f in LP whose Taylor coefficients at 0 are all nonnegative; equivalently, f in LP^+ if and only if f can be written as
  f(x) = c x^m e^{a x} ∏_{n} (1 + α_n x),
with c ≥ 0, m ∈ Z_{≥0}, a ≥ 0, α_n ≥ 0, and ∑ α_n < ∞.

A real sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} is called a multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial p(x) = ∑_{k=0}^n a_k x^k whose zeros are all real, the polynomial
  Γ[p](x) := ∑_{k=0}^n γ_k a_k x^k
also has only real zeros. By the Pólya–Schur theorem, a sequence of nonnegative real numbers {γ_k} is a multiplier sequence if and only if the formal power series
  Φ_Γ(x) := ∑_{k=0}^∞ γ_k x^k / k!
represents an entire function in LP^+.

A real sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if, for every real polynomial p(x) = ∑_{k=0}^n a_k x^k,
  Z_c(Γ[p]) ≤ Z_c(p),
where Z_c(q) denotes the number of nonreal zeros of the polynomial q (counted with multiplicity).

Problem. Consider the sequence
  γ_k = √k / k!,  k = 0, 1, 2, ….

(a) Determine whether {γ_k}_{k≥0} is a multiplier sequence. Equivalently, decide whether the entire function
  φ(x) = ∑_{k=0}^∞ (√k / (k! k!)) x^k
belongs to the Laguerre–Pólya class LP^+.

(b) Determine whether {γ_k}_{k≥0} is a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS).
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of whether {√k/k!} is a multiplier sequence or a CZDS, nor a proof that φ(x)=∑ √k x^k/(k!)^2 lies in LP^+. The problem is stated as a conjecture/open problem in the originating work, and surveys on the Laguerre–Pólya class and multiplier sequences (e.g., the 2022 Oberwolfach report on "The Laguerre–Pólya Class and Combinatorics") do not record a solution. Status appears to remain open, though absence of evidence is not conclusive.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
context_brief: Implications for nano and biological systems
original_question: What concrete limitations do information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems impose on the operation and achievable performance of nanotechnology devices and biological systems in which one subsystem uses bidirectional interaction with another subsystem to improve that subsystem's performance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a composite stochastic system consisting of two interacting subsystems A and B, where B acts as a controller that observes A through a noisy measurement channel and applies a feedback action to A in order to improve some performance measure of A (for example, to extract work, reduce entropy, or stabilize a target state). Let I denote the mutual information acquired by B about A per unit time, let W denote the average work extracted (or analogous performance gain) by the feedback protocol, let ΔS denote the entropy production of the joint system, and let kT be the thermal energy scale. Generalized second-law inequalities of the Sagawa–Ueda type assert that the achievable performance is bounded by information-theoretic quantities, e.g. ⟨W⟩ ≤ −ΔF + kT·I, with related bounds on entropy reduction and control accuracy.

Problem: Derive the concrete, quantitative limitations that such information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for bidirectional feedback-controlled systems place on the operation and achievable performance of physical realizations relevant to nanotechnology devices and biological systems (e.g., molecular motors, ion channels, sensory adaptation networks, single-electron transistors with feedback). Specifically, identify the optimal trade-offs between (i) the rate of information acquisition by the controller, (ii) the energetic/dissipative cost of measurement and feedback, and (iii) the resulting performance gain of the controlled subsystem, and characterize attainability of these bounds in concrete model classes.
status_search_result: The general program of deriving information-thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems has seen substantial progress since 2012 (Sagawa–Ueda inequalities, thermodynamics of information, work extraction by Maxwell demons, bounds on biochemical sensing such as Lan–Sartori–Tu, thermodynamic uncertainty relations). However, the broad question of pinning down the concrete operational limitations these bounds impose on real nanoscale and biological devices, including attainability and tightness in physically realistic models, remains an active and largely open research direction with no single definitive resolution.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Compact AdS rigidity in odd dimension > 3
original_question: Let n = 2m + 1 > 3, and let M = Γ\AdS^n be a compact anti-de Sitter manifold where Γ is a discrete group of isometries acting properly discontinuously on AdS^n. Must Γ, up to conjugacy in the isometry group, be a uniform lattice in U(m,1)?
self_contained_problem:
Let n = 2m + 1 with n > 3, and let AdS^n denote n-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, i.e., the Lorentzian symmetric space of constant sectional curvature −1 realized as the quadric

  AdS^n = { x ∈ ℝ^{n−1,2} : ⟨x,x⟩ = −1 },

equipped with the Lorentzian metric induced from the bilinear form of signature (n−1,2) on ℝ^{n−1,2}. Its identity component of the isometry group is G = PO(n−1,2)°. The indefinite unitary group U(m,1) embeds in G as the stabilizer of a compatible complex structure on ℝ^{2m,2}, and uniform lattices in U(m,1) act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on AdS^{2m+1}, producing the so-called standard compact AdS manifolds.

Suppose Γ ⊂ Isom(AdS^n) is a discrete subgroup acting properly discontinuously on AdS^n such that the quotient M = Γ \ AdS^n is a compact (closed) anti-de Sitter manifold. Must Γ be conjugate, inside Isom(AdS^n), to a uniform lattice in U(m,1)?
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter manifolds and Clifford–Klein forms
status_search_result: The question of whether every compact AdS manifold in odd dimension n = 2m+1 > 3 is, up to conjugacy, a quotient by a uniform lattice in U(m,1) appears to remain open. Web search returned no resolution: known constructions of compact AdS manifolds in higher odd dimensions are still standard (lattices in U(m,1)), and recent work on related Clifford–Klein questions (e.g., on GHMC AdS manifolds and exotic structures by Lee–Marquis and others) addresses neighboring problems but does not settle this rigidity question for closed AdS manifolds.

original_question: Let gamma_k=1/(k+1)^(k+1). Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_{k>=0}={1/((k+1)^(k+1)k!)}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence, and determine whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence.
self_contained_problem:
A sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is called a multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k x^k$ all of whose zeros are real, the polynomial
$$\Gamma[p](x) := \sum_{k=0}^{n} \gamma_k a_k x^k$$
also has only real zeros. The sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k x^k$,
$$Z_c\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n} \gamma_k a_k x^k\right) \le Z_c\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k x^k\right),$$
where $Z_c(q)$ denotes the number of nonreal zeros of $q$, counted with multiplicity.

Define
$$\gamma_k := \frac{1}{(k+1)^{k+1}}, \qquad k=0,1,2,\dots,$$
and consider the sequence
$$T_k := \frac{\gamma_k}{k!} = \frac{1}{(k+1)^{k+1}\, k!}, \qquad k = 0,1,2,\dots.$$

Determine:
(a) whether $\{T_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is a multiplier sequence;
(b) whether $\{T_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is a complex zero decreasing sequence.

original_question: Characterize all multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation: there exist functions phi, Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u)=sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r} when phi(x)=sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ denote the Laguerre–Pólya class of nonnegative type, that is, the set of entire functions $\phi$ that are locally uniform limits of polynomials of the form $C\, x^n \prod_{k=1}^N (1+\alpha_k x)$ with $C\ge 0$, $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, and $\alpha_k\ge 0$. Equivalently, $\phi\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ iff $\phi(x)=C x^n e^{\sigma x}\prod_k(1+\alpha_k x)$ with $C,\sigma,\alpha_k\ge 0$ and $\sum\alpha_k<\infty$.

For $\phi\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ with Taylor expansion $\phi(x)=\sum_{m\ge 0} a_m x^m/m!$, define the Jensen-type polynomial
$$B_m^{\phi}(u)\;=\;\sum_{r=0}^{m}\binom{m}{r}(1-u)^{r}\,a_{m-r}\,u^{m-r}\qquad (m\ge 0,\ u\in\mathbb{R}).$$
For $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$, set
$$C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)\;=\;\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j} B_j^{\phi}(t)\,B_{k-j}^{\Phi}(s)\qquad (k\ge 0).$$

A real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a multiplier sequence if for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n c_k x^k$ with only real zeros, the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^n \gamma_k c_k x^k$ also has only real zeros (or is identically zero). The sequence is said to admit a $C_k$-representation if there exist $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\gamma_k \;=\; C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)\qquad\text{for all } k\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

Problem: Characterize explicitly all multiplier sequences $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ that admit a $C_k$-representation.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published characterization of the multiplier sequences admitting a $C_k$-representation as defined; the surrounding literature on multiplier sequences and the Laguerre–Pólya class does not appear to contain a resolution of this specific characterization problem. Status could not be verified from available sources.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Topology of the admissible representation space
original_question: Fix a closed hyperbolic surface S of genus at least 2. Let Adm(S) be the space of admissible pairs (j,ρ) of representations π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) with j Fuchsian and such that the induced action on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact. How many connected components does Adm(S) have, and what is its topology?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, with fundamental group $\pi_1(S)$. Identify the three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ with the Lie group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ endowed with (a multiple of) its Killing form, so that the isometry group of $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ contains $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ acting by left and right multiplication.

A pair $(j,\rho)$ of representations $j,\rho : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is called admissible if:
(i) $j$ is Fuchsian, i.e. discrete and faithful; and
(ii) the diagonal action of $\pi_1(S)$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ defined by $\gamma \cdot x = j(\gamma)\, x\, \rho(\gamma)^{-1}$ is free, properly discontinuous, and cocompact.

Let $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ denote the space of all such admissible pairs $(j,\rho)$, equipped with the topology induced from $\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(S),\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))^2$.

Determine the number of connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ and describe its topology.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. Barbot (J. Diff. Geom. 2015, arXiv:1301.4309) showed that the connected component of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ containing Fuchsian pairs consists exactly of quasi-Fuchsian (Anosov) representations, extending earlier work of Barbot–Mérigot. Tholozan and subsequent authors have shown that $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ is disconnected and identified admissible representations distributed among multiple components (with counts of order $4g-5$ noted in related settings). However, a complete enumeration of the connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ together with a full description of its topology does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Which numerical values can occur as the volume of a compact anti-de Sitter 3-manifold? For a quotient Γ\AdS^3 coming from an admissible pair (j,ρ) in Adm(S), does the volume depend only on the Euler number of ρ, or can it vary within a fixed connected component of Adm(S)?
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a closed oriented surface of genus g ≥ 2, with fundamental group Γ = π_1(S). Let AdS^3 denote 3-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, identified with the Lie group PSL(2,ℝ) endowed with (a constant multiple of) its Killing form, so that its isometry group contains PSL(2,ℝ) × PSL(2,ℝ) acting by left and right multiplication. For a pair of representations (j, ρ) ∈ Hom(Γ, PSL(2,ℝ))² with j Fuchsian (i.e. discrete and faithful), let
   Γ_{j,ρ} = { (j(γ), ρ(γ)) : γ ∈ Γ } ⊂ PSL(2,ℝ) × PSL(2,ℝ).
The pair (j, ρ) is called admissible if the action of Γ_{j,ρ} on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact; let Adm(S) denote the space of admissible pairs. In that case the quotient Γ_{j,ρ}\AdS^3 is a closed Lorentzian 3-manifold, and every closed AdS 3-manifold arises (up to finite cover) in this way. Each representation ρ ∈ Hom(Γ, PSL(2,ℝ)) has an Euler number e(ρ) ∈ ℤ with |e(ρ)| ≤ 2g − 2.

Answer the following:

(a) Determine the set of real numbers that occur as the volume vol(Γ_{j,ρ}\AdS^3) as (j, ρ) ranges over Adm(S) and S over all closed oriented surfaces of genus g ≥ 2.

(b) Show whether vol(Γ_{j,ρ}\AdS^3) depends only on e(ρ) (and the topology of S), or whether it can vary as (j, ρ) varies within a single connected component of Adm(S).
status_search_result: Part (b) was solved by Tholozan (arXiv:1509.04178, "The volume of complete anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds"): the volume of Γ_{j,ρ}\AdS^3 is proportional to e(j) + e(ρ), hence depends only on the Euler numbers and is constant on connected components of Adm(S). Part (a) — the precise set of values realized as volumes of compact AdS 3-manifolds — appears to be answered as a consequence: volumes take a discrete set of values determined by the Euler numbers, but a complete characterization in full generality (including all admissible topologies) does not appear definitively settled in the surveyed literature.

original_question: Let beta_k=e^{sqrt(k)}/k!. The paper reports that the degree-n Jensen polynomials associated with {beta_k} have only real zeros for 1<=n<=30. Does that reality property continue for all degrees?
self_contained_problem:
For a real sequence $\{\alpha_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$, the degree-$n$ Jensen polynomial associated with $\{\alpha_k\}$ is defined by
$$J_n(x) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, \alpha_k\, x^{k}.$$
Define the sequence
$$\beta_k \;=\; \frac{e^{\sqrt{k}}}{k!}, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \dots,$$
and let $J_n^{\beta}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}\beta_k x^{k}$ denote the Jensen polynomials associated with $\{\beta_k\}$.

Numerical computation shows that $J_n^{\beta}(x)$ has only real zeros for every $1 \le n \le 30$. Determine whether this property persists for all degrees: that is, prove or disprove that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial $J_n^{\beta}(x)$ has only real zeros.
status_search_result: A targeted search for results about the hyperbolicity (real-rootedness) of Jensen polynomials associated with the sequence $\beta_k = e^{\sqrt{k}}/k!$ did not return any subsequent paper resolving the question for all $n$. The literature contains general results on Jensen polynomials (Pólya, Craven–Csordas, Griffin–Ono–Rolen–Zagier) and on multiplier sequences, but no specific resolution of this particular numerical observation could be located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

original_question: Let X be the feature space, let the binary label set be {-1, +1}, let D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m be a dataset sampled from a probability space (D, Sigma, P), and let H be a weak-hypothesis class that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, meaning that H contains the constant classifier h(x) = 1, is closed under negation, and every h in H misclassifies at least one example in D. For Optimal AdaBoost, let w_t in Delta_m denote the example-weight distribution at round t, let err(h; w, D) = sum_{l=1}^m w(l) 1[h(x^(l)) != y^(l)], and let H(w_t, D) = arg min_{h in H} err(h; w_t, D), with the weak learner using a deterministic tie-breaking rule to select a representative hypothesis. Is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P), for any dataset D sampled from P, and for mu-almost all such H, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0, then P-almost surely, for every t > T_0, either H(w_t, D) contains exactly one hypothesis, or every pair of hypotheses in H(w_t, D) agrees on all training examples in D, or the total w_t-weight of the training examples on which two tied optimal hypotheses disagree converges to 0 as t tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a feature space and consider binary labels in {-1, +1}. Let (D, Sigma, P) be a probability space on X × {-1, +1}, and let D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m be a dataset of m i.i.d. samples drawn from P. Let H be a class of binary hypotheses h : X → {-1, +1} (the weak-hypothesis class). Call H AdaBoost-natural with respect to D if:
 (i) the constant classifier h ≡ 1 belongs to H;
 (ii) H is closed under negation (h ∈ H implies -h ∈ H);
 (iii) every h ∈ H misclassifies at least one example of D.

Optimal AdaBoost is the version of AdaBoost in which, at each round t, the weak learner returns a hypothesis minimizing the weighted training error under the current example-weight distribution w_t ∈ Δ_m. For w ∈ Δ_m, define
 err(h; w, D) = Σ_{l=1}^m w(l) · 1[h(x^(l)) ≠ y^(l)],
 H(w, D) = arg min_{h ∈ H} err(h; w, D),
and assume the weak learner uses a fixed deterministic tie-breaking rule when |H(w, D)| > 1.

Suppose probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) are equipped with a measure μ on the space of admissible distributions, and likewise μ denotes a natural measure on AdaBoost-natural hypothesis classes.

Prove or disprove: For μ-almost every probability space (D, Sigma, P), for every dataset D drawn from P, and for μ-almost every AdaBoost-natural class H, there exist constants m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0, then P-almost surely at least one of the following holds:

(1) For every round t > T_0, either
  (1.a) |H(w_t, D)| = 1, or
  (1.b) for every pair h_t, h'_t ∈ H(w_t, D) one has h_t(x^(l)) = h'_t(x^(l)) for all l = 1, …, m;

or

(2) lim_{t→∞} Σ_{l=1}^m w_t(l) · 1[h_t(x^(l)) ≠ h'_t(x^(l))] = 0 for any h_t, h'_t ∈ H(w_t, D).
status_search_result: The No-Ties Conjecture for Optimal AdaBoost is presented as a conjecture supported by empirical evidence on high-dimensional real-world datasets, but has not been proved. Subsequent work on the convergence properties of Optimal AdaBoost (framing it as an ergodic dynamical system) continues to assume the no-ties condition rather than establish it, indicating the conjecture remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Bending laminations determine GHMC AdS structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let M = S × R, and let l_- and l_+ be two measured laminations on S that fill S. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations exactly l_- and l_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $M$ contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$ and is maximal (with respect to isometric embeddings) among such spacetimes. Each GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ admits a convex core, the smallest non-empty closed convex subset whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence; when this convex core is not a totally geodesic surface, its boundary consists of two spacelike pleated surfaces (the "upper" and "lower" components), each carrying a transverse measured geodesic lamination on $S$, called the measured bending lamination. Two measured laminations $\ell_-, \ell_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every nontrivial simple closed curve $\gamma$ on $S$, the sum of geometric intersection numbers $i(\gamma, \ell_-) + i(\gamma, \ell_+)$ is strictly positive.

Question: Given any two measured laminations $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has $\ell_-$ as the measured bending lamination of its lower component and $\ell_+$ as the measured bending lamination of its upper component?
status_search_result: Existence of a GHMC AdS structure realizing a pair of filling measured laminations as bending laminations of the convex core boundary has been established (notably by Bonsante–Schlenker for small multiples, and further work on realization). Rigidity (uniqueness) near the Fuchsian locus has been obtained by Prosanov (JLMS 2026), but the full uniqueness statement for arbitrary filling pairs appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let l_- and l_+ be measured laminations that fill S. If E_l(l_-) and E_l(l_+) denote the corresponding right earthquakes of Teichmüller space T, does the composition E_l(l_-) ◦ E_l(l_+) have a unique fixed point in T?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the Teichmüller space of $S$ (the space of isotopy classes of complete hyperbolic metrics on $S$). A measured geodesic lamination on $S$ is a closed subset of $S$ foliated by simple geodesics, equipped with a transverse measure invariant under holonomy. Two measured laminations $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ are said to fill $S$ if for every essential simple closed curve $\gamma$ on $S$, the sum of the geometric intersection numbers $i(\gamma, \ell_-) + i(\gamma, \ell_+)$ is strictly positive.

For a measured lamination $\ell$, the right earthquake along $\ell$ is the homeomorphism $E_\ell : \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T}$ defined by Thurston's earthquake construction (cutting along the leaves of $\ell$ and reglueing with a rightward shear prescribed by the transverse measure).

Suppose $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ are measured laminations that fill $S$. Does the composition
$$E_{\ell_-} \circ E_{\ell_+} : \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T}$$
have a unique fixed point in $\mathcal{T}$?
status_search_result: Existence of a fixed point of the composition $E_{\ell_-} \circ E_{\ell_+}$ when $\ell_\pm$ fill was proved by Bonsante and Schlenker (Duke Math. J. 161 (2012), arXiv:0812.3471). Uniqueness remains open and is known to be equivalent to a conjecture of Mess on globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds (uniqueness of the GHMC AdS manifold whose convex core has prescribed upper and lower bending laminations). No subsequent resolution of the uniqueness question appears in the literature.
