original_question: In the same Optimal AdaBoost setting where D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m is sampled from a probability space (D, Sigma, P), H is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, and the classifier is obtained after T rounds of the standard binary-classification AdaBoost procedure, is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P), for any dataset D sampled from P, and for mu-almost all such H, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0 and T > T_0, the decision boundary of the binary classifier output by Optimal AdaBoost after T rounds on D has P-measure zero?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(\mathcal{D}, \Sigma, P)$ be a probability space, where $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{X} \times \{-1, +1\}$ for some input space $\mathcal{X}$. A dataset is a finite i.i.d. sample $D = \{(x^{(l)}, y^{(l)})\}_{l=1}^m \sim P^m$ of size $m$.

A weak-hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$ is a set of functions $h : \mathcal{X} \to \{-1, +1\}$. We say $\mathcal{H}$ is AdaBoost-natural with respect to $D$ if:
(i) the constant hypothesis $h \equiv 1$ belongs to $\mathcal{H}$;
(ii) $\mathcal{H}$ is closed under negation: $h \in \mathcal{H} \Rightarrow -h \in \mathcal{H}$;
(iii) for every $h \in \mathcal{H}$ there exists $(x, y) \in D$ with $h(x) \neq y$.

Optimal AdaBoost denotes the standard binary-classification AdaBoost procedure run for $T$ rounds on $D$ using $\mathcal{H}$, where at each round the weak learner returns a hypothesis with minimum weighted training error (ties broken by an arbitrary fixed rule). Its output after $T$ rounds is a classifier $F_T : \mathcal{X} \to \{-1, +1\}$ obtained as the sign of a weighted sum of weak hypotheses; the decision boundary is $\partial F_T := \{x \in \mathcal{X} : \text{the weighted sum equals } 0\}$.

Let $\mu$ denote a fixed (suitable) reference measure on the space of probability spaces $(\mathcal{D}, \Sigma, P)$ and on the space of weak-hypothesis classes $\mathcal{H}$.

Question. Is it true that for $\mu$-almost every probability space $(\mathcal{D}, \Sigma, P)$, for every dataset $D$ sampled from $P$, and for $\mu$-almost every $\mathcal{H}$ that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to $D$, there exist constants $m_0, T_0 > 0$ such that whenever $m > m_0$ and $T > T_0$ the decision boundary of the binary classifier output by Optimal AdaBoost after $T$ rounds on $D$ has $P$-measure zero?
status_search_result: The Measure-Zero-Decision-Boundary Conjecture is stated as one of several open conjectures concerning Optimal AdaBoost dynamics. Related work by Belanich and Ortiz on convergence properties of Optimal AdaBoost (arXiv:1212.1108) provides partial evidence for related conjectures (cycling, ergodicity, convergence of the classifier under mild conditions) but does not establish this measure-zero decision-boundary statement. No subsequent resolution was located.

original_question: In the same decision-stump setting where X = [0, 1]^n, H_b is the midpoint-rule stump class induced by the dataset, E_b is the effective stump set obtained after removing dominated stumps, and U_b^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t} is the set of unique decision stumps selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_b during T rounds, is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D sampled from P, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0 and T > T_0, the conditional expectation E[|U_b^T| | D] is bounded above by (log T + 1)^c for some c in [1, 2), P-almost surely?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X=[0,1]^n$ and consider binary classification with labels in $\{-1,+1\}$. A decision stump is a classifier of the form $h_{j,\theta,s}(x)=s\cdot\mathrm{sign}(x_j-\theta)$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, $\theta\in[0,1]$, $s\in\{-1,+1\}$. Given a dataset $D=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ sampled i.i.d. from a probability space $(\mathcal D,\Sigma,P)$ on $X\times\{-1,+1\}$, define the midpoint-rule stump class $H_b$ to consist of all stumps whose threshold $\theta$ is the midpoint between two consecutive observed values of some coordinate $j$ in $D$ (together with the two extreme stumps in each coordinate). Let $E_b\subseteq H_b$ be the effective stump set obtained from $H_b$ by removing every stump that is (weakly) dominated, in empirical error on $D$ over all reweightings, by another stump in $H_b$.

Run Optimal AdaBoost on $D$ using $E_b$ as the weak-hypothesis class: at every round $t=1,2,\dots$, the algorithm selects $h_t\in E_b$ minimizing the weighted error under the current distribution on $D$. Define
$$U_b^T \;=\; \bigcup_{t=1}^{T}\{h_t\}\subseteq E_b,$$
the set of unique decision stumps chosen during the first $T$ rounds.

Let $\mu$ be a fixed prior measure on the space of probability measures on $X\times\{-1,+1\}$.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Convex-core boundary metrics determine GHMC structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let T be its Teichmüller space, and let m_- and m_+ be two points of T. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M = S × R such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of the convex core are m_- and m_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote its Teichmüller space, i.e., the space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structure on $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ is a Lorentzian metric $h$ on $M$ of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $(M,h)$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $S \times \{0\}$, the inclusion of any Cauchy surface induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and $(M,h)$ is maximal among such structures (it admits no isometric extension to a larger spacetime with the same property). Each such GHMC anti-de Sitter spacetime contains a convex core, the smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset that is a deformation retract of $M$; when the holonomy is not Fuchsian, the boundary of the convex core has two connected components, each a pleated spacelike surface whose induced metric is a hyperbolic metric on $S$, defining a point in $\mathcal{T}(S)$.

Question: Given any two points $m_-, m_+ \in \mathcal{T}(S)$, does there exist a unique GHMC anti-de Sitter structure $h$ on $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ (up to isotopy) such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of its convex core are exactly $m_-$ and $m_+$?
status_search_result: The existence part of this conjecture (every pair $(m_-,m_+)$ is realized) was established by Diallo. Uniqueness (rigidity) is known only near the Fuchsian locus: Bonsante–Schlenker proved rigidity near the Fuchsian locus in the context of pleating laminations, and recent work by Prosanov (2025/2026) establishes rigidity of GHMC AdS (2+1)-spacetimes with convex boundary near the Fuchsian locus, including induced-metric rigidity for smooth/polyhedral strictly convex boundaries with holonomy close to Fuchsian. The full uniqueness (rigidity) part of the conjecture remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: For a closed surface S of genus at least 2 with Teichmüller space T, define U : T × T → T × T by sending a pair of hyperbolic metrics (h_l,h_r) to the midpoints (h_-,h_+) of the left and right earthquake paths from h_l to h_r. Is U a homeomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote its Teichmüller space, the space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$. By Thurston's Earthquake Theorem, given any ordered pair $(h_l, h_r) \in \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S)$, there exist unique measured geodesic laminations $\lambda_L$ and $\lambda_R$ on $S$ such that the left earthquake along $\lambda_L$ takes $h_l$ to $h_r$, and the right earthquake along $\lambda_R$ takes $h_l$ to $h_r$. For $t \in [0,1]$, let $E^L_{t\lambda_L}(h_l)$ and $E^R_{t\lambda_R}(h_l)$ denote the left and right earthquake paths from $h_l$ to $h_r$, respectively. Define
$$U : \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S), \qquad U(h_l, h_r) = (h_-, h_+),$$
where $h_- = E^L_{\frac{1}{2}\lambda_L}(h_l)$ is the midpoint of the left earthquake path and $h_+ = E^R_{\frac{1}{2}\lambda_R}(h_l)$ is the midpoint of the right earthquake path. Determine whether $U$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S)$ onto itself.
status_search_result: Web search returned related work by Bonsante–Schlenker on cyclic extensions of the earthquake flow and circle actions on $\mathcal{T}\times\mathcal{T}$, but no explicit resolution of whether the earthquake midpoint map $U$ is a homeomorphism was found. The status appears unresolved in the available sources.

context_brief: Bounds on effective and selected stumps
original_question: Consider the decision-stump specialization of Optimal AdaBoost in which the feature space is X = [0, 1]^n and the labeled example space is D = [0, 1]^n x {-1, +1}. Let H_hat be the finite set of decision stumps induced on a finite dataset D by the midpoint rule: for each feature dimension i, project D along that dimension and, whenever two distinct consecutive examples have different labels, create a stump using the midpoint x'_i = (x_i^(l_j) + x_i^(l_{j+1})) / 2 and h(x) = sign(x_i - x'_i). Remove every dominated hypothesis h in H_hat for which there exists another h' in H_hat such that h'(x^(l)) != y^(l) implies h(x^(l)) != y^(l) for every l = 1, ..., m, and call the resulting effective set E_hat. Let U_hat^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t} be the set of unique decision stumps actually selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_hat after T rounds. Given a measurable space (D, Sigma, P), a dataset D sampled from P, and the number of rounds T, provide non-trivial upper and lower bounds on |H_hat|, |E_hat|, and |U_hat^T|.
self_contained_problem:
Let n, m, T be positive integers. Take the feature space X = [0,1]^n and the labeled-example space D = [0,1]^n × {−1, +1}. Fix a measurable space (D, Σ, P) and let a dataset D = {(x^(l), y^(l)) : l = 1, …, m} be drawn i.i.d. from P.

For each feature dimension i ∈ {1, …, n}, sort the examples by their i-th coordinate, obtaining an ordering l_1, l_2, …, l_m (depending on i). For every pair of consecutive examples in this ordering whose i-th coordinates are distinct and whose labels differ, y^(l_j) ≠ y^(l_{j+1}), define the midpoint x'_i = (x_i^(l_j) + x_i^(l_{j+1}))/2 and form the decision stump h(x) = sign(x_i − x'_i). Let Ĥ denote the (finite) collection of all stumps produced this way over all dimensions and consecutive pairs (the "midpoint rule" stumps).

Call h ∈ Ĥ dominated if there exists h' ∈ Ĥ such that for every l ∈ {1, …, m},
   h'(x^(l)) ≠ y^(l)  ⟹  h(x^(l)) ≠ y^(l).
Remove all dominated hypotheses from Ĥ to obtain the effective set Ê.

Run Optimal AdaBoost on D using Ê as the weak-hypothesis class for T rounds, and let h_1, …, h_T be the stumps it selects. Define
   Û^T = ⋃_{t=1}^T {h_t}.

Problem. Provide non-trivial upper and lower bounds (in terms of n, m, T, and the structure of D and P) on each of the cardinalities |Ĥ|, |Ê|, and |Û^T|.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem ("Problem 1: Bounding the Number of Effective Stumps") in a 2015 preprint listing open problems on Optimal AdaBoost and decision stumps. A web search returns the original 2015 listing but no later work providing the requested non-trivial bounds on |Ĥ|, |Ê|, and |Û^T|, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let RT^2_2 be the statement that every 2-coloring of pairs of natural numbers has an infinite homogeneous set, let SRT^2_2 be its restriction to stable colorings, and let COH be the statement that every uniform sequence of sets has an infinite cohesive set. Over ω-models, does SRT^2_2 imply RT^2_2, equivalently, does SRT^2_2 imply COH?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of second-order arithmetic / reverse mathematics. Define the following principles:

- RT²₂: For every coloring c : [ℕ]² → {0,1} of unordered pairs of natural numbers with two colors, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ that is homogeneous for c (i.e. c is constant on [H]²).
- SRT²₂: The restriction of RT²₂ to stable colorings, where c is stable if for every n ∈ ℕ the limit lim_{m→∞} c({n,m}) exists.
- COH: For every sequence (R_n)_{n∈ℕ} of subsets of ℕ, there exists an infinite set C ⊆ ℕ that is cohesive for the sequence, meaning that for each n, C is almost contained in R_n or almost contained in ℕ ∖ R_n.

An ω-model of RCA₀ is a structure whose first-order part is the standard natural numbers ℕ and whose second-order part is a Turing ideal 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒫(ℕ) (closed under Turing reducibility and join).

Question: Does every ω-model of RCA₀ + SRT²₂ satisfy RT²₂? Equivalently, does every ω-model of RCA₀ + SRT²₂ satisfy COH?
status_search_result: Monin and Patey (2019, "SRT²₂ does not imply RT²₂ in ω-models", arXiv:1905.08427) constructed an ω-model of SRT²₂ that is not a model of COH, thereby answering the question negatively. This resolves a long-standing problem in the reverse mathematics of Ramsey's theorem.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Smooth strictly convex AdS boundary metrics
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be two metrics on S with curvature strictly less than -1 everywhere. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter 3-manifold N with smooth, space-like, strictly convex boundary such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are h_- and h_+, respectively?
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a closed orientable surface of genus at least 2. Recall that an anti-de Sitter (AdS) 3-manifold is a Lorentzian 3-manifold of constant sectional curvature −1. Consider AdS 3-manifolds N diffeomorphic to S × [0,1] whose boundary ∂N consists of two connected components, each a smooth space-like surface that is strictly convex (its second fundamental form is positive definite with respect to the inward normal). The induced Riemannian metric on each boundary component is then well defined.

Given two smooth Riemannian metrics h₋ and h₊ on S, each having Gaussian curvature strictly less than −1 at every point, determine whether there exists a unique (up to isometry) AdS 3-manifold N as above, with smooth space-like strictly convex boundary, such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are isometric to h₋ and h₊ respectively.
status_search_result: Existence has been established: Tamburelli (arXiv:1303.7406) proved that for any two metrics on S with curvature strictly less than −1, there exists a globally hyperbolic AdS manifold diffeomorphic to S × [0,1] with smooth space-like strictly convex boundary realizing the prescribed induced metrics. Uniqueness, however, does not appear to have been established in this two-boundary setting; subsequent work (e.g., Chen–Schlenker, arXiv:2405.01912) addresses uniqueness only in restricted/asymptotic settings (one Cauchy surface with fixed left metric). The full uniqueness question therefore remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Polyhedral AdS boundaries with prescribed cone metrics
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities whose cone angles are greater than 2π. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter manifold with convex polyhedral boundary whose induced boundary metrics are h_- and h_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g \geq 2$. A hyperbolic cone-metric on $S$ is a metric of constant curvature $-1$ on $S$ minus a finite set of points, such that near each removed point the metric is isometric to a hyperbolic cone of some angle $\theta > 0$. Let $h_-$ and $h_+$ be two hyperbolic cone-metrics on $S$ all of whose cone angles are strictly greater than $2\pi$.

A 3-dimensional anti-de Sitter (AdS) manifold is a Lorentzian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Consider globally hyperbolic AdS manifolds $M$ homeomorphic to $S \times [0,1]$ whose boundary consists of two spacelike convex polyhedral surfaces (each isometric to a finite union of totally geodesic spacelike triangles meeting along edges, convex from the side of $M$), one in the past and one in the future of $M$. The induced intrinsic metrics on the two boundary components are then hyperbolic metrics with cone singularities.

Question: Given $h_-$ and $h_+$ as above, does there exist a unique such globally hyperbolic AdS manifold with convex polyhedral boundary whose induced past and future boundary metrics are isometric to $h_-$ and $h_+$ respectively?
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry with polyhedral boundary
status_search_result: Recent work by Prosanov (2025) establishes that any two hyperbolic cone-metrics with cone angles greater than 2π on a closed surface of genus ≥2 can be simultaneously realized as past- and future-convex bent Cauchy surfaces in a GHMC anti-de Sitter (2+1)-spacetime, giving existence in a generalized (bent, not strictly polyhedral) sense. Uniqueness is established only when the cone-metrics are sufficiently small. Thus the question is partially solved: existence in the bent generalization is known, but the full polyhedral existence/uniqueness statement as originally posed does not appear to have a complete answer in the literature.

original_question: Is there a natural computable instance of the stable Ramsey theorem for pairs, SRT^2_2, with no low solution? The intended sense of “natural” is an instance whose difficulty reflects more than the bare fact of having no low solution.
self_contained_problem:
A 2-coloring $c:[\omega]^2 	o 2$ of unordered pairs of natural numbers is called stable if for every $x \in \omega$ the limit $\lim_{y	o\infty} c(\{x,y\})$ exists. An infinite set $H \subseteq \omega$ is homogeneous for $c$ if $c$ is constant on $[H]^2$. The stable Ramsey theorem for pairs ($\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$) asserts that every stable 2-coloring of $[\omega]^2$ admits an infinite homogeneous set; an instance of $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ is such a coloring, and a solution is an infinite homogeneous set for it. A Turing degree $\mathbf{a}$ is low if $\mathbf{a}' = \mathbf{0}'$.

Downey, Hirschfeldt, Lempp, and Solomon constructed a computable stable 2-coloring of $[\omega]^2$ no infinite homogeneous set of which has low Turing degree. Such an instance is, however, produced by a diagonalization whose only manifest feature is the absence of low solutions.

Problem. Exhibit a computable instance of $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ — i.e., a computable stable 2-coloring $c:[\omega]^2	o 2$ — that is "natural" in the following sense: its construction (or its description as a specific combinatorial or computability-theoretic object) carries informational content beyond merely encoding the requirement of having no low infinite homogeneous set, while still admitting no infinite homogeneous set of low Turing degree. Equivalently, find a natural computable stable coloring of pairs every solution of which computes a non-low set, where naturality is to be witnessed by features of the instance itself rather than by the bare diagonalization against low solutions.
category_tag: Ramsey theorem for pairs / reverse mathematics
status_search_result: A search did not turn up an explicit resolution of this question. Subsequent work by Monin–Patey, Cholak–Dzhafarov–Hirschfeldt–Patey, and others has addressed related problems on $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ (e.g., the SRT$^2_2$ vs. COH problem, low${}_2$ basis theorems, and absence of universal instances), but these do not appear to settle the question of producing a natural computable $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$-instance with no low solution. Status appears to remain unresolved in the literature surveyed.

original_question: Does every Δ^0_2 set A admit an infinite subset H of either A or its complement such that H is both low^2 and Δ^0_2?
self_contained_problem:
Working in classical computability theory, recall that a set $A \subseteq \omega$ is $\Delta^0_2$ if it is computable from the halting problem $\emptyset'$ (equivalently, $A$ has a computable approximation $\{A_s\}_{s\in\omega}$ with $\lim_s A_s(n) = A(n)$ for every $n$). A set $X \subseteq \omega$ is said to be $\mathrm{low}_2$ if $(X \oplus \emptyset')' \equiv_T \emptyset''$, i.e., the double Turing jump of $X$ is as low as possible.

Question: Does every $\Delta^0_2$ set $A \subseteq \omega$ admit an infinite subset $H \subseteq A$ or an infinite subset $H \subseteq \omega \setminus A$ such that $H$ is simultaneously $\mathrm{low}_2$ and $\Delta^0_2$?
status_search_result: The analogous question with "low" in place of "low_2" was answered negatively by Downey, Hirschfeldt, Lempp, and Solomon (JSL 2001), who constructed a Δ^0_2 set with no infinite low subset in either it or its complement. The strengthened low_2 version (with the additional Δ^0_2 requirement on the homogeneous subset) appears in the context of work on the SRT^2_2 vs. COH problem and does not appear to have been resolved in subsequent literature; recent papers (Cholak–Dzhafarov–Hirschfeldt–Patey 2020 and follow-ups) treat related questions but do not announce a solution.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold M = S × R with closed surface S of genus at least 2, is either the total volume V(M) or the convex-core volume V(C(M)) quasi-equivalent to a natural distance, such as the Teichmüller distance or the Weil–Petersson distance, between the induced metrics on the convex-core boundary or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ carry a globally hyperbolic maximal Cauchy-compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter Lorentzian structure. Such a structure is determined by Mess's parametrization by a pair $(\mu_\ell, \mu_r)$ of hyperbolic metrics on $S$ (the left and right hyperbolic metrics). The manifold $M$ has finite total Lorentzian volume $V(M)$, and contains a smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset $C(M) \subset M$, the convex core, whose boundary (when $M$ is non-Fuchsian) consists of two spacelike pleated surfaces inducing two hyperbolic metrics $m^+, m^-$ on $S$; let $V(C(M))$ denote its volume.

Endow the Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(S)$ with the Teichmüller distance $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}$ and with the Weil–Petersson distance $d_{\mathrm{WP}}$. Recall that two non-negative functions $F, G$ on the same space are said to be quasi-equivalent if there exist constants $A \geq 1$ and $B \geq 0$ with
$$\tfrac{1}{A} G - B \leq F \leq A\, G + B.$$

Question. Is either $V(M)$ or $V(C(M))$, viewed as a function on the deformation space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on $S \times \mathbb{R}$, quasi-equivalent to one of the distances $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}(\mu_\ell, \mu_r)$, $d_{\mathrm{WP}}(\mu_\ell, \mu_r)$, $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}(m^+, m^-)$, or $d_{\mathrm{WP}}(m^+, m^-)$?
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and Teichmüller theory
status_search_result: Partial progress is documented: the volume of GHMC anti-de Sitter manifolds is known to be bounded below by an exponential of the Weil–Petersson distance between the left/right hyperbolic metrics, and is coarsely equivalent to the length of the measured geodesic lamination of the associated earthquake (Bonsante–Seppi). However, a full quasi-equivalence between $V(M)$ or $V(C(M))$ and the Teichmüller or Weil–Petersson distance does not appear to have been established in the literature, so the question seems to remain partially open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Is the total volume V(M) of a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold minimized at the Fuchsian locus?
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a closed orientable surface of genus g ≥ 2. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter 3-manifold is a Lorentzian 3-manifold M of constant sectional curvature −1, diffeomorphic to S × ℝ, that contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface and is maximal (with respect to inclusion) among such manifolds. By a theorem of Mess, the moduli space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on S × ℝ is parametrized by Teich(S) × Teich(S), where Teich(S) is the Teichmüller space of S; the diagonal {(X,X) : X ∈ Teich(S)} is called the Fuchsian locus, consisting of those manifolds whose holonomy preserves a totally geodesic spacelike plane.

Each GHMC anti-de Sitter manifold M has a finite total volume V(M) (defined, e.g., as the volume of its convex core or, equivalently up to convention, the volume bounded by appropriate Cauchy surfaces in a canonical way).

Question: Is V(M) minimized over the moduli space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on S × ℝ precisely at (and only at) the Fuchsian locus?
status_search_result: A 2026 preprint by Mondello and Tholozan, "Minimizing the volume of globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds" (arXiv:2602.14806), proves that the volume of a maximal globally hyperbolic Cauchy-compact anti-de Sitter 3-manifold is at least π²|χ(S)|, with equality if and only if the manifold is Fuchsian, thus answering the question affirmatively. Earlier partial results (e.g., Bonsante–Seppi, GAFA 2017) had established related bounds and local rigidity near the Fuchsian locus.

context_brief: PA-degree jumps for all infinite sides
original_question: Is there a Δ^0_2 set A such that every infinite subset of either A or its complement has jump of PA degree relative to 0′?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:
- A set A ⊆ ℕ is Δ⁰₂ if both A and its complement are limits of computable sequences of finite sets; equivalently, A ≤_T ∅′.
- For X ⊆ ℕ, let X′ denote the Turing jump of X.
- A Turing degree d is a PA degree if it computes a completion of Peano Arithmetic; equivalently, d computes a {0,1}-valued DNC function. We say a set X has PA degree relative to ∅′ if X computes (relative to ∅′) a completion of PA, i.e. the degree of X ⊕ ∅′ is a PA degree over ∅′.

Question:
Does there exist a Δ⁰₂ set A ⊆ ℕ such that for every infinite set G ⊆ ℕ with G ⊆ A or G ⊆ ℕ \ A, the jump G′ has PA degree relative to ∅′?

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Convexity and properness of AdS volume functions
original_question: Fix a closed surface S and a hyperbolic metric h_l on S. For each h_r in Teichmüller space T, let M(h_l,h_r) be the unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold with left and right hyperbolic metrics h_l and h_r. Are the functions h_r ↦ V(M(h_l,h_r)) and h_r ↦ V(C(M(h_l,h_r))) convex? Are they proper? Does each have a unique minimum at h_l?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote the Teichmüller space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$. By a theorem of Mess, for every pair $(h_l, h_r) \in \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S)$ there exists a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter 3-manifold $M(h_l, h_r)$ whose holonomy decomposes (via the identification $\mathrm{Isom}_0(\mathrm{AdS}_3) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$) as a pair of Fuchsian representations with hyperbolic quotients $(S, h_l)$ and $(S, h_r)$. Let $V(M(h_l, h_r))$ denote the total Lorentzian volume of $M(h_l, h_r)$, and let $C(M(h_l, h_r))$ denote its convex core, with volume $V(C(M(h_l, h_r)))$.

Fix $h_l \in \mathcal{T}(S)$ and consider the two functions
$$F_1 : \mathcal{T}(S) \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, \quad h_r \mapsto V(M(h_l, h_r)),$$
$$F_2 : \mathcal{T}(S) \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, \quad h_r \mapsto V(C(M(h_l, h_r))).$$

Determine whether each of $F_1$ and $F_2$ is:
(a) convex with respect to the Weil–Petersson (or some natural) structure on $\mathcal{T}(S)$;
(b) proper as a function on $\mathcal{T}(S)$;
(c) endowed with a unique minimum, attained at $h_r = h_l$ (i.e., the Fuchsian locus).
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and Teichmüller theory
status_search_result: Partial progress is known. Bonsante–Seppi (GAFA 2018) showed that the volume of a GHMC AdS 3-manifold is comparable to minima of $L^1$-energies of maps between hyperbolic surfaces, giving coarse properness-type estimates. A 2026 preprint establishes the sharp lower bound $V(M) \geq \pi^2|\chi(S)|$ with equality iff $M$ is Fuchsian, confirming that $h_l$ is a (global) minimum of $F_1$ at $h_r = h_l$. Full convexity of $F_1$ and $F_2$ on Teichmüller space, and uniqueness/properness in the strict sense for the convex core volume, do not appear to be fully resolved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Topology of higher-dimensional GHMC AdS Cauchy surfaces
original_question: Let n ≥ 1. Are the Cauchy hypersurfaces of every globally hyperbolic maximal compact manifold locally modeled on AdS^(n+1) diffeomorphic to a quotient of H^p × H^q by a uniform lattice in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q), where p + q = n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and consider the (n+1)-dimensional anti–de Sitter space AdS^(n+1), the model Lorentzian manifold of constant sectional curvature −1. A Lorentzian manifold (M, g) is said to be locally modeled on AdS^(n+1) if it is a (G, X)-manifold with X = AdS^(n+1) and G = Isom(AdS^(n+1)); equivalently, every point has a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of AdS^(n+1). Such a manifold is globally hyperbolic if it admits a Cauchy hypersurface (a spacelike hypersurface met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve), and globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) if, in addition, its Cauchy hypersurfaces are compact and (M, g) is maximal among globally hyperbolic AdS spacetimes containing it (no isometric embedding into a strictly larger such spacetime).

For nonnegative integers p, q with p + q = n, let H^p and H^q denote real hyperbolic spaces of dimensions p and q, with isometry groups SO(1, p) and SO(1, q). A uniform lattice Γ ⊂ SO(1, p) × SO(1, q) acts properly discontinuously on H^p × H^q with compact quotient.

Question: Is it true that for every GHMC manifold locally modeled on AdS^(n+1), each Cauchy hypersurface is diffeomorphic to a quotient (H^p × H^q)/Γ for some decomposition p + q = n and some uniform lattice Γ ⊂ SO(1, p) × SO(1, q)?
status_search_result: Recent work on Gromov–Thurston manifolds and anti-de Sitter geometry constructs quasifuchsian GHMC AdS spacetimes (in dimensions ≥ 4) whose Cauchy hypersurfaces are Gromov–Thurston manifolds. Such manifolds are not diffeomorphic — and their fundamental groups are not even commensurable to lattices in any Lie group — to any quotient of H^p × H^q by a uniform lattice in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q). This provides a negative answer to the question.

context_brief: SRT^2_2 versus sequential thin set theorem
original_question: Over ω-models, does SRT^2_2 imply Seq*(TS^1), the sequential version of the thin set theorem for colorings of singletons into ℕ where one set must, up to finite changes, be thin for each instance in a sequence?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of second-order arithmetic / reverse mathematics. An ω-model is a structure for second-order arithmetic whose first-order part is the standard natural numbers ℕ and whose second-order part is some collection of subsets of ℕ closed under Turing reducibility and join.

Define the following principles.

(1) SRT²₂ (Stable Ramsey's Theorem for pairs and 2 colors): For every coloring c : [ℕ]² → 2 that is stable (i.e., for every x ∈ ℕ, lim_{y→∞} c(x,y) exists), there is an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ that is homogeneous for c, meaning c is constant on [H]².

(2) TS¹ (Thin Set Theorem for singletons): For every coloring f : ℕ → ℕ, there exist an infinite set A ⊆ ℕ and a color i ∈ ℕ such that i ∉ f(A); equivalently, A avoids at least one color.

(3) Seq*(TS¹) (the "almost-everywhere" sequential version of TS¹): For every sequence ⟨f_n⟩_{n∈ℕ} of colorings f_n : ℕ → ℕ, there exists a sequence ⟨A_n⟩_{n∈ℕ} of infinite subsets of ℕ such that, for every n, A_n is, up to finite modification, thin for f_n; that is, there exists i_n ∈ ℕ with f_n(A_n) ⊆ ℕ ∖ {i_n} except possibly on a finite subset of A_n.

Question: Does SRT²₂ imply Seq*(TS¹) over ω-models? In other words, is it the case that every ω-model of RCA₀ + SRT²₂ is also a model of Seq*(TS¹)?
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a specific resolution of whether SRT²₂ implies Seq*(TS¹) over ω-models. Related results exist (e.g., Monin–Patey 2019 showing SRT²₂ does not imply RT²₂ over ω-models, and Liu–Patey work on the reverse mathematics of the thin set theorem and on sequential theorems), but none of the located references appear to settle this particular implication.

original_question: Is every globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold a deformation of a GH-standard anti-de Sitter manifold, namely one obtained from a quotient Γ\Ω with Γ contained in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q) ⊂ SO(2,n) for some p + q = n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and consider the model anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^{1,n}$, the Lorentzian symmetric space of constant sectional curvature $-1$, realized as a quadric in $\mathbb{R}^{2,n}$ with isometry group $\mathrm{SO}(2,n)$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter manifold is a Lorentzian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that is globally hyperbolic, admits a compact Cauchy hypersurface, and is maximal among such manifolds with respect to isometric embeddings.

context_brief: Existence of K-time in arbitrary dimension
original_question: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold of arbitrary dimension, does the past of the convex core always admit a K-time, meaning a time function whose level sets have constant Gauss–Killing–Kronecker–Lipschitz curvature ranging in (-∞,0)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti–de Sitter manifold of arbitrary dimension $n+1 \geq 3$; that is, $M$ is a Lorentzian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that contains a compact Cauchy hypersurface and is maximal among such manifolds (any isometric embedding into another globally hyperbolic AdS spacetime with the same Cauchy hypersurface is onto). Let $C(M) \subset M$ denote the convex core of $M$, defined as the smallest non-empty closed convex subset whose inclusion into $M$ is a homotopy equivalence, and let $P(M)$ denote the past of $C(M)$ in $M$.

A $K$-time on an open subset $U \subset M$ is a smooth time function $\tau : U \to (-\infty, 0)$ (i.e. a function whose gradient is everywhere past-directed timelike) such that for each $c \in (-\infty,0)$ the level set $\tau^{-1}(c)$ is a smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface of $U$ of constant Gauss–Killing–Kronecker–Lipschitz curvature equal to $c$ (for hypersurfaces in higher dimension, this means the determinant of the shape operator with respect to the future-directed unit normal is identically $c$), and such that these level sets foliate $U$ as $c$ ranges over $(-\infty,0)$.

Question: Does the past $P(M)$ of the convex core of every GHMC anti–de Sitter manifold of arbitrary dimension always admit a $K$-time?

original_question: Does Ramsey-type weak König’s lemma, RWKL, admit a universal instance, that is, a computable RWKL-instance whose every solution computes a solution to every other computable RWKL-instance?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of computability theory and reverse mathematics. Identify subsets of ω with their characteristic functions in 2^ω, and let 2^{<ω} denote the set of finite binary strings.

The Ramsey-type weak König's lemma, denoted RWKL, is the following principle. An instance of RWKL is an infinite subtree T ⊆ 2^{<ω} (i.e., a set of finite binary strings closed under taking initial segments and containing strings of every length). A solution to T is an infinite set H ⊆ ω together with a color i ∈ {0,1} such that there exists an infinite path P ∈ [T] (a function P : ω → {0,1} all of whose initial segments lie in T) satisfying P(n) = i for every n ∈ H; equivalently, H is an infinite set such that for some i ∈ {0,1} the tree T has, for every length ℓ, a node σ of length ℓ with σ(n) = i for all n ∈ H ∩ ℓ.

Given a problem P of this form (instances together with their solutions), say that a computable P-instance X is universal if for every computable P-instance Y, every solution to X computes a solution to Y (in the sense of Turing reducibility).

original_question: Let S be a closed surface with marked points x_1, ..., x_n and cone angles θ_1, ..., θ_n in (0,π). If h and h' are hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities of angle θ_i at x_i, is there a unique minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphism from (S,h) to (S,h') that is isotopic to the identity and fixes each x_i?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface, and fix distinct marked points $x_1, \dots, x_n \in S$ together with cone angles $\theta_1, \dots, \theta_n \in (0, \pi)$. A diffeomorphism $\phi : (S, h) \to (S, h')$ is called minimal Lagrangian if its graph is a minimal Lagrangian submanifold of $(S \times S, h \oplus h')$ equipped with the natural symplectic and pseudo-Riemannian structure; equivalently, $\phi$ is area-preserving and there exists a bundle automorphism $b$ of $TS$ that is $h$-self-adjoint, positive, with $\det b = 1$, satisfies the Codazzi equation $d^{\nabla^h} b = 0$, and such that $\phi^* h' = h(b\,\cdot, b\,\cdot)$.

Question: Does there exist a unique minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphism $\phi : (S, h) \to (S, h')$ that is isotopic to the identity and satisfies $\phi(x_i) = x_i$ for each $i = 1, \dots, n$?

original_question: Is there either an instance of RT^1_2, or a computable instance of RT^2_2, whose solutions are RWKL-bounding, meaning that every such solution computes solutions to all computable RWKL-instances?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of computability theory and reverse mathematics. Recall the following principles.

- RT^1_2 (the pigeonhole principle for two colors): an instance is a function f: ω → {0,1}; a solution is an infinite set H ⊆ ω such that f is constant on H.
- RT^2_2 (Ramsey's theorem for pairs and two colors): an instance is a function f: [ω]^2 → {0,1}; a solution is an infinite set H ⊆ ω such that f is constant on [H]^2.
- RWKL (Ramsey-type weak König's lemma): an instance is an infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<ω} together with a coloring c: ω → {0,1}; a solution is an infinite set H ⊆ ω together with a color i ∈ {0,1} and an infinite path P through T such that for every n ∈ H, P(n) = i (equivalently, an infinite homogeneous "path-set" witnessing that some infinite path through T takes a fixed value on H).

A Turing degree d is said to be RWKL-bounding if for every computable RWKL-instance there exists a solution of Turing degree ≤ d. More generally, a set X is RWKL-bounding if deg(X) is RWKL-bounding (in the unrelativized sense above).

Question. Does there exist:
(a) an instance f: ω → {0,1} of RT^1_2 such that every infinite f-homogeneous set H is RWKL-bounding, or
(b) a computable instance f: [ω]^2 → {0,1} of RT^2_2 such that every infinite f-homogeneous set H is RWKL-bounding?

Equivalently: is there a (computable) Ramsey instance at the level of RT^1_2 or RT^2_2 all of whose solutions compute solutions to every computable instance of RWKL?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a paper announcing a resolution of this specific question about the existence of an RT^1_2-instance or computable RT^2_2-instance whose solutions are all RWKL-bounding. Related literature on RWKL, RT^2_2, and degrees bounding principles in reverse mathematics exists, but no clear solution was identified, so the status is recorded as unknown.

original_question: Does RCOLOR_2, the Ramsey-type graph coloring principle asserting that every infinite locally 2-colorable graph has an infinite 2-homogeneous set, imply RWKL, or even imply the existence of a diagonally non-computable function, over RCA_0?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of second-order arithmetic with base theory RCA_0. A (countable, undirected, simple) graph G = (V, E) with V ⊆ ℕ is said to be locally k-colorable if every finite subgraph of G admits a proper k-coloring. A set H ⊆ V is k-homogeneous for G if there is a proper k-coloring of the induced subgraph G ↾ H. Define the principle RCOLOR_k as the statement: "every infinite locally k-colorable graph G = (V, E) has an infinite k-homogeneous set H ⊆ V."

A function f : ℕ → ℕ is diagonally non-computable (DNC) if f(e) ≠ φ_e(e) for every e ∈ ℕ such that φ_e(e) is defined, where (φ_e) is a fixed standard enumeration of the partial computable functions. Let DNC denote the principle "there exists a diagonally non-computable function." Let RWKL (Ramsey-type weak König's lemma) denote the principle: "for every infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<ℕ}, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ and a color i ∈ {0,1} such that for every n there is some σ ∈ T of length n with σ(j) = i for all j ∈ H ∩ n."

Question: Does RCOLOR_2 imply RWKL over RCA_0? Does RCOLOR_2 even imply DNC over RCA_0?
status_search_result: A related paper by Patey (arXiv:1412.0917) establishes the converse non-implication: for every computable order h, there is an ω-model of DNR_h which is not a model of RCOLOR_2, so DNR does not imply RCOLOR_2. However, the direction asked here — whether RCOLOR_2 implies DNC, or RWKL, over RCA_0 — does not appear to be resolved in the sources located, and is listed among open questions about Ramsey-type statements in reverse mathematics. Status could not be definitively confirmed as solved.

original_question: Does the Erdős-Moser theorem EM admit a universal instance, that is, a computable EM-instance whose every solution computes solutions to all computable EM-instances?
self_contained_problem:
A tournament on a set $V$ is an irreflexive binary relation $T \subseteq V \times V$ such that for every pair of distinct $x, y \in V$, exactly one of $T(x,y)$ or $T(y,x)$ holds. A tournament is transitive if the relation $T$ is transitive. The Erdős–Moser theorem (EM) asserts that every infinite tournament on $\mathbb{N}$ admits an infinite transitive subtournament.

An EM-instance is an infinite tournament $T$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and a solution to $T$ is (the characteristic function of) an infinite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ on which $T$ is transitive. An EM-instance is computable if $T$ is a computable relation.

Question: Does there exist a computable EM-instance $T^*$ that is universal in the following sense: for every solution $S$ to $T^*$ and every computable EM-instance $T$, $S$ computes some solution to $T$?
status_search_result: Liu and Patey answered the question negatively: the Erdős–Moser theorem does not admit a universal computable instance. The result appears in their work "The reverse mathematics of the thin set and Erdős–Moser theorems" (Journal of Symbolic Logic, 2022).

original_question: Does the Erdős-Moser theorem EM imply cohesiveness COH over RCA_0?
self_contained_problem:
Work in second-order arithmetic with the base theory RCA₀ (recursive comprehension axiom).

Definitions:
- For sets X, Y ⊆ ℕ, write X ⊆* Y to mean X \ Y is finite.
- A tournament on ℕ is an irreflexive binary relation T ⊆ ℕ × ℕ such that for all distinct x, y ∈ ℕ, exactly one of T(x,y), T(y,x) holds.
- A tournament T is transitive on a set H ⊆ ℕ if for all x, y, z ∈ H, T(x,y) ∧ T(y,z) → T(x,z).

context_brief: Geometric detection of proper actions on AdS^3
original_question: Let S be the interior of a compact surface with boundary, let h_l and h_r be complete convex cocompact hyperbolic metrics on S, and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) be the corresponding holonomies. How can one detect geometrically whether the action of (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(S)) on AdS^3 is proper or non-proper from the hyperbolic metrics on the boundary components of the convex core or from the bending laminations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be the interior of a compact orientable surface with non-empty boundary, and let $h_l$ and $h_r$ be two complete convex cocompact hyperbolic metrics on $S$ (so each $(S,h_\bullet)$ is the interior of a compact convex core inside a convex cocompact hyperbolic surface with funnels). Let $\rho_l, \rho_r : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the corresponding holonomy representations.

Identify $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ with the Lie group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ equipped with (a multiple of) its Killing form, so that $\mathrm{Isom}_0(\mathrm{AdS}^3) \cong \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ acts by left and right multiplication. Consider the diagonal-type action of $\pi_1(S)$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ given by
$$(\rho_l, \rho_r)(\gamma)\cdot x = \rho_l(\gamma)\, x\, \rho_r(\gamma)^{-1}, \qquad \gamma \in \pi_1(S).$$

For each metric $h_\bullet$ ($\bullet \in \{l,r\}$), the boundary $\partial C_\bullet$ of the convex core of $(S,h_\bullet)$ carries an induced hyperbolic metric on its boundary components, together with a measured bending lamination $\beta_\bullet$ on these components.

Question: Give a geometric criterion, expressed purely in terms of either
(a) the induced hyperbolic metrics on the boundary components of the convex cores of $(S,h_l)$ and $(S,h_r)$, or
(b) the bending laminations $\beta_l$ and $\beta_r$ of these convex cores,
which determines whether the action of $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\pi_1(S))$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ is properly discontinuous.

status_search_result: Search results show substantial progress on properness criteria for actions on AdS^3 via Anosov-representation/contraction methods (Guéritaud–Kassel, Danciger–Guéritaud–Kassel, Barbot–Mérigot), giving algebraic/dynamical characterizations of properness. However, no source was found that explicitly resolves the question of reading properness from the induced boundary metrics on the convex cores or directly from the bending laminations of the two convex cocompact hyperbolic structures, so the geometric form of the question appears to remain unresolved.

original_question: Does the Erdős-Moser theorem EM imply 1-GEN over RCA_0, where 1-GEN says that for every set X there exists a real that meets or avoids each Σ^0_1 set of strings relative to X?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the language of second-order arithmetic. Let RCA_0 denote the usual base system (recursive comprehension with Σ^0_1 induction). 

Define the Erdős–Moser theorem (EM) as the statement: for every infinite tournament T on ω (a binary relation T ⊆ ω×ω such that for all distinct x,y exactly one of T(x,y), T(y,x) holds), there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ω on which T is transitive.

For a set X ⊆ ω, a real G ⊆ ω is said to be 1-generic relative to X if for every Σ^0_1(X) set S of finite binary strings, some initial segment of (the characteristic function of) G either lies in S or has no extension lying in S; equivalently, G meets or avoids every Σ^0_1(X) set of strings. context_brief: minimal-degree solutions for EM and RWKL
original_question: Does every computable EM-instance, and even every computable RWKL-instance, admit a solution of minimal Turing degree?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) A tournament on an infinite set X ⊆ ℕ is an irreflexive binary relation T on X such that for every distinct x,y ∈ X exactly one of T(x,y), T(y,x) holds. A tournament T is transitive if T(x,y) and T(y,z) imply T(x,z). The Erdős–Moser principle (EM) states: for every infinite tournament T on ℕ there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ such that the restriction T↾H is transitive. An EM-instance is an infinite tournament on ℕ; a solution is any infinite transitive subtournament. The instance is computable if T (as a subset of ℕ × ℕ) is computable.

(2) For each n, let [n]² = {(i,j) : i < j < n}. A 2-coloring of pairs is a function f : [ℕ]² → 2. A subtree T ⊆ 2^{<ℕ} is an infinite binary tree if it is closed under prefixes and has infinitely many nodes. The Ramsey-type Weak König's Lemma (RWKL) says: for every infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<ℕ} and every 2-coloring c : ℕ → 2, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ and a color i ∈ 2 such that some path through T agrees with the constant color i on every element of H. (Equivalently, in the standard formulation: for every infinite binary tree T and every coloring of ℕ in finitely many colors, there is an infinite H ⊆ ℕ that is "homogeneous" relative to some path through T.) An RWKL-instance is a pair (T, c) of this form, taken to be computable when both T and c are computable; a solution is a corresponding pair (H, P) consisting of an infinite homogeneous set H together with a witnessing path P ∈ [T].

(3) A Turing degree d > 0 is minimal if there is no Turing degree e with 0 < e < d. Equivalently, a set A has minimal Turing degree if A is not computable and every set Turing-reducible to A is either computable or computes A.

Question. Does every computable EM-instance admit a solution of minimal Turing degree? More generally, does every computable RWKL-instance admit a solution of minimal Turing degree?
status_search_result: A targeted search for results on minimal-degree solutions for computable instances of the Erdős–Moser principle and the Ramsey-type Weak König's Lemma did not turn up an explicit affirmative or negative resolution. Subsequent works on EM and RWKL have established related computational-weakness results (e.g., low/low₂-type solutions, non-universality of EM-instances, and arithmetic-reduction weakness), but none of the sources retrieved explicitly answer the minimal-degree question. The status appears to remain open or unresolved in the accessible literature.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let GH be the space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structures on a closed surface bundle M = S × R. Using the maximal-surface parameterization GH ≅ T*Teich(S) and the left-right parameterization GH ≅ Teich(S) × Teich(S), one gets a map φ : T*Teich(S) → Teich(S) × Teich(S). Is φ symplectic, in the sense that the pullback of the difference of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms equals, up to a constant, the canonical cotangent symplectic structure on T*Teich(S)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. Denote by $\mathcal{GH}(M)$ the deformation space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structures on $M$, i.e., maximal globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metrics of constant sectional curvature $-1$ on $M$ admitting a Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$, considered up to isotopy.

There are two classical parameterizations of $\mathcal{GH}(M)$:

(i) Krasnov–Schlenker maximal-surface parameterization: every class in $\mathcal{GH}(M)$ contains a unique embedded spacelike maximal Cauchy surface $\Sigma$. Its induced conformal class $[g]$ defines a point in the Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(S)$, and its second fundamental form is the real part of a holomorphic quadratic differential $q$ on $(\Sigma,[g])$. The map $[(M,h)] \mapsto ([g], q)$ is a diffeomorphism
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{ms}} : \mathcal{GH}(M) \longrightarrow T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S).$$

(ii) Mess left–right parameterization: holonomy considerations identify the holonomy of an AdS GHMC manifold with a pair $(\rho_{\ell},\rho_{r})$ of Fuchsian representations of $\pi_1(S)$, giving a diffeomorphism
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{Mess}} : \mathcal{GH}(M) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S).$$

Let $\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$ denote the Weil–Petersson symplectic form on $\mathcal{T}(S)$, and equip $\mathcal{T}(S)\times\mathcal{T}(S)$ with the difference symplectic form $\omega_{-} := \pi_{1}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}} - \pi_{2}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$. Equip $T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S)$ with its canonical (Liouville) cotangent symplectic form $\omega_{\mathrm{can}}$. Define
$$\varphi := \Phi_{\mathrm{Mess}} \circ \Phi_{\mathrm{ms}}^{-1} : T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S).$$

Question. Is $\varphi$ symplectic up to a constant? That is, does there exist a nonzero constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\varphi^{*}\omega_{-} \;=\; c\,\omega_{\mathrm{can}} \quad\text{on } T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S)?$$
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and Teichmüller theory
status_search_result: The question appears to have been answered affirmatively. Scarinci and Schlenker ("Symplectic Wick rotations between moduli spaces of 3-manifolds", 2018) proved that the natural maps between moduli spaces of GHMC AdS 3-manifolds and related Teichmüller-type spaces are symplectic with respect to the canonical symplectic structures, in particular obtaining symplecticity of the Mess parameterization with respect to the difference of Weil–Petersson forms. Mazzoli–Seppi–Tamburelli ("Para-hyperKähler geometry of the deformation space of maximal globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter three-manifolds", arXiv:2107.10363) place this in a para-hyperKähler framework that explicitly compares the cotangent symplectic structure coming from the Krasnov–Schlenker maximal-surface parameterization with the difference of Weil–Petersson forms via the Mess homeomorphism, identifying the symplectic structures up to a constant.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Harmonic extension of quasisymmetric circle maps
original_question: Let ψ : S^1 → S^1 be an orientation-preserving quasisymmetric homeomorphism. Is there a unique quasiconformal harmonic diffeomorphism φ : H^2 → H^2 that extends continuously to the boundary at infinity and restricts there to ψ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^2$ denote the hyperbolic plane, with ideal boundary at infinity $\partial_\infty \mathbb{H}^2 \cong S^1$. A homeomorphism $\psi: S^1 \to S^1$ is called quasisymmetric if there exists $M \geq 1$ such that for every triple of distinct points $a,b,c \in S^1$ with $|a-b|=|b-c|$ (in arc length on $S^1$), one has $\frac{1}{M} \leq \frac{|\psi(a)-\psi(b)|}{|\psi(b)-\psi(c)|} \leq M$. A diffeomorphism $\varphi: \mathbb{H}^2 \to \mathbb{H}^2$ is called harmonic if it is a critical point of the Dirichlet energy with respect to the hyperbolic metric, equivalently, if its tension field vanishes; it is called quasiconformal if its dilatation $K(\varphi) = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{H}^2}\frac{|\partial \varphi| + |\bar\partial \varphi|}{|\partial \varphi| - |\bar\partial \varphi|}$ is finite.

Prove or disprove: For every orientation-preserving quasisymmetric homeomorphism $\psi: S^1 \to S^1$, there exists a unique quasiconformal harmonic diffeomorphism $\varphi: \mathbb{H}^2 \to \mathbb{H}^2$ that extends continuously to $\overline{\mathbb{H}^2} = \mathbb{H}^2 \cup \partial_\infty \mathbb{H}^2$ and whose restriction to $\partial_\infty \mathbb{H}^2$ equals $\psi$.
category_tag: Harmonic maps and hyperbolic geometry (Schoen conjecture)
status_search_result: This is the Schoen conjecture on harmonic extensions of quasisymmetric maps of the circle. The existence part was proven by Vladimir Marković ("Harmonic maps and the Schoen conjecture", J. Amer. Math. Soc., 2017), establishing that every quasisymmetric homeomorphism of $S^1$ admits a harmonic quasiconformal extension to $\mathbb{H}^2$. Uniqueness had been established earlier (Li–Tam, and others). Hence the conjecture is fully resolved in the affirmative.

context_brief: strictness of free-set and thin-set hierarchies
original_question: Do the free set theorem FS^n, and likewise the thin set theorem TS^n with ω many colors, form strict hierarchies as n increases?
self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 1, write [ω]^n for the set of n-element subsets of the natural numbers ω. Given a coloring f : [ω]^n → ω, an infinite set H ⊆ ω is called f-free if for every σ ∈ [H]^n, f(σ) ∈ H implies f(σ) ∈ σ; H is called f-thin if f([H]^n) ≠ ω, i.e. f omits at least one color on [H]^n. Define the principles:

• FS^n: every coloring f : [ω]^n → ω has an infinite f-free set.
• TS^n (with ω many colors): every coloring f : [ω]^n → ω has an infinite f-thin set.

Working over the base system RCA_0 of second-order arithmetic, decide the following:

(a) Is the sequence (FS^n)_{n ≥ 1} a strict hierarchy? That is, does there exist, for every n ≥ 1, a model of RCA_0 + FS^n that is not a model of FS^{n+1}? Equivalently, does FS^{n+1} fail to be provable from RCA_0 + FS^n for every n?

(b) Is the sequence (TS^n)_{n ≥ 1} (with ω many colors) a strict hierarchy in the same sense, i.e. does RCA_0 + TS^n fail to prove TS^{n+1} for every n ≥ 1?
status_search_result: The strictness of the free-set and ω-color thin-set hierarchies in reverse mathematics is widely cited as an open problem. Surveys of open questions in Ramsey-type reverse mathematics (e.g., Patey's "Open questions about Ramsey-type statements in reverse mathematics" and Cholak–Patey's "Thin set theorems and cone avoidance") explicitly note that, among the Ramsey, free-set, thin-set, and rainbow-Ramsey hierarchies, only Ramsey's theorem is known to collapse, and the strictness of the others remains unresolved. No source found establishes a strict separation FS^n ↛ FS^{n+1} or TS^n ↛ TS^{n+1} for all n.

original_question: For every n ≥ 3, does every computable instance of FS^n, respectively TS^n, admit a low^n solution?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of computability theory and reverse mathematics on the natural numbers $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and an integer $n \geq 1$, write $[X]^n$ for the collection of $n$-element subsets of $X$. A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is called low${}_n$ if its $n$-th Turing jump satisfies $A^{(n)} \leq_T \emptyset^{(n)}$.

For each integer $n \geq 1$ define the following two principles.

(i) Free set theorem $\mathsf{FS}^n$: For every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n 	o \mathbb{N}$, there exists an infinite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $s \in [H]^n$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$. Such an $H$ is called a free set for $f$, and $f$ is called an instance of $\mathsf{FS}^n$.

(ii) Thin set theorem $\mathsf{TS}^n$: For every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n 	o \mathbb{N}$, there exists an infinite set $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and some $i \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f(s) 
eq i$ for every $s \in [T]^n$. Such a $T$ is called a thin set for $f$, and $f$ is called an instance of $\mathsf{TS}^n$.

An instance $f$ is computable if $f$, viewed as a function $[\mathbb{N}]^n 	o \mathbb{N}$, is computable.

Question: For every integer $n \geq 3$, does every computable instance of $\mathsf{FS}^n$ admit a low${}_n$ free set? Likewise, does every computable instance of $\mathsf{TS}^n$ admit a low${}_n$ thin set?
status_search_result: Web searches surface the principles $\mathsf{FS}^n$ and $\mathsf{TS}^n$ as active topics in reverse mathematics, with related results on cone avoidance and on low${}_2$ solutions for $n=2$, but no source clearly resolves the question of low${}_n$ solutions to all computable instances of $\mathsf{FS}^n$ or $\mathsf{TS}^n$ for $n\geq 3$. The current status appears to be unresolved based on available evidence.

context_brief: CMC foliations with prescribed boundary at infinity
original_question: Let Λ ⊂ ∂_∞AdS^3 be the graph of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism RP^1 → RP^1, and let D be the domain of dependence defined by Λ. Is there a unique foliation of D by spacelike constant-mean-curvature surfaces with bounded principal curvatures and boundary at infinity Λ?
self_contained_problem:
Work in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$, the Lorentzian symmetric space of constant sectional curvature $-1$, with conformal boundary at infinity $\partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3$ naturally identified with the Einstein universe of dimension $2$, foliated by two transverse families of projective lines $\mathbb{RP}^1$. Let $\phi : \mathbb{RP}^1 \to \mathbb{RP}^1$ be a quasisymmetric homeomorphism, and let $\Lambda \subset \partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3$ be its graph, an acausal topological circle in the boundary. Let $D \subset \mathrm{AdS}^3$ be the invisible domain (domain of dependence) of $\Lambda$, namely the set of points whose dual spacelike plane is disjoint from $\Lambda$; equivalently, $D$ is the maximal globally hyperbolic convex domain whose boundary at infinity is $\Lambda$.

Question: Does there exist a unique foliation of $D$ by spacelike surfaces of constant mean curvature, each with uniformly bounded principal curvatures, whose asymptotic boundary at infinity equals $\Lambda$, and such that the mean curvature varies monotonically across the leaves taking every value in $(-\infty,\infty)$?
category_tag: CMC foliations in anti-de Sitter geometry
status_search_result: A. Tamburelli (arXiv:1610.08867, published in Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2019) proves that for the domain of dependence $D$ associated to the graph $\Lambda$ of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism $\mathbb{RP}^1\to\mathbb{RP}^1$, there exists a unique foliation of $D$ by constant mean curvature spacelike surfaces with bounded second fundamental form and asymptotic boundary $\Lambda$. This affirmatively resolves the question.

original_question: For every n ≥ 3, does every Δ^0_n set admit an infinite low^n subset of either the set or its complement?
self_contained_problem:
Work in classical computability theory on $\omega = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. For $n \geq 1$, a set $A \subseteq \omega$ is $\Delta^0_n$ if it is definable by both a $\Sigma^0_n$ and a $\Pi^0_n$ formula in the arithmetical hierarchy; equivalently, $A \leq_T \emptyset^{(n-1)}$, the $(n-1)$st Turing jump of the empty set. A set $X \subseteq \omega$ is called $\mathrm{low}_n$ if its $n$th Turing jump satisfies $X^{(n)} \equiv_T \emptyset^{(n)}$.

Question: For every integer $n \geq 3$ and every $\Delta^0_n$ set $A \subseteq \omega$, does there exist an infinite $\mathrm{low}_n$ set $H$ such that either $H \subseteq A$ or $H \subseteq \omega \setminus A$?
status_search_result: The analogous question at level $n=2$ was answered negatively by Downey, Hirschfeldt, Lempp, and Solomon (JSL, 2001), who constructed a $\Delta^0_2$ set with no infinite low subset in either it or its complement. The corresponding question for $n \geq 3$ (with $\mathrm{low}_n$ in place of low) appears as an explicit open question in surveys of Ramsey-type problems in reverse mathematics, and no resolution was found in the literature.

original_question: Let (X, d) be a complete metric space, and let T: X -> C(X) be a multivalued mapping such that each value T(x) is closed and, for all x, y in X, the Hausdorff distance H(Tx, Ty) satisfies H(Tx, Ty) < phi(d(x, y)), where phi: [0, +infinity) -> [0, +infinity) is an L-function in the sense that phi(0) = 0, phi(s) > 0 for every s > 0, and for every s > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that phi(t) <= s for all t in a right-neighborhood [delta, delta + epsilon]. Must T have a fixed point, meaning a point x in X such that x belongs to T(x)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a complete metric space, and let $C(X)$ denote the family of nonempty closed subsets of $X$. The Hausdorff (generalized) distance between $A,B\in C(X)$ is
$$H(A,B)=\max\Big\{\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}d(a,b),\ \sup_{b\in B}\inf_{a\in A}d(a,b)\Big\}.$$
A function $\varphi:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ is called an L-function if $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi(s)>0$ for every $s>0$, and for every $s>0$ there exist $\delta>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\varphi(t)\le s$ for every $t\in[\delta,\delta+\varepsilon]$.

Suppose $T:X\to C(X)$ is a multivalued mapping such that $T(x)$ is closed for every $x\in X$ and
$$H(T(x),T(y))<\varphi(d(x,y))\quad\text{for all }x,y\in X\text{ with }x\ne y,$$
where $\varphi$ is an L-function.

Question: Must $T$ have a fixed point, i.e., a point $x\in X$ with $x\in T(x)$?
status_search_result: A brief web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this multivalued fixed-point question for L-function contractions in complete metric spaces. A weighted multicurve on $S$ is a finite formal sum $\sum_i a_i \gamma_i$, with $a_i > 0$ and $\gamma_i$ pairwise disjoint simple closed geodesics, regarded as a measured lamination. A pair $(\ell_-, \ell_+)$ of measured laminations is said to fill $S$ if every essential simple closed curve on $S$ has positive total intersection number with $\ell_- + \ell_+$.

Question: Suppose $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ are weighted multicurves on $S$ that together fill $S$. Does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations equal to $\ell_-$ (lower) and $\ell_+$ (upper)?

Let $\Gamma$ be the class of all maps $\gamma:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ that are subadditive (i.e. $\gamma(x+y)\le \gamma(x)+\gamma(y)$ for all $x,y\ge 0$), nondecreasing, continuous, and satisfy $\gamma^{-1}(\{0\})=\{0\}$. A set-valued map $T:X\to CB(X)$ is called weakly contractive if there exists $\theta\in\mathcal A$ with
$$H(Tx,Ty)\ \le\ d(x,y)-\theta(d(x,y))\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in X.$$

Question: must every such weakly contractive set-valued map $T$ admit a fixed point, that is, a point $x\in X$ with $x\in Tx$?

original_question: Does there exist a satisfactory structure theory for nondiscrete prodiscrete groups, and more specifically for abelian nondiscrete prodiscrete groups? original_question: If G is a pro-Lie group and G0 is its identity component, must the quotient group G/G0 be complete? Equivalently in the paper's discussion, is G/G0 always prodiscrete?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a pro-Lie group, that is, a topological group isomorphic (as a topological group) to a closed subgroup of a (possibly infinite) product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups; equivalently, $G$ is a complete Hausdorff topological group such that every identity neighborhood contains a closed normal subgroup $N$ for which $G/N$ is a finite-dimensional Lie group, and $G \cong \varprojlim G/N$. Let $G_0$ denote the identity component of $G$ (the connected component containing the identity), which is a closed normal subgroup. Endow the quotient group $G/G_0$ with the quotient topology, making it a Hausdorff topological group.

A topological group $H$ is called complete if every Cauchy filter on $H$ (with respect to the two-sided uniformity) converges in $H$. A topological group is called prodiscrete if it is isomorphic, as a topological group, to a projective limit of discrete groups; equivalently, it is a complete Hausdorff topological group whose open normal subgroups form a basis of identity neighborhoods.

Question: Must the quotient group $G/G_0$ be complete? Equivalently, must $G/G_0$ always be a prodiscrete topological group?

original_question: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive under Pontryagin duality, meaning that the canonical evaluation morphism from the group to the double dual is an isomorphism of topological groups?
self_contained_problem:
A topological group $G$ is called a pro-Lie group if it is isomorphic, as a topological group, to a projective limit of finite-dimensional real Lie groups. For an abelian Hausdorff topological group $G$, write $\widehat{G}$ for its Pontryagin dual, i.e. the group of continuous homomorphisms $G\to \mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ equipped with the compact-open topology. There is a canonical evaluation homomorphism
$$\alpha_G : G \longrightarrow \widehat{\widehat{G}}, \qquad \alpha_G(g)(\chi)=\chi(g),$$
and $G$ is called reflexive if $\alpha_G$ is an isomorphism of topological groups.

Characterize the abelian pro-Lie groups that are reflexive: give necessary and sufficient conditions on an abelian pro-Lie group $G$ for $\alpha_G$ to be a topological isomorphism onto $\widehat{\widehat{G}}$.
status_search_result: Partial results are known: every almost connected abelian pro-Lie group is known to be reflexive, and its dual structure has been described. However, a full characterization of reflexivity for general (not almost connected) abelian pro-Lie groups does not appear to have been established, and pro-Lie groups with poor reflexivity behavior exist. The general question therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive, in the sense that every subgroup and every Hausdorff quotient group is reflexive?
self_contained_problem:
A topological group $G$ is called a pro-Lie group if it is isomorphic (as a topological group) to a projective limit of finite-dimensional real Lie groups; equivalently, $G$ is complete, Hausdorff, and every identity neighborhood contains a closed normal subgroup $N$ such that $G/N$ is a finite-dimensional Lie group. There is a canonical evaluation homomorphism $\alpha_G : G \to G^{\wedge\wedge}$, $\alpha_G(g)(\chi) = \chi(g)$. The group $G$ is called reflexive (or Pontryagin reflexive) when $\alpha_G$ is an isomorphism of topological groups. Call $G$ strongly reflexive if every closed subgroup of $G$ and every Hausdorff quotient group of $G$ is reflexive.

original_question: Is there a more elaborate duality theory relating real Hopf algebras and weakly complete Hopf algebras in which the pro-Lie group and pro-Lie algebra facts described in the paper play an essential role, and does the existence of weakly complete enveloping algebras of weakly complete Lie algebras imply that for every pro-Lie algebra L there is an associative weakly complete Hopf algebra U(L) such that L is isomorphic to a closed Lie subalgebra of the primitive elements P(U(L))?
self_contained_problem:
A weakly complete topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ is a real topological vector space isomorphic (as a topological vector space) to $\mathbb{R}^X$ with the product topology, for some set $X$. A pro-Lie algebra is a topological real Lie algebra that is isomorphic, as a topological Lie algebra, to a strict projective limit of finite-dimensional real Lie algebras; the underlying topological vector space of any pro-Lie algebra is weakly complete. For a weakly complete Hopf algebra $H$ with comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, the set of primitive elements is $P(H) = \{x \in H : \Delta(x) = x \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes x\}$, which is a closed Lie subalgebra of $H$ under the commutator bracket.

(b) Assuming that every weakly complete Lie algebra admits a weakly complete universal enveloping algebra, prove or disprove the following: for every pro-Lie algebra $L$ there exists an associative weakly complete Hopf algebra $U(L)$ such that $L$ is isomorphic, as a topological Lie algebra, to a closed Lie subalgebra of $P(U(L))$.

original_question: Is every transfinitely nilpotent connected pro-Lie group pronilpotent?
self_contained_problem:

context_brief: Sign-changing limit as delta tends to zero
original_question: Consider the Kirchhoff-type Brezis-Nirenberg problem on a smooth bounded domain Omega subset R^4 with Dirichlet boundary condition u = 0 on dOmega, given by -(a + b integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx) Delta u = lambda u + delta|u|^2u, where a > 0, b > 0, lambda > a lambda_1, and 0 < delta < bS^2. Let (1.4) denote the associated eigenvalue problem obtained as the limiting problem when delta -> 0^+. Is there a solution of (1.3), other than the positive ground state solution, that converges to a sign-changing solution of (1.4) as delta -> 0^+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ be a smooth bounded domain. Fix constants $a>0$ and $b>0$, and let $S$ denote the best Sobolev constant for the embedding $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^4)\hookrightarrow L^4(\mathbb{R}^4)$, i.e.
$$S=\inf_{u\in D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^4)\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}^4}|\nabla u|^2\,dx}{\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^4}|u|^4\,dx\right)^{1/2}}.$$
Let $\lambda_1>0$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$. For parameters $\lambda>a\lambda_1$ and $0<\delta<bS^2$, consider the Kirchhoff-type Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$(P_\delta)\qquad -\Bigl(a+b\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\Bigr)\Delta u=\lambda u+\delta|u|^2u\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$
The formal limit problem as $\delta\to 0^+$ is the Kirchhoff eigenvalue-type problem
$$(P_0)\qquad -\Bigl(a+b\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\Bigr)\Delta u=\lambda u\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$

original_question: For the Kirchhoff-type Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.3) on a smooth bounded domain Omega subset R^4 with u = 0 on dOmega and equation -(a + b integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx) Delta u = lambda u + delta|u|^2u, when lambda >= a lambda_1 and delta > bS^2, does there exist a ground state solution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let $a, b > 0$ and $\lambda, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$ be parameters. Consider the Kirchhoff-type Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$
-\Bigl(a + b\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx\Bigr)\Delta u = \lambda u + \delta |u|^2 u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega.
$$
Weak solutions are critical points in $H_0^1(\Omega)$ of the energy functional
$$
I(u) = \frac{a}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + \frac{b}{4}\Bigl(\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx\Bigr)^2 - \frac{\lambda}{2}\int_\Omega u^2\,dx - \frac{\delta}{4}\int_\Omega u^4\,dx.
$$
A ground state solution is a nontrivial weak solution that minimizes $I$ among all nontrivial weak solutions. Let $\lambda_1 > 0$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, and let
$$
S = \inf_{u \in H_0^1(\Omega) \setminus \{0\}} \frac{\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx}{\bigl(\int_\Omega u^4\,dx\bigr)^{1/2}}
$$
be the best constant of the Sobolev embedding $H_0^1(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^4(\Omega)$.

Question: When $\lambda \ge a\lambda_1$ and $\delta > b S^2$, does the problem admit a ground state solution?

context_brief: Sharpness of the L < L_max(ε, λ_1) existence condition
original_question: For the semilinear Dirichlet problem on an arbitrary open set Omega subset of R^d, given by -Delta u(x) = f(x, u(x), grad u(x)) for x in Omega and u(x) = 0 on the boundary of Omega, where f satisfies the coerciveness bound f(x, s, xi)s <= (lambda_1 - epsilon)s^2 + L|xi s| + h(x)|s| with epsilon > 0 and lambda_1 the optimal Poincare-Steklov constant, is the restriction L < L_max(epsilon, lambda_1) actually necessary for existence of weak solutions? Equivalently, if one allows L >= L_max(epsilon, lambda_1), must existence fail?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be an arbitrary open set, and consider the semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$-\Delta u(x) = f(x, u(x), \nabla u(x)) \quad \text{for } x \in \Omega, \qquad u(x) = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
sought in the weak sense $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$. Let $\lambda_1 = \lambda_1(\Omega) > 0$ denote the optimal Poincaré–Steklov constant, i.e., the largest constant such that
$$\lambda_1 \int_\Omega u^2 \, dx \le \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2 \, dx \qquad \forall\, u \in H_0^1(\Omega).$$
Assume the Carathéodory nonlinearity $f : \Omega \times \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies the coerciveness/growth condition
$$f(x, s, \xi)\, s \le (\lambda_1 - \varepsilon) s^2 + L\, |\xi\, s| + h(x)\,|s| \qquad \forall\, x \in \Omega,\ s \in \mathbb{R},\ \xi \in \mathbb{R}^d,$$
for some $\varepsilon > 0$, $L > 0$, and $h \in L^2(\Omega)$. There is a known constant $L_{\max}(\varepsilon, \lambda_1) > 0$ such that the strict inequality $L < L_{\max}(\varepsilon, \lambda_1)$ guarantees the existence of a weak solution.

Question: Is the bound $L < L_{\max}(\varepsilon, \lambda_1)$ sharp? Equivalently, does there exist an open set $\Omega$, a function $h \in L^2(\Omega)$, and a nonlinearity $f$ satisfying the above condition with some $\varepsilon > 0$ and $L \ge L_{\max}(\varepsilon, \lambda_1)$ for which the Dirichlet problem admits no weak solution?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not reveal any subsequent work establishing or refuting the sharpness of the threshold $L_{\max}(\varepsilon, \lambda_1)$ for existence in this class of semilinear Dirichlet problems on arbitrary open sets. No published resolution was located.

context_brief: Optimality of the Robin-setting L^{q**} a priori bounds
original_question: For the generalized Robin boundary-value problem in which the a priori L^{q**} bounds are derived from an embedding of D(a_S) into L^p(Omega) together with Moser iteration, are those resulting L^{q**} a priori bounds best possible?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary $\partial \Omega$, and let $\beta \in L^{\infty}(\partial\Omega)$ be a non-negative function. Consider the symmetric, closed, densely defined quadratic form on $L^2(\Omega)$ given by
$$ a_S(u,v) = \int_{\Omega} \nabla u \cdot \nabla v \, dx + \int_{\partial \Omega} \beta\, u v \, d\sigma, \qquad u,v \in D(a_S) := H^1(\Omega), $$
which generates the (negative of the) Robin Laplacian $-\Delta_\beta$ on $L^2(\Omega)$. Suppose that $D(a_S) = H^1(\Omega)$ embeds continuously into $L^p(\Omega)$ for some $p \in (2, 2N/(N-2)]$ (with $p<\infty$ if $N=2$), and define the dual exponent $q$ by $1/q + 1/p = 1$. Let $q^{**}$ denote the iterated Sobolev exponent obtained from $q$ via the standard Moser iteration scheme applied to weak solutions $u \in H^1(\Omega)$ of the generalized Robin problem
$$ -\Delta u = f \ \text{in } \Omega, \qquad \partial_\nu u + \beta u = g \ \text{on } \partial\Omega, $$
with data $f \in L^{q}(\Omega)$ and $g \in L^{q_\partial}(\partial\Omega)$ in suitable Lebesgue classes, yielding an a priori bound of the form
$$ \| u \|_{L^{q^{**}}(\Omega)} \le C \big( \| f \|_{L^q(\Omega)} + \| g \|_{L^{q_\partial}(\partial\Omega)} \big). $$

Question: Is the exponent $q^{**}$ in this $L^{q^{**}}$ a priori bound optimal? Equivalently, does there exist no $r > q^{**}$ for which the analogous a priori bound $\| u \|_{L^{r}(\Omega)} \le C (\| f \|_{L^q} + \| g \|_{L^{q_\partial}})$ holds for all weak solutions of the Robin problem above?
status_search_result: The optimality of the $L^{q^{**}}$ a priori bounds derived via Moser iteration in this setting is established; the bounds are best possible, as shown by a result on optimal Sobolev-type embeddings and elliptic regularity of Daners (Theorem 5.11 in his 2000 work on Robin boundary value problems).
