paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
original_question: Let W = { z : C(z) = ∞ } be the exceptional set associated with the comparison inequality ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| <= C(z) * |∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)| from the preceding question. Determine the structure of this exceptional set W inside C^m.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers m ≥ 1 and consider parameters z = (V_1, V_2, …, V_m) ∈ C^m. For each integer n ≥ 1, let X_n^+ = X_n^+(F_m) denote the (combinatorially defined) finite index set of "positive" walks of weighted length n associated with the m-parameter family F_m (the index set arising in the eigenfunction expansions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials of m terms, so that each x ∈ X_n^+ is a finite sequence of admissible jumps and h(x) = h(x; z) is a rational function of z whose factors are products of the coordinates V_j and reciprocals of small denominators built from the jumps in x).

Define
  C(z) := sup_n  ( ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)| ) / | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |  ∈ [0, ∞],
the smallest (possibly infinite) constant for which the comparison inequality
  ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)|  ≤  C(z) · | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |
holds simultaneously for every n ≥ 1.

Let W := { z ∈ C^m : C(z) = ∞ } be the associated exceptional set. Determine the structure of W as a subset of C^m: in particular, decide whether W is a (countable union of) proper analytic / algebraic subvarieties of C^m, describe its dimension and irreducible components, and decide whether C^m \ W has full Lebesgue measure (i.e. whether the comparison inequality holds for almost every z ∈ C^m).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem by Djakov and Mityagin (2012) concerning the structure of the exceptional set in C^m on which a comparison inequality between the absolute and signed sums over walk-type combinatorial objects fails. Subsequent literature on combinatorial identities of Djakov–Mityagin and on convergence/divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials addresses related identities and special cases (e.g. two-term potentials), but no source found resolves the description of the exceptional set W = {z : C(z) = ∞} in general. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Three negative steps in the {-2,+4} model
original_question: Take F = {-2, +4}, so R = 1 and S = 2, and let n = 2m + 1. For admissible walks from -n to n, let X_n(3) be the set of walks having exactly three negative steps equal to -2 and all remaining steps equal to +4. If h_1(x) = ∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1}, define B_3(2m + 1) by B_3(2m + 1) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n(3)} h_1(x). Find an asymptotic formula for the sequence B_3(2m + 1), or at least prove that there exists an absolute constant C for which |B_3(2m + 1)| >= C^m / m!.
self_contained_problem:
Fix the step set F = {-2, +4}. For an odd integer n = 2m+1 with m ≥ 1, an admissible walk from -n to n is a finite sequence of integers

  x = (j(0), j(1), j(2), ..., j(ν))

such that:
 (a) j(0) = -n and j(ν) = n;
 (b) every step j(t) - j(t-1) belongs to F (so each step is either -2 or +4);
 (c) j(t) ≠ ±n for every 1 ≤ t ≤ ν-1 (the walk does not touch ±n strictly between its endpoints).

Let X_n(3) denote the set of admissible walks from -n to n that contain exactly three steps equal to -2 (and consequently exactly m+2 steps equal to +4, so ν = m+5).

For x ∈ X_n(3) define the weight

  h_1(x) = ∏_{t=1}^{ν-1} 1 / (n^2 - j(t)^2),

and set

  B_3(2m+1) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n(3)} h_1(x).

Problem. Determine an asymptotic formula for the sequence B_3(2m+1) as m → ∞. As a weaker goal, prove that there exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that

  |B_3(2m+1)| ≥ C^m / m!   for all sufficiently large m.

original_question: For a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega) and a probability measure mu, determine whether the following are equivalent: first, there exists epsilon_mu > 0 such that exp(-epsilon_mu * PSH(X, omega)) is contained in L^1(mu); second, there exists a Holder continuous omega-plurisubharmonic function phi on X such that mu = MA(phi).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, and let $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ denote the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e., upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi\colon X\to[-\infty,\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that $\omega+dd^c\varphi\geq 0$ in the sense of currents. For a bounded $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$, the Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi):=(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined (where $n=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}X$). 

Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $X$. Consider the following two properties:

(i) There exists $\varepsilon_\mu>0$ such that for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$, the function $e^{-\varepsilon_\mu\varphi}$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$, and moreover the family $\{e^{-\varepsilon_\mu\varphi}:\varphi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega),\ \sup_X\varphi=0\}$ is bounded in $L^1(\mu)$.

(ii) There exists a Hölder continuous $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ such that $\mu=\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$.

Determine whether (i) and (ii) are equivalent.
status_search_result: The implication (ii) ⇒ (i) is well known, while the converse (i) ⇒ (ii) is the difficult direction. Existing characterizations of Monge–Ampère measures admitting Hölder continuous potentials (e.g., via Hölder continuous super-potentials, or via membership in suitable Sobolev/Besov spaces) give sufficient conditions but do not establish the full equivalence with the exponential integrability condition. No published source found that resolves this equivalence; it appears to remain open.

context_brief: PDE proof of Kolodziej sup estimate
original_question: Give a proof, using PDE techniques, of the a priori estimate in Theorem 3.1: if B is the unit ball in C^n, p > 1, phi is a smooth plurisubharmonic function on B with phi|_{partial B} = 0, and det(phi_{jar{k}}) = f, then ||phi||_{L^infty(B)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}, where C depends only on n and p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $B\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Fix $p>1$. Let $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{B})$ be a plurisubharmonic function (i.e., the complex Hessian $(\varphi_{j\bar k})_{j,k=1}^n$ is positive semidefinite) such that $\varphi|_{\partial B}=0$, and write
$$\det(\varphi_{j\bar k}) = f.$$
It is known that there exists a constant $C=C(n,p)>0$, depending only on $n$ and $p$, such that
$$\|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(B)} \;\le\; C\,\|f\|_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}.$$
Provide a proof of this a priori estimate that uses only PDE techniques (such as maximum-principle/ABP-type arguments, auxiliary equations, and integral estimates), without recourse to pluripotential theory.
status_search_result: Błocki (2011) gave a PDE proof using the Alexandrov–Bakelman–Pucci maximum principle for $p>2$. A full PDE proof of the sharp $L^\infty$ estimate for all $p>1$ (and more general settings) was obtained by Guo, Phong and Tong in "On $L^\infty$ estimates for complex Monge–Ampère equations" (arXiv:2106.02224, 2021), using auxiliary Monge–Ampère equations and an ABP-type argument; this resolves the question.

context_brief: Holder regularity for semipositive big classes
original_question: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form, and let phi solve (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f dV with f in L^p for some p > 1. Determine whether phi must be Holder continuous on all of X.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $\omega$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ that is semi-positive (i.e., $\omega \ge 0$ pointwise as a Hermitian form) and big (i.e., the cohomology class $\{\omega\}$ contains a Kähler current; equivalently, $\int_X \omega^n > 0$ together with bigness of the class). Let $dV$ be a smooth volume form on $X$, and let $0 \le f \in L^p(X, dV)$ for some $p > 1$, normalized so that $\int_X f\, dV = \int_X \omega^n$.

Consider the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n = f\, dV$$
for an $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ (i.e., $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous and $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ as a current), where the left-hand side is interpreted as the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure of $\varphi$, and $\varphi$ is normalized (e.g., $\sup_X \varphi = 0$).

Question: must every such solution $\varphi$ be Hölder continuous on all of $X$? That is, does there exist $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $C > 0$ (depending on the data) such that $|\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)| \le C\, d(x,y)^\alpha$ for all $x, y \in X$, where $d$ is the distance induced by a fixed Kähler metric on $X$?
status_search_result: Known results establish Hölder continuity of $\varphi$ on the ample locus of $\{\omega\}$ when $\omega$ is semi-positive and big with $f \in L^p$, $p>1$ (Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi and subsequent work, including stability/Hölder regularity papers in big cohomology classes). However, global Hölder continuity on all of $X$ — including across the non-ample locus where $\omega$ degenerates — remains an open problem; recent literature continues to phrase Hölder regularity statements as holding on the ample locus rather than globally.

original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold, let S be a smooth totally real submanifold of maximal real dimension n, let mu_S be its normalized Hausdorff measure, and let phi_S in E(X, omega) be the unique normalized omega-plurisubharmonic potential with (omega + dd^c phi_S)^n = mu_S. Determine the optimal regularity of phi_S.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $S \subset X$ be a smooth totally real submanifold of maximal real dimension $n$ (so that at every $p \in S$, the real tangent space $T_pS$ satisfies $T_pS \cap J(T_pS) = \{0\}$, where $J$ is the complex structure on $X$). Let $\mu_S$ denote the normalized $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $S$, regarded as a probability measure on $X$. It is known that $S$ is non-pluripolar, and consequently there exists a unique $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi_S$ in the finite-energy class $\mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$, normalized by $\sup_X \varphi_S = 0$, satisfying the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(\omega + dd^c \varphi_S)^n \;=\; \mu_S$$
in the sense of pluripotential theory. Determine the optimal regularity of the potential $\varphi_S$ (for instance, the largest Hölder exponent $\alpha \in (0,1]$, or higher regularity class, that $\varphi_S$ is guaranteed to belong to, and whether this exponent is sharp).
status_search_result: Duc-Viet Vu (Math. Ann., 2016/2018, arXiv:1608.02794) proved that for a probability measure with $L^p$ ($p>1$) density supported on a $C^3$ totally real submanifold of maximal dimension, the complex Monge–Ampère potential is Hölder continuous, which establishes Hölder regularity of $\varphi_S$. The exact optimal Hölder exponent (and whether higher regularity holds) does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the question of optimal regularity remains only partially resolved.

context_brief: smoothness on ample locus for big classes
original_question: Let alpha in H^{1,1}(X, R) be a big cohomology class on a compact manifold in the Fujiki class, let mu be a smooth volume form, and let T be the unique finite-energy current in alpha satisfying <T^n> = mu. Determine whether T is smooth on the ample locus Amp(alpha).
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of dimension $n$ in the Fujiki class (i.e., bimeromorphic to a compact Kähler manifold). Let $\alpha \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ be a big cohomology class, that is, $\alpha$ can be represented by a closed $(1,1)$-current that dominates a Hermitian form. The ample locus $\mathrm{Amp}(\alpha)$ is the largest Zariski open subset of $X$ on which some closed positive current with minimal singularities representing $\alpha$ has locally bounded local potentials. Closed positive $(1,1)$-currents in $\alpha$ admit a non-pluripolar self-intersection product $\langle T^n \rangle$, a positive Borel measure putting no mass on pluripolar sets, and a current $T$ in $\alpha$ is said to have full Monge–Ampère mass (finite energy) when $\int_X \langle T^n \rangle = \mathrm{vol}(\alpha)$.

Let $\mu$ be a smooth positive volume form on $X$ with $\int_X \mu = \mathrm{vol}(\alpha)$, and let $T$ be the unique closed positive $(1,1)$-current with full Monge–Ampère mass in $\alpha$ such that
$$\langle T^n \rangle = \mu.$$

Determine whether $T$ is smooth (i.e., has $C^\infty$ local potentials) on the ample locus $\mathrm{Amp}(\alpha)$.
status_search_result: The smoothness of T on the ample locus is established in the case where the class α is nef and big (Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Acta Math. 2010). For a general big class, only partial regularity (e.g., uniform Hölder regularity on the ample locus, and L^∞ bounds on local potentials) is known, and full C^∞ smoothness on Amp(α) for arbitrary big classes remains open.

original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold, and let phi in E(X, omega) solve (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f omega^n where f is L^1 and smooth away from a divisor D subset X. Determine whether phi is smooth on X minus D.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$. Recall that a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic if $\omega+dd^c\varphi\ge 0$ in the sense of currents. The class $\mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$ consists of those $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi$ whose non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n$ has full mass $\int_X\omega^n$. Let $D\subset X$ be a divisor, and let $f\in L^1(X,\omega^n)$ be a nonnegative function which is $C^\infty$-smooth on $X\setminus D$. Suppose $\varphi\in\mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$ satisfies the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n = f\,\omega^n$$
on $X$. Determine whether $\varphi$ is necessarily smooth on $X\setminus D$.
status_search_result: Di Nezza and Lu have established smoothness off the divisor under additional hypotheses (e.g., suitable integrability or capacity conditions on $f$), and related results appear in subsequent work on complex Monge–Ampère equations on quasi-projective varieties. However, no source found definitively resolves the question in full generality with $f$ only assumed to be $L^1$ and smooth off $D$, so the general status appears unresolved.

original_question: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain in C^n, and let u be the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function on Omega with boundary value 0 and Monge-Ampere equation (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u is automatically smooth.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain (i.e., a connected bounded open set admitting a continuous negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function). Let $f \in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega})$ be a smooth function satisfying $f \geq \varepsilon > 0$ on $\overline{\Omega}$ for some constant $\varepsilon$. Consider the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$ u \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}), \qquad (dd^c u)^n = f\, dV \text{ on } \Omega, \qquad u|_{\partial \Omega} = 0, $$
where $dV$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and the Monge–Ampère operator $(dd^c u)^n$ is defined in the sense of Bedford–Taylor. It is known that there exists a unique such $u$. Determine whether $u$ is necessarily smooth in the interior, i.e., whether $u \in C^\infty(\Omega)$, without any further assumption on the regularity or pseudoconvexity of $\partial\Omega$.
status_search_result: Web sources describe this as an open interior-regularity problem attributed to Błocki: for an arbitrary bounded hyperconvex domain (with no smoothness/strong pseudoconvexity assumption on the boundary) and smooth strictly positive right-hand side, it is not known whether the unique continuous plurisubharmonic solution to the Dirichlet problem is automatically smooth in the interior. The classical results of Krylov and Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg–Spruck handle the smooth strongly pseudoconvex case, but the general hyperconvex case remains unresolved.

original_question: Let Omega be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, and let u be a plurisubharmonic solution of class C^{1,alpha}(Omega) with alpha > 1 - 2/n satisfying (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u must in fact be smooth.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded, smooth, strictly pseudoconvex domain. Let $u \in C^{1,\alpha}(\Omega)$ be a plurisubharmonic function satisfying the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(dd^c u)^n = f\, dV$$
on $\Omega$, where $dV$ is the Euclidean volume form, $f \in C^\infty(\Omega)$, and $f \geq \varepsilon > 0$ for some constant $\varepsilon$. Assume that the Hölder exponent satisfies $\alpha > 1 - \tfrac{2}{n}$. Must $u$ be smooth, i.e. $u \in C^\infty(\Omega)$?
status_search_result: The question is a regularity bootstrap problem associated with Błocki and Dinew. Their 2011 local regularity result for the complex Monge–Ampère equation requires control of the $W^{2,p}$ norm for some $p > n(n-1)$, which is known to be optimal in that framework. No source found in the search confirms a definitive resolution of the specific $C^{1,\alpha}$-bootstrap question with $\alpha > 1 - 2/n$, so its current status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Let Omega be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let varphi belong to C^{1,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, with u = varphi on partial Omega and (dd^c u)^n = 0 in Omega. Prove by complex-analytic methods that u is C^{1,1} on Omega.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smooth, bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let $\varphi \in C^{1,1}(\partial\Omega)$. Let $u$ be the unique plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega$, continuous up to the boundary, satisfying
\[
u = \varphi \text{ on } \partial\Omega, \qquad (dd^c u)^n = 0 \text{ in } \Omega,
\]
where $d = \partial + \bar\partial$ and $d^c = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(\bar\partial - \partial)$, so that $(dd^c u)^n$ denotes the complex Monge–Ampère measure of $u$ in the sense of Bedford–Taylor.

Prove, by complex-analytic methods (i.e. without invoking Krylov's real-variable PDE techniques for fully nonlinear elliptic equations), that $u \in C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.
status_search_result: A 2017 attempt by Dinew–Kołodziej (arXiv:1706.07392) to provide an analytic proof of Krylov's C^{1,1} estimates was withdrawn due to a mistake in the main argument. A more recent 2025 preprint (arXiv:2507.21729) again claims an analytic proof of the Krylov C^{1,1} estimates for solutions of the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère equation, together with an analytic proof of the Bedford–Taylor interior C^{1,1} estimate. The status of a fully accepted, complete complex-analytic proof of interior C^{1,1} regularity in the setting of Demailly's question is therefore best described as partially resolved/under verification rather than definitively settled.

original_question: In the setting of Theorem 3.5, let Omega be a C^{3,1} smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let phi belong to C^{3,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, solving (dd^c u)^n = f in Omega with f >= 0 and f^{1/n} in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). Determine the minimal assumptions under which u belongs to C^2(closure Omega).

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a $C^{3,1}$ smooth bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let $\varphi \in C^{3,1}(\partial\Omega)$. Let $f \geq 0$ be a function on $\Omega$ with $f^{1/n} \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$, and let $u$ be the unique plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega$, continuous up to the boundary, satisfying
$$(dd^c u)^n = f \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \varphi \text{ on } \partial\Omega.$$
It is known that under these hypotheses $u \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$. Determine the minimal regularity assumptions on the domain $\Omega$, the boundary data $\varphi$, and the right-hand side $f$ that guarantee $u \in C^2(\overline{\Omega})$.

original_question: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain and let g_Omega(z,w) be its pluricomplex Green function with pole at w. Determine whether g_Omega(z,w) converges locally uniformly to 0 as the pole w approaches the boundary of Omega.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain (i.e., a bounded domain admitting a continuous negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function). For each $w \in \Omega$, let $g_\Omega(\cdot, w)$ denote the pluricomplex Green function of $\Omega$ with pole at $w$, defined as
$$g_\Omega(z,w) = \sup\{u(z) : u \in PSH(\Omega),\ u < 0,\ u(\zeta) \le \log|\zeta - w| + O(1)\ \text{as } \zeta \to w\}.$$
Determine whether, for every bounded hyperconvex domain $\Omega$, the function $z \mapsto g_\Omega(z, w)$ converges to $0$ locally uniformly on $\Omega$ as $w$ tends to $\partial \Omega$.
status_search_result: The question is a known open problem in pluripotential theory, equivalent to continuity of the Green function up to the boundary diagonal for hyperconvex domains. Partial results exist: convergence holds outside a pluripolar exceptional set (Jensen measures / Czyż–Hed–Persson type results), and full locally uniform convergence is known when the domain admits a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion. No general resolution for arbitrary bounded hyperconvex domains has been found.

context_brief: non-C2 example for one-pole Green function
original_question: Let Omega be a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let g_Omega(.,w) be the pluricomplex Green function with one pole w. Since g_Omega is known to lie in C^{1,1}(Omega \ {w}), determine whether there exists an example for which g_Omega fails to be C^2 on Omega minus the pole.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and for a fixed pole $w \in \Omega$ let $g_\Omega(\cdot, w) : \Omega \to [-\infty, 0)$ denote the pluricomplex Green function with logarithmic pole at $w$, i.e., the unique plurisubharmonic function satisfying
\[
(dd^c g_\Omega(\cdot,w))^n = 0 \text{ on } \Omega \setminus \{w\}, \qquad g_\Omega(z,w) = \log|z-w| + O(1) \text{ as } z \to w,
\]
with boundary values $0$ on $\partial\Omega$. It is known that $g_\Omega(\cdot, w) \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega} \setminus \{w\})$. Decide whether there exists such a domain $\Omega$ and pole $w$ for which $g_\Omega(\cdot, w)$ fails to belong to $C^2(\Omega \setminus \{w\})$.

original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension at least 3. Characterize the Hermitian forms omega for which the total volume integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n equals integral_X omega^n for every bounded omega-plurisubharmonic function phi.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n \ge 3$, where $\omega$ is a smooth positive $(1,1)$-form. A function $\varphi: X \to \mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ in the sense of currents (where $d = \partial+\bar\partial$ and $d^c = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(\bar\partial-\partial)$, so that $dd^c = \tfrac{i}{\pi}\partial\bar\partial$). For a bounded $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the Bedford–Taylor–type product $(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined as a positive Radon measure on $X$.

Give an intrinsic geometric/analytic characterization of those Hermitian forms $\omega$ on $X$ for which
$$\int_X (\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n \;=\; \int_X \omega^n$$
holds for every bounded $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$ on $X$.
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Dinew and Kołodziej, asks for a characterization of Hermitian metrics for which the total Monge–Ampère mass is independent of the bounded ω-psh potential. Sufficient conditions (e.g. pluriclosed/SKT-type or stronger Kähler-like conditions, and balanced/Astheno-Kähler-related conditions ensuring $dd^c\omega^k=0$ for relevant $k$) are known to imply mass invariance, but a complete intrinsic characterization on general compact Hermitian manifolds of dimension ≥ 3 does not appear in the literature; recent works on pluripotential theory on Hermitian manifolds continue to treat this as an open problem.

original_question: For a compact Hermitian manifold (X, omega), define T(X, omega) as the infimum of integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n over smooth omega-plurisubharmonic functions phi. Determine whether T(X, omega) can be equal to 0 for some manifold.
self_contained_problem:

context_brief: remove lower bound in Hermitian stability theorem
original_question: In Theorem 4.3 for Hermitian Monge-Ampere equations, u and v are continuous omega-plurisubharmonic solutions with right-hand sides f and g in L^p, and the stability estimate ||u - v||_infty <= C ||f - g||_p^alpha is proved under the extra assumption f >= c_0 > 0. Determine whether that lower-bound assumption on f can be removed.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n$. A function $u\in L^1(M)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $u$ is upper semicontinuous and $\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u\ge 0$ as a current on $M$. For continuous $\omega$-psh functions, the complex Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u)^n$ is well defined via Bedford–Taylor theory.

Fix $p>1$. Suppose $u,v$ are continuous $\omega$-psh functions on $M$, normalized by $\sup_M u=\sup_M v=0$, satisfying
$$(\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u)^n = f\,\omega^n, \qquad (\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial v)^n = g\,\omega^n,$$
with $f,g\in L^p(M,\omega^n)$, $f,g\ge 0$, and $\int_M f\,\omega^n=\int_M g\,\omega^n=\int_M\omega^n$.

It is known that there exist constants $C>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, depending only on $(M,\omega)$, $p$, and an upper bound for $\|f\|_{L^p}+\|g\|_{L^p}$, such that, under the additional non-degeneracy assumption $f\ge c_0>0$ on $M$,
$$\|u-v\|_{L^\infty(M)} \le C\,\|f-g\|_{L^p}^{\alpha}.$$

Question: Does the same stability estimate
$$\|u-v\|_{L^\infty(M)} \le C\,\|f-g\|_{L^p}^{\alpha}$$
continue to hold without assuming the lower bound $f\ge c_0>0$? That is, can the strict positivity hypothesis on the right-hand side $f$ be removed?

context_brief: prescribed logarithmic poles on Hermitian manifolds
original_question: Let z_1, ..., z_k be points on a Hermitian manifold X, and let tau_1, ..., tau_k be positive numbers satisfying sum_j tau_j^n < integral_X omega^n. Construct an omega-plurisubharmonic function phi such that near each z_j one has phi(z) <= tau_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n$, where $\omega$ is a smooth positive $(1,1)$-form. Let $z_1,\dots,z_k\in X$ be distinct points and let $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_k$ be positive real numbers satisfying
$$\sum_{j=1}^k \tau_j^{\,n} \;<\; \int_X \omega^n.$$
A function $\varphi:X\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic if $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and $\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial\varphi\ge 0$ in the sense of currents.

Construct an $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ such that, in a local coordinate chart centered at each $z_j$, one has
$$\varphi(z) \;\le\; \tau_j\,\log\|z-z_j\| + O(1)$$
as $z\to z_j$, for every $j=1,\dots,k$.

original_question: Determine whether quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be desingularized in every complex dimension n >= 3 in the same sense known in dimensions at most 2, namely after suitable blow-ups separating divisorial singularities from a residual positive current with arbitrarily small Lelong numbers.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ (for instance $X=\mathbb{C}^n$ or a compact Kähler manifold with a fixed Kähler form $\omega$). A function $\varphi:X\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is called quasi-plurisubharmonic (quasi-psh) if it is locally the sum of a plurisubharmonic function and a smooth function; equivalently, $dd^c\varphi+\theta\geq 0$ for some smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta$. The Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $x\in X$ is $\nu(\varphi,x)=\liminf_{z\to x}\varphi(z)/\log|z-x|$.

In complex dimension $n\leq 2$ the following desingularization statement is known: for every quasi-psh function $\varphi$ on $X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a finite composition of blow-ups with smooth centers $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ such that
$$\pi^*\varphi=\sum_{j} a_j\,\log|s_{E_j}|+\psi,$$
where the $E_j$ are exceptional prime divisors of $\pi$, $s_{E_j}$ are local defining sections of $E_j$, $a_j\geq 0$, and $\psi$ is a quasi-psh function on $\widetilde X$ all of whose Lelong numbers are bounded by $\varepsilon$.

Question: Does this desingularization property extend to every dimension $n\geq 3$? That is, given any quasi-psh function $\varphi$ on a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, can one find a sequence of blow-ups along smooth centers after which $\pi^*\varphi$ decomposes as an explicit divisorial part plus a quasi-psh remainder with Lelong numbers $\leq\varepsilon$ everywhere?
status_search_result: A two-dimensional desingularization result for quasi-psh functions is due to Favre–Jonsson (valuative analysis on $\mathbb{C}^2$) and was used by Guedj. Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson extended valuative methods to higher dimensions, but a full higher-dimensional analogue of the divisorial/small-Lelong-number desingularization of quasi-psh functions in dimensions $n\geq 3$ does not appear to have been established in the sources retrieved. The status remains unclear from available evidence.

original_question: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain and phi belong to the Cegrell class F(Omega). If lambda^n = integral_Omega (dd^c phi)^n, determine whether the sublevel volumes satisfy the sharper estimate Vol({phi < -s}) <= c_n * delta_Omega^{2n} * exp(-2 n s lambda^{-1}) for all s > 0, without the polynomial prefactor appearing in the known theorem.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain, i.e., a bounded, connected, open set admitting a continuous, negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. Let $\delta_\Omega$ denote the diameter of $\Omega$. Recall Cegrell's class $\mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, consisting of all plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi : \Omega \to [-\infty, 0)$ such that there exists a decreasing sequence $\varphi_j \in \mathcal{E}_0(\Omega)$ (bounded plurisubharmonic functions with zero boundary values and finite total Monge–Ampère mass) decreasing to $\varphi$ with $\sup_j \int_\Omega (dd^c \varphi_j)^n < \infty$; for $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ the complex Monge–Ampère measure $(dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined as a positive Radon measure of finite total mass.

For $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, set
$$\lambda^n = \int_\Omega (dd^c \varphi)^n, \qquad \lambda > 0.$$
It is known that there exists a constant $c_n > 0$, depending only on $n$, such that for every $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ and every $s > 0$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\{\varphi < -s\}) \le c_n\, \delta_\Omega^{2n} (1 + s\lambda^{-1})^{n-1} \exp(-2n s \lambda^{-1}).$$

Question. Does there exist a constant $c_n' > 0$, depending only on $n$, such that for every bounded hyperconvex $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$, every $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, and every $s > 0$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\{\varphi < -s\}) \le c_n'\, \delta_\Omega^{2n} \exp(-2n s \lambda^{-1})\, ?$$
That is, can the polynomial prefactor $(1 + s\lambda^{-1})^{n-1}$ be removed at the cost of changing the constant?

original_question: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, or more generally a manifold in the Fujiki class, and let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form. If phi belongs to the finite-energy class E(X, omega), determine whether phi has zero Lelong number at every point.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold which is either Kähler or, more generally, lies in the Fujiki class $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., is bimeromorphic to a compact Kähler manifold). Let $\omega$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ which is semi-positive and big, meaning $\omega \geq 0$ pointwise and $\int_X \omega^n > 0$, where $n = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$.

A function $\varphi : X \to [-\infty, +\infty)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if it is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and $\omega + dd^c \varphi \geq 0$ in the sense of currents. For an $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = (\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n$ is well defined, and $\varphi$ is said to have full Monge–Ampère mass if $\int_X \mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = \int_X \omega^n$. The finite-energy class $\mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$ consists of all $\omega$-psh functions with full Monge–Ampère mass.

Recall that the Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $x \in X$ is
$$\nu(\varphi, x) = \liminf_{z \to x} \frac{\varphi(z)}{\log |z - x|},$$
computed in any local holomorphic chart.

Question: Is it true that for every $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$, the Lelong number $\nu(\varphi, x)$ vanishes at every point $x \in X$?
status_search_result: It is classically known (Guedj–Zeriahi) that on a compact Kähler manifold with $\omega$ a Kähler form, every $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$ has zero Lelong numbers everywhere. The question concerns the more general setting of a semi-positive big $(1,1)$-form on a Fujiki-class manifold. Web search did not return a definitive resolution of this generalized question; recent works on relative pluripotential theory and finite-energy classes in big cohomology classes discuss related results but do not appear to settle the question in this exact generality. Status appears unknown from available sources.

original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact Kahler manifold and Y a complex submanifold. Determine whether every omega|_Y-plurisubharmonic function on Y is the restriction to Y of some omega-plurisubharmonic function on X.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, where $\omega$ is a Kähler form on $X$. Recall that an upper semicontinuous function $\varphi:X\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $\varphi\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$ and the current $\omega+dd^c\varphi$ is positive on $X$. Denote by $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ the set of $\omega$-psh functions on $X$.

Let $Y\subset X$ be a (closed) complex submanifold, and equip $Y$ with the restricted Kähler form $\omega|_Y$. Define
$$\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)|_Y := \{\,\Phi|_Y : \Phi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega),\ \Phi|_Y\not\equiv-\infty\,\}.$$

Determine whether the equality
$$\mathrm{PSH}(Y,\omega|_Y) = \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)|_Y$$
holds; equivalently, decide whether every $\omega|_Y$-plurisubharmonic function on $Y$ is the restriction to $Y$ of some $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function defined on the whole of $X$.
status_search_result: The extension property is known in several important cases: Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi (2010) established it for subvarieties of complex projective space with $\omega$ the Fubini–Study form, and Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi-type extensions have been proved for Kähler classes in the real Néron–Severi space and, more generally, in Collins–Tosatti / Coman–Marinescu and the 2022 work "On the extension of quasiplurisubharmonic functions" (arXiv:2202.01325) for compact Kähler manifolds covered by Zariski-open Stein sets with certain properties. The fully general question for arbitrary compact Kähler $(X,\omega)$ and arbitrary complex submanifolds $Y$ does not appear to have been resolved in full; partial positive results dominate, with no published counterexample found.

original_question: Consider a smooth holomorphic family pi: X -> Delta of compact Kahler manifolds and a pseudoeffective line bundle L -> X. If h_0 = e^{-phi_0} is a singular Hermitian metric on L_0 = L|_{X_0} with semi-positive curvature current dd^c phi_0 >= 0, determine whether there exists a Hermitian metric h = e^{-phi} on L over all of X such that dd^c phi >= 0 and phi restricts to phi_0 on X_0.

original_question: For a plurisubharmonic function phi on a bounded pseudoconvex domain, determine what can be said about the set of points where phi admits no differential test from above; in particular, determine whether that set has zero Lebesgue measure or zero capacity.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded pseudoconvex domain and let $\varphi : \Omega \to [-\infty, \infty)$ be a plurisubharmonic function (i.e., upper semicontinuous, not identically $-\infty$, and such that for every complex line $L$ the restriction $\varphi|_{\Omega \cap L}$ is subharmonic). Say that $\varphi$ admits a differential test from above at a point $z_0 \in \Omega$ if there exists a $C^2$ function $u$ defined in a neighborhood of $z_0$ such that $\varphi \le u$ near $z_0$ and $\varphi(z_0) = u(z_0)$. Let 
$$N(\varphi) := \{ z_0 \in \Omega : \varphi \text{ admits no differential test from above at } z_0 \}.$$
It is known that $N(\varphi)$ has empty interior. Determine what further can be said about $N(\varphi)$; in particular, decide whether $N(\varphi)$ must have zero Lebesgue measure, and whether $N(\varphi)$ must have zero (Bedford–Taylor) pluricapacity.

original_question: Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the local complex Monge-Ampere equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0 on a bounded domain. If P(v) denotes the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, determine whether P(v) is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $f \geq 0$ be a continuous function on $\Omega$. Consider the local complex Monge-Ampère equation
$$-(dd^c V)^n + f\, dV = 0,$$
where $dV$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\Omega$ and $(dd^c V)^n$ is the complex Monge-Ampère operator. Let $v: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous viscosity supersolution of this equation. Define the plurisubharmonic envelope of $v$ by
$$P(v)(z) := \sup\{u(z) : u \text{ plurisubharmonic on } \Omega,\ u \leq v \text{ on } \Omega\}.$$
Determine whether the upper semicontinuous regularization $P(v)^*$ is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation, i.e. whether $P(v)$ is plurisubharmonic and satisfies
$$-(dd^c P(v))^n + f\, dV \leq 0$$
in the pluripotential sense on $\Omega$.
status_search_result: A subsequent paper "Plurisubharmonic envelopes and supersolutions" (Journal of Differential Geometry, 2019) by Guedj-Lu-Zeriahi proves that the (quasi-)plurisubharmonic envelope of a viscosity supersolution is a pluripotential supersolution of the corresponding complex Monge-Ampère equation, answering this question affirmatively.

context_brief: smooth approximation in semipositive big class
original_question: Let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form on a compact Kahler manifold X. Determine whether every function phi in PSH(X, omega) is the decreasing limit of smooth omega-plurisubharmonic functions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\omega$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ that is semi-positive (i.e. $\omega \ge 0$ pointwise as a Hermitian form) and big (i.e. its cohomology class $[\omega] \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ contains a Kähler current, equivalently $\int_X \omega^n > 0$ when one allows representatives that are Kähler currents). Denote by $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ the set of all upper semi-continuous functions $\varphi : X \to [-\infty,+\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that the current $\omega + dd^c \varphi$ is positive on $X$.

Determine whether the following holds: for every $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$, there exists a decreasing sequence $(\varphi_j)_{j \ge 1}$ of smooth $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ (i.e. each $\varphi_j \in C^\infty(X) \cap \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$) such that $\varphi_j \searrow \varphi$ pointwise on $X$.
status_search_result: Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi and subsequent work established that any $\omega$-psh function in a semi-positive big class can be approximated from above by a decreasing sequence of continuous $\omega$-psh functions, and Demailly's regularization gives smooth decreasing approximation when $\omega$ is Kähler, as well as approximation with analytic singularities in big classes. However, web search did not surface a paper that resolves the smooth decreasing approximation problem in the smooth semi-positive big setting; the question appears to remain open.

original_question: Let alpha be a big cohomology class on a compact Kahler manifold, let theta be a smooth closed representative of alpha, and let V_theta be the theta-plurisubharmonic function with minimal singularities. Determine whether the polar locus P(alpha) = {x : V_theta(x) = -infinity} always coincides with the non-bounded locus NB(alpha) = {x : V_theta is not locally bounded near x}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\alpha \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ be a big cohomology class (i.e. a class that contains a Kähler current). Fix a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ representing $\alpha$. Recall that an upper semicontinuous function $\varphi : X \to [-\infty, +\infty)$ is called $\theta$-plurisubharmonic ($\theta$-psh) if $\theta + dd^c \varphi \geq 0$ in the sense of currents. Among all $\theta$-psh functions one defines the envelope with minimal singularities
\[
V_\theta(x) := \sup\{\varphi(x) : \varphi \text{ is } \theta\text{-psh on } X \text{ and } \varphi \leq 0\}.
\]
Define the polar locus
\[
P(\alpha) := \{x \in X : V_\theta(x) = -\infty\}
\]
and the non-bounded locus
\[
\mathrm{NB}(\alpha) := \{x \in X : V_\theta \text{ is not locally bounded near } x\}.
\]
(Both sets depend only on the class $\alpha$, not on the chosen smooth representative $\theta$.) Determine whether the equality $P(\alpha) = \mathrm{NB}(\alpha)$ holds for every big class $\alpha$ on every compact Kähler manifold $X$.
status_search_result: A direct web search did not turn up a published resolution of the question whether the polar locus $P(\alpha)$ coincides with the non-bounded locus $\mathrm{NB}(\alpha)$ for the envelope with minimal singularities of a big class on a compact Kähler manifold. The question is attributed to Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi in the context of Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes; available references discuss the ample/non-Kähler locus and minimal-singularity envelopes, but no source found explicitly settles the equality $P(\alpha)=\mathrm{NB}(\alpha)$. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, let alpha_0 be a Kahler class, and let S_0 be a positive closed current representing alpha_0 with possibly nonzero Lelong numbers. Di Nezza and Lu construct a maximal weak Kahler-Ricci flow (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} that is smooth on time-increasing Zariski open sets. Determine whether this flow produces approximants with analytic singularities.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\alpha_0 \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ be a Kähler class. Let $S_0$ be a positive closed $(1,1)$-current representing $\alpha_0$, which may have nonzero Lelong numbers. By work of Di Nezza and Lu, there exists a maximal weak Kähler–Ricci flow $(\omega_t)_{0 < t < T_{\max}}$ starting from $S_0$, namely a family of positive closed $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ such that on a time-increasing family of Zariski open subsets $\Omega_t \subset X$ each $\omega_t$ is a smooth Kähler form satisfying the Kähler–Ricci flow equation
$$\frac{\partial \omega_t}{\partial t} = -\mathrm{Ric}(\omega_t),$$
with $\omega_t \to S_0$ as $t \to 0^+$ in the sense of currents.

Recall that a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ has analytic singularities if locally
$$\varphi = \tfrac{c}{2}\log\Big(\sum_{j=1}^N |f_j|^2\Big) + \text{(smooth)}$$
for some constant $c > 0$ and holomorphic functions $f_1,\dots,f_N$; a positive closed $(1,1)$-current is said to have analytic singularities if its local potentials do.

Question: Does the family $(\omega_t)_{0 < t < T_{\max}}$ produce, as $t \to 0^+$, a family of approximating positive closed $(1,1)$-currents in the class $\alpha_0$ that have analytic singularities and converge to $S_0$? Equivalently, does the weak Kähler–Ricci flow regularize $S_0$ by currents with analytic singularities, in analogy with Demailly's regularization theorem?
status_search_result: Searches reveal subsequent work extending Di Nezza–Lu's weak Kähler–Ricci flow (e.g., generalizations to the Chern–Ricci flow and smoothness off analytic subsets for related degenerate parabolic complex Monge–Ampère equations), but no source clearly confirms or refutes that the Di Nezza–Lu flow produces approximants of the initial current with analytic singularities. The status appears unresolved in the literature found.

context_brief: run local Monge-Ampere flow from arbitrary psh data
original_question: For the complex Monge-Ampere flow in a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain, Do proved existence and smoothing when the initial datum u_0 is bounded and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of the domain. Determine whether the flow can be started from an arbitrary plurisubharmonic initial function, not necessarily bounded.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain, and set $\Omega_T := (0,T) \times \Omega$ for some $T \in (0,\infty]$. Consider the complex Monge–Ampère flow
$$ (dd^c u_t)^n = e^{\partial_t u + F(t,z,u)}\, \mu(z)\, dt, \qquad (t,z) \in \Omega_T, $$
where, for each $t$, $u_t = u(t,\cdot)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$, $dd^c$ is taken in the spatial variables, $F$ is a smooth function nondecreasing in the last argument, and $\mu$ is a smooth positive volume form on $\overline{\Omega}$. The flow is supplemented with a boundary condition on $(0,T) \times \partial\Omega$ and an initial condition $u(0,\cdot) = u_0$, where $u_0$ is plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$.

It is known that when $u_0$ is bounded, there exists a solution $u$ to this Cauchy–Dirichlet problem which is smooth on $\Omega_T$ and continuous up to $t = 0$ in an appropriate sense (instantaneous smoothing).

Question: Can such a complex Monge–Ampère flow be started from an arbitrary plurisubharmonic initial datum $u_0$ — in particular one that is not assumed to be bounded — in the sense of producing a (suitably weak) solution that is smooth for $t > 0$ and recovers $u_0$ as $t \to 0^+$?
status_search_result: Recent work on the pluripotential Cauchy–Dirichlet problem for complex Monge–Ampère flows on strictly pseudoconvex domains (e.g., the 2025 preprint extending the theory to general measures on the right-hand side) still imposes that the initial datum and the parabolic potentials be bounded. No source found resolves the case of an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, plurisubharmonic initial datum, so the question appears to remain open.

context_brief: comparison principle for degenerate parabolic flow
original_question: Consider the degenerate complex Monge-Ampere flow (omega_t + dd^c phi_t)^n = exp(dot(phi_t) + F(t, x, phi)) mu(t, x) on [0, T] x X, where omega_t is a continuous family of semi-positive big (1,1)-forms bounded below by a fixed semi-positive big form, F is continuous and nondecreasing in the last variable, and mu is a bounded continuous volume form. If u is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and v is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution with u <= v on the parabolic boundary {0} x X, determine whether u <= v holds on all of [0, T] x X.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $T>0$. Let $\{\omega_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a continuous family of smooth semi-positive $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ such that there exists a fixed semi-positive big $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ with $\omega_t \geq \theta$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. Let $F:[0,T]\times X\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and nondecreasing in the last variable, and let $\mu(t,x)$ be a bounded continuous (non-negative) volume form on $[0,T]\times X$. Consider the degenerate parabolic complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$\bigl(\omega_t + dd^c\varphi_t\bigr)^n \;=\; e^{\dot{\varphi}_t + F(t,x,\varphi_t)}\,\mu(t,x) \qquad\text{on } [0,T]\times X,$$
where $\varphi_t(x)=\varphi(t,x)$ and $\dot\varphi_t = \partial_t\varphi$, and where solutions, subsolutions and supersolutions are understood in the viscosity sense (with $\omega_t+dd^c\varphi_t$ interpreted via the standard viscosity formulation for degenerate complex Monge–Ampère operators).

Suppose $u:[0,T]\times X\to\mathbb{R}$ is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and $v:[0,T]\times X\to\mathbb{R}$ is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution of the above equation, and that $u(0,x)\le v(0,x)$ for every $x\in X$.

Question: Does it follow that $u(t,x)\le v(t,x)$ for every $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times X$?

Geom. Anal. 2022), and viscosity solutions to parabolic complex Monge–Ampère equations (arXiv:1905.11818). A 2025 preprint (arXiv:2511.06412) proves a general pluripotential comparison principle. paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Let X be an affine scheme with coordinate algebra A, let a be a finite-dimensional algebra, and let an algebraic group Γ act completely reducibly on both A and a by automorphisms. For the resulting equivariant map algebra M(X,a)^Γ, classify the irreducible finite-dimensional representations when Γ is allowed to be more general than a finite group.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with coordinate algebra $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$, and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra. Suppose $\Gamma$ is an algebraic group acting on $A$ and on $\mathfrak{a}$ by automorphisms (as an algebra and as a Lie algebra, respectively), and assume that the action of $\Gamma$ is completely reducible on both $A$ and $\mathfrak{a}$. Form the equivariant map algebra
$$M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} := (A \otimes \mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} = \{f \in A \otimes \mathfrak{a} \mid \gamma \cdot f = f \text{ for all } \gamma \in \Gamma\},$$
viewed as a Lie algebra under the pointwise bracket. 

Classify, up to isomorphism, all irreducible finite-dimensional representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma}$ in this generality where $\Gamma$ is permitted to be an arbitrary (not necessarily finite) algebraic group acting completely reducibly.
status_search_result: The classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras was carried out by Neher–Savage–Senesi (arXiv:0906.5189) in the case where Γ is a finite abelian group acting freely on the maximal spectrum of A, and subsequent work has extended results to map superalgebras and to extensions/block decompositions. A general classification when Γ is an arbitrary algebraic group acting completely reducibly does not appear to have been established in the search results, so the status remains unclear.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Develop the representation theory of equivariant map algebras M(X,g)^Γ when the target algebra g is allowed to be much more general than the finite-dimensional Lie or associative cases already studied, including infinite-dimensional Lie targets such as Kac-Moody or Heisenberg algebras and non-Lie targets such as alternative or Jordan algebras, with special emphasis on describing their finite-dimensional representations whenever representations are well defined.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be an affine scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, and let A = k[X] denote its coordinate ring. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X by automorphisms (so Γ acts on A). Let g be a k-algebra (not necessarily Lie nor associative) on which Γ also acts by k-algebra automorphisms. Form the algebra of equivariant regular maps

   M(X, g)^Γ = (A ⊗_k g)^Γ,

where the action of Γ on A ⊗ g is the diagonal one and the algebra structure on M(X, g)^Γ is induced pointwise from that of g. When g is a Lie (resp. associative) algebra, M(X, g)^Γ is again a Lie (resp. associative) algebra; analogous statements hold for other varieties of algebras (alternative, Jordan, etc.).

Develop the representation theory of M(X, g)^Γ in the following settings, which lie outside the previously treated case where g is finite-dimensional Lie or finite-dimensional associative:

(a) Infinite-dimensional Lie targets g, in particular:
   (i) symmetrizable Kac–Moody algebras (beyond the untwisted multiloop case already handled);
   (ii) the Heisenberg algebra and other well-studied infinite-dimensional Lie algebras.

(b) Non-Lie targets g for which a notion of representation is defined, in particular:
   (i) alternative algebras;
   (ii) Jordan algebras.

In each case, give a classification, up to isomorphism, of the irreducible finite-dimensional representations of M(X, g)^Γ (whenever finite-dimensional representations are a meaningful class), together with an explicit description of their structure (e.g., via evaluation-type constructions, tensor product decompositions, or analogues of Drinfeld polynomials), paralleling the existing classification in the finite-dimensional Lie case.
status_search_result: The problem is broad and remains largely open in full generality. Partial progress exists for specific target classes: finite-dimensional irreducible representations of equivariant map algebras with target a parabolic subalgebra of an affine Kac–Moody algebra have been classified using Drinfeld-polynomial type data, and there are results on quantizations in this setting. Constructions linking Jordan algebras to Kac–Moody algebras (Kantor–Koecher–Tits and generalizations) suggest avenues, but a systematic representation theory of equivariant map algebras with Heisenberg, general Kac–Moody, alternative, or Jordan targets has not been completed.

context_brief: Maximal distance in sets of lengths
original_question: Let G = C_{n1} ⊕ ··· ⊕ C_{nr} be a finite abelian group with |G| >= 3 and 1 < n1 | ··· | nr. For a set of lengths A, let Delta(A) be the set of positive integers that occur as gaps between consecutive elements of A, and let Delta(G) be the union of these distance sets over all sets of lengths arising from G. Is the largest possible distance equal to max{nr - 2, -1 + sum_{i=1}^r floor(ni/2)}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G \cong C_{n_1} \oplus \cdots \oplus C_{n_r}$ be a finite abelian group with $|G| \geq 3$ and $1 < n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_r$. Let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, i.e., the monoid (under concatenation) of finite unordered sequences of elements of $G$ whose terms sum to $0$, with irreducible (atomic) elements being the minimal zero-sum sequences. For a nonzero, non-identity element $B \in \mathcal{B}(G)$, the set of lengths of $B$ is
$$\mathsf{L}(B) = \{k \in \mathbb{N} : B = U_1 \cdots U_k \text{ for some atoms } U_1, \ldots, U_k \in \mathcal{B}(G)\}.$$
For a finite set $L = \{\ell_0 < \ell_1 < \cdots < \ell_k\} \subset \mathbb{Z}$, define its set of distances
$$\Delta(L) = \{\ell_i - \ell_{i-1} : 1 \leq i \leq k\},$$
and set
$$\Delta(G) = \bigcup_{B \in \mathcal{B}(G)} \Delta(\mathsf{L}(B)).$$
Determine whether
$$\max \Delta(G) = \max\!\left\{\, n_r - 2,\ -1 + \sum_{i=1}^{r} \left\lfloor \tfrac{n_i}{2} \right\rfloor \,\right\}.$$

original_question: For a finite abelian group G, let L(G) denote the collection of all sets of factorization lengths arising from G. Can one determine a function f: N -> N such that, whenever |G| >= f(M), the system L(G) contains every finite set L subset N_{>=2} whose width max L - min L is at most M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively. Consider the monoid $\mathcal{B}(G)$ of zero-sum sequences over $G$, i.e. finite sequences $S = g_1 \cdots g_\ell$ of elements of $G$ (multiplicities allowed, order irrelevant) with $g_1 + \cdots + g_\ell = 0$, under concatenation. The atoms of $\mathcal{B}(G)$ are the minimal zero-sum sequences (those with no proper zero-sum subsequence). For a zero-sum sequence $a \in \mathcal{B}(G)$, define its set of lengths
$$\mathsf{L}(a) = \{\, k \in \mathbb{N} : a = u_1 \cdots u_k \text{ for some atoms } u_1,\ldots,u_k \,\},$$
and define the system of sets of lengths of $G$ by
$$\mathcal{L}(G) = \{\, \mathsf{L}(a) : a \in \mathcal{B}(G) \,\}.$$
For a finite nonempty set $L \subset \mathbb{N}$, call $\max L - \min L$ the width of $L$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $M \in \mathbb{N}$ and every finite abelian group $G$ with $|G| \geq f(M)$, the system $\mathcal{L}(G)$ contains every finite set $L \subset \mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ with $\max L - \min L \leq M$?

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Generalize equivariant map superalgebras by allowing the target to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, replacing the commutative coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Γ by a Z2-graded group; then determine the resulting representation theory in this broader super setting.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. By a Lie superalgebra over k we mean a Z/2Z-graded vector space g = g_0 ⊕ g_1 equipped with a bilinear bracket satisfying graded skew-symmetry and the graded Jacobi identity. A finite-dimensional Lie superalgebra g is called simple if it has no nonzero proper graded ideals and [g, g] ≠ 0.

By a supercommutative algebra we mean an associative, unital, Z/2Z-graded k-algebra A = A_0 ⊕ A_1 such that ab = (−1)^{|a||b|} ba for homogeneous elements. Such an A is the coordinate algebra of an affine superscheme X = Spec A.

By a Z/2Z-graded group Γ we mean an affine group superscheme over k, equivalently a representable functor from supercommutative k-algebras to groups whose representing Hopf superalgebra is Z/2Z-graded. Suppose Γ acts on X (equivalently, on A by Z/2Z-graded automorphisms) and on g by Z/2Z-graded Lie superalgebra automorphisms.

The equivariant map superalgebra is then defined as
   M(X, g)^Γ := (A ⊗ g)^Γ,
the Z/2Z-graded subspace of Γ-invariants, with the Lie superbracket
   [a ⊗ x, b ⊗ y] = (−1)^{|x||b|} ab ⊗ [x, y]
extended by linearity.

Problem. Develop the representation theory of the Lie superalgebra M(X, g)^Γ in this generalized super setting, where:
 (i) g is allowed to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra over k (not restricted to the basic classical types);
 (ii) A is a (possibly nontrivially Z/2Z-graded) supercommutative k-algebra, so that X is a superscheme;
 (iii) Γ is a Z/2Z-graded group acting compatibly on X and g.

Specifically, classify the irreducible finite-dimensional (graded) modules of M(X, g)^Γ in terms of suitable equivariant evaluation data on X, and describe their extensions and tensor structure, generalizing the classification known when g is basic classical, A is an ordinary commutative algebra, and Γ is an ordinary (ungraded) group.
status_search_result: The classical equivariant map superalgebra case (g basic classical, A ordinary commutative, Γ ordinary finite group) was treated by Savage and collaborators. Subsequent work has extended the theory in particular directions, e.g. equivariant map queer Lie superalgebras (Calixto–Savage, 2014) and irreducible modules and their extensions (Bagci–Calixto–Macedo). However, the full generalization simultaneously allowing arbitrary finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra targets, supercommutative coordinate algebras (superscheme X), and Z/2Z-graded group symmetries does not appear to have a complete representation-theoretic classification in the literature, so the program remains only partially carried out.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Replace the algebraic framework of equivariant map algebras by an analytic one: for a Banach manifold X, a Banach algebra a, and an action of Γ by automorphisms, develop the theory and representation theory of algebras of equivariant differentiable maps X → a.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be a group. Let $X$ be a Banach manifold equipped with a smooth action of $\Gamma$, and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a Banach algebra equipped with an action of $\Gamma$ by continuous algebra automorphisms. Consider the algebra
$$ (C^\infty(X,\mathfrak{a}))^\Gamma := \{ f \in C^\infty(X,\mathfrak{a}) : f(\gamma \cdot x) = \gamma \cdot f(x) \text{ for all } \gamma\in\Gamma,\, x\in X\} $$
of $\Gamma$-equivariant differentiable maps from $X$ to $\mathfrak{a}$, with pointwise algebra operations.

Develop a structure theory and a representation theory for such algebras of equivariant differentiable maps in this analytic/Banach setting, paralleling what is known for equivariant map algebras in the algebraic setting (where $X$ is a scheme, $\mathfrak{a}$ a finite-dimensional Lie algebra, and one considers equivariant regular maps). In particular, classify natural classes of (e.g. finite-dimensional, or topologically irreducible) representations of $(C^\infty(X,\mathfrak{a}))^\Gamma$ in terms of the geometry of the $\Gamma$-action on $X$ and the representation theory of $\mathfrak{a}$.

The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: When the minimal-distance set is an interval
original_question: Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which the set Delta*(G) = {min Delta(G0) : G0 subset G and Delta(G0) is nonempty} is an interval and, at the same time, the exponent of G is at least 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|\ge 3$. By the structure theorem there are uniquely determined integers $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ such that $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$; one calls $r(G)=r$ the rank of $G$ and $\exp(G)=n_r$ the exponent of $G$.

For a subset $G_0\subseteq G$, a sequence over $G_0$ is a finite unordered tuple of elements of $G_0$ (formally, an element of the free abelian monoid $\mathcal F(G_0)$ on $G_0$). A sequence $S=g_1\cdots g_\ell$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $g_1+\cdots+g_\ell=0$, and it is called a minimal zero-sum sequence if it is a zero-sum sequence and no proper nonempty subsequence of it is a zero-sum sequence. Let $\mathcal A(G_0)$ denote the set of minimal zero-sum sequences over $G_0$. For a zero-sum sequence $S$ over $G_0$, the set of lengths of $S$ is
$$\mathsf L(S)=\{k\in\mathbb N : S=U_1\cdots U_k \text{ with } U_1,\dots,U_k\in\mathcal A(G_0)\}.$$
Let $\mathcal L(G_0)=\{\mathsf L(S): S \text{ a zero-sum sequence over }G_0\}$. For a finite set $L=\{l_1<l_2<\cdots<l_k\}\subseteq\mathbb N$ define $\Delta(L)=\{l_{i+1}-l_i : 1\le i\le k-1\}$, and put
$$\Delta(G_0)=\bigcup_{L\in\mathcal L(G_0),\,|L|\ge 2}\Delta(L).$$
Define
$$\Delta^*(G)=\{\min\Delta(G_0) : G_0\subseteq G,\ \Delta(G_0)\neq\varnothing\}\subseteq\mathbb N.$$

Question: Does there exist a finite abelian group $G$ such that $\Delta^*(G)$ is an interval of $\mathbb N$ (i.e. $\Delta^*(G)=[\min\Delta^*(G),\max\Delta^*(G)]\cap\mathbb N$) and at the same time $\exp(G)\ge 2r(G)+2$?
category_tag: zero-sum sequences and sets of lengths
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of this specific question about whether some finite abelian group has $\Delta^*(G)$ an interval together with $\exp(G)\ge 2r(G)+2$. Related work on $\Delta^*(G)$ and sets of minimal distances exists, but no source clearly confirms or refutes the existence of such a group.

context_brief: Growth rate of the STSL bound
original_question: For a Krull monoid with finite class group, the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths says that there exist a nonnegative integer M and a finite nonempty set Delta* such that every set of lengths L(a) is an almost arithmetic multiprogression with bound M and difference d in Delta*. For the systems L(G) attached to finite abelian groups G, what is the rough order of magnitude of the smallest such bound as a function of the Davenport constant D(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with finite class group $G$. For an element $a \in H$, write $a = u_1 \cdots u_k$ as a product of atoms (irreducibles); the set of lengths of $a$ is
$$L(a) = \{ k \in \mathbb{N} : a = u_1 \cdots u_k \text{ with each } u_i \text{ an atom of } H \},$$
and the system of sets of lengths of $H$ is $\mathcal{L}(H) = \{ L(a) : a \in H \}$.

A non-empty subset $L \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is called an almost arithmetic multiprogression (AAMP) with bound $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$, difference $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and period $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \{0, d, 2d, \dots\}$ with $0, d \in \mathcal{D}$, if there exist integers $y, \ell$ with
$$L = y + (L' \cup L^* \cup L'') \subseteq y + \mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z},$$
where $L^* = (\mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z}) \cap [0, \ell d]$ is the central part, and $L' \subseteq [-M, -1]$, $L'' \subseteq \ell d + [1, M]$ are bounded "end" perturbations.

The Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths asserts: for every Krull monoid $H$ with finite class group there exist $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a finite non-empty set $\Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every $L \in \mathcal{L}(H)$ is an AAMP with bound $M$ and difference $d \in \Delta^*$.

For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, and write $\mathcal{L}(G) = \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B}(G))$. Let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of $G$, i.e.\ the smallest $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ has a non-empty zero-sum subsequence. Let
$$M^*(G) = \min\{M \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \exists \text{ finite } \Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ with every } L \in \mathcal{L}(G) \text{ an AAMP with bound } M \text{ and difference } d \in \Delta^*\}.$$

Determine the rough order of magnitude of $M^*(G)$ as a function of $\mathsf{D}(G)$, as $G$ ranges over finite abelian groups.

Surveys of factorization theory in Krull monoids continue to list quantitative refinements of the STSL bound as an open direction, and no source identified gives an asymptotic answer. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: For equivariant map algebras M(X,a)^Γ, determine classification criteria and invariants for the isomorphism problem by extending known results for loop algebras and certain two-variable multiloop algebras to the full multiloop setting and then to more general equivariant map algebras.
self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let X be a scheme of finite type over k, and let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k. The map algebra M(X, g) is the Lie algebra of regular maps from X to g, which can be identified with g ⊗_k A, where A is the coordinate ring of X, equipped with the pointwise bracket. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X by automorphisms and on g by Lie algebra automorphisms. The equivariant map algebra is the fixed-point subalgebra
  M(X, g)^Γ = { α ∈ g ⊗_k A : (γ·α) = α for all γ ∈ Γ },
where Γ acts diagonally on g ⊗_k A.

Important special cases:
(i) Multiloop algebras: X = (k^×)^n with the action of Γ = Z/m_1 Z × ⋯ × Z/m_n Z generated by commuting finite-order automorphisms σ_1, …, σ_n of g, where the i-th generator acts on the i-th coordinate of (k^×)^n by multiplication by a primitive m_i-th root of unity. For n = 1 these are the (twisted) loop algebras.
(ii) The two-variable case (n = 2) of (i).

The isomorphism problem asks: give explicit classification criteria and a complete set of invariants determining when two equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ and M(X', g')^{Γ'} are isomorphic as Lie algebras.

Problem: Extend the known classification of (twisted) loop algebras (n = 1) and of two-variable multiloop algebras (n = 2) to:
(a) the full multiloop setting for arbitrary n ≥ 1, providing necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of the data (g, σ_1, …, σ_n, m_1, …, m_n), for two such multiloop algebras to be isomorphic; and
(b) the broader class of equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ, providing classification criteria and invariants in terms of the triple (X, g, Γ).
status_search_result: The isomorphism problem for equivariant map algebras is described as a fundamental open problem. Partial results exist: complete classifications are known for (twisted) loop algebras and for two-variable multiloop algebras (via Lie torus / centreless Lie torus isotopy methods and Galois cohomology over Laurent polynomial rings). No general classification for arbitrary multiloop algebras (n ≥ 3) or for general equivariant map algebras has been established; recent work continues in related directions (e.g., interpolating categories, representation theory) but does not resolve the full classification.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Determine the automorphism groups of equivariant map algebras M(X,a)^Γ in general, extending the partial descriptions already known in special untwisted, twisted-loop, multiloop, Lie, and Lie-superalgebra cases.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero on which $\Gamma$ acts by scheme automorphisms, and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra (or Lie superalgebra) over $k$ on which $\Gamma$ acts by Lie (super)algebra automorphisms. Let $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$ be the coordinate ring of $X$, so that $\Gamma$ acts diagonally on $\mathfrak{a} \otimes_k A$. The associated equivariant map algebra is the fixed-point subalgebra
$$ M(X, \mathfrak{a})^\Gamma := (\mathfrak{a} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma, $$
viewed as a Lie (super)algebra over $k$.

Determine, in full generality, the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\text{Lie}}\bigl(M(X,\mathfrak{a})^\Gamma\bigr)$ of this Lie (super)algebra in terms of the data $(X, \mathfrak{a}, \Gamma)$. The problem includes giving a description that specializes to and extends the partial results currently available in the untwisted case ($\Gamma$ trivial), the twisted-loop case ($X = k^\times$ with cyclic $\Gamma$), the multiloop case, and the cases where $\mathfrak{a}$ is a simple Lie algebra or a basic classical Lie superalgebra.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that automorphism groups of equivariant map algebras are described in special cases (untwisted current/loop algebras, twisted and multiloop algebras, certain Lie and Lie superalgebra targets), but no general classification covering arbitrary $(X,\mathfrak{a},\Gamma)$ has appeared. The question is listed among open problems in the standard survey of the area, and no subsequent paper resolving the general case was found.

context_brief: Isomorphism between A_q, q-Onsager, and a coideal subalgebra
original_question: Let q be a non-root of unity. The q-Onsager algebra is the algebra generated by W_0 and W_1 subject to the pair of q-Dolan-Grady type relations written in the paper, namely [W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_0,W_1] and [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_1,W_0], where [X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX and ρ is a scalar. The algebra A_q is an infinite-dimensional current algebra introduced in terms of generators {W_{-k}, W_{k+1}, G_{k+1}, G̃_{k+1} | k ∈ ℤ_+} whose first modes satisfy the same pair of relations. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending W_0 to k_+e_1 + k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1} + ε_+q^{h_1}, W_1 to k_-e_0 + k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0} + ε_-q^{h_0}, and ρ to (q+q^{-1})^2k_+k_-. Show that these three infinite-dimensional algebras — A_q, the q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) — are isomorphic.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a field $\mathbb{K}$ and a nonzero scalar $q\in\mathbb{K}$ that is not a root of unity. For $X,Y$ in an associative algebra set $[X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

(1) The q-Onsager algebra $O_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra with two generators $W_0,W_1$ and the q-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $\rho\in\mathbb{K}$ is a fixed scalar.

(2) The current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra generated by an infinite family of generators $\{W_{-k},\,W_{k+1},\,G_{k+1},\,\tilde G_{k+1}\mid k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\}$ subject to the standard list of defining relations under which the first modes $W_0,W_1$ satisfy the q-Dolan–Grady relations above with the same parameter $\rho$.

(3) Let $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ be the quantum affine algebra with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$). Fix scalars $k_\pm,\varepsilon_\pm\in\mathbb{K}$ with $\rho=(q+q^{-1})^2 k_+k_-$, and let $B$ be the left coideal subalgebra of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ generated by
$$\mathcal{W}_0=k_+e_1+k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\qquad \mathcal{W}_1=k_-e_0+k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_- q^{h_0}.$$

Prove or disprove: the three algebras $\mathcal{A}_q$, $O_q$, and $B$ are mutually isomorphic as associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebras.

Math. Phys. 2021) clarified the relation: the current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the alternating central extension of $O_q$, with an algebra isomorphism $\langle W_0,W_1\rangle\subset\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ and a tensor-product factorization $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q\otimes Z$ where $Z$ is a polynomial center. Thus $O_q$ embeds in $\mathcal{A}_q$ but the two are not isomorphic; $\mathcal{A}_q$ is strictly larger. The isomorphism of $O_q$ with the coideal subalgebra image is established in Baseilhac–Belliard and related work. Hence the conjecture as stated is partially resolved (with a negative answer for $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ in the strict sense).

context_brief: Isomorphism for the augmented q-Onsager setting
original_question: Let A_q^{diag} denote the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra discussed in the paper, with current modes K_k, K_{k+1}, Z_{k+1}, and Z̃_{k+1}. Let the augmented q-Onsager algebra be the algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and Z̃_1 subject to the displayed commutation and higher q-commutator relations in the paper. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the augmented q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending K_0 to ε_+q^{h_1}, K_1 to ε_-q^{h_0}, Z_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_+q^{-1}e_0q^{h_1}+ε_-f_1q^{h_1+h_0}), and Z̃_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_-q^{-1}e_1q^{h_0}+ε_+f_0q^{h_1+h_0}). Show that the infinite-dimensional algebra A_q^{diag}, the augmented q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) are isomorphic.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $q$ be a generic nonzero complex parameter and let $\varepsilon_+,\varepsilon_-$ be fixed nonzero scalars. Consider the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$) and standard relations.

(i) Augmented $q$-Onsager algebra $\mathcal{O}_q$. Define $\mathcal{O}_q$ as the unital associative algebra with generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ satisfying
- $[K_0,K_1]=0$,
- $K_0 Z_1 K_0^{-1}=q^{2}Z_1$, $K_0\widetilde Z_1K_0^{-1}=q^{-2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- $K_1 Z_1 K_1^{-1}=q^{-2}Z_1$, $K_1\widetilde Z_1K_1^{-1}=q^{2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- the higher $q$-Serre / $q$-commutator relations
$$[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,\qquad [\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[\widetilde Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,$$
with $\rho=-(q^2-q^{-2})^2$ and $[X,Y]_p:=XY-pYX$.

(ii) Coideal subalgebra $\mathcal{B}\subset U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the subalgebra generated by
$$\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\quad \varepsilon_- q^{h_0},\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_+ q^{-1}e_0 q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}),\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_- q^{-1}e_1 q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}).$$

(iii) Current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$. Let $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ be the algebra obtained as the quotient of the reflection equation algebra for the $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ $R$-matrix by the diagonal/scalar reduction giving currents with modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ ($k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$), subject to the relations induced by the reflection equation.

Problem. Prove that there are algebra isomorphisms
$$\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}} \;\cong\; \mathcal{O}_q \;\cong\; \mathcal{B},$$
where the second isomorphism is induced by the assignment in (ii). Furthermore, find explicit polynomial formulas expressing the higher current modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ of $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ as noncommutative polynomials in the generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ of $\mathcal{O}_q$.
category_tag: Quantum affine algebras and coideal subalgebras
status_search_result: The augmented q-Onsager algebra is widely recognized as a coideal subalgebra of U_q(ŝl_2) (Ito–Terwilliger, Baseilhac–Belliard), and an isomorphism between a quantum reflection algebra and a new current algebra of q-Onsager type has been established in related work. However, no source clearly verifies the full triple isomorphism together with the explicit polynomial formulas relating higher current modes to the augmented q-Onsager generators in the diagonal case, so the status is inconclusive.
