paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: When a is an associative algebra and M = M(X,a)^Γ, go beyond the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules and describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules, together with the block decomposition of the corresponding module category.
self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let X be a scheme of finite type over k, let a be a finite-dimensional associative k-algebra, and let Γ be a finite group acting on X by scheme automorphisms and on a by k-algebra automorphisms. Define the equivariant map algebra
   M = M(X, a)^Γ = { f ∈ a ⊗ k[X] : (γ·f)(x) = γ·f(γ^{-1}x) for all γ ∈ Γ, x ∈ X }
with multiplication induced from that of a and k[X]. Consider the category of finite-dimensional left M-modules.

(a) Classify, up to isomorphism, all indecomposable finite-dimensional M-modules.

(b) Determine the block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules; that is, describe explicitly the equivalence classes of indecomposable objects under the equivalence relation generated by the existence of nontrivial extensions, and give a structural description of each block.
status_search_result: The block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map (Lie) algebras has been described in terms of spectral characters by Neher–Savage (Transformation Groups, 2015), and analogous block results exist for equivariant map superalgebras. However, a complete classification of indecomposable finite-dimensional modules remains open in general (the representation type is typically wild), so the full problem is only partially resolved.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: If a is an associative bialgebra and M = M(X,a)^Γ, understand the multi-orbit evaluation representations that arise from the comultiplication on a, including their construction, classification, and structural properties.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, let $\mathfrak{a}$ be an associative $k$-algebra, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by automorphisms on both $X$ and $\mathfrak{a}$. Define the equivariant map algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} = \{\,\varphi \in \mathrm{Mor}(X,\mathfrak{a}) : \varphi(\gamma \cdot x) = \gamma \cdot \varphi(x) \text{ for all } \gamma \in \Gamma,\ x \in X\,\},$$
viewed as an associative $k$-algebra under pointwise multiplication, where $\mathrm{Mor}(X,\mathfrak{a}) \cong \mathcal{O}(X) \otimes_k \mathfrak{a}$.

Suppose in addition that $\mathfrak{a}$ carries the structure of an associative bialgebra over $k$, with comultiplication $\Delta : \mathfrak{a} \to \mathfrak{a} \otimes \mathfrak{a}$ that is $\Gamma$-equivariant. Given a finite collection of distinct $\Gamma$-orbits $\Gamma x_1,\dots,\Gamma x_n$ in $X$ and finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_i$ of the isotropy-twisted fibers $\mathfrak{a}_{x_i}$ (the appropriate evaluation algebras at $x_i$), use the iterated comultiplication of $\mathfrak{a}$ to construct a "multi-orbit evaluation representation" of $M$ on $V_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_n$ via
$$\varphi \cdot (v_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes v_n) = \sum (\varphi(x_1)_{(1)} \cdot v_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes (\varphi(x_n)_{(n)} \cdot v_n),$$
using Sweedler notation for the $(n-1)$-fold coproduct.

Problem: Give an explicit construction of this class of multi-orbit evaluation representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{a})^\Gamma$, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for irreducibility, classify them up to isomorphism, and describe their structural properties (such as their place among all finite-dimensional representations of $M$, extensions between them, and their relationship with the single-orbit evaluation representations).
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published construction or classification of multi-orbit evaluation representations for equivariant map algebras with associative bialgebra targets defined via comultiplication. The survey itself flags this as a problem of interest, and no follow-up work explicitly addressing it could be confirmed; the status is therefore taken as unknown.

context_brief: Polynomial formulae relating A_q^{diag} and augmented q-Onsager
original_question: For the current algebra A_q^{diag} arising from a quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and the augmented q-Onsager algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and Z̃_1 with the displayed defining relations, determine explicit polynomial formulae expressing the generators or current modes of A_q^{diag} in terms of the augmented q-Onsager algebra, so that the precise algebraic relationship between A_q^{diag} and the augmented q-Onsager algebra is made explicit.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a nonzero complex number that is not a root of unity. The augmented $q$-Onsager algebra is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by elements $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ subject to the relations
$$K_0K_1=K_1K_0,\qquad K_0K_0^{-1}=K_1K_1^{-1}=1,$$
$$K_iZ_1K_i^{-1}=q^{a_i}Z_1,\qquad K_i\widetilde Z_1K_i^{-1}=q^{-a_i}\widetilde Z_1\quad(i=0,1),$$
with $a_0=2$, $a_1=-2$, together with the cubic $q$-Serre type relations
$$[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=-q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 Z_1(K_0K_1)Z_1,$$
$$[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=-q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 \widetilde Z_1(K_0K_1)^{-1}\widetilde Z_1,$$
where $[X,Y]_p:=XY-pYX$.

Let $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ denote the current algebra obtained as the quotient of the reflection equation algebra associated with $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ at a diagonal $K$-matrix, with its standard system of mode generators (Cartan-type modes and root-type current modes indexed by nonnegative integers).

Problem. Provide explicit polynomial formulae that express each generator (equivalently, each current mode) of $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ as a noncommutative polynomial in $K_0^{\pm 1},K_1^{\pm 1},Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$, thereby exhibiting an explicit algebra homomorphism (and, in particular, an isomorphism) between $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ and the augmented $q$-Onsager algebra.
status_search_result: The web search shows extensive subsequent work by Baseilhac, Terwilliger, and others on current algebras for the q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension, together with PBW-basis isomorphisms. However, even for the (non-augmented) q-Onsager algebra it is reported that closed-form polynomial expressions for the alternating/current generators in terms of the standard generators are not known. No source found explicitly states that the analogous problem for A_q^diag and the augmented q-Onsager algebra has been completely solved with explicit polynomial formulae, so the status appears to be unknown / at most partially addressed.

original_question: For finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q, q-analogs of Davies' relations are described as polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on the module, and A_q^{[2N+1]} is defined to be the quotient of A_q by these relations. When N=1 this quotient is isomorphic to the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3), and there is a known homomorphism from AW(3) to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨. Is there a homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra that generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A_q$ denote the $q$-Onsager algebra, defined as the unital associative algebra over $\mathbb{C}(q)$ generated by two elements $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho \in \mathbb{C}(q)$ is fixed.

For each integer $N \geq 1$, on every finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q$-module of "type 1" with diameter $N$, there exist $q$-analogues of Davies' relations: certain explicit polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ act as zero on the module. Let $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ be the quotient of $A_q$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these universal polynomial relations.

For $N=1$, $A_q^{[3]}$ is isomorphic to the Askey–Wilson algebra $AW(3)$ of Zhedanov, and there is a known algebra homomorphism from $AW(3)$ into the double affine Hecke algebra (DAHA) of type $(C_1^\vee,C_1)$.

Question: For general $N \geq 2$, does there exist an algebra homomorphism from $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ into an algebra that naturally generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type $(C_1^\vee, C_1)$?
status_search_result: Searches related to the q-Onsager algebra, the quotients $A_q^{[2N+1]}$, and homomorphisms into generalized DAHAs surface related work (FRT presentations of classical Askey–Wilson algebras, the q-Onsager / universal Askey–Wilson connection, generalized q-Onsager algebras and boundary affine Toda theories), but no source found explicitly constructs, for general $N\ge 2$, a homomorphism from $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ into an algebra generalizing the $(C_1^\vee,C_1)$ DAHA. The current status is therefore unclear from public sources.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X,g)^Γ, compute the higher Ext groups between finite-dimensional M-modules, explain how these Ext groups interact with both the representation theory of g and the geometry of X, and determine how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules is governed by that geometry.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over $\Bbbk$, let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\Bbbk$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by automorphisms on $X$ and on $\mathfrak{g}$. Define the equivariant map algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = \{\,f \in \mathfrak{g}\otimes_{\Bbbk}\mathcal{O}(X) : (\gamma\cdot f)(\gamma\cdot x) = \gamma\cdot f(x)\ \text{for all}\ \gamma\in\Gamma,\, x\in X\,\},$$
viewed as a Lie algebra under the pointwise bracket. Let $\mathcal{F}(M)$ denote the category of finite-dimensional $M$-modules.

(a) For all pairs $(V,W)$ of finite-dimensional $M$-modules and all integers $n\ge 0$, compute the Ext groups
$$\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{M}(V,W),$$
giving an explicit description in terms of the representation theory of $\mathfrak{g}$ and of geometric invariants of $X$ (such as tangent spaces, cotangent complexes, or other local data of $X$ at the support points of $V$ and $W$).

(b) Determine the global dimension of the category $\mathcal{F}(M)$, expressed as an invariant of the scheme $X$ (and of the action of $\Gamma$).
status_search_result: First Ext groups between finite-dimensional simple modules have been computed for equivariant map algebras and for twisted current algebras (work of Kodera, Lau, and others), and these results have been applied to block decompositions. However, a general computation of higher Ext^n groups between arbitrary finite-dimensional modules and a determination of the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules in terms of the geometry of X do not appear to have been carried out in full generality.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules from currently understood cases to more general equivariant map algebras, including determining lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules, and extending BGG reciprocity to this broader EMA setting.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be an irreducible affine scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, with coordinate ring A = k[X], and let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k. Suppose a finite group Γ acts on X by automorphisms and on g by Lie algebra automorphisms. The associated equivariant map algebra is

  M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗_k A)^Γ,

the Lie subalgebra of Γ-fixed points in g ⊗ A under the diagonal action.

For a triangular-type decomposition of M(X,g)^Γ (when one is available, e.g. when g is reductive with a fixed Cartan and Borel preserved compatibly with Γ), one defines:
 (i) the global Weyl module W(λ) attached to a dominant integral weight λ, as the universal cyclic highest-weight module on which the positive part acts by zero and a chosen Cartan-type subalgebra acts via λ;
 (ii) the local Weyl module W_loc(λ, m), obtained from W(λ) by quotienting by the action of a maximal ideal m of the commutative algebra A_λ := End_{M(X,g)^Γ}(W(λ))^{op}.

The problem is to:

(a) For general data (X, g, Γ) as above (going beyond the cases of untwisted loop algebras, twisted loop algebras, multi-loop algebras, current algebras, and equivariant map algebras with free abelian group action treated in the existing literature), determine the length, the k-dimension, and the (graded) character of every local Weyl module W_loc(λ, m).

(b) Formulate and prove a version of Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand (BGG) reciprocity in the category of finite-dimensional graded (or suitably restricted) modules over M(X, g)^Γ: namely, exhibit a class of "standard" modules (e.g. global or local Weyl modules) and a class of indecomposable projective covers P(λ) of the simple objects L(λ), and prove that the projective P(λ) admits a filtration whose multiplicities [P(λ) : Δ(μ)] equal the multiplicities [Δ(μ) : L(λ)] of L(λ) as a composition factor of the standard module Δ(μ), in this general equivariant map algebra setting.
category_tag: Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: local Weyl modules are understood for equivariant map algebras with free abelian group actions (Fourier–Khandai–Kus, 2011), global Weyl modules for general equivariant map algebras have been studied (Feigin–Loktev, Chari–Fourier–Khandai, and subsequent work), and BGG reciprocity has been established for current algebras (Bennett–Chari–Manning, 2012; Bennett–Bianchi–Chari et al., 2014). Recent extensions include hyper-map algebras and equivariant map Lie superalgebras (2025). However, a uniform treatment giving lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules and BGG reciprocity for fully general equivariant map algebras remains incomplete. The problem is therefore partially solved.

context_brief: Classification of finite-dimensional irreducibles of A_q^{[2N+1]}
original_question: Let A_q^{[2N+1]} be the quotient of A_q obtained by imposing the polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on finite-dimensional modules. Classify the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q^{[2N+1]}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and $q\in\mathbb{F}^\times$ a nonzero scalar that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebra with generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q^2-q^{-2})^2$.

For a fixed positive integer $N$, on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module certain polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ are known to act as zero. Let $I_{2N+1}\subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all such polynomial relations of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0,W_1$ that vanish on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module, and define
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem. Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules.
status_search_result: While the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of the full q-Onsager algebra A_q are known to correspond to tridiagonal pairs of q-Racah type, no source found explicitly establishes a complete classification for the truncated quotient A_q^{[2N+1]} defined by the degree-(2N+1) relations. The status of this specific classification problem appears to be unresolved in the readily accessible literature.

original_question: The paper states that some multivariable polynomials introduced by Gasper and Rahman in 2006 provide an infinite-dimensional basis of the q-Onsager algebra. Study in detail the finite-dimensional modules associated with these Gasper-Rahman multivariable polynomials, in the setting of the quotient algebra A_q^{[2N+1]} built from the polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 that vanish on finite-dimensional A_q-modules.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $q$ be a nonzero complex parameter that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with two generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1], \qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q-q^{-1})^2$.

Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials. Let $\{P_{n_1,\dots,n_k}(x_1,\dots,x_k)\}$ denote the family of multivariable orthogonal $q$-Racah polynomials of Gasper and Rahman (a multivariable extension of the Askey–Wilson/$q$-Racah scheme). Suppose that, viewed as elements built from $W_0, W_1$ via a fixed substitution, these polynomials yield a linear basis of $A_q$.

Quotient. For an integer $N \ge 1$, let $I_{2N+1} \subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all polynomial relations in $W_0, W_1$ of total degree $2N+1$ that act as zero on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module of "level" $2N+1$, and set
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem. 
(a) Classify, up to isomorphism, the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of $A_q^{[2N+1]}$.
(b) Carry out a detailed study of the finite-dimensional $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules naturally associated with the Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials: describe their structure, weights/eigenvalues of natural commuting subalgebras, decomposition into irreducibles, and the role played by the Gasper–Rahman polynomials as overlap coefficients between distinguished eigenbases.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Develop representation-theoretic categories for equivariant map algebras beyond finite-dimensional modules, including analogues of category O, categories of integrable highest-weight representations, categories of quasifinite representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces, and other suitable infinite-dimensional module categories.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}$, let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting on $X$ by automorphisms of schemes and on $\mathfrak{g}$ by Lie algebra automorphisms. The associated equivariant map algebra is
$$M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = \{\, \alpha \in \mathfrak{g}\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\mathcal{O}(X) : (\gamma\cdot\alpha)=\alpha \text{ for all } \gamma\in\Gamma\,\},$$
where $\Gamma$ acts diagonally on $\mathfrak{g}\otimes\mathcal{O}(X)$ via its actions on $\mathfrak{g}$ and on $\mathcal{O}(X)$. This class includes (twisted and untwisted) loop algebras and current algebras as special cases.

The finite-dimensional representation theory of $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$ has been developed in considerable generality. The problem is to develop a representation theory of $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$ in infinite-dimensional settings, by introducing and studying natural module categories that extend the known frameworks for loop and current algebras to arbitrary equivariant map algebras. Specifically:

(a) Define and study an analogue of the Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand category $\mathcal{O}$ for $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$, including a suitable triangular decomposition, characters, Verma-type modules, and classification of simple objects.

(b) Define and classify the integrable highest-weight representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$, generalising the integrable highest-weight theory available for affine Kac–Moody (loop) algebras.

(c) Define and classify the quasifinite representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$, that is, weight modules all of whose weight spaces are finite-dimensional, with respect to an appropriate Cartan-type subalgebra.

(d) Identify and study other natural infinite-dimensional module categories for $M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma}$ (for example, smooth modules, restricted modules, or global/local Weyl module categories) and relate them to the categories in (a)–(c).
status_search_result: The program is broad and ongoing. Partial progress exists: integrable representations have been studied for equivariant map algebras associated with Borel–de Siebenthal pairs and for root-graded Lie algebras (which include EMAs); global/local Weyl modules and uniformly bounded weight modules have been investigated for various map algebras (e.g., map Witt, map Virasoro, map extended special/Hamiltonian). However, a uniform development of category O, integrable highest-weight, and quasifinite categories for arbitrary EMAs has not been completed, so the overall problem remains open in general.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Assume g is semisimple and M = M(X,g)^Γ. Describe the first cohomology group H1(M,V) for a general M-module V, extending the partial results already known for some equivariant map algebras and locally finite modules; in particular, clarify this cohomology for the adjoint module Mad, where H1(M,Mad) = Der_k(M) / IDer(M).
self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let g be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over k, and let X be a scheme of finite type over k. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X by scheme automorphisms and on g by Lie algebra automorphisms. The associated equivariant map algebra is

  M = M(X, g)^Γ = { f ∈ g ⊗_k 𝒪(X) : (id ⊗ γ*)·f = γ·f for all γ ∈ Γ },

with Lie bracket induced from that of g and pointwise multiplication on 𝒪(X). For an M-module V, let H^1(M, V) denote the first Chevalley–Eilenberg Lie algebra cohomology of M with coefficients in V, which classifies equivalence classes of abelian extensions / outer derivations valued in V.

Problem. Give an explicit description of H^1(M, V) for a general M-module V, in terms of invariants of (X, g, Γ) and of V. In particular:

(a) Specialize to the adjoint module M_ad = M (with action by the Lie bracket) and produce an explicit description of

  H^1(M, M_ad) = Der_k(M) / IDer(M),

the space of outer k-linear derivations of M (where IDer(M) denotes inner derivations).

(b) Extend the result beyond the previously known cases (such as multiloop algebras and locally finite modules) to a uniform statement covering arbitrary M-modules V and arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ with g semisimple.
category_tag: Equivariant map algebras / Lie algebra cohomology
status_search_result: A targeted search did not return a definitive description of H^1(M, V) for general M-modules V and arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ with g semisimple. Partial results exist (Neher–Savage and related work) for multiloop algebras and locally finite modules, and general derivation results are known in special cases, but no uniform answer for general V appears to have been published. The status of the general problem could not be conclusively verified.

context_brief: Direct problem for ordinary h-fold sumsets
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let A be an m-element subset of G with m <= p < hm - h + 1. Is it true that the minimum possible size of the h-fold sumset hA is p, and that equality |hA| = p holds if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a positive integer $h$ and a finite subset $A\subseteq G$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA=\{a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h\in A\}\,. $$
For positive integers $m,h$, let
$$\rho(G,m,h)=\min\{|hA| : A\subseteq G,\ |A|=m\}\,. $$
Assume that $m\le p<hm-h+1$. Prove or disprove the following statement: under these hypotheses one has $\rho(G,m,h)=p$, and for every $m$-element subset $A\subseteq G$ the equality $|hA|=p$ holds if and only if $A$ is contained in a coset of some subgroup $H\le G$ of order $p$.
status_search_result: The conjecture appears in Bajnok's compendium of open problems on sumsets in finite abelian groups. Subsequent surveys (including recent ones in 2023–2025) continue to discuss direct and inverse problems for $\rho(G,m,h)$, but no source found in the search definitively establishes a full proof or disproof of the inverse characterization stated above. The status is therefore reported as unknown based on the available evidence.

original_question: In the boundary case where p is the smallest prime divisor of n and p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of a finite abelian group G for which the h-fold sumset hA has minimum possible size. In particular, beyond arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p, determine all subsets that can occur in this extremal case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A\}.$$
For positive integers $m, h$ with $1 \le m \le |G|$, let
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Consider the boundary case in which $p = hm - h + 1$. In this regime two known families of $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ achieve the minimum value of $|hA|$:
(i) arithmetic progressions of length $m$ in $G$ (i.e., subsets of the form $\{a, a+d, a+2d, \ldots, a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$);
(ii) $m$-element subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of order $p$.

Problem: Classify completely all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ for which $|hA|$ equals the minimum value $\rho(G, m, h)$ when $p = hm - h + 1$. In particular, determine all extremal configurations beyond the two families (i) and (ii).

status_search_result: A web search for the inverse classification problem for h-fold sumsets in finite abelian groups in the boundary case p = hm - h + 1 did not return any specific resolution. Related work by Bajnok and others studies ρ(G,m,h) and inverse problems, but no explicit classification of all extremal m-subsets in this boundary case was located. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: Determine the homology groups H_*(M,V) for equivariant map Lie algebras M and M-modules V, including the structural consequences for the abelianization H0(M,Mad) = M / [M,M] and for identifying perfect equivariant map algebras.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by Lie algebra automorphisms on $\mathfrak{g}$ and by scheme automorphisms on $X$. Form the equivariant map algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = \{\,\alpha \in \mathfrak{g}\otimes_k \mathcal{O}(X) : (\gamma\cdot \alpha) = \alpha \text{ for all } \gamma\in\Gamma\,\},$$
viewed as a Lie algebra under the pointwise bracket, where $\Gamma$ acts diagonally on $\mathfrak{g}\otimes \mathcal{O}(X)$.

For an $M$-module $V$, let $H_*(M,V)$ denote the Chevalley–Eilenberg homology of $M$ with coefficients in $V$.

(a) Compute the homology groups $H_*(M,V)$ for general pairs $(M,V)$ of equivariant map algebras and modules; in particular, identify the structure of these homology groups in terms of the data $(\mathfrak{g}, X, \Gamma)$.

(b) Compute the abelianization $H_0(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$, where $M_{\mathrm{ad}}$ denotes $M$ acting on itself by the adjoint action.

(c) Use (b) to characterize, in terms of $(\mathfrak{g}, X, \Gamma)$, exactly which equivariant map algebras $M$ are perfect (i.e. satisfy $[M,M] = M$).
category_tag: Equivariant map algebras / Lie algebra homology
status_search_result: Partial results are known: the abelianization $H_0(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$ has been computed in several cases, leading to classifications of perfect equivariant map algebras (work of Neher–Savage and collaborators). However, a full computation of the higher homology groups $H_*(M,V)$ for general equivariant map algebras and general modules $V$ does not appear to have been carried out, and the problem is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
original_question: For a perfect equivariant map Lie algebra M = (g ⊗ A)^Γ, understand its central extensions, especially the universal central extension uce(M), and determine when the universal central extension of the fixed-point algebra agrees with the fixed points of the universal central extension of the untwisted algebra, namely when uce((g ⊗ A)^Γ) is naturally isomorphic to uce(g ⊗ A)^Γ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a Lie algebra over $k$, and let $A$ be a commutative associative unital $k$-algebra. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by Lie algebra automorphisms on $\mathfrak{g}$ and by $k$-algebra automorphisms on $A$. The diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on the (untwisted) map algebra $\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A$ is given by $\gamma \cdot (x \otimes a) = (\gamma \cdot x) \otimes (\gamma \cdot a)$. The corresponding equivariant map algebra is the fixed-point Lie subalgebra
$$M := (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma = \{ z \in \mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A : \gamma \cdot z = z 	ext{ for all } \gamma \in \Gamma\}.$$

For any perfect Lie algebra $L$ (i.e.\ $[L,L] = L$) there exists a universal central extension $\mathrm{uce}(L) 	woheadrightarrow L$, characterized up to unique isomorphism by being a perfect central extension that uniquely covers every central extension of $L$.

Assume that $M = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma$ is perfect. The action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A$ lifts uniquely to an action on $\mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)$ by Lie algebra automorphisms, so the fixed-point algebra $\mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma$ is well-defined.

Describe the universal central extension $\mathrm{uce}(M)$ explicitly. In particular, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the triple $(\mathfrak{g}, A, \Gamma)$ under which there is a natural isomorphism
$$\mathrm{uce} igl((\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma igr) \;\cong\; \mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma.$$
category_tag: universal central extensions of Lie algebras
status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found in the literature. Related work on central extensions of equivariant map algebras and twisted current/loop algebras (e.g., by Neher, Chernousov, Pianzola, and collaborators) treats important special cases (twisted loop algebras, multiloop algebras), but a general criterion for the natural isomorphism uce((g⊗A)^Γ) ≅ uce(g⊗A)^Γ does not appear to be established in full generality. Status appears to remain open or only partially understood.

context_brief: Restricted sumset formula when m <= p
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume h < m <= p. Is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset of an m-element subset always min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}? In other words, does rho_hat(G, m, h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1} hold throughout this range?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For an integer $h \ge 1$ and a subset $A \subseteq G$, define the $h$-fold restricted sumset of $A$ by
$$h^{\wedge} A = \{\, a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h \in A,\ a_i \neq a_j \text{ for } i \neq j\,\}.$$
For integers $m, h$ with $1 \le h \le m \le |G|$, define
$$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, |h^{\wedge} A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\,\}.$$
Assume $h < m \le p$. Prove or disprove:
$$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, p,\ hm - h^2 + 1\,\}.$$
status_search_result: For cyclic groups of prime order, the formula follows from the Dias da Silva–Hamidoune theorem (1994). For general finite abelian groups with $h<m\le p$ (smallest prime divisor of $|G|$), the equality is stated as a conjecture in Bajnok's work on restricted sumsets, and recent literature on critical numbers and restricted sumsets does not report a full proof for arbitrary finite abelian groups; only partial/related results and tight upper bounds are available. Status appears to remain open in general.

context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets above the prime threshold
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume 2 <= h <= m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Classify the m-element subsets A of G whose h-fold restricted sumset has the minimum size hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that equality |h_hat A| = hm - h^2 + 1 occurs only in the exceptional case h = 2, m = 4 with A = {a, a + g1, a + g2, a + g1 + g2}, or when A is an arithmetic progression in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and an integer $h$ with $1 \le h \le |A|$, define the $h$-fold restricted sumset by
$$h^{\wedge} A \;=\; \{\, a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A \text{ are pairwise distinct}\,\}.$$
Fix integers $m \ge 4$ and $h$ with $2 \le h \le m-2$, and assume that $p > hm - h^2 + 1$. It is known that under these hypotheses every $m$-element subset $A \subseteq G$ satisfies $|h^{\wedge} A| \ge hm - h^2 + 1$. Classify all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ for which equality $|h^{\wedge} A| = hm - h^2 + 1$ holds. Specifically, prove or disprove: equality holds if and only if either
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h = 2$, $m = 4$, and $A = \{a,\; a+g_1,\; a+g_2,\; a+g_1+g_2\}$ for some $a, g_1, g_2 \in G$, or
\item $A$ is an arithmetic progression in $G$, i.e., $A = \{a,\; a+d,\; a+2d,\; \ldots,\; a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$.
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: For finite sets of integers, the analogous inverse result (equality forcing an arithmetic progression for $m \ge 5$) is established. For general finite abelian groups under the prime threshold $p > hm - h^2 + 1$, the classification appears to be stated as a conjecture; recent works on Kneser-type theorems and inverse Erdős–Heilbronn problems address related cases but no source verifying a complete proof of this exact classification in arbitrary finite abelian groups was found.

context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets at size p
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume m <= p < hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that an m-element subset A satisfies |h_hat A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For an integer $h\ge 1$ and a finite subset $A\subseteq G$, define the restricted $h$-fold sumset
$$\hat{h}A \;=\; \{\,a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h\in A\text{ are pairwise distinct}\,\}.$$
Fix positive integers $h$ and $m$ with $m\le p$, and assume the inequality
$$p \;<\; hm - h^2 + 1.$$

context_brief: Frequency of disagreement for two-fold signed sumsets
original_question: For an abelian group G of order n, compare the minimum size of a 2-fold signed sumset with the minimum size of the ordinary 2-fold sumset. Is it true that the values rho_plusminus(G, m, 2) and rho(G, m, 2) differ for fewer than n/4 choices of m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_i \in A\}$$
and the $h$-fold signed sumset
$$h_{\pm}A = \{\varepsilon_1 a_1 + \varepsilon_2 a_2 + \cdots + \varepsilon_h a_h : a_i \in A,\ \varepsilon_i \in \{+1,-1\}\}.$$
For integers $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ and $h \ge 1$, set
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\},$$
$$\rho_{\pm}(G, m, h) = \min\{|h_{\pm}A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every finite abelian group $G$ of order $n$, the number of integers $m \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ for which
$$\rho_{\pm}(G, m, 2) \ne \rho(G, m, 2)$$
is strictly less than $n/4$.
status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,h)$ vs $\rho(G,m,h)$, including results showing equality when $G$ is cyclic and resolution of related conjectures (e.g., for elementary abelian $p$-groups). However, no source directly confirming or refuting the specific quantitative claim that $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)$ and $\rho(G,m,2)$ disagree on fewer than $n/4$ values of $m$ for all finite abelian groups $G$ of order $n$ was found.

context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for chi_hat(Z_n,3)
original_question: For cyclic groups Z_n, determine whether the known lower bounds for the three-term restricted critical number chi_hat(Z_n, 3) are always sharp. More precisely, if n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 3 when n = p, (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 2 when n = 3p, and (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 1 otherwise? If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal floor(n/3) + 4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite abelian group G and a positive integer h, define the restricted h-fold sumset of a subset A ⊆ G by
  h^∧ A = { a_1 + a_2 + ⋯ + a_h : a_1, …, a_h ∈ A, a_i ≠ a_j for i ≠ j },
and define the restricted h-critical number χ̂(G, h) to be the smallest positive integer m such that h^∧ A = G for every subset A ⊆ G with |A| = m (when such an m exists).

Take G = Z_n, the cyclic group of order n, and h = 3. Determine whether the following equalities hold for all n ≥ 16:

(1) If n has at least one prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), and p denotes the smallest such prime divisor, then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 3   if n = p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 2   if n = 3p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 1   otherwise.

(2) If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 4   if 9 | n,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 3   otherwise.

The corresponding inequalities "≥" are known to hold; the question is whether equality always holds.
status_search_result: The conjectured equality is a known generalization of a Gallardo–Grekos-type conjecture; the lower bound is proved, and equality is verified for n even, n prime, and (by computer) small n. No general proof for all n appears in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: embedding problem for H^p Dirichlet series
original_question: Let H^p denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}, with norm induced by vertical translation and equivalently by the Hardy space on the infinite-dimensional torus under the Bohr correspondence. Is there a constant C_p,L depending only on p and the fixed segment length L, but not on the coefficients or on N, such that every Dirichlet polynomial satisfies an inequality of the form \int_I |\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-1/2-it}|^p \, dt \le C_{p,L} \|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}\|_{H^p}^p for every interval I of length L on the vertical line Re s = 1/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet polynomials, i.e., finite sums $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ with complex coefficients $a_n$. For $1\le p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal H^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of $\mathscr{D}$ with respect to the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p \;=\; \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt,$$
which, via the Bohr lift $n^{-s}\mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional torus.

Fix a real number $L>0$. The question is the following:

For which $p\in[1,\infty)$ does there exist a constant $C_{p,L}>0$, depending only on $p$ and $L$, such that the inequality
$$\int_I \Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-1/2 - it}\Big|^p\,dt \;\le\; C_{p,L}\,\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p$$
holds for every Dirichlet polynomial $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ (with $N\ge 1$ arbitrary and coefficients arbitrary) and for every interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ of length $L$ on the critical line $\operatorname{Re} s=1/2$?
status_search_result: The embedding inequality is known to hold when $p$ is an even integer (a classical consequence of Montgomery–Vaughan-type estimates) and is established with explicit constants in subsequent work. For $p<2$ in particular and for non-even $p$ in general, the inequality remains an open problem; surveys on the analysis of Dirichlet series continue to list it as a central open question.

original_question: For the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series on the half-plane Re s > 1/2, characterize the Carleson measures when p<2; that is, characterize the positive measures μ on {Re s > 1/2} for which there is a constant C such that \int_{Re s>1/2} |F(s)|^p \, dμ(s) \le C \|F\|_{H^p}^p for all F in H^p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet series $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$. For $0<p<\infty$, define the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series as the completion of the set of Dirichlet polynomials $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
$$\|P\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Bigl|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Bigr|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p}.$$
Every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

A positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ is called a Carleson measure for $\mathcal{H}^p$ if there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb{C}_{1/2}} |F(s)|^p\,d\mu(s) \;\le\; C\,\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p \qquad \text{for every } F\in\mathcal{H}^p.$$

Problem: For $0<p<2$, give an intrinsic geometric or capacitary characterization of all positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ that are Carleson measures for $\mathcal{H}^p$.
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Carleson measures for Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series on the half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$ for $p<2$ is repeatedly stated as open in surveys and recent work on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., the 2019 survey on Hardy spaces of general Dirichlet series and subsequent work on Volterra/multiplier operators, which use partial Carleson-type embeddings without obtaining a full characterization). Even the case $p=2$ — known as the embedding problem — remains only partially understood, so the case $p<2$ is a fortiori open.

original_question: If F belongs to H^p for some p<2, must the zero set of F in the half-plane Re s > 1/2 satisfy the Blaschke condition for that half-plane, i.e. the natural summability condition on the zeros analogous to the classical Hardy-space Blaschke condition?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}^p$ (for $0<p<\infty$) denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series defined as follows. For a Dirichlet polynomial $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, set
$$\|P\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}:=\left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|P(it)|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},$$
and define $\mathcal{H}^p$ as the completion of the Dirichlet polynomials in this norm. Equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n=\mathfrak{p}^{\alpha}$ identifying $n^{-s}$ with the monomial $z^{\alpha}$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus $\mathbb{T}^{\infty}$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometric to $H^p(\mathbb{T}^{\infty})$. Every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ has an analytic extension to the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

A sequence $\{s_k\}\subset\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ is said to satisfy the Blaschke condition for $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ if
$$\sum_{k}\frac{\operatorname{Re}(s_k)-\tfrac12}{1+|s_k|^2}<\infty,$$
equivalently $\sum_k(\operatorname{Re}(s_k)-\tfrac12)/|s_k+\tfrac12|^2<\infty$ once one accounts for the conformal map onto the unit disk.

Question: Suppose $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ for some $0<p<2$ and $F\not\equiv 0$. Must the zero set of $F$ in the half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$, counted with multiplicities, satisfy the Blaschke condition for that half-plane?

No solution has been verifiably located, and the problem appears to remain open, but available evidence is inconclusive.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: At present collider energies, for QCD processes involving partons with small longitudinal momentum fraction x and transverse momentum kT of order the saturation scale Qs(x), is the nonlinear parton-saturation description implemented by the Color Glass Condensate phenomenology actually necessary, or can the data be described adequately by purely linear gluon distributions supplemented with a non-perturbative ad hoc cutoff? Here parton saturation means the weakly coupled nonlinear QCD regime that appears when parton densities grow at small x, and Qs(x) is the momentum scale separating dense and dilute regimes.
self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD) processes at present-day high-energy hadron and nuclear colliders that probe partons carrying a small longitudinal momentum fraction x of their parent hadron and having transverse momentum k_T of the order of the saturation scale Q_s(x). Here "parton saturation" denotes the weakly coupled nonlinear QCD regime expected to set in when gluon densities at small x become so large that nonlinear effects (such as gluon recombination) balance linear BFKL-type growth, and Q_s(x) is the momentum scale separating the dense (k_T ≲ Q_s) from the dilute (k_T ≫ Q_s) regime, with Q_s(x) increasing as x decreases. The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) is the effective field theory implementation of this nonlinear saturation regime.

Question: Is it necessary, at currently accessible collider energies, to use the nonlinear CGC/saturation framework to describe QCD data in the kinematic region x ≪ 1, k_T ∼ Q_s(x)? Equivalently: can the relevant observables in this regime be adequately described instead by purely linear (collinear or k_T-factorized) gluon distributions supplemented by an ad hoc non-perturbative infrared cutoff, or does an adequate description of the data require properly incorporating the nonlinear dynamics at k_T ∼ Q_s(x)?

The task is to determine, on the basis of comparison with collider data, whether nonlinear saturation dynamics is unavoidable for a satisfactory phenomenological description, or whether linear-evolution descriptions with a tunable infrared cutoff suffice.
category_tag: QCD parton saturation / Color Glass Condensate
status_search_result: The question of whether nonlinear saturation/CGC dynamics is strictly necessary at current colliders, as opposed to linear gluon distributions with an ad hoc infrared cutoff, remains an active phenomenological question. Recent work (e.g. NLO CGC phenomenology with threshold resummation for forward hadron production at RHIC/LHC, and CMS observations of long-range two-particle correlations in p–Pb collisions) provides increasingly suggestive but not yet conclusive evidence for saturation. The community generally still treats this as an open question, motivating future facilities such as the Electron-Ion Collider.

original_question: If F belongs to H^p for some p<2, is F locally in the Nevanlinna class in the half-plane Re s > 1/2; in other words, on every bounded subregion of that half-plane, does F have the local logarithmic-integrability property characteristic of Nevanlinna-class functions?
self_contained_problem:
For $0<p<\infty$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} |F(it)|^p \, dt\right)^{1/p}.$$
Equivalently, via Bohr's correspondence $n^{-s} \mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional polytorus. Each $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

Recall that a holomorphic function $f$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ is said to belong locally to the Nevanlinna class if for every relatively compact subdomain $U\Subset\Omega$ with smooth boundary,
$$\sup_{r}\int_{\partial U_r} \log^+ |f(z)|\, |dz| < \infty,$$
where $\{U_r\}$ is an exhaustion of $U$; equivalently, $\log^+|f|$ has a positive harmonic majorant on every relatively compact subdomain of $\Omega$.

Question: For every $p<2$ and every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$, does $F$ belong locally to the Nevanlinna class on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$?

Related work on Nevanlinna-class Dirichlet series and a mean counting function for $\mathcal{H}^p$ exists, but no source explicitly settles this problem. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: For exponents p in (1,\infty) with p\neq 2, does the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series admit an unconditional basis; that is, does it have a basis for which convergence is stable under arbitrary sign changes or bounded coefficient multipliers in the usual Banach-space sense?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $p\in[1,\infty)$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series defined as follows. For a Dirichlet polynomial $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$, set
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \lim_{T\to\infty}\Big(\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt\Big)^{1/p},$$
and define $\mathcal{H}^p$ as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials in this norm. Equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots\mapsto z_1^{\alpha_1}z_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus equipped with normalized Haar measure.

A Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of a Banach space $X$ is called unconditional if for every $x\in X$ with expansion $x=\sum_n c_n e_n$, the series converges unconditionally (equivalently, $\sum_n \varepsilon_n c_n e_n$ converges in $X$ for every choice of signs $\varepsilon_n\in\{-1,+1\}$).

Question: For every $p\in(1,\infty)$ with $p\neq 2$, does the Banach space $\mathcal{H}^p$ admit an unconditional Schauder basis?
status_search_result: The question of whether the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series admits an unconditional basis for $p\in(1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$ appears to remain open. It is known that the canonical Dirichlet monomial basis $\{n^{-s}\}$ is unconditional in $\mathcal{H}^p$ only for $p=2$, but the existence of some other unconditional basis is unresolved. Recent literature on linear-space properties of $\mathcal{H}^p$ and on related dilation/translation systems continues to treat this as an outstanding question.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: How fast, and by what QCD dynamics, does a high-energy nuclear collision observable transition from the nonlinear saturation regime to the high-transverse-momentum leading-twist regime, given that current running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov small-x evolution equations do not include the DGLAP limit and predict that proton-nucleus nuclear-modification observables return to unity only at unrealistically large transverse momentum pT?
self_contained_problem:
In the framework of small-$x$ QCD evolution for high-energy nuclear collisions, the running-coupling Balitsky–Kovchegov (rcBK) equation governs the nonlinear evolution of the dipole scattering amplitude $N(r,x)$ in the saturation regime, while DGLAP evolution governs the linear, leading-twist regime at large transverse momentum $p_T \gg Q_s(x)$, where $Q_s(x)$ is the saturation scale. The nuclear modification factor for proton–nucleus collisions is defined as
$$R_{pA}(p_T,y) = \frac{1}{A}\,\frac{d^2N_{pA}/dp_T\,dy}{d^2N_{pp}/dp_T\,dy},$$
which by collinear-factorization expectations should approach unity for $p_T \gg Q_s$. Current rcBK-based predictions, however, do not embed the DGLAP limit and yield $R_{pA}\to 1$ only at unrealistically large $p_T$, especially at forward rapidities where small-$x$ evolution has acted.

Determine, within QCD, the dynamics and rate of the transition from the nonlinear saturation regime to the high-$p_T$ leading-twist DGLAP regime. Specifically:

(i) Construct a small-$x$ evolution scheme for the unintegrated gluon distribution (or dipole amplitude) that simultaneously reduces to rcBK in the saturation regime ($p_T \lesssim Q_s$) and to DGLAP evolution in the leading-twist regime ($p_T \gg Q_s$), with a controlled matching at intermediate $p_T$.

(ii) Quantify, in this scheme, how rapidly $R_{pA}(p_T,y)\to 1$ as $p_T$ grows above $Q_s(x)$, identifying the parametric dependence of the transition scale on $x$ (or rapidity $y$), $A$, and the strong coupling $\alpha_s$.

(iii) Show that the resulting predictions are consistent with proton–nucleus collider data and, where available, electron–nucleus deep-inelastic scattering data.
category_tag: Small-x QCD evolution and gluon saturation
status_search_result: Recent literature confirms that the precise matching between nonlinear (rcBK/JIMWLK) small-$x$ evolution and linear DGLAP leading-twist evolution remains phenomenologically unsettled: theoretical arguments only establish each framework in its asymptotic limit, and the intermediate-$(x,Q^2)$ kinematics relevant to $R_{pA}$ at the LHC is still unclear. Various DGLAP-improved saturation models (e.g., color-dipole DGLAP-improved fits) and unified evolution proposals exist, but no consensus solution embeds DGLAP into rcBK so that $R_{pA}\to 1$ at realistic $p_T$.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: What is the transverse impact-parameter dependence of the nuclear gluon density and of the saturation scale Qs in a nucleus, and is the current phenomenological Color Glass Condensate practice of modeling a nucleus as Woods-Saxon distributed CGCs whose gluon densities are evolved independently at different impact parameters sufficient for a conceptually accurate description of small-x nuclear structure?
self_contained_problem:
In the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory of small-x QCD, a large nucleus at high energy is characterized by a transverse-position-dependent gluon distribution and a local saturation scale Q_s(x, b), where x is the longitudinal momentum fraction and b is the transverse impact parameter relative to the nuclear center. A common phenomenological prescription is to model the nucleus as an ensemble of independent CGC sources distributed in the transverse plane according to a Woods–Saxon profile

  ρ(r) = ρ_0 / (1 + exp((r - R)/a)),

and to evolve the gluon density at each impact parameter b independently in x via small-x evolution equations (e.g., the JIMWLK or BK equations), with no transverse coupling between different b.

Determine, from first principles in QCD at high parton density:

(a) the correct functional dependence of the nuclear gluon density xG_A(x, b) and of the saturation scale Q_s,A(x, b) on the transverse impact parameter b in a large nucleus at small x;

(b) whether the prescription of treating the nucleus as a Woods–Saxon distribution of independent CGC sources with b-independent (locally evolved) small-x evolution provides a conceptually accurate description of the transverse structure of nuclei at small x, or whether non-trivial transverse correlations and/or coupling between different impact parameters during small-x evolution must be included for a correct description.

original_question: Does the Hardy space H^1 of Dirichlet series admit a Schauder basis at all, and if it does, can such a basis be chosen to be unconditional?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the set of formal Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$. For a Dirichlet polynomial $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, define
$$\|P\|_{H^1} := \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Bigl|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Bigr|\,dt.$$
Equivalently, via the Bohr lift identifying $n^{-s}$ with the monomial $z^{\kappa(n)}$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ (where $\kappa(n)=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\dots)$ is the exponent vector in the prime factorization $n=\prod_j p_j^{\kappa_j}$), the norm equals $\|P\|_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^\infty)}$. The Hardy space $H^1$ of Dirichlet series is the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials under this norm.

Recall that a sequence $(e_k)_{k\geq 1}$ in a Banach space $X$ is a Schauder basis if every $x\in X$ has a unique norm-convergent expansion $x=\sum_k c_k(x)e_k$, and it is unconditional if this convergence is unconditional for every $x\in X$.

(a) Does $H^1$ admit a Schauder basis?

(b) If so, can such a basis be chosen to be unconditional?
status_search_result: The canonical system $\{n^{-s}\}$ is known to be a Schauder basis of $H^p$ for $1<p<\infty$ and only a Markushevich basis (not Schauder) for $H^1$; it is unconditional only when $p=2$. Whether $H^1$ of Dirichlet series admits any Schauder basis, and whether it admits an unconditional one, appears to remain open in the literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series; recent works (e.g., on translated Hardy spaces and Fourier multipliers) treat related but distinct questions without resolving these.

original_question: Let H^p(T^\infty) be the Hardy space on the infinite-dimensional torus, viewed as boundary values of analytic functions on the infinite polydisc D^\infty. What general conditions on a radial or non-tangential approach to a boundary point of T^\infty guarantee that a Fatou-type theorem holds, meaning that functions in H^p(T^\infty) have almost-everywhere boundary limits along that approach?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}^\infty = \{ z = (z_1, z_2, \ldots) : z_j \in \mathbb{C},\ |z_j| < 1 \text{ for all } j,\ \sup_j |z_j| < 1 \}$ be the infinite polydisc, and let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{j=1}^\infty \{ |w_j| = 1 \}$ be the infinite-dimensional torus, equipped with the product Haar (Lebesgue) measure $m_\infty$. For $1 \le p \le \infty$, let $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ denote the Hardy space defined as the closure in $L^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty, m_\infty)$ of the analytic trigonometric polynomials (those whose Fourier coefficients are supported on multi-indices $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ with $\alpha_j \ge 0$ for all $j$). Each $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ corresponds to an analytic function $\widetilde{f}$ on $\mathbb{D}^\infty$ (defined for instance on $\bigcup_{0<r<1} r\,\mathbb{D}^\infty$ via its monomial expansion), and $f$ is recovered as a boundary value of $\widetilde{f}$.

For a point $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, an "approach family" to $w$ is a family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ of subsets $A_w \subset \mathbb{D}^\infty$ accumulating at $w$ (e.g., the radial approach $\{rw : 0 < r < 1\}$, or some non-tangential analogue).

Problem. Determine general conditions on such an approach family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ — radial or non-tangential — under which a Fatou-type theorem holds: namely, for every $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ and for $m_\infty$-almost every $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, the limit
$$\lim_{\substack{z \to w \\ z \in A_w}} \widetilde{f}(z)$$
exists and equals $f(w)$.
category_tag: Hardy spaces on the infinite polydisc
status_search_result: The problem of identifying general radial or non-tangential approach regions yielding a.e. boundary limits for $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ functions remains a delicate one. Aleman, Olsen, and Saksman (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique, 2019) established several Fatou-type theorems for restricted modes of radial convergence and showed that the pointwise Fatou theorem fails in infinite dimensions without such restrictions even for bounded analytic functions. No comprehensive characterization of admissible radial/non-tangential approaches has been found in subsequent literature, so the problem appears to remain open in its general form, with only partial results.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: How does QCD make the transition from the high-parton-density saturation regime, where small-x gluons form a weakly coupled nonlinear many-body system, to the confinement regime of QCD?
self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the dynamics of hadrons probed at very small Bjorken-x is governed by a high-density system of gluons. In this regime, nonlinear gluon recombination effects balance linear gluon emission, leading to the phenomenon of parton saturation, characterized by a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x) that grows as x decreases. When Q_s is large compared to Lambda_QCD, the strong coupling alpha_s(Q_s) is small, so the saturated gluon system can be described as a weakly coupled but highly nonlinear many-body system (e.g., via the Color Glass Condensate effective theory, the JIMWLK/BK evolution equations, and classical Yang-Mills fields as the relevant degrees of freedom). At the opposite extreme, when momentum scales approach Lambda_QCD, QCD becomes strongly coupled and exhibits color confinement, with hadrons rather than gluons as the appropriate degrees of freedom.

Provide a quantitative theoretical description of how QCD interpolates between these two regimes. Specifically:

(a) Determine how the small-x, high-density (saturation) description of hadronic matter, formulated in terms of weakly coupled nonlinear classical color fields, evolves into the confining regime of QCD as the saturation scale Q_s is decreased toward Lambda_QCD.

(b) In particular, characterize whether classical color fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom throughout the transition, determine whether and how the QCD coupling should be taken to run with Q_s in this crossover, and describe the universality properties (if any) of observables in the transition region.
status_search_result: The question of how QCD transitions from the weakly coupled small-x saturation regime to the strongly coupled confining regime is a long-standing open conceptual problem in high-energy QCD. It remains an active research topic addressed by Color Glass Condensate, JIMWLK/BK evolution studies, and ongoing experimental programs (p+A at the LHC and forthcoming e+A at the EIC), with no complete theoretical solution reported.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: In the QCD saturation regime at high parton density, does the QCD coupling run with the saturation scale Qs, the momentum scale that separates dense and dilute small-x regimes and increases as x decreases?
self_contained_problem: In quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at high parton density and small Bjorken x, the transition between the dense (high-occupancy) and dilute regimes of the gluon distribution inside a hadron or nucleus is characterized by a dynamically generated momentum scale Q_s(x), called the saturation scale, which grows as x decreases. The strong coupling α_s(μ) of QCD depends on a renormalization scale μ via the QCD β-function, and in many small-x evolution equations (e.g., the Balitsky–Kovchegov and JIMWLK equations) the choice of the scale at which α_s is evaluated is not uniquely fixed by the leading-order formalism.\n\nDetermine whether, in the saturation regime at small x, the appropriate renormalization scale for the running QCD coupling is set by the saturation scale Q_s(x) itself. Concretely: establish, from first principles within perturbative QCD beyond leading order, whether α_s should run with μ = Q_s(x) (or some specified function of Q_s) when describing observables and evolution equations in the high-parton-density regime, and characterize precisely the kinematic conditions under which such a prescription is correct.
status_search_result: This is posed as a fundamental open conceptual question in small-x/saturation QCD. While running-coupling corrections to the BK and JIMWLK equations have been computed (Balitsky; Kovchegov–Weigert) and phenomenological fits often use scales related to Q_s, there is no rigorous derivation establishing that the coupling universally runs with Q_s; the choice of scale remains a topic of ongoing research and debate. Status appears open.

original_question: For the Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series, especially in the non-locally-convex range 0<p<1 highlighted just before the question, describe their dual spaces; equivalently, determine the continuous linear functionals on H^p and represent them in an explicit usable form.
self_contained_problem:
For a Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$, recall the following construction. By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, each integer $n\ge 1$ factors uniquely as $n=p_1^{\kappa_1}p_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$ where $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ are the primes. The Bohr correspondence assigns to $f$ the formal power series $\mathcal{B}f(z)=\sum_n a_n z^{\kappa(n)}$ in infinitely many variables $z=(z_1,z_2,\dots)$, where $z^{\kappa(n)}=z_1^{\kappa_1}z_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$. For $0<p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm (quasi-norm when $0<p<1$)
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\int_{\mathbb{T}^\infty} |\mathcal{B}f(z)|^p\, dm_\infty(z)\right)^{1/p},$$
where $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ is the infinite-dimensional torus and $m_\infty$ is its normalized Haar measure. Equivalently (by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem), $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T |f(it)|^p\,dt$ for Dirichlet polynomials.

For $1<p<\infty$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is a reflexive Banach space, but for $0<p\le 1$ — and especially in the non-locally-convex range $0<p<1$ — the structure of the topological dual is far less understood.

Problem. Describe the dual space $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$. That is, characterize all continuous linear functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ and provide an explicit, usable concrete representation of them (for instance, as a space of Dirichlet series or via pairings with such, together with a norm or quasi-norm equivalent to the dual norm).
status_search_result: Subsequent literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., works on linear space properties of $\mathcal{H}^p$, multipliers, and Volterra operators) continues to investigate functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ for $0<p\le 1$ — for instance establishing that $\varphi_\beta(s)=\sum n^{-\beta-s}$ defines a bounded functional on $\mathcal{H}^p$ when $\beta>1/p$ and not when $\beta<1/p$, and conjecturing the boundary case. However, no full description of $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$ appears in the literature; the problem is referenced as still open in recent surveys and papers.

original_question: On the infinite-dimensional torus T^\infty, what should replace Nehari’s theorem for Hankel forms or small Hankel operators? In particular, how should one characterize the Riesz projection of L^\infty(T^\infty) and the corresponding bounded-mean-oscillation-type spaces on T^\infty?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{T}$ denote the infinite-dimensional torus equipped with its normalized Haar measure. For a multi-index $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ (finitely supported integer sequences), let $z^\alpha = \prod_n z_n^{\alpha_n}$ denote the corresponding character. Define the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ as the closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ spanned by $\{z^\alpha : \alpha \ge 0\}$ (i.e., $\alpha_n \ge 0$ for all $n$), and let $P_+ : L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty) \to H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ be the orthogonal Riesz projection. For an analytic symbol $\psi = \sum_{\alpha \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha) z^\alpha$, the (small) Hankel form is defined on finite analytic polynomials by
$$H_\psi(f,g) = \sum_{\alpha,\beta \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha+\beta)\, \hat f(\alpha)\, \hat g(\beta),$$
with norm $\|H_\psi\|$ as a bilinear form on $H^2 \times H^2$.

Nehari's classical theorem on $\mathbb{T}$ states that $H_\psi$ is bounded if and only if $\psi = P_+\varphi$ for some $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$, with $\|H_\psi\| \asymp \inf\{\|\varphi\|_\infty : P_+\varphi = \psi\}$.

Problem: Formulate and establish the appropriate counterpart of Nehari's theorem on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. Specifically, characterize intrinsically the space $P_+(L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty))$ — the Riesz projection of $L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ — and identify natural BMO-type spaces on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ that govern the boundedness of Hankel forms / small Hankel operators in this infinite-dimensional setting.
category_tag: Hankel forms and BMO on the infinite torus
status_search_result: Searches indicate this remains an open problem. The classical Nehari theorem holds on finite polydisks $\mathbb{T}^d$ (Ferguson–Lacey for $d=2$, Lacey–Terwilleger for $d>2$), but the constants grow at least exponentially in the dimension (work building on Helson), which precludes a direct passage to $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. No intrinsic characterization of $P_+(L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty))$ or of a corresponding BMO space adequate to characterize bounded Hankel forms on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ has been established.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
context_brief: Effective degrees of freedom in high-density QCD
original_question: Are classical fields still the correct effective degrees of freedom for describing the many-body system of strongly correlated gluons in QCD at high parton density, especially in the parton-saturation regime explored by proton-nucleus and electron-nucleus collisions?
self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at high parton densities, hadrons and nuclei are dominated by gluons whose occupation numbers grow until nonlinear interactions balance gluon emission, producing a characteristic saturation momentum scale $Q_s$. In the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework, fast partons are treated as static color sources with random color charge density $\rho^a(x_\perp)$ governed by a weight functional $W_Y[\rho]$ (with rapidity $Y$ evolution given by the JIMWLK equation), while slower gluons are described by classical Yang–Mills fields $A^\mu_a$ obeying $[D_\mu, F^{\mu\nu}]_a = J^\nu_a$ sourced by $\rho^a$. Observables are computed as path integrals $\langle \mathcal{O}\rangle = \int \mathcal{D}\rho\, W_Y[\rho]\, \mathcal{O}[A_{\rm cl}[\rho]]$ together with quantum fluctuations on top of these classical solutions.

Determine whether classical color fields, in the sense above, remain the correct effective degrees of freedom for the strongly correlated many-gluon system of QCD in the saturation regime probed by proton–nucleus and electron–nucleus collisions. Concretely: identify a parametric regime (in terms of $Q_s$, $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, the strong coupling $\alpha_s(Q_s)$, the atomic number $A$, and the rapidity $Y$) and an observable for which the leading-order classical-field description, supplemented by the standard small-$x$ quantum evolution, either (i) provides a controlled approximation to full QCD with quantifiable corrections, or (ii) demonstrably fails, requiring a different effective description (for instance, one in which the relevant degrees of freedom are not classical fields).
category_tag: Color Glass Condensate and parton saturation
status_search_result: The question of whether classical color fields are the correct effective degrees of freedom in saturated QCD is conceptual and remains an active research direction. The CGC effective theory continues to be developed and tested phenomenologically at RHIC and the LHC, and is a central motivation for the Electron-Ion Collider, but no definitive proof of its validity (or its replacement) in the strongly correlated saturation regime has been established. The status is therefore best characterized as open.

paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
original_question: What universality properties characterize the QCD saturation regime of high-density small-x gluons, and how can proton-nucleus and electron-nucleus collisions explore those properties in the strongly correlated gluonic many-body system?
self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), at small Bjorken-x the gluon density inside a hadron grows rapidly and is conjectured to enter a non-linear regime, called parton saturation, characterized by a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x,A) (depending on x and on the nuclear mass number A) at which non-linear gluon recombination balances linear BFKL-type growth, while the strong coupling α_s(Q_s) remains weak. In this regime the small-x gluon system is described as a strongly correlated many-body state, often modeled by classical Yang–Mills color fields (the Color Glass Condensate effective theory) with stochastic color sources.

Formulate and establish the universality properties of this saturation regime. Specifically:

(a) Identify and prove which observables (e.g., dipole scattering amplitudes, unintegrated gluon distributions, multi-parton correlators, n-point Wilson-line correlators) become universal functions of the single combination Q_s(x,A) times a transverse scale, independent of the specific hadronic target (proton vs. nucleus) and of details of the initial non-perturbative input.

(b) Determine the precise sense (geometric scaling, fixed points of the JIMWLK / Balitsky–Kovchegov non-linear evolution equations, scaling solutions of these renormalization-group equations) in which such universality holds, including the dependence on the running of α_s and on impact parameter.

(c) Specify which measurements in proton–nucleus (p+A) and electron–nucleus (e+A) collisions—such as forward single-inclusive hadron production, di-hadron azimuthal correlations, diffractive vector-meson production, inclusive and diffractive deep inelastic structure functions—can isolate and quantitatively test these universality predictions, distinguishing genuine saturation universality from leading-twist collinear-factorization expectations.

(d) Characterize how the saturation regime connects, as Q_s decreases, to the confinement regime, and whether classical color fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom in that transition.
status_search_result: The universality of the QCD saturation regime and its experimental exploration via p+A and e+A collisions remains an active open research direction. While partial universality results (geometric scaling, BK/JIMWLK fixed-point analyses, CGC factorization theorems for limited classes of observables) have been established, a complete characterization is unresolved and is a central scientific motivation for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), expected to begin operations in the early 2030s.

original_question: Consider the Dirichlet-series symbol \u03d5_0(s)=1+\sum_{n=2}^\infty (\log n)^{-1} n^{-1/2-s}, which arises as the analytic symbol of the multiplicative Hilbert matrix. Is \u03d5_0 the Riesz projection of some essentially bounded function on the infinite-dimensional torus T^\infty?

the sum being taken over multi-indices with all nonnegative entries. Via the Bohr correspondence $z_j \leftrightarrow p_j^{-s}$ (where $p_j$ is the $j$-th prime), an analytic function on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ corresponds to a Dirichlet series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$.

Consider the Dirichlet series
$$\phi_0(s) = 1 + \sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{\log n}\, n^{-1/2 - s},$$
which is the analytic symbol of the multiplicative Hilbert matrix $\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{mn}\,\log(mn)}\bigr)_{m,n\geq 2}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $F \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ such that, under the Bohr correspondence, $\phi_0$ corresponds to the analytic projection $P_+ F$?
status_search_result: The problem was posed in connection with the multiplicative Hilbert matrix and its analytic symbol. Subsequent literature on Riesz projection for Dirichlet series and on critical exponents of the Riesz projection (through 2024) discusses the question and related embedding problems but does not appear to resolve it. No source located indicates that $\phi_0$ has been shown to be (or fail to be) the Riesz projection of an $L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ function, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Characterize the compact composition operators on H^2, the Hilbert space of Dirichlet series with square-summable coefficients. Equivalently, determine exactly which analytic self-maps that induce composition on Dirichlet series act compactly on H^2.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{H}^2$ denote the Hilbert space of Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$ with square-summable coefficients, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_{\mathscr{H}^2}^2=\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2$. By a theorem of Gordon and Hedenmalm, an analytic function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}_{1/2}\to\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ (where $\mathbb{C}_\theta=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>\theta\}$) induces a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi f = f\circ\varphi$ on $\mathscr{H}^2$ if and only if $\varphi$ admits a representation
$$\varphi(s) = c_0 s + \sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n n^{-s},$$
with $c_0\in\mathbb{N}_0$ a non-negative integer, the Dirichlet series $\sum_n c_n n^{-s}$ converges uniformly in $\mathbb{C}_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and either (a) $c_0\geq 1$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_0$, or (b) $c_0=0$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$.

Problem: Give a complete characterization of those symbols $\varphi$ in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class for which the composition operator $C_\varphi:\mathscr{H}^2\to\mathscr{H}^2$ is compact.
category_tag: Composition operators on Dirichlet series spaces
status_search_result: Brevig and Perfekt (Advances in Mathematics 385 (2021), 107775; arXiv:2005.05094) introduced a mean counting function for Dirichlet series and characterized the compact composition operators with Dirichlet series symbols on $\mathscr{H}^2$: $C_\varphi$ is compact iff the mean counting function of $\varphi$ satisfies a specified decay condition at the boundary of the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$. This resolves the characterization problem in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class.
