original_question: Does there exist, for a general invariant random-matrix ensemble, a corresponding Wigner-like family that has the same limiting spectral density, in the same way that Wigner ensembles correspond to the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble and Wishart ensembles correspond to the Laguerre Unitary Ensemble?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) An invariant random-matrix ensemble on the space of N×N Hermitian matrices is a probability measure of the form
   dP_N(H) = (1/Z_N) exp(-N Tr V(H)) dH,
where V: ℝ → ℝ is a (sufficiently regular, confining) potential, dH is Lebesgue measure on Hermitian matrices, and Z_N is the normalizing constant. Such measures are invariant under unitary conjugation H ↦ U H U*. The empirical spectral distribution μ_N = (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^N δ_{λ_i(H)} converges, as N → ∞, to a deterministic compactly supported probability measure μ_V on ℝ (the equilibrium measure associated with V), called the limiting spectral density of the ensemble.

(2) A Wigner-type ensemble is an ensemble of N×N Hermitian matrices W = (W_{ij}) whose entries are independent (up to the Hermitian symmetry W_{ji} = conjugate(W_{ij})) and centered, with variances scaled so that an N → ∞ limiting spectral density exists. The classical Wigner ensembles share the semicircle law as their limiting spectral density with the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE), the invariant ensemble corresponding to V(x) = x²/2. Similarly, Wishart-type ensembles (sample covariance matrices with i.i.d. entries) share the Marchenko–Pastur law as their limiting spectral density with the Laguerre Unitary Ensemble (LUE), an invariant ensemble built from a quadratic potential on positive matrices.

Problem. Given an arbitrary confining potential V (or, more generally, an arbitrary invariant ensemble) with limiting spectral density μ_V, does there exist a corresponding Wigner-type family — that is, an ensemble of Hermitian random matrices with independent entries (subject to Hermitian symmetry), centered, with appropriately scaled variances — whose empirical spectral distribution also converges almost surely (or in probability) to μ_V as N → ∞? In other words, for every limiting spectral density μ_V arising from an invariant ensemble, construct a Wigner-type ensemble realizing the same limiting spectral density, or else prove that no such Wigner-type family exists for some μ_V.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not return a definitive result settling this question in full generality. The known correspondences (semicircle law for GUE/Wigner, Marchenko–Pastur for LUE/Wishart) are widely cited as special cases. Wigner-type matrices with variance profiles can produce a broad family of limiting densities, but a complete dictionary matching every invariant-ensemble equilibrium measure μ_V to a Wigner-type ensemble does not appear to be established in the literature retrieved.

original_question: For parameters delta > 0, lambda > 0, and n in N_0, define F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) = integral from 0 to t of (t-theta)^delta C_n^lambda(cos theta) (sin theta)^(2 lambda) dtheta for 0 < t < pi, where C_n^lambda is the Gegenbauer polynomial. Is it true that F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) > 0 for all t in (0, pi] if and only if delta >= lambda + 1?
self_contained_problem:
For a real parameter $\lambda > 0$ and a nonnegative integer $n$, let $C_n^{\lambda}$ denote the Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomial of degree $n$ and parameter $\lambda$, defined by the generating function
$$\frac{1}{(1-2xr+r^2)^{\lambda}} = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} C_n^{\lambda}(x)\, r^n, \qquad |r|<1,\ x\in[-1,1].$$
For real parameters $\delta>0$, $\lambda>0$, and $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, define
$$F_n^{\lambda,\delta}(t) \;=\; \int_0^t (t-\theta)^{\delta}\, C_n^{\lambda}(\cos\theta)\, (\sin\theta)^{2\lambda}\, d\theta, \qquad 0<t\le \pi.$$
Decide whether the following statement is true: $F_n^{\lambda,\delta}(t) > 0$ for every $t\in(0,\pi]$ and every $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ if and only if $\delta \ge \lambda+1$.
status_search_result: A web search did not return any subsequent paper that resolves this positivity conjecture about the integral $F_n^{\lambda,\delta}$. It appears in a list of open problems from a 2015 special-functions meeting and no proof or counterexample could be located, so the status is taken to be unknown.

paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
original_question: For open-loop quantum control, where the task is to vary a Hamiltonian H = sum_n c_n H_n in time to obtain a desired evolution, which control objectives and which available sets of control Hamiltonians H_n make the control problem easy, with the time-dependent-control complexity scaling polynomially in the logarithm of the system size? Does the class of easy objectives depend nontrivially on the chosen set of available Hamiltonians?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open-loop quantum control setting in which the controller drives a finite-dimensional quantum system of Hilbert-space dimension N via a time-dependent Hamiltonian of the form
   H(t) = Σ_n c_n(t) H_n,
where {H_n} is a fixed finite set of available control Hamiltonians and the classical control coefficients c_n(t) may be varied (essentially) arbitrarily as functions of time. Given a control objective (for example, preparing a specified target state from a fixed initial state, or implementing a specified unitary on the system, up to a prescribed error tolerance), define the time-dependent-control complexity of the objective to be the minimal description complexity (e.g., number of bits or piecewise-constant control segments) of a control schedule {c_n(t)} that achieves the objective. Call the control problem "easy" for the pair (objective, {H_n}) if this complexity scales as a polynomial in log N as N grows along a natural family of systems.

(a) Characterize the pairs consisting of a control objective and a set of available control Hamiltonians {H_n} for which the open-loop control problem is easy in the sense above.

(b) Determine whether the class of easy objectives depends nontrivially on the choice of the set {H_n}: that is, exhibit objectives that are easy for some admissible sets of control Hamiltonians but not for others, or prove that the class of easy objectives is independent of the choice of {H_n} within a suitable family.
status_search_result: The question is posed as one of twenty open problems in quantum control (2013) and asks for a general characterization of "easy" open-loop control problems. A targeted web search did not surface any work claiming a complete characterization of which (objective, control-Hamiltonian set) pairs admit polylogarithmic-in-system-size control complexity, nor a resolution of whether the class of easy objectives depends nontrivially on the chosen Hamiltonian set. Related progress exists on Hamiltonian simulation and gate-synthesis complexity, but the broad characterization sought appears to remain open.

paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
context_brief: Complex measurement-based protocols for small systems
original_question: For continuous-measurement-based feedback control of small quantum systems, including even a single qubit, can more complex protocols than those previously tried—especially protocols that modify the measurement as part of feedback—improve performance, and when they do improve performance, does the improvement reveal anything about coherent feedback control?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a small open quantum system $S$ (for example, a single qubit with Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^2$) coupled to an environment and subject to a continuous quantum measurement whose record is fed back, in real time, into the system's Hamiltonian and/or into the choice of measurement itself. Formally, the conditional state $\rho_t$ evolves according to a stochastic master equation
$$d\rho_t = -i[H(u_t),\rho_t]\,dt + \mathcal{D}[L(v_t)]\rho_t\,dt + \mathcal{H}[L(v_t)]\rho_t\,dW_t,$$
where $\mathcal{D}[L]\rho = L\rho L^\dagger - \tfrac{1}{2}\{L^\dagger L,\rho\}$, $\mathcal{H}[L]\rho = L\rho + \rho L^\dagger - \mathrm{Tr}[(L+L^\dagger)\rho]\rho$, $dW_t$ is a Wiener increment associated with the measurement record, and the control parameters $u_t$ (Hamiltonian control) and $v_t$ (measurement-basis/operator control) are causal functionals of the past measurement record. Fix a control objective such as the steady-state fidelity with a target pure state $|\psi\rangle$, i.e.\ maximize
$$J[u,v] = \liminf_{T\to\infty}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\tfrac{1}{T}\int_0^T \langle\psi|\rho_t|\psi\rangle\,dt\right].$$

(a) Construct continuous-measurement-based feedback protocols for such small systems—in particular for a single qubit—that are strictly more general than those considered to date by allowing the measurement operator $L(v_t)$ itself to be modified in feedback, and determine whether such protocols can strictly improve $J[u,v]$ over the best known protocols that use only a fixed measurement and Hamiltonian feedback.

(b) For any protocol that does yield such an enhancement, determine what the structure of the enhancement implies about coherent feedback control, in which the controller is itself a quantum system coupled to $S$ without any classical measurement step.

Identify, where possible, the optimal feedback protocol for the single-qubit case under physically natural noise models and control constraints.

The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let A_n(t) be the polynomial sequence defined by (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3) A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1) A_{n+1}(t) + ((n+2)^2/(n+1)) A_{n+2}(t) = 0 with A_0 = 1 and A_1 = 0, and let A_tilde_n(t) = sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t). If A_tilde_n satisfies (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3) A_tilde_{n-1} + (2n+1)n A_tilde_n - (n+1)^2 n A_tilde_{n+1} = 0, is there an argument that deduces directly from this recurrence that lim_{n->infinity} A_tilde_n(t) = product over j>=1 of (1 + t^3/(8 j^3))?
self_contained_problem:
Define a sequence of polynomials $\{A_n(t)\}_{n\ge 0}$ in a variable $t$ by the initial conditions $A_0(t)=1$, $A_1(t)=0$, and the three-term recurrence
$$(n^3-(-1)^n t^3)\,A_n(t)+(n+1)^2(2n+1)\,A_{n+1}(t)+\frac{(n+2)^2}{n+1}\,A_{n+2}(t)=0,\qquad n\ge 0.$$
Set $\widetilde A_n(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} A_k(t)$. It is known that this partial-sum sequence satisfies the three-term recurrence
$$(n^3-(-1)^n t^3)\,\widetilde A_{n-1}(t)+(2n+1)n\,\widetilde A_n(t)-(n+1)^2 n\,\widetilde A_{n+1}(t)=0,\qquad n\ge 1,$$
and that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\widetilde A_n(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}\left(1+\frac{t^3}{8j^3}\right).$$
Provide a proof of this limit identity that proceeds directly from the three-term recurrence satisfied by $\widetilde A_n(t)$, i.e., deduce the value of $\lim_{n\to\infty}\widetilde A_n(t)$ from this recurrence alone, without recourse to the closed-form/combinatorial expressions for $A_n(t)$.

Status could not be verified.

original_question: For the polynomial sequences A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t) associated with the modified multiple-zeta-value identity in Section 7, can these polynomials be expressed explicitly in hypergeometric form?
self_contained_problem:
Define two sequences of polynomials $\{A_n(t)\}_{n\ge 0}$ and $\{\widetilde{A}_n(t)\}_{n\ge 0}$ in the variable $t$ by the following recurrences.

The polynomials $A_n(t)$ are determined by the three-term recurrence
$$(n^3-(-1)^n t^3)\,A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1)\,A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1)\,A_{n+2}(t) = 0,$$
with initial conditions $A_0(t)=1$ and $A_1(t)=0$.

The polynomials $\widetilde{A}_n(t)$ are determined by the recurrence
$$(n^3-(-1)^n t^3)\,\widetilde{A}_{n-1}(t) + (2n+1)n\,\widetilde{A}_n(t) - (n+1)^2 n\,\widetilde{A}_{n+1}(t) = 0,$$
with appropriate initial conditions ensuring the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \widetilde{A}_n(t) = \prod_{j=1}^{\infty}\left(1+\frac{t^3}{8j^3}\right).$$

paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
context_brief: Feedforward control in mesoscopic quantum systems
original_question: Are there situations in mesoscopic quantum systems where feedforward control is useful, where feedforward means that the controller receives information about the noise realization without interacting with the system rather than obtaining information only through the system as in feedback control? If such situations exist, what explicit examples demonstrate the feedforward-control paradigm, and how does feedforward control compare with feedback control in those examples?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a mesoscopic quantum system (e.g., a superconducting circuit, quantum dot, optomechanical resonator, or ultracold atomic ensemble) modeled as an open quantum system whose dynamics are governed by a controlled master equation or stochastic Schrödinger equation, and which is subject to a classical or quantum noise process N(t) generated by an identifiable environment.

Define two control paradigms:

1. Feedback control: the controller obtains information about the system only by performing measurements on the system itself (or on its output fields), and uses the measurement record to choose control inputs applied back to the system.

2. Feedforward control: the controller obtains information about the realization of the noise N(t) without interacting with the system — for example, by directly probing the noise source or environment before (or independently of) the noise's action on the system — and uses this information to apply a control input to the system designed to compensate for the upcoming noise.

The problem is the following:

(a) Identify physically meaningful situations in mesoscopic quantum systems for which feedforward control, in the sense above, is useful — that is, situations where access to the noise realization (without measuring the system) provides a control advantage with respect to relevant figures of merit such as fidelity, decoherence suppression, gate error, or state transfer efficiency.

(b) Construct explicit example models (with concrete Hamiltonians, noise sources, and control inputs) demonstrating the feedforward-control paradigm in such systems.

(c) For each such example, quantitatively compare feedforward control with feedback control on the same system and noise model, identifying the regimes (in terms of noise statistics, bandwidth, measurement back-action, accessibility of the environment, and control resources) in which feedforward outperforms feedback, and vice versa.
status_search_result: Several explicit feedforward-control demonstrations in mesoscopic-scale quantum systems have appeared, e.g., feedforward cancellation of optical phase noise in STIRAP state transfer of ultracold RbCs molecules (Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 253202, 2024), and feedforward implementations in superconducting circuits and quantum networks. However, a systematic theoretical framework comparing feedforward vs. feedback across mesoscopic platforms is not yet complete, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: On Completions, neat atom structures, and omitting types
context_brief: Elementary status of weak-unit complete representability
original_question: Is the class of countable completely representable algebras of countably infinite dimension, when representability is taken on weak units (equivalently, via weak representations or weak models rather than square units), an elementary class; that is, can this class be characterized by first-order sentences and shown to be closed under elementary equivalence?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of algebraic logic. For a countably infinite ordinal α, let CA_α denote the variety of cylindric algebras of dimension α. A representation of an algebra 𝔄 ∈ CA_α on a square unit is an embedding into a cylindric set algebra whose unit is a Cartesian power ^αU for some non-empty set U. A representation on a weak unit (also called a weak representation, or representation on a weak space) is an embedding into a generalized cylindric set algebra whose unit is a weak space ^αU^{(p)} = { s ∈ ^αU : |{ i ∈ α : s(i) ≠ p(i) }| < ω } for some fixed p ∈ ^αU. Such a representation is called complete if it preserves all existing infinitary suprema and infima of the algebra.

Let CRCA_α^w denote the class of all atomic algebras 𝔄 ∈ CA_α that admit a complete representation on a weak unit, where α is countably infinite and 𝔄 is countable.

Question: Is CRCA_α^w an elementary class? Equivalently, can membership in CRCA_α^w be characterized by a set of first-order sentences in the signature of CA_α, so that CRCA_α^w is closed under elementary equivalence?
status_search_result: It is known (Hirsch–Hodkinson) that the class of completely representable cylindric algebras of dimension ≥ 3 with square units is non-elementary, and that for infinite-dimensional polyadic algebras the class of completely representable algebras is elementary. The variant for weak units (weak representations) in countably infinite dimension does not have a clearly identified resolution in the available sources; the Hirsch–Hodkinson cardinality argument is noted not to transfer to weak units, and no later paper located in the search definitively settles whether the weak-unit version is elementary. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Let 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure such that the Banach space L^p(μ) is non-separable. Can L^p(μ) occur as a subspace of some Banach space that has an unconditional basis?
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, and let $\mu$ be a finite (positive) measure such that the Banach space $L^p(\mu)$ is non-separable. Recall that a sequence $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in a Banach space $X$ is called an unconditional (Schauder) basis if every $x \in X$ has a unique representation $x = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n e_n$ that converges unconditionally (i.e., the convergence is independent of the order of summation).

Question: Does there exist a Banach space $Y$ which possesses an unconditional basis and contains $L^p(\mu)$ as a (closed linear) subspace?

Equivalently, can a non-separable $L^p(\mu)$ space (with $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$) be embedded isomorphically into a Banach space having an unconditional basis?
category_tag: Non-separable L^p spaces and unconditional bases
status_search_result: Enflo and Rosenthal proved that the answer is "no" when the density character of $L^p(\mu)$ is at least $\aleph_\omega$, and conjectured the same conclusion in the entire non-separable range. Subsequent work (e.g., by Johnson and Schechtman) has obtained partial results on non-separable $L^p$ spaces, but the problem in full generality (for all non-separable densities, in particular $\aleph_1$) appears to remain open.

original_question: Let 2 < p < ∞, and let X be a subspace of an L^p space that does not contain a copy of ℓ^p(ω_1). Must there exist a finite measure μ such that X embeds into L^p(μ)?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a real number $p$ with $2 < p < \infty$. Recall that for a (possibly non-$\sigma$-finite) measure space $(\Omega,\Sigma,
u)$, the Banach space $L^p(
u)$ consists of (equivalence classes of) measurable functions $f$ with $\int |f|^p\,d
u < \infty$, equipped with the usual norm. For an index set $I$, $\ell^p(I)$ denotes the Banach space of functions $x : I 	o \mathbb{R}$ with $\sum_{i \in I} |x_i|^p < \infty$. Let $\omega_1$ denote the first uncountable ordinal, viewed as an index set of cardinality $\aleph_1$.

Say that a Banach space $X$ is a \emph{subspace of an $L^p$ space} if there exists some measure space $(\Omega,\Sigma,
u)$ such that $X$ is linearly isomorphic to a closed linear subspace of $L^p(
u)$. Say that $X$ \emph{contains a copy of} $\ell^p(\omega_1)$ if $X$ has a closed subspace linearly isomorphic to $\ell^p(\omega_1)$.

Question: Suppose $X$ is a subspace of an $L^p$ space (for some measure space) and $X$ does not contain a copy of $\ell^p(\omega_1)$. Must there exist a finite measure $\mu$ such that $X$ embeds isomorphically as a closed subspace of $L^p(\mu)$?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question by Johnson and Schechtman. Web searches did not turn up a published resolution for the case $2 < p < \infty$. Related work by Johnson–Schechtman handles aspects of the $1 < p < 2$ case (showing $\ell^p(\aleph_1)$ does not embed into $L^p(\mu)$ for finite $\mu$), but the stated dichotomy for $p > 2$ does not appear to have been settled.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Let a graph be obtained as a limit of a network of thin tubes or guides joined at junctions, and let a nonlinear Schrödinger equation be posed on the shrinking tube system before the limit is taken. Does the vanishing-transverse-size limit produce a nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the limiting graph, and if so, which vertex boundary conditions appear at the junction? More specifically, how do the limiting vertex conditions depend on the way the tubes and junction are shrunk and on the boundary conditions imposed on the tube walls, such as Neumann or Dirichlet conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For each ε>0, let Ω_ε ⊂ ℝ^d be a "fat graph" obtained by thickening a finite metric graph G=(V,E): replace each edge e of G by a tubular neighborhood of transverse diameter of order ε, and join these tubes at neighborhoods of the vertices v∈V whose size shrinks at some prescribed rate as ε→0. On Ω_ε pose the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
   i ∂_t Ψ_ε = −Δ_{Ω_ε} Ψ_ε + κ |Ψ_ε|^{2σ} Ψ_ε,    in Ω_ε,
with κ∈ℝ, σ>0, equipped with either homogeneous Neumann or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω_ε (after appropriate rescaling/subtraction of the transverse ground-state energy in the Dirichlet case), and with suitable initial data concentrated on the lowest transverse mode.

Question. Does Ψ_ε converge, in an appropriate sense as ε→0, to a function ψ defined on the metric graph G that solves a nonlinear Schrödinger equation
   i ∂_t ψ = −Δ_G ψ + κ |ψ|^{2σ} ψ
on each edge, coupled at every vertex v by some self-adjoint vertex (boundary) condition C_v? If so, identify the vertex conditions C_v explicitly, and describe how they depend on:
(a) the geometric way in which the tubes and the junction regions are shrunk (relative scaling between transverse tube size, junction size, and edge lengths, as well as the angles/shapes of the junction);
(b) the choice of boundary conditions imposed on the lateral walls of the tubes (Neumann versus Dirichlet, and possibly mixed/Robin).

Determine whether standard Kirchhoff conditions, δ-type couplings, δ'-type couplings, or other self-adjoint conditions on G arise in the various scaling regimes.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Partial progress exists. In the linear case, thin-tube limits to quantum graphs are well studied (Kuchment–Zeng, Exner–Post, Molchanov–Vainberg). For the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, work such as Sabirov et al. "Soliton transport in tubular networks: transmission at vertices in the shrinking limit" (Phys. Rev. E 91, 023209, 2015) studies the NLS shrinking limit on Y-junctions and finds Kirchhoff/reflectionless transmission in particular regimes. A general rigorous derivation identifying vertex conditions for arbitrary junction geometries and lateral boundary conditions in the nonlinear case does not appear to be available, so the problem remains open in full generality.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Can one derive an effective one-dimensional Gross–Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics on graph-like structures, such as a Y-junction, directly from a many-body Bose system or another first-principles model? In particular, if one starts from an N-body theory on a graph and takes the many-particle limit with suitable scalings, how should the vertex or defect boundary conditions be handled in the limiting equation, given that even the corresponding problem for a line with a single defect is still open?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph consisting of a single vertex $v$ to which $k\ge 2$ half-lines (edges) $e_1,\dots,e_k$ are attached (e.g., $k=3$ corresponds to a Y-junction; $k=2$ corresponds to the real line with a single point defect at $v$). On each edge $e_j$ identified with $[0,\infty)$, consider an $N$-body bosonic Hamiltonian
$$H_N = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl(-\Delta_{x_i}\bigr) + \sum_{1\le i<j\le N} N^{2}V\bigl(N(x_i-x_j)\bigr),$$
acting on the symmetric $N$-fold tensor product of $L^2(\mathcal{G})$, where $-\Delta$ on $\mathcal{G}$ is the self-adjoint Laplacian determined by a prescribed family of vertex (matching) conditions at $v$ (for example Kirchhoff, $\delta$-type with strength $\alpha$, or a general self-adjoint coupling parametrized by a unitary matrix), and $V\ge 0$ is a short-range, spherically symmetric, compactly supported pair potential.

Question. Starting from a sequence of $N$-particle states whose one-particle reduced density matrices converge to a pure condensate $|\varphi\rangle\langle\varphi|$ with $\varphi\in L^2(\mathcal{G})$, derive rigorously, in the mean-field/Gross–Pitaevskii scaling limit $N\to\infty$, an effective one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger (Gross–Pitaevskii) equation
$$i\partial_t \varphi = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\varphi + g|\varphi|^{2}\varphi$$
on $\mathcal{G}$, identifying the effective coupling constant $g$ in terms of the scattering length of $V$, and—crucially—determine which self-adjoint vertex condition at $v$ the limiting one-particle operator $-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ must satisfy as a function of the microscopic vertex condition imposed on $H_N$. Treat in particular the case $k=2$ (a line with a single point defect) and the case $k=3$ (Y-junction).
category_tag: Mean-field limits and NLS on metric graphs
status_search_result: Rigorous derivations of the 1D Gross–Pitaevskii equation from many-body bosonic dynamics are well established on the line and on strongly confined 3D domains, but no derivation appears in the literature for metric graphs with non-trivial vertex (defect) conditions. Even on the line with a single point defect, the corresponding mean-field/Gross–Pitaevskii limit does not appear to have been carried out, consistent with the problem being posed as open.

original_question: Let 2 < p < ∞ and let μ be a finite measure. Is the Banach space L^p(μ) Hilbert generated, meaning that some Hilbert space H admits a bounded linear operator T: H → L^p(μ) with dense range?
self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $X$ is said to be Hilbert generated if there exist a Hilbert space $H$ and a bounded linear operator $T : H \to X$ with dense range. It is known that $L^p(\mu)$ is Hilbert generated for every $1 \le p \le 2$ and every finite measure $\mu$ (and, more generally, whenever $L^p(\mu)$ is separable).

Question: Let $2 < p < \infty$ and let $\mu$ be an arbitrary finite (positive) measure (so that $L^p(\mu)$ need not be separable). Is the Banach space $L^p(\mu)$ Hilbert generated, i.e., does there exist a Hilbert space $H$ and a bounded linear operator $T : H \to L^p(\mu)$ with dense range?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2016 list of open problems in Banach spaces and measure theory. It is known to hold for $1 \le p \le 2$ and for separable $L^p(\mu)$, but the general non-separable case for $2 < p < \infty$ does not appear to have been resolved in subsequent literature.

original_question: Let X be a Banach lattice for which there exists a weakly compact set L ⊆ X whose generated sublattice is dense in X. Must X be weakly compactly generated, that is, must there exist a weakly compact set K ⊆ X with X = span(K)?
self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be a Banach lattice. Suppose there exists a weakly compact subset $L \subseteq X$ such that the sublattice of $X$ generated by $L$ is norm-dense in $X$ (equivalently, $X$ is lattice-weakly compactly generated). Must $X$ be weakly compactly generated as a Banach space, i.e., must there exist a weakly compact subset $K \subseteq X$ whose linear span is norm-dense in $X$?
status_search_result: The problem has been solved in the negative. Using free Banach lattices, it has been shown that the free Banach lattice FBL[ℓ_p(Γ)] for p ∈ [1,2] and uncountable Γ is lattice-weakly compactly generated but not weakly compactly generated as a Banach space, providing a counterexample to Diestel's question. Positive answers are known under additional assumptions (e.g., order continuity with weakly sequentially continuous lattice operations, or X = C(K)).

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Is the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on trees well posed? More precisely, for a tree graph equipped with the relevant vertex coupling conditions, can one prove existence, uniqueness, and appropriate continuous dependence for solutions in the natural energy spaces, analogous to the well-posedness theory available for the star-graph case?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a metric tree graph: a connected, finite or locally finite graph without cycles whose edges $e\in E(\mathcal{T})$ are identified with intervals $[0,\ell_e]$ (with $\ell_e\in(0,+\infty]$ for unbounded external edges), and whose vertices $v\in V(\mathcal{T})$ are the endpoints. A function $u:\mathcal{T}\to\mathbb{C}$ is a collection $u=(u_e)_{e\in E(\mathcal{T})}$ of functions $u_e:[0,\ell_e]\to\mathbb{C}$. Define
\[
L^2(\mathcal{T})=\bigoplus_{e\in E(\mathcal{T})}L^2(0,\ell_e),\qquad H^1(\mathcal{T})=\{u\in\bigoplus_e H^1(0,\ell_e):\ u\text{ is continuous at every vertex}\},
\]
and let $H^2_K(\mathcal{T})$ consist of $u\in\bigoplus_e H^2(0,\ell_e)$ that are continuous at every vertex and satisfy the Kirchhoff condition
\[
\sum_{e\succ v}\partial_e u_e(v)=0\qquad\text{for every vertex }v\in V(\mathcal{T}),
\]
where $\partial_e u_e(v)$ denotes the derivative of $u_e$ at $v$ taken in the outgoing direction along $e$. Let $\Delta_\mathcal{T}$ be the Laplacian on $\mathcal{T}$ with domain $H^2_K(\mathcal{T})$, acting edgewise as the second derivative.

Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
\[
i\,\partial_t u(t,x)=-\Delta_\mathcal{T} u(t,x)+\lambda\,|u(t,x)|^{p-1}u(t,x),\qquad x\in\mathcal{T},\ t\in\mathbb{R},
\]
with $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ and $p>1$, subject to an initial datum $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$.

Prove (or disprove) the following: for every $u_0\in H^1(\mathcal{T})$, there exist $T=T(\|u_0\|_{H^1})>0$ and a unique solution
\[
u\in C\bigl([-T,T];H^1(\mathcal{T})\bigr)\cap C^1\bigl([-T,T];H^{-1}(\mathcal{T})\bigr)
\]
of the equation, the mass $\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2$ and the energy
\[
E(u(t))=\tfrac12\sum_e\int_0^{\ell_e}|\partial_x u_e|^2\,dx+\tfrac{\lambda}{p+1}\sum_e\int_0^{\ell_e}|u_e|^{p+1}\,dx
\]
are conserved on $[-T,T]$, and the solution map $u_0\mapsto u$ depends continuously on the initial datum in $H^1(\mathcal{T})$, in analogy with the corresponding theory for the star graph. Determine in particular the range of exponents $p$ for which local (and global) well-posedness in the energy space $H^1(\mathcal{T})$ holds.
status_search_result: Subsequent literature has established local and global well-posedness of NLS in the energy space on broad classes of metric graphs (including non-compact metric graphs with Kirchhoff-type conditions, of which trees are a case), via Strichartz/dispersive estimates and standard energy-method contraction arguments, together with mass and energy conservation. Thus the problem appears to be partially solved (well-posedness on trees with Kirchhoff conditions is now standard for energy-subcritical nonlinearities), although a fully unified statement for arbitrary trees with general admissible vertex couplings is not pinpointed by a single definitive reference.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: When the threshold condition ensuring existence of an absolute constrained minimizer fails for the action functional on a star graph, does the action still possess a local constrained minimum that is strictly larger than its infimum? Likewise, when the analogous threshold fails for the energy constrained at fixed mass, does the constrained energy still have a local constrained minimum above its infimum?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a star graph consisting of $N\ge 3$ half-lines joined at a common vertex $v$. For $\Psi=(\psi_j)_{j=1}^N\in L^2(\mathcal{G})=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N L^2(\mathbb{R}^+)$, denote the mass by $M(\Psi)=\sum_j\int_0^\infty|\psi_j(x)|^2\,dx$. Fix a coupling constant $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and a focusing power $p>2$. Consider on $\mathcal{G}$ the nonlinear Schrödinger problem with an attractive $\delta$-interaction of strength $\alpha$ at $v$: functions are continuous at $v$, $\psi_1(0)=\cdots=\psi_N(0)$, and the Kirchhoff-type condition $\sum_j\psi_j'(0)=\alpha\psi_1(0)$ holds. Define the energy
$$E(\Psi)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^N\int_0^\infty|\psi_j'|^2\,dx+\frac{\alpha}{2}|\Psi(v)|^2-\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j=1}^N\int_0^\infty|\psi_j|^p\,dx,$$
on the form domain $H^1(\mathcal{G})$, and, for $\omega>0$, the action
$$S_\omega(\Psi)=E(\Psi)+\frac{\omega}{2}M(\Psi).$$
There is a known threshold $\alpha^\ast<0$ (depending on $N$ and $p$) such that:

(i) for every $\omega>0$ with $-N\sqrt{\omega}<\alpha<\alpha^\ast$, the action $S_\omega$ admits an absolute minimizer on the natural Nehari-type constraint;

(ii) for every $\alpha<0$, the energy $E$ admits an absolute minimizer at fixed mass $M(\Psi)=m$ for all $m$ below an explicit critical value $m^\ast(\alpha)$.

Prove or disprove the following:

(a) When the condition $-N\sqrt{\omega}<\alpha<\alpha^\ast$ in (i) fails, the action $S_\omega$ still possesses, on the constrained set, a local minimizer whose action value is strictly greater than the infimum.

(b) When the analogous mass condition $m<m^\ast(\alpha)$ in (ii) fails, the energy $E$ at fixed mass $m$ still possesses a local minimizer on $\{M(\Psi)=m\}$ whose energy value is strictly greater than the infimum.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on quantum graphs
status_search_result: The energy part (b) of the conjecture has been addressed by Adami, Cacciapuoti, Finco, and Noja in "Stable standing waves for a NLS on star graphs as local minimizers of the constrained energy" (arXiv:1509.01810, 2016), where they prove that on a star graph with attractive delta interaction the symmetric standing wave is a local minimizer of the constrained energy at fixed mass for all admissible masses, even when the absolute-minimum threshold fails, yielding orbital stability. The corresponding statement for the action functional (part (a)) does not appear to be explicitly resolved in the same generality, so the full conjecture is at least partially solved.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Can the orbital-stability and instability analysis for standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation be extended from star graphs to more complex graphs, such as trees or graphs with loops? In such settings, where explicit formulas for stationary states are generally unavailable, can one still identify standing-wave branches and verify the spectral and variational conditions needed to prove stability or instability?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a connected metric graph (i.e., a finite or countable collection of edges, each identified isometrically with an interval of $\mathbb{R}$ or with a half-line, glued at vertices), and consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
$$ i \partial_t \psi(t,x) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi(t,x) - |\psi(t,x)|^{2\mu}\psi(t,x), \qquad x \in \mathcal{G},\ t \in \mathbb{R}, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ defined edgewise as $\partial_x^2$ with Kirchhoff (free) boundary conditions at each vertex, and $\mu>0$ is the focusing power. A standing wave is a solution of the form $\psi(t,x) = e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega(x)$, where $\Phi_\omega \in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ solves the stationary equation
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}\Phi_\omega + \omega \Phi_\omega - |\Phi_\omega|^{2\mu}\Phi_\omega = 0. $$
A standing wave is called orbitally stable if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that any solution with initial data within $\delta$ (in $H^1$-norm) of $\Phi_\omega$ remains within $\varepsilon$ of the orbit $\{e^{i\theta}\Phi_\omega : \theta \in \mathbb{R}\}$ for all time; otherwise it is orbitally unstable.

For star graphs (finite collections of half-lines joined at a single vertex), explicit formulas for the stationary states $\Phi_\omega$ are available, and orbital stability/instability has been analyzed via variational and spectral methods.

Problem: Extend the orbital stability and instability analysis of standing waves to more complex metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$, such as metric trees or graphs containing loops (e.g., tadpole, dumbbell, or bubble-tower graphs), where explicit closed-form expressions for the stationary states are generally unavailable. Specifically, identify branches $\omega \mapsto \Phi_\omega$ of standing-wave solutions on such graphs and establish the spectral conditions (on the linearized operator around $\Phi_\omega$) and variational/energy conditions sufficient to determine the orbital stability or instability of these branches.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was raised: orbital stability/instability of standing waves has been studied on tadpole graphs, dumbbell graphs, bubble-tower graphs, and metric trees, with both existence results and (in)stability theorems for specific branches. However, a complete, general theory covering arbitrary trees and graphs with loops remains incomplete, so the broad question is only partially solved.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: For nonlinear Schrödinger equations on graphs whose linear part has eigenvalues, bifurcation theory can produce nonlinear standing-wave branches that emerge from linear bound states. How can one also obtain and analyze branches of nonlinear standing waves that have no linear counterpart, such as nonlinear excited or bound states that do not bifurcate from the zero solution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (a finite or infinite collection of edges, each identified with an interval, glued at vertices). Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi(t,x) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi(t,x) + V(x)\,\psi(t,x) - |\psi(t,x)|^{p-1}\psi(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ equipped with self-adjoint (e.g. Kirchhoff) vertex conditions, $V:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a (possibly zero) external potential, and $p>1$. Standing waves are solutions of the form $\psi(t,x)=e^{-i\omega t}\varphi_\omega(x)$ with frequency $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$, where $\varphi_\omega$ solves the stationary equation
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \varphi_\omega + V\varphi_\omega - |\varphi_\omega|^{p-1}\varphi_\omega = \omega\,\varphi_\omega.$$

Assume the linear operator $H=-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}+V$ has discrete eigenvalues. Standard local bifurcation theory then produces, for every eigenvalue $\omega_0$ of $H$ with eigenfunction $\phi_0$, a smooth branch $\omega\mapsto\varphi_\omega$ of small nonlinear standing waves emanating from the trivial solution with $\varphi_{\omega_0}=0$ and tangent to $\phi_0$. Such branches are said to have a linear counterpart.

It is known, however, that on certain metric graphs (e.g. star graphs) there exist nonlinear bound and excited states $\varphi_\omega$ that do not belong to any branch bifurcating from the zero solution at a linear eigenvalue — i.e. nonlinear standing waves without linear counterpart.

Problem. Develop a general method to construct and analyze (existence, multiplicity, parameter dependence on $\omega$, qualitative shape, and orbital/spectral stability) branches of nonlinear standing waves $\varphi_\omega$ on a metric graph $\mathcal{G}$ that do not bifurcate from the zero solution at any eigenvalue of $H=-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}+V$. In particular, determine whether such "branches without linear counterpart" can always be obtained as bifurcations from (non-small) solitary waves of the potential-free problem when the external potential $V$ is switched on, and characterize the metric graphs and nonlinearity exponents $p$ for which such branches exist.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: existence and multiplicity results for non-bifurcating ("peaked") positive bound states on metric graphs have been obtained via Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction (e.g., solutions concentrating at vertices of odd degree ≥ 3 that are not minimizers). For specific graphs like the tadpole, families of continuous branches of solitons without linear analog have been constructed alongside bifurcating branches. However, a general theory covering arbitrary graphs, exponents, and the full conjecture that such branches arise as bifurcations from non-small solitary waves when an external potential is turned on does not appear to be established, so the problem as a whole is partially solved.

original_question: Let X be a Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. Must X have the Gelfand-Phillips property, meaning that every limited subset of X is relatively norm compact?
self_contained_problem:
A bounded subset $A$ of a Banach space $X$ is called limited if every weak* null sequence $(x_n^*)$ in the dual $X^*$ converges to $0$ uniformly on $A$, i.e. $\sup_{x \in A} |x_n^*(x)| \to 0$. The Banach space $X$ is said to have the Gelfand–Phillips property if every limited subset of $X$ is relatively norm compact.

original_question: What is the smallest cardinal κ for which there exists a family of κ Banach spaces, each having property (K), such that their ℓ^1-direct sum fails property (K), where property (K) means that every weak*-null sequence in the dual admits a convex block subsequence converging to 0 in the Mackey topology?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a (real) Banach space and X* its topological dual. Recall that the Mackey topology μ(X*, X) on X* is the topology of uniform convergence on weakly compact, absolutely convex subsets of X. Given a sequence (x*_n) in X*, a convex block subsequence of (x*_n) is a sequence (y*_k) of the form
   y*_k = Σ_{n ∈ I_k} a_n^{(k)} x*_n,
where I_1 < I_2 < ⋯ are nonempty finite subsets of ℕ (with max I_k < min I_{k+1}), a_n^{(k)} ≥ 0, and Σ_{n ∈ I_k} a_n^{(k)} = 1 for every k.

The Banach space X is said to have property (K) if every weak*-null sequence in X* admits a convex block subsequence that converges to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X).

For an index set Γ and a family {X_γ : γ ∈ Γ} of Banach spaces, the ℓ^1-direct sum is
   (⨁_{γ ∈ Γ} X_γ)_{ℓ^1} = { (x_γ)_{γ ∈ Γ} : x_γ ∈ X_γ, Σ_{γ ∈ Γ} ‖x_γ‖ < ∞ },
endowed with the norm ‖(x_γ)‖ = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ} ‖x_γ‖.

Determine the least cardinal κ such that there exists a family {X_γ : γ ∈ Γ} of Banach spaces with |Γ| = κ, where each X_γ has property (K), but the ℓ^1-direct sum (⨁_{γ ∈ Γ} X_γ)_{ℓ^1} fails property (K).
status_search_result: Known partial results show that the ℓ^1-sum of fewer than 𝔭 (the pseudo-intersection number) Banach spaces with property (K) again has property (K), while Pełczyński's example shows the ℓ^1-sum of continuum-many copies of L^1[0,1] fails property (K). Thus the threshold cardinal lies between 𝔭 and 𝔠, but its exact value does not appear to have been determined; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: What new nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics arise on graphs when one changes the vertex boundary conditions away from the standard cases studied here? In particular, can different vertex couplings produce new branches of standing waves, bifurcations of ground states, or symmetry-breaking phenomena analogous to those known for the line with a δ′ interaction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (a finite or locally finite collection of vertices joined by edges, each edge identified isometrically with an interval of $\mathbb{R}$ or a half-line). On $\mathcal{G}$ consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_V \psi - |\psi|^{2\mu}\psi, \qquad \mu>0, $$
where $\psi:\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{C}$ and $-\Delta_V$ denotes the self-adjoint Laplacian on $L^2(\mathcal{G})$ associated with a chosen family $V$ of linear vertex (boundary) conditions. Standing waves are solutions of the form $\psi(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\phi(x)$ with $\phi$ satisfying
$$ -\Delta_V \phi - |\phi|^{2\mu}\phi = -\omega\phi. $$
Ground states are minimizers of the energy
$$ E_V(\phi) = \tfrac{1}{2}\langle \phi, -\Delta_V\phi\rangle - \tfrac{1}{2\mu+2}\int_{\mathcal{G}}|\phi|^{2\mu+2}\,dx $$
restricted to the mass constraint $\|\phi\|_{L^2(\mathcal{G})}^2 = m$.

For the standard Kirchhoff (free) vertex conditions and $\delta$-type vertex conditions the existence, structure, and stability of ground states have been investigated. The question concerns alternative vertex couplings, in particular $\delta'$-type vertex conditions (defined, on each vertex of degree $d$, by continuity of the normal derivatives and a jump in the values weighted by a coupling constant, generalizing the $\delta'$ point interaction on the line).

Problem. For metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$ equipped with non-standard vertex couplings (e.g., $\delta'$-type or other self-adjoint couplings beyond Kirchhoff and $\delta$-type), determine:
(i) whether new families/branches of standing waves $e^{i\omega t}\phi(x)$ exist that are not present in the Kirchhoff or $\delta$ cases;
(ii) whether bifurcations of constrained ground states occur as the mass $m$, the nonlinearity exponent $\mu$, or the coupling strength varies;
(iii) whether spontaneous symmetry-breaking phenomena occur for ground states, in analogy with the symmetry-breaking pitchfork bifurcation established for the NLS on $\mathbb{R}$ with a $\delta'$ point interaction.

Provide existence/nonexistence theorems, identify bifurcation thresholds, and describe the resulting symmetry-broken ground state profiles.
category_tag: NLS on metric graphs with vertex conditions
status_search_result: Subsequent research has partially addressed this question. Works on NLS with $\delta'$-type vertex conditions on star graphs (Adami–Cacciapuoti–Finco–Noja and follow-ups) establish existence/nonexistence of ground states in mass-subcritical and supercritical regimes, and recent papers (2020–2025) treat non-Kirchhoff vertex conditions and demonstrate spontaneous symmetry-breaking bifurcations on star graphs (including transcritical bifurcations driven by Dirac-delta inhomogeneities). However, a complete classification for general metric graphs and general self-adjoint vertex couplings remains incomplete.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs asymptotically stable? More precisely, if a solution starts close in the energy norm to a standing wave e^{iωt}Φ_ω, does the solution converge at large time to another nearby standing wave plus a dispersive linear term and a decaying remainder? In order to prove such a result, can one develop the necessary analysis of the Hamiltonian linearization JL on graphs, including spectral information and dispersive estimates for exp(tJL), and can this be done for important cases such as subcritical power nonlinearities, where the methods described in the paper presently fail?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (for instance a star graph with a finite number of half-line edges joined at a single vertex), equipped with a self-adjoint realization $H$ of the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ determined by suitable vertex coupling conditions. Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\partial_t u(t,x) = H u(t,x) - f(|u(t,x)|^2) u(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R}, $$
where $f$ is a nonlinearity (for example a pure power $f(s)=s^{p/2}$ in the subcritical regime, or a nonlinearity concentrated at the vertex). For $\omega>0$ let $\Phi_\omega\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ be a bound state, i.e.\ a real-valued solution of
$$ H\Phi_\omega - f(\Phi_\omega^2)\Phi_\omega = -\omega \Phi_\omega, $$
generating the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega(x)$. Linearizing the equation around such a standing wave yields a Hamiltonian operator $JL$ acting on $\mathbb{C}$-valued functions on $\mathcal{G}$ that is neither self-adjoint nor skew-adjoint.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic stability statement: there exist $\delta>0$, a phase $\omega_\infty$ near $\omega$, an asymptotic profile $\Phi_{\omega_\infty}$, an asymptotic state $\Psi_\infty$, and a remainder $R_\infty$ with $\|R_\infty(t)\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})}	o 0$ as $t	o\infty$, such that whenever the initial datum $u(0)$ satisfies $\inf_{	heta\in\mathbb{R}}\|u(0)-e^{i	heta}\Phi_\omega\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})}<\delta$, the corresponding global solution decomposes as
$$ u(t) = e^{i\omega_\infty t}\Phi_{\omega_\infty} + U_t^\ast \Psi_\infty + R_\infty(t), $$
where $U_t = e^{-itH}$ is the free Schrödinger evolution on $\mathcal{G}$.

As steps toward this result, develop the spectral theory of the Hamiltonian linearization $JL$ on $\mathcal{G}$ (location of the spectrum, generalized kernel, embedded eigenvalues, resonances), and establish dispersive and Strichartz estimates for $e^{tJL}$ on $\mathcal{G}$ sufficient to control the nonlinear remainder. In particular, address the case of subcritical power nonlinearities, where standard methods based on weighted dispersive estimates do not apply.
status_search_result: Asymptotic stability of standing waves has been established in restricted settings on metric graphs, notably for the NLS on a star graph with a delta-type concentrated nonlinearity at the vertex (Adami–Noja–Sacchetti and subsequent works), where dispersive estimates are available in weighted spaces. For subcritical power nonlinearities on graphs, however, the spectral analysis of the Hamiltonian linearization $JL$ and the corresponding dispersive/Strichartz estimates needed to close the asymptotic stability argument have not been fully developed, and the general question remains open.

original_question: Let X be a separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete. Must X have property (K), meaning that every weak*-null sequence in X* has a convex block subsequence converging to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space with continuous dual X*. Recall that:

(a) X is weakly sequentially complete if every sequence in X that is Cauchy with respect to the weak topology σ(X, X*) converges weakly to some element of X.

(b) The Mackey topology μ(X*, X) on X* is the topology of uniform convergence on weakly compact, absolutely convex subsets of X.

(c) X is said to have property (K) if every weak*-null sequence (x_n*) in X* admits a convex block subsequence
   y_k* = ∑_{n ∈ I_k} a_n^{(k)} x_n*  (where I_1 < I_2 < … are finite intervals of integers and a_n^{(k)} ≥ 0, ∑_{n ∈ I_k} a_n^{(k)} = 1)
that converges to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X).

Question: Suppose X is a separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete. Must X have property (K)?
status_search_result: A targeted search did not produce evidence that this question has been resolved. Related literature on weakly sequentially complete Banach spaces and Kwapień's property (K) appears in subsequent work, but no source explicitly confirming a positive or negative answer for separable weakly sequentially complete Banach spaces was located.

original_question: For a Banach space X, is property D′ equivalent to property D? Here property D means that Ba(X, σ(X, Γ)) = Ba(X, w) for every total set Γ ⊆ X*, and property D′ means that every weak*-sequentially closed linear subspace of X* is weak*-closed.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space with topological dual $X^*$. For a subset $\Gamma \subseteq X^*$, denote by $\sigma(X,\Gamma)$ the weakest topology on $X$ making every functional in $\Gamma$ continuous, and write $w$ for the weak topology $\sigma(X,X^*)$. A subset $\Gamma \subseteq X^*$ is called total if $x^*(x) = 0$ for all $x^* \in \Gamma$ implies $x = 0$. For a topology $\tau$ on $X$, let $\mathrm{Ba}(X,\tau)$ denote the Baire $\sigma$-algebra of $(X,\tau)$, that is, the smallest $\sigma$-algebra of subsets of $X$ that makes every $\tau$-continuous real-valued function on $X$ measurable.

Say that $X$ has:
- Property (D) if for every total subset $\Gamma \subseteq X^*$ one has $\mathrm{Ba}(X, \sigma(X,\Gamma)) = \mathrm{Ba}(X, w)$;
- Property (D$'$) if every weak$^*$-sequentially closed linear subspace of $X^*$ is weak$^*$-closed.

Question: Are properties (D) and (D$'$) equivalent for every Banach space $X$?
status_search_result: The question, posed by Plichko, concerning the equivalence of properties (D) and (D$'$) for Banach spaces, is recorded in surveys of weak$^*$-sequential closures in Banach space theory and remains, to the best of available evidence, an open problem. Web searches turn up survey and follow-up works on properties (D$'$) and (E$'$) and their applications to Pettis integrability via total subspaces, but no result establishing or disproving the equivalence of (D) and (D$'$).

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Do multisoliton states exist for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on star graphs, and what happens when several solitons collide simultaneously at a vertex? In particular, can one construct or analyze solutions representing more than one incoming or outgoing soliton interacting through the junction?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on a star graph G consisting of N≥2 half-lines (edges) e_1,…,e_N joined at a single vertex v. On each edge e_j, parametrized by x∈[0,∞) with x=0 at v, the wave function ψ_j(t,x) satisfies
   i ∂_t ψ_j = −∂_{xx} ψ_j − |ψ_j|^2 ψ_j,    j=1,…,N,
with vertex coupling at x=0 given by Kirchhoff (or, more generally, δ-type) conditions:
   ψ_1(t,0) = … = ψ_N(t,0),    Σ_{j=1}^N ∂_x ψ_j(t,0) = α ψ_1(t,0),
for some fixed α∈ℝ (α=0 corresponds to the free Kirchhoff vertex).

A "soliton" on a single edge is, away from the vertex, asymptotically of the form of a 1-d NLS soliton
   φ_{c,v_0}(t,x) = sech(√c (x − v_0 t − x_0)) e^{i(v_0 x/2 + (c − v_0^2/4) t + θ_0)},
with speed v_0, amplitude parameter c>0, and phase/translation parameters x_0,θ_0.

Questions:
(a) Do there exist (orbitally stable or unstable) multisoliton solutions of this NLS problem on the star graph, that is, solutions which, as t→±∞, behave on each edge as a finite linear superposition of soliton profiles φ_{c_{j,k},v_{j,k}} traveling on edge e_j with distinct asymptotic parameters?
(b) Construct, or rigorously analyze, solutions representing several solitons that arrive simultaneously at the vertex v (multiple incoming solitons on possibly different edges colliding at the same time at x=0), and describe the outgoing radiation: how many outgoing solitons emerge on each edge, with what amplitudes, speeds, phases, and how much energy is radiated as dispersive waves?
status_search_result: A literature search returns related results on stationary states, orbital (in)stability of standing waves with δ-interaction on star graphs, and scattering of a single fast soliton through a Y-junction, as well as multisoliton constructions for integrable matrix NLS on graphs with special vertex conditions. However, no rigorous result was found constructing or analyzing genuine multisoliton solutions of the scalar cubic NLS on a star graph with Kirchhoff/δ vertex conditions, nor a description of simultaneous multi-soliton collisions at the vertex. The problem appears to remain open in the general scalar non-integrable setting.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: How do solitons scatter on graphs with nontrivial topology beyond the simple star-graph setting? In particular, for graphs such as trees or other networks with internal structure, can one rigorously describe propagation and scattering of solitons and determine how the topology and available dispersive estimates affect the dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a connected metric graph with nontrivial topology beyond a star graph — for instance, a finite or infinite tree with bounded vertex degrees, or a network containing internal edges and/or loops. Each edge e of G is identified with an interval (of finite or infinite length), and a function u on G is a collection {u_e}_{e∈E(G)} of functions on the edges. On each edge consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
   i ∂_t u_e = −∂_{xx} u_e − |u_e|^2 u_e,
coupled at every vertex v by Kirchhoff (free) boundary conditions: continuity of u across v, and vanishing of the signed sum of outgoing derivatives ∑_{e∋v} ∂_x u_e(v) = 0. Let H = −Δ_G denote the corresponding self-adjoint Kirchhoff Laplacian on L^2(G).

A soliton on a single edge (viewed as a line) is the standard NLS profile φ_{c,v}(x,t) = √(2c) sech(√c (x−vt)) e^{i(vx/2 − (v^2/4 − c)t)} with speed v ∈ ℝ and amplitude parameter c > 0.

(a) Establish dispersive and Strichartz-type estimates for the linear propagator e^{−itH} on G that are sufficient to develop a local and global well-posedness theory for the cubic NLS on G in an appropriate energy space.

(b) Using such estimates, prove a rigorous scattering theorem for incoming solitons: given a high-velocity soliton ψ_0 ≈ φ_{c,v}(·,0) initially supported far from the vertex set on a chosen incoming edge, describe the asymptotic behavior of the solution u(t) as t → +∞, in particular decompose u(t) along each outgoing edge into a sum of transmitted/reflected soliton-like profiles plus a dispersive remainder, and compute the corresponding transmission and reflection coefficients in terms of the topology (vertex degrees, edge lengths, internal cycles) of G.

(c) Determine how the topology of G — e.g. branching of trees, presence of bounded internal edges, or loops — quantitatively affects the dispersive decay rates, the validity of Strichartz inequalities, and the resulting soliton dynamics.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that while dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger propagator have been established on star graphs and have been extended in some works to certain tree, loop, and combined graphs, a rigorous theory of soliton scattering on metric graphs of nontrivial topology (transmission/reflection laws, asymptotic completeness with soliton resolution) remains an active and apparently open research problem; no source was found that resolves it in full generality.

original_question: Let K be a compact space such that the Baire sigma-algebras Ba(C(K), T_p) and Ba(C(K), w) coincide, where T_p is the topology of pointwise convergence on K. Must every probability measure in P(K) belong to the weak*-sequential closure Seq(co(Δ_K)) of the convex hull of the point-evaluation measures Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $C(K)$ denote the space of continuous real-valued functions on $K$. Consider two locally convex topologies on $C(K)$: the topology $T_p$ of pointwise convergence on $K$, and the weak topology $w$ induced by the dual $C(K)^*$. For a topological vector space $(E,\tau)$, let $\mathrm{Ba}(E,\tau)$ denote the Baire $\sigma$-algebra, i.e., the smallest $\sigma$-algebra on $E$ making every $\tau$-continuous real-valued function measurable.

Let $P(K)$ denote the set of Radon probability measures on $K$, regarded as a subset of $C(K)^*$ equipped with the weak* topology, and let $\Delta_K = \{\delta_t : t \in K\} \subset P(K)$ be the set of Dirac measures. For a subset $A \subseteq C(K)^*$, let $\mathrm{Seq}(A)$ denote the smallest set containing $A$ that is closed under taking weak*-limits of weak*-convergent sequences (the sequential closure in the weak* topology).

Assume that $\mathrm{Ba}(C(K),T_p) = \mathrm{Ba}(C(K),w)$. Does it follow that
$$\mathrm{Seq}(\mathrm{conv}(\Delta_K)) = P(K)\,?$$

The status could not be verified from available sources.

context_brief: Weak Baire measurability of the supremum norm
original_question: Let K be compact. Is the weak Baire measurability of the supremum norm on C(K), viewed as measurability with respect to Ba(C(K), w), equivalent to weak*-separability of the dual unit ball B_{C(K)^*} or of the whole dual space C(K)^*?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on $K$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. Let $w$ denote the weak topology on $C(K)$, and let $\mathrm{Ba}(C(K),w)$ denote the Baire $\sigma$-algebra of $(C(K),w)$, i.e., the smallest $\sigma$-algebra on $C(K)$ that makes every weakly continuous real-valued function on $C(K)$ measurable (equivalently, the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the weakly continuous real-valued functions, or by all continuous linear functionals on $C(K)$). Let $C(K)^*$ be the topological dual of $C(K)$ equipped with the weak* topology, and let $B_{C(K)^*}$ denote its closed unit ball.

Determine whether the following equivalence holds for every compact Hausdorff space $K$: the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty : C(K) \to \mathbb{R}$ is measurable with respect to $\mathrm{Ba}(C(K),w)$ if and only if $B_{C(K)^*}$ is weak*-separable. Determine likewise whether such measurability is equivalent to weak*-separability of the whole dual space $C(K)^*$.
status_search_result: The known general implications are: weak*-separability of $B_{X^*}$ implies weak Baire measurability of the norm, which in turn implies weak*-separability of $X^*$; the reverse implications fail in general Banach spaces. For the specific case $X = C(K)$, whether these properties are equivalent is stated as an open problem, and recent literature on weak Baire measurability of balls in Banach spaces and on weak*-separability of $C(K)^*$ does not appear to resolve it.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Can one extend the time interval over which the post-collision dynamics of a fast soliton on a graph is accurately approximated by outgoing solitary waves? More specifically, beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity timescale obtained in the paper, are there longer timescales of validity, perhaps depending on the initial data or on the vertex interaction, for which the outgoing-wave approximation remains accurate?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on a star graph $\mathcal{G}$ consisting of $N$ half-lines joined at a single vertex $v$:
$$ i\partial_t \psi_j(t,x) = -\partial_x^2 \psi_j(t,x) - |\psi_j(t,x)|^2 \psi_j(t,x), \qquad x>0,\ j=1,\dots,N, $$
where $\psi=(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_N)$ and the components are coupled at $v$ through a self-adjoint vertex condition (e.g., Kirchhoff, $\delta$ of strength $\alpha$, or $\delta'$). The free 1D soliton of velocity $v$, position $a$, phase $\gamma$ and amplitude $1$ is
$$ \phi_v(t,x;a,\gamma) = \operatorname{sech}(x-a-vt)\, e^{i(\tfrac{v}{2}(x-a) + (1-\tfrac{v^2}{4})t + \gamma)}. $$
Take an initial datum supported on the first edge that, at $t=0$, equals a fast soliton $\phi_v(0,x;a_0,\gamma_0)$ with $v$ large and $a_0<0$ far from the vertex, so that the soliton hits $v$ at a time $T_{\mathrm{coll}}\sim |a_0|/v$. It is known that there exist outgoing solitary waves $\{\phi^{\mathrm{out}}_j\}_{j=1}^N$ on the edges, with amplitudes/phases determined by the linear scattering coefficients of the vertex condition, such that for some constants $C,\delta>0$,
$$ \sup_{0\le t \le \delta\,\log v / v}\, \Big\| \psi(t) - \sum_{j} \phi^{\mathrm{out}}_j(t)\,\mathbf{1}_{\text{edge }j} \Big\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})} \le C\, v^{-1/2}. $$

Question: Can the time interval of validity of this outgoing-solitary-wave approximation be extended beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity scale $O(v^{-1}\log v)$? Specifically, do there exist longer timescales $T(v)$ (possibly depending on the initial soliton parameters $(v,a_0,\gamma_0)$ and on the choice of self-adjoint vertex coupling) such that the post-collision dynamics $\psi(t)$ remains close in $H^1(\mathcal{G})$ to a superposition of outgoing solitary waves uniformly for $T_{\mathrm{coll}}\le t \le T(v)$, with an error tending to $0$ as $v\to\infty$?
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Available literature confirms the logarithmic-in-velocity timescale of validity for the outgoing solitary-wave approximation after a fast soliton hits the vertex of a star graph (extending Holmer–Marzuola–Zworski to graphs). No subsequent work was found that establishes a longer timescale of validity for this approximation in the graph setting; analogous extensions exist only in heuristic/special-case discussions for two-soliton scattering on the line. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: For nonlinear Schrödinger equations on graphs with nonlinearities that are close to, but not exactly, the integrable cubic case, do outgoing waves produced by a fast soliton-vertex interaction remain close to solitons on timescales comparable to those proved for cubic NLS? In other words, how stable is the fast-soliton scattering picture under non-integrable perturbations of the cubic nonlinearity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation posed on a metric graph $\mathcal{G}$ (a connected graph whose edges are identified with intervals of $\mathbb{R}$, joined at vertices on which Kirchhoff or other self-adjoint coupling conditions are imposed):
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi + f(|\psi|^2)\psi, \qquad \psi(t,\cdot)\in L^2(\mathcal{G}), $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian determined by the vertex conditions. For the cubic case $f(s)=-s$ on the line, the equation is integrable, and on graphs it is known that an incoming soliton of speed $v$ approaching a vertex produces, on each outgoing edge, a wave that is close in $H^1$ to a (rescaled) soliton on a time-scale of order $\log v / v$ as $v\to\infty$ (with explicit error bounds depending on $v$).

Let $f$ be a smooth, real-valued nonlinearity that is a small perturbation of the cubic case in a suitable norm (e.g. $f(s) = -s + \varepsilon g(s)$ with $g$ smooth, $\varepsilon$ small, and appropriate decay/growth conditions ensuring local well-posedness of the equation in $H^1(\mathcal{G})$ and existence of ground-state solitons close to the cubic ones). 

Question: For an incoming high-speed solitary wave (a solitary wave of the perturbed NLS with speed $v$ large) interacting with a vertex of $\mathcal{G}$, do the outgoing waves on each edge remain $H^1$-close to (rescaled) solitary waves of the perturbed equation, with closeness valid on a time-scale comparable to the cubic case (in particular, of order $\log v / v$ as $v \to \infty$, uniformly for $\varepsilon$ small enough)? Equivalently, prove or disprove the stability of the fast-soliton scattering picture at vertices under non-integrable perturbations of the cubic nonlinearity.
category_tag: nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any work that establishes (or refutes) fast-soliton scattering at graph vertices for non-integrable perturbations of the cubic NLS on metric graphs on a time-scale comparable to that obtained via integrability in the pure cubic case. The available literature on NLS on graphs and on soliton perturbation theory does not appear to contain a definitive resolution, so the status is taken as unknown / likely open.

original_question: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) differ, so Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Must there exist a norm-discrete subset of C(K) that is not weak-Borel, that is, does not belong to Bo(C(K), w)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of real-valued continuous functions on $K$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty = \sup_{x\in K}|f(x)|$. Consider on $C(K)$ two topologies: the norm topology induced by $\|\cdot\|_\infty$, and the weak topology $w$ induced by the dual space $C(K)^*$. Let $\mathrm{Bo}(C(K))$ denote the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel subsets of $C(K)$ generated by the norm topology, and $\mathrm{Bo}(C(K), w)$ the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel subsets generated by the weak topology. A subset $D \subseteq C(K)$ is called norm-discrete if there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $\|f - g\|_\infty \geq \varepsilon$ for all distinct $f, g \in D$.

Assume that $K$ is such that $\mathrm{Bo}(C(K), w) \neq \mathrm{Bo}(C(K))$. Must there exist a norm-discrete subset of $C(K)$ which does not belong to $\mathrm{Bo}(C(K), w)$?
status_search_result: A 2019 work on weak-star and norm Borel sets in the dual of C(K) addresses related questions but does not appear to resolve the specific Burke–Pol problem on whether norm-discrete subsets witness the discrepancy between weak-Borel and norm-Borel σ-algebras in C(K). No source found indicates the problem has been settled.

original_question: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) coincide, so Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)). Does it follow that the pointwise and norm Borel sigma-algebras also coincide, meaning Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on $K$ equipped with the supremum norm. Consider three natural topologies on $C(K)$: the norm topology, the weak topology $w$ (induced by the dual $C(K)^*$), and the pointwise convergence topology $\tau_p$ (induced by viewing $C(K) \subset \mathbb{R}^K$). For a topological space $(X,\tau)$, let $\mathrm{Bo}(X,\tau)$ denote the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel subsets of $X$ generated by $\tau$; write $\mathrm{Bo}(C(K))$ for the norm Borel $\sigma$-algebra.

Suppose that $K$ is a compact Hausdorff space such that the weak and norm Borel $\sigma$-algebras on $C(K)$ coincide, i.e.
$$\mathrm{Bo}(C(K), w) = \mathrm{Bo}(C(K)).$$
Does it then follow that the pointwise and norm Borel $\sigma$-algebras on $C(K)$ also coincide, i.e.
$$\mathrm{Bo}(C(K), \tau_p) = \mathrm{Bo}(C(K))?$$
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem of Marciszewski and Pol concerning Borel structures on function spaces C(K). Related work by Marciszewski–Pol (RACSAM 2010) constructs compact spaces where weak and pointwise Borel structures differ, but no resolution of this specific implication was found in available sources. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Can one develop a rigorous mathematical theory for the capture and generation of solitons in nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics on graphs? More specifically, in dynamical regimes that lie between the standing-wave regime and the fast-soliton-scattering regime, can one explain when junction interactions or graph geometry trap a soliton, create a new one, or transfer mass into a localized coherent structure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}=(V,E)$ be a metric graph: a connected combinatorial graph in which each edge $e\in E$ is identified with a real interval (either $[0,\ell_e]$ for finite edges or a half-line $[0,\infty)$ for unbounded edges), with edges glued at their endpoints according to the vertex structure of $\mathcal{G}$. A function $u:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{C}$ is a tuple $(u_e)_{e\in E}$ of functions on the corresponding intervals. On $\mathcal{G}$ consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
$$ i\,\partial_t u_e(t,x) = -\partial_{xx} u_e(t,x) - |u_e(t,x)|^{p-1} u_e(t,x), \qquad e\in E,$$
with $p>1$, equipped at every vertex $v\in V$ with Kirchhoff (free) boundary conditions: continuity of $u$ across $v$ and vanishing of the sum of outgoing derivatives at $v$. The mass $M(u)=\int_{\mathcal{G}} |u|^2\,dx$ and energy
$$E(u)=\tfrac{1}{2}\int_{\mathcal{G}} |\partial_x u|^2\,dx-\tfrac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathcal{G}}|u|^{p+1}\,dx$$
are conserved. By a soliton on a half-line $[0,\infty)\subset\mathcal{G}$ we mean the standard NLS soliton profile
$$ \phi_{c,v}(t,x)=A\,\operatorname{sech}\!\big(\kappa(x-vt-x_0)\big)\,e^{i(\frac{v}{2}x-\omega t)} $$
of the line, suitably translated and modulated, where the parameters $A,\kappa,\omega$ are determined by $p$ and the soliton speed $v$. Two extreme dynamical regimes are well understood: the standing-wave regime, in which $u(t,\cdot)=e^{-i\omega t}\Phi(\cdot)$ for a bound state $\Phi$ on $\mathcal{G}$, and the fast-soliton-scattering regime, in which an incoming soliton with $|v|\gg 1$ on a half-edge approaches a vertex and is scattered into outgoing solitons on the other half-edges with effective transmission/reflection coefficients given, to leading order in $1/|v|$, by the linear scattering matrix at the vertex.

The problem is to develop a rigorous mathematical theory describing intermediate regimes (moderate soliton speeds, finite size of localized structures relative to graph features) for the NLS equation on metric graphs. Specifically, formulate and prove theorems giving necessary and/or sufficient conditions, in terms of the graph geometry (edge lengths, topology, vertex structure), the nonlinearity exponent $p$, and the initial data, under which the dynamics:
(a) traps an incoming soliton at a vertex or in a compact subgraph (capture), producing a long-time localized coherent structure;
(b) generates one or more new solitons emerging from a junction after the interaction (generation);
(c) transfers a quantitatively controlled portion of the mass $M(u)$ from a propagating soliton into a localized bound-state-like coherent structure supported near a vertex or compact subgraph.

Provide a rigorous framework (e.g., modulation analysis, effective dynamics for soliton parameters, asymptotic stability statements, or scattering-type results) that quantifies these phenomena in the intermediate regime between the standing-wave and fast-scattering limits.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any rigorous theory addressing soliton capture and generation for NLS on metric graphs in regimes intermediate between standing waves and fast scattering. Existing rigorous results concern bound states/standing waves (Adami–Cacciapuoti–Finco–Noja and others) and fast-soliton scattering at vertices, but the intermediate dynamical regime appears to remain open with no published resolution found.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Consider the single-input time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic smooth pair of vector fields. Must every time-optimal trajectory for this generic 3-dimensional problem be piecewise smooth, meaning that the trajectory has only finitely many switching points and is smooth between them?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth $3$-dimensional manifold and consider the single-input control-affine system
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $(f,g)$ is a generic pair of smooth vector fields on $M$ (genericity in the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology on the space of pairs of smooth vector fields). A measurable control $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$ together with the corresponding absolutely continuous trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ is called time-optimal if no other admissible control steers $q(0)$ to $q(T)$ in time strictly less than $T$.

Question: Is it true that, for a generic pair $(f,g)$, every time-optimal trajectory of the system is piecewise smooth, meaning that it has only finitely many switching times and is smooth on each interval between consecutive switching times?
status_search_result: The question of piecewise smoothness (finiteness of switchings) for time-optimal trajectories of a generic single-input control-affine system on a 3-manifold is explicitly stated as open. Related work by Agrachev–Sigalotti and Agrachev–Biolo establishes regularity results under additional genericity conditions and treats 2D-control variants in dimension 3, but no general resolution of the n=3 single-input generic case has been located in the search results.

original_question: Does there exist a probability measure defined on the weak Borel sigma-algebra Bo(ℓ_∞, w) that does not admit any extension to a probability measure on the norm Borel sigma-algebra Bo(ℓ_∞)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell_\infty$ denote the Banach space of bounded real sequences $x=(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with the supremum norm $\|x\|_\infty=\sup_n|x_n|$. Let $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty)$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by the norm topology on $\ell_\infty$, and let $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty,w)$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by the weak topology $\sigma(\ell_\infty,\ell_\infty^*)$ on $\ell_\infty$. Note that $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty,w)\subseteq \mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty)$. 

Question: Does there exist a (countably additive) probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty,w)$ such that there is no probability measure $\widetilde{\mu}$ on $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty)$ whose restriction to $\mathrm{Bo}(\ell_\infty,w)$ equals $\mu$?
status_search_result: The question is a problem of Fremlin concerning whether every probability measure on the weak Borel σ-algebra of ℓ_∞ extends to the norm Borel σ-algebra. It is listed in Fremlin's regularly updated problem list and discussed in surveys on measures on Banach spaces; no published solution appears in the literature, so the problem is currently regarded as open.
