original_question: Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a multifunction from a complete probability space into the nonempty subsets of a Banach space X. If F has convex closed values and is scalarly measurable, meaning F^{-}(H) is measurable for every open half-space H ⊆ X, must F admit a selector f: Ω → X that is itself scalarly measurable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a (real) Banach space. Denote by $\mathcal{P}_0(X)$ the family of nonempty subsets of $X$. A multifunction $F:\Omega \to \mathcal{P}_0(X)$ is called scalarly measurable if for every open half-space $H \subseteq X$ (equivalently, for every $x^* \in X^*$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, taking $H = \{x \in X : x^*(x) < \alpha\}$), the lower inverse image
$$F^{-}(H) = \{\omega \in \Omega : F(\omega) \cap H \ne \emptyset\}$$
belongs to $\Sigma$. Equivalently, this means that for each $x^* \in X^*$ the support function $\omega \mapsto \sup_{x \in F(\omega)} x^*(x)$ is $\Sigma$-measurable as an extended real-valued function. A function $f:\Omega \to X$ is called a selector of $F$ if $f(\omega) \in F(\omega)$ for every $\omega \in \Omega$, and it is called scalarly measurable if $\omega \mapsto x^*(f(\omega))$ is $\Sigma$-measurable for every $x^* \in X^*$.

Question: Suppose $F:\Omega \to \mathcal{P}_0(X)$ is a scalarly measurable multifunction whose values $F(\omega)$ are convex and closed subsets of $X$. Must $F$ admit a scalarly measurable selector $f:\Omega \to X$?
category_tag: Measurable selectors of multifunctions in Banach spaces
status_search_result: A celebrated result of Cascales–Kadets–Rodríguez (2009) establishes that every scalarly measurable multifunction with weakly compact (not necessarily convex) values in an arbitrary Banach space admits a scalarly measurable selector. The general case of closed convex (possibly unbounded, not weakly compact) values appears to remain open in the literature; recent works (e.g., Di Piazza–Sambucini 2025 on selections of integrable multifunctions in arbitrary Banach spaces, and surveys on Pettis integration of multifunctions) discuss closely related selection problems but do not provide a definitive resolution of this specific question. No source found explicitly claims a solution.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For the same generic single-input time-optimal control problem qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional manifold, let sw(q) denote the smallest local uniform bound on the number of switching points of sufficiently short time-optimal trajectories near q, with sw(q) = ∞ if arbitrarily close optimal trajectories can have infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth control-affine system on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ of the form
$$\dot q = f(q) + u\, g(q), \qquad |u(t)|\le 1,$$
where $f$ and $g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$, and assume the pair $(f,g)$ is generic (in the sense of the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology) and that the time-optimal control problem is well posed locally. For a point $q\in M$, define $\mathrm{sw}(q)$ to be the smallest natural number $N$ with the following property: there exist a neighborhood $U$ of $q$ and a time $T>0$ such that every time-optimal trajectory of the system that is contained in $U$ and has duration at most $T$ has at most $N$ switching points of the corresponding optimal control (where a switching point is a time at which the control $u(\cdot)$ is not locally constant or changes between the values $\pm 1$ and a singular arc). If no such finite $N$ exists, set $\mathrm{sw}(q)=\infty$.

Question: Is $\mathrm{sw}(q)<\infty$ for every $q\in M$?
status_search_result: Subsequent literature on regularity of time-optimal trajectories for generic control-affine systems in dimension three (e.g., works on iterated Fuller singularities and on the 3D case with 2D control) refines the local structure of optimal controls but does not appear to establish a uniform local bound on the number of switchings at every point. No source found that proves sw(q) is finite for all q on a 3-manifold for the generic single-input problem; the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a generic smooth pair of vector fields f and g in the single-input time-optimal system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1, on a 3-dimensional manifold, must each individual time-optimal trajectory have only finitely many switching points, even if no uniform bound over nearby trajectories is assumed?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth control-affine single-input time-optimal control system on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ of the form
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$ and admissible controls are measurable functions $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. A trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ corresponding to such a control is called time-optimal if it minimizes the transfer time $T$ between its endpoints among all admissible trajectories.

A switching point of a trajectory associated to a control $u$ is a time $t\in(0,T)$ such that $u$ is not constant on any neighborhood of $t$.

Endow the space of pairs $(f,g)$ of smooth vector fields on $M$ with the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology. Prove or disprove: there exists a residual (generic) subset of pairs $(f,g)$ such that for every pair in this subset, every individual time-optimal trajectory of the corresponding system has only finitely many switching points (no uniform bound over nearby trajectories is required).
status_search_result: Recent work on switching structure for generic single-input time-optimal systems in dimension 3 (notably results showing local bounds on the number of switchings near generic points, and results showing that optimal controls are smooth outside a countable set whose accumulation structure is bounded by iterated Fuller-type singularities) does not establish the finiteness of switchings along an individual time-optimal trajectory; infinitely many (Fuller-like) switchings remain compatible with the known generic regularity. No source located that resolves the question for individual trajectories, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Suppose a Banach space X has density ω_1. Does the family wk(X) of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X have property (SC), meaning that there exists a set selector ψ on wk(X) such that ψ ∘ F is scalarly measurable for every scalarly measurable multifunction F with values in wk(X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space with dual X*. A multifunction F : Ω → 2^X defined on a measurable space (Ω, Σ) is called scalarly measurable if for every x* ∈ X* the real-valued function ω ↦ sup{x*(x) : x ∈ F(ω)} is Σ-measurable. Let wk(X) denote the family of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X. A set selector on wk(X) is a map ψ : wk(X) → X such that ψ(C) ∈ C for every C ∈ wk(X). The family wk(X) is said to have property (SC) if there exists a set selector ψ on wk(X) such that, for every scalarly measurable multifunction F : Ω → wk(X) defined on any measurable space (Ω, Σ), the composition ψ ∘ F : Ω → X is scalarly measurable (i.e. x* ∘ ψ ∘ F is Σ-measurable for every x* ∈ X*).

Question: Assume that the density character of X equals ω₁. Does wk(X) necessarily have property (SC)?
status_search_result: The problem is attributed to Fremlin and is listed as an open problem in surveys on measurability and selections of multifunctions in Banach spaces. Partial positive answers are known (e.g., when X* is w*-separable, or when (X*, w*) is angelic with density character ω₁), but the general case for Banach spaces of density ω₁ remains open.

context_brief: Property (SC) for convex weakly compact sets
original_question: Does the family cwk(X) of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of a Banach space X have property (SC), meaning that one can choose a selector on cwk(X) whose composition with every scalarly measurable multifunction into cwk(X) is scalarly measurable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ denote the family of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of $X$. A multifunction $F:\Omega\to\mathrm{cwk}(X)$, defined on a complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$, is called scalarly measurable if for every $x^*\in X^*$ the real-valued support function $\omega\mapsto \delta^*(x^*,F(\omega)):=\sup\{x^*(x):x\in F(\omega)\}$ is $\Sigma$-measurable. A function $f:\Omega\to X$ is called scalarly measurable if $x^*\circ f$ is $\Sigma$-measurable for every $x^*\in X^*$, and $f$ is a selector of $F$ if $f(\omega)\in F(\omega)$ for all $\omega\in\Omega$.

We say that $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ has property (SC) if there exists a map $s:\mathrm{cwk}(X)\to X$ with $s(C)\in C$ for every $C\in\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ such that, for every complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ and every scalarly measurable multifunction $F:\Omega\to\mathrm{cwk}(X)$, the composition $s\circ F:\Omega\to X$ is scalarly measurable.

Question: Does $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ have property (SC) for every Banach space $X$?

status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on measurable selections of multifunctions with values in cwk(X) (e.g., work by Cascales, Kadets, and Rodríguez and the 2025 paper on selections of integrable multifunctions in arbitrary Banach spaces) continue to reference Fremlin's problem on property (SC) for cwk(X) without reporting a resolution. While related selection results (e.g., scalarly measurable selectors exist for scalarly measurable cwk(X)-valued multifunctions) are known, the existence of a single universal selector witnessing property (SC) appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields in the time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, is there always a time-optimal trajectory joining the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a real analytic manifold and let $f, g$ be real analytic vector fields on $M$. Consider the single-input control-affine time-optimal control system
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
with measurable controls $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. A time $t\in(0,T)$ is called a switching point of a bang-bang control $u$ if $u$ is not locally constant in any neighborhood of $t$. Suppose $q_0, q_1\in M$ are two points that are connected by some time-optimal trajectory of the system. Must there exist a time-optimal trajectory joining $q_0$ to $q_1$ whose set of switching points is at most countable?

No general resolution for arbitrary real-analytic f, g has been found.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: In the same real analytic time-optimal control setting, can one always avoid time-optimal trajectories whose switching points occupy a set of positive measure? Equivalently, whenever two points can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory, must there exist such a trajectory whose switching set has measure zero?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a real analytic time-optimal control problem of the form
  ẋ(t) = f(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ M,  u(t) ∈ U,
where M is a real analytic manifold, U ⊂ ℝ^m is a control set (e.g. a compact polytope), and f is real analytic in x and (in standard formulations) affine in u. A time-optimal trajectory is an absolutely continuous curve x(·) : [0, T] → M, generated by a measurable control u(·) : [0, T] → U, that joins two given points x(0) = p and x(T) = q in minimum time among all admissible trajectories.

For an admissible control u(·), define its switching set to be the set of times t ∈ [0, T] at which u is not locally constant (equivalently, every neighborhood of t contains points where u takes at least two distinct values). Call this the switching set of the corresponding trajectory.

Question: Is it true that whenever two points p, q ∈ M can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory, there exists a time-optimal trajectory from p to q whose switching set has Lebesgue measure zero? Equivalently, can time-optimal trajectories whose switching sets have positive Lebesgue measure always be avoided?
status_search_result: Web search returned classical regularity-of-time-optimal-trajectories results for real analytic systems (Sussmann and others), establishing bang-bang structure with finitely many switchings in low dimensions and outside an exceptional analytic stratum, but no source was found that directly resolves the general question of whether time-optimal trajectories with switching sets of positive Lebesgue measure can always be avoided. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces with the Lebesgue property, meaning those spaces X for which every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is continuous almost everywhere.
self_contained_problem:
A function $f:[0,1]\to X$ with values in a Banach space $X$ is called Riemann integrable if there exists $v\in X$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ with the property that for every tagged partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=1$ of $[0,1]$ with $\max_i(t_i-t_{i-1})<\delta$ and every choice of tags $s_i\in[t_{i-1},t_i]$, one has $\bigl\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}(t_i-t_{i-1})f(s_i)-v\bigr\|<\varepsilon$. A Banach space $X$ is said to have the Lebesgue property (LP) if every Riemann integrable function $f:[0,1]\to X$ is continuous at almost every point of $[0,1]$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of those Banach spaces $X$ that have the Lebesgue property.
status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2024) provides a characterization of the Lebesgue property in terms of a new sequential asymptotic structure lying strictly between spreading models and asymptotic models, and shows that a subspace $X\subset L_1[0,1]$ has LP iff every spreading model of $X$ is equivalent to the unit vector basis of $\ell_1$. While substantial progress and partial characterizations exist, a fully general intrinsic characterization for arbitrary Banach spaces does not appear to be settled.

context_brief: Weak Lebesgue property for Hilbert spaces
original_question: For which cardinals κ does the Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property, meaning that every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → ℓ_2(κ) is weakly continuous almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let κ be an infinite cardinal and let ℓ₂(κ) denote the Hilbert space of all functions x : κ → ℝ such that {γ ∈ κ : x(γ) ≠ 0} is countable and ∑_{γ∈κ} |x(γ)|² < ∞, equipped with the inner product ⟨x, y⟩ = ∑_{γ∈κ} x(γ)y(γ).

A function f : [0, 1] → X with values in a Banach space X is said to be Riemann integrable if there exists v ∈ X such that for every ε > 0 there is a partition 0 = t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < tₙ = 1 of [0, 1] with the property that ‖∑_{i=1}^{n} f(s_i)(t_i − t_{i−1}) − v‖ < ε for every choice of points s_i ∈ [t_{i−1}, t_i]. The function f is called weakly continuous at a point t ∈ [0, 1] if for every continuous linear functional x* ∈ X*, the scalar function x* ∘ f is continuous at t.

A Banach space X is said to have the weak Lebesgue property (WLP) if every Riemann integrable function f : [0, 1] → X is weakly continuous at almost every point of [0, 1] with respect to the Lebesgue measure.

Determine the cardinals κ for which the Hilbert space ℓ₂(κ) has the weak Lebesgue property.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems in Banach spaces and measure theory. Available results show that separable Banach spaces have the WLP and that L₁(μ) fails WLP whenever it contains a closed subspace isomorphic to ℓ₂(c); under the Continuum Hypothesis, L₁(μ) has WLP iff it is separable. No complete characterization of cardinals κ for which ℓ₂(κ) has WLP appears in the literature retrieved, suggesting the problem remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Let Δ ⊂ TM be a bracket-generating distribution defining a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M, and let γ0, γ1 : [0,1] → M be smooth admissible paths with the same starting point q0 and linearly independent initial velocities at q0. Must there always exist an admissible path from γ0(1) to γ1(1) whose length is strictly less than the length of the broken path obtained by concatenating γ0 and γ1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure: a smooth bracket-generating distribution $\Delta \subset TM$ together with a smoothly varying inner product on the fibers of $\Delta$. A Lipschitz curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ is called admissible (horizontal) if $\dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ for almost every $t$, and its length is defined by $\ell(\gamma)=\int_0^1\|\dot\gamma(t)\|\,dt$ using the given inner product on $\Delta$.

Suppose $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to M$ are two smooth admissible paths with the same starting point $\gamma_0(0)=\gamma_1(0)=q_0$ and with linearly independent initial velocities $\dot\gamma_0(0),\dot\gamma_1(0)\in\Delta_{q_0}$. Consider the broken concatenation $\gamma_0\ast\gamma_1^{-1}$ (or equivalently the broken path going from $\gamma_0(1)$ back to $q_0$ along $\gamma_0$ and then forward to $\gamma_1(1)$ along $\gamma_1$), whose length equals $\ell(\gamma_0)+\ell(\gamma_1)$.

Question: Does there always exist an admissible path joining $\gamma_0(1)$ to $\gamma_1(1)$ whose length is strictly less than $\ell(\gamma_0)+\ell(\gamma_1)$? Equivalently, can a length-minimizing admissible curve in a sub-Riemannian manifold ever have a corner (a point where two tangent half-lines in $\Delta$ are linearly independent)?
status_search_result: The "corner conjecture" was resolved affirmatively by Eero Hakavuori and Enrico Le Donne in "Non-minimality of corners in subriemannian geometry" (Inventiones mathematicae 206, 693–704, 2016; arXiv:1509.05578). They prove that any admissible curve with a corner can be shortened, so corners cannot occur on length minimizers; equivalently, the answer to the question is yes in every sub-Riemannian manifold.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M and a fixed starting point q0, consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H1 admissible paths starting at q0 to M, sending each path γ to γ(1). Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or can the singular curves issuing from q0 fill the entire manifold M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure, that is, a smooth subbundle $\Delta \subset TM$ together with a smooth fibrewise inner product on $\Delta$. Fix a base point $q_0 \in M$. Let $\Omega_{q_0}$ denote the Hilbert manifold of admissible (horizontal) paths $\gamma:[0,1] \to M$ of Sobolev class $H^1$ that start at $q_0$, i.e. absolutely continuous curves with $\dot\gamma(t) \in \Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ a.e. and $\int_0^1 \langle \dot\gamma(t),\dot\gamma(t)\rangle\, dt < \infty$. Define the endpoint map
$$E_{q_0}: \Omega_{q_0} \longrightarrow M, \qquad E_{q_0}(\gamma) = \gamma(1).$$
A point $q \in M$ is called a regular value of $E_{q_0}$ if every $\gamma \in E_{q_0}^{-1}(q)$ is a regular point of $E_{q_0}$ (i.e. the differential $dE_{q_0}(\gamma)$ is surjective); equivalently, $q$ is not the endpoint of any singular (abnormal) horizontal curve issuing from $q_0$.

Question: Must the endpoint map $E_{q_0}$ always possess at least one regular value in $M$? Equivalently, is it possible that the set of endpoints of singular horizontal curves starting at $q_0$ covers the entire manifold $M$?
status_search_result: Recent literature on the structure of the endpoint map near singular curves and on sub-Riemannian Jacobi/exponential maps (e.g. work on normal forms near "nice" singular curves and the survey literature on singular curves) discusses partial structural results but does not establish existence of regular values of the endpoint map in general. No source found resolves whether singular curves from a fixed point can fill the whole manifold; the question appears to remain open.

context_brief: Convexity of limit sets of Riemann sums
original_question: Let f: [0, 1] → c_0 be bounded, and let I(f) denote the set of all limits of sequences of Riemann sums of f taken over partitions whose diameters tend to 0. Must I(f) always be convex?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to $0$, equipped with the supremum norm. For a bounded function $f:[0,1]\to c_0$, a Riemann sum of $f$ associated with a tagged partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=1$ with tags $\xi_i\in[t_{i-1},t_i]$ is the vector
$$S(f,\{t_i,\xi_i\})=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(\xi_i)\,(t_i-t_{i-1})\in c_0,$$
and the diameter of the partition is $\max_i(t_i-t_{i-1})$. Define
$$I(f)=\bigl\{x\in c_0 : \text{there exist tagged partitions }P_k\text{ with diameter}\to 0\text{ such that }S(f,P_k)\to x\bigr\}.$$
Question: For every bounded function $f:[0,1]\to c_0$, must the set $I(f)\subseteq c_0$ be convex?
status_search_result: The Kadets–Kadets question on convexity of the set of limits of Riemann sums for bounded $c_0$-valued functions appears to remain open. Convexity of $I(f)$ is known for finite-dimensional target spaces (Halperin–Miller for Hilbert; finite-dimensional case of more recent work) and for B-convex spaces, but $c_0$ is not B-convex, and a 2023 arXiv preprint on the topic does not claim a resolution for $c_0$.

original_question: Suppose a Banach space X has the Pettis integrability property, meaning that every scalarly bounded and scalarly measurable X-valued function is Pettis integrable. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure ν_f be separable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a Banach space with topological dual $X^*$. A function $f:\Omega\to X$ is said to be scalarly measurable if $x^*\circ f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ is $\Sigma$-measurable for every $x^*\in X^*$, and scalarly bounded if there exists a constant $M$ such that for every $x^*\in X^*$ with $\|x^*\|\le 1$ one has $|x^*(f(\omega))|\le M$ for $\mu$-almost every $\omega\in\Omega$ (the exceptional null set may depend on $x^*$). The function $f$ is called Pettis integrable if $x^*\circ f\in L^1(\mu)$ for every $x^*\in X^*$ and if for every $A\in\Sigma$ there exists a vector $\int_A f\,d\mu\in X$ satisfying
$$x^*\!\left(\int_A f\,d\mu\right)=\int_A x^*\circ f\,d\mu\qquad\text{for all }x^*\in X^*.$$
Associated with such $f$ is the vector measure $\nu_f:\Sigma\to X$ given by $\nu_f(A)=\int_A f\,d\mu$, with range
$$R(\nu_f)=\{\nu_f(A):A\in\Sigma\}\subset X.$$
The Banach space $X$ is said to have the Pettis Integrability Property (PIP) if, for every complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$, every scalarly bounded and scalarly measurable function $f:\Omega\to X$ is Pettis integrable.

Question: Suppose $X$ has the PIP. Must $R(\nu_f)$ be a separable subset of $X$ for every Pettis integrable function $f:\Omega\to X$ defined on every complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$?
status_search_result: The question is recorded as an open problem of Plebanek concerning the Pettis Integrability Property. Surveys on Pettis integration (e.g., Musiał's lectures) and the relevant 2016 survey list it among unresolved problems, and no later publication has been found that resolves it. Related results show that PIP combined with separability of Pettis integrals is equivalent to weak Baire measures being concentrated on separable subspaces, but the implication PIP ⇒ separable range remains unsettled.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For the same endpoint-map setting in sub-Riemannian geometry, can length-minimizing singular curves issuing from a fixed point q0 fill a subset of M of positive measure, or is their image always measure-theoretically small?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure, that is, a smooth bracket-generating distribution $D \subset TM$ together with a smooth fiberwise inner product on $D$. A horizontal curve is an absolutely continuous path $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ such that $\dot\gamma(t)\in D_{\gamma(t)}$ for almost every $t$, with finite length $\ell(\gamma)=\int_0^1 |\dot\gamma(t)|\,dt$. Fix a point $q_0\in M$ and let $\Omega_{q_0}$ denote the Hilbert manifold of horizontal curves issuing from $q_0$ (with suitable Sobolev regularity). The endpoint map $\mathrm{End}:\Omega_{q_0}\to M$ sends $\gamma$ to $\gamma(1)$. A horizontal curve $\gamma\in\Omega_{q_0}$ is called singular (or abnormal) if it is a critical point of $\mathrm{End}$, i.e.\ the differential $d\,\mathrm{End}_\gamma$ is not surjective. A horizontal curve is length-minimizing if it realizes the sub-Riemannian distance between its endpoints.

Question: Can the union of the images of all length-minimizing singular horizontal curves issuing from $q_0$ have positive Lebesgue measure in $M$, or must this set always have Lebesgue measure zero?
status_search_result: This question is closely related to the (minimizing) Sard conjecture in sub-Riemannian geometry. In full generality the question remains open. Substantial partial results exist: for analytic sub-Riemannian structures in dimension 3, the strong Sard conjecture has been established, showing the set of endpoints of singular minimizing horizontal curves from a fixed point has Hausdorff dimension at most 1 (hence Lebesgue measure zero). Generic results and corank-one cases are also known, but the general smooth case—including whether minimizing singular curves from $q_0$ can fill a positive-measure subset of $M$—has not been resolved.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a rank-2 Martinet distribution in ℝ3, where points of the Martinet surface lie on optimal singular curves, what is the C1 classification of the germs of small sub-Riemannian spheres at points where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve? In other words, how do these sphere singularities look up to local C1 diffeomorphism in the generic Martinet case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider ℝ³ with coordinates (x, y, z) equipped with a rank-2 distribution Δ ⊂ TℝR³, that is, a smooth field of 2-planes. Such a distribution is called a Martinet distribution if Δ is bracket-generating and the Martinet surface

  Σ = { p ∈ ℝ³ : Δ(p) + [Δ, Δ](p) ≠ T_p ℝ³ }

is a smooth 2-dimensional submanifold (the locus where the Lie bracket of sections of Δ fails to span the tangent space). Endow Δ with a smooth sub-Riemannian metric g (a smoothly varying inner product on the 2-plane field), and consider the associated sub-Riemannian distance d: a horizontal curve is an absolutely continuous curve tangent a.e. to Δ, its length is computed via g, and d(p, q) is the infimum of lengths of horizontal curves joining p to q. The sub-Riemannian sphere of radius r centered at p₀ is

  S(p₀, r) = { q ∈ ℝ³ : d(p₀, q) = r }.

A horizontal curve γ is called a singular (abnormal) curve of Δ if it is a critical point of the endpoint map restricted to horizontal curves with fixed initial point; in the Martinet case, the singular curves are precisely the integral curves of the line field Δ ∩ TΣ on the Martinet surface, and for generic metrics these singular curves are locally length-minimizing.

Assume (Δ, g) is generic among Martinet sub-Riemannian structures on ℝ³, and let p₀ ∈ Σ. For sufficiently small r > 0, the sphere S(p₀, r) intersects an optimal singular curve issuing from p₀; let q be such an intersection point.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to germs of local C¹ diffeomorphisms of ℝ³ at q, of the possible germs of S(p₀, r) at q.
status_search_result: The C¹ classification of germs of small sub-Riemannian spheres at points of optimal singular curves in the generic Martinet case is described as an open question. Subsequent literature (e.g., the survey on singular curves in sub-Riemannian geometry, results on non-subanalyticity of Martinet spheres, and the 2022 work establishing the strong Sard conjecture and C¹ regularity of singular minimizers in analytic 3D sub-Riemannian structures) has advanced understanding of the singular minimizers and the (non-)regularity of Martinet spheres but does not appear to provide a complete C¹ classification of the relevant sphere germs.

context_brief: Norm compactness for quasi-Radon Pettis ranges
original_question: Suppose μ is a quasi-Radon probability measure. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure be relatively norm compact in X?

(ii) for every $A \in \Sigma$ there exists a vector $\int_A f\,d\mu \in X$ such that
$$x^*\!\left(\int_A f\,d\mu\right) = \int_A x^*\!\circ f\,d\mu \quad \text{for all } x^* \in X^*.$$

$$R(\nu_f) = \{\nu_f(A) : A \in \Sigma\} \subset X.$$

Suppose that $X$ does not contain an isomorphic copy of $c_0$ (the Banach space of real sequences converging to $0$, with the supremum norm). Must $R(\nu_f)$ be relatively norm compact in $X$ for every Pettis integrable function $f : \Omega \to X$?

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For the Engel distribution, that is, a rank-2 distribution in ℝ4 with n3(q) = 3 and n4(q) = 4, what is the C1 classification of the germs of sub-Riemannian spheres at points lying on the optimal singular curve through the point? Equivalently, how should one classify these 3-dimensional hypersurface singularities in ℝ4 up to local C1 diffeomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta \subset T\mathbb{R}^4$ be an Engel distribution, i.e. a smooth rank-2 distribution on $\mathbb{R}^4$ such that, for every point $q \in \mathbb{R}^4$,
$$\dim \Delta^2(q) = 3, \qquad \dim \Delta^3(q) = 4,$$
where $\Delta^1 = \Delta$ and $\Delta^{k+1} = \Delta^k + [\Delta, \Delta^k]$. Equip $\Delta$ with a smooth sub-Riemannian metric and let $d$ denote the induced sub-Riemannian distance on $\mathbb{R}^4$. For $q_0 \in \mathbb{R}^4$ and $r > 0$ sufficiently small, let
$$S(q_0,r) = \{ q \in \mathbb{R}^4 : d(q_0,q) = r \}$$
be the sub-Riemannian sphere of radius $r$ centered at $q_0$; it is a 3-dimensional hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

Through every point of $\mathbb{R}^4$ there passes exactly one (up to reparametrization) singular (abnormal) curve of $\Delta$, and short arcs of these singular curves are length-minimizers. Let $\gamma$ be the optimal singular curve issuing from $q_0$, and let $q \in \gamma$ with $r = d(q_0,q)$ small. The germ of $S(q_0,r)$ at $q$ is then a germ of a 3-dimensional hypersurface singularity in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

Problem. Classify, up to local $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$, the germs at $q$ of the sub-Riemannian spheres $S(q_0,r)$ as $q$ ranges over the optimal singular curve through $q_0$. Equivalently, give a complete list of normal forms, under local $C^1$ equivalence, for the 3-dimensional hypersurface singularities arising in this way.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. analyses of the front asymptotics of the flat sub-Riemannian Engel structure and of cut time on the Engel group) has produced detailed information about the Engel sphere—showing in particular that it fails to be subanalytic at points where abnormal geodesics meet it—but no source found provides a complete local $C^1$ classification of the sphere germs along the optimal singular curve. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Let q0 ∈ ℝ2 and let f0, f1 be smooth vector fields defined near q0 such that f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2. For the almost-Riemannian control system qdot = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with unit-speed constraint, what is the C1 classification of the germs of the distance function Sq0 for generic pairs (f0, f1) satisfying these conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a pair of smooth vector fields $f_0, f_1$ defined in a neighborhood of a point $q_0 \in \mathbb{R}^2$. Associated with this pair is the almost-Riemannian control system
$$\dot q = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q), \qquad u_0^2 + u_1^2 = 1,$$
with the unit-speed constraint. The almost-Riemannian distance $S_{q_0}(q)$ from $q_0$ is the infimum of times $T \ge 0$ such that there exists a measurable control $(u_0, u_1)$ with $u_0^2 + u_1^2 = 1$ steering $q_0$ to $q$ in time $T$.

Let $\Delta(q) = \det(f_0(q), f_1(q))$ and define the singular set $\mathcal{Z} = \{q : \Delta(q) = 0\}$. For $q$ in the singular set, write $n_2(q)$ for the order of vanishing of $\Delta$ at $q$ along $\mathcal{Z}$, and $n_3(q)$ for an associated higher-order invariant (the number of additional brackets needed beyond second order to span the tangent space at $q$), defined so that $(n_2, n_3) = (0,0)$ at Riemannian points, $(1,0)$ at generic singular points, etc.

Assume $f_0(q_0) \wedge f_1(q_0) = 0$, $n_2(q_0) = 1$, and $n_3(q_0) = 2$.

Determine the $C^1$-classification of the germs at $q_0$ of the distance function $S_{q_0}$ for generic pairs $(f_0, f_1)$ subject to the conditions above.

context_brief: Non-uniform Eberlein compacta in class K
original_question: Does there exist a non-uniform Eberlein compact space K such that C(K) belongs to the class U of Banach spaces for which every Pettis integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is McShane integrable? Equivalently, are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K = {K : C(K) ∈ U}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ denote the class of Banach spaces $X$ with the property that every Pettis integrable function $f\colon [0,1]\to X$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$) is McShane integrable. Recall that:

- A function $f\colon [0,1]\to X$ is Pettis integrable if $x^*\circ f$ is Lebesgue integrable for every $x^*\in X^*$ and, for each measurable $E\subseteq[0,1]$, there exists $x_E\in X$ such that $x^*(x_E)=\int_E x^*\circ f\,d\lambda$ for all $x^*\in X^*$.
- $f$ is McShane integrable with integral $x\in X$ if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a gauge $\delta\colon[0,1]\to(0,\infty)$ such that $\bigl\|\sum_{i=1}^n f(t_i)(b_i-a_i)-x\bigr\|<\varepsilon$ for every $\delta$-fine McShane partition $\{(t_i,[a_i,b_i])\}_{i=1}^n$ of $[0,1]$.

A compact Hausdorff space $K$ is called Eberlein compact if it is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space, and uniform Eberlein compact if it is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of a Hilbert space (equivalently, $C(K)$ is Hilbert generated).

Let $\mathcal{K}=\{K \text{ compact Hausdorff} : C(K)\in\mathcal{U}\}$. It is known that every uniform Eberlein compact belongs to $\mathcal{K}$, while some Eberlein compacta do not.

Question: Does there exist a non-uniform Eberlein compact space $K$ that belongs to $\mathcal{K}$?

context_brief: Topology dependence of the McShane integral
original_question: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a Banach space. Recall that a topology $\mathcal{T}$ on $\Omega$ is said to make $\mu$ quasi-Radon if $\mathcal{T} \subseteq \Sigma$, $\mu$ is inner regular with respect to closed sets, $\mu$ is $\tau$-additive (i.e., $\mu(\bigcup \mathcal{U}) = \sup_{U \in \mathcal{U}} \mu(U)$ for every upward directed family $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$), and $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ is complete and locally determined.

Given a topology $\mathcal{T}$ on $\Omega$ for which $\mu$ is quasi-Radon, a generalized McShane partition of $\Omega$ (with respect to $\mathcal{T}$) is a countable family $\{(E_i, t_i)\}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ where $\{E_i\}$ is a disjoint family of measurable sets with $\mu(\Omega \setminus \bigcup_i E_i) = 0$ and $t_i \in \Omega$ for each $i$. A gauge is a function $\Delta: \Omega \to \mathcal{T}$ with $t \in \Delta(t)$ for every $t \in \Omega$; a partition is $\Delta$-fine if $E_i \subseteq \Delta(t_i)$ for all $i$. A function $f: \Omega \to X$ is McShane integrable (with respect to $\mathcal{T}$) with integral $x \in X$ if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a gauge $\Delta$ such that $\big\| \sum_{i} \mu(E_i) f(t_i) - x \big\| \leq \varepsilon$ for every $\Delta$-fine generalized McShane partition for which the sum converges absolutely.

Question: Suppose $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ are two topologies on $\Omega$ for both of which $\mu$ is quasi-Radon, and suppose $f: \Omega \to X$ is McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_1$. Must $f$ be McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_2$?
status_search_result: The question is a problem of Fremlin on the topology-dependence of the McShane integral for Banach-space-valued functions on quasi-Radon probability spaces. Partial results are known: an affirmative answer holds when one of the topologies has a countable base, and McShane integrability with respect to one topology implies a weaker MC-integrability independent of topology. The general case appears to remain open, and the problem still appears in Fremlin's published list of open problems.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Let Δ ⊂ TM be a smooth vector distribution on a manifold M. Suppose Δ is singular transitive, meaning that any two points of M can be joined by a concatenation of singular curves of Δ. Does this singular transitivity force the full symmetry group of Δ—the diffeomorphisms Φ with Φ_*Δ = Δ—to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $\Delta \subset TM$ be a smooth vector distribution on $M$ (a smooth subbundle, possibly of non-constant rank, of the tangent bundle). A smooth curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ that is tangent to $\Delta$ (i.e. $\dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ for all $t$) is called a singular (or abnormal) curve of $\Delta$ if it is a critical point of the endpoint map on the space of $\Delta$-horizontal curves with fixed endpoints, in the standard sense of sub-Riemannian/control-theoretic geometry. Say that $\Delta$ is singular transitive on $M$ if any two points of $M$ can be joined by a concatenation of finitely many singular curves of $\Delta$. The symmetry group of $\Delta$ is 
$$\mathrm{Sym}(\Delta) := \{\Phi \in \mathrm{Diff}(M) : \Phi_*\Delta = \Delta\}.$$
Question: Does singular transitivity of $\Delta$ imply that $\mathrm{Sym}(\Delta)$ is a finite-dimensional Lie group?

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For rank-2 distributions that are not singular transitive, is the symmetry group always infinite-dimensional? The question asks whether the finite-dimensionality phenomenon might fail completely outside the singular-transitive case for rank-2 distributions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold and let $D \subset TM$ be a rank-2 distribution on $M$ (a smooth subbundle of the tangent bundle of fiber rank 2). The symmetry algebra of $D$ is the Lie algebra $\mathrm{sym}(D)$ of vector fields $X$ on $M$ whose local flow preserves $D$, i.e. $[X, \Gamma(D)] \subset \Gamma(D)$.

Iteratively define the weak derived flag of $D$ by $D^{(0)} = D$ and $D^{(i+1)} = D^{(i)} + [D, D^{(i)}]$ (as sheaves of vector fields). The distribution $D$ is called singular transitive if, on a dense open subset of $M$, the weak derived flag stabilizes at a proper subbundle $D^{(\infty)} \subsetneq TM$ of constant rank, so that the leaves of $D^{(\infty)}$ provide a non-trivial foliation to which $D$ is tangent.

Question: Is it true that for every rank-2 distribution $D$ on a manifold $M$ (of dimension $\geq 4$) that is not singular transitive, the symmetry algebra $\mathrm{sym}(D)$ is infinite-dimensional?
status_search_result: A targeted web search for the symmetry dimension of non-singular-transitive rank-2 distributions did not return direct evidence of a resolution. The question is phrased as an expectation rather than a theorem, and no follow-up paper establishing or refuting the infinite-dimensionality claim in full generality was located.

context_brief: Weakly compact subsets of c_0 as vector-measure ranges
original_question: Let K be a weakly compact subset of c_0. Must there exist a c_0-valued countably additive vector measure whose range contains K?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real (or complex) sequences converging to zero, equipped with the supremum norm. A function $\mu : \Sigma \to c_0$ defined on a $\sigma$-algebra $\Sigma$ of subsets of some set $\Omega$ is called a countably additive vector measure if $\mu(\bigcup_{n=1}^\infty E_n) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mu(E_n)$ in the norm topology of $c_0$ for every sequence $(E_n)$ of pairwise disjoint members of $\Sigma$. The range of $\mu$ is the set $\{\mu(E) : E \in \Sigma\} \subseteq c_0$.

Question: Is it true that for every weakly compact subset $K$ of $c_0$ there exist a measurable space $(\Omega,\Sigma)$ and a countably additive vector measure $\mu : \Sigma \to c_0$ such that $K \subseteq \{\mu(E) : E \in \Sigma\}$?

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For each n > 3, determine the smallest integer μ(n) such that any convex plane curve run μ(n) times admits arbitrarily small perturbations as a nondegenerate closed curve in ℝn, and decide whether every regular closed curve in ℝn has Frenet-frame length strictly greater than μ(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) ⊂ O(n).
self_contained_problem:
Let $n>3$ be an integer. A smooth regular closed curve $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is called nondegenerate (or has a well-defined Frenet frame) if at every point its first $n-1$ derivatives $\gamma'(t),\gamma''(t),\dots,\gamma^{(n-1)}(t)$ are linearly independent. Given a smooth convex closed curve $c$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, the curve "$c$ run $k$ times" is the closed curve obtained by traversing $c$ exactly $k$ times. Define
$$\mu(n) = \min\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0} : \text{for every smooth convex plane curve } c, \text{ the curve } c \text{ run } k \text{ times admits arbitrarily }C^\infty\text{-small perturbations that are nondegenerate closed curves in }\mathbb{R}^n\}.$$

For each regular closed curve $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, its Frenet frame defines a closed loop in the orthogonal group $O(n)$, whose length (with respect to the bi-invariant Riemannian metric on $O(n)$) is denoted $L(\gamma)$. Let $\ell_n$ denote the length of the standard closed geodesic $SO(2)\subset O(n)$ in this metric.

(a) Determine $\mu(n)$ for every $n>3$.

(b) Decide whether for every regular closed curve $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ one has the strict inequality
$$L(\gamma) > \mu(n)\cdot \ell_n.$$

No paper resolving the value of μ(n) for n>3 or proving/disproving the Frenet-frame length bound was located, so the status remains unverified.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equation on the torus with forcing restricted to a control space E. If D is an open subset of the torus, does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace E of the closure of {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D} that is independent of the viscosity ν and still makes the system approximately controllable, or controllable in finite-dimensional projections, by localized degenerate forcing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d/2\pi\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be the torus, and let $V$ denote the space of divergence-free, mean-zero smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{T}^d$. For $\nu>0$, consider the controlled incompressible Navier–Stokes system
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = \eta(t,x), \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
on $\mathbb{T}^d$, where the forcing $\eta(t,\cdot)$ takes values in a prescribed finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset V$ (the control space) and is otherwise arbitrary.

Let $D\subset \mathbb{T}^d$ be a fixed nonempty open set, and let $\overline{\{u\in V : \mathrm{supp}\,u\subset D\}}$ denote the closure (in a suitable Sobolev topology on $V$) of divergence-free vector fields supported in $D$.

Question: Does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace 
$$E \subset \overline{\{u\in V : \mathrm{supp}\,u\subset D\}},$$
chosen independently of the viscosity $\nu>0$, such that the controlled system above is
(a) approximately controllable in $V$, and/or
(b) controllable in projection onto every finite-dimensional subspace of $V$,
by forcings $\eta$ valued in $E$? Provide an effective construction of such a space $E$.
status_search_result: Controllability of 2D Navier–Stokes and Euler equations by degenerate (low-mode) forcing has been established by Agrachev–Sarychev and extended by others, including approximate controllability and controllability in finite-dimensional projections, with criteria valid uniformly in viscosity (including ν=0). However, those results use forcings supported on a finite set of Fourier modes, which are not localized in space. The localized version — where the control space E lies in the closure of vector fields supported in a prescribed open set D, is finite-dimensional, and independent of ν — does not appear to have been resolved in the literature reviewed; recent works (e.g., Nersesyan and collaborators) continue to address related localized controllability questions but do not explicitly settle this. Status appears open.

original_question: For a fixed compact 3-dimensional contact manifold with a chosen contact distribution, can one define a natural averaging or heat-type evolution on the space of sub-Riemannian metrics that converges, possibly after suitable rescaling, to a nonzero generalized metric preserved by the Reeb field, even when no smooth Reeb-invariant metric exists? This includes understanding whether the discrete averaging scheme or the continuous equation ∂h/∂t = c{uh,{uh,h}} can produce meaningful limiting Hamiltonians with controlled singularities.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed 3-dimensional contact manifold equipped with a smooth contact distribution $\Delta\subset TM$ (a smooth corank-1 subbundle whose annihilator is locally generated by a 1-form $\alpha$ with $\alpha\wedge d\alpha$ nowhere vanishing). For any choice of contact form $\alpha$ representing $\Delta$, the associated Reeb vector field $R_\alpha$ is the unique vector field satisfying $\alpha(R_\alpha)=1$ and $\iota_{R_\alpha}d\alpha=0$.

A sub-Riemannian metric on $\Delta$ is a smooth fiberwise positive definite quadratic form $g:\Delta\to\mathbb{R}$. Equivalently, it is encoded by its sub-Riemannian Hamiltonian $h:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$, the fiberwise nonnegative quadratic form on $T^*M$ defined by $h(\lambda)=\tfrac12\max_{v\in\Delta_x\setminus\{0\}}\langle\lambda,v\rangle^2/g(v)$ for $\lambda\in T^*_xM$. Let $u_h:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ denote the function $u_h(\lambda)=\langle\lambda,R_\alpha\rangle$ (with respect to a fixed choice of contact form $\alpha$), and let $\{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\}$ be the canonical Poisson bracket on $T^*M$.

Question. Does there exist a natural averaging procedure (either a discrete iteration $h_{n+1}=A_{\varepsilon_n,c_n}(h_n)$ depending on positive parameters $\varepsilon_n,c_n$, or the continuous evolution
$$\frac{\partial h}{\partial t}=c\,\{u_h,\{u_h,h\}\}$$
on the space of sub-Riemannian Hamiltonians associated to metrics on $\Delta$) such that, for any smooth initial sub-Riemannian metric on $\Delta$, the resulting evolution converges, after a suitable rescaling, to a nonzero limiting generalized fiberwise quadratic form $h_\infty$ on $T^*M$ that is invariant under the Reeb flow of $\alpha$ (i.e.\ satisfies $\{u_h,h_\infty\}=0$ in an appropriate weak sense), even on those contact 3-manifolds that admit no smooth Reeb-invariant sub-Riemannian metric on $\Delta$? In particular, can the parameters $\varepsilon_n,c_n$ be chosen so that the limit $h_\infty$ is nontrivial, and can the singularities of $h_\infty$ be controlled?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this Reeb-field "heat-type" averaging problem on sub-Riemannian metrics over contact 3-manifolds was found. Recent related work (e.g., on quantitative tightness via sub-Riemannian methods, spiraling of sub-Riemannian geodesics around Reeb orbits, and Ricci-curvature/Reeb-flow estimates in 3D contact sub-Riemannian geometry) explores neighbouring questions but does not construct or analyze the proposed discrete averaging or continuous flow $\partial_t h=c\{u_h,\{u_h,h\}\}$ or its limiting Reeb-invariant Hamiltonians. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Suppose ν is a non-atomic vector measure. Do there exist a set Γ and a vector measure ν̃: Σ → c_0(Γ) such that the associated spaces of integrable functions coincide, namely L^1(ν) = L^1(ν̃)?
self_contained_problem:
Let (Ω, Σ) be a measurable space and let X be a Banach space. A countably additive vector measure ν : Σ → X is called non-atomic if for every A ∈ Σ with ν(A) ≠ 0 there is B ∈ Σ, B ⊆ A, with ν(B) ≠ 0 and ν(A \ B) ≠ 0. A scalar function f : Ω → ℝ is integrable with respect to ν if it is integrable with respect to every scalar measure x*ν (x* ∈ X*) and for each A ∈ Σ there exists a vector ∫_A f dν ∈ X satisfying x*(∫_A f dν) = ∫_A f d(x*ν) for all x* ∈ X*. The space L¹(ν) consists of (equivalence classes of) such integrable functions, equipped with the norm ‖f‖ = sup{ ∫ |f| d|x*ν| : x* ∈ X*, ‖x*‖ ≤ 1 }.

For a set Γ, let c₀(Γ) denote the Banach space of all scalar functions on Γ that vanish at infinity, with the supremum norm.

Question: Suppose ν : Σ → X is a non-atomic vector measure. Do there necessarily exist a set Γ and a vector measure ν̃ : Σ → c₀(Γ) such that L¹(ν) = L¹(ν̃) (as Banach lattices, with the same underlying integrable functions)?
status_search_result: Curbera's classical result handles the separable case (representing L¹(ν) via a c₀-valued vector measure). For the non-separable version asked by Lipecki, J. Rodríguez ("On non-separable L¹-spaces of a vector measure") obtained partial answers: e.g., one can always represent L¹(ν) as L¹(ν̃) with ν̃ taking values in ℓ^∞(Γ), and a c₀(Γ) representation can be obtained under additional hypotheses (such as density character ω₁ or specific structural assumptions). The general problem in full generality does not appear to be settled.

original_question: Characterize when the norming set Γ = {γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*}} is a James boundary of L^1(ν), meaning that every f ∈ L^1(ν) attains its norm at some functional γ_{g,x*} in Γ.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a (real) Banach space with closed unit ball B_{X*} of its dual, and let ν : Σ → X be a countably additive vector measure defined on a measurable space (Ω, Σ). Let L^1(ν) denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) ν-integrable real-valued functions on Ω, equipped with the norm

  ‖f‖_{L^1(ν)} = sup_{x* ∈ B_{X*}} ∫_Ω |f| d|⟨x*, ν⟩|,

and let L^∞(ν) be the corresponding L^∞-space, with closed unit ball B_{L^∞(ν)}. For each g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)} and each x* ∈ B_{X*}, define the bounded linear functional γ_{g,x*} ∈ L^1(ν)* by

  γ_{g,x*}(f) = ∫_Ω f g d⟨x*, ν⟩,  f ∈ L^1(ν),

and set

  Γ = { γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*} } ⊂ B_{L^1(ν)*}.

Recall that a subset B of B_{Y*} is called a James boundary of a Banach space Y if every y ∈ Y attains its norm at some element of B; that is, for every y ∈ Y there exists b ∈ B with b(y) = ‖y‖.

Problem. Characterize, in terms of the vector measure ν (and the Banach space X), exactly when Γ is a James boundary of L^1(ν): i.e., when every f ∈ L^1(ν) satisfies ‖f‖_{L^1(ν)} = γ_{g,x*}(f) for some g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)} and some x* ∈ B_{X*}.
category_tag: James boundaries in L^1 of a vector measure
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning the characterization of when the canonical norming set Γ in the dual of L^1(ν) is a James boundary. Related work by Fernández, Mayoral, Naranjo, and Rodríguez gives sufficient conditions under which such norming sets behave as James boundaries (e.g., for testing integrability), but a complete characterization has not been located in the searched literature. The status appears to remain open.

context_brief: Weak-star sequential compactness in Lebesgue-Bochner duals
original_question: If the dual unit ball B_{X^*} is weak*-sequentially compact, must the dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} of the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) also be weak*-sequentially compact?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a probability space (or more generally a finite measure space), let $X$ be a real Banach space, and fix $1\le p<\infty$. Denote by $L^p(\mu,X)$ the Lebesgue–Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) strongly measurable functions $f:\Omega\to X$ with $\|f\|_p=\bigl(\int_\Omega \|f(\omega)\|_X^p\,d\mu(\omega)\bigr)^{1/p}<\infty$. For a Banach space $Y$, let $B_{Y^*}$ denote the closed unit ball of its topological dual $Y^*$, equipped with the weak$^*$ topology $\sigma(Y^*,Y)$; we say that $B_{Y^*}$ is weak$^*$-sequentially compact if every sequence in $B_{Y^*}$ admits a weak$^*$-convergent subsequence with limit in $B_{Y^*}$.

Question: Suppose that $B_{X^*}$ is weak$^*$-sequentially compact. Does it follow that $B_{L^p(\mu,X)^*}$ is weak$^*$-sequentially compact?
status_search_result: A web search did not produce a definitive resolution of this question. Related work characterizes weakly (sequentially) compact subsets of Lebesgue–Bochner spaces (Diestel–Ruess–Schachermayer, Ülger, and recent work by Rodríguez), but no source clearly confirms or refutes the implication that weak$^*$-sequential compactness of $B_{X^*}$ transfers to $B_{L^p(\mu,X)^*}$. The status appears to remain unresolved in the public literature accessible via search.

original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a finite (or $\sigma$-finite) measure space and let $X$ be a real Banach space. Recall that a bounded subset $K$ of a Banach space $Y$ is weakly compact if it is compact in the weak topology of $Y$. A Banach space $Y$ is said to be strongly weakly compactly generated (SWCG) if there exists a weakly compact subset $G \subseteq Y$ such that for every weakly compact set $K \subseteq Y$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $K \subseteq nG + \varepsilon B_Y$, where $B_Y$ denotes the closed unit ball of $Y$.

Let $L^1(\mu, X)$ denote the Lebesgue–Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) Bochner-integrable functions $f : \Omega \to X$, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_1 = \int_\Omega \|f(\omega)\|_X \, d\mu(\omega)$.

Question: If $X$ is SWCG, must $L^1(\mu, X)$ also be SWCG?
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Schlüchtermann and Wheeler, appears to remain open. Recent work (e.g., Avilés–Rodríguez and subsequent papers around 2015–2022) provides partial results, such as showing $L^1(\mu, X)$ is SWCG when $X$ is an SWCG subspace of an $L^1$-space, and characterizations via δS-sets, but the general implication is still listed as an open problem.

original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly K-analytic, or strongly weakly countably determined, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) inherit the same corresponding property?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space. Recall the following definitions.

(1) A topological space T is called K-analytic if there exists an upper semicontinuous compact-valued map from the Baire space ℕ^ℕ onto T (equivalently, T is the continuous image of a Lindelöf Čech-complete space). A Banach space X is weakly K-analytic (WKA) if (X, weak) is K-analytic.

(2) A topological space T is called countably determined (or Lindelöf Σ) if there exist a subspace Σ of ℕ^ℕ and an upper semicontinuous compact-valued map from Σ onto T. A Banach space X is weakly countably determined (WCD) if (X, weak) is countably determined.

(3) A WKA Banach space X is called strongly WKA if there exists an upper semicontinuous compact-valued map φ: ℕ^ℕ → 2^X with φ(ℕ^ℕ) = X (where 2^X is equipped with weak compact subsets) such that, in addition, for every weakly compact set L ⊂ X there is some σ ∈ ℕ^ℕ with L ⊂ φ(σ). Analogously, a WCD Banach space X is called strongly WCD if there exist a subspace Σ ⊂ ℕ^ℕ and an upper semicontinuous compact-valued map φ: Σ → 2^X covering X such that every weakly compact subset of X is contained in some φ(σ).

Given a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) and 1 ≤ p < ∞, let L^p(μ, X) denote the Lebesgue–Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) strongly μ-measurable functions f: Ω → X with ∫_Ω ‖f(ω)‖^p dμ(ω) < ∞.

Question: If X is strongly WKA (respectively, strongly WCD), must L^p(μ, X) also be strongly WKA (respectively, strongly WCD)?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper resolving the question of whether L^p(μ, X) inherits the strongly WKA or strongly WCD property from X. Closely related results concerning SWCG spaces and weakly compact sets in Lebesgue–Bochner spaces exist, but no explicit resolution of the strongly WKA / strongly WCD inheritance was found.

original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ and let $X$ be a (real or complex) Banach space. Consider the Bochner–Lebesgue space $L^p([0,1], X)$ consisting of (equivalence classes of) strongly measurable functions $f : [0,1] \to X$ with finite norm $\|f\|_{L^p([0,1],X)} = \big(\int_0^1 \|f(t)\|_X^p \, dt\big)^{1/p}$, where $[0,1]$ is equipped with Lebesgue measure. A Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of a Banach space $E$ is called unconditional if for every $x \in E$ the basis expansion $x = \sum_n a_n e_n$ converges unconditionally in $E$ (equivalently, converges for every reordering of the indices).

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of those Banach spaces $X$ for which $L^p([0,1], X)$ admits an unconditional Schauder basis.
category_tag: Unconditional bases in vector-valued L^p spaces

original_question: Are there infinite-dimensional reflexive Banach spaces with property (D_1), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → X which is bounded in L^1([0, 1], X) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 has a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $([0,1],\mathcal{L},\lambda)$ denote the unit interval with Lebesgue measure. A function $f:[0,1]\to X$ is strongly measurable if it is the almost-everywhere limit of a sequence of simple $X$-valued measurable functions. The Bochner space $L^1([0,1],X)$ consists of (equivalence classes of) strongly measurable $f:[0,1]\to X$ with $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1\|f(t)\|\,dt<\infty$.

A sequence $(f_n)$ of strongly measurable $X$-valued functions on $[0,1]$ is said to converge scalarly in measure to $0$ if for every $x^*\in X^*$ the real-valued sequence $\langle x^*, f_n(\cdot)\rangle$ converges to $0$ in Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. It is said to converge scalarly to $0$ almost everywhere if for every $x^*\in X^*$ there is a set $N_{x^*}\subseteq[0,1]$ of measure $0$ (depending on $x^*$) such that $\langle x^*, f_n(t)\rangle\to 0$ for every $t\in[0,1]\setminus N_{x^*}$.

The space $X$ is said to have property $(D_1)$ if every sequence $(f_n)$ of strongly measurable $X$-valued functions on $[0,1]$ which is bounded in $L^1([0,1],X)$ and converges scalarly in measure to $0$ admits a subsequence that converges scalarly to $0$ almost everywhere.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional reflexive Banach space $X$ with property $(D_1)$?

original_question: Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set P (whose elements are called faces) satisfying the standard axioms: P has a minimum face and a maximum face; every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 faces; P is strongly flag-connected; and P satisfies the diamond condition (so for every flag Φ and every i ∈ {0, 1, …, n−1} there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its i-face). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on flags. P is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on the flag set.

For a regular abstract n-polytope (the case k = 1), fixing a base flag Φ produces distinguished generators ρ_0, …, ρ_{n−1} of Γ(P), where ρ_i sends Φ to Φ^i. These generators satisfy the intersection condition
  ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩ for all I, J ⊆ {0, …, n−1},
and together with the standard string Coxeter-type relations this characterizes which groups arise as automorphism groups of regular abstract polytopes.

For a general k-orbit abstract n-polytope P, one can analogously associate a symmetry type graph and a distinguished generating set of Γ(P) determined by representatives of the flag orbits and the involutions exchanging i-adjacent flags.

Problem. Formulate, for every k ≥ 1, the precise analogue of the intersection condition that the distinguished generating set of the automorphism group of a k-orbit abstract n-polytope must satisfy, and show that, together with appropriate relations dictated by the symmetry type graph, these conditions characterize exactly the groups arising as automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract n-polytopes.
status_search_result: A 2022 preprint and subsequent published work titled "All polytopes are coset geometries: characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes" provides a general characterization, for arbitrary k and any prescribed symmetry type graph, of automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes in terms of distinguished generators, relations, and intersection conditions, thereby answering the problem.

original_question: How can one build a general polytope as a coset geometry of its automorphism group when a distinguished generating set is given?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a strictly monotone rank function with values in $\{-1,0,\dots,n\}$, possessing a unique minimum element of rank $-1$ and unique maximum element of rank $n$, in which every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly $n+2$ elements; for each flag $\Phi$ and each rank $i\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ there is exactly one flag $\Phi^i$ differing from $\Phi$ only in its element of rank $i$ (the diamond condition); and any two flags can be connected by a sequence of such adjacent flags through elements lying in any chosen interval (strong flag-connectedness). The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is the group of order-preserving bijections of $\mathcal{P}$.

Given a flag $\Phi_0$ of $\mathcal{P}$, a distinguished generating set for $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ (relative to $\Phi_0$) is a subset $S\subseteq\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ that generates $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ and satisfies natural compatibility conditions with the flag-adjacency structure (e.g. for regular polytopes, $S=\{ho_0,\dots,ho_{n-1}\}$ where $ho_i$ sends $\Phi_0$ to $\Phi_0^i$). A coset geometry construction of $\mathcal{P}$ from $(\Gamma(\mathcal{P}),S)$ specifies, for each rank $i$, a subgroup $\Gamma_i\le\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ (typically a stabilizer associated with $S$) so that the rank-$i$ elements of $\mathcal{P}$ are recovered as the cosets of $\Gamma_i$, with incidence given by non-empty intersection, and so that $\Gamma_0,\dots,\Gamma_{n-1}$ satisfy an intersection property guaranteeing that the resulting incidence system is indeed an abstract polytope isomorphic to $\mathcal{P}$.

Problem. Describe, for an arbitrary abstract n-polytope $\mathcal{P}$ (not assumed regular or chiral, and with arbitrarily many flag-orbits under $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$), an explicit general procedure that, given a distinguished generating set $S$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, produces subgroups $\Gamma_0,\dots,\Gamma_{n-1}$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ together with an intersection-type condition on $(S,\Gamma_0,\dots,\Gamma_{n-1})$ such that $\mathcal{P}$ is recovered (up to isomorphism) as the coset geometry on these subgroups; and conversely, characterize which pairs $(\Gamma,S)$ of a group with a distinguished generating set arise from an abstract polytope in this way.
status_search_result: A 2023 paper "All polytopes are coset geometries: characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes" (Hubard et al., published in J. Combin. Theory Ser. A) addresses this problem, providing a characterization in terms of generators, relations, and intersection conditions for the automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes with prescribed symmetry type graph. The general problem thus appears to have been substantially resolved, though earlier work covered only regular, chiral, and small-orbit cases, indicating gradual progress rather than a single complete solution at the time the question was originally posed.

original_question: Can one find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for coverings that works beyond the regular and chiral cases?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a unique minimum and maximum element, all of whose maximal chains (flags) have length n+1, which is strongly flag-connected and satisfies the diamond condition. Given two abstract polytopes P and Q of the same rank, a covering P → Q is an order-preserving, rank-preserving surjection that maps flags of P onto flags of Q.

For regular abstract polytopes (those whose automorphism group acts transitively on flags) and for chiral abstract polytopes (those with two flag orbits exchanged by adjacency), there is a "quotient criterion": a regular (resp. chiral) polytope P covers a regular (resp. chiral) polytope Q if and only if Q is isomorphic to a quotient P/N, where N is a subgroup of the automorphism group Aut(P) (resp. of the rotation group of P) satisfying explicit intersection conditions with the distinguished generators of that group. This criterion characterizes coverings purely in terms of subgroups of a string C-group (or string rotation group).

Problem. Formulate and prove a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion that determines, for an arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytope P (k ≥ 1), exactly which abstract polytopes Q are covered by P, in terms of combinatorial data attached to P (such as flag-orbit structure, voltages, or symmetry-type graphs) rather than restricting to the regular (k=1) or chiral (k=2 with two orbits exchanged by adjacency) cases.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2016 list of open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes. No subsequent work located in the search establishes a general combinatorial quotient criterion beyond the regular and chiral cases, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Which polytopes P have the property that their monodromy group Mon(P) is a string C-group?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be an abstract polytope of rank n, i.e., a partially ordered set satisfying the standard axioms of an abstract polytope (existence of a least and greatest element, every maximal chain (flag) has length n+1, the diamond condition, and strong flag-connectedness). For each i in {0,1,...,n-1}, the i-adjacency relation pairs each flag Φ with its unique i-adjacent flag Φ^i (the flag differing from Φ only in its element of rank i). Let F(P) denote the set of flags of P, and let r_i be the permutation of F(P) sending Φ to Φ^i. The monodromy group of P is

   Mon(P) := ⟨ r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1} ⟩,

a subgroup of the symmetric group on F(P). The generators satisfy r_i^2 = 1 and (r_i r_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i-j| ≥ 2; thus Mon(P) is a quotient of a string Coxeter group with the standard string diagram.

A group G generated by involutions s_0, s_1, ..., s_{n-1} is called a string C-group (with respect to this generating set) if (s_i s_j)^2 = 1 for |i-j| ≥ 2, and the intersection condition holds:

   ⟨ s_i : i ∈ I ⟩ ∩ ⟨ s_i : i ∈ J ⟩ = ⟨ s_i : i ∈ I ∩ J ⟩  for all I, J ⊆ {0, ..., n-1}.

Problem. Give a characterization of those abstract polytopes P for which the monodromy group Mon(P), with its generating set (r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1}), is a string C-group.
status_search_result: Standard results (Schulte's correspondence) imply that for regular polytopes Mon(P) is automatically a string C-group, since it equals the automorphism group. Subsequent work by Monson, Pellicer, Hartley, Williams and others has investigated when monodromy groups of non-regular polytopes give string C-groups (e.g., for two-orbit polytopes and via regular covers), but a general characterization of all polytopes with this property does not appear to be established in the literature found via search. The problem appears to remain open in full generality.

original_question: Does there exist a polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but that still has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or can one prove that no such polytope exists?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P, with a unique minimum element and a unique maximum element, satisfying the standard diamond and strong flag-connectedness conditions, so that every maximal chain (flag) has exactly n+2 elements. For each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1} and each flag Φ of P, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its element of rank i; this defines involutions r_0,…,r_{n−1} acting on the set F(P) of flags of P.

The monodromy group (or connection group) of P is
   Mon(P) = ⟨r_0, r_1, …, r_{n−1}⟩,
viewed as a permutation group on F(P).

A string C-group of rank n is a group G generated by involutions s_0,…,s_{n−1} satisfying:
 (i) the string (commuting) condition: (s_i s_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i−j| ≥ 2;
 (ii) the intersection condition: for all I, J ⊆ {0,…,n−1},
       ⟨s_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨s_j : j ∈ J⟩ = ⟨s_k : k ∈ I ∩ J⟩.
Equivalently, string C-groups are exactly the automorphism groups of abstract regular polytopes (with their distinguished generators).

A regular polytopal cover of an abstract polytope P is an abstract regular polytope R together with a rank- and incidence-preserving surjection R → P. A minimal regular cover of P is a regular cover R such that any regular cover of P factors through R; if it exists, the minimal regular cover of P need not in general be unique up to isomorphism.

It is known that whenever Mon(P) is a string C-group (with respect to its canonical generators r_0,…,r_{n−1}), the polytope P admits a unique minimal regular cover.

Problem.

Determine whether there exists an abstract polytope P such that:
 (a) Mon(P) is not a string C-group, and
 (b) P nevertheless admits a unique minimal regular polytopal cover;

or else prove that no such polytope P exists.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any explicit resolution of this question. Related literature confirms that a string C-group monodromy implies a unique minimal regular cover, and that for rank ≥ 4 minimal covers need not be unique, but no source was found that either constructs a polytope with non–string-C-group monodromy yet a unique minimal regular cover, or proves the non-existence of such a polytope. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Given a string group generated by involutions, what are the minimal string C-groups that cover it?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer. A string group generated by involutions (sggi) of rank n is a pair (G, S) where G is a group and S = (ρ_0, ρ_1, …, ρ_{n−1}) is an ordered generating set of involutions of G satisfying the commuting (string) relations (ρ_i ρ_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i − j| ≥ 2. A string C-group of rank n is an sggi (G, S) that additionally satisfies the intersection property: for all subsets I, J ⊆ {0, 1, …, n−1},
  ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_j : j ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_k : k ∈ I ∩ J⟩.

Given two sggi's (G, S) and (H, T) of the same rank n with S = (ρ_0, …, ρ_{n−1}) and T = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}), we say (H, T) covers (G, S) if the map ρ_i ↦ σ_i extends to a surjective group homomorphism from H onto G (equivalently, (G, S) is a quotient of (H, T) preserving the ordered generators). A cover (H, T) of (G, S) by a string C-group is called minimal if no proper quotient of (H, T) that is itself a string C-group still covers (G, S).

Problem: Given an arbitrary sggi (G, S), determine all minimal string C-groups (H, T) that cover (G, S).
category_tag: String C-groups and abstract regular polytopes

original_question: What is the correct way to generalize the chirality group from two-orbit polytopes to k-orbit polytopes?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a ranked partially ordered set (with a minimum and a maximum element) satisfying the standard diamond, flag-connectedness, and strong flag-connectedness conditions that generalize the face lattice of a convex polytope. A flag is a maximal chain. For each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, every flag Φ has a unique i-adjacent flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in the element of rank i.

The automorphism group Γ(P) of an abstract polytope P acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope P is called regular if Γ(P) acts transitively on flags, and chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on flags with adjacent flags belonging to different orbits. More generally, P is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on flags.

For a chiral polytope P (a 2-orbit polytope of a particular type), one defines its chirality group X(P) as follows. Let W be the abstract rotation group with the standard presentation such that the rotation subgroup Γ^+(P) of any chiral or directly-regular polytope of the given Schläfli type is a quotient of W. Let M and M' be the kernels of the natural surjections W → Γ^+(P) and W → Γ^+(P*), where P* is the mirror image (enantiomorphic form) of P. The chirality group of P is defined as
   X(P) := M·M' / (M ∩ M'),
or equivalently as the smallest normal subgroup of Γ^+(P) whose quotient is the rotation group of a directly-regular polytope. The polytope P is "totally chiral" when X(P) = Γ^+(P) and "minimally chiral" when X(P) is as small as possible.

Problem. Find a "correct" generalization of the chirality group from chiral (two-orbit) polytopes to k-orbit polytopes. That is, for an arbitrary k ≥ 2 and an arbitrary symmetry type graph T on k vertices, define a group invariant X_T(P) attached to every k-orbit abstract polytope P of symmetry type T, having the following properties:

(i) When k = 2 and T is the symmetry type graph of a chiral polytope, X_T(P) coincides with the classical chirality group X(P) defined above.

(ii) X_T(P) is trivial if and only if P admits a "regular cover" appropriate to the symmetry type T, in the sense that there exists a regular polytope Q and a covering Q → P that identifies the relevant flag orbits; equivalently, X_T(P) measures the obstruction for P to be obtained as a quotient of a regular polytope by a normal subgroup respecting the orbit structure encoded by T.

(iii) X_T(P) admits an intrinsic group-theoretic description in terms of the automorphism group Γ(P), generators corresponding to the symmetry type graph T, and the canonical surjection from a universal "T-rotation" group analogous to W.

Provide such a definition and verify properties (i)–(iii), or prove that no definition satisfying (i)–(iii) exists.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra and on characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes via coset geometries, 2022–2023) develops machinery toward symmetry-type-graph generalizations of chirality, but no canonical "chirality group" for arbitrary k-orbit polytopes that simultaneously specializes to the classical chirality group of two-orbit chiral polytopes and captures regular-cover obstructions has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Given a polytope P, how can one determine the size of its monodromy group |Mon(P)|?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be an abstract polytope of rank n, i.e., a ranked partially ordered set of faces (with a least face and a greatest face) satisfying the standard diamond and strong flag-connectedness axioms of an abstract polytope. Let F(P) denote the set of flags of P (maximal totally ordered chains). For each i ∈ {0, 1, …, n−1}, let σ_i : F(P) → F(P) be the involution that sends each flag Φ to the unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face. The monodromy group of P is

   Mon(P) = ⟨σ_0, σ_1, …, σ_{n−1}⟩,

a subgroup of the symmetric group on F(P). Equivalently, Mon(P) is isomorphic to the automorphism group of the minimal regular cover of P.

Problem. Develop a method that, given an arbitrary abstract polytope P (for instance, presented combinatorially via its face lattice or its set of flags together with the adjacency involutions), determines the order |Mon(P)|. In particular, find general formulas or algorithms expressing |Mon(P)| in terms of combinatorial data of P, and compute |Mon(P)| for natural infinite families of polytopes.
status_search_result: No general formula or algorithm for |Mon(P)| is known; results exist only for specific families (e.g., truncated simplices, n-pyramids), where Mon(P) has been computed case-by-case. The problem in its general form remains open.
