paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
original_question: Generalize the spectral existence results for odd and even cycles to signed graphs: determine for which signed simple graphs Nikiforov-type eigenvalue conditions force the existence of negative or positive circles, and determine whether the Yuan and Nikiforov–Yuan upper-bound theorems for forbidden odd or even cycle lengths extend to signed simple graphs with negative or positive circles of prescribed lengths.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a simple graph and $\sigma: E \to \{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function. The sign of a circle (cycle) $C$ in $\Sigma$ is the product of the signs of its edges; the circle is called positive if its sign is $+1$ and negative if its sign is $-1$. A signed graph is balanced if every circle is positive, and unbalanced otherwise. The adjacency matrix $A(\Sigma)$ is the $|V|\times|V|$ matrix with $A_{uv} = \sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise; let $\lambda_1(\Sigma) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(\Sigma)$ be its eigenvalues. For an unsigned graph $G$, write $\lambda_1(G)$ for the spectral radius of its (ordinary) adjacency matrix.

The following classical spectral existence theorems for unsigned simple graphs are taken as given:

(N) Nikiforov's theorem on non-bipartiteness: there exists an explicit eigenvalue condition on $\lambda_1(G)$ (and on $G$'s edge count or order) which forces $G$ to be non-bipartite, equivalently to contain an odd circle.

(Y) Yuan's theorem and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorem: if a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains no circle of a prescribed odd length (resp. no circle of a prescribed even length) $\ell$, then $\lambda_1(G)$ satisfies an explicit upper bound depending on $n$ and $\ell$, with the extremal graphs characterized.

Problems.

(1) Determine the class of signed simple graphs $\Sigma$ for which the analogue of (N), with "non-bipartite" replaced by "unbalanced" (i.e., containing a negative circle), holds. Specifically, identify a sharp spectral condition on $\lambda_1(\Sigma)$ (or on a suitable spectral invariant of $\Sigma$) that forces $\Sigma$ to contain a negative circle, and characterize precisely the signed simple graphs satisfying the hypotheses of (N) for which this implication is valid.

(2) Determine whether Yuan's theorem and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorem extend to signed simple graphs in the following form: for prescribed $\ell$, give a sharp upper bound on $\lambda_1(\Sigma)$ for signed simple graphs $\Sigma$ on $n$ vertices that contain no negative circle of length $\ell$ (when one seeks an analogue of the odd-cycle case) and, separately, no positive circle of length $\ell$ (when one seeks an analogue of the even-cycle case). In each case, characterize the extremal signed graphs.
status_search_result: Several recent works (2022–2025) have addressed signed-graph analogues of Nikiforov-type spectral Turán theorems. Results include spectral conditions forcing negative 3-cycles in unbalanced signed graphs, the maximum spectral radius among negative-$C_4$-free unbalanced signed graphs, extremal results for $C_3^-$-free signed graphs, and spectral Turán problems for $C_k^-$-free, $K_4^-$-free, $K_{3,3}^-$-free, and $K_5^-$-free signed graphs. Thus the program has been carried out for specific small/short forbidden circles, but a complete generalization of Nikiforov's, Yuan's, and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorems to arbitrary negative or positive circle lengths in signed simple graphs has not been fully established.

(b) hadronic processes, such as proton synchrotron radiation in strong magnetic fields, or photo-pion / photo-pair cascades initiated by interactions of relativistic protons with ambient photon fields and matter; or

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
original_question: For a signed digraph (D, σ), determine when the directed frustration index—the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes the digraph cycle balanced—equals the ordinary frustration index of the underlying undirected signed graph.
self_contained_problem:
Let $D = (V, A)$ be a directed graph (digraph), and let $\sigma : A \to \{+1, -1\}$ be a signing of its arcs; the pair $(D, \sigma)$ is called a signed digraph. The sign of a directed cycle in $D$ is the product of the signs of its arcs. The signed digraph $(D, \sigma)$ is said to be cycle balanced if every directed cycle of $D$ has positive sign. Define the directed frustration index $\ell(D, \sigma)$ to be the minimum number of arcs whose deletion from $D$ yields a cycle balanced signed digraph.

Let $\Gamma$ denote the underlying undirected multigraph of $D$, with each arc replaced by an edge keeping the same sign, giving a signed graph $(\Gamma, \sigma)$. A signed undirected graph is balanced if every cycle has positive sign, and its (undirected) frustration index $\ell(\Gamma, \sigma)$ is the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $(\Gamma, \sigma)$ balanced. One always has
$$\ell(D, \sigma) \le \ell(\Gamma, \sigma).$$

Problem. Characterize the signed digraphs $(D, \sigma)$ for which equality $\ell(D, \sigma) = \ell(\Gamma, \sigma)$ holds; that is, give necessary and sufficient structural conditions on $(D, \sigma)$ under which the directed frustration index coincides with the frustration index of the underlying undirected signed graph.
status_search_result: The directed frustration index has been studied computationally (e.g., Aref et al.'s optimization models for signed networks), and it is known to be bounded above by the undirected frustration index, with computation of the frustration index itself being NP-hard. No publication located characterizes when the directed and undirected frustration indices coincide; the question appears to remain an open problem in the signed-graph literature.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
original_question: For a signed digraph (D, σ), determine when the directed frustration number—the minimum number of vertices whose deletion makes the digraph cycle balanced—equals the ordinary frustration number of the underlying undirected signed graph.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected graph and let $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ be a sign function on its edges; the pair $(\Gamma,\sigma)$ is called a signed graph. The sign of a cycle in $(\Gamma,\sigma)$ is the product of the signs of its edges; the cycle is positive (balanced) if this product is $+1$, and negative otherwise. The signed graph is balanced if every cycle is positive. The (undirected) frustration number $l_0(\Gamma,\sigma)$ is the minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a balanced signed graph.

Now let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite directed graph (digraph) whose underlying undirected graph is $\Gamma$, and consider the signed digraph $(D,\sigma)$ obtained by retaining the same edge signs. A directed cycle in $D$ inherits a sign as the product of the signs of its arcs. The signed digraph $(D,\sigma)$ is called cycle balanced if every directed cycle of $D$ is positive. Define the directed frustration number $l_0(D,\sigma)$ to be the minimum number of vertices whose deletion makes the resulting signed digraph cycle balanced.

Since balance of $(\Gamma,\sigma)$ implies cycle balance of $(D,\sigma)$, one always has 
$$l_0(D,\sigma)\le l_0(\Gamma,\sigma).$$

Problem: Characterize the signed digraphs $(D,\sigma)$ for which equality $l_0(D,\sigma)=l_0(\Gamma,\sigma)$ holds, where $\Gamma$ is the underlying undirected graph of $D$.
status_search_result: The question is part of a problem collection on signed graphs concerning the directed frustration number of signed digraphs. A web search did not turn up any published characterization of when the directed frustration number of a signed digraph equals the frustration number of its underlying undirected signed graph; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
original_question: How reliable are the different methods for estimating black-hole masses in active galactic nuclei, including reverberation mapping, single-epoch reverberation-mapping estimates, methods using Balmer lines, methods using the CIV line for objects at redshift greater than about 2, and estimates based on the black-hole-mass–stellar-velocity-dispersion correlation?
self_contained_problem:
In active galactic nuclei (AGN), the mass $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$ of the central supermassive black hole is commonly estimated by several techniques:

(i) Reverberation mapping (RM), which uses the time delay $\tau$ between continuum variability and the response of a broad emission line to derive a characteristic broad-line-region (BLR) radius $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}=c\tau$, and then sets
$$M_{\mathrm{BH}} = f\,\frac{R_{\mathrm{BLR}}\,(\Delta V)^2}{G},$$
where $\Delta V$ is a measure of the broad-line velocity width and $f$ is a dimensionless virial factor (typically $\langle f\rangle\sim 5$) encoding the unknown geometry and kinematics of the BLR.

(ii) Single-epoch (SE) "virial" estimates, which calibrate against RM by using an empirical $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}$–luminosity relation together with a single-epoch line-width measurement.

(iii) Balmer-line based estimates (using $\mathrm{H}\beta$ or $\mathrm{H}\alpha$) within (i) or (ii).

(iv) C IV $\lambda 1549$-based estimates, used for high-redshift quasars ($z\gtrsim 2$) where Balmer lines are not accessible to optical spectroscopy.

(v) Estimates obtained from the $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$–$\sigma_\star$ relation, where $\sigma_\star$ is the stellar velocity dispersion of the host galaxy bulge.

Quantify the reliability of each of these methods. Specifically:

(a) Determine, with rigorous uncertainty propagation, the systematic and statistical uncertainty (in dex of $\log_{10} M_{\mathrm{BH}}$) inherent to RM masses arising from the virial factor $f$, and assess whether the commonly used value $\langle f\rangle\sim 5$ yields masses accurate at the $0.3$–$0.4$ dex level.

(b) Determine the corresponding uncertainty for single-epoch Balmer-line estimates relative to RM masses.

(c) Determine whether C IV-based single-epoch estimates at $z\gtrsim 2$ are biased relative to Balmer-line and RM estimates, and, if so, characterize the bias as a function of luminosity, Eddington ratio, line shape (e.g., blueshift/asymmetry of C IV), and other observables.

(d) Determine the intrinsic scatter and possible systematic offsets of $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$–$\sigma_\star$ based estimates for AGN, especially Type 1 AGN, relative to direct dynamical or RM masses.

Provide a quantitative comparison establishing the relative trustworthiness of methods (i)–(v).
status_search_result: This is a longstanding open question in AGN astrophysics. Recent reviews (e.g., Shen 2013; Peterson 2014; Czerny et al. 2019; SDSS-RM and AGN STORM campaigns through the 2020s) report that RM masses based on Balmer lines are reliable to roughly 0.3–0.5 dex when an average virial factor is adopted, single-epoch Balmer estimates carry ~0.3–0.5 dex scatter, C IV estimates remain controversial with biases that depend on line blueshift and shape, and $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$–$\sigma_\star$ based AGN masses show significant scatter and possible offsets. No consensus calibration eliminating these systematics has been established, so the question remains open.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
original_question: Do active galactic nuclei that genuinely lack a broad-line region exist, or are observed cases without broad emission lines mainly caused by observational biases such as spatial resolution and sensitivity, by obscuration and orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration?
self_contained_problem:
In the standard unified model of active galactic nuclei (AGN), every AGN possesses a broad-line region (BLR): a population of dense gas clouds, located close to the central supermassive black hole, that produces broad permitted emission lines (with full-widths of order 10^3–10^4 km/s) in the rest-frame optical/UV spectrum. Within this model, AGN that do not display broad emission lines (so-called type 2 AGN) are interpreted as objects in which the BLR is hidden from the observer's line of sight by an obscuring dusty torus, by orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration; alternatively, broad lines may be missed because of insufficient spatial resolution or sensitivity, or because they are diluted by host-galaxy starlight.

An alternative hypothesis posits that there exist genuine "non-hidden BLR" AGN (sometimes called "true type 2" AGN) in which the BLR is physically absent, for instance because at sufficiently low Eddington-scaled accretion rates the accretion flow transitions to a radiatively inefficient mode that cannot sustain the BLR clouds.

Question: Do AGN that intrinsically lack a broad-line region truly exist as a physical class, or can every observed AGN without detected broad emission lines be accounted for by observational biases (spatial resolution, sensitivity, host-galaxy dilution), by obscuration and orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration?
status_search_result: Multiple observational studies since the late 2000s have identified candidate "true type 2" Seyfert galaxies (e.g., NGC 3147, NGC 3660, Q2131-427) which display narrow emission lines without evidence of X-ray absorption and without polarized broad lines, supporting the existence of AGN intrinsically lacking a BLR, typically at low Eddington ratios. However, the size and purity of this class remain debated, with ongoing work refining samples and ruling out obscuration/dilution alternatives, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully settled.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
context_brief: edge cover for positive directed cycles
original_question: For a signed digraph, determine the smallest number of edges that meet every positive directed cycle.
self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,E,\sigma)$ be a finite signed digraph: a directed graph with arc set $E$ together with a sign function $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$. The sign of a directed cycle (a closed directed walk with no repeated vertices) is the product of the signs of its arcs. A directed cycle is called positive if its sign is $+1$.

An arc set $F\subseteq E$ is said to cover all positive directed cycles if every positive directed cycle of $D$ contains at least one arc of $F$. Define
$$\tau^+(D)=\min\{|F|:F\subseteq E\text{ and }F\text{ meets every positive directed cycle of }D\}.$$

Determine $\tau^+(D)$: give a combinatorial formula, structural characterization, or efficient algorithm to compute the minimum number of arcs needed to cover every positive directed cycle of an arbitrary signed digraph $D$.
status_search_result: The corresponding decision problem (covering all positive, resp. negative, directed cycles by a minimum set of arcs in a signed digraph) is known to be NP-complete via reductions to covering even/odd directed cycles in unsigned digraphs. No closed-form combinatorial formula or efficient algorithm for the minimum cover number is known, and the problem is listed among open questions in the signed-graphs problem literature.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
context_brief: vertex cover for positive directed cycles
original_question: For a signed digraph, determine the smallest number of vertices that meet every positive directed cycle.
self_contained_problem:
A signed digraph is a pair $(D,\sigma)$ where $D=(V,E)$ is a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs allowed if desired) and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on the arcs. The sign of a directed cycle $C$ in $D$ is the product $\sigma(C)=\prod_{e\in C}\sigma(e)$; the cycle is called positive if $\sigma(C)=+1$ and negative otherwise. A vertex set $S\subseteq V$ is said to cover the positive directed cycles of $(D,\sigma)$ if every positive directed cycle of $D$ contains at least one vertex of $S$.

Define
$$\tau^{+}(D,\sigma) \;=\; \min\bigl\{\,|S| \;:\; S\subseteq V \text{ covers every positive directed cycle of } (D,\sigma)\,\bigr\}.$$

Problem: Determine $\tau^{+}(D,\sigma)$. More precisely, give a combinatorial formula, a min–max characterization, or sharp bounds (in terms of natural parameters of $(D,\sigma)$) for the smallest number of vertices needed to meet every positive directed cycle of an arbitrary signed digraph, and analyze the computational complexity of computing this minimum.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of the minimum positive-directed-cycle vertex cover problem for signed digraphs was located. The question appears in a problem collection on signed graphs and remains, to the best of available evidence, open. Related undirected versions (covering negative/positive cycles in signed graphs) are known to be NP-hard via connections with odd-cycle transversal and even-cycle problems, but a definitive solution for the directed positive-cycle case was not found.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
original_question: Do the same kinds of galaxies host active and quiescent black holes, and do the same kinds of galaxies host Type 1 and Type 2 active galactic nuclei, or are these categories phases in an evolutionary sequence whose outcome depends on star formation and active-galactic-nucleus feedback?
self_contained_problem:
Consider galaxies harboring a central supermassive black hole. Such black holes are classified as "active" (actively accreting and powering an active galactic nucleus, AGN) or "quiescent." Active galactic nuclei are further divided into Type 1 (showing both broad and narrow optical emission lines, with a direct view of the central engine) and Type 2 (showing only narrow optical emission lines, with the central engine obscured). Determine which of the following hypotheses is correct for the population of galaxies in the local and intermediate-redshift universe:

(a) Active and quiescent black holes are hosted by statistically indistinguishable populations of galaxies (in terms of stellar mass, morphology, color, environment, and star-formation properties), and Type 1 and Type 2 AGN are likewise hosted by indistinguishable populations, differing only by orientation as predicted by the strict unified model;

(b) These categories instead correspond to distinct phases of an evolutionary sequence, with transitions among quiescent, Type 2, and Type 1 phases governed by ongoing star formation and by feedback from the AGN onto the host's gas content.

Specifically, characterize the host-galaxy properties (morphology, environment, stellar mass, star-formation rate) that do or do not distinguish Type 1 from Type 2 AGN hosts, and from quiescent-black-hole hosts, and decide whether the observed distinctions are consistent with pure orientation effects or require an evolutionary scenario driven by star formation and AGN feedback.
status_search_result: Empirical studies since 2014 have produced partial answers. Star-formation rates of Type 1 and Type 2 AGN appear similar once redshift and X-ray luminosity are controlled, consistent with the unified model. However, statistically significant differences in host stellar mass (Type 1 hosts ~0.2 dex lower), morphology, color, and environment of neighbors of Type 1 vs. Type 2 AGN have been reported, suggesting an evolutionary link rather than pure orientation. The full question — whether these categories are distinct populations or phases of an evolutionary sequence shaped by star formation and AGN feedback — remains an active area of research without consensus.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
context_brief: high-redshift AGN triggering and host evolution
original_question: At high redshift, how is active-galactic-nucleus activity triggered, what are the characteristics of active-galactic-nucleus host galaxies, and how does the relation between black-hole accretion and host-galaxy star formation evolve with redshift?
self_contained_problem:
Consider active galactic nuclei (AGN), defined as galaxies whose central supermassive black holes are actively accreting matter and emitting strong, non-stellar electromagnetic radiation, observed at high cosmological redshift (z ≳ 1). Address the following three connected questions:

1. By what physical mechanisms is AGN activity triggered at high redshift? In particular, characterize the relative contributions of major galaxy mergers, minor mergers, secular processes (e.g. disk instabilities, bar-driven inflows), and cold gas accretion from the cosmic web in producing nuclear accretion onto the central black hole.

2. What are the observational and physical characteristics of the host galaxies of high-redshift AGN, including their stellar masses, morphologies, gas content, dust content, star-formation rates, environments, and how these properties differ from those of non-active galaxies of comparable mass and redshift.

3. How does the relation between the black-hole accretion rate (or AGN luminosity) and the star-formation rate of the host galaxy evolve with redshift? Specifically, determine the functional form, normalization, and scatter of any correlation between these two quantities as a function of z, and assess whether AGN feedback enhances, suppresses, or has no causal effect on host star formation across cosmic time.
category_tag: AGN triggering and host galaxy coevolution
status_search_result: This is a broad open research question in extragalactic astrophysics rather than a single well-posed problem with a definitive answer. As of recent literature (JWST and ALMA-era studies), high-redshift AGN triggering, host properties, and the AGN–star-formation connection remain actively debated, with partial empirical results but no consensus resolution.

original_question: For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider perturbations of the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation
    u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = F(u, u_x, u_{xx}, ...),  x ∈ ℝ, t ∈ ℝ,
where F denotes a (suitably regular and small) perturbation term that breaks the complete integrability of KdV. A function v: ℝ → ℝ is called almost periodic (in the sense of Bohr) if for every ε > 0 the set of ε-almost periods {τ ∈ ℝ : sup_{x∈ℝ} |v(x+τ) − v(x)| < ε} is relatively dense in ℝ; equivalently, v lies in the closure (in the uniform norm) of the trigonometric polynomials. A solution u(x,t) is said to evolve almost periodically in time if, for each fixed x ∈ ℝ, the map t ↦ u(x,t) is almost periodic, and more strongly if the orbit {u(·,t) : t ∈ ℝ} is precompact in the uniform topology.

Question: Identify a natural class of perturbations F and a natural class of almost periodic initial data u_0(x) on ℝ such that the Cauchy problem
    u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = F(u, u_x, ...),    u(x,0) = u_0(x)
admits a unique global-in-time solution u(x,t) which is almost periodic in x for every t and evolves almost periodically in time. Prove or disprove the conjecture that, for suitable choices of F and u_0, this global existence, uniqueness, and almost periodicity holds.
status_search_result: For the unperturbed (integrable) KdV equation with almost periodic initial data, work by Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic (Duke Math J., 2018) established almost periodicity in time for suitable classes of initial data, addressing a conjecture of Deift. However, for non-integrable perturbations of KdV the question remains open: no general results establishing global existence, uniqueness, and almost periodicity in time on almost periodic backgrounds for perturbed KdV are known. Recent work (Damanik–Lukić–Volberg–Yuditskii and follow-ups, 2021–2024) has produced counterexamples in related settings, indicating the problem is delicate, but the perturbed-KdV conjecture itself is still considered open.

original_question: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and $1 \leq w \leq n$ be integers. Consider an $n \times n$ random band matrix $H = (H_{ij})$ defined as follows:

- $H$ is either real symmetric or complex Hermitian;
- $H_{ij} = 0$ whenever $|i-j| \geq w$ (with indices viewed either on the line or on the cycle $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$);
- the entries $\{H_{ij} : i \leq j,\ |i-j| < w\}$ are independent (subject to the symmetry/Hermitian constraint), centered, and have variance proportional to $1/w$, so that the empirical spectral distribution converges to the semicircle law.

For an energy $E$ in the bulk of the semicircle, study the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ near $E$ on the natural microscopic scale $1/(n\rho_{sc}(E))$. Prove the following dichotomy:

(i) If $w/\sqrt{n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ converge to those of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (in the Hermitian case) or Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (in the real symmetric case); equivalently, the appropriately rescaled $k$-point correlation functions converge to the sine-kernel determinantal/Pfaffian limits.

(ii) If $w/\sqrt{n} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ near $E$ converge to those of a Poisson point process with intensity $n\rho_{sc}(E)$.

Establish (i) and (ii) in both the real symmetric and the complex Hermitian settings.
status_search_result: The Fyodorov–Mirlin conjecture remains open in its full form. Significant partial progress exists: GUE/GOE bulk universality has been established for bandwidths well above $\sqrt{n}$ (e.g., $w \gg n^{3/4}$ and subsequent improvements by Bourgade–Erdős–Yau–Yin and others), and the conjecture has been fully proved for special chiral band-matrix models at zero energy (Letters in Mathematical Physics, 2024). Recent 2025 works combine localization results with Yau–Yin/Erdős–Riabov delocalization to obtain a localization–delocalization transition for a wide class of 1D band matrices, but proving Poisson statistics in the regime $w \ll \sqrt{n}$ for general band matrices is still not completed.

original_question: At low and high redshift, is the relation between active galactic nuclei and star formation coincidental, causal, self-regulated, or some combination of these, especially when distinguishing galaxy-wide star formation from nuclear star formation near the central black hole?
status_search_result: The character of the AGN/star-formation connection remains an actively debated open question in extragalactic astrophysics. Recent observational and theoretical studies (using e.g. Herschel, ALMA, JWST data) have produced mixed evidence for positive correlations, anti-correlations, and time-delay/self-regulated scenarios at both low and high redshift, with no consensus on whether the relation is coincidental, causal, or self-regulated, especially when separating nuclear from galaxy-wide star formation.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
original_question: How important is active-galactic-nucleus feedback in shaping the observed relations between black-hole mass and host-galaxy properties in nearby and high-redshift quasars?
self_contained_problem:
Let M_BH denote the mass of the supermassive black hole at the center of a galaxy, and let σ_* denote the stellar velocity dispersion of its host galaxy's bulge (or other host structural/dynamical properties such as bulge mass, luminosity, or Sérsic index). Empirical observations across nearby galaxies have established tight scaling relations between M_BH and these host properties (e.g., the M_BH–σ_* relation), suggesting a coevolutionary link between central black holes and their hosts. "Active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback" refers to the energy and momentum injection from accreting supermassive black holes into the surrounding interstellar and circumgalactic medium, via radiative winds, radio jets, and outflows, which can heat, expel, or otherwise regulate the gas reservoir available for star formation and further black-hole accretion.

Problem: Quantitatively determine the role of AGN feedback in establishing and maintaining the observed scaling relations between M_BH and host-galaxy structural/dynamical properties, both for the local (z ≈ 0) quasar population and for high-redshift (z ≳ 2) quasars. Specifically, characterize whether AGN feedback is the dominant physical mechanism setting the normalization, slope, and intrinsic scatter of these relations, or whether it plays a subdominant role compared to alternative mechanisms (e.g., hierarchical merger-driven averaging, stellar feedback, or self-regulated gas supply), and identify how the relative importance of AGN feedback evolves with redshift.
status_search_result: The relative importance of AGN feedback in establishing the M_BH–host-galaxy scaling relations remains an active and unresolved area of research in extragalactic astrophysics. While AGN-driven outflows are widely observed in both local and high-redshift quasars and are incorporated as a key ingredient in cosmological simulations (IllustrisTNG, EAGLE, SIMBA), recent reviews continue to debate whether feedback is the causal driver of the relations or whether non-causal mechanisms (e.g., merger averaging) suffice. No definitive consensus has been reached.

original_question: For random Schrodinger operators H = -Delta + V with random potential V, can one rigorously analyze the bulk spectral regime where eigenfunctions are expected to delocalize and eigenvalues are expected to follow random-matrix statistics, and can one construct and analyze models that exhibit the conjectured transition from Poisson statistics to random-matrix statistics at a mobility edge?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H = -\Delta + V$ act on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ (or on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$), where $\Delta$ is the discrete (resp. continuum) Laplacian and $V$ is a random potential (for example, $V(x) = \omega_x$ with i.i.d. random variables $\{\omega_x\}_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ having a bounded density). For finite-volume restrictions $H_L$ to a box of side $L$, denote the eigenvalues by $E_1(L) \le E_2(L) \le \cdots$ and consider, for an energy $E$ in the spectrum, the rescaled local eigenvalue point process
$$\xi_L^E := \sum_i \delta_{L^d (E_i(L) - E)}.$$

The mobility edge conjecture asserts the existence of a threshold $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ such that:
(i) for energies $E$ in the localization regime (e.g. $E < \mu$ in $d \ge 3$, or throughout the spectrum in $d = 1, 2$), $H$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions and $\xi_L^E$ converges to a Poisson point process;
(ii) for energies $E$ in the delocalized (bulk) regime ($E > \mu$, $d \ge 3$, weak disorder), $H$ has absolutely continuous spectrum with extended eigenfunctions and $\xi_L^E$ converges to the local eigenvalue statistics of a random matrix ensemble (e.g. the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble $\operatorname{Sine}_1$ process).

Problem: Rigorously establish, for a non-trivial random Schrödinger operator $H = -\Delta + V$, the existence of the delocalized regime with random-matrix-type local eigenvalue statistics and absolutely continuous spectrum, and prove the existence of a mobility edge $\mu$ separating the Poisson and random-matrix statistical regimes. Equivalently, construct and rigorously analyze a concrete model in which the transition from Poisson to random-matrix local eigenvalue statistics at a mobility edge is proved.
category_tag: Random Schrödinger operators and mobility edge
status_search_result: The mobility edge conjecture for random Schrödinger operators in dimension d ≥ 3 — including the existence of absolutely continuous spectrum/extended states and a Poisson-to-random-matrix transition — remains widely regarded as open. Poisson statistics in the localized regime are known (Minami and successors, including results on regular graphs and continuum operators), but the delocalized regime with GOE/Sine_1 statistics has not been established for any standard Anderson-type model. Partial results exist for related toy models (e.g. random band matrices, regular graphs/trees), but the full conjecture is unresolved.

original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?
self_contained_problem:
Let $W_N=(w_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le N}$ be an $N\times N$ Hermitian (or real symmetric) Wigner-type random matrix whose entries $\{w_{ij}:i\le j\}$ are independent with mean zero and a (possibly site-dependent) variance profile $S=(s_{ij})$, $s_{ij}=\mathbb{E}|w_{ij}|^2$. Assume the variance profile is chosen so that, as $N\to\infty$, the empirical spectral measure $\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\delta_{\lambda_k(W_N)}$ converges weakly to a deterministic equilibrium (self-consistent) probability measure $\rho$ on $\mathbb{R}$ whose support $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)=\bigcup_{r=1}^{p}[a_r,b_r]$ consists of $p\ge 2$ disjoint compact intervals.

(i) Prove bulk universality: for every fixed energy $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)$ with $\rho(E)>0$, the local correlation functions of the eigenvalues of $W_N$, rescaled by $1/(N\rho(E))$, converge to the sine-kernel correlation functions of the GUE (resp. GOE).

(ii) Prove edge universality at every spectral edge: for each endpoint $a_r$ and $b_r$ of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)$, the suitably rescaled extremal eigenvalues near that edge converge to the Tracy–Widom $\beta=2$ (resp. $\beta=1$) distribution.

(iii) Consider one-parameter families $W_N=W_N(t)$ of such ensembles in which the variance profile (or an external deformation) depends continuously on a parameter $t$, and in which two adjacent intervals of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho_t)$ merge (closing a gap) or a single interval splits (opening a gap) as $t$ crosses a critical value $t_*$. Establish the corresponding local eigenvalue statistics at the critical parameter $t_*$, in particular at the cusp/critical points where intervals meet or separate, and describe the universal limiting process governing the transition.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since 2017. For Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval (multi-cut) self-consistent density, bulk universality (Ajanki–Erdős–Krüger), edge universality with Tracy–Widom statistics in both single- and multi-cut cases, and cusp universality with the Pearcey process at points where intervals meet or split (Erdős–Krüger–Schröder; Cipolloni–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder) have been established for complex Hermitian and real symmetric symmetry classes, completing the Wigner–Dyson–Mehta program for these singularity types. Full quantitative control of arbitrary one-parameter families through gap-opening/closing transitions in the most general Wigner setting still receives ongoing refinements, so the broader program is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
context_brief: AGN class status of gamma-ray radio-loud NLSy1s
original_question: Gamma-ray-emitting radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are Seyfert active galactic nuclei characterized by narrow permitted Hβ lines, [OIII]/Hβ < 3, an Fe II bump, strong X-ray variability, steep X-ray spectra, substantial soft X-ray excess, relatively small central black-hole masses, high accretion rates, and an expected association with spiral hosts. Do the five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies detected by Fermi-LAT in gamma rays constitute a distinct third class of active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets, in addition to blazars and radio galaxies, and what is the physical nature of that class?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxy is a type of Seyfert active galactic nucleus (AGN) defined by the following optical and X-ray properties: (i) narrow permitted Balmer emission lines from the broad-line region with FWHM(Hβ) < 2000 km s⁻¹; (ii) a flux ratio [O III] λ5007 / Hβ < 3; (iii) a prominent Fe II emission bump; (iv) strong X-ray variability, a steep X-ray continuum, and a substantial soft X-ray excess; (v) inferred central black-hole masses in the range 10⁶–10⁸ M_⊙; (vi) accretion rates close to or above the Eddington limit; and (vii) host galaxies that are typically spiral. A radio-loud NLSy1 is an NLSy1 whose radio loudness parameter exceeds the standard threshold separating radio-loud from radio-quiet AGN. Among AGN, two well-established classes are known to host powerful relativistic jets pointing close to (blazars) or away from (radio galaxies) the line of sight.

Problem. Consider the population of radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies that have been detected in GeV γ-rays by the Fermi Large Area Telescope (initially comprising five sources). Determine whether these γ-ray-emitting radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies form a genuinely distinct third class of jetted AGN — separate from blazars and from radio galaxies — and characterize the physical nature of such a class. Specifically: (a) establish whether their jet production mechanism, jet power, central black-hole mass distribution, accretion regime, host-galaxy morphology, and cosmological evolution differ in an essential way from those of blazars and radio galaxies; and (b) identify the physical mechanism(s) responsible for the high-energy γ-ray emission in these objects and explain how relativistic jets can be launched and maintained in systems with comparatively low black-hole masses and high (near- or super-Eddington) accretion rates hosted in spiral galaxies.
status_search_result: The classification of γ-ray-emitting radio-loud NLSy1s as a distinct third jetted-AGN class remains an active and unresolved question. Subsequent work has expanded the sample of γ-ray-detected NLSy1s and has revealed that some hosts may be ellipticals or merging systems, blurring the boundary with blazars/radio galaxies; the issues of jet launching at low black-hole masses, near-Eddington accretion, and host morphology remain debated in recent literature.

paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
original_question: For the five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies detected by Fermi-LAT, whose apparent isotropic luminosities in the 0.1–100 GeV band are about 10^44–10^47 erg s−1 and therefore blazar-like, are the high gamma-ray luminosities mainly produced because the relativistic jet is viewed at a small angle and has a high beaming factor?
self_contained_problem: Consider five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 (RL-NLS1) galaxies — 1H 0323+342, SBS 0846+513, PMN J0948+0022, PKS 1502+036, and PKS 2004−447 — that have been detected at high significance in the 0.1–100 GeV band by a space-based gamma-ray telescope, with apparent isotropic gamma-ray luminosities in the range 10^44–10^47 erg s^−1, comparable to those of blazars. Assuming each source hosts a relativistic jet whose Doppler-boosted emission depends on the bulk Lorentz factor Γ and on the viewing angle θ between the jet axis and the line of sight (with beaming factor δ = [Γ(1−β cos θ)]^−1), determine whether the observed high apparent gamma-ray luminosities of these five RL-NLS1 galaxies are predominantly explained by a small viewing angle θ and a correspondingly large beaming factor δ, analogous to the situation in blazars.
status_search_result: Subsequent VLBI/MOJAVE kinematic studies and multiwavelength SED modeling of the gamma-ray-detected RL-NLS1 sources support the interpretation that their high apparent gamma-ray luminosities are due to relativistic jets viewed at small angles with high beaming factors, similar to flat-spectrum radio quasars. High bulk Lorentz factors and small viewing angles have been confirmed in several of these sources, though precise jet parameters and the population as a whole are still being characterized.

original_question: For random-matrix models that depend on external parameters p and undergo critical changes in the support of the equilibrium measure at values p_c, can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits in which p approaches p_c while the matrix size n tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a family of unitary-invariant Hermitian random matrix ensembles on the space of n×n Hermitian matrices M, with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

   (1/Z_{n,p}) · ∏_{i<j}(x_i − x_j)^2 · ∏_i exp(−n V(x_i; p)),

where V(·; p): ℝ → ℝ is a real-analytic confining potential depending smoothly on an external parameter p ∈ I ⊂ ℝ, and Z_{n,p} is the normalization constant. As n → ∞ with p fixed, the empirical eigenvalue measure (1/n)∑_i δ_{x_i} converges weakly to a deterministic equilibrium measure μ_p, defined as the unique minimizer of the weighted logarithmic energy functional

   E_p(μ) = ∬ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x; p) dμ(x)

over Borel probability measures μ on ℝ.

Assume there exists a critical value p_c ∈ I at which the topology or regularity of the support of μ_p changes (for example, the number of connected components of supp(μ_p) jumps, or the equilibrium density develops a higher-order vanishing point or merges into a singular endpoint).

Develop a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the local eigenvalue statistics, partition function Z_{n,p}, and correlation kernels in the double-scaling limit

   n → ∞,   p = p_c + c · n^{−α},   c ∈ ℝ fixed,

for the appropriate critical exponent α > 0, and more generally in multi-scaling regimes where several parameters approach their critical values simultaneously at coordinated rates. Identify the limiting kernels (expressible via solutions to Painlevé-type equations or Riemann–Hilbert problems associated with the type of critical transition) and establish universality of these limits within natural classes of potentials V(·; p) producing the same critical behavior.
status_search_result: The general program of rigorously analyzing double-scaling and multi-scaling limits at critical transitions of equilibrium measures in random matrix theory remains broadly open. Several specific cases (e.g., Painlevé II at the soft edge / one-cut-to-two-cut transitions, Painlevé I/II hierarchies at singular interior points, certain birth-of-a-cut transitions) have been resolved via Riemann–Hilbert steepest-descent methods by Bleher–Its, Claeys, Kuijlaars, Vanlessen and others, but a comprehensive theory covering arbitrary critical transitions and multi-parameter scaling limits has not been completed.

original_question: Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?
self_contained_problem:
For each $\beta>0$, consider the soft-edge scaling limit of the largest eigenvalue of the $\beta$-ensemble on $\mathbb{R}$ with joint density proportional to
$$\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}|x_i-x_j|^{\beta}\,\prod_{i=1}^{N} e^{-\beta N V(x_i)/2},$$
and let $F_\beta(s)$ denote the corresponding Tracy–Widom$_\beta$ distribution function (the limiting distribution of the appropriately centered and scaled largest eigenvalue, which is known to exist and to be universal in $V$).

For $\beta\in\{1,2,4\}$, classical results of Tracy and Widom express $F_\beta$ in closed form via the Hastings–McLeod solution of the Painlevé II equation $q''(s)=sq(s)+2q(s)^3$.

(a) For every even integer $\beta>0$, give a fully rigorous derivation of an explicit Painlevé/Lax-pair representation of $F_\beta(s)$ extending the formulas obtained for $\beta=6$ via the Bloemendal–Virág PDE and a corresponding Lax pair (the "Rumanov-type" approach), including a complete justification of the integrability of the associated auxiliary ordinary differential equation and of the asymptotic analysis of the resulting Riemann–Hilbert / isomonodromic system.

(b) For general real $\beta>0$, rigorously establish the asymptotic expansions of $F_\beta(s)$ as $s\to\pm\infty$ that have been proposed for the right and left tails, of the schematic form
$$\log F_\beta(s) \sim -\tfrac{2\beta}{24}|s|^3 + \cdots \quad (s\to-\infty), \qquad 1-F_\beta(s) \sim e^{-\tfrac{2\beta}{3}s^{3/2}+\cdots}\quad (s\to+\infty),$$
together with all subleading coefficients (including the nonperturbative constants).

State and prove such explicit formulas and rigorous asymptotic expansions, or prove that no such closed-form Painlevé representation exists.
status_search_result: The β=6 case has seen significant progress: Rumanov (2014) derived a Painlevé-type representation, and subsequent work by Grava–Its–Kapaev–Mezzadri (2016) and Bertola–Cafasso–Rubtsov (2017–2020) connected it to the second Calogero–Painlevé system and proved Lax integrability, bringing the analysis closer to rigor. However, the rigorous integrability and asymptotic analysis of the auxiliary ODE in Rumanov's β=6 formula remains incomplete, no analogous explicit formulas have been rigorously established for even β>6, and the conjectured tail asymptotics of Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal for general β>0 have not been fully rigorously verified. Thus the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
original_question: In the radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy PKS 1502+036, how can evidence for relativistic boosting—a one-sided radio structure and radio spectral variability—be reconciled with the absence of detected apparent superluminal motion at 15 GHz in VLBA observations from 2002 to 2012?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a radio-loud active galactic nucleus exhibiting the following observational features in its parsec-scale radio jet (as imaged by Very Long Baseline Interferometry at 15 GHz over a decade-long monitoring campaign):

(i) a one-sided core–jet morphology (a bright compact core with a faint jet extending on one side only),
(ii) significant radio spectral variability suggestive of a compact, opacity-evolving emission region,
(iii) no measurable apparent superluminal motion of jet components, with all detected pattern speeds consistent with sub-luminal apparent velocities β_app c (β_app < 1).

In the standard relativistic-beaming framework, a jet with bulk Lorentz factor Γ and viewing angle θ to the line of sight produces an apparent transverse speed
   β_app = β sin θ / (1 − β cos θ),
a Doppler factor δ = 1/[Γ(1 − β cos θ)], and a jet-to-counterjet flux ratio R = ((1 + β cos θ)/(1 − β cos θ))^(2+α) for a continuous jet of spectral index α. One-sidedness and spectral variability typically demand δ ≫ 1, while the absence of superluminal motion bounds β_app.

Problem. Determine a physically self-consistent set of jet parameters (Γ, θ, β) — and, where relevant, a distinction between the bulk flow speed and the pattern speed of moving features — that simultaneously:
(a) produces a jet-to-counterjet brightness ratio large enough to render the counterjet undetectable (consistent with the observed one-sidedness),
(b) yields a Doppler factor δ sufficiently large to account for the observed radio spectral variability (and high gamma-ray luminosity, if applicable),
(c) keeps the apparent component speed β_app ≤ 1 throughout a ≥10-year monitoring baseline.

In particular, identify the regime of (Γ, θ) compatible with all three conditions, and explain how the apparent tension (sometimes called a "Doppler-factor crisis") between strong boosting indicators and the lack of superluminal motion can be resolved (e.g., by a small viewing angle θ ≲ 1/Γ, by a difference between pattern speed and bulk speed, by jet bending or geometry, or by intrinsic variability mimicking variability without large-scale component motion).
status_search_result: Subsequent VLBI monitoring and SED modeling of this source confirmed the apparent tension: the one-sided structure, spectral variability, and high gamma-ray luminosity require a high Doppler factor, yet only sub-luminal pattern speeds have been measured, resembling a "Doppler-factor crisis" similar to that in TeV BL Lacs. Proposed reconciliations include a very small viewing angle (θ ≲ 1/Γ, where the apparent-speed formula yields β_app < 1 even for highly relativistic flows) and/or a pattern speed slower than the bulk-flow speed. The issue has thus been partially understood phenomenologically but no unique parameter solution has been definitively established.

original_question: For the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with general initial data, can one prove full 3:2:1 KPZ universality in the strong sense proposed by Corwin, Quastel, and Remenik for solutions of the Cauchy problem, and can one identify the limiting process that arises in that scaling limit?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic PDE on the real line,
  ∂_t h(t,x) = (1/2) ∂_x^2 h(t,x) + (1/2) (∂_x h(t,x))^2 + ξ(t,x),  t > 0, x ∈ ℝ,
where ξ is a space–time Gaussian white noise, interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transform h = log Z, with Z solving the multiplicative stochastic heat equation ∂_t Z = (1/2) ∂_x^2 Z + Z ξ.

For ε > 0, define the 3:2:1 (equivalently 1:2:3) rescaled height process
  h_ε(t,x) := ε^{1/2} ( h(ε^{-3/2} t, ε^{-1} x) + (1/24) ε^{-3/2} t ),
with initial profile h_ε(0,·) prescribed from a class of admissible initial data (e.g. functions of at most linear growth, possibly plus narrow wedges, sampled from a broad subclass of continuous functions).

Strong KPZ universality problem (Cauchy problem, full form):
(a) Prove that, as ε → 0, the random space–time field (t,x) ↦ h_ε(t,x) converges in distribution (with respect to a suitable topology, e.g. uniform on compacts in (t,x), with t > 0) to a universal random field H(t,x) — the so-called KPZ fixed point — for the widest possible class of initial data h_ε(0,·) → 𝔥(·).
(b) Identify the limiting space–time process H explicitly: describe its finite-dimensional distributions, its Markov property in t, its dependence on the initial datum 𝔥, and its joint law as a space–time random field (i.e. as the directed landscape composed with the initial datum).

Goal: establish 3:2:1 universality in this strong (process-level, general-initial-data) sense for solutions of the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation, and explicitly characterize the limit.
status_search_result: The KPZ fixed point was constructed by Matetski–Quastel–Remenik (2017, published 2021). Convergence of the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point under the 1:2:3 scaling was subsequently established by Quastel–Sarkar (arXiv:2008.06584) for a class of initial data (continuous functions of at most linear growth plus finitely many narrow wedges), and independently/related results by Virág and by Wu use the directed landscape. Thus the strong universality problem for the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation has been substantially solved for broad classes of initial data, with the limit identified as the KPZ fixed point / directed landscape; full universality for the most general initial data and complete process-level statements remain an active area, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation
$$\partial_t h(t,x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 h(t,x) + \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x h(t,x))^2 + \xi(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\xi$ is a space-time white noise on $\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R}$, and the nonlinearity is interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transform $h = \log Z$, with $Z$ solving the multiplicative stochastic heat equation $\partial_t Z = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 Z + Z\,\xi$.

For a fixed admissible initial condition (e.g. narrow wedge $h(0,\cdot) = -\tfrac{x^2}{2\varepsilon}$ in the $\varepsilon\to 0$ limit, flat, or stationary), and for any finite collection of distinct space-time points $(t_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_n,x_n)$ with $t_i>0$, develop an exact and tractable description of the joint probability distribution of the random vector
$$\bigl(h(t_1,x_1),\,h(t_2,x_2),\,\ldots,\,h(t_n,x_n)\bigr).$$

Specifically, obtain explicit formulas (for example, Fredholm determinant or contour-integral representations) for the multi-point joint distribution function
$$F_n(s_1,\ldots,s_n) = \mathbb{P}\bigl(h(t_1,x_1)\le s_1,\ldots,h(t_n,x_n)\le s_n\bigr),$$
suitable for asymptotic analysis as the points are scaled into the KPZ scaling limit, and use them to study the resulting multi-point correlation structure (in space, in time, and in space-time jointly), going beyond the previously known one-point statistics.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since 2017. The KPZ fixed point (Matetski–Quastel–Remenik) gives multi-point spatial distributions, and the directed landscape (Dauvergne–Ortmann–Virág) provides a full space-time scaling limit. Convergence of the narrow-wedge KPZ equation to the directed landscape has recently been established (Wu and others, 2023+), and explicit multi-time/multipoint Fredholm-determinant formulas for the KPZ fixed point with various initial conditions (including compactly supported ones) have been obtained as recently as 2024–2025. Multi-point analysis of the positive-temperature KPZ equation itself (not just the fixed point) is now accessible but a complete tractable theory at the level of one-point Tracy–Widom asymptotics remains under active development.

original_question: What physical parameters determine whether a radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy can form an efficient relativistic jet: is a large central black-hole mass required, or can the relatively small black-hole masses traditionally estimated for gamma-ray-emitting radio-loud NLSy1s, about 10^7–10^8 solar masses, still produce powerful jets?
self_contained_problem:
Active galactic nuclei (AGN) host supermassive black holes that can launch collimated relativistic outflows ("jets"). Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are a class of AGN identified by optical spectroscopic criteria (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km s⁻¹, weak [O III], strong Fe II), and a subset of them are radio-loud and have been detected in GeV gamma rays, indicating the presence of a powerful relativistic jet. Their central black-hole masses, estimated by virial methods from broad-line region kinematics, fall in the range M_BH ≈ 10⁷–10⁸ M_⊙, substantially smaller than the M_BH ≳ 10⁸–10⁹ M_⊙ inferred for blazars and jetted radio galaxies hosted in giant ellipticals.

Determine which physical parameters of the central engine control the formation of an efficient relativistic jet in radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies. In particular, decide whether a large black-hole mass (M_BH ≳ 10⁸–10⁹ M_⊙) is a necessary condition for launching a powerful relativistic jet, or whether the comparatively small masses M_BH ≈ 10⁷–10⁸ M_⊙ inferred for gamma-ray-emitting radio-loud NLSy1s are by themselves sufficient — possibly with other parameters (such as black-hole spin, accretion rate relative to Eddington, magnetic flux threading the horizon as in magnetically arrested disc states, or host-galaxy properties) playing the dominant role.
category_tag: Relativistic jets in active galactic nuclei
status_search_result: Recent reviews and observational studies (e.g., 2019 MDPI review on relativistic jets in gamma-ray NLSy1s, 2021 spectral-index map studies, and 2024–2025 papers on jet triggers) report that the physical parameters controlling jet formation in radio-loud NLSy1s remain under active debate. Some works argue that virial mass estimates underestimate M_BH (e.g., 1H 0323+342, PKS J1222+0413 ≈ 2×10⁸ M_⊙), while others emphasize black-hole spin, Eddington ratio, and magnetically arrested disc states. No consensus has emerged.

original_question: If corrected estimates place black-hole masses in radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies as high as 10^8–10^9 solar masses, including about 10^9 solar masses for PMN J0948+0022 and 2×10^8 solar masses for PKS 1502+036, how can such large black holes exist in galaxies that are thought to be spiral hosts?
self_contained_problem:
Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are a class of active galactic nuclei (AGN) characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) < 2000 km/s), strong Fe II multiplets, and weak [O III] emission. They are commonly believed to be hosted in spiral galaxies. A subset of radio-loud NLSy1s has been detected at γ-ray energies, indicating the presence of relativistic jets analogous to those in blazars. 

Standard virial estimates of the central black-hole (BH) masses in such NLSy1s typically yield values of order 10^6–10^8 M_⊙, but modelling of their optical/UV continuum with a standard Shakura–Sunyaev geometrically-thin, optically-thick accretion-disc spectrum can yield substantially larger masses: in particular, BH masses of approximately 10^9 M_⊙ for the source PMN J0948+0022 and 2 × 10^8 M_⊙ for PKS 1502+036 have been inferred.

Problem. Within the framework of galaxy–black-hole co-evolution and the standard M_BH–σ and M_BH–M_bulge scaling relations for spiral galaxies (whose bulges, particularly pseudo-bulges typical of late-type spirals, are generally associated with BH masses ≲ 10^8 M_⊙):

(a) Determine whether it is physically and statistically consistent with current knowledge of host-galaxy morphology, bulge-to-total ratios, and BH–host scaling relations for a spiral galaxy to harbour a central black hole of mass 10^8–10^9 M_⊙.

(b) Identify the mechanism(s) — e.g. major or minor mergers, secular evolution, misclassified host morphology (S0/elliptical rather than spiral), pseudo-bulge growth, or systematic biases/anisotropy corrections in the disc-fitting BH-mass estimators — that could account for the apparent presence of such massive black holes in radio-loud, γ-ray-emitting NLSy1s if these high mass estimates are correct.

State precisely under which assumptions (corrections for disc inclination, spin, accretion efficiency, host-galaxy classification) the tension is resolved or remains.
category_tag: Astrophysics: AGN host galaxies and black-hole masses
status_search_result: The question of how γ-ray-emitting radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies can host black holes of 10^8–10^9 M_⊙ while residing in spiral hosts remains an active and unresolved topic. Recent imaging studies (e.g. host-galaxy surveys of southern NLSy1s, 2023; PKS 2004-447 study, 2021) continue to debate host morphology, with some γ-ray NLSy1s showing evidence of disturbed or non-spiral hosts, mergers, or pseudo-bulges. Studies (e.g. 2019 ApJL "Are NLSy1s powered by low-mass black holes?") also question whether virial vs. accretion-disc mass estimates are systematically biased. No consensus resolution exists.

original_question: For last-passage percolation with general weights, can one prove the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling law, meaning time scale 3, spatial-correlation scale 2, and fluctuation scale 1 in the KPZ normalization?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\omega(i,j) : (i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge 0}\}$ be a family of i.i.d. real-valued random variables (the "weights") with a common distribution $F$ satisfying mild moment/regularity conditions (for instance, finite exponential moments and a non-degenerate continuous distribution). For $(m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge 0}$ define the last-passage time
$$T(m,n) \;=\; \max_{\pi : (0,0) \to (m,n)} \sum_{(i,j) \in \pi} \omega(i,j),$$
where the maximum runs over all up-right lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$. By Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem there exists a deterministic shape function $g$ with $T(\lfloor xN \rfloor, \lfloor yN \rfloor)/N \to g(x,y)$ a.s.

The conjectural Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) $3{:}2{:}1$ scaling law for this model asserts that, along a fixed direction $(x,y)$ with $x,y>0$:

(i) (fluctuation exponent $1/3$) There exist constants $c_1>0$ and a non-degenerate distribution $\mathcal{L}$ such that
$$\frac{T(\lfloor xN \rfloor,\lfloor yN \rfloor) - N\, g(x,y)}{c_1 N^{1/3}} \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathcal{L} \quad\text{as } N\to\infty;$$

(ii) (transversal exponent $2/3$) The maximizing path (geodesic) from $(0,0)$ to $(\lfloor xN \rfloor,\lfloor yN \rfloor)$ has typical transversal fluctuations of order $N^{2/3}$ around the straight line joining its endpoints;

(iii) (time exponent $1$) The time scale is linear, so that exponents $(1, 2/3, 1/3)$ — i.e. the $3{:}2{:}1$ ratio between time, space, and fluctuation scales — appear in the natural KPZ normalization.

Prove that this $3{:}2{:}1$ KPZ scaling holds for last-passage percolation with general weight distribution $F$ (subject only to mild non-degeneracy/moment assumptions), without using exact-solvability features specific to particular weight distributions such as the exponential or geometric ones.
status_search_result: Establishing the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling for last-passage percolation with general (non-integrable) weight distributions is widely regarded as a major open problem. Rigorous proofs of the 1/3 fluctuation and 2/3 transversal exponents currently exist only for exactly solvable models (e.g., exponential or geometric weights) via integrable-probability methods. Recent works (e.g., Ganguly–Hegde 2020 and follow-ups) obtain optimal tail exponents in general LPP under curvature/tail assumptions on the shape function, but the full scaling-limit statement for general weights remains unresolved.

original_question: For the longest increasing subsequence problem, can one prove KPZ-class fluctuation results when the permutation is sampled from distributions more general than the uniform distribution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and for a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ let $L(\pi)$ be the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\pi$, i.e. the largest $k$ such that there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k$ with $\pi(i_1)<\pi(i_2)<\dots<\pi(i_k)$.

When $\pi$ is sampled from the uniform distribution on $S_n$, it is known (Baik–Deift–Johansson) that
$$\frac{L(\pi)-2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}}\;\xrightarrow{d}\;F_{\mathrm{TW}_2},$$
where $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$ is the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution, placing the model in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class with characteristic fluctuation exponent $1/3$ (here $n^{1/6}=(\sqrt n)^{1/3}$) and limit law $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$.

Problem. Identify natural families of non-uniform probability distributions $\{\mu_n\}$ on $S_n$ (for instance Mallows measures with parameters $q=q_n$ in suitable regimes, or other inversion-weighted, descent-weighted, or pattern-restricted ensembles) for which the centered and rescaled longest increasing subsequence
$$\frac{L(\pi)-a_n}{b_n},\qquad \pi\sim\mu_n,$$
admits, with appropriate centering $a_n$ and scaling $b_n$ of order $n^{1/3}$ (up to slowly varying factors), a limiting distribution belonging to the KPZ universality class (e.g. the Tracy–Widom $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$ law). Prove a KPZ-class fluctuation theorem in such a setting, or characterize the regimes in which KPZ-type behavior holds versus crosses over to Gaussian or other limits.
category_tag: KPZ universality and longest increasing subsequences
status_search_result: For Mallows-distributed permutations, limit theorems for the longest increasing/decreasing subsequence have been established (Bhatnagar–Peled and others), but the limit is Gaussian rather than Tracy–Widom in the regime $0<q<1$ with $n(1-q)\to\infty$. KPZ-class (Tracy–Widom) fluctuations for the LIS have been rigorously established essentially only for the uniform distribution and a few closely related Schur-measure-type models; obtaining KPZ fluctuations for genuinely different non-uniform permutation ensembles remains largely open, though scaling-limit results (Dauvergne) further confirm KPZ behavior in the uniform case.

original_question: What are the host-galaxy morphologies of gamma-ray-emitting radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, and can their relativistic jets be explained by strong merger activity rather than ordinary spiral-galaxy evolution, given that only 1H 0323+342 has a clearly detected host and observations of it have been interpreted either as spiral arms or as merger residual structure?
self_contained_problem:
Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are active galactic nuclei characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II emission, and typically low-mass central black holes. A small subset of NLSy1 galaxies are radio-loud and have been detected at GeV energies, indicating the presence of relativistic jets pointed close to the line of sight. According to the conventional paradigm, powerful relativistic jets are launched almost exclusively by very massive black holes hosted in elliptical galaxies built up through major mergers, whereas NLSy1 galaxies are commonly believed to reside in disk/spiral hosts with pseudobulges.

Determine, on the basis of resolved imaging of the host galaxies of the currently known sample of γ-ray–detected radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies:

(a) The morphological classification (spiral/disk versus elliptical versus merger remnant or interacting system) of these hosts.

(b) Whether their relativistic jets can be plausibly attributed to ongoing or recent strong merger activity (rather than to ordinary secular evolution of a disk/spiral host), in particular for the nearest such object, whose imaging shows a feature that has been interpreted alternatively as a one-armed spiral or as a circumnuclear ring/merger residual.
status_search_result: Subsequent imaging studies of 1H 0323+342 (HST, 2014; deep optical, 2020) favor an asymmetric ring/merger-residual interpretation rather than a regular spiral arm, supporting the hypothesis that the relativistic jet is connected with a recent galaxy interaction. However, host-galaxy imaging of the broader sample of γ-ray–emitting radio-loud NLSy1s remains sparse, and a definitive, sample-wide morphological classification—and a confirmed merger origin for the jets—has not been established. The question is therefore partially answered for the prototype but remains open for the population.

paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
context_brief: Modified spin paradigm in spiral-host NLSy1s
original_question: Can the modified spin paradigm for relativistic jet production accommodate radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies if these systems are hosted by spiral galaxies: specifically, how can a central supermassive black hole in such a system acquire enough spin for efficient jet production when the paradigm associates high average spin and efficient spin-up with elliptical galaxies and major mergers?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are powered by accretion onto a central supermassive black hole (SMBH). A subclass of AGN known as narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies is characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II multiplets, and weak [O III] emission; these objects are believed to host SMBHs of comparatively low mass that accrete at high (near- or super-Eddington) rates, and they are typically found in late-type, spiral host galaxies. A small fraction of NLSy1s are radio-loud and have been detected as persistent γ-ray emitters, indicating the presence of a powerful, relativistically beamed jet pointed close to the line of sight.

The "modified spin paradigm" for relativistic jet production in AGN posits the following:
(1) The launching efficiency of a relativistic jet from an accreting SMBH depends primarily on the dimensionless spin a = Jc/(GM²) of the black hole, with the Blandford–Znajek-type extraction of rotational energy requiring high a.
(2) SMBHs in elliptical hosts on average carry large spins, because such galaxies have undergone at least one major merger that delivers a coherent, large-mass accretion event capable of efficiently spinning the hole up.
(3) SMBHs in spiral hosts on average carry low spins, because their growth histories are dominated by many small accretion episodes whose angular-momentum vectors are randomly oriented, producing cancellation rather than coherent spin-up.
Under (1)–(3), efficient relativistic jet formation should be confined to elliptical hosts.

Problem. Reconcile, within the framework above, the existence of γ-ray–detected, jetted radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies whose host galaxies are spiral (disk-dominated). Specifically, construct or identify a physically consistent mechanism by which a SMBH residing in a spiral host can attain and maintain a dimensionless spin a sufficiently close to the maximal Kerr value to power an observed relativistic jet, despite a merger and accretion history dominated by stochastic, small-mass events with randomly oriented angular momenta. Determine what additional ingredients (e.g., correlated phases of accretion, secular disk-fed coherent accretion, the role of black hole mass, alternative jet-launching channels not requiring near-maximal spin, or modifications to the statistics of spin evolution under chaotic accretion) must be added to the modified spin paradigm so that it is compatible with the observed population of jetted spiral-hosted NLSy1s.
category_tag: AGN jet production and black hole spin
status_search_result: Subsequent observational work has firmly established that a substantial population of jetted, γ-ray-emitting NLSy1 galaxies reside in disk/spiral hosts, which is generally taken to falsify the strict form of the modified spin paradigm tying jet launching to elliptical hosts and major mergers. On the theoretical side, recent modeling (e.g., hybrid Blandford–Znajek/Blandford–Payne jet-power analyses) shows that the observed jet powers can be reproduced with moderate-to-high spins attainable through coherent secular accretion in disk hosts, but no fully predictive replacement paradigm linking host morphology, accretion history, and spin distribution has been universally accepted, so the underlying question is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Can one explain the mechanism behind Tracy and Widom's solution of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with step initial data, and extend that method to more general initial data sets?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$: particles occupy sites of $\mathbb{Z}$ subject to the exclusion rule (at most one particle per site), and each particle independently attempts to jump one step to the right at rate $p$ and one step to the left at rate $q = 1 - p$, with $p \neq q$, executing a jump only if the target site is empty. For step initial data (sites $\{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ initially occupied and all other sites empty), Tracy and Widom derived exact contour-integral formulas for the distribution of the position of the $m$-th leftmost particle at time $t$ via a coordinate Bethe ansatz, leading after asymptotic analysis to Tracy–Widom GUE fluctuation limits for the current.

(a) Provide a conceptual explanation of why the Tracy–Widom method works: identify the structural mechanism (algebraic, combinatorial, or analytic) responsible for reducing the Bethe-ansatz sum over the symmetric group, applied to step initial data, to a Fredholm determinant amenable to asymptotic analysis.

(b) Using this mechanism, extend the Tracy–Widom solution method to a broader class of deterministic or random initial configurations on $\mathbb{Z}$ (beyond step and step-Bernoulli initial data) so as to obtain explicit, asymptotically tractable formulas for the distribution of particle positions and current fluctuations.
status_search_result: The Tracy–Widom coordinate Bethe ansatz approach to ASEP has, to date, produced asymptotic current fluctuation results only for step and step-Bernoulli initial data. A recognized limitation of the method is that it requires combinatorial guesswork to match a sum identity to the initial configuration, and no general mechanism extending the method to broader initial data has been established. The conceptual question of why the method "works" and how to extend it remains open.

original_question: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a general perturbation theory for KPZ-type interacting-particle systems and stochastic growth models that plays, for the integrable/exactly solvable models in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class, a role analogous to that of Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) theory for integrable Hamiltonian dynamical systems.

Concretely, the KPZ universality class consists of (1+1)-dimensional random growth processes (e.g. the asymmetric simple exclusion process, last-passage percolation with exponential or geometric weights, the q-TASEP, the log-gamma polymer, the KPZ equation itself, etc.) whose height function h(t,x) is conjectured to satisfy, in suitable scaling, h(t,x) ≈ v∞ t + t^{1/3} ξ(x t^{-2/3}), where ξ is a universal limiting field (e.g. the Airy_2 process). For a small but distinguished family of "exactly solvable" models, this scaling and the limiting distributions (Tracy–Widom GUE/GOE, Baik–Rains, etc.) have been rigorously established by means of exact algebraic identities (determinantal/Pfaffian structure, Bethe ansatz, Macdonald processes, stochastic vertex models, etc.).

The problem is the following. Construct a robust mathematical framework in which:

(a) one defines a notion of "integrability" for a stochastic interacting-particle / growth model that captures the algebraic structure used to obtain exact one-point and multi-point asymptotics in the solvable cases;

(b) given an exactly solvable model M_0 and a perturbation M_ε within a suitable class of local stochastic perturbations of its dynamics (with ε a small parameter), one proves that, for ε in some non-trivial set (possibly of positive measure, in analogy with the Cantor-like sets of KAM tori), the perturbed model M_ε retains enough of the integrable structure of M_0 to deduce KPZ-class scaling exponents (1/3, 2/3) and the same universal limiting distributions for its height function;

(c) the framework yields quantitative stability statements: explicit (and sharp in ε) bounds on the deformation of the integrable structure and on the convergence to the universal limit.

Equivalently, give a perturbative scheme that proves persistence of the KPZ scaling limit and of the asymptotic distributional invariants under small non-integrable perturbations of integrable stochastic growth models, in the same way that KAM theory proves persistence of invariant tori under small non-integrable perturbations of integrable Hamiltonian systems.
status_search_result: No general "KAM-type" perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-class models is known. Surveys and lecture notes on KPZ universality and integrable probability continue to describe universality beyond exactly solvable models as a major open conceptual challenge, with progress confined to specific solvable models and limited robustness results (e.g., comparison/coupling techniques, slow-decorrelation, and recent invariance results), but no systematic perturbative framework analogous to KAM has been established.

paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
context_brief: Rarity and evolutionary duration of radio-loud NLSy1s
original_question: Why is the fraction of radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies so small compared with radio-loud quasars, and is the rarity explained by only some NLSy1 galaxies experiencing high-accretion episodes that last long enough to spin up their central black holes?
self_contained_problem:
Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are a class of active galactic nuclei (AGN) characterized by narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) < 2000 km/s), a [O III]/Hβ ratio less than 3, and strong Fe II emission. They are typically powered by relatively low-mass central supermassive black holes (≈10^6–10^8 M_⊙) accreting near or above the Eddington limit. The radio-loudness of an AGN is conventionally defined as R = F_{5 GHz}/F_{4400 Å}, with sources called radio-loud if R > 10 and very radio-loud if R > 100.

Empirically, only a small fraction (≲7%) of NLSy1 galaxies are radio-loud, and only ≈2.5% have R > 100, whereas about 15% of optically selected quasars are radio-loud.

Provide a quantitative astrophysical explanation of the following:

(a) Why is the fraction of radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies substantially smaller than the radio-loud fraction among quasars?

(b) Test the hypothesis that this rarity is explained by the requirement that only those NLSy1 galaxies that undergo high-accretion episodes lasting long enough to spin up their central black holes (to a high dimensionless spin parameter a ≈ 1) become radio-loud. In particular, determine whether the observed black hole mass distributions, accretion histories, and spin distributions of radio-loud versus radio-quiet NLSy1 galaxies are consistent with this scenario, and identify what duration of sustained near-Eddington accretion would be required to produce the observed radio-loud fraction.
status_search_result: The question remains an open issue in AGN astrophysics. Recent reviews and studies (e.g., 2018 review on radio properties of NLSy1 galaxies and 2017 work on radio/gamma-ray-loud NLSy1s) continue to discuss the rarity of radio-loud NLSy1s and the possible role of black hole spin and prolonged accretion episodes, but no consensus quantitative explanation has been established. Individual sources show evidence of high spin (a > 0.6), supporting the spin-up hypothesis, yet population-level confirmation is still lacking.
