paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Why is the elliptic flow v2 of direct photons in heavy-ion collisions as large as the charged-particle v2 within sizeable experimental errors, and what theoretical ingredients are needed for hydrodynamic or radiation-rate models to reproduce it quantitatively?
self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (such as Au+Au at RHIC and Pb+Pb at the LHC), direct photons are real photons produced by the colliding system, defined as the inclusive photon yield with the photons coming from final-state hadronic decays subtracted. The elliptic flow coefficient v_2 of an emitted particle species is the second Fourier coefficient of its azimuthal distribution with respect to the event-plane angle Ψ_2:

  dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 v_2 cos(2(φ − Ψ_2)) + … .

Experimentally, the direct-photon v_2(p_T) measured in non-central A+A collisions is found, within sizeable error bars, to be comparable in magnitude to the v_2(p_T) of inclusive charged hadrons over a wide transverse-momentum range of roughly 1–4 GeV/c. Since direct photons are emitted throughout the entire space-time evolution of the fireball — including the early, hot stage when collective flow has not yet developed — naive thermal-emission plus hydrodynamic models predict a direct-photon v_2 substantially smaller than the hadronic v_2.

Problem. Provide a quantitative theoretical explanation of this "direct-photon v_2 puzzle." Specifically:

(a) Identify the physical ingredients (e.g. choice of QGP-to-hadron transition temperature T_c, pre-equilibrium photon emission, hadronic-phase emission rates, magnetic-field induced photon production, viscous corrections, glasma/initial-state contributions, or other mechanisms) that must be included in a hydrodynamic or photon-radiation-rate model so that the model simultaneously reproduces the measured direct-photon spectrum dN_γ/dp_T and the measured direct-photon v_2(p_T) in non-central A+A collisions.

(b) Demonstrate, within a consistent theoretical framework, that the resulting computed v_2^{γ_dir}(p_T) is of the same order as the inclusive charged-hadron v_2(p_T) for p_T in the range 1–4 GeV/c, while keeping the direct-photon yield consistent with measurements.
category_tag: Direct photon elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions
status_search_result: The direct-photon v_2 puzzle remains an active and unresolved problem as of 2024. While several mechanisms (magnetic-field induced photon emission, EPOS3-based hydrodynamic evolution, integrated hydrokinetic models, two-gluon-one-photon vertex contributions) have been shown to improve agreement with data, no single framework has yet produced a fully accepted, quantitative simultaneous description of the direct-photon spectrum and v_2. Recent papers (e.g. arXiv:2403.13599, arXiv:2311.03929) continue to propose new ingredients, indicating the puzzle is still open.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is aabaacbaab 3-D0L-avoidable (i.e. is there a ternary morphism g such that g ω (a) avoids aabaacbaab)?
self_contained_problem:
Setting and definitions. Let $\Sigma_3=\{a,b,c\}$ be a three-letter alphabet and let $\Sigma_3^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma_3$. A morphism is a map $g:\Sigma_3^*\to\Sigma_3^*$ satisfying $g(uv)=g(u)g(v)$ for all words $u,v$. A morphism $g$ is called prolongable on the letter $a$ if $g(a)=a w$ for some non-empty word $w\in\Sigma_3^*$ such that $g^n(w)\neq\varepsilon$ for every $n\geq 0$; in that case the iterates $g^n(a)$ form a sequence of words each a prefix of the next, and their limit is a well-defined infinite word denoted $g^{\omega}(a)$. An infinite word $w\in\Sigma_3^{\mathbb N}$ is said to avoid a finite word $p$ if no factor (contiguous subword) of $w$ equals $p$.

Question. Does there exist a morphism $g:\Sigma_3^*\to\Sigma_3^*$, prolongable on $a$, such that the infinite word $g^{\omega}(a)$ contains no occurrence of the factor
$$aabaacbaab\,?$$
Equivalently: is the word $aabaacbaab$ avoidable by an infinite ternary D0L word (a pure morphic word over a 3-letter alphabet)?
status_search_result: Web search located the question on Ochem's "interesting ternary formulas" list, where it is recorded among open avoidability questions. No publication was found explicitly resolving whether aabaacbaab admits an avoiding ternary pure-morphic (D0L) word, so the current status could not be verified.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Can J/ψ regeneration during hadronisation be established quantitatively as evidence for deconfinement and colour conductivity by measuring the total charm cross section, finding a second unambiguous heavy-quark recombination channel such as Bc production, and excluding final-state hadronic D + D recombination into J/ψ + X?
self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the QCD vacuum is expected to undergo a transition to a deconfined phase (the quark–gluon plasma), in which coloured partons can propagate over distances much larger than the deconfinement scale. One proposed signature of this colour conductivity is the regeneration of the charmonium ground state J/ψ during hadronisation: charm and anti-charm quarks produced in independent initial hard parton scatterings travel through the deconfined medium and recombine at hadronisation to form J/ψ mesons. Experimentally, the nuclear modification factor R_AA(J/ψ) at LHC energies, together with its transverse-momentum and centrality dependence, has been argued to display features consistent with such regeneration.

Establish—or refute—J/ψ regeneration during hadronisation as a quantitative, unambiguous signature of deconfinement and colour conductivity by simultaneously achieving the following:

(a) Determine the total charm production cross section in heavy-ion collisions at LHC energies with sufficient precision to serve as a quantitative input to regeneration calculations, and demonstrate quantitative agreement between such calculations and the measured J/ψ yields, R_AA, transverse-momentum spectra, and elliptic flow.

(b) Identify and measure a second, unambiguous heavy-quark recombination channel from independently produced heavy quarks—canonically the production of B_c mesons (b-cbar bound states) formed by recombination of independently produced b and c quarks—and verify that its yield in heavy-ion relative to pp collisions is enhanced in a manner consistent with parton-level recombination in a deconfined medium.

(c) Conclusively exclude the alternative scenario in which the observed J/ψ enhancement is generated by final-state hadron-level recombination D + D̄ → J/ψ + X, rather than by parton-level coalescence of deconfined charm quarks.

Provide a rigorous quantitative framework that incorporates (a)–(c) and decides whether J/ψ regeneration constitutes evidence for deconfinement and colour conductivity.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made since 2017. LHC Run 2 measurements (larger R_AA at midrapidity, low-pT enhancement, sizeable J/ψ elliptic flow) strongly support the regeneration picture, and B_c enhancement in Pb–Pb collisions has begun to be reported as an additional recombination signature. However, a precise total charm cross section in Pb–Pb, fully quantitative regeneration agreement, and conclusive exclusion of hadron-level D+D̄ → J/ψ+X recombination remain works in progress, so the question is partially—but not fully—resolved.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Explore the applications of the probabilistic method in the scope of pattern avoidance.
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the free monoid of finite words over A. A pattern is a nonempty word p over an alphabet of variables E = {x_1, x_2, ...}. A word w in A* is said to encounter the pattern p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h: E* -> A* (i.e. h(x_i) is a nonempty word for each variable x_i appearing in p) such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p. The pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exist infinitely many words over an alphabet of size k that avoid p, and the avoidability index λ(p) is the least such k (or ∞ if no such k exists).

Develop and apply probabilistic techniques (for instance, the Lovász Local Lemma, the entropy compression method, and related random constructions) to obtain results in the theory of pattern avoidance over finite alphabets. Concretely, address problems of the following types:

(a) Establish general upper bounds on the avoidability index λ(p) as a function of structural parameters of p (length, number of variables, number of occurrences of each variable).

(b) For a given pattern p (or class of patterns), determine, via probabilistic arguments, the smallest alphabet size k for which the number of words of length n over an alphabet of size k avoiding p grows exponentially in n, and provide explicit lower bounds on the corresponding growth rate.

(c) Give probabilistic proofs of avoidability for specific open instances, such as long doubled patterns, formulas, and patterns with bounded variable multiplicities, improving on existing constructive bounds.

State precise theorems (with hypotheses and quantitative conclusions) realizing the probabilistic method in the context above.
status_search_result: The question is a broad research program rather than a single precise statement, and remains an active area. The probabilistic method (especially the Lovász Local Lemma and entropy compression introduced by Moser–Tardos and adapted by Grytczuk and others) has yielded results on pattern avoidance and nonrepetitive sequences, but many specific avoidability questions remain open and the program of systematically applying probabilistic tools to pattern avoidance is ongoing.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Why do measured elliptic-flow signals of photons and heavy flavours in heavy-ion collisions tend to be larger than hydrodynamic calculations predict, and what does resolving this discrepancy imply for the space-time evolution and transport properties of the strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma?
self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (e.g., Au+Au at RHIC and Pb+Pb at the LHC), the produced strongly coupled quark–gluon plasma (sQGP) is commonly modeled by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics characterized by transport coefficients such as shear viscosity to entropy density ratio η/s and bulk viscosity ζ/s, together with an initial-state energy-density profile and a freeze-out/decoupling prescription. For an azimuthal particle distribution dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_n v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)], the elliptic flow coefficient is v_2.

Experimentally, the elliptic flow v_2(p_T) of (i) direct photons and (ii) heavy-flavour hadrons (containing charm or beauty quarks) is observed to be systematically larger than the values obtained from state-of-the-art hydrodynamic (and hydrodynamic + transport) calculations that simultaneously reproduce the corresponding p_T spectra and the bulk hadronic v_2.

Provide a quantitative theoretical mechanism that resolves both discrepancies simultaneously — i.e., a modification of the space-time evolution (initial conditions, pre-equilibrium dynamics, emission rates, electromagnetic fields, hadronization, or freeze-out) and/or of the QGP transport properties (η/s(T), ζ/s(T), heavy-quark spatial diffusion coefficient 2πT D_s, photon emission rates) such that:

1. The computed direct-photon v_2(p_T) and yield agree with measurements over the relevant p_T range.
2. The computed heavy-flavour (D-meson, non-prompt J/ψ, heavy-flavour electrons/muons) v_2(p_T) agrees with measurements while preserving the description of nuclear modification factor R_AA.
3. Bulk soft-hadron observables (spectra and v_n, n=2,3,4) remain described.

Determine and justify the implications of such a resolution for: the early-time (pre-equilibrium) photon and heavy-quark production; the temperature dependence of η/s and ζ/s; the heavy-quark diffusion coefficient near T_c; and the magnitude/lifetime of electromagnetic fields in the medium.
status_search_result: The direct-photon v_2 puzzle (and the related heavy-flavour v_2 tension) remains an active open problem. Multiple partial resolutions have been proposed through 2024 — including additional photon emission from late hadronic stages, pre-equilibrium contributions, magnetic-field-induced photon radiation (suggesting B ~ 10^16 G), hydrokinetic models, and EPOS3-based evolutions — but no single framework has been established that simultaneously reproduces photon spectra, photon v_2, heavy-flavour v_2 and R_AA, and bulk observables. Hence the question is best classified as open / partially addressed.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: If p is k-avoidable that a k-letter circular word of length |p| avoiding p exist.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A_k = \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$ be a $k$-letter alphabet, and let $E$ be a separate alphabet of pattern variables. A pattern is a word $p \in E^+$. A word $w \in A_k^*$ is said to encounter $p$ if there exists a non-erasing morphism $h : E^* \to A_k^*$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The pattern $p$ is called $k$-avoidable if there exist arbitrarily long words over $A_k$ that avoid $p$ (equivalently, an infinite word over $A_k$ avoiding $p$).

A circular word of length $n$ over $A_k$ is an equivalence class of words in $A_k^n$ under cyclic rotation; equivalently, it is a word arranged on a cycle. A factor of a circular word is any word read consecutively along the cycle (wrapping around is allowed). A circular word avoids $p$ if none of its factors encounters $p$.

Let $|p|$ denote the length of $p$ as a word over $E$.

Prove or disprove: For every pattern $p$ and every integer $k \geq 1$, if $p$ is $k$-avoidable, then there exists a circular word of length $|p|$ over the $k$-letter alphabet $A_k$ that avoids $p$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific conjecture relating $k$-avoidability of a pattern $p$ to the existence of a $k$-ary circular word of length $|p|$ avoiding $p$. Related work on circular words avoiding patterns and circular repetition thresholds exists (e.g., circular repetition threshold conjectures of Gorbunova, Currie and collaborators; results on circular words avoiding $7/3^+$-powers), but no source directly confirms or refutes the stated conjecture, so its status is treated as unknown.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: In ultra-central heavy-ion collisions with centrality below 1%, why are the second- and third-harmonic flow coefficients v2 and v3 observed to be about the same even though fluctuation-dominated initial eccentricities are expected to satisfy ε2 ≈ ε3 and positive shear viscosity should damp v3 more strongly than v2?
self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (e.g., Pb+Pb at LHC energies), define the azimuthal anisotropy flow coefficients $v_n$ as the Fourier coefficients of the final-state single-particle azimuthal distribution,
$$\frac{dN}{d\phi} \propto 1 + 2\sum_{n\ge 1} v_n \cos\bigl(n(\phi-\Psi_n)\bigr),$$
and the initial-state eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ as
$$\varepsilon_n = \frac{|\langle r^n e^{in\phi}\rangle|}{\langle r^n\rangle},$$
averaged with the initial energy- (or entropy-) density profile in the transverse plane.

For ultra-central collisions (centrality below 1%, where the impact parameter is essentially zero and the geometry is dominated by event-by-event fluctuations), one expects $\varepsilon_2 \approx \varepsilon_3$. Standard relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with positive shear viscosity to entropy density ratio $\eta/s>0$ predicts that the response to higher harmonics is more strongly damped, so $v_3 < v_2$ should follow.

However, experimental data show $v_2 \approx v_3$ in this ultra-central regime.

Problem: Provide a mechanism, model, or set of physical parameters within the framework of relativistic heavy-ion modeling (initial conditions plus viscous hydrodynamic evolution and freeze-out) that quantitatively reconciles the measured $v_2$ and $v_3$ in ultra-central collisions (< 1% centrality) with theoretical expectations, simultaneously reproducing the observed ratios for other centrality classes and other harmonics.
status_search_result: The ultra-central v2/v3 puzzle remains an active area of research. Hydrodynamic fluctuations alone have been shown to be qualitatively helpful but quantitatively insufficient (2023). More recent works (2024–2025) propose modifications of initial-state nuclear and sub-nucleon structure (e.g., minimum nucleon separation, enhanced sub-nucleon fluctuations) and anisotropy scaling functions that substantially improve agreement with data, indicating partial resolution but not a definitive consensus solution.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k ≤ 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [24]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_q$ be an alphabet of $q \ge 2$ letters. For a rational number $k > 1$, a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ over $\Sigma_q$ is said to contain a $k$-power if it has a (contiguous) factor of the form $u^{(k)}$, meaning a factor of length $\lfloor k|u|\rfloor$ that is a prefix of the infinite word $uuu\cdots$ for some nonempty word $u$; the word $w$ is $k$-power-free if it contains no $k$-power. Let $L_q(k,n)$ denote the number of $k$-power-free words of length $n$ over $\Sigma_q$, and define the language $L_q(k) = \bigcup_n L_q(k,n)$.

For binary alphabets ($q=2$) the following is known: there is a threshold $k^*_2 = 7/3$ such that $|L_2(k,n)|$ grows only polynomially in $n$ when $k \le 7/3$, while $|L_2(k,n)|$ grows exponentially in $n$ when $k > 7/3$.

Determine, for each integer $q \ge 3$, the analogous polynomial/exponential growth dichotomy: identify a threshold $k^*_q$ (and corresponding $k^+$ refinement) such that $|L_q(k,n)|$ grows polynomially in $n$ for $k \le k^*_q$ and exponentially for $k > k^*_q$. Establish the growth rate function $\alpha(q,k) = \limsup_{n\to\infty} |L_q(k,n)|^{1/n}$ and characterize precisely the values of $k$ at which the transition from polynomial growth ($\alpha = 1$) to exponential growth ($\alpha > 1$) occurs over an alphabet of size $q$.
status_search_result: The problem has been the subject of substantial progress. The "exponential conjecture" of Shur predicts that for alphabets of size $q \ge 3$, every infinite power-free language has exponential growth, and asymptotic formulas for the growth rates $\alpha(q,k)$ have been established for $k \ge 2$ and partially for $k < 2$. A 2025 paper (MFCS 2025) proves Shur's conjecture on the asymptotic growth rates of $(n/(n-1))$-free and $(n/(n-1))^+$-free languages over large alphabets up to corrections of order $O(1/q^2)$. However, a complete characterization of the polynomial/exponential threshold for every alphabet size $q \ge 3$ analogous to the precise $7/3$ threshold for $q=2$ does not appear to be fully resolved in all regimes.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: What response, if any, does a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma produce after a jet deposits concentrated local energy, and can high-statistics measurements, especially γ-jet measurements and new detector data, identify medium responses such as a Mach cone or collective wake?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an energetic parton (a "jet") propagating through a strongly coupled quark–gluon plasma (QGP) — the deconfined state of QCD matter produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions — and depositing concentrated local energy and momentum into the medium along its trajectory. Because the jet moves faster than the speed of sound in the QGP, hydrodynamic considerations predict that the deposited energy could excite collective medium responses such as a Mach cone (a conical shock wave) and an accompanying diffusion wake (a depletion of soft hadrons in the direction opposite to the jet).

Problem: Determine, on the basis of experimental observables in heavy-ion collisions:
(a) Whether the QGP exhibits a non-trivial collective response to the localized energy deposition of a jet, and if so, characterize its structure (e.g., Mach cone, diffusion wake, or other collective excitation).
(b) Identify which observables — in particular the "golden" γ-jet channel (where a prompt photon tags the original parton energy) and high-statistics jet–hadron correlations from new and upgraded detectors — can unambiguously isolate such medium-response signatures from background.
(c) Using these measurements, establish the temperature dependence of the partonic stopping power (jet quenching parameter) between RHIC and LHC energies, and extract its dependence on parton type, parton energy, and in-medium path length.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: theoretical frameworks (coupled linear Boltzmann transport + hydrodynamics) predict a Mach-cone-like response and an accompanying diffusion wake, with proposals to detect a double-peak rapidity structure in γ/Z-tagged jets. Experimental hints of jet-induced medium response have been reported, and sPHENIX began taking physics-quality Au+Au data in 2024 to deliver high-statistics γ-jet measurements. However, an unambiguous experimental confirmation of the Mach cone / diffusion wake and a definitive mapping of the temperature, parton-type, energy, and path-length dependence of stopping power remain outstanding.

original_question: Let Σ be an alphabet and let w ∈ Σ∗ a p-free word. Then w is a factor of a maximal p-free word over Σ.
self_contained_problem:

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
context_brief: Origin of collectivity in small systems
original_question: Are long-range near-side ridge correlations and collective multi-particle flow signals in high-multiplicity proton-proton, proton-nucleus, deuteron-nucleus, and helium-nucleus collisions generated primarily by initial-state Colour Glass Condensate quantum correlations or by final-state interactions that create hydrodynamic collective flow?
self_contained_problem:
In high-energy hadronic and nuclear collisions, two-particle azimuthal correlations measured at large pseudorapidity separation reveal a long-range "near-side ridge", and the n-th order azimuthal anisotropy coefficients v_n (extracted from the Fourier decomposition dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_n v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)]) can be obtained both from two-particle cumulants and from multi-particle cumulants v_n{2k} for k ≥ 2. In high-multiplicity events of small collision systems — proton–proton (pp), proton–nucleus (pA), deuteron–nucleus (dA), and helium-3–nucleus (³HeA) — these observables exhibit features traditionally associated with collective hydrodynamic flow in heavy-ion (AA) collisions, including the approximate equality v_n{4} ≈ v_n{6} ≈ v_n{8} for the second harmonic, and a v_2, v_3 hierarchy controlled by the geometry of the projectile.

Two competing theoretical paradigms are proposed to explain these observations:
(i) Initial-state quantum correlations among gluons in the wavefunctions of the colliding hadrons/nuclei, as described by the Colour Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory of high-energy QCD, generating azimuthal correlations without any final-state collective evolution; and
(ii) Final-state interactions among produced partons or hadrons that drive the system toward local equilibration and produce collective anisotropic flow described by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics applied to the small fireball, translating the spatial geometry (eccentricities ε_n) of the initial overlap region into momentum-space anisotropies v_n.

Determine which of these two mechanisms is the primary origin of the observed long-range near-side ridge correlations and the multi-particle collective flow signals (in particular the harmonics v_2, v_3, …, and their cumulants) measured in high-multiplicity pp, pA, dA, and ³HeA collisions: are they generated principally by initial-state CGC quantum correlations, by final-state hydrodynamic collective flow, or by a quantitatively specified combination of the two?
category_tag: QCD collectivity in small collision systems
status_search_result: Recent reviews and conference proceedings (2022–2024), including a "Decade of Collectivity in Small Systems" review and CERN workshops on light-ion collisions at the LHC, indicate that the origin of collectivity in pp/pA/dA/³HeA systems remains an open and actively debated question. While experimental evidence (e.g., RHIC d+Au and ³He+Au geometry-scan results, multi-particle cumulant relations) strongly favors a hydrodynamic interpretation, CGC-based initial-state models with refinements (e.g., glasma + Lund fragmentation) continue to offer competing or complementary descriptions, and a definitive resolution has not been reached.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Let Σ be an alphabet, k ∈ [1, 2], and w ∈ Σ∗ be a k-power-free word. Then in any case, w is a factor of a maximal k-power-free word over Σ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^{*}$ denote the set of all finite words over $\Sigma$. For a real number $k\ge 1$, a finite word $w\in\Sigma^{*}$ is called a $k$-power if it can be written as $w=u^{\lfloor k\rfloor}u'$, where $u'$ is a prefix of $u$ and $|w|=k\,|u|$ (so for integer $k$ this means $w=u^{k}$). A word $v\in\Sigma^{*}$ is $k$-power-free if no factor (contiguous subword) of $v$ is a $k$-power. A $k$-power-free word $v\in\Sigma^{*}$ is called maximal if for every letter $a\in\Sigma$ both $av$ and $va$ contain a $k$-power as a factor (equivalently, $v$ cannot be extended on either side, by a single letter, while remaining $k$-power-free).

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every finite alphabet $\Sigma$, every real number $k\in[1,2]$, and every $k$-power-free word $w\in\Sigma^{*}$, there exists a maximal $k$-power-free word over $\Sigma$ that contains $w$ as a factor.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific embedding-into-maximal-k-power-free-word conjecture for k ∈ [1,2]. Related extendability questions for power-free words (e.g., the Restivo–Salemi problems and transition-property results for α-power-free languages) have been studied and partially resolved, but no source clearly confirms or refutes the precise statement above.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Can microscopic transport models describe both large dense nucleus-nucleus systems and small dilute systems, as well as the transition between them, well enough to explain the actual dynamics behind collective correlations, particle spectra, and particle ratios?
self_contained_problem:
Consider microscopic transport models of relativistic nuclear collisions (for example, parton/hadron cascade frameworks such as AMPT-type models) which evolve a many-body system of partons and/or hadrons via classical transport equations with a chosen set of cross sections, mean fields, and hadronization prescriptions. Such models are applied across a wide range of colliding systems, from large and dense systems (heavy nucleus–nucleus collisions, e.g. Au+Au, Pb+Pb) producing thousands of final-state particles, to small and dilute systems (proton–nucleus and high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions) producing only tens to hundreds of particles, as well as the smooth transition between these regimes as a function of system size and multiplicity.

Determine whether a single microscopic transport description, with a fixed and physically motivated set of inputs, can simultaneously and quantitatively reproduce, across all of these regimes:

(i) collective azimuthal correlation observables, including the Fourier flow coefficients v_n (n = 2, 3, 4, ...) and their multi-particle cumulants v_n{2}, v_n{4}, ... as functions of transverse momentum, pseudorapidity, and centrality/multiplicity;

(ii) single-particle transverse-momentum spectra dN/dp_T for identified hadrons; and

(iii) integrated and p_T-differential particle yield ratios (e.g. K/π, p/π, Λ/K, Ξ/π, Ω/π).

If such a unified description is achievable, identify the underlying microscopic dynamical mechanism (e.g. partonic rescattering, hadronic rescattering, string-melting, mean-field interactions) responsible for generating the observed collectivity in both large and small systems and for governing the transition between them. If not, characterize the obstructions to a unified transport description.
category_tag: Relativistic transport models in heavy-ion collisions
status_search_result: Recent reviews of small-system collectivity and transport modeling indicate that while transport codes such as AMPT reproduce many flow observables across system sizes, a unified, simultaneously quantitative description of flow, p_T spectra, and particle ratios from large to small systems remains unresolved, with ongoing debate about partonic vs. hadronic origins of collectivity in small systems.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Does a given word generate a finite or infinite subtree?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 2 and a finite alphabet Σ. A finite word w ∈ Σ* is called k-th power-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form u^k = uu…u (k copies). Let L_k(Σ) denote the language of all k-th power-free words over Σ.

Order L_k(Σ) by the prefix relation: u ≤ v iff u is a prefix of v. The Hasse diagram of (L_k(Σ), ≤) is a rooted tree T (rooted at the empty word) in which every node v has, as children, all words va with a ∈ Σ that still belong to L_k(Σ). For each w ∈ L_k(Σ), let T(w) denote the subtree of T rooted at w, that is, the set of all k-th power-free words having w as a prefix, with the induced prefix order.

Problem. Provide an algorithm that, given as input the integer k ≥ 2, the finite alphabet Σ, and a word w ∈ L_k(Σ), decides whether the subtree T(w) is finite or infinite. Equivalently, decide whether w admits arbitrarily long k-th power-free extensions in Σ*.

(More generally, the same question is posed for any "repetition-free" language defined by avoidance of a fixed set of patterns or fractional powers, viewed as a prefix poset whose Hasse diagram is a tree.)
status_search_result: The question, posed by Petrova and Shur at WORDS, has been shown decidable for certain power-free languages (e.g., specific k and alphabet sizes), and partial structural results are known (every subtree generated by a single word has at least one leaf for k-th power-free languages). A general decision procedure covering all repetition-free languages does not appear to be established, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Is the physics underlying soft collective signals and apparently hadronisation the same in all high-energy reactions, from electron-positron events through proton-proton and proton-nucleus reactions to central nucleus-nucleus collisions, perhaps as a generic property of strongly interacting many-body systems with two or more particles?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of high-energy particle collision processes, ranging from electron–positron annihilation events, through proton–proton and proton–nucleus collisions, to central nucleus–nucleus collisions. In each such process one observes "soft" final-state phenomena, including:

(i) collective azimuthal anisotropies of produced hadrons (e.g. long-range angular correlations and flow-like coefficients vₙ),
(ii) strangeness enhancement and modifications of identified-hadron yield ratios with event multiplicity, and
(iii) the hadronisation step by which colored partons are converted into observed color-singlet hadrons.

Determine whether there exists a single underlying dynamical mechanism — characterising strongly interacting many-body systems with N ≥ 2 constituents — that governs these soft collective signals (including hadronisation) uniformly across all of the above reaction types, with the differences between systems being merely quantitative (driven by the size and density of the produced system) rather than qualitative. Equivalently: is the soft-collectivity/hadronisation physics universal across e⁺e⁻, pp, pA, and AA collisions, manifesting as a generic property of strongly interacting many-body systems and being merely more prominent in AA than in pp?
status_search_result: Recent reviews and studies (2024) such as "A Decade of Collectivity in Small Systems" and "Hadronization in small and large systems" continue to investigate whether soft collectivity and hadronisation share a common origin from pp through AA. Evidence for collective flow, strangeness enhancement, and recombination-like baryon-to-meson behavior in small systems supports a partial unification, but reviews explicitly note that hadronisation is not yet established as universal and the question remains an active area of debate.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Which square-free words u can be shuffled to obtain a square-free word u ▷β u?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w\in\Sigma^*$ is called a square if $w=xx$ for some nonempty $x\in\Sigma^*$, and $w$ is called square-free if no nonempty factor (contiguous subword) of $w$ is a square.

Given two words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$, a shuffle of $u$ and $v$ is any word obtained by interleaving the letters of $u$ and $v$ while preserving the relative order of letters within each of $u$ and $v$. Equivalently, if $u=u_1u_2\cdots u_m$ and $v=v_1v_2\cdots v_n$, a shuffle is determined by a binary sequence $\beta\in\{0,1\}^{m+n}$ with exactly $m$ zeros and $n$ ones, telling at each position whether to take the next letter from $u$ or from $v$; the resulting shuffle is denoted $u\triangleright_\beta v$.

Problem. Characterize the square-free words $u\in\Sigma^*$ for which there exists a shuffle parameter $\beta\in\{0,1\}^{2|u|}$ (with $|u|$ zeros and $|u|$ ones) such that the self-shuffle $u\triangleright_\beta u$ is again a square-free word.
status_search_result: The problem of which square-free words admit a square-free self-shuffle has received partial answers but no complete characterization. Harju (2013–2015) showed that for every n ≥ 3 there exists a ternary square-free word of length n that can be shuffled with itself to give a square-free word, and Currie–Saari and others established the existence of infinite square-free self-shuffling words. However, a complete classification of which square-free words u admit such a shuffle does not appear to have been obtained.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
context_brief: Critical point at high baryon density
original_question: Does the QCD phase diagram contain a critical point and a first-order phase transition at high baryon density, and can beam-energy scans and low-energy heavy-ion programs locate them through matter properties at large baryochemical potential?
self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the phase diagram of strongly interacting matter is commonly drawn in the plane of temperature $T$ versus baryochemical potential $\mu_B$. At $\mu_B = 0$, lattice QCD has established that the transition between hadronic matter and the quark–gluon plasma is a smooth analytic crossover. Several effective-theory and model calculations conjecture that, as $\mu_B$ is increased, the crossover line terminates at a second-order critical endpoint, beyond which (at larger $\mu_B$) the transition becomes first order.

(a) Determine whether the QCD phase diagram contains such a critical endpoint and a first-order deconfinement/chiral phase transition at large baryochemical potential, and if so, determine its location $(T_c, \mu_B^c)$.

(b) Decide whether observables accessible in heavy-ion collisions at low center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ (corresponding to large $\mu_B$) — for instance higher-order cumulants of conserved charges (net-baryon, net-electric-charge, net-strangeness distributions), light-nuclei yield ratios, and other fluctuation/correlation measures — can unambiguously locate the critical endpoint and the first-order phase boundary through a beam-energy scan and an energy–volume mapping of bulk matter properties at large $\mu_B$.
category_tag: QCD phase diagram and critical point
status_search_result: The existence and location of a QCD critical point at large baryochemical potential remain open as of 2025–2026. The STAR Beam Energy Scan Phase II (BES-II) at RHIC has produced high-statistics data over √s_NN = 3–27 GeV (μ_B ≈ 200–700 MeV), ruling out a critical point in the region probed by top RHIC and LHC energies but leaving the low-energy / high-μ_B region inconclusive. Future programs (STAR fixed-target, CBM at FAIR, MPD at NICA) are designed to settle the question.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Which words w can be obtained in more than one way from a single word u using different conducting sequences?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $u = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n \in \Sigma^*$ be a finite word. Consider two disjoint copies of $u$, written with positions $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ for the first copy and $\{1',2',\dots,n'\}$ for the second copy. A conducting sequence for $u$ is a word $c \in \{1,2\}^{2n}$ that contains exactly $n$ occurrences of the symbol $1$ and exactly $n$ occurrences of the symbol $2$. Such a conducting sequence determines a shuffle of $u$ with itself: read the $2n$ symbols of $c$ from left to right and, on the $k$-th occurrence of the symbol $i \in \{1,2\}$, output the letter $u_k$ taken from the $i$-th copy of $u$. The resulting word $w \in \Sigma^{2n}$ is said to be obtained from $u$ via the conducting sequence $c$. Equivalently, $w$ lies in the shuffle product $u \shuffle u$.

Characterize all pairs $(u, w)$ with $u \in \Sigma^*$ and $w \in u \shuffle u$ such that there exist two distinct conducting sequences $c \neq c'$ in $\{1,2\}^{2n}$ both producing the same word $w$ from $u$. In other words, describe the set of words $w$ that can be obtained from a single word $u$ in more than one way using different conducting sequences.
status_search_result: A web search located the broader literature on shuffled-square-free words (Currie, Guégan–Ochem, Harju, Müller, Buss–Soltys, Juge), with recent advances on the minimum alphabet size for infinite shuffled-square-free words and on the NP-completeness of recognizing shuffled-squares. However, no source was found that explicitly resolves the characterization of words $w$ obtainable from a single $u$ via two different conducting sequences, so the current status of this specific question could not be confirmed.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: What underlying dynamics makes thermalisation in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion and small-system collisions appear so fast, if thermalisation is really achieved, including in tiny or dilute systems where only a handful of particles may be present?
self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic collisions of hadrons and nuclei (ranging from electron–positron and proton–proton collisions to central nucleus–nucleus collisions), measured particle yields and momentum distributions are well described by thermal/statistical hadronization models and exhibit collective-flow patterns characteristic of a strongly interacting fluid. These features appear even in very small or dilute final states containing only a handful of produced particles, and on time scales that seem too short for conventional kinetic equilibration via 2→2 scatterings.

Identify and characterise the underlying microscopic dynamics responsible for the apparently rapid approach to (or appearance of) thermal behaviour in such systems. Specifically:

1. Determine whether genuine local thermal equilibrium is actually achieved in small/dilute collision systems, or whether the observed thermal-like spectra and statistical particle ratios arise from another mechanism (for example, quantum entanglement between observed and unobserved degrees of freedom in the incoming hadronic wave functions, hydrodynamic attractor behaviour far from equilibrium, eigenstate thermalisation, or maximum-entropy hadronisation constraints).

2. Provide a quantitative dynamical mechanism — within QCD or an effective theory thereof — that explains both (a) the short equilibration/isotropisation time scales inferred from hydrodynamic modelling of heavy-ion data and (b) the emergence of statistical particle ratios and collective flow signatures in systems with only a few produced particles.

3. Predict observables that would discriminate between true kinetic thermalisation and non-equilibrium origins of the statistical and collective patterns.
status_search_result: The mechanism behind apparently fast thermalisation in heavy-ion and small-system collisions remains an active research question. paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Does there exist an infinite square-free word w such that w = w ▷β w for some infinite β?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet. An infinite word over $\Sigma$ is square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form $xx$. Given two infinite words $u = u_1 u_2 u_3 \cdots$ and $v = v_1 v_2 v_3 \cdots$ over $\Sigma$ and an infinite binary sequence $\beta \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ with infinitely many $0$'s and infinitely many $1$'s, the shuffle $u \triangleright_\beta v$ is the unique infinite word obtained by reading $u_1, u_2, \ldots$ at positions where $\beta$ has a $0$ and $v_1, v_2, \ldots$ at positions where $\beta$ has a $1$. An infinite word $w$ is called self-shuffling if there exists an infinite $\beta$ such that $w = w \triangleright_\beta w$, i.e., $w$ admits a factorization $w = U_1 V_1 U_2 V_2 \cdots$ with $\prod_i U_i = \prod_i V_i = w$.

Question: Does there exist an infinite square-free word $w$ over some finite alphabet that is self-shuffling, i.e., $w = w \triangleright_\beta w$ for some infinite $\beta$?
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Harju, has been answered affirmatively. Charlier, Kamae, Puzynina, and Zamboni (arXiv:1401.6536, "Infinite square-free self-shuffling words") construct an infinite square-free word over a finite alphabet that is self-shuffling, establishing existence.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: If a pattern is not k-avoidable, but is (k + 1)-avoidable, what is the minimal frequency of a letter in an infinite word over k + 1 letters that avoids that pattern?
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. A pattern is a non-empty word $p$ over an alphabet of variables $V = \{X_1, X_2, \dots\}$. A word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$ is said to encounter the pattern $p$ if there exists a non-erasing morphism $h : V^* \to A^*$ (i.e., $h(X_i) \neq \varepsilon$ for every variable $X_i$) such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The pattern $p$ is called $k$-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over an alphabet of size $k$ that avoids $p$, and the avoidability index $\lambda(p)$ is the smallest such $k$ (and $\infty$ if no such $k$ exists).

Given an infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$ and a letter $a \in A$, the frequency of $a$ in $w$ is defined (when the limit exists) as
$$\mathrm{freq}_w(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{|w[1..n]|_a}{n},$$
where $|u|_a$ counts the occurrences of $a$ in $u$. For a pattern $p$ that is $(k+1)$-avoidable but not $k$-avoidable, define
$$\mu(p) = \inf_{w} \min_{a \in A} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{|w[1..n]|_a}{n},$$
where the infimum is over all infinite words $w$ on a $(k+1)$-letter alphabet $A$ that avoid $p$.

Problem. Determine $\mu(p)$ for patterns $p$ with $\lambda(p) = k+1$. In particular, for each such $p$, give the exact value (or sharp bounds) of the minimal possible frequency of a letter in an infinite word over $k+1$ letters that avoids $p$. As a concrete instance, evaluate $\mu(p)$ for the pattern $p = AB\,BC\,CA\,BA\,AC$ over variables $\{A,B,C\}$ (which is known to be $4$-avoidable but not $3$-avoidable): what is the minimal possible frequency of the fourth letter in an infinite word on four letters avoiding $p$?
status_search_result: The general question of the minimal letter frequency in infinite words over $(k+1)$ letters avoiding patterns of avoidability index $k+1$ remains open. Related results (e.g., asymptotic $1/n$ for $n$-th-power-free binary words by Ochem and others) address specific cases, and follow-up work on avoidability of formulas with two variables and on regularities in words discusses partial cases, but no general formula or solution to the question is reported.

original_question: We have FRT(4) = RT (4) = 7/5. Advances in problem solving The conjecture was solved by Golnaz Badkobeh, Maxime Crochemore and Michaël Rao. In addition they proved that FRT(k) = RT (k) for k ≤ 6 (private communication at WORDS 2015).
self_contained_problem:
For a finite word w, the exponent of w is |w|/p where p is its smallest period. For a real number r > 1 and an integer k ≥ 2, an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet is called r⁺-free if every finite factor has exponent strictly less than r. 

The repetition threshold RT(k) is defined as the infimum of all real numbers r ≥ 1 such that there exists an infinite r⁺-free word over a k-letter alphabet. The finite repetition threshold FRT(k) is defined as the infimum of all real numbers r ≥ 1 such that there exists an infinite r⁺-free word over a k-letter alphabet that contains only finitely many factors of exponent equal to r.

It is known that RT(k) ≤ FRT(k) for every k ≥ 2, and that RT(4) = 7/5.

Prove or disprove: FRT(4) = 7/5; that is, show that there exists an infinite word over a 4-letter alphabet that is (7/5)⁺-free and contains only finitely many factors of exponent exactly 7/5. More generally, determine whether FRT(k) = RT(k) for k ∈ {4, 5, 6}.
status_search_result: Badkobeh, Crochemore and Rao established FRT(4) = 7/5 by constructing an infinite Dejean word on a 4-letter alphabet with only two factors of exponent 7/5, published as "Finite repetition threshold for large alphabets" in RAIRO - Theoretical Informatics and Applications (2014). They also showed FRT(k) = RT(k) for k ≤ 6.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is it decidable, given a pattern p and an integer k, whether p is k-avoidable?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet of variables and let E be a separate finite alphabet of letters. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ A*. An occurrence of p in a word w ∈ E* is a factor of w of the form h(p), where h : A* → E* is a nonerasing morphism (i.e., h(a) is a nonempty word for every variable a ∈ A). A word w ∈ E* avoids p if no factor of w is an occurrence of p. For a positive integer k, the pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some alphabet of size k that avoids p; otherwise p is k-unavoidable. The avoidability index of p is the smallest k for which p is k-avoidable (and ∞ if p is unavoidable for every k).

Question: Is the following decision problem decidable? Given as input a pattern p ∈ A* and a positive integer k (in unary or binary), determine whether p is k-avoidable.
status_search_result: The decidability of determining, given a pattern p and an integer k, whether p is k-avoidable is widely cited as an open problem in combinatorics on words. There is no known algorithm to compute the avoidability index, and even for specific short patterns (e.g., ααββγγ) the exact avoidability index remains undetermined. Surveys and recent works on pattern avoidance continue to list the general decidability question as unresolved.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: What is the minimum exponent of a repetion which is avoidable by an infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix)-suffix duplication?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet. For a finite word $w \in \Sigma^*$, the suffix duplication operation produces a word of the form $w\cdot s$, where $s$ is a suffix of $w$; symmetrically, the prefix duplication operation produces $p\cdot w$ where $p$ is a prefix of $w$. Starting from a fixed seed letter (or finite seed word) and iteratively applying suffix duplications (resp. prefix-or-suffix duplications), one obtains, in the limit, an infinite word.

For a real number $\alpha > 1$, a word is said to contain an $\alpha$-power if it has a factor of the form $u^k v$, where $v$ is a prefix of $u$ and $(k|u| + |v|)/|u| \ge \alpha$; an infinite word avoids $\alpha$-powers if none of its factors is an $\alpha'$-power for any $\alpha' \ge \alpha$.

Determine the infimum, over all infinite words $\mathbf{w}$ obtainable by iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication starting from some finite seed over some finite alphabet, of the smallest real number $\alpha$ such that $\mathbf{w}$ avoids all repetitions of exponent strictly greater than $\alpha$. Equivalently: what is the minimum exponent of a repetition that is avoidable by an infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication?
status_search_result: Searches surface the foundational works on prefix-suffix duplication (Ito et al., "Prefix–suffix duplication") and bounded prefix-suffix duplication, which establish that iterated prefix-suffix square completion can produce infinite words avoiding repetitions of exponent greater than 2, but no source located gives a definitive value for the minimum avoidable repetition exponent under iterated (prefix-)suffix duplication. The status therefore appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Is there a pattern that is 6-avoidable but not 5-avoidable?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet of letters and E = {a, b, c, ...} a disjoint countable alphabet of variables. A pattern is a non-empty word p over E. The pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some alphabet A of size k that avoids p, and k-unavoidable otherwise. paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Does the language of finite words constructed, starting with a single word, by iterating prefix-suffix square completion remains semi-linear?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, define the prefix-suffix square completion relation $\Rightarrow$ on $\Sigma^*$ as follows: $w \Rightarrow w'$ if either
(i) $w = yxy \cdot u$ for some words $x \in \Sigma^*$, $y \in \Sigma^+$, $u \in \Sigma^*$, and $w' = x \cdot w$ (prefix square completion: prepend $x$ when $w$ begins with a factor $yxy$), or
(ii) $w = u \cdot yxy$ for some words $x \in \Sigma^*$, $y \in \Sigma^+$, $u \in \Sigma^*$, and $w' = w \cdot x$ (suffix square completion: append $x$ when $w$ ends with a factor $yxy$).

Equivalently, from $w$ one may produce a new word by appending (resp. prepending) a word $x$ whenever $w$ has a suffix (resp. prefix) of the form $yxy$ with $y$ nonempty.

Let $\Rightarrow^*$ denote the reflexive-transitive closure of $\Rightarrow$. For a word $w_0 \in \Sigma^*$, define
$$L(w_0) = \{ w \in \Sigma^* : w_0 \Rightarrow^* w \}.$$

A language $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ is called semi-linear if its image under the Parikh map (sending each word to its vector of letter counts) is a semi-linear subset of $\mathbb{N}^{|\Sigma|}$, i.e., a finite union of sets of the form $\{ v_0 + n_1 v_1 + \cdots + n_k v_k : n_i \in \mathbb{N} \}$.

Question: Is $L(w_0)$ semi-linear for every choice of finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and starting word $w_0 \in \Sigma^*$?
status_search_result: The prefix-suffix square completion operation was introduced and studied with related results on regularity of square-root languages and an algorithm for the membership problem. Related work on prefix-suffix duplication shows semilinearity in that setting, but I did not find a definitive published resolution of the semi-linearity question for iterated prefix-suffix square completion starting from a single word.

original_question: If a pattern is k-avoidable then it is k-HD0L-avoidable (i.e. are there morphisms f : Σ∗ −→ A∗ , g : Σ∗ −→ Σ∗ , with |Σ| = k such that f (g ω (a)) avoids p)?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the free monoid of finite words over A. A pattern is a word p over an alphabet E of "pattern variables" (disjoint from A). A word w ∈ A* is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : E* → A* such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p. An infinite word avoids p if every finite factor of it avoids p. A pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some alphabet of size k that avoids p.

Given morphisms g : Σ* → Σ* and f : Σ* → A*, and a letter a ∈ Σ such that g(a) starts with a and |g^n(a)| → ∞, the limit g^ω(a) is the unique infinite fixed point of g starting with a, and f(g^ω(a)) ∈ A^ω is called an HD0L word. A pattern p is k-HD0L-avoidable if there exist a finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| = k, a letter a ∈ Σ, and morphisms g : Σ* → Σ* and f : Σ* → A* (for some finite alphabet A) such that the infinite word f(g^ω(a)) is well defined and avoids p.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: What is the minimum number of steps of square completion needed to obtain a word from one of its factors?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, the prefix square completion of $w$ is any word of the form $uw$, where $u$ is a non-empty word such that $uu$ is a prefix of $uw$ (equivalently, $w$ starts with $u$). Symmetrically, the suffix square completion of $w$ is any word of the form $wv$, where $v$ is a non-empty word such that $vv$ is a suffix of $wv$ (equivalently, $w$ ends with $v$). A prefix-suffix square completion step on a word is the application of either a prefix square completion or a suffix square completion.

Given a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ and a factor (contiguous substring) $f$ of $w$, define $c(w,f)$ to be the minimum number of prefix-suffix square completion steps needed to transform $f$ into $w$ (or $\infty$ if no such sequence exists). Set
$$C(w) = \min\{c(w,f) : f \text{ is a factor of } w\}.$$

Determine $C(w)$ as a function of $w$, and in particular determine
$$\max\{C(w) : w \in \Sigma^*,\ |w| = n\}$$
as a function of the length $n$ and the alphabet size $|\Sigma|$.
status_search_result: Prefix-suffix square completion is an operation introduced in the combinatorics on words literature, with subsequent works studying iterated reductions, closure properties of language classes, and algorithmic determination of primitive square roots. No source located in the search explicitly resolves the minimum number of square completion steps required to recover a word from one of its factors, so the problem appears to remain open, though this could not be definitively confirmed.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: If p is k-avoidable, then arbitrarily long k-letter circular words avoiding p exist.
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let E be a (disjoint) alphabet of pattern variables. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E^+. A word w ∈ A^* is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : E^+ → A^+ such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p. A circular word of length n over A is an equivalence class of words in A^n under cyclic rotation; equivalently, it is a word a_0 a_1 ... a_{n-1} read modulo n, and its factors are all words of the form a_i a_{i+1} ... a_{i+ℓ-1} with indices taken modulo n (for every length ℓ ≥ 1, including ℓ > n, in which case the factor wraps around the circle multiple times). A circular word avoids p if none of its factors encounters p. A pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exist arbitrarily long words over a k-letter alphabet that avoid p.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every pattern p and every integer k ≥ 1, if p is k-avoidable, then there exist arbitrarily long circular words over a k-letter alphabet that avoid p.

Status appears unresolved in the available literature.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Show that the number of abelian cube-free ternary words grows exponentially with length. Given a n-letter alphabet, define the sequence Zn recursively by Z1 = 1, Zn = Zn1 nZn1 , n > 1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_n = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ be an alphabet of $n$ letters and let $\Sigma_n^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma_n$. For a word $w \in \Sigma_n^*$, the Parikh vector of $w$ is the vector $(|w|_1, \ldots, |w|_n)$ where $|w|_i$ is the number of occurrences of letter $i$ in $w$. Two words $u, v$ are said to be abelian-equivalent if they have the same Parikh vector. An abelian cube is a nonempty word of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$ where $u_1, u_2, u_3$ are pairwise abelian-equivalent. A word $w$ is abelian cube-free if no factor (contiguous subword) of $w$ is an abelian cube.

Let $A_n(\ell)$ denote the number of abelian cube-free words of length $\ell$ over $\Sigma_n$.

Prove that $A_3(\ell)$ grows exponentially in $\ell$; that is, show there exists a real number $c > 1$ such that $A_3(\ell) \geq c^\ell$ for all sufficiently large $\ell$.

(Auxiliary recursive sequence considered in connection with this question: for each integer $n \geq 1$, define $Z_n$ by $Z_1 = 1$ and $Z_n = Z_{n-1}^n \cdot n \cdot Z_{n-1}^n$ for $n > 1$, where exponentiation denotes word concatenation.)

original_question: Let p be k-avoidable. 1. If the number of p-free words on k letters of length n grows exponentially with n, then an integer N0 exists such that, for every n > N0 , there are circular p-free words on k letters with length n. 2. If the number of p-free words on k letters of length n grows polynomially with n, then the set of possible lengths for circular p-free words on k letters has density 0 in the set IN \ {0}.
self_contained_problem:
Let A_k = {0,1,...,k-1} be an alphabet of k letters. A pattern p is a nonempty word over an alphabet of variables. A word w over A_k is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h from the variable alphabet to A_k^+ such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w is called p-free. The pattern p is k-avoidable if there exist infinitely many p-free words over A_k.

A circular word of length n over A_k is an equivalence class of words in A_k^n under cyclic rotation; such a circular word is p-free if every linear factor (read around the cycle, of any length) is p-free. Let f_k(n) denote the number of p-free words of length n over A_k, and let C_k(p) ⊆ ℕ \ {0} be the set of integers n for which there exists at least one p-free circular word of length n over A_k.

Assume p is k-avoidable. Prove or disprove the following two statements:

1. If f_k(n) grows exponentially with n, then there exists an integer N_0 such that for every n > N_0 the set C_k(p) contains n (i.e., p-free circular words of length n exist for all sufficiently large n).

2. If f_k(n) grows polynomially with n, then C_k(p) has natural density 0 in ℕ \ {0}, i.e.,
   lim_{N → ∞} |C_k(p) ∩ {1,...,N}| / N = 0.

original_question: Given pattern p and integer n, what is the complexity of deciding whether Zn encounters p in the abelian sense? Define the abelian repetitive threshold function and the dual abelian repetitive threshold function on (1, 2] by: ART(n) = inf{s : y s is avoidable on n letters in the abelian sense} DART(r) = min{n ∈ IN : y r is avoidable in the abelian sense on n letter}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let Σ_n = {0,1,...,n−1} denote an alphabet of n letters, and let Σ_n^* be the set of finite words over Σ_n. Two words u, v ∈ Σ_n^* are abelian-equivalent, written u ~_a v, if v is a permutation of the letters of u (equivalently, |u|_a = |v|_a for every a ∈ Σ_n).

A pattern is a non-empty word p over a separate alphabet of variables. Given a word w ∈ Σ_n^*, we say that w encounters p in the abelian sense if w contains a factor of the form h(p), where h is a non-erasing morphism from the variable alphabet to Σ_n^* such that any two occurrences of the same variable x in p are mapped to abelian-equivalent (but not necessarily equal) words. Otherwise, w avoids p in the abelian sense. The pattern p is said to be avoidable in the abelian sense on n letters if there exists an infinite word over Σ_n that avoids p in the abelian sense.

For a real number s > 1, let y_s denote the "fractional power" pattern: writing s = k + t/q with 0 ≤ t < q in lowest terms, y_s is interpreted in the standard way as the pattern requiring a factor uvu... whose abelian-equivalent repetition has exponent s. Define on (1, 2]:

  ART(n) = inf{ s ∈ (1,2] : y_s is avoidable on n letters in the abelian sense },
  DART(r) = min{ n ∈ ℕ : y_r is avoidable in the abelian sense on n letters }.

Problems.

(1) Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a pattern p and an integer n ≥ 1, decide whether the alphabet Σ_n encounters p in the abelian sense (equivalently, whether every sufficiently long word over Σ_n contains an abelian instance of p, i.e. whether p is unavoidable on n letters in the abelian sense).

(2) Determine the exact values of the abelian repetitive threshold function ART(n) for all integers n ≥ 2, and determine the exact values of the dual abelian repetitive threshold function DART(r) for all r ∈ (1, 2].
status_search_result: The problem of computing the abelian repetitive threshold function ART(n) is open: only lower bounds are known (Samsonov–Shur 2012 proved ART(2) ≥ 11/3, ART(3) ≥ 2, ART(4) ≥ 9/5, ART(k) ≥ (k−2)/(k−3) for k ≥ 5, conjectured tight). A 2021–2022 work ("Abelian Repetition Threshold Revisited") shows the Samsonov–Shur lower bounds are not tight for k ∈ {6,7,8,9,10}, indicating exact values remain unknown. The complexity of deciding abelian encounterability of a pattern on n letters also remains open.

original_question: How many k-abelian equivalence classes of words of a given length contain an nth power?
self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet with |Σ| ≥ 2 and let k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2 be integers. For words u, v ∈ Σ*, write u ≡_k v (k-abelian equivalence) if for every word w ∈ Σ* with |w| ≤ k, the number of occurrences of w as a factor of u equals the number of occurrences of w as a factor of v. This is an equivalence relation on Σ*, and each equivalence class consists of words of a common length.

A word x ∈ Σ* is called an nth power if there exists y ∈ Σ* such that x = y^n (the concatenation of n copies of y).

For positive integers N, k, n and an alphabet Σ, let
   f_{Σ,k,n}(N) = #{ C : C is a k-abelian equivalence class of words of length N over Σ that contains at least one nth power }.

Determine f_{Σ,k,n}(N), or its asymptotic behavior as N → ∞, as a function of N (for fixed Σ, k, n).

However, no source was found that gives a closed form or matching asymptotic bounds specifically for the number of k-abelian classes of length N containing an nth power. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Given an alphabet Σ and a pattern p, maximal p-free word over Σ exists.
self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let Δ be another finite alphabet of pattern variables. A pattern is a non-empty word p ∈ Δ⁺. A word w ∈ Σ* is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : Δ⁺ → Σ⁺ such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w is p-free. A p-free word w ∈ Σ* is called maximal if for every letter a ∈ Σ both wa and aw encounter p (equivalently, w cannot be extended on either side while remaining p-free).

Question: For every finite alphabet Σ and every pattern p such that the language of p-free words over Σ is finite (or more generally, in all cases), does there exist a maximal p-free word over Σ? Equivalently, characterize the pairs (Σ, p) for which a maximal p-free word over Σ exists, and decide whether such a maximal p-free word always exists whenever p is avoidable / unavoidable on Σ.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of the question of whether, for arbitrary alphabet Σ and pattern p, a maximal (i.e., two-sided non-extendable) p-free word over Σ must exist. Pattern avoidance over words is an active research area with results on avoidability and computational complexity, but no source located clearly settles this specific existence question in full generality.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: What is the length of the longest word avoiding strongly k-abelian nth powers?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2$ and a finite alphabet $\Sigma$. For words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$, write $u\sim_k v$ (k-abelian equivalence) if $|u|=|v|$ and for every word $w\in\Sigma^*$ with $|w|\le k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $v$. A word $W\in\Sigma^*$ is called a strongly k-abelian nth power if there exist words $u_1,u_2,\dots,u_n\in\Sigma^*$ such that $W=u_1u_2\cdots u_n$ and $u_i\sim_k u_1$ for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. A word $X\in\Sigma^*$ is said to avoid strongly k-abelian nth powers if no factor of $X$ is a strongly k-abelian nth power.

It is known that for every choice of $k$, $n$, and finite alphabet $\Sigma$, there is no infinite word over $\Sigma$ avoiding strongly k-abelian nth powers, so the supremum
$$L(k,n,|\Sigma|) := \sup\{|X| : X\in\Sigma^*\text{ avoids strongly k-abelian nth powers}\}$$
is finite. Determine $L(k,n,|\Sigma|)$ as an explicit function of $k$, $n$, and the alphabet size $|\Sigma|$ (or, equivalently, determine the length of the longest word over $\Sigma$ that avoids strongly k-abelian nth powers).
status_search_result: Strongly k-abelian nth powers are known to be unavoidable on every finite alphabet, so the longest avoiding word is finite. However, no explicit formula or sharp bounds for this length appear in the literature found via search; the question of determining the exact maximum length seems not to be settled.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is it possible to avoid an arbitrary pattern p by an infinite sequence of palindromes over each alphabet on which p is avoidable?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let E = {x_1, x_2, ...} be a countable set of pattern variables disjoint from A. A pattern is a nonempty word p over E. An occurrence of p in a word w over A is a non-erasing morphism h : E* -> A* such that h(p) is a factor of w. A word w avoids p if no such occurrence exists. The pattern p is said to be avoidable on A if there exists an infinite word over A that avoids p; in that case A is called an avoiding alphabet for p.

A palindrome over A is a finite word u with u = u^R, where u^R denotes the reversal of u. Say that an infinite word w over A is "an infinite sequence of palindromes" if it can be written as an infinite concatenation w = u_1 u_2 u_3 ... where each u_i is a nonempty palindrome over A.

Question: Is it true that for every avoidable pattern p and every finite alphabet A on which p is avoidable, there exists an infinite word w over A that avoids p and is an infinite sequence of palindromes (in the sense above)?

Combinatorics, 2021) and on repetitions in palindrome-rich infinite words (Currie–Mol–Rampersad, 2019), but none of these explicitly resolve the question of whether, on every alphabet on which a pattern p is avoidable, p can be avoided by an infinite concatenation of palindromes. No source consulted reports the question as solved, so its current status is unclear.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Are the subtrees generated by two given words isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite alphabet $A$ and an integer $k\ge 2$. A finite word $w\in A^{*}$ is called $k$-power-free if it contains no factor of the form $u^{k}=uu\cdots u$ ($k$ times) with $u\in A^{+}$. Let $L\subseteq A^{*}$ denote the set of all $k$-power-free words over $A$ (the case $k=3$, the cube-free language, is the principal motivating example).

Order $L$ by the prefix relation $\le_{\mathrm{pref}}$: for $u,v\in L$, $u\le_{\mathrm{pref}} v$ iff $u$ is a prefix of $v$. The Hasse diagram of $(L,\le_{\mathrm{pref}})$ is a rooted tree $T(L)$ (rooted at the empty word), in which the children of a node $w\in L$ are exactly the words $wa\in L$ with $a\in A$. For each $w\in L$ define the subtree generated by $w$ to be 
$$T_w \;=\; \{v\in L : w\le_{\mathrm{pref}} v\},$$ 
viewed as a rooted tree with root $w$ under the inherited prefix order.

Two such rooted trees $T_{w_1}$ and $T_{w_2}$ are isomorphic if there exists a bijection $\varphi:T_{w_1}\to T_{w_2}$ preserving the root and the parent–child relation (i.e., a rooted, unordered tree isomorphism; edge labels in $A$ need not be preserved).

Problem. Determine the decidability and (if decidable) the computational complexity of the following problem: given two words $w_1,w_2\in L$, decide whether the subtrees $T_{w_1}$ and $T_{w_2}$ are isomorphic as rooted trees.
status_search_result: The question, posed in the context of structural properties of power-free (e.g. cube-free) languages, asks whether one can decide isomorphism of the prefix subtrees generated by two given words. Searches turned up related work on isomorphism of regular trees and on the structure of subtrees in cube-free languages (showing arbitrarily large finite subtrees occur), but no source explicitly resolving the isomorphism decision problem for subtrees generated by words in a power-free language. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Is there a pure morphic binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ be a binary alphabet, and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. For an integer $k \geq 1$, two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_k v$, if for every word $w \in \Sigma^*$ with $|w| \leq k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor in $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor in $v$. A $k$-abelian cube is a non-empty word of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$ with $u_1 \sim_k u_2 \sim_k u_3$ and $|u_1|=|u_2|=|u_3|>0$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ is said to avoid $k$-abelian cubes if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a $k$-abelian cube.

A morphism is a map $h : \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ satisfying $h(xy) = h(x)h(y)$. A morphism $h$ is called prolongable on a letter $a \in \Sigma$ if $h(a) = a x$ for some $x \in \Sigma^*$ with $h^n(x) \neq \varepsilon$ for all $n \geq 0$; in this case the iteration produces a unique infinite fixed point $h^{\omega}(a) = a\, x\, h(x)\, h^2(x)\, h^3(x)\, \cdots \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$. An infinite word is called pure morphic if it equals $h^{\omega}(a)$ for some morphism $h:\Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ prolongable on some letter $a \in \Sigma$.

Question: Does there exist a pure morphic infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ that avoids $2$-abelian cubes?
status_search_result: While it is known that 2-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet (via morphic images / suitable constructions), the specific question of whether such an avoiding word can be obtained as a pure morphic word (the fixed point of iterating a single binary morphism) does not appear to be resolved in the literature; existing constructions yield morphic but not necessarily pure morphic words, and analogous pure-morphic avoidance is known to fail for k-abelian squares over ternary alphabets. No source clearly settles the binary 2-abelian cube case for pure morphic words.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Which words u can be shuffled to obtain a unique square-free word u ▷β u?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called a square if $w = vv$ for some non-empty word $v$, and a word is called square-free if none of its factors (contiguous subwords) is a square. 

Given two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$, the shuffle of $u$ and $v$, denoted $u \shuffle v$, is the set of all words obtained by interleaving the letters of $u$ and $v$ while preserving the relative order of the letters within each of $u$ and $v$. A self-shuffle of $u$ is any word in $u \shuffle u$.

For a word $u$, write $u \triangleright_\beta u$ for a self-shuffle of $u$ (i.e., an element of $u \shuffle u$).

Characterize all words $u \in \Sigma^*$ for which there exists exactly one square-free word in the set $u \shuffle u$ — that is, words $u$ that admit a unique square-free self-shuffle.

original_question: Is there a natural integer p such that 2-abelian-squares of period at least p can be avoided over a binary alphabet?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ be the binary alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a positive integer $k$ and words $u,v \in \Sigma^*$, write $u \sim_k v$ if $|u|=|v|$ and, for every word $w \in \Sigma^*$ with $|w| \le k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a (contiguous) factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $v$. The relation $\sim_k$ is called $k$-abelian equivalence.

A nonempty word $W \in \Sigma^*$ is called a $2$-abelian-square if $W = uv$ with $|u|=|v| \ge 1$ and $u \sim_2 v$; the integer $|u|$ is called the period of the $2$-abelian-square. An infinite word $\mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^{\mathbb N}$ is said to avoid $2$-abelian-squares of period at least $p$ if no factor of $\mathbf{x}$ is a $2$-abelian-square of period $\ge p$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $p$ for which there is an infinite word over the binary alphabet $\Sigma$ that avoids all $2$-abelian-squares of period at least $p$?

A 2021 extension of Dekking's construction discusses related questions but does not settle this one. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Which square-free words w are themselves shuffles of square-free words: w = u ▷β u?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form $xx$ (i.e., there are no nonempty $x \in \Sigma^*$ and words $p, s \in \Sigma^*$ with $w = pxxs$).

For two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$, a shuffle of $u$ and $v$ is any word obtained by interleaving the letters of $u$ and $v$ while preserving the internal orders of $u$ and the internal orders of $v$. Equivalently, writing $|u|=m$ and $|v|=n$, a shuffle is determined by a binary mask $\beta \in \{0,1\}^{m+n}$ with exactly $m$ zeros, and the resulting word $u \shuffle_\beta v$ is obtained by placing the successive letters of $u$ at the positions marked $0$ and the successive letters of $v$ at the positions marked $1$. A word $w$ is called a self-shuffle (or shuffle square) if there exist a word $u$ and a mask $\beta$ such that $w = u \shuffle_\beta u$.

Problem. Characterize the square-free words $w$ over a finite alphabet that are themselves shuffles of a square-free word with itself; that is, determine all square-free $w$ for which there exist a square-free word $u$ and a shuffle mask $\beta$ with $w = u \shuffle_\beta u$.
status_search_result: Existence of (infinite) square-free self-shuffling words over a 3-letter alphabet was established affirmatively, answering Harju's question (Currie–Saari, 2014). Subsequent work (Müller; Charlier et al.; "Square-Free Shuffles of Words"; "On shuffled-square-free words") has produced further constructions and complexity results, including NP-completeness of recognizing shuffled-squares on general alphabets. However, a full characterization of which square-free words arise as self-shuffles of a square-free word remains unresolved.

paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: In the tree T , the size of any minimal subtree of index n is O(log n).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma=\{0,1,2\}$ be a three-letter alphabet. A finite word $w\in\Sigma^*$ is called square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form $uu$. Let $T$ be the rooted tree whose vertices are all ternary square-free words, in which the root is the empty word and the parent of any nonempty square-free word $w$ is obtained by deleting the last letter of $w$ (so the children of $w$ are exactly the square-free words of the form $wa$ with $a\in\Sigma$). The level (or index) of a vertex $w$ equals its length $|w|$.

For a vertex $v$ of $T$, the subtree $T(v)$ rooted at $v$ consists of $v$ together with all its descendants. Call $T(v)$ a minimal subtree if $v$ has a unique child in $T$ that itself has a unique child, and so on — equivalently, $T(v)$ is a non-branching path emanating from $v$ that ends at a leaf or at the first descendant of $v$ which has at least two children. The index of such a minimal subtree is the level of its root $v$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every minimal subtree of $T$ of index $n$, the number of vertices in this subtree is at most $C\log n$ (for all sufficiently large $n$). In other words, the size of any minimal subtree of index $n$ in $T$ is $O(\log n)$.
status_search_result: Petrova and Shur (2015, "On the Tree of Ternary Square-Free Words") proved that in the tree T of ternary square-free words ordered by prefix, every non-branching path from a node of level n has length O(log n), which establishes the stated bound on the size of minimal subtrees of index n. Thus the conjecture is solved.
