paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? (Large fields existentially closed in function fields with rational place)
original_question: Let K be a field. A field K is called large if it is existentially closed in the power series field K((t)) in the language of rings. Hypothesis (R4) states: for an arbitrary field K, if a function field F|K (a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree at least 1) admits a K-rational place (a valuation on F with residue field isomorphic to K), then K is existentially closed in F. It is known that local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields (in all characteristics and all dimensions) implies (R4). By the work of Hironaka, local uniformization holds in characteristic 0. It is also known (Anscombe-Dittmann-Fehm 2023) that if (R4) holds, then the existential L_val(t)-theory of F_p((t)) (the formal Laurent series field over F_p in variable t, with t-adic valuation) is decidable. Does hypothesis (R4) hold in general (i.e., for all fields K and all function fields F|K with a K-rational place, is K existentially closed in F)?
self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called large if it is existentially closed (in the language of rings) in the formal power series field $K((t))$. A function field over $K$ is a finitely generated field extension $F\mid K$ of transcendence degree at least $1$. A $K$-rational place of $F$ is a place (equivalently, a valuation ring) of $F$ whose residue field is $K$-isomorphic to $K$.

Question: Is the following statement true? For every field $K$ and every function field $F\mid K$ that admits a $K$-rational place, the field $K$ is existentially closed in $F$ in the language of rings (i.e., every existential first-order $L_{\mathrm{ring}}$-formula with parameters from $K$ that has a solution in $F$ already has a solution in $K$).

(Equivalently: does local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields, in all characteristics and dimensions, follow at the level of existential closedness?)

status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a recent survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. It is known to follow from local uniformization of rational places (established in characteristic 0 by Hironaka), and Anscombe–Dittmann–Fehm (2023) showed that it would imply decidability of the existential theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$. No proof in full generality appears in the literature.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Converse of Kuhlmann-Rzepka: characterization of rdr fields via independent defect property
original_question: Let (K, v) be a henselian valued field. A finite Galois extension E = (L|K, v) of prime degree p (where p = char Kv) with nontrivial defect (i.e., [L:K] > (vL:vK)[Lv:Kv]) is said to have independent defect if the set Sigma_E = {v(sigma(f)/f - 1) | f in L^x} (for any non-identity sigma in Gal(L|K)) satisfies: Sigma_E = {alpha in vK | alpha > H_E} for some proper convex subgroup H_E of vK such that vK/H_E has no smallest positive element. Otherwise E has dependent defect. The field (K, v) is called an independent defect field if, for some extension of v to K' = K(zeta_p) (a primitive p-th root of unity, or K' = K in characteristic p), all Galois extensions of (K', v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect have independent defect. A valued field (K, v) is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if it satisfies: (DRvp) if char Kv = p > 0, then v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK; and (DRvr) if char Kv = p > 0, then the completion's O_{K-hat}/pO_{K-hat} is semiperfect. It is proven (Kuhlmann-Rzepka 2023) that every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field, and (Rzepka-Szewczyk 2023) that a henselian field is roughly tame (satisfying (TF1r): if char Kv = p > 0 then [-v(p),v(p)] is p-divisible; (TF2): Kv is perfect; (TF3): algebraically maximal) if and only if all its algebraic extensions are defectless fields. By analogy, the conjecture is that a henselian field is roughly deeply ramified if and only if all its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields. Is this conjecture true? That is, if all algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field (K, v) are independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified field?
self_contained_problem:
Let (K, v) be a henselian valued field with value group vK, residue field Kv, and valuation ring O_K. Write p = char Kv when this is positive.

Definitions.

(1) A finite Galois extension (L|K, v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect (meaning [L:K] > (vL:vK)·[Lv:Kv], so that [L:K] = p, (vL:vK) = 1, and [Lv:Kv] = 1) is said to have independent defect if for some (equivalently, any) non-identity σ ∈ Gal(L|K), the set
   Σ_E := { v(σ(f)/f − 1) : f ∈ L^× , σ(f) ≠ f }
equals { α ∈ vK : α > H_E } for some proper convex subgroup H_E of vK such that the quotient vK/H_E has no smallest positive element. Otherwise E has dependent defect.

(2) The henselian field (K, v) is called an independent defect field if, choosing K' := K(ζ_p) (a primitive p-th root of unity) when char K ≠ p, and K' := K when char K = p, and fixing an extension of v to K', every Galois extension of (K', v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect has independent defect.

(3) (K, v) is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if:
   (DRvp) when char Kv = p > 0, the value v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK; and
   (DRvr) when char Kv = p > 0, the ring O_{K̂}/pO_{K̂} is semiperfect, where K̂ denotes the completion of (K, v).

Question. Suppose (K, v) is a henselian valued field such that every algebraic extension of (K, v) is an independent defect field. Does it follow that (K, v) is roughly deeply ramified?
status_search_result: The question is presented as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on model theory of tame valued fields (December 2025). One direction—that every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field—was established by Kuhlmann–Rzepka (2023). The converse, asked here, has not been established in the literature available; no resolution was located.

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
original_question: What is the topological type of the achievement set E(x_n) for the sequence x_n = 1/2^n + (-1)^n/3^n?
self_contained_problem:
For a sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty |x_n|<\infty$, the achievement set (or set of subsums) of $(x_n)$ is defined by
$$E(x_n) := \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n : (\varepsilon_n)_{n\ge 1} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}.$$
It is known that $E(x_n)$ is always a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$, and that for absolutely summable sequences $E(x_n)$ is one of the following: a finite set, a finite union of closed intervals, a set homeomorphic to the Cantor ternary set, or a so-called Cantorval (a non-empty compact set which is the closure of its interior, in which both endpoints of every non-degenerate component are accumulation points of one-point components, yet which is not a finite union of intervals).

Determine the topological type of the achievement set $E(x_n)$ for the specific sequence
$$x_n = \frac{1}{2^n} + \frac{(-1)^n}{3^n}, \qquad n=1,2,3,\ldots$$

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
context_brief: Generic Palis dichotomy for central Cantor sets
original_question: Does the Palis dichotomy hold generically for central Cantor sets?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions and setup. For a sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive reals with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n<\infty$, its achievement set is
$$E(a_n)=\Big\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n a_n : \varepsilon_n\in\{0,1\}\Big\}.$$
A central Cantor set is constructed from a sequence $(\alpha_n)\subset(0,1)$ as follows. Set $C_0=[0,1]$. Given $C_{n-1}$, which is a disjoint union of $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals each of the same length $\ell_{n-1}$, remove from the middle of each component an open interval of length $\alpha_n\ell_{n-1}$, obtaining $C_n$ as a union of $2^n$ closed intervals each of length $\ell_n=\ell_{n-1}(1-\alpha_n)/2$. The resulting set $C=\bigcap_{n\ge 1}C_n$ is the central Cantor set associated with $(\alpha_n)$. Equivalently, every central Cantor set coincides with the achievement set of the sequence $a_n=\ell_{n-1}(1-\alpha_n)/2$ (so that $C=E(a_n)$).

The space of central Cantor sets is naturally parametrized by sequences $(\alpha_n)\in(0,1)^{\mathbb N}$ endowed with the product topology, making it a Polish space; "generic" below means "for a residual (comeagre) set of parameters $(\alpha_n)$".

The Palis dichotomy for a pair $(C,C')$ of Cantor sets in $\mathbb R$ asserts that the arithmetic difference $C-C'=\{x-y:x\in C,\,y\in C'\}$ either has Lebesgue measure zero or contains an interval.

Problem. Is it true that for a generic pair of central Cantor sets $(C,C')$ (i.e., for a residual set of parameter pairs $((\alpha_n),(\alpha'_n))\in(0,1)^{\mathbb N}\times(0,1)^{\mathbb N}$), the Palis dichotomy holds: $C-C'$ either has Lebesgue measure zero or contains an interval?

original_question: Whenever the set {t ∈ ℝ : F_x(t) = c} is nonempty, must it contain a Cantor set; and likewise, whenever {t ∈ ℝ : F_x(t) = ω} is nonempty, must it contain a Cantor set?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x = (x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of nonzero real numbers such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |x_n| < \infty$. Define the continuous map
$$f_x : \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad f_x\big((\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\big) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n,$$
and let the achievement set be $E(x) = f_x(\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}})$. For each $t \in \mathbb{R}$ define the multiplicity (cardinality) function
$$F_x(t) = \operatorname{card}\big(f_x^{-1}(t)\big),$$
which takes values in $\{0,1,2,\dots\} \cup \{\omega, \mathfrak{c}\}$ (where $\omega = \aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$).

By a Cantor set we mean a nonempty, compact, perfect, totally disconnected subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is it true that for every such sequence $x$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item the set $\{t \in \mathbb{R} : F_x(t) = \mathfrak{c}\}$ is either empty or contains a Cantor set, and
\item the set $\{t \in \mathbb{R} : F_x(t) = \omega\}$ is either empty or contains a Cantor set?
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent (2025) survey on achievement sets of series. Web searches did not surface any published resolution of this dichotomy for the loci where the multiplicity function equals ω or 𝔠, so it appears to remain open.

original_question: If A ⊂ [0,∞) is a Borel set containing 0, must there exist a Borel set B ⊂ ℝ whose center of distances C(B) equals A? Here C(B) = {α ≥ 0 : for every x in B there exists y in B with d(x,y)=α}.
self_contained_problem:
For a nonempty subset $A$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, define the center of distances of $A$ by
$$C(A) := \{\alpha \geq 0 : \text{for every } x \in A \text{ there exists } y \in A \text{ with } d(x,y) = \alpha\}.$$
Consider $\mathbb{R}$ with the standard Euclidean metric. 

Question: Is it true that for every Borel set $A \subseteq [0,\infty)$ with $0 \in A$, there exists a Borel set $B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that $C(B) = A$?
category_tag: centers of distances and achievement sets
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets and centers of distances. A web search did not reveal any published resolution; related work has characterized centers of distances in particular cases (e.g., for achievement sets of series, Cantorvals) but the general Borel realizability question for subsets of $[0,\infty)$ containing $0$ appears to remain unresolved.

original_question: For q in (0, 1/2), compute the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval associated with the geometric central Cantor set E(q^n).
self_contained_problem:
For a nonempty subset $A$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, define the center of distances of $A$ by
$$S(A):=\{\alpha\in[0,\infty): \forall x\in A\ \exists y\in A\ \ d(x,y)=\alpha\}.$$

Given a sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of positive reals with $a_n\le \tfrac{1}{2}(a_{n-1}+\cdots)$ (so that the construction below produces a Cantor-type set in $[0,1]$), the central Cantor set $C=C(a_n)$ is constructed as follows. Start with $I_0=[0,1]$. At step $n\ge 1$, from each of the $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals of length $\ell_{n-1}$ obtained at the previous step, remove an open middle interval so that each remaining interval has length $a_n$; this yields $2^n$ closed intervals of length $a_n$ and an additional collection of $2^{n-1}$ open "gap" intervals removed at step $n$, whose union is denoted $G_n$. Then $C=\bigcap_{n\ge 0} I_n$, where $I_n$ is the union of the $2^n$ closed intervals at step $n$.

The adjoint Cantorval of $C$ is defined as
$$\widehat C := C\ \cup\ \bigcup_{n\in 2\mathbb{N}-1} G_n,$$
i.e., $C$ together with all gaps removed at odd-numbered steps.

For $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$ let $E(q^n)$ denote the geometric central Cantor set obtained by taking $a_n=q^n$ in the construction above (so the surviving intervals at step $n$ have length $q^n$). 

Determine explicitly the center of distances $S(\widehat{E(q^n)})$ of the adjoint Cantorval of $E(q^n)$, as a function of $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2025) develops the center-of-distances theory for central Cantor sets and Cantorvals (e.g., Banakiewicz–Bartoszewicz–Filipczak; Bielas–Plewik), but no published computation of the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval of the geometric central Cantor set $E(q^n)$ for $q\in(0,1/2)$ was located. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).
self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a simple graph with adjacency matrix $A(G)$, and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius (the largest eigenvalue of $A(G)$). A graph is called triangle-free (or $C_3$-free) if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices, and bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets. Let $m$ be a positive even integer. Among all non-bipartite, triangle-free graphs $G$ with exactly $m$ edges, determine the maximum value of $\lambda(G)$ and characterize all graphs that attain this maximum.
category_tag: Spectral graph theory / extremal spectral radius
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Zhai and Shu in 2022 for the even-edge case, has been resolved. A paper in the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (v31i1p52) characterizes three kinds of spectral extremal graphs among triangle-free non-bipartite graphs of even size, providing the sharp bound and extremal graphs.

original_question: Fix k >= 2 and an even integer m. Among all non-bipartite graphs with m edges that avoid every odd cycle C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}, which graph has the largest spectral radius?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. For an integer $k\ge 2$, a graph $G$ is said to be $\{C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free if it contains no cycle of odd length $3,5,\ldots,2k+1$ as a subgraph. A graph is non-bipartite if it contains at least one odd cycle (necessarily of length $\ge 2k+3$ under the above forbidden-cycle hypothesis).

Fix an integer $k\ge 2$ and an even positive integer $m$. Let $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}$ denote the family of all non-bipartite, $\{C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. Determine
$$\max\{\lambda(G) : G\in\mathcal{G}_{k,m}\}$$
and characterize all extremal graphs that attain this maximum.
status_search_result: Recent (2024–2025) work has resolved related cases (e.g., the triangle-free non-bipartite case with even size, and strong spectral stabilities for $C_{2k+1}$-free graphs), but the general problem for arbitrary $k\ge 2$ and even $m$ — identifying the extremal non-bipartite $\{C_3,\dots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free graph maximizing the spectral radius — does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature found. It is posed as an open problem in current surveys.

original_question: Fix r >= 1. For all sufficiently large m, must every B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfy lambda(G) <= sqrt(m), with equality only for complete bipartite graphs? Here B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \/ ((r+1)K_1) is the book graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge between the two vertices of degree r+1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $r \geq 1$ be a fixed integer. Define the book graph $B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \vee ((r+1)K_1)$, i.e., the graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,r+1}$ by adding an edge between its two vertices of degree $r+1$. For a simple graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix, and let $e(G)$ denote the number of edges of $G$. A graph is called $B_{2,r+1}$-free if it does not contain $B_{2,r+1}$ as a subgraph.

Prove or disprove: there exists $m_0 = m_0(r)$ such that for every $B_{2,r+1}$-free graph $G$ with $m = e(G) \geq m_0$,
$$\lambda(G) \leq \sqrt{m},$$
with equality if and only if $G$ is a complete bipartite graph.
status_search_result: The conjecture by Zhai, Lin, and Shu (2021) is verified for sufficiently large $m \geq (12r)^4$ by recent work in spectral extremal graph theory, but a fully tight resolution covering all $r \geq 1$ with optimal threshold has not been confirmed. Search results show several papers addressing closely related book/theta graph spectral problems, indicating partial progress rather than a complete resolution.

original_question: Fix r >= 1 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is a B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph with m edges, is it true that lambda(G) is at most rho(m, r), where rho(m, r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m - 1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, with equality exactly when m == 1 mod r and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $r \ge 1$ be a fixed integer. For a simple graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue) of its adjacency matrix, and let $e(G)$ denote its number of edges (its size). The generalized book $B_{2,r+1}$ is defined as the graph consisting of $r+1$ copies of the cycle $C_4$ that all share a common edge (equivalently, $K_2 + \overline{K_{r+1}}$ with an additional matching, in the standard convention $B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \vee (r+1)K_2$ — i.e., the join of an edge with $r+1$ independent edges). A graph $G$ is $B_{2,r+1}$-free if it contains no copy of $B_{2,r+1}$ as a subgraph.

For an integer $r \ge 1$ and a real $m > 0$, let $\rho(m,r)$ be the largest real root of the cubic equation
$$ x^3 - x^2 - (m-1)x + (m - 2r - 1) = 0. $$

For positive integers $r$ and $k$, let $K^{+}_{r,k}$ denote the graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,k}$ by adding a single edge inside the part of size $k$ (so that $K^{+}_{r,k}$ is non-bipartite and has $rk + 1$ edges).

Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists $m_0 = m_0(r)$ such that for every integer $m \ge m_0$, every $B_{2,r+1}$-free non-bipartite graph $G$ with $e(G) = m$ satisfies
$$ \lambda(G) \le \rho(m, r), $$
with equality if and only if $m \equiv 1 \pmod{r}$ and $G \cong K^{+}_{r,(m-1)/r}$.
status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in very recent work on edge-spectral Turán problems for forbidden generalized books. Related results by Zhai–Lin and others address the order (vertex-count) version and the simple book $B_{r+1}$ case, but the size (edge-count) version for $B_{2,r+1}$-free non-bipartite graphs with the cubic-root extremal value $\rho(m,r)$ does not appear to have been resolved in the literature. No published proof or disproof was found.

original_question: Fix k >= 2. If G has m edges and contains neither theta_{1,2,2k-1} nor theta_{1,2,2k}, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2, for all sufficiently large m?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph with m edges and let λ(G) denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix. For integers 1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ c, the theta graph θ_{a,b,c} is the graph obtained by joining two distinct vertices with three internally disjoint paths of lengths a, b, and c. For a positive integer n, let K_n ∨ I_t denote the graph obtained by joining every vertex of the complete graph K_n to every vertex of an independent set I_t of size t (so K_n ∨ I_t has n+t vertices and (n choose 2) + nt edges).

Fix an integer k ≥ 2. Prove or disprove: there exists M = M(k) such that for every graph G with m ≥ M edges that contains neither θ_{1,2,2k−1} nor θ_{1,2,2k} as a subgraph,
    λ(G) ≤ (k − 1 + √(4m − k² + 1)) / 2,
and equality holds if and only if G is isomorphic to K_k ∨ I_t with t = m/k − (k − 1)/2 (so in particular k divides 2m − k(k−1)).
status_search_result: A recent survey on edge-spectral-Turán type problems states that Li, Zhai and Shu completely settled the conjecture for all k ≥ 3 for sufficiently large m. The remaining case k = 2 (forbidding θ_{1,2,3} and θ_{1,2,4}) is not reported as fully resolved in the same source, so the conjecture is partially solved.

original_question: For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.
self_contained_problem:
For integers $q \ge p \ge 3$, the theta graph $\theta_{1,p,q}$ is the graph obtained from two distinct vertices $u,v$ by joining them with three internally disjoint paths of lengths $1$, $p$, and $q$ (so $\theta_{1,p,q}$ has the edge $uv$ together with two internally disjoint $u$-$v$ paths of lengths $p$ and $q$). For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$ denote the family of simple graphs with exactly $m$ edges that contain no subgraph isomorphic to $\theta_{1,p,q}$. The spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Determine, for all integers $q \ge p \ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $m$, the maximum value of $\rho(G)$ over $G \in \mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$, and characterize all graphs attaining this maximum.
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Li, Zhao and Zou (2025) as Problem 8 concerning the maximum spectral radius among $\theta_{1,p,q}$-free graphs with $m$ edges, has reportedly been resolved completely; a recent survey/paper indicates that two of its theorems (corresponding to Theorem 3.27 and Theorem 3.36) together solve this problem. Independent confirmation via search was limited, so the resolution rests on this single source.

original_question: For each t >= 5, what is the maximum spectral radius among all F_t-free graphs with m edges, and which extremal graphs attain that value, where F_t = K_1 \/ P_{t-1} is the fan graph on t vertices?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer t ≥ 2, let the fan graph F_t be the graph on t vertices defined as F_t = K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}, i.e., the join of a single vertex with a path on t-1 vertices. A simple graph G is called F_t-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to F_t. The spectral radius λ(G) of G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

For each integer t ≥ 5, determine the maximum value of λ(G) over all F_t-free simple graphs G with exactly m edges, and characterize all extremal graphs attaining this maximum.
status_search_result: The problem is partially solved. The case t = 5 (gem-related) was settled by Zhang and Wang (2024) for odd m, and the case t = 6 was resolved for m ≥ 88 in arXiv:2412.13792. More general results for t = 2k+1 and t = 2k+2 with m sufficiently large appear in recent works (e.g., arXiv:2409.15918, published in J. Graph Theory 2025), giving λ(G) ≤ (k-1+√(4m-k²+1))/2 with equality for K_k ∨ ((m/k - (k-1)/2)K_1). However, the full problem for all t ≥ 5 and all m is not completely resolved.

original_question: For integers q >= p >= r >= 2, how can one characterize the graphs in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that have the largest spectral radius?
self_contained_problem:
For integers q ≥ p ≥ r ≥ 2, the theta graph θ_{r,p,q} is the simple graph obtained by taking two distinct vertices u and v and joining them by three internally disjoint paths of lengths r, p, and q respectively. Given a graph F, a graph G is called F-free if G contains no subgraph isomorphic to F, and G(m, F) denotes the family of all F-free simple graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices. The spectral radius of a graph G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Problem: For all integers q ≥ p ≥ r ≥ 2, characterize completely the graphs in G(m, θ_{r,p,q}) attaining the maximum spectral radius (for all sufficiently large m, identifying the unique extremal graph or the family of extremal graphs).
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Li, Zhao and Zou (2025) on characterizing the θ_{r,p,q}-free graphs of given size with maximum spectral radius, has been resolved. Subsequent work by Li, Liu and Zhang reportedly settled the general case, complementing earlier partial resolutions for specific subcases such as θ_{1,3,3}-free and θ_{2,2,3}-free graphs that appear in the recent literature.

original_question: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{k,3}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?
self_contained_problem:
Setup and notation.

- For an integer k ≥ 2, the friendship graph F_{k,3} is the graph obtained from k triangles by identifying exactly one common vertex (so |V(F_{k,3})| = 2k+1 and |E(F_{k,3})| = 3k).
- For a graph H, a graph G is called H-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to H.
- Given a positive integer m and a graph H, let G(m, H) denote the family of all H-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices.
- For a graph G, let λ(G) denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix.
- Disjoint union of graphs is denoted by ∪, and the join of two graphs A and B (the disjoint union together with all edges between V(A) and V(B)) is denoted A ∨ B. Let K_t denote the complete graph on t vertices and tK_1 the empty graph on t vertices.
- For integers n, k with k ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ l ≤ k, define
   S^{1,l}_{n,k} := K_l ∨ ( ( K_{k−l} ∨ (n − k − 1)K_1 ) ∪ K_1 ).
  (So S^{1,l}_{n,k} has n vertices.)

Question. Fix k ≥ 2. Does there exist an integer m_0 = m_0(k) with the following property: for every m ≥ m_0 and every G ∈ G(m, F_{k,3}), if l is the unique integer with 1 ≤ l ≤ k − 1 such that
   m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k),
then
   λ(G) ≤ λ( S^{1,l}_{ (m−l)/k + (k+3)/2 , k } ),
with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to S^{1,l}_{ (m−l)/k + (k+3)/2 , k }?

Related results have established the spectral extremal F_{k,3}-free bound in some residue classes (notably the case treated by Li–Lu–Peng and the confirmation for general k under a divisibility/edge-count hypothesis), but the full congruence-refined statement covering all residue classes 1 ≤ l ≤ k−1 with the extremal graph S^{1,l}_{n,k} appears to remain open.

original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+1}-free, where W_{2k+1} is the odd wheel on 2k+1 vertices, must the extremal graph for lambda(G) depend only on the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, taking the complete join K_k \/ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the other residue classes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a fixed integer. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix (the spectral radius). The odd wheel $W_{2k+1}$ is the graph on $2k+1$ vertices obtained by joining a single vertex to every vertex of a cycle of length $2k$. For two graphs $A$ and $B$, let $A \vee B$ denote their join (the disjoint union together with all edges between $V(A)$ and $V(B)$), and let $tK_1$ denote the empty graph on $t$ vertices. For integers $a \ge 1$, $\ell \ge 1$, and $k \ge 2$, define $S^{1,\ell}_{a,k}$ to be the graph obtained from $K_k \vee aK_1$ by selecting one vertex $v$ of the $K_k$-part and attaching $\ell$ pendant vertices to $v$ (so $v$ has $\ell$ extra neighbors of degree $1$).

Consider the class of $W_{2k+1}$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges, and let an extremal graph be one that maximizes $\lambda(G)$ over this class.

Prove or disprove the following: there exists $m_0 = m_0(k)$ such that for every $m \ge m_0$, every extremal graph is determined (up to isomorphism) only by the residue class of $m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2}$ modulo $k$, and is given by
\[
G^*_m \;=\; \begin{cases} K_k \vee \left(\tfrac{m}{k} - \tfrac{k-1}{2}\right) K_1 & \text{if } k \mid m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2}, \\[4pt] S^{1,\ell}_{\tfrac{m-\ell}{k} + \tfrac{k+3}{2},\, k} & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases}
\]
where in the non-divisible case $\ell \in \{1,2,\dots,k-1\}$ is chosen so that $m - \ell$ makes the indicated formula a non-negative integer corresponding to the residue class of $m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2} \pmod k$.
status_search_result: The conjecture concerns the edge-version (graphs with a fixed number of edges $m$) of the spectral Turán problem for odd wheels. While the vertex-version (graphs with $n$ vertices) has been largely resolved for $k \ge 2$, $k \notin \{4,5\}$, and recent work has addressed $k \in \{4,5\}$, the edge-version stated here is reported as still open in the source listing the conjecture.

original_question: Let r >= 3 and let G be a K_{r+1}-free graph with m >= r + 1 edges. Must the sum of squares of the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= 2m(1 - 1/r)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $r \geq 3$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with $m \geq r+1$ edges that contains no clique of size $r+1$ (i.e., $G$ is $K_{r+1}$-free). Let $A(G)$ denote the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $\lambda_1(G) \geq \lambda_2(G) \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n(G)$ be its eigenvalues. Prove or disprove that
$$\lambda_1(G)^2 + \lambda_2(G)^2 \leq 2m\left(1 - \frac{1}{r}\right).$$
status_search_result: The Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture is established for r=2 (triangle-free case) by Lin, Ning, and Wu, and partial results exist (regular graphs, complete multipartite graphs, dense K_4-free graphs, graphs with few triangles, asymptotically almost surely for random graphs). For general r ≥ 3 the conjecture remains open as of 2026.

original_question: Fix k >= 1 and r >= 3. For all sufficiently large m, if G is B_{r,k+1}-free, where B_{r,k+1} = K_r \/ (k+1)K_1 is the generalized book graph, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(2m(r - 1)/r), with equality only for complete regular r-partite graphs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $r\ge 3$ and $k\ge 1$ be integers. The generalized book graph $B_{r,k+1}$ is defined as the join $K_r \vee (k+1)K_1$, that is, the graph obtained from a clique on $r$ vertices and an independent set on $k+1$ vertices by adding all edges between the clique and the independent set. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix, and let $m=e(G)$ denote its number of edges. A graph is called $B_{r,k+1}$-free if it contains no copy of $B_{r,k+1}$ as a subgraph.

Prove or disprove: there exists $m_0=m_0(r,k)$ such that for every $B_{r,k+1}$-free graph $G$ with $m\ge m_0$ edges,
$$\lambda(G)\le \sqrt{2m\cdot\frac{r-1}{r}},$$
with equality if and only if $G$ is a complete regular $r$-partite graph.
status_search_result: The conjecture, originally posed by Li, Liu and Feng (2022), has been resolved. A subsequent paper by Li, Liu and Zhang establishes the stated spectral bound for $B_{r,k+1}$-free graphs with sufficiently many edges, with equality characterized by complete regular $r$-partite graphs. A 2026 survey on spectral booksize conjectures also lists this conjecture as confirmed.

original_question: Given a color-critical graph F with chromatic number chi(F) = r + 1, determine the F-free graphs with m edges that attain the maximum spectral radius.
self_contained_problem:
Let r ≥ 2 be an integer and let F be a color-critical graph with chromatic number χ(F) = r+1; that is, F contains an edge e such that χ(F − e) = r. For an integer m ≥ 1, let G(m, F) denote the family of F-free simple graphs with exactly m edges (and no isolated vertices). The spectral radius λ(G) of a graph G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Determine, for all sufficiently large m, the graphs in G(m, F) that maximize λ(G), i.e., characterize the extremal graph(s) attaining
   max { λ(G) : G is F-free with m edges }.
status_search_result: The problem has been resolved by Li, Liu, and Zhang, who characterized the F-free graphs of given size m with maximum spectral radius when F is color-critical with χ(F)=r+1, generalizing Nikiforov-type spectral Turán results. Related work on spectral Turán problems for color-critical graphs (e.g., books, theta graphs, cliques) supports this resolution.

context_brief: Characterization of doubly connected periodic Fatou components
original_question: Does every doubly connected periodic Fatou component of a meromorphic function have to be a Herman ring, rather than some other kind of doubly connected periodic component?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a meromorphic function (rational or transcendental), and let $F(f)$ denote its Fatou set, i.e. the set of points in $\mathbb{C}$ at which the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family. A connected component $U$ of $F(f)$ is called periodic of period $p\geq 1$ if $f^p(U)\subseteq U$ and $p$ is minimal with this property. Such a component $U$ is said to be doubly connected if it is conformally equivalent to an annulus $\{z:1<|z|<R\}$ for some $1<R\leq\infty$ (equivalently, $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus U$ has exactly two connected components). A Herman ring is a periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p$ on which $f^p$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus.

Question: Must every doubly connected periodic Fatou component of a meromorphic function $f$ be a Herman ring?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent survey on Herman rings (Dec 2025). Related partial results are known: for meromorphic functions with an omitted value, every doubly connected periodic Fatou component is indeed a Herman ring (Nayak, 2016). However, for general transcendental meromorphic functions, the question does not appear to be settled in the literature reviewed; the survey explicitly states "the opposite has not been proven yet."

context_brief: Classification of rational maps with Herman rings
original_question: Which rational maps, especially in low degrees such as 3 and 4, admit Herman rings? More specifically, can one give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a Herman ring in terms of the map's degree, the configuration of critical orbits, and combinatorial data, and can one describe the associated parameter slices using tools such as Teichmuller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory?
self_contained_problem:
A Herman ring of a rational map $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ is a periodic Fatou component $U$ that is conformally isomorphic to a round annulus $A_r=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:1<|z|<r\}$ for some $r>1$, on which (for some period $p\geq 1$) the iterate $f^{\circ p}$ is conjugate, via this isomorphism, to an irrational rigid rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ of $A_r$. By a theorem of Shishikura, every rational map possessing a Herman ring has degree at least $3$.

Provide a complete classification of rational maps $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ that admit a Herman ring, with emphasis on low degrees (in particular degrees $3$ and $4$). More precisely, accomplish the following:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a Herman ring of $f$ purely in terms of:
   (i) the degree $d=\deg(f)$,
   (ii) the configuration of the critical orbits of $f$ (the forward orbits of the critical points, including their mutual interactions and accumulation behavior), and
   (iii) combinatorial data describing how the Julia set and the Fatou components of $f$ are arranged (such as a suitable invariant graph, lamination, or puzzle-piece structure encoding the dynamics).

(b) For natural one- or several-parameter families of rational maps containing maps with Herman rings, describe the corresponding parameter slices — i.e. the loci of parameters for which a Herman ring of given combinatorics persists — using Teichmüller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory, and determine the topology, conformal structure, and boundary behavior of these loci.
status_search_result: The classification of rational maps admitting Herman rings, especially in degrees 3 and 4, is widely recognized as open. Shishikura proved degree ≥ 3 is necessary, and explicit constructions exist (e.g., cubic rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings, due to Yang and collaborators), but no necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of degree, critical orbit configurations, and combinatorial data are known, and the structure of associated parameter slices remains under active investigation.

original_question: What geometric regularity can the boundary components of a Herman ring have? In particular, under what hypotheses are these boundaries Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they have fractal structure, what can be said about their Hausdorff dimension or Lebesgue measure, and can a Herman-ring boundary ever have positive area?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least $2$ acting on the Riemann sphere. The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the maximal open set on which the iterates $\{f^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ form a normal family, and its complement is the Julia set $J(f)$. A periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p\geq 1$ is called a Herman ring if $U$ is conformally isomorphic to a round annulus $A_r=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:1<|z|<r\}$ for some $r>1$, and the first-return map $f^p:U\to U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ on $A_r$ for some $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. The boundary $\partial U\subset J(f)$ consists of two disjoint connected components in $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.

Investigate the geometric regularity of the boundary components of Herman rings of rational maps. Specifically, address the following:

(a) Under what hypotheses on $f$ (e.g., diophantine conditions on $\alpha$, the orbits of critical points, or quasiconformal surgery origins) is each boundary component of $U$ a Jordan curve? When is each boundary component a quasicircle, i.e., the image of a round circle under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$?

(b) Under what conditions does a boundary component of $U$ exhibit fractal structure, in the sense of having Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $1$?

(c) What can be said about the Hausdorff dimension and the (planar) Lebesgue measure of $\partial U$? In particular, can a boundary component of a Herman ring have strictly positive two-dimensional Lebesgue measure?
status_search_result: The geometric nature of Herman-ring boundaries remains largely unresolved. While analogous questions for Siegel disks have seen substantial progress (e.g., dimension results for quasiconformal Siegel disks, Astala's bound on quasicircle dimension), no general results determining when Herman-ring boundaries are Jordan curves/quasicircles, characterizing their Hausdorff dimension, or settling whether they can have positive Lebesgue measure appear in the literature. The problem is widely cited as open.

original_question: Must every rational map that has a Herman ring also have buried Julia components, or are additional global dynamical or topological assumptions needed before the existence of a Herman ring forces buried Julia components to appear?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least $2$ on the Riemann sphere. Recall:

- The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the set of points where the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family, and the Julia set is $J(f)=\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus F(f)$.
- A Herman ring of $f$ is a periodic Fatou component $U$ (of period $p\geq 1$) on which $f^p:U\to U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ of a round annulus $\{1<|z|<r\}$.
- A connected component $K$ of $J(f)$ is called a buried Julia component if $K$ does not meet the boundary of any Fatou component of $f$; equivalently, $K\cap\partial U=\emptyset$ for every connected component $U$ of $F(f)$.

Question: Does every rational map $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ that admits a Herman ring necessarily have at least one buried Julia component? If not, determine additional global dynamical or topological hypotheses on $f$ under which the existence of a Herman ring forces the existence of a buried Julia component.
category_tag: Complex dynamics: Herman rings and Julia sets
status_search_result: Web sources show explicit constructions of rational maps with Herman rings that have buried Julia components (Godillon) and recent work on degenerate Herman rings, but none establishes a general implication or a counterexample. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Upper bounds on period from relevant poles
original_question: Given a periodic Herman ring H of period p for a meromorphic function, can one prove an upper bound on p in terms of the number h of H-relevant poles, complementing the known lower bounds? This is especially asked for meromorphic maps with finitely many poles and at least one omitted value, such as functions of the form E(z)/((z-z0)(z-z1)...(z-zp)) where E is an entire function omitting a finite point.
self_contained_problem:
Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane. A Herman ring of f is a periodic Fatou component H of f on which the first-return map f^p (where p is the period) is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus. Let H be a p-periodic Herman ring with cycle H = H_0, H_1, ..., H_{p-1} (so f(H_i) = H_{i+1 mod p}). A pole z* of f is called H-relevant if z* is surrounded by some H_i in the sense that z* lies in the bounded component of the complement of the core curve of H_i. Let h denote the number of H-relevant poles.

It is known that p ≥ h(h+1)/2 in general (with the stronger bound p ≥ h(h+3)/2 in certain situations).

Question: Establish an upper bound on the period p in terms of h (and other natural data of f). The question is of particular interest for meromorphic maps having only finitely many poles and at least one omitted value, namely functions of the form
    f(z) = E(z) / ((z - z_0)(z - z_1) ... (z - z_p)),
where p ≥ 1, z_0, z_1, ..., z_p ∈ C are distinct, and E is an entire function omitting a finite value of C. Prove or disprove the existence of such an upper bound, and if it exists, give an explicit form.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem complementing known lower bounds (p ≥ h(h+1)/2 by Nayak–collaborators, published in Indian J. Pure Appl. Math., 2022). No published upper bound on the period of a Herman ring in terms of the number of relevant poles appears in the literature; the problem is explicitly listed as an open question in a recent (Dec 2025) survey on Herman rings.

original_question: For each natural number n, is there a finite upper bound on the number of distinct geometric or combinatorial configurations that an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n can realize?
self_contained_problem:
Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane having at least one omitted value (i.e., a value that is not in the image of f). A Herman ring of f is a periodic Fatou component U of period n, meaning f^n(U) = U with n minimal, such that f^n restricted to U is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus. An n-cycle of Herman rings is an ordered family {U_0, U_1, …, U_{n-1}} of Herman rings with f(U_i) = U_{i+1 mod n} and minimal period n. Two n-cycles of Herman rings are said to have the same configuration if there is an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere carrying one cycle to the other while preserving the cyclic dynamical labeling and the nesting/separation pattern of the rings together with the locations of the poles and omitted values they surround.

Question: For each integer n ≥ 1, is there a finite upper bound C(n) on the number of distinct configurations that can be realized by an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n among all such meromorphic functions f with at least one omitted value?
status_search_result: The general question of whether the number of configurations of an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n is finite for every n is posed as an open question. Partial results are known for small periods: there is at most one configuration when the period is 3 or 4, and exactly six configurations are realized for period 5. No general bound for arbitrary n appears in the literature.

context_brief: Finite omitted values obstructing Herman rings
original_question: If a general transcendental meromorphic function has a finite omitted value, does that condition alone force the map to have no Herman rings of any period?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a transcendental meromorphic function. The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the set of points $z\in\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ at which the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family in some neighbourhood of $z$ (where defined). A periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p\ge 1$ (so $f^p(U)=U$ and $f^k(U)\ne U$ for $0<k<p$) is called a Herman ring if $U$ is conformally equivalent to a round annulus $\{1<|w|<r\}$ and $f^p|_U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of that annulus.

A point $a\in\mathbb{C}$ is called a finite omitted value of $f$ if $a\notin f(\mathbb{C})$, i.e., the equation $f(z)=a$ has no solution in $\mathbb{C}$.

Question: Is it true that every transcendental meromorphic function $f$ which possesses at least one finite omitted value has no Herman ring of any period $p\ge 1$?
status_search_result: The full conjecture appears to remain open. Partial results are known: meromorphic functions with a finite omitted value cannot have Herman rings of period 1 or 2, and functions whose omitted value is a pole have no Herman rings at all. No example of a meromorphic function with both an omitted value and a Herman ring has been constructed, but a proof for all periods is not available in the literature.

paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
original_question: What is the magnitude, origin, and transport mechanism of the additional energy that must be deposited during the gradual phase of a solar flare, after the impulsive phase dominated by high-energy electrons, in order to explain cooling and mass-flow timescales that observed flares show but standard flare models fail to reproduce?
self_contained_problem:
A solar flare is commonly modeled as a two-phase event. In the impulsive phase, magnetic reconnection in the corona accelerates a population of non-thermal electrons whose energy deposition into the chromosphere is inferred from hard X-ray bremsstrahlung emission; this energy then drives chromospheric evaporation and heats coronal loops to temperatures of order 10^7 K. In the subsequent gradual phase, the loops cool and drain on observed timescales (typically tens of minutes to hours), characterized by the temporal evolution of soft X-ray and EUV emission and by Doppler-measured mass flows.

Standard one-dimensional hydrodynamic flare loop models (e.g., field-aligned models with classical Spitzer thermal conduction, optically thin radiative losses, and a heating function calibrated to the hard X-ray–inferred non-thermal electron beam) predict cooling and draining timescales that are systematically shorter than those observed, even after allowing for suppression of thermal conduction and for non-equilibrium, non-Maxwellian plasma effects. To reconcile model and observation, an additional volumetric heating term Q_grad(s,t) (energy per unit volume per unit time, as a function of position s along the loop and time t) must be supplied during the gradual phase.

Determine:
(a) the total energy E_grad = ∫∫ Q_grad(s,t) A(s) ds dt deposited in a representative flare loop during the gradual phase, and in particular whether E_grad is comparable to the impulsive-phase energy deposited by non-thermal electrons;
(b) the physical origin of this additional energy (for example, continued or secondary magnetic reconnection, stored magnetohydrodynamic wave energy, turbulence, or a separate non-thermal particle population);
(c) the transport mechanism by which this energy is delivered to the radiating and flowing plasma (for example, Alfvén-wave Poynting flux, ion beams, suprathermal electrons not detected in hard X-rays, or in-situ heating by turbulent dissipation),
in such a way that a self-consistent loop model reproduces the observed gradual-phase cooling curves and mass-flow timescales.
status_search_result: The magnitude, source, and transport mechanism of the additional gradual-phase heating in solar flares is widely recognized as an unresolved problem in solar physics. Reviews and recent modeling work (Reep et al., Warren et al., Bradshaw & Cargill) acknowledge that standard electron-beam-driven models underpredict observed cooling/draining timescales and that the missing energy may rival that of the impulsive phase, with its source largely unknown.

paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
original_question: To what extent does solar-flare physics scale continuously from the largest stellar and solar superflares through X-class events down to microflares, nanoflares, and campfires, and what similarities or differences in reconnection, particle acceleration, and plasma heating emerge across that full range of event sizes?
self_contained_problem:
Solar and stellar flares are impulsive releases of magnetic energy in a plasma atmosphere, driven by magnetic reconnection and accompanied by particle acceleration and plasma heating. Observed events span an enormous energy range, conventionally classified (in approximate order of decreasing radiative energy) as: stellar superflares and solar superflares (≳10^33 erg), X-class flares (≳10^32 erg in soft X-rays at GOES X1 level), through M-, C-, B-, and A-class flares, microflares (≈10^26–10^28 erg), nanoflares (≈10^24 erg, as hypothesized by Parker for coronal heating), and the small ubiquitous EUV brightenings known as campfires (≈10^22–10^24 erg).

Formulate and resolve the following question. Let E denote the total released magnetic/radiative energy of a flare-like event. Consider the key physical observables and parameters associated with each event:

• reconnection rate M_A (the inflow Alfvén Mach number at the reconnection region) and reconnected magnetic flux Φ_rec;
• nonthermal particle acceleration efficiency, characterized by the fraction η_nt of E going into accelerated electrons and ions, the power-law index δ of the accelerated electron spectrum, and the cutoff energies;
• plasma heating, characterized by the peak temperature T_peak, the emission measure EM, and the partition between direct heating and chromospheric evaporation driven by accelerated particles.

The problem is: determine, on the basis of magnetohydrodynamic and kinetic plasma physics, whether there exist universal scaling laws of the form

  T_peak ∝ E^{a}, EM ∝ E^{b}, Φ_rec ∝ E^{c}, η_nt ∝ E^{d}, δ = δ(E), M_A = M_A(E)

that hold continuously across the full range from campfires (E ∼ 10^22 erg) to stellar superflares (E ∼ 10^36 erg), and identify which scaling relations (if any) extend uniformly across this ≳14-decade range in energy, and where, if anywhere, qualitative breaks occur (for instance, transitions in the dominant reconnection regime, in the efficiency or spectral hardness of particle acceleration, or in the relative role of direct versus evaporative heating). Specifically, characterize the similarities and differences in reconnection geometry and rate, in particle-acceleration mechanisms (e.g., DC electric field, stochastic, shock, or termination-shock acceleration), and in chromospheric/coronal heating responses, as a function of E across this range.
status_search_result: This is an explicitly stated open question in current solar/stellar flare physics. Reviews and recent surveys describe partial scaling relations (e.g., Shibata–Yokoyama temperature–emission-measure scaling, Aschwanden's flare statistics, stellar superflare studies with Kepler/TESS) but no unified theory verified across the full range from campfires to superflares; the question remains open.

paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
context_brief: Unified solar and stellar flare framework
original_question: How can spatially resolved solar-flare observations be combined with unresolved observations of diverse stellar flares, including superflares, to build a common framework that constrains flare position on the stellar disk, flaring-area size, coronal mass ejection identification and characterization, and flare energetics across stars?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a unified quantitative framework that combines two classes of flare observations into a single inference scheme:

(a) spatially resolved solar flare observations, in which the location, geometry, time evolution, and multi-wavelength emission of a flare on the solar disk can be measured directly; and

(b) spatially unresolved observations of flares on other stars (including superflares with bolometric energies up to roughly 10^36 erg), in which only disk-integrated time series and spectra are available.

Within this framework, propose explicit forward models, observables, and inversion procedures that simultaneously constrain the following quantities for an arbitrary stellar flare event observed only as disk-integrated data:

1. The position of the flare on the visible stellar disk (e.g., a center-to-limb angle or projected coordinates), inferred from limb-darkening signatures, rotational modulation, and time-dependent line profiles.

2. The size (area) of the flaring region as a function of time, inferred from the relation between continuum/line flux, blackbody-equivalent temperature, and filling factor.

3. The identification and characterization (mass, velocity, kinetic energy, geometry) of any associated coronal mass ejection, inferred from blue-shifted absorption/emission features, dimming signatures, and multi-band light-curve morphology.

4. The total flare energetics, including the partition among thermal, non-thermal, radiative, and kinetic components, calibrated against the spatially resolved solar case.

Specifically, formulate scaling relations and statistical priors, calibrated on the resolved solar dataset, that allow the four quantities above to be extracted from unresolved stellar flare observations with quantified uncertainties, and demonstrate that the framework reproduces solar flare ground truth when the Sun is treated as a star.
status_search_result: This is a forward-looking research program rather than a fully posed mathematical theorem. While partial progress exists on individual components (Sun-as-a-star analyses, superflare statistics, stellar CME signatures via Doppler-shifted lines, area-temperature degeneracies), no complete unified framework jointly constraining flare position, area, CME properties, and energetics across the solar–stellar regime has been established as of 2026.

original_question: Do measurable solar-flare properties provide predictive insight into the later effects of those eruptions on the near-Earth environment, and can that knowledge be turned into operational guidance that better protects technological assets and infrastructure from space-weather impacts?
self_contained_problem:

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
original_question: Let (K,v) be a tame valued field, meaning a henselian valued field whose algebraic closure with the unique extension of v is a tame extension. Do tame valued fields admit quantifier elimination in some suitable expansion of the language of valued rings? The surrounding discussion indicates that the obstruction is poor understanding of purely wild extensions, i.e. algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field that are linearly disjoint from tame extensions.
self_contained_problem:
Let (K, v) be a valued field. Recall the following definitions:

- (K, v) is henselian if v extends uniquely to the algebraic closure K^alg of K.
- For a henselian valued field (K, v), let v^alg denote the unique extension of v to K^alg. The extension (K^alg | K, v^alg) is called tame if, for every finite subextension L | K with residue field extension k_L | k_K and value group extension v(L) | v(K):
  (i) the residue characteristic p = char(k_K) does not divide the ramification index [v(L) : v(K)];
  (ii) the residue field extension k_L | k_K is separable;
  (iii) the extension L | K is defectless, i.e. [L : K] = [v(L) : v(K)] · [k_L : k_K].
  When p = 0, every algebraic extension of (K, v) is automatically tame.
- A henselian valued field (K, v) is called a tame valued field (or tame field) if (K^alg, v^alg) is a tame extension of (K, v).
- A purely wild extension of a henselian valued field (K, v) is an algebraic extension that is linearly disjoint from every tame algebraic extension of (K, v).

The language of valued rings L_vr is the language of rings expanded by a binary predicate for the valuation divisibility relation x | y (meaning v(x) ≤ v(y)).

Question: Does there exist a natural expansion L* of L_vr (for instance, by sorts/predicates/functions for the value group, the residue field, leading-term structures, or related auxiliary structures) such that the theory of tame valued fields admits quantifier elimination in L*?
status_search_result: While Ax–Kochen–Ershov style results, model completeness, and relative completeness for tame valued fields are established (notably via work of Kuhlmann), a quantifier elimination result for tame valued fields in a suitable language remains an outstanding question, with the main obstruction being the lack of a structural understanding of purely wild extensions of henselian valued fields. Searches did not turn up a published QE theorem covering tame valued fields in general.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Model theory of deeply ramified fields
original_question: What model-theoretic statements can be proved for (roughly) deeply ramified valued fields relative to their value groups and residue fields? In particular, what can be said about the model theory of the perfect hull F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, which is discussed as a central example of a deeply ramified field that remains outside the existing tame and roughly tame transfer results?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_K$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_K$, value group $vK$, and residue field $Kv = \mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_K$. Recall:

- $(K,v)$ is henselian if $v$ extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of $K$.
- $(K,v)$ is tame if it is henselian, $Kv$ is perfect, $vK/p\,vK = 0$ when $\operatorname{char}(Kv)=p>0$, and every finite extension is defectless.
- $(K,v)$ of residue characteristic $p>0$ is deeply ramified if $\Omega^1_{\mathcal{O}_L/\mathcal{O}_K} = 0$ for every finite extension $L/K$; equivalently (in the henselian case of characteristic $p$) the Frobenius $\Phi:\mathcal{O}_K/p\mathcal{O}_K \to \mathcal{O}_K/p\mathcal{O}_K$ is surjective and the field is dense in its perfect hull.

A standard transfer (Ax–Kochen/Ershov) principle for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of valued fields states: for $(K_1,v_1),(K_2,v_2)\in\mathcal{C}$,
$$ (K_1,v_1)\equiv (K_2,v_2) \iff v_1K_1 \equiv v_2K_2 \text{ (as ordered abelian groups) and } K_1v_1 \equiv K_2v_2 \text{ (as fields)},$$
with an analogous principle for elementary substructures.

Problem. Develop the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified valued fields relative to their value groups and residue fields. Specifically:

(a) Formulate and prove an Ax–Kochen/Ershov style transfer principle (for elementary equivalence and for elementary substructure) for a natural class of deeply ramified valued fields that strictly contains the class of (roughly) tame valued fields and that is not covered by existing tame or roughly tame transfer results.

(b) Determine a complete set of axioms, in a suitable first-order language of valued fields, for the theory of the perfect hull
$$ \mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^{\infty}} = \bigcup_{n\ge 0} \mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^n} $$
equipped with its $t$-adic valuation, and decide its decidability, model-completeness, NIP, and the structure of its definable sets, relative to its value group $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ and residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
status_search_result: Jahnke and Kartas (Beyond the Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem, JAMS 2025) established AKE-type principles for certain perfect deeply ramified / perfectoid fields, in particular showing that the perfect hull of $\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h$ is elementarily embedded in the perfect hull of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$. Recent work (e.g., the 2026 preprint "AKE principles for deeply ramified fields" and related theses) extends some results to deeply ramified fields of positive characteristic with fixed finite degree of imperfection. However, a full model-theoretic understanding of arbitrary (roughly) deeply ramified fields relative to value group and residue field remains open, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Tame-field analogues for perfect henselian fields
original_question: Can one prove for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic model-theoretic results analogous to the existing theorems for tame fields, perhaps after imposing only mild additional hypotheses? This question is motivated by the positive result that F_p(t^{1/p^∞})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with value group $vK$ and residue field $Kv$. Recall:

- $(K,v)$ is henselian if $v$ extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of $K$; equivalently, Hensel's lemma holds.
- $(K,v)$ is perfect if $K$ is a perfect field, i.e., $\mathrm{char}(K)=0$ or $\mathrm{char}(K)=p>0$ and the Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective on $K$.
- $(K,v)$ of residue characteristic $p>0$ is called tame if it is henselian, the value group $vK$ is $p$-divisible, the residue field $Kv$ is perfect, and every finite extension $(L|K,v)$ is defectless (i.e., $[L:K]=(vL:vK)\cdot[Lv:Kv]$).
- For a valued field $(K,v)$, $K^h$ denotes its henselization, and $K^{1/p^\infty}=\bigcup_{n\ge 0} K^{1/p^n}$ its perfect hull (in characteristic $p$).

The model theory of tame valued fields is well developed: in particular, the Ax–Kochen/Ershov style Theorem of F.-V. Kuhlmann states that if $(K_1,v_1)$ and $(K_2,v_2)$ are tame valued fields, then $(K_1,v_1)\equiv(K_2,v_2)$ as valued fields if and only if $v_1K_1\equiv v_2K_2$ as ordered abelian groups and $K_1v_1\equiv K_2v_2$ as fields; analogous relative completeness, model completeness, and Ax–Kochen–Ershov principles for elementary equivalence and substructure relations are known in the tame setting.

There is a positive instance suggesting an extension of such results outside the tame realm: for any prime $p$, equipped with the natural $t$-adic valuation, the henselization $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h$ is an elementary substructure of the perfect hull $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^\infty}$ of the Laurent series field. Note that these fields are perfect and henselian but are not tame in general (they may carry nontrivial defect).

Problem. Develop a model theory of henselian perfect valued fields of positive residue characteristic that parallels the model theory of tame valued fields. Concretely, identify mild additional hypotheses $(\ast)$ on a class $\mathcal{C}$ of henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic (containing examples such as $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h$ and $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^\infty}$) under which one can prove an Ax–Kochen–Ershov style theorem for $\mathcal{C}$: namely, for $(K_1,v_1),(K_2,v_2)\in\mathcal{C}$,
$$(K_1,v_1)\equiv(K_2,v_2)\iff v_1K_1\equiv v_2K_2\ \text{and}\ K_1v_1\equiv K_2v_2,$$
together with corresponding relative model-completeness and elementary-substructure transfer results.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
original_question: In the setting of Kuhlmann's incomplete axiom systems for F_p((t)), one can construct henselian defectless extensions that satisfy the basic axioms but fail existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions because of behavior of additive polynomials. Is there a simple and usable extra condition on the immediate extensions that repairs this failure and yields a satisfactory axiomatization?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ denote the field of formal Laurent series over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, equipped with its $t$-adic valuation $v_t$, and consider it as a structure in the language $L_{\mathrm{val}}$ of valued fields (a one-sorted or three-sorted language sufficient to express the valuation, the value group, and the residue field). A valued field $(K,v)$ is said to be henselian if $v$ extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of $K$, and defectless if for every finite extension $(L,v)|(K,v)$ one has $[L:K] = e\cdot f$, where $e$ is the ramification index and $f$ the residue degree. An extension $(L,v)|(K,v)$ is called immediate if the value group and residue field do not change. A maximal immediate extension of $(K,v)$ is an immediate extension that admits no proper immediate extension.

It is known that there exist henselian defectless extensions $(L,v)$ of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ which satisfy a natural list of basic first-order axioms (henselianity, defectlessness, residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$, value group a $\mathbb{Z}$-group, etc.) intended to axiomatize the complete theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$, but for which $(L,v)$ fails to be $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-existentially closed in some maximal immediate extension; this failure is caused by the behavior of additive polynomials (i.e., $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear polynomials of the form $\sum_i a_i X^{p^i}$) over $L$.

Problem: Find a simple, first-order expressible additional condition on the immediate extensions of a henselian defectless valued field (of mixed or equal characteristic $p$ with residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$ and value group a $\mathbb{Z}$-group), which when added to the basic axiom list above guarantees that every model is $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-existentially closed in each of its maximal immediate extensions, and which together with the basic axioms yields a complete (and thus satisfactory) recursive axiomatization of the theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$.
status_search_result: The problem is presented as an explicitly stated open problem in a recent survey on the model theory of tame valued fields (December 2025). No published solution is indicated, and decidability/complete axiomatization of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ remains a long-standing open question.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
original_question: Suppose a valuation v decomposes as v = w ◦ ̄w, where both w and ̄w are extremal and the value group of w is divisible. Must the composite valuation v also be extremal?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field. Recall that $(K,v)$ is called extremal if for every polynomial $f \in K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the set
$$\{v(f(a_1,\dots,a_n)) : a_1,\dots,a_n \in \mathcal{O}_v\}$$
attains its maximum in $vK \cup \{\infty\}$, where $\mathcal{O}_v$ is the valuation ring of $v$. Extremality is a property of the valued field, not just the field, and depends on $v$.

Suppose $v$ decomposes as a composition of two nontrivial valuations $v = w \circ \bar{w}$, where $w$ is the valuation on $K$ with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_w \supseteq \mathcal{O}_v$, and $\bar{w}$ is the induced valuation on the residue field $Kw$ whose valuation ring corresponds to the image of $\mathcal{O}_v$ in $Kw$. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item $(K,w)$ is extremal,
\item $(Kw,\bar{w})$ is extremal,
\item the value group $wK$ of $w$ is divisible.
\end{itemize}

Question: Must the composite valued field $(K,v)$ be extremal?
status_search_result: The behavior of extremality under composition of valuations is explicitly listed as an open problem in Kuhlmann's notes on extremal and tame valued fields and on the Valuation Theory Home Page open-problems list. Partial results are known (e.g., for perfect residue fields a characterization exists), but the general question with $w$ having divisible value group and both $w,\bar w$ extremal is not resolved in the literature found.

original_question: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions? This is asked after observing that a particular extension (L,v) of F_p((t)) fails this existential-closedness property and, by a theorem cited in the paper, is therefore not extremal.
self_contained_problem:
Let (K, v) be a valued field, with value group vK and residue field Kv. Recall the following definitions.

(1) An extension (L, v) ⊇ (K, v) is called immediate if vL = vK and Lv = Kv. A valued field (K, v) is called maximal if it admits no proper immediate extension; every valued field has at least one maximal immediate extension.

(2) (K, v) is existentially closed in an extension (L, v) (in the language of valued fields) if every existential first-order formula with parameters from K that has a solution in L already has a solution in K.

(3) For a polynomial f ∈ K[X_1, …, X_n], let f(O_K^n) ⊆ K denote the image of the valuation ring O_K^n under f. The set f(O_K^n) is said to have the optimal approximation property if the supremum sup{v(a) : a ∈ f(O_K^n)} ∈ vK ∪ {∞} is attained by some element of f(O_K^n). The valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every n ≥ 1 and every f ∈ K[X_1, …, X_n], the set f(O_K^n) has the optimal approximation property.

Question: Is every extremal valued field (K, v) existentially closed in each of its maximal immediate extensions?
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a December 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. Related literature (notes on extremal and tame valued fields, characterization of extremal valued fields) discusses partial results — e.g., existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions implies henselian and defectless — but no source found resolves the implication from extremality to existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions.

original_question: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a useful analogue of (R4), namely an "(R4) by alteration" statement, and more generally is there a satisfactory form of "model theory by alteration" in which one is allowed to pass to finite extensions in order to recover the desired existential-closedness or decidability conclusions?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_v$, value group $vK$, and residue field $Kv$. Recall:

(a) A place $P$ of an algebraic function field $F\mid K$ is said to admit local uniformization if for every finite set of elements $f_1,\dots,f_n\in\mathcal{O}_P$ there is a model of $F\mid K$ on which the center of $P$ is a regular point and on which all $f_i$ are regular.

(b) Local uniformization by alteration is the weaker statement that the above can be achieved after passing to a suitable finite extension $F'\mid F$ of the function field (an "alteration" in the sense of de Jong), i.e. one is allowed to replace $F$ by $F'$ before requiring smoothness of the chosen model at the (extended) center of $P$.

(c) Call a valued field $(K,v)$ an "(R4)-field" if it satisfies the model-theoretic hypothesis used to deduce existential closedness / Ax–Kochen–Ershov-type transfer results from local uniformization, namely: for every valued function field $(F\mid K, v)$ and every finite tuple from $\mathcal{O}_v\cap F$, there exists, after a suitable valuation-theoretic adjustment, a smooth model of $F\mid K$ realizing the data, allowing one to embed $(F,v)$ into an $|K|^+$-saturated extension of $(K,v)$ over $K$.

Question. Formulate and establish (or refute) an analogue "(R4) by alteration" of hypothesis (R4) in which the smooth model is required to exist only after passing to a finite extension of the valued function field, and which is implied by local uniformization by alteration. More generally, develop a "model theory by alteration": a framework of model-completeness, existential closedness and decidability transfer theorems for valued fields (in particular tame, deeply ramified, or semitame valued fields) in which one is permitted to replace function fields by finite extensions in order to recover the desired conclusions.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent (2025) survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. While local uniformization by alteration has been established (Knaf–Kuhlmann, building on de Jong), no formulation of an "(R4) by alteration" hypothesis or a corresponding "model theory by alteration" appears in the literature, and the question is listed as open.

paper_title: Open Questions in Massive Star Research across Cosmic Scales
original_question: What larger, conflict-free framework can reconcile massive-star theory and observations across individual stars, interacting systems, stellar winds, compact-object environments, star clusters, and integrated star-forming galaxies? The framework must explain why some current descriptions conflict across subfields, such as stellar-wind clumps needing to be tiny in spectral modeling but large in X-ray accretion variability, and why single-star evolution models can reproduce integrated star-forming galaxies even though massive stars have high multiplicity and many individual stars and systems are not reproduced by current models.
self_contained_problem:
Construct a unified, internally consistent theoretical framework for massive stars (initial masses roughly above 8 solar masses) that simultaneously accounts for observations and modeling at all of the following scales without internal contradiction:

1. Individual massive stars (atmospheres, interiors, evolution).
2. Interacting binary and higher-order multiple systems, given the empirically high multiplicity fraction of massive stars.
3. Radiation-driven stellar winds, including their inhomogeneous (clumped) structure.
4. Environments of compact objects accreting from such winds, including X-ray binary lightcurve variability.
5. Star clusters as ensembles of coevolving massive stars and binaries.
6. Integrated stellar populations of star-forming galaxies.

The framework must in particular resolve at least the following currently conflicting requirements:

(a) Wind clumping: spectral modeling of single massive stars requires the inhomogeneities ("clumps") in radiation-driven winds to be small in spatial/optical-depth scale in order to reproduce the temporally smooth appearance of stellar spectra; whereas modeling X-ray lightcurve variability of compact-object accretors fed by such winds requires clumps of substantially larger scale. Provide one physical description of wind structure that is quantitatively compatible with both regimes.

(b) Population synthesis vs. individual systems: explain why single-star evolution population synthesis suffices to reproduce integrated observables of star-forming galaxies, even though (i) the massive-star multiplicity fraction is high so binary interactions should dominate the population, and (ii) current single- and binary-star models fail to reproduce many specific individual stars and interacting systems that are observed. The framework must reconcile these facts within one consistent set of physical assumptions and parameters.

State the framework precisely enough that it makes falsifiable predictions across all six scales above, and demonstrate that no pair of its predictions conflict in the way that current subfield-specific descriptions do.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open programmatic challenge in massive-star astrophysics: no unified, conflict-free cross-scale framework currently exists, and the listed tensions (wind-clump sizes for spectral vs. X-ray accretion modeling; success of single-star population synthesis despite high binary fractions and failures at the individual-system level) remain active research topics as of 2026. No source claims a resolution.

original_question: What sources produce the highly ionized environments observed in many low-metallicity and high-redshift galaxies, including nebular helium-ionizing radiation? The answer must determine whether hot Wolf-Rayet stars with comparatively weaker winds, chemically homogeneous-evolution products, Population III stars, or other massive-star channels can supply the necessary hard ionizing flux under the metallicity and evolutionary conditions of those galaxies.
self_contained_problem: Identify the astrophysical sources responsible for the highly ionized environments observed in many low-metallicity and high-redshift star-forming galaxies, in particular those producing nebular He II emission (which requires photons of energy at least 54 eV). Determine, under realistic metallicity and evolutionary conditions of such galaxies, which massive-star channels — including (i) hot Wolf-Rayet stars (e.g., WN2 and WN3h-type) with comparatively weak, optically thin winds, (ii) products of chemically homogeneous evolution, (iii) Population III stars, or (iv) other massive-star pathways — can supply the required hard ionizing flux, and assess whether stellar evolution and population-synthesis models can reproduce these populations (including the predominance of apparently single WN2/WN3h stars) so as to account for the observed nebular He II ionizing radiation.

The question is therefore not yet definitively resolved.
