paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
original_question: If a manifold carries an SU(2)-action and its orbit space satisfies a suitable geometric condition, such as carrying an Einstein metric, must the manifold itself admit an Einstein metric?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a smooth (effective) action of the Lie group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and let $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ denote the corresponding orbit space. A Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$.

Determine whether the following implication holds: if the orbit space $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ carries a "nice" geometric structure—in particular, if it admits an Einstein metric (in the appropriate orbifold/stratified sense)—then $M$ itself must admit an Einstein metric. Equivalently, formulate and prove (or disprove by counterexample) general conditions on the orbit space $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ under which an Einstein metric on $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ guarantees the existence of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-invariant Einstein metric on $M$.
category_tag: Einstein metrics with Lie group actions
status_search_result: The general question of when an SU(2)-action on a manifold with a "nice" orbit space (e.g., one admitting an Einstein metric) guarantees an invariant Einstein metric on the total space remains open. Partial results exist in special settings: cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics constructed by Böhm in dimensions 5–9, recent computer-assisted constructions of SU(2)-invariant negative Einstein metrics, and Kähler–Einstein metrics with SU(2)-action in dimension four. No general theorem matching the broad formulation is known.

original_question: Can bosonic quantum error-correcting encodings such as GKP, cat, and binomial codes be integrated into multiparty quantum key agreement so that key agreement is performed at the logical-qubit level on protected continuous-variable modes, while preserving distributed-protocol compatibility, fault-tolerant logical operations, compatible syndrome extraction, acceptable resource overheads, and fairness and security guarantees?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol in which N ≥ 3 spatially separated parties jointly generate a shared secret bit string K ∈ {0,1}^L through exchange of quantum states over noisy continuous-variable (CV) bosonic channels and authenticated classical communication. The protocol must satisfy:

(i) Correctness: with probability at least 1 − ε_c, all honest parties output the same key K.
(ii) Fairness: every honest party contributes equally to K, in the sense that no proper subset of parties can bias any bit of K.
(iii) Security: against any coalition of up to t < N dishonest parties and any external eavesdropper, the trace distance between the joint state of the key and the adversary's quantum side information and the ideal uniform-and-independent state is at most ε_s.

Bosonic encodings. For each CV mode, fix one of the following logical-qubit encodings into a single harmonic oscillator with quadratures (q̂, p̂):
 • GKP code: code states are (regularized) +1 eigenstates of the stabilizers e^{i 2√π q̂} and e^{i 2√π p̂}.
 • Cat code: even/odd superpositions of coherent states (|α⟩ ± |−α⟩)/N_±.
 • Binomial code: finite superpositions Σ_k √(C(N,k))/2^{N/2} |k(S+1)⟩ in the Fock basis with appropriate parameters (N, S).

Question. Does there exist an MQKA protocol with the following properties simultaneously?

(a) Logical-level execution: every key-generation operation (state preparation, entangling gate, measurement) is performed on logical qubits encoded in CV modes by one of the bosonic codes above.

(b) Fault tolerance: the logical Clifford operations and measurements used by the protocol admit a fault-tolerant implementation on the chosen bosonic code, with a syndrome-extraction circuit whose physical error per round is below the code's threshold.

(c) Distributed compatibility: the protocol remains executable when the N parties are connected by a network of lossy bosonic channels (transmissivity η < 1, thermal noise n̄ ≥ 0) together with local operations and classical communication, with no requirement of a central trusted node.

(d) Resource overhead: the number of physical bosonic modes, photons, and ancillas per generated secret bit is polynomial in N, log(1/ε_c), and log(1/ε_s).

(e) Fairness and security: properties (ii) and (iii) above hold with the stated parameters under a fully quantum adversary.

Provide such a protocol together with a proof of (a)–(e), or prove that no protocol simultaneously satisfying (a)–(e) exists for any of the three bosonic encodings.
status_search_result: No published construction integrates GKP/cat/binomial bosonic codes into a fully fault-tolerant multiparty quantum key agreement protocol with proven fairness, security, and polynomial overhead. The question is posed as a forward-looking open direction, and a targeted search did not surface a complete solution.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: Ricci-flat manifolds and the Hitchin-Thorpe-type inequality
original_question: Is there an interesting example of a Ricci-flat 4-manifold M with 2χ(M) > 3|τ(M)|? In particular, does the 4-sphere S^4 admit a Ricci-flat metric?
self_contained_problem:
Background. For a closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifold M, let χ(M) denote its Euler characteristic and τ(M) its signature. A Riemannian metric g on M is called Ricci-flat if its Ricci tensor vanishes identically, Ric(g) ≡ 0. The Hitchin–Thorpe inequality states that any closed oriented 4-manifold admitting an Einstein metric satisfies 2χ(M) ≥ 3|τ(M)|, with equality only for flat manifolds or for Ricci-flat Kähler metrics on (quotients of) the K3 surface.

Problem. 
(a) Does there exist a closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifold M admitting a Ricci-flat Riemannian metric g such that the strict inequality 2χ(M) > 3|τ(M)| holds, beyond the already classically known examples (flat tori and K3-type manifolds, which lie on the equality boundary)? Equivalently, exhibit an "interesting" Ricci-flat 4-manifold satisfying this strict inequality, or prove that no such example exists. 

(b) In particular, does the 4-sphere S^4 admit a Ricci-flat Riemannian metric?
status_search_result: The existence of Ricci-flat (non-flat) metrics on the 4-sphere S^4, and more generally interesting Ricci-flat closed 4-manifolds with 2χ > 3|τ|, remains a well-known open problem in 4-dimensional Einstein/Ricci-flat geometry. Surveys of Einstein metrics on 4-manifolds (e.g., Anderson) and works on collapsing almost Ricci-flat 4-manifolds (Lott) discuss the known constraints (Hitchin–Thorpe, hyperkähler rigidity in the simply connected case) but do not resolve whether S^4 admits a Ricci-flat metric.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can multiparty quantum key agreement be integrated into quantum-internet control and networking stacks so that software-defined quantum networks can automatically select, route, schedule, and synthesize appropriate MQKA protocols based on the current network topology, available quantum resources, participant latency, security, and fairness requirements, device heterogeneity, and historical performance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a software-defined quantum network modeled as a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)) whose vertices V represent quantum-capable nodes (each with a heterogeneous device profile specifying available qubit registers, gate sets, memory coherence times, measurement bases, and entanglement-generation rates) and whose edges E(t) carry quantum and classical channels with time-dependent capacities, fidelities, and latencies. A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol for a participant set S ⊆ V is an interactive procedure that outputs a common secret key k_S known to every member of S such that (i) every participant contributes equally to k_S (fairness), (ii) k_S is information-theoretically secret against any external eavesdropper and against any proper subset of dishonest insiders up to a specified threshold t < |S|, and (iii) the protocol terminates within a prescribed latency bound τ_S using only resources available on the induced subnetwork.

Let Π = {π_1, π_2, …} be a (possibly infinite) library of MQKA protocols, each π_i specified by its participant-size range, required topology (e.g. star, ring, complete, GHZ-distribution tree), per-round quantum and classical resource cost, achievable fairness model, security threshold, and latency profile.

Design a control-plane decision procedure A that, given as input
  • the current network state G(t) together with per-node device profiles,
  • a request (S, τ_S, σ_S, φ_S) consisting of a participant set S, a latency budget τ_S, a security level σ_S, and a fairness requirement φ_S,
  • a history H of past protocol executions with measured performance metrics,
outputs in polynomial time
  (a) a selected protocol π* ∈ Π (or a synthesized protocol expressed as a circuit/message-flow program),
  (b) a routing assignment of the quantum and classical messages of π* onto the edges of G(t),
  (c) a schedule that coexists with all other concurrently admitted MQKA sessions without enabling key-reuse attacks or violating resource contention constraints,
such that the realized execution of π* on G(t) provably satisfies the requested fairness, security threshold, and latency bound, and is competitive (within a guaranteed multiplicative factor) with the optimal offline choice over Π for the same request.

Does such a decision procedure A exist, and if so, what are the achievable competitive ratios and complexity bounds? In particular, is the joint problem of automated MQKA selection, routing, scheduling, and on-the-fly protocol synthesis decidable, and is it tractable under realistic resource and adversary models?
status_search_result: No published work demonstrates an automated control-plane procedure that selects, routes, schedules, and synthesizes MQKA protocols in software-defined quantum networks under the joint constraints described. Existing literature on quantum network control planes (e.g., QNodeOS, SeQUeNCe, NetSquid orchestration) and MQKA protocol design treats these problems separately, and rapid automated synthesis of MQKA protocols is generally identified as a future-research direction rather than an accomplished result.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: positive sectional curvature on 6-manifolds with χ>0
original_question: Does every compact oriented 6-manifold M with positive Euler characteristic χ(M) > 0 admit a metric of positive sectional curvature?
self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a compact, oriented, smooth 6-dimensional manifold with positive Euler characteristic, $\chi(M) > 0$. Determine whether $M$ necessarily admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature (i.e., a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ such that for every point $p \in M$ and every 2-plane $\sigma \subset T_p M$, the sectional curvature $K_g(\sigma) > 0$).
status_search_result: The question is closely tied to the Hopf-type problems on existence and obstructions for positively curved metrics. In dimension 6, classification of compact oriented manifolds admitting positive sectional curvature is widely regarded as open; only a handful of examples are known (S^6, CP^3, the Wallach space SU(3)/T^2, and the Eschenburg biquotient SU(3)//T^2), and topological obstructions for general 6-manifolds with χ>0 have not been established. Recent work (e.g., on 6-manifolds with non-abelian symmetry, 2019) continues to investigate the problem, indicating it remains open.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can twin-field multiparty quantum key agreement, in which multiple parties send phase-encoded weak coherent pulses to a central interference station so that the final key depends symmetrically on all users’ phases, be scaled beyond small groups of three or four users while preserving strong fairness, handling multi-photon events from several parties, and securing the central station as an untrusted relay?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a twin-field multiparty quantum key agreement (TF-MQKA) protocol defined as follows. Let n ≥ 3 mutually distrustful parties P_1, …, P_n each prepare phase-encoded weak coherent pulses |α e^{iϕ_k}⟩ with chosen phases ϕ_k ∈ [0, 2π), and transmit them through lossy quantum channels to a single central interference (measurement) station, treated as an untrusted relay. The station performs single-photon interference measurements whose detection statistics depend on the global phase combination e^{i(ϕ_1 + ⋯ + ϕ_n)}, and announces classical outcomes from which the parties distill a shared secret key K such that K is a symmetric function of (ϕ_1, …, ϕ_n).

Call the protocol strongly fair if no proper subset S ⊊ {1, …, n} of colluding parties can bias, predetermine, or learn nontrivial information about the final key K beyond what a single honest party contributes; that is, the distribution of K conditioned on any choice of inputs by S remains uniformly determined by the contributions of the honest parties. Call the protocol secure under an untrusted relay if no strategy by the central station (including arbitrary measurements and classical announcements) leaks information about K to an eavesdropper above a vanishing bound, and call it robust to multi-photon events if the security and key-rate analysis remains valid when two or more parties simultaneously contribute photons to the interference.

Problem: Construct, for arbitrary n, a TF-MQKA protocol of the above form that simultaneously
(i) achieves strong fairness against any coalition of up to n − 1 dishonest parties,
(ii) is provably secure against an untrusted central station,
(iii) correctly accounts for multi-photon contributions from multiple parties in its security proof, and
(iv) preserves the single-photon-interference distance-scaling advantage of two-party twin-field QKD (i.e. key rate scaling as O(√η) in the total channel transmittance η rather than O(η)),
or else prove that no such protocol can satisfy all four properties for sufficiently large n.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2024 preprint on twin-field-based multi-party quantum key agreement and reviews of MQKA architectures) indicates that existing TF-MQKA frameworks demonstrate feasibility only for three or four users, with explicit remarks that extending to N > 3 parties is nontrivial due to misalignment issues and exponential growth in combinatorics of participant choices. Strong fairness, untrusted-relay security, and rigorous handling of multi-photon contributions for general n have not been jointly resolved, so the problem appears open.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: from almost complex to integrable complex structures
original_question: If a 2n-dimensional manifold admits an almost complex structure, must it also admit an integrable complex structure when n > 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M^{2n}$ be a smooth closed manifold of real dimension $2n$ with $n>2$. An almost complex structure on $M$ is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J:TM\to TM$ satisfying $J^2=-\mathrm{Id}$. Such a $J$ is called integrable (i.e., comes from a holomorphic atlas making $M$ a complex manifold) if and only if its Nijenhuis tensor
$$N_J(X,Y)=[X,Y]+J[JX,Y]+J[X,JY]-[JX,JY]$$
vanishes identically (Newlander–Nirenberg theorem).

Question: If $M^{2n}$ admits an almost complex structure, must $M^{2n}$ also admit an integrable complex structure (possibly a different one) when $n>2$?
status_search_result: The question is widely regarded as open. It coincides with Yau's Problem 52, which conjectures that every compact almost complex manifold of real dimension at least 6 admits an integrable complex structure. The most famous special case—whether the 6-sphere $S^6$ admits a complex structure—remains an unresolved problem in differential geometry.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can high-dimensional multiparty quantum key agreement protocols that replace qubits with d-level qudits realize higher information density and key rates in noisy multiparty networks while still preserving fairness and security, given the engineering difficulty of generating high-quality d-dimensional entangled states, performing stable d-ary encodings, and measuring in high-dimensional bases?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol involving N ≥ 3 parties who wish to jointly establish a shared secret key such that (i) every participant contributes equally to the final key (fairness: no proper subset of parties can predetermine the key), and (ii) the protocol is secure against both external eavesdroppers and dishonest internal participants (with security quantified, e.g., by an exponentially small trace distance between the real protocol output and an ideal uniformly random key conditioned on the adversary's quantum side information). Standard MQKA protocols use qubit (d = 2) carriers. A high-dimensional MQKA protocol replaces these qubits with d-level qudits (d ≥ 3), encoding key information in mutually unbiased bases of ℂ^d and distributing multipartite entangled qudit states (e.g., generalized GHZ states |GHZ_d^N⟩ = (1/√d) Σ_{j=0}^{d-1} |j⟩^{⊗N}) among the N parties.

Problem. Design and rigorously analyze a high-dimensional MQKA protocol with the following properties, or prove that no such protocol exists under reasonable physical assumptions:

(a) For a fixed number M of transmitted quantum carriers and a fixed channel noise model (e.g., depolarizing channel with single-qudit error rate p, or a multipartite analogue), the asymptotic secret-key rate R(d, N, p) (bits of secure shared key per transmitted carrier) strictly exceeds the corresponding rate R(2, N, p) achievable by any qubit-based MQKA protocol on the same network, for some non-trivial regime of p.

(b) The protocol satisfies fairness in the above sense, with composable security against coalitions of up to N − 1 dishonest participants colluding with an external adversary.

(c) Quantify the threshold noise level p*(d, N) below which positive secret-key generation is possible, and determine how p*(d, N) scales with d and N.

Establish such a protocol together with its security proof and rate analysis, or provide an impossibility result delimiting the achievable trade-off between dimension d, fairness, and noise tolerance in multiparty networks.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in multiparty quantum key agreement. While individual high-dimensional QKD and some bipartite/multiparty qudit-based key agreement schemes have been proposed in the literature, no comprehensive, fairness-preserving, composably secure high-dimensional MQKA protocol with a proven advantage in noise tolerance and key rate over qubit MQKA appears to be established. The status is best described as open.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: circle actions on positively curved manifolds
original_question: If a manifold M has positive sectional curvature, must it admit a faithful S^1-action? If such an action exists, must it be isometric for some positively curved metric?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature (i.e., for every point $p \in M$ and every $2$-plane $\sigma \subset T_pM$, the sectional curvature $K(\sigma) > 0$). A smooth action of the circle group $S^1$ on $M$ is called faithful if the homomorphism $S^1 \to \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ defining it is injective. The action is called isometric with respect to a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ if $S^1$ acts by $g$-isometries.

(a) Must $M$ admit a faithful smooth $S^1$-action?

(b) If $M$ admits a faithful smooth $S^1$-action, must this action be isometric with respect to some Riemannian metric on $M$ of positive sectional curvature?
status_search_result: The classification of positively curved manifolds with symmetry (the Grove symmetry program) remains a very active area, with strong partial results when an isometric torus action of sufficiently high rank is assumed (Hsiang–Kleiner, Grove–Searle, Wilking, etc.), but no general result asserting that every positively curved closed manifold admits a faithful (let alone isometric) circle action is known. Surveys by Ziller and others list the existence of symmetries on positively curved manifolds among the central open problems. No solution to this question was found.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: If G is an Erdős–Rényi random graph distributed as G(n, 1/2), is its Lovász number asymptotically equal to √n in expectation, namely E[ϑ(G)] = (1 + o(1))√n as n → ∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$ denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph on the vertex set $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which every edge of the complete graph $K_n$ is included independently with probability $1/2$. For a finite simple graph $H = (V, E)$, the Lovász theta number $\vartheta(H)$ is defined by
$$\vartheta(H) = \max \sum_{i,j \in V} \langle u_i, u_j \rangle,$$
where the maximum ranges over all unit vectors $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and families $(u_i)_{i \in V}$ of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for any dimension $d \ge 1$) satisfying $\langle u_i, u_i \rangle = \langle c, u_i \rangle$ for every $i \in V$ and $\langle u_i, u_j \rangle = 0$ for every edge $\{i,j\} \in E$. Equivalently, $\vartheta(H)$ is the optimum of the standard semidefinite program associated with the Lovász number.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic: as $n \to \infty$,
$$\mathbb{E}\,\vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1))\sqrt{n}.$$
status_search_result: The precise asymptotics of $\mathbb{E}\,\vartheta(G(n,1/2))$ remain open. Juhász established the order $\Theta(\sqrt{n/p})$ for a wide range of $p$, and recent work (e.g., on random circulant graphs and partial bounds) has narrowed the upper bound to $O(\sqrt{n}\log\log n)$ with matching lower bound up to constants, but the conjectured sharp constant $1$ in front of $\sqrt{n}$ has not been confirmed.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: rational curves from positive bisectional curvature
original_question: Suppose the tangent bundle TM of a manifold M carries a Hermitian metric, not assumed Kähler, with positive bisectional curvature. Can one produce rational curves on M by an analytic method?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact complex manifold whose holomorphic tangent bundle $TM$ admits a Hermitian metric $h$ (not assumed to come from a Kähler metric on $M$) with positive bisectional curvature; that is, the Chern curvature $\Theta(h)$ of $(TM,h)$ satisfies
$$\Theta(h)(X,\overline X,Y,\overline Y) > 0$$
for every pair of nonzero vectors $X,Y \in T_pM$ at every point $p\in M$.

Develop an analytic method (for instance via harmonic maps from $\mathbb{P}^1$, deformation of holomorphic disks, or related variational/PDE techniques, as opposed to purely algebro-geometric bend-and-break arguments) that produces a non-constant holomorphic map $\mathbb{P}^1 \to M$, i.e. a rational curve on $M$, from such a Hermitian metric of positive bisectional curvature.
status_search_result: Searches reveal extensive related work on positive bisectional/real bisectional curvature in the Hermitian (non-Kähler) setting, including criteria for rational connectedness via mean curvature positivity of the tangent bundle and classification results for compact Hermitian manifolds with various positivity conditions. However, no source explicitly resolves the question of constructing rational curves on a compact complex manifold whose tangent bundle carries a (non-Kähler) Hermitian metric with positive bisectional curvature by an analytic method. The status is therefore not clearly established as solved.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Fix M and let N = 4M − 5. Draw a complex matrix A ∈ C^{N×M} at random so that im(A) is uniformly distributed over the Grassmannian of M-dimensional subspaces of C^{4M−5} (for example, A may have i.i.d. Gaussian entries). If p_M denotes the probability that the phaseless measurement map x mod 𝕋 ↦ |Ax|^2 is injective, must one have (a) p_M < 1 for every M and (b) p_M → 0 as M → ∞?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer M ≥ 2 and set N = 4M − 5. Let A ∈ C^{N×M} be a random complex matrix whose image im(A) is distributed according to the unique unitarily invariant (Haar) probability measure on the Grassmannian of M-dimensional complex subspaces of C^{N} (equivalently, A may be taken to have i.i.d. complex Gaussian entries). Consider the phaseless measurement map

  Φ_A : C^M / 𝕋 → R^N,  [x] ↦ (|(Ax)_1|^2, …, |(Ax)_N|^2),

where 𝕋 = {e^{iθ} : θ ∈ R} acts on C^M by global phase. Let

  p_M := Pr(Φ_A is injective on C^M / 𝕋).

Prove or disprove the following two claims:
(a) p_M < 1 for every M ≥ 2.
(b) lim_{M→∞} p_M = 0.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture on the Randomstrasse101 open-problems list (Stable Phase Retrieval, Problems 19–21). It is known in the complex case that 4M−4 generic measurements suffice for injectivity, but at the threshold N = 4M−5 the probability of generic injectivity is conjectured to be strictly less than 1 and to tend to 0 as M → ∞. No proof or disproof has been located in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: uniformization for complete Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature
original_question: Conjecture: every complete Kähler manifold M^n with positive bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to complex Euclidean space C^n.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M^n$ be a connected complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, equipped with a Kähler metric whose holomorphic bisectional curvature is everywhere positive. (Recall that the holomorphic bisectional curvature at a point $p \in M$ is the function that assigns to each pair of nonzero vectors $X, Y \in T_p^{1,0}M$ the quantity $R(X,\bar X, Y, \bar Y)/(\|X\|^2\|Y\|^2)$, where $R$ is the curvature tensor of the Kähler metric.)

Prove or disprove: every such manifold $M^n$ is biholomorphic to complex Euclidean space $\mathbb{C}^n$.
status_search_result: This is Yau's uniformization conjecture, which remains open in full generality. Substantial partial results exist: G. The general conjecture without auxiliary assumptions is still unresolved.

original_question: If A is a real matrix with i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries in the phase-retrieval setting above, what is the typical value of the stability quantity ω(A) = min_{S ⊆ [N] : rank(A_{S^c}) < M} σ_M(A_S)? In particular, does ω(A) satisfy a bound of the type conjectured above, and if so, what exponent β is valid?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a real matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times M}$ with rows $A_1,\dots,A_N$, and for any subset $S\subseteq [N]:=\{1,\dots,N\}$, let $A_S\in\mathbb{R}^{|S|\times M}$ denote the submatrix of rows indexed by $S$, and let $\sigma_M(A_S)$ denote its smallest (i.e., $M$-th) singular value (with $\sigma_M(A_S)=0$ when $|S|<M$). Define the stability quantity
$$\omega(A)\;=\;\min_{\substack{S\subseteq[N]\\ \operatorname{rank}(A_{S^c})<M}}\sigma_M(A_S),$$
where $S^c=[N]\setminus S$.

Specialize to $N=2M-1$, and consider the conjecture: there exist universal constants $C>0$ and $0<\beta<1$ such that for every $M\ge 2$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ in which every $M$ rows are linearly independent,
$$\omega(A)\;\le\;C\,\max_{k\in[N]}\|A_k\|\,\beta^M.$$

Question. Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ have i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. Determine the typical value (e.g., the order of magnitude with high probability as $M\to\infty$) of $\omega(A)$. In particular, decide whether $\omega(A)$ satisfies a bound of the form $\omega(A)\le C\,\max_k\|A_k\|\,\beta^M$ with high probability, and if so identify the optimal admissible exponent $\beta\in(0,1)$.

original_question: Can one prove nonexistence of seven mutually unbiased bases in C^6 using a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares certificate? Equivalently, is there a degree-4 SoS proof that no collection of 7 × 6 vectors in C^6 can satisfy the mutually unbiased basis constraints for seven bases?
self_contained_problem:
A set of orthonormal bases $B_1, \dots, B_m$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$, with $B_k = \{v_1^{(k)}, \dots, v_d^{(k)}\}$, is called a collection of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if for every pair of distinct bases $k \ne \ell$ and every pair of indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, d\}$,
$$|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{d}.$$
For $d = 6$, it is a long-standing open question whether more than three MUBs can exist; in particular, no seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ are known. Encode the existence of seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ as a system of polynomial equations in the real and imaginary parts of the entries of $7 \times 6$ vectors of $\mathbb{C}^6$, consisting of:
(i) the unit-norm and orthogonality constraints making each of the seven sets of six vectors an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^6$, and
(ii) the unbiasedness constraints $|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = 1/6$ for all $k \ne \ell$ and all $i,j$.

A degree-$2t$ Sum-of-Squares (SoS) refutation of this system is an identity
$$-1 = \sigma_0(x) + \sum_a \sigma_a(x)\, p_a(x),$$
where $\{p_a = 0\}$ are the polynomial constraints above (or their natural reformulation), each $\sigma_a$ is a sum of squares of real polynomials, and the total degree of every term $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_a p_a$ is at most $2t$.

Question: Does there exist a degree-$4$ Sum-of-Squares refutation certifying that no seven mutually unbiased bases exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$?
category_tag: Sum-of-Squares hierarchy and mutually unbiased bases
status_search_result: The problem appears open. Prior work has shown that degree-2 SoS / low-level relaxations cannot rule out 7 MUBs in dimension 6, and numerical evidence in related work suggests SoS refutations for stronger statements (e.g. >3 MUBs) may require very high degree (≥12). Whether a degree-4 SoS certificate suffices to refute 7 MUBs in C^6 has not been resolved in the literature found.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: complex Soul-type question for non-negative bisectional curvature
original_question: Suppose N is a complete Kähler manifold with non-negative bisectional curvature. Must N be biholomorphic to a holomorphic vector bundle V over a compact totally geodesic complex submanifold M ⊂ N?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a complete Kähler manifold with non-negative holomorphic bisectional curvature. Must there exist a compact totally geodesic complex submanifold $M \subset N$ and a holomorphic vector bundle $V \to M$ such that $N$ is biholomorphic to the total space of $V$?

(Here, the holomorphic bisectional curvature $H(X,Y)$ for $(1,0)$-type tangent vectors $X,Y$ is the sectional-curvature-like quantity $R(X,\bar X,Y,\bar Y)/(\|X\|^2\|Y\|^2)$, and "non-negative bisectional curvature" means $H(X,Y) \ge 0$ for all such $X,Y$. A submanifold $M \subset N$ is totally geodesic if every geodesic of $N$ tangent to $M$ at a point of $M$ stays in $M$. The question asks whether every such $N$ admits a "complex soul" structure, i.e., is biholomorphically the total space of a holomorphic vector bundle over such an $M$.)
status_search_result: This is a complex analogue of the Cheeger–Gromoll soul theorem, closely related to Yau's uniformization conjecture for complete Kähler manifolds with non-negative holomorphic bisectional curvature. While progress has been made in special cases (e.g., maximal volume growth, low dimension, or under positivity), no general proof of the full statement appears in the literature, and recent surveys treat the broader uniformization program as still ongoing.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Let G_p be the Paley graph on a prime number p ≡ 1 (mod 4), and let ω(G_p) be its clique number. Is ω(G_p) bounded by a polylogarithmic function of p, i.e. does ω(G_p) = O(polylog(p)) hold?
self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, the Paley graph $G_p$ is the graph whose vertex set is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$, with two distinct vertices $x,y \in \mathbb{F}_p$ joined by an edge if and only if $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo $p$ (this relation is symmetric because $-1$ is a square modulo $p$). Let $\omega(G_p)$ denote the clique number of $G_p$, i.e. the largest size of a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ such that $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue for every pair of distinct elements $x, y \in S$.

Determine whether $\omega(G_p)$ grows at most polylogarithmically in $p$. Specifically, do there exist absolute constants $C > 0$ and $k \geq 1$ such that
$$\omega(G_p) \leq C (\log p)^k$$
for every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$? Equivalently, is $\omega(G_p) = O(\mathrm{polylog}(p))$?
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. The best known unconditional upper bound is $\omega(G_p) \leq (1+o(1))\sqrt{p/2}$ due to Hanson and Petridis (2021), far from polylogarithmic. Recent work by Kunisky and Yu (2023) shows the degree-4 sum-of-squares relaxation has value at least $\Omega(p^{1/3})$, so SOS-based methods alone cannot establish a polylog bound at low degree. No proof or refutation of the polylogarithmic conjecture has been reported.

paper_title: Open problems in differential geometry.
context_brief: positive bisectional curvature on total spaces of holomorphic bundles
original_question: For which holomorphic vector bundles over a complex manifold M does the total space admit a complete Kähler or Hermitian metric of positive bisectional curvature? In particular, what conditions, possibly including a stability condition on the bundle, are needed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a complex manifold and let $E \to M$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $r \geq 1$. The total space of $E$ is a complex manifold of dimension $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} M + r$. A Hermitian metric $g$ on a complex manifold $X$ is said to have positive holomorphic bisectional curvature if for every point $x \in X$ and every pair of nonzero $(1,0)$-tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x^{1,0} X$, the bisectional curvature
$$ R(u, \bar u, v, \bar v) > 0. $$
The metric is Kähler if its associated $(1,1)$-form is closed.

Determine, as completely as possible, the holomorphic vector bundles $E \to M$ whose total space admits a complete Kähler (respectively, Hermitian) metric of positive holomorphic bisectional curvature. In particular:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(M, E)$ for the existence of such a metric on the total space of $E$.

(b) Treat the case in which the base $M$ is a Hermitian symmetric space.

(c) Identify whether a stability condition on the bundle $E$ (for instance, slope stability with respect to a chosen polarization on $M$) must be imposed, and if so, formulate the precise stability hypothesis required.
category_tag: complex differential geometry, positive bisectional curvature
status_search_result: The general question appears to remain open. Recent partial results characterize complete Kähler metrics of nonnegative bisectional curvature on total spaces of line bundles over elliptic curves, and study positive holomorphic sectional curvature on certain line bundles (e.g., Hirzebruch manifolds), but no general criterion in terms of the base and a stability condition on the bundle is known. The closely related Greene–Wu–Yau / Yau uniformization conjecture for complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature is also still active.

original_question: Let G_{p,2} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to both 0 and 1 (the 2-localization). For sufficiently large primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4), is its Lovász theta number at most (2/3)√p, i.e. does ϑ(G_{p,2}) ≤ (2/3)√p hold?

paper_title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}}
context_brief: Asymptotically stable 2-cycle for the square-root delay equation when A>15/4.
original_question: Consider the nonlinear delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}} for n=0,1,2,\ldots with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. When A>15/4, does this equation possess an asymptotically stable periodic orbit of prime period two?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear second-order delay difference equation
\[ x_{n+1} \;=\; \frac{A}{x_n^{2}} \;+\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{x_{n-1}}}, \qquad n=0,1,2,\dots, \]
where $A>0$ is a real parameter and the initial conditions $x_{-1}, x_0$ are arbitrary positive real numbers (so that all iterates are positive and well-defined).

A prime period-two solution is a sequence $\{x_n\}$ satisfying $x_{n+2}=x_n$ for all $n$ but $x_{n+1}\neq x_n$; equivalently, it is given by alternating values $\dots,\phi,\psi,\phi,\psi,\dots$ with $\phi\neq\psi$, $\phi,\psi>0$, satisfying
\[ \phi = \frac{A}{\psi^{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\phi}}, \qquad \psi = \frac{A}{\phi^{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\psi}}. \]
Such a 2-cycle is called (locally) asymptotically stable if the corresponding fixed point $(\phi,\psi)$ of the second iterate map (viewed as a map on the positive quadrant via $(x_{n-1},x_n)\mapsto(x_n,x_{n+1})$) is locally asymptotically stable.

Question: Prove or disprove that whenever $A > \tfrac{15}{4}$, the equation admits a prime period-two solution which is asymptotically stable.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of this specific question for the equation $x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}}$. General results on period-two solutions of rational/algebraic delay difference equations exist, but none directly addresses the asymptotic stability of a prime period-two cycle when $A>15/4$ for this equation. The current status appears to be unverified.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Consider the Paley equiangular tight frame associated with a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4). Does this deterministic frame satisfy a restricted isometry property beyond the square-root bottleneck: namely, is there some ε > 0 such that for m ≍ p^{1/2+ε}, every submatrix formed by choosing m distinct frame vectors has condition number bounded by a constant independent of p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and let $\chi$ denote the quadratic (Legendre) character on $\mathbb{F}_p$, extended by $\chi(0)=0$. The Paley equiangular tight frame is the collection of $N=p$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{C}^n$ (with $n=(p-1)/2$, or equivalently the $p\times n$ Paley ETF matrix obtained by an explicit normalization of rows of the Paley conference matrix) such that the inner product of any two distinct vectors has modulus exactly $\sqrt{(N-n)/(n(N-1))}=1/\sqrt{p}$ and the frame is tight.

Equivalently, form the $n \times p$ matrix $\Phi$ whose columns are these unit vectors. For an integer $m \le p$ and a subset $S \subset \{1,\dots,p\}$ with $|S|=m$, let $\Phi_S$ denote the $n \times m$ submatrix of $\Phi$ with columns indexed by $S$, and let $\kappa(\Phi_S)$ denote its condition number (the ratio of its largest to its smallest singular value).

Question: Does there exist a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and a constant $C < \infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and for $m = \lfloor p^{1/2+\varepsilon}\rfloor$, every subset $S \subset \{1,\dots,p\}$ with $|S|=m$ satisfies
$$\kappa(\Phi_S) \le C ?$$

Equivalently, does the Paley equiangular tight frame satisfy the restricted isometry property at sparsity $m \asymp p^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, breaking the square-root bottleneck?
category_tag: Restricted isometry property / equiangular tight frames
status_search_result: The conjecture is widely cited as open. Partial results exist: it is known that the Paley graph conjecture (on clique numbers of Paley graphs) would imply RIP for the Paley matrix beyond the square-root bottleneck, and a Kesten–McKay-type law has been established for random subensembles of the Paley ETF. However, no unconditional proof of the conjectured RIP for the Paley ETF beyond the square-root bottleneck appears in the literature.

x_{n+1}=\frac{a}{x_n^{2}}+\frac{1}{x_{n-1}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots,

\[
p=\frac{a+\sqrt{a^{2}+2-2\sqrt{1+4a^{2}}}}{2},\qquad q=\frac{a-\sqrt{a^{2}+2-2\sqrt{1+4a^{2}}}}{2}.
\]

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
context_brief: Sharp asymptotics for graph matrix norms
original_question: Fix a finite shape α and let M_α be the associated graph matrix built from injective realizations of α into [n], with entries given by products of the corresponding edge-sign variables ε_{i,j}. Do there exist functions f(α) and g(α), depending only on α, such that the expected operator norm satisfies E||M_α|| = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)})? In particular, can one determine the correct polynomial exponent and the correct polylogarithmic factor for every fixed shape α?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite "shape" α, defined as a graph on a vertex set partitioned into two ordered tuples (left and right boundary vertices) U_α and V_α together with additional internal vertices W_α, with edge set E(α). For each integer n ≥ 1 let {ε_{i,j} : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n} be independent ±1 (or independent standard Gaussian) random variables, with ε_{j,i}=ε_{i,j}. The graph matrix M_α associated to α is the matrix whose rows are indexed by injective tuples I ∈ [n]^{|U_α|} and columns by injective tuples J ∈ [n]^{|V_α|}, with entry
   (M_α)_{I,J} = Σ_{φ} ∏_{{u,v} ∈ E(α)} ε_{φ(u),φ(v)},
where the sum runs over all injective maps φ from the vertex set of α into [n] that extend the given assignments on U_α and V_α, and the entry is 0 unless I and J are disjoint as required.

Question: For every fixed shape α, do there exist constants f(α) ∈ ℝ and g(α) ∈ ℝ, depending only on α, such that the expected operator (spectral) norm satisfies
   E‖M_α‖ = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)})
as n → ∞? Equivalently, determine the exact polynomial exponent f(α) and the exact polylogarithmic exponent g(α) for every fixed shape α.
status_search_result: Existing work (Ahn–Medarametla–Potechin and follow-ups, including 2024–2025 papers on switching graph matrix norm bounds and decoupling-based bounds) provides upper bounds on graph matrix norms that are tight up to polylogarithmic factors, but the exact polylogarithmic exponent g(α) and matching lower bounds have not been established for every shape. The conjecture of sharp Θ(n^{f(α)}(log n)^{g(α)}) asymptotics appears to remain open in general.

paper_title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}}
context_brief: Existence, stability, and basins of 2-cycles for Eq. (19).
original_question: Consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,2,\ldots. What conditions on the parameters A, p, and k ensure that this equation has periodic cycles of period two; under what conditions are those period-two cycles stable; and what are their basins of attraction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A>0$, $p>0$, and $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ be parameters. Consider the delay difference equation
$$x_{n+1}=\frac{A}{x_n^{2}}+\frac{1}{x_{n-k}^{\,p}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots,$$
with positive initial conditions $x_{-k},x_{-k+1},\ldots,x_{0}>0$.

A period-two cycle is a pair of distinct positive numbers $(\phi,\psi)$ such that the sequence defined by $x_{-k}=\cdots$ alternating between $\phi$ and $\psi$ (in a way consistent with the recurrence depending on the parity of $k$) satisfies $x_{n+1}=x_{n-1}$ for all $n\ge 0$ and is not constant. The basin of attraction of such a cycle is the set of positive initial conditions $(x_{-k},\ldots,x_0)\in(0,\infty)^{k+1}$ for which the resulting solution converges to the cycle.

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $A$, $p$, and $k$ under which the above equation admits a period-two cycle.

(b) Among such cycles, determine the conditions on $A$, $p$, and $k$ under which they are locally (and/or globally) asymptotically stable.

(c) Describe explicitly the basin of attraction of each stable period-two cycle.
status_search_result: No specific resolution found; the problem appears to remain open in the literature on delay difference equations.

original_question: Describe the divisors of the following subclasses of finite 0-simple semigroups: (1) finite Brandt semigroups; and (2) finite 0-simple semigroups given in Rees matrix form by a matrix whose entries are only 0 and 1.
self_contained_problem:
A finite semigroup S with zero is called 0-simple if S^2 ≠ {0} and S has no two-sided ideals other than {0} and S. By the Rees theorem every finite 0-simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup M^0(G; I, Λ; P) over a finite group G, with index sets I and Λ and a regular Λ×I sandwich matrix P with entries in G ∪ {0}. A finite Brandt semigroup is a finite 0-simple inverse semigroup; equivalently, it is a Rees matrix semigroup M^0(G; I, I; P) with P the I×I identity matrix over G.

Recall that a semigroup T is called a divisor of a semigroup S if T is a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup of S. For a class K of semigroups let D(K) denote the class of all divisors of members of K, i.e. all semigroups isomorphic to a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup of some S ∈ K.

(1) K is the class of all finite Brandt semigroups.

(2) K is the class of all finite 0-simple semigroups whose sandwich matrix in some Rees matrix representation has all entries equal to 0 or 1 (i.e. M^0({1}; I, Λ; P) with P a 0–1 matrix, viewed as a Rees matrix semigroup over the trivial group).

original_question: Describe the identities satisfied by the full transformation semigroup T(n) on an n-element set.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $X$ be an $n$-element set. The full transformation semigroup $T(n)$ is the semigroup of all functions $f : X \to X$ under composition. A semigroup identity is a formal equation $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words in a countable alphabet of variables; a semigroup $S$ satisfies the identity $u = v$ if every substitution of elements of $S$ for the variables makes the two sides equal in $S$. The set of all identities satisfied by $T(n)$ generates the equational theory (variety) of $T(n)$.

Problem: Give an explicit description of all identities satisfied by the full transformation semigroup $T(n)$ on an $n$-element set, for each $n \geq 2$ (equivalently, describe a basis of identities for the variety generated by $T(n)$).
status_search_result: The problem of describing the identities of the full transformation semigroup T(n) is a long-standing open question in semigroup theory. Only partial results are known: certain classes of identities have been described, and short identities (shorter than the natural unary ones) have been constructed for infinitely many n, but no full description / identity basis is known for general n. The problem connects to the words separation problem in automata theory.

paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
original_question: Can gate elimination alone be used to prove a 4n lower bound on the number of gates needed to compute some n-input Boolean function by a Boolean circuit?
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean circuit over the full binary basis B_2 (the set of all Boolean functions {0,1}^2 → {0,1}) is a directed acyclic graph whose sources are labeled by input variables x_1, …, x_n or constants, whose internal nodes (gates) have fan-in 2 and are labeled by functions in B_2, and which has a designated output node; the size of the circuit is the number of gates. The "gate elimination" method is the standard inductive technique for proving circuit-size lower bounds: one identifies a small set of input variables whose restriction (substituting constants 0/1) is guaranteed to eliminate at least k gates from any optimal circuit for the function, yielding by induction a lower bound of the form k·n − O(1) on the circuit size of an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1}.

Question: Does there exist an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1} for which a pure gate-elimination argument can prove that every B_2-circuit computing f_n has size at least 4n − O(1)?
category_tag: Boolean circuit lower bounds via gate elimination
status_search_result: Lower bounds of 4n−O(1), 4.5n−o(n) (Lachish–Raz), and 5n−o(n) (Iwama–Morizumi) have been proved using gate-elimination style arguments, but these are over the U_2 basis (B_2 minus parity/its negation), not the full binary basis B_2 considered here. Over B_2 the best known bound is 3.1n−o(n) (Li–Yang, STOC 2022), and works such as "On the Limits of Gate Elimination" (Golovnev et al., MFCS 2016) explicitly establish barriers for the gate-elimination technique over B_2. Whether a 4n lower bound over B_2 is achievable via pure gate elimination appears to remain open.

original_question: Let c(u) be the number of distinct letters occurring in a non-blocking word u, and let m(u) be the smallest alphabet size for which there exists an infinite word avoiding all substitution images of u. Determine m(u) for a non-blocking word u containing c(u) letters.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^+$ denote the set of finite non-empty words over $A$. A substitution is a map $\sigma : A 	o B^+$ (for some alphabet $B$) extended to a monoid homomorphism $A^+ 	o B^+$ by concatenation. A word $w \in B^\omega$ (finite or infinite) is said to contain a substitution image of $u \in A^+$ if there exist a substitution $\sigma : A 	o B^+$ and a factor $v$ of $w$ such that $v = \sigma(u)$; otherwise $w$ avoids all substitution images of $u$.

A word $u \in A^+$ is called blocking if every sufficiently long word over any finite alphabet contains a substitution image of $u$ (equivalently, no infinite word over any finite alphabet avoids all substitution images of $u$); otherwise $u$ is called non-blocking.

For a word $u$, let $c(u)$ denote the number of distinct letters occurring in $u$, and define
$$ m(u) = \min\{|B| : 	ext{there exists an infinite word over } B 	ext{ that contains no substitution image of } u\},$$
where the minimum is taken over all finite alphabets $B$ (with $m(u) = \infty$ if $u$ is blocking).

Problem. Determine $m(u)$ for every non-blocking word $u$, expressed as a function of $u$ (and in particular of $c(u)$).

Melnichuk, with only partial estimates known in the cited literature. No general solution determining m(u) for all non-blocking words appears in the literature; pattern avoidability remains an active area with only specific cases resolved.

paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
original_question: Can one prove a 5n lower bound for the Boolean-circuit size of an n-input, n-output Boolean function, that is, for some function in B_{n,n}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $B_{n,n}$ denote the set of all Boolean functions $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$ with $n$ inputs and $n$ outputs. The (combinational) circuit size of $f$, denoted $C(f)$, is the minimum number of gates in a Boolean circuit over the full binary basis $B_2$ (the set of all binary Boolean operations) that computes $f$. 

Exhibit an explicit family of functions $f_n \in B_{n,n}$ together with a proof that 
$$C(f_n) \ge 5n - o(n)$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.

original_question: Determine when a system of identical inequalities, also called identical relations of precedence, is equivalent to a system of identities for ordered semigroups.

paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
original_question: Can one improve on brute-force search for the satisfiability problem for Boolean circuits of size 4n on n inputs?
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean circuit on n inputs is a directed acyclic graph whose sources are labeled with input variables x_1,...,x_n (or constants), whose internal nodes (gates) are labeled with binary Boolean operations chosen from the full binary basis B_2 (all functions {0,1}^2 -> {0,1}), and which has one designated output node. paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
context_brief: Producing hard families from small hard functions
original_question: Suppose one starts with a Boolean function on a constant number of inputs that already has high circuit complexity. Can one systematically turn it into a family of n-input Boolean functions whose circuit complexity stays high, rather than losing hardness through the mass production effect?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C(f)$ denote the minimum number of gates in a Boolean circuit over the binary basis $B_2$ (the set of all two-input Boolean functions) that computes a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}$. It is known by counting that for every $k$ there exists a Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^k\to\{0,1\}$ with $C(g) \ge (2^k/k)(1-o(1))$, but no explicit such $g$ is known for super-constant $k$.

Suppose one is given, as an oracle or fixed combinatorial object, a Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^k\to\{0,1\}$ on a constant number $k$ of inputs whose circuit complexity $C(g)$ is as large as possible (i.e., close to $2^k/k$). The question is whether such a hard "seed" $g$ can be used to construct, in a systematic and uniform way, an explicit family $\{f_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\}_{n\ge 1}$ of Boolean functions such that $C(f_n)$ grows superlinearly (or even, ideally, matches the best known existential lower bounds up to constants) as $n\to\infty$.

More precisely: does there exist a polynomial-time (or otherwise effective) procedure that, given the truth table of any Boolean function $g$ on $k$ variables with $C(g)\ge c\cdot 2^k/k$ for some constant $c>0$, outputs a description of an $n$-variable Boolean function $f_n$ (for each $n$) such that $C(f_n) = \omega(n)$, avoiding the "mass production" phenomenon by which natural reductions from a $k$-input hard function only yield circuit lower bounds that vanish in $n$?

The "mass production" obstruction described by Valiant remains unresolved.

paper_title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX
original_question: Let L ∈ Q_b^n, let F be an entire function on C^n, and for r > 0 define G_r^b(F) as the union over zeros z of F of the discs {z + tb : |t| < r/L(z)} along the direction b. For z_0 ∈ C^n, let n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) count the zeros of the slice t ↦ F(z_0 + tb) in the disc |t| ≤ r/L(z_0), and let F(z_0 + tb) ≡ 0 force this quantity to be -1. Is F of bounded L-index in the direction b exactly when both of the following hold: (1) there exist r > 0 and P(r) > 0 such that for every z outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |(1/F(z)) ∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P(r)L(z); and (2) there exist r > 0 and n_e(r) ∈ Z_+ such that for every z_0 with F(z_0 + tb) not identically zero, and every t_0 ∈ C, one has n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) ≤ n_e(r)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $b\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction and let $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous positive function belonging to the class $Q_b^n$, i.e. for every $r>0$,
$$\lambda_b(r):=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{C}^n}\sup_{|t_1|,|t_2|\le r/L(z)}\frac{L(z+t_1 b)}{L(z+t_2 b)}<\infty.$$
Let $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. Recall that $F$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists $m_0\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $m\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^m F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\le \max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_b F(z):=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\partial F/\partial z_j$.

For $r>0$ define the exceptional set
$$G_r^b(F):=\bigcup_{z:\,F(z)=0}\bigl\{z+tb:\,|t|<r/L(z)\bigr\}.$$
For $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$, let $n_b(\rho,z_0,1/F)$ denote the number of zeros (counted with multiplicities) of the entire slice function $t\mapsto F(z_0+tb)$ in the disc $\{t\in\mathbb{C}:|t|\le\rho\}$ when this slice is not identically zero, and set $n_b(\rho,z_0,1/F):=-1$ if $F(z_0+tb)\equiv 0$ in $t$.

Assume $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^b(F)\ne\varnothing$. Decide whether the following equivalence holds:

$F$ is of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if and only if both
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exist $r>0$ and $P(r)>0$ such that
$$\Bigl|\frac{\partial_b F(z)}{F(z)}\Bigr|\le P(r)\,L(z)\quad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^b(F),$$
\item there exist $r>0$ and $n_e(r)\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for every $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ for which $F(z_0+tb)\not\equiv 0$,
$$n_b\bigl(r/L(z_0),z_0,1/F\bigr)\le n_e(r).$$
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: The equivalence is known to hold under the additional restriction $2n(r_2)r_1<r_2/\lambda_b(r_2)$, but whether this technical restriction can be removed appears to remain open. Subsequent works by Bandura and Skaskiv on directional logarithmic derivatives and zero distribution provide criteria of boundedness of $L$-index in direction, but a complete unrestricted proof of the stated equivalence has not been clearly established.

original_question: Let rho(n) be the limiting minimum density of 1s in binary nth-power-free words and extend rho to real exponents x via binary words avoiding factors of exponent at least x. Does rho have discontinuities other than the known right-discontinuities at 7/3 and the integers n >= 3, and is rho piecewise constant?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite or infinite word w over the alphabet {0,1}, the exponent of a nonempty factor u of w is defined as |u|/p, where p is the smallest period of u (so a factor of exponent ≥ n is exactly an n-th power for integer n, and more generally factors of fractional exponent are considered for real exponents). For a real number x ≥ 2, call an infinite binary word x-power-free if it contains no factor of exponent ≥ x. Define the density of 1s in a finite binary word as the number of occurrences of the letter 1 divided by the length of the word, and define the lower density of 1s in an infinite binary word w as the liminf over n → ∞ of the density of 1s in the length-n prefix of w. Let
   ρ(x) = inf { lower density of 1s in w : w is an infinite x-power-free binary word },
defined for all real x ≥ 2 for which x-power-free infinite binary words exist (in particular for x ≥ 2 since binary 2⁺-power-free words such as the Thue–Morse word exist; ρ is also defined at integer values n ≥ 3 via n-th-power-free words). It is known that ρ has right-discontinuities at x = 7/3 and at every integer n ≥ 3.

(a) Determine whether ρ has any discontinuities other than these known right-discontinuities at 7/3 and at the integers n ≥ 3, and if so describe them.

(b) Decide whether ρ is piecewise constant on its domain.

The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
original_question: Describe the endomorphism semigroup and the tower of endomorphisms or automorphisms: (1) for endomorphism semigroups of semigroups that are free in basic classes, especially idempotent, commutative Clifford, and Clifford semigroups; and (2) for endomorphism semigroups of algebras free in basic classes of mathematical structures.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{V}$ be a variety (basic class) of semigroups, in particular one of the following: the variety of idempotent semigroups (bands), the variety of commutative Clifford semigroups, or the variety of Clifford semigroups. (Recall that a Clifford semigroup is a completely regular inverse semigroup, equivalently a semilattice of groups.) For an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, let $F_\mathcal{V}(\kappa)$ denote the free semigroup of rank $\kappa$ in $\mathcal{V}$, and let $\mathrm{End}(F_\mathcal{V}(\kappa))$ denote its semigroup of endomorphisms and $\mathrm{Aut}(F_\mathcal{V}(\kappa))$ its group of automorphisms.

The tower of automorphisms of a group $G$ is the transfinite sequence $G \le \mathrm{Aut}(G) \le \mathrm{Aut}(\mathrm{Aut}(G)) \le \cdots$, where each group is embedded in the next via inner automorphisms; analogously one defines the tower of endomorphism semigroups $S \le \mathrm{End}(S) \le \mathrm{End}(\mathrm{End}(S)) \le \cdots$ via the canonical embedding by inner endomorphisms (left multiplications) where applicable.

Problem.
(1) Give an explicit structural description of the endomorphism semigroup $\mathrm{End}(F_\mathcal{V}(\kappa))$ and of the tower of endomorphisms (respectively automorphisms) of $F_\mathcal{V}(\kappa)$, when $\mathcal{V}$ is one of the basic classes of semigroups, in particular the variety of idempotent semigroups, the variety of commutative Clifford semigroups, and the variety of Clifford semigroups.
(2) More generally, describe the endomorphism semigroup and the tower of endomorphisms (automorphisms) of free algebras in basic classes (varieties) of mathematical structures other than semigroups.
status_search_result: The problem is attributed to G. Mashevitzky and appears in Lyapin's notebook of unsolved problems in semigroup theory. While the endomorphism semigroups of free objects in the variety of all semigroups and of inverse semigroups, and the towers of automorphisms of free inverse semigroups, have been described in earlier literature, the analogous descriptions for free idempotent, free commutative Clifford, free Clifford semigroups, and more general free algebras remain open. No conclusive resolution was located.

original_question: Kirby Baker, Georges F. McNulty and Walter Taylor have shown that the pattern abXbcYcaZbaTac is 4-avoidable, but not 3- avoidable [8]. What is the minimal proportion of the fourth letter needed to avoid that pattern?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_k=\{0,1,\dots,k-1\}$ be a finite alphabet. A pattern is a word $p$ over an alphabet of variables. An infinite word $w\in\Sigma_k^{\mathbb N}$ is said to encounter $p$ if there exists a non-erasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to $\Sigma_k^{+}$ such that $h(p)$ is a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The pattern $p$ is $k$-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over $\Sigma_k$ avoiding $p$.

Consider the pattern 
$$p \;=\; ab\,X\,bc\,Y\,ca\,Z\,ba\,T\,ac,$$
on the variable alphabet $\{a,b,c,X,Y,Z,T\}$. It is known that $p$ is $4$-avoidable but not $3$-avoidable.

For an infinite word $w$ over $\Sigma_4=\{0,1,2,3\}$, let
$$\mathrm{freq}_w(\alpha) \;=\; \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{|w[1..n]|_{\alpha}}{n}$$
denote the (lower) frequency of letter $\alpha$ in $w$.

Determine the value of
$$\mu \;=\; \inf\Bigl\{\,\max_{\alpha\in\Sigma_4}\bigl(1 - 3\,\mathrm{freq}_w(\alpha)\bigr)\,\Bigr\}^{-1}\quad\text{(equivalently)}$$
$$\mu \;=\; \inf_{w}\;\min_{\alpha\in\Sigma_4}\mathrm{freq}_w(\alpha),$$
where the infimum is taken over all infinite words $w\in\Sigma_4^{\mathbb N}$ that avoid the pattern $p$. In other words, what is the minimal possible asymptotic proportion of the least-frequent (fourth) letter in an infinite $4$-letter word avoiding $ab\,X\,bc\,Y\,ca\,Z\,ba\,T\,ac$?
status_search_result: Searches in the combinatorics-on-words literature (Ochem and collaborators, palindrome/pattern-avoidance surveys, HDOL constructions) did not yield a published value of the minimal frequency of the fourth letter in infinite 4-letter words avoiding the pattern abXbcYcaZbaTac. The question, originally raised by Baker, McNulty and Taylor and reposed in the WORDS open-problems compilation, appears to remain open.

paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Given a pattern p, what is the complexity of deciding whether p is avoidable?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet of letters and let E be a disjoint countably infinite alphabet of variables. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E*. An occurrence of p in a word w ∈ A* is the image h(p) of p under a non-erasing morphism h : E* → A* such that h(p) is a factor of w. An infinite word w over A is said to avoid p if no factor of w is an occurrence of p. The pattern p is called avoidable if there exists some finite alphabet A and some infinite word over A that avoids p; otherwise p is called unavoidable.

It is known (Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty, Zimin) that avoidability of patterns is decidable. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

  Input: a pattern p ∈ E*.
  Question: is p avoidable?

That is, determine the precise complexity class (e.g., in P, NP-complete, coNP-complete, PSPACE-complete, etc.) of deciding pattern avoidability.
status_search_result: Deciding whether a pattern is unavoidable is known to be coNP-complete (equivalently, deciding avoidability is NP-complete), as established for the unavoidability problem and reported in recent work on "The Complexity of Unavoidable Word Patterns" (Theory of Computing Systems, 2022). However, fine-grained questions about the complexity of avoidability for restricted classes of patterns and related variants remain active. The general decidability question has long been answered, while the precise complexity classification matching upper and lower bounds appears settled at NP-completeness for the basic version.

context_brief: Complete solvability for regular aperiodic semigroups
original_question: Determine whether the class of finite regular aperiodic semigroups is completely solvable, where a semigroup is aperiodic when all of its subgroups are trivial.
self_contained_problem:
A finite semigroup is called aperiodic if every subgroup contained in it is trivial (equivalently, for every element $s$ there exists $n\ge 1$ with $s^n = s^{n+1}$). A semigroup is called regular if for every element $a$ there exists an element $x$ such that $a x a = a$.

A class $\mathcal{C}$ of finite semigroups is said to be completely solvable if there exists an algorithm which, given a finite semigroup $S \in \mathcal{C}$ presented by its multiplication table, decides every basic algorithmic predicate for $S$ — in particular, given any finite subset $A \subseteq S$ and an element $b \in S$, decides whether $b$ belongs to the subsemigroup of $S$ generated by $A$ (the membership/divisibility problem), whether $b$ lies in the ideal generated by $A$, and whether $b$ lies in the maximal subgroup determined by $A$.

Question: Is the class of all finite regular aperiodic semigroups completely solvable?

A web search did not surface any published resolution; related results by Kublanovsky show non-recursiveness of subsemigroup membership for some classes of finite completely 0-simple semigroups, but the specific question for finite regular aperiodic semigroups appears to remain open.

Background. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet. A morphism $g:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ is called prolongable on a letter $a\in\Sigma$ if $g(a)$ starts with $a$ and $|g^n(a)|\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$; in this case the iterated images $g^n(a)$ converge to a unique infinite word $g^\omega(a)\in\Sigma^\omega$, called the pure morphic (D0L) word generated by $g$ from $a$.

An infinite word $w$ over $\Sigma$ is said to avoid $p$ if there is no nonerasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to $\Sigma^+$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$. We say $p$ is $k$-D0L-avoidable if there exists an alphabet $\Sigma$ with $|\Sigma|=k$, a morphism $g:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ prolongable on some letter $a\in\Sigma$, such that the infinite word $g^\omega(a)$ avoids $p$.

Does there exist a morphism $g:\{0,1,2\}^*\to\{0,1,2\}^*$ prolongable on some letter $\alpha\in\{0,1,2\}$ such that the infinite word $g^\omega(\alpha)$ contains no factor of the form $h(aabaacbaab)$ for any nonerasing morphism $h:\{a,b,c\}^+\to\{0,1,2\}^+$? self_contained_problem:
For a class $\Phi$ of semigroups, let $H$, $S$, $P$, $P_S$ denote the standard Birkhoff-style class operators: $H(\Phi)$ is the class of all homomorphic images of members of $\Phi$, $S(\Phi)$ the class of all subsemigroups of members of $\Phi$, $P(\Phi)$ the class of all direct products of members of $\Phi$, and $P_S(\Phi)$ the class of all subdirect products of members of $\Phi$. Composing these one forms the operators

$$HP,\quad HP_S,\quad SHP,\quad SHP_S,$$

applied in the indicated order to $\Phi$. The variety generated by a semigroup $M$ is $HSP(M)$.

Given a class $\mathcal{C}$ of semigroups, define its kernel by
$$\operatorname{Cor}(\mathcal{C}) \;=\; \{\,M \in \mathcal{C} \;:\; HSP(M) \subseteq \mathcal{C}\,\}.$$

A class $\mathcal{D}$ of finite semigroups is called decidable if there exists an algorithm that, on input a finite semigroup $M$ (given by its multiplication table), decides whether $M \in \mathcal{D}$.

original_question: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k<= 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [39]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.

For a real number $\alpha > 1$, a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n \in \Sigma_k^*$ is called an $\alpha$-power if it can be written as $w = u^p v$ where $u$ is a nonempty word, $p \geq 1$ is an integer, $v$ is a (possibly empty) prefix of $u$, and $|w|/|u| = \alpha$. A word is $\alpha$-power-free if none of its factors is a $\beta$-power for any $\beta \geq \alpha$. Let $L_k(\alpha, n)$ denote the number of $\alpha$-power-free words of length $n$ over $\Sigma_k$.

It is known that for $k = 2$ there exists a threshold $\alpha^*_2 = 7/3$ such that $L_2(\alpha, n)$ grows polynomially in $n$ for $\alpha \leq 7/3$ and exponentially in $n$ for $\alpha > 7/3$.

Shur and others established asymptotic growth rates for $\beta$-power-free languages over $k$-letter alphabets, and a 2025 result (Dagstuhl/MFCS) proves Shur's conjecture on the exponential growth rates of $(k/(k-1))$-free and $(k/(k-1))^+$-free languages over large alphabets, with $O(1/k^2)$ corrections. The "exponential conjecture" (that for $k \geq 3$ all infinite power-free languages over $k$ letters have exponential size at the Dejean threshold) has been confirmed in several regimes. Thus the analogue of the binary 7/3 threshold is partially understood: the threshold is conjecturally the Dejean repetition threshold $k/(k-1)$, with strong supporting results, but a complete characterization for all $k$ matching the binary case is not fully settled.

original_question: Find an analogue of Birkhoff’s theorem for inclusive varieties by determining a minimal set of Birkhoff-type operators such that a class of semigroups is an inclusive variety if and only if it is closed under those operators.

Background. A semigroup is a set equipped with an associative binary operation. An identical inclusion (over a countable alphabet X) is a formal expression of the form w ⊆ {w₁, …, wₙ}, where w, w₁, …, wₙ are words in X⁺. original_question: Study inclusive varieties by: (1) finding minimal and maximal inclusive varieties of semigroups that cannot be defined by elementary identical inclusions; (2) describing elementary inclusive varieties all of whose inclusive subvarieties are elementary; and (3) describing nonelementary inclusive varieties of periodic semigroups whose inclusive supervarieties inside periodic semigroups are nonelementary.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S$ be a semigroup and let $X$ be a countably infinite alphabet. An identical inclusion (or inclusion identity) on $S$ is a formal expression of the form
$$ w \subseteq \{w_1, w_2, \dots, w_n\}, $$
where $w, w_1, \dots, w_n$ are words in the free semigroup $X^+$. The semigroup $S$ is said to satisfy this identical inclusion if for every homomorphism $\varphi : X^+ \to S$ one has $\varphi(w) \in \{\varphi(w_1), \dots, \varphi(w_n)\}$. The identical inclusion is called elementary if $n = 1$, i.e. it has the form $w \subseteq \{w_1\}$ (equivalently, an ordinary identity $w = w_1$).

A class $\mathcal V$ of semigroups is called an inclusive variety if there exists a set $\Sigma$ of identical inclusions such that $\mathcal V$ is exactly the class of all semigroups satisfying every member of $\Sigma$. The inclusive variety $\mathcal V$ is called elementary if it can be defined by a set of elementary identical inclusions (equivalently, by ordinary identities); otherwise it is called nonelementary. Two semigroups are inclusively equivalent if they satisfy the same identical inclusions, equivalently if they generate the same inclusive variety. An inclusive subvariety of $\mathcal V$ is an inclusive variety contained in $\mathcal V$, and an inclusive supervariety is one that contains $\mathcal V$. A semigroup is periodic if every one of its monogenic subsemigroups is finite.

Problem. Investigate the lattice of inclusive varieties of semigroups by addressing the following three tasks.

(1) Determine the minimal, and the maximal, inclusive varieties of semigroups that cannot be defined by any set of elementary identical inclusions (i.e. classify the atoms and coatoms among nonelementary inclusive varieties).

(2) Describe all elementary inclusive varieties of semigroups with the property that every inclusive subvariety of them is again elementary.

(3) Describe all nonelementary inclusive varieties of periodic semigroups whose inclusive supervarieties, taken within the class of periodic semigroups, are all nonelementary.

self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $S$ be a semigroup, and let $X = \{x_1, x_2, \dots\}$ be a countably infinite set of variables. Denote by $X^+$ the free semigroup on $X$. An identical inclusion (also called an inclusive identity) over $S$ is a formal expression of the form
$$ w \subseteq \{u_1, u_2, \dots, u_k\}, $$
where $w, u_1, \dots, u_k \in X^+$. The semigroup $S$ is said to satisfy this identical inclusion if for every homomorphism (substitution) $\varphi : X^+ \to S$ one has
$$ \varphi(w) \in \{\varphi(u_1), \varphi(u_2), \dots, \varphi(u_k)\}. $$
The set of all identical inclusions satisfied by $S$ is called the inclusive theory of $S$.

Two semigroups $S$ and $T$ are said to satisfy the same identical inclusions if their inclusive theories coincide. A semigroup $S$ is determined by its identical inclusions up to isomorphism if every semigroup $T$ satisfying exactly the same identical inclusions as $S$ is isomorphic to $S$.

Known examples of semigroups that are determined by their identical inclusions up to isomorphism include:
- the two-element semilattice;
- every quasicyclic group (Prüfer $p$-group) $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$;
- every finite group.

Within the basic classes of semigroups (such as semilattices, bands, completely simple semigroups, inverse semigroups, periodic semigroups, commutative semigroups, etc.), characterize, or exhibit further families of, the semigroups that are determined up to isomorphism by their identical inclusions.

context_brief: Infinite inclusive-subvariety lattices from finite generators
original_question: Determine whether there exists a finite semigroup that generates an inclusive variety with an infinite lattice of inclusive subvarieties.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A semigroup is a set equipped with an associative binary operation. An identical inclusion (or inclusion identity) over a countable alphabet of variables is a formal expression of the form $W \subseteq \{w_1, w_2, \dots, w_k\}$, where $W$ and $w_1,\dots,w_k$ are semigroup words. A semigroup $S$ satisfies the inclusion $W \subseteq \{w_1,\dots,w_k\}$ if, for every assignment of the variables of $W,w_1,\dots,w_k$ to elements of $S$, the value of $W$ in $S$ coincides with the value of $w_i$ for at least one $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$.

A class $\mathcal{V}$ of semigroups is called an inclusive variety if it is the class of all semigroups satisfying some (possibly infinite) set of identical inclusions. Inclusive subvarieties of $\mathcal{V}$ are inclusive varieties contained in $\mathcal{V}$; under inclusion, they form a complete lattice $L_{\mathrm{incl}}(\mathcal{V})$.

For a semigroup $S$, the inclusive variety generated by $S$, denoted $\mathrm{Var}^{\subseteq}(S)$, is the smallest inclusive variety containing $S$ (equivalently, the class of all semigroups satisfying every identical inclusion that holds in $S$).

Problem. Does there exist a finite semigroup $S$ such that the lattice $L_{\mathrm{incl}}(\mathrm{Var}^{\subseteq}(S))$ of inclusive subvarieties of the inclusive variety generated by $S$ is infinite?

original_question: For a conducting sequence beta in {0,1}*, which words u can be shuffled with themselves to obtain a unique square-free word?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form $xx$ (i.e., no nonempty word repeated twice consecutively appears as a contiguous block of $w$).

For two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ of lengths $m$ and $n$ respectively, and a binary "conducting sequence" $\beta \in \{0,1\}^{m+n}$ containing exactly $m$ zeros and $n$ ones, the shuffle of $u$ and $v$ controlled by $\beta$, denoted $u \shuffle_\beta v$, is the unique word of length $m+n$ obtained by reading the $i$-th letter from $u$ when the $i$-th symbol of $\beta$ is $0$ (in order) and from $v$ when it is $1$ (in order).

Define a self-shuffle of $u$ as any word of the form $u \shuffle_\beta u$ where $\beta \in \{0,1\}^{2|u|}$ has exactly $|u|$ zeros and $|u|$ ones.

Problem: Characterize all words $u \in \Sigma^*$ for which there exists a conducting sequence $\beta$ such that $u \shuffle_\beta u$ is square-free, and moreover such a square-free self-shuffle is unique (i.e., $u \shuffle_\beta u$ is square-free for exactly one $\beta$).
