paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Describe the structure of the Rauzy graphs of words reaching the mentioned supremum.
self_contained_problem:
Let $u$ be a uniformly recurrent infinite word over a finite alphabet. For each integer $n\ge 0$, let $\mathcal L_n(u)$ denote the set of factors of $u$ of length $n$, and define the factor complexity $p(n)=\#\mathcal L_n(u)$ and the palindromic complexity $P(n)=\#\{w\in\mathcal L_n(u):w\text{ is a palindrome}\}$. Set $\Delta p(n)=p(n+1)-p(n)$. It is known that for every uniformly recurrent infinite word $u$ and every $n\ge 0$ one has
$$P(n)+P(n+1)\le \Delta p(n)+2.$$
The Rauzy graph $\Gamma_n(u)$ of order $n$ is the directed graph whose vertex set is $\mathcal L_n(u)$ and whose edge set is $\mathcal L_{n+1}(u)$, where an edge labelled $w\in\mathcal L_{n+1}(u)$ goes from the prefix of $w$ of length $n$ to the suffix of $w$ of length $n$.

Describe the structure of the Rauzy graphs $\Gamma_n(u)$ of those uniformly recurrent infinite words $u$ for which the above inequality is attained with equality (equivalently, for which the supremum $P(n)+P(n+1)=\Delta p(n)+2$ is reached).
status_search_result: The problem comes from a list of open problems posed at the WORDS conferences. Searches reveal active subsequent research on palindromic complexity and Rauzy graphs (e.g., on rich/closed-rich words and palindromic defect), but no source explicitly announces a complete structural description of the Rauzy graphs of uniformly recurrent words attaining equality in the bound $P(n)+P(n+1)\le \Delta p(n)+2$. The status thus appears to be unresolved in general.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
context_brief: Chow rings for regular noetherian schemes
original_question: For a regular noetherian scheme X admitting an ample invertible module, can one define rational equivalence of cycles and construct a Chow ring A(X) that generalizes the known construction for schemes smooth over a field? In particular, can one prove a moving lemma ensuring that a cycle can be moved within its class so as to meet a given cycle in the correct dimension, study the resulting ring's functorial properties, compare it with Gr'_top(X), and formulate the denominator-free Riemann-Roch problem in terms of this Chow ring?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a regular noetherian scheme that admits an ample invertible sheaf. For each integer $p \ge 0$, let $Z^p(X)$ denote the free abelian group on the irreducible closed subschemes of $X$ of codimension $p$.

(a) Define a notion of rational equivalence on $Z^p(X)$ and form the resulting graded abelian group $A^\bullet(X) = \bigoplus_p Z^p(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, in such a way that, when $X$ is smooth over a field, the construction recovers the classical Chow ring.

(b) Establish a "moving lemma" in this generality: given cycles $\alpha \in Z^p(X)$ and $\beta \in Z^q(X)$, prove that within the rational equivalence class of $\alpha$ one can find a representative $\alpha'$ such that every component of the set-theoretic intersection $|\alpha'| \cap |\beta|$ has codimension $p+q$ in $X$.

(c) Use the moving lemma in (b) to define an intersection product making $A^\bullet(X)$ a graded commutative ring, and develop its functorial properties (pullback along arbitrary morphisms when defined, proper pushforward, projection formula, compatibility with flat base change).

(d) Let $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ denote the graded ring associated to the topological filtration on the Grothendieck group $K_0(X)$ of coherent sheaves (the filtration by codimension of support), tensored or not with $\mathbb{Q}$ as appropriate. Compare $A^\bullet(X)$ with $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$, generalizing the relations (and conjectured relations) known in the smooth-over-a-field case: in particular, identify the kernel and cokernel of the natural cycle-class map $A^\bullet(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ up to torsion.

(e) In terms of $A^\bullet(X)$, formulate and study the "denominator-free Riemann–Roch problem" for proper morphisms $f \colon Y \to X$ of regular noetherian schemes admitting ample invertible sheaves: namely, produce a Riemann–Roch type formula relating $f_*$ on $K_0$ to $f_*$ on $A^\bullet$ via Chern character / Todd-class data, with the Todd correction expressed using only integral classes (no denominators) in $A^\bullet$.
status_search_result: A general construction of a Chow ring with all expected functorial properties for arbitrary regular noetherian schemes admitting an ample invertible sheaf, together with a moving lemma in that generality, comparison with the topological filtration on $K_0$, and a denominator-free Riemann–Roch formula, is not known. Partial results exist: Fulton's operational Chow groups, Gillet's K-theoretic intersection product on regular separated schemes (which gives a $\mathbb{Q}$-intersection theory but does not produce an integral Chow ring with a moving lemma), and various moving lemmas in special cases (quasi-projective over a field, higher Chow groups with modulus by Krishna–Park and others). The full problem as formulated remains open.

paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: What is the number of rich words of a given length?
self_contained_problem:
A finite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ is called *rich* (or *full*) if it contains exactly $|w|+1$ distinct palindromic factors (including the empty word), which is the maximum possible number of distinct palindromic factors of a word of length $|w|$. For an integer $q\ge 2$ and an integer $n\ge 0$, let $R_q(n)$ denote the number of rich words of length $n$ over an alphabet of cardinality $q$.

Determine $R_q(n)$ exactly, i.e., give a closed-form expression (or an exact enumeration formula) for the number of rich words of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. In particular, settle the case $q=2$ of binary rich words.
category_tag: Combinatorics on words / rich words enumeration
status_search_result: No exact formula for the number $R_q(n)$ of rich words of length $n$ is known. Only bounds and growth-rate results have been established: it is known that $\lim_{n\to\infty} R_q(n)^{1/n}=1$ (subexponential growth), and a 2025 preprint provides the first explicit subexponential upper bound of the form involving iterated logarithms. A binary upper bound $R_2(n)\le c\cdot 1.605^n$ has also been recorded. The enumeration problem itself remains open.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Let D be a divisor in complex projective space P^n with normal crossings, meaning that D is a sum of distinct smooth irreducible hypersurfaces with multiplicity one and, at each point, the local defining equations of the components through that point form part of a holomorphic coordinate system. In terms of deg(D), the total degree of D, and #(D), the number of components of D, what conditions ensure that every holomorphic mapping f: C^m -> P^n \ D is necessarily constant?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^n$ denote complex projective $n$-space. A divisor $D \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is said to have normal crossings if $D = D_1 + D_2 + \cdots + D_q$ is a sum of distinct smooth irreducible hypersurfaces $D_1, \dots, D_q$, each appearing with multiplicity one, and if at every point $p \in \mathbb{P}^n$ the local holomorphic defining equations of those components $D_i$ that pass through $p$ form part of a system of holomorphic local coordinates at $p$. Write $\deg(D) = \sum_{i=1}^{q} \deg(D_i)$ for the total degree and $\#(D) = q$ for the number of components.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the two integers $\deg(D)$ and $\#(D)$ (and the dimensions $m, n$), such that for every positive integer $m$ every holomorphic mapping
$$ f : \mathbb{C}^m \longrightarrow \mathbb{P}^n \setminus D $$
must be constant.
status_search_result: The general Picard-type problem of characterizing, in terms of total degree and number of components, when the complement of a normal-crossings divisor in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is Brody/Kobayashi hyperbolic (or admits only constant entire maps) is a longstanding open problem in value distribution theory. Partial results are known (e.g. constancy when components are in general position with $q \ge n+2$ hyperplanes by Borel/Fujimoto/Green, and various sufficient degree bounds for hypersurfaces), but a complete characterization purely in terms of $\deg(D)$ and $\#(D)$ is not established. Recent work (e.g. on Fermat-type and general normal-crossings configurations) continues to provide only partial answers.

paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
original_question: If u is a palindromic fixed point of a primitive morphism, must there exist a class P₀ morphism whose fixed point has the same language as u?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the free monoid of finite words over A. A morphism φ: A* → A* is called primitive if there exists an integer n ≥ 1 such that, for every pair of letters a, b ∈ A, the letter b occurs in φ^n(a). An infinite word u ∈ A^ℕ is a fixed point of φ if φ(u) = u. The language L(u) of u is the set of all finite factors (contiguous subwords) of u. A finite word w is a palindrome if it equals its reverse. The infinite word u is called palindromic if L(u) contains infinitely many palindromes.

A morphism φ: A* → A* is said to belong to class P₀ if there exist a palindrome p ∈ A* and palindromes q_a ∈ A* (one for each a ∈ A) such that φ(a) = p q_a for every a ∈ A.

Question: Suppose u is a palindromic infinite word that is a fixed point of some primitive morphism. Must there exist a morphism ψ of class P₀ admitting a fixed point v with L(v) = L(u)?
status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Hof, Knill and Simon) is resolved in the negative: a ternary counterexample to the class-P question was provided by Labbé (2014, Electronic J. Combinatorics; arXiv:1307.1589). The binary case was confirmed earlier (B. Tan, 2007). Subsequent work (Labbé–Pelantová, 2015) shows that, up to conjugacy, primitive palindromic substitutive subshifts are generated by morphisms close to but not always exactly of class P, so the original question has a negative answer in general.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Let f: C^m -> P^n be a holomorphic mapping. Let |D| be the complete linear system of divisors of degree d in P^n, and let D_1,...,D_t be smooth divisors in |D| such that D_1+...+D_t has normal crossings. Assume f(C^m) is not contained in any divisor in |D|. For the Nevanlinna defects delta(D_j), defined from the counting function N(D,r) and order function T(r) by delta(D)=1-limsup_{r->infinity} N(D,r)/T(r), is sum_{j=1}^t delta(D_j) <= (n+1)/d?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f : \mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n(\mathbb{C})$ be a holomorphic mapping. For a divisor $D$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ not containing the image $f(\mathbb{C}^m)$, define the Nevanlinna order (characteristic) function $T(r)$ of $f$ with respect to the hyperplane bundle and the counting function $N(D,r)$ of the pullback divisor $f^*D$ in the standard way, and set the Nevanlinna defect
$$\delta(D) \;=\; 1 - \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{N(D,r)}{T(r)} \in [0,1].$$
Fix a positive integer $d$ and let $|D|$ denote the complete linear system of divisors of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$. Suppose $D_1,\dots,D_t \in |D|$ are smooth divisors such that the divisor $D_1 + \cdots + D_t$ has only simple normal crossings, and assume that $f(\mathbb{C}^m)$ is not contained in any divisor of $|D|$.

Prove or disprove: under these assumptions
$$\sum_{j=1}^{t} \delta(D_j) \;\leq\; \frac{n+1}{d}.$$

Min Ru (2004) proved the weaker Shiffman conjecture sum δ(D_j) ≤ n+1 for hypersurfaces in general position when f is algebraically nondegenerate, and later extensions handle further cases, but the sharp bound (n+1)/d for smooth divisors with normal crossings (and for holomorphic maps from C^m, not only curves) is generally regarded as still open in this generality.

paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
context_brief: Sets of sequences of a given complexity
original_question: Can one find an analogue of the FC algorithm in dimension d >= 4 that generates S-adic sequences of complexity (d-1)n+1 for almost every vector of letter frequencies?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For an infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$, the factor complexity $p_w(n)$ is the number of distinct factors of length $n$ that occur in $w$. An $S$-adic sequence is an infinite word produced by an infinite composition of substitutions $\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \ldots$ chosen from a finite or countable set $S$ of substitutions on $A$, in the sense that $w = \lim_{k\to\infty} \sigma_1\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_k(a_k)$ for suitable letters $a_k \in A$. For a word $w$ on a $d$-letter alphabet, the vector of letter frequencies is the vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d) \in \Delta_{d-1} = \{(x_1,\ldots,x_d) : x_i \ge 0,\ \sum x_i = 1\}$ where $f_i = \lim_{n\to\infty} |w_1\cdots w_n|_i / n$ (when the limits exist), with $|u|_i$ denoting the number of occurrences of letter $i$ in $u$.

A known three-letter construction (often called the FC algorithm), based on a multidimensional continued fraction algorithm, produces, for Lebesgue-almost every frequency vector $(f_1,f_2,f_3)\in\Delta_2$, an $S$-adic sequence on a 3-letter alphabet with factor complexity $p(n) = 2n+1$ for all $n\ge 0$.

Problem. For each integer $d \ge 4$, does there exist an algorithm analogous to the FC algorithm — specifically, a finite set $S$ of substitutions on a $d$-letter alphabet together with a rule (driven by a multidimensional continued fraction-type algorithm) for selecting an infinite sequence of substitutions from $S$ — such that for Lebesgue-almost every letter-frequency vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d) \in \Delta_{d-1}$, the resulting $S$-adic sequence has letter frequency vector $(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$ and factor complexity $p(n) = (d-1)n + 1$ for all $n \ge 0$?
status_search_result: The d=3 case (complexity 2n+1 for almost every frequency vector via a multidimensional continued fraction algorithm conjugate to Selmer / FC) is established. For d ≥ 4, no analogous construction producing S-adic sequences of complexity (d−1)n+1 for almost every frequency vector appears to be known; existing higher-dimensional algorithms (Arnoux–Rauzy–Poincaré, Brun, Selmer, etc.) do not achieve the minimal complexity (d−1)n+1 almost everywhere. Recent work (e.g. on symbolic codings of generic toral translations) addresses related but distinct questions, suggesting the problem remains open.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Let V be a smooth projective variety with canonical bundle K_V and let L be a positive line bundle. Let D_1,...,D_t be smooth divisors in the complete linear system |L| such that D_1+...+D_t has normal crossings. Suppose f:C -> V is a holomorphic curve whose image is not contained in any divisor in |L+K_V|. With Nevanlinna defects delta(D_j) and the Chern-class comparison notation in which lambda > [alpha/beta] means lambda beta - alpha is represented by a positive definite (1,1)-form, is sum_{j=1}^t delta(D_j) <= [c_1(K_V)/c_1(L)]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a smooth complex projective variety with canonical line bundle $K_V$, and let $L$ be a positive (ample) line bundle on $V$. Suppose $D_1,\dots,D_t$ are smooth divisors, each belonging to the complete linear system $|L|$, such that the sum $D_1+\cdots+D_t$ has only normal crossings. Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to V$ be a (nonconstant) holomorphic curve whose image is not contained in any divisor of the linear system $|L+K_V|$. Define the Nevanlinna defect of a divisor $D$ for $f$ in the standard way as
$$\delta(D)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{m_f(r,D)+N_f(r,D)\;\text{(appropriate combination)}}{T_{f,L}(r)},$$
i.e., the usual Nevanlinna defect attached to $D$ relative to a Weil function and the order function $T_{f,L}$. For two real $(1,1)$-cohomology classes one writes $\lambda>[\alpha/\beta]$ (with $\beta$ represented by a positive form) to mean that $\lambda\,\beta-\alpha$ is represented by a positive definite $(1,1)$-form, and similarly for "$\le$".

Prove or disprove the following inequality:

(ii) Count the number of distinct $\mathcal{F}$-factorizations of $w$.
(iii) Compute an $\mathcal{F}$-factorization of $w$ that minimizes (respectively maximizes) the number of factors $k$.

original_question: Is the polynomial-time class P-TIME equal to the nondeterministic polynomial-time class NP-TIME? Equivalently, does every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in polynomial time also admit a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm?
self_contained_problem:
Let P denote the class of languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine $M$ and a polynomial $p$ such that $M$ decides $L$ and halts on every input $x$ within $p(|x|)$ steps. Let NP denote the class of languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exists a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a polynomial $q$ such that $x \in L$ if and only if some computation branch of $N$ on input $x$ accepts within $q(|x|)$ steps. Equivalently, $L \in \mathrm{NP}$ if there is a polynomial-time deterministic verifier $V$ and a polynomial $r$ such that $x \in L$ iff there exists a string $y$ with $|y| \le r(|x|)$ and $V(x,y)$ accepts.

Decide whether $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$: that is, prove that every language in NP is also in P, or prove that there exists a language in NP that is not in P.
status_search_result: The P vs NP problem is one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains open as of 2026. No accepted proof in either direction exists.

original_question: Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f(a), is it decidable whether the fixed point f^ω(a) is quasiperiodic?

Let A be a finite alphabet, and let A* (resp. A^ω) denote the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over A. A morphism f : A* → A* extends to A^ω by concatenation. A finite nonempty word q ∈ A* is called a quasiperiod of an infinite word w ∈ A^ω if every position of w lies inside at least one occurrence of q in w (equivalently, w can be covered by occurrences of q). The infinite word w is called quasiperiodic if it admits at least one quasiperiod.

  Input: a finite alphabet A, a morphism f : A* → A*, and a letter a ∈ A such that f(a) begins with a (so that the fixed point f^ω(a) is well-defined as an infinite word).
  Question: Is f^ω(a) quasiperiodic?

That is, does there exist an algorithm that, given any such (A, f, a), decides whether the pure morphic fixed point f^ω(a) admits a quasiperiod?

Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ (resp. $A^\omega$) denote the set of finite (resp. infinite) words over $A$. (i) Given a morphism $\varphi : A^* \to A^*$, decide whether $\varphi$ is weakly quasiperiodic on finite words.
(ii) Given a morphism $\varphi : A^* \to A^*$, decide whether $\varphi$ is weakly quasiperiodic on infinite words.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
original_question: For every space bound S(n) greater than log n, does giving a space-bounded Turing machine an auxiliary pushdown stack fail to increase its computational power? Equivalently, is the class PDM(S(n)) of languages accepted by pushdown-stack Turing machines using O(S(n)) counted work-tape space equal to DSPACE(S(n))?
self_contained_problem:
A space-bounded deterministic Turing machine with an auxiliary pushdown stack is a deterministic Turing machine equipped with: (i) a read-only input tape, (ii) one or more two-way read/write work tapes whose used cells are counted toward the space bound, and (iii) an additional pushdown stack whose contents are not counted toward the space bound. For a function S: ℕ → ℕ, let PDM(S(n)) denote the class of languages accepted by such machines that, on every input of length n, use at most O(S(n)) cells on the counted work tapes (the pushdown stack may grow arbitrarily). Let DSPACE(S(n)) denote the class of languages accepted by ordinary deterministic Turing machines using O(S(n)) work-tape cells.

Question: For every space bound S(n) with S(n) ≥ log n, does the equality
    PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n))
hold? Equivalently, is it true that for every such S(n) augmenting a deterministic S(n)-space-bounded Turing machine with an unrestricted auxiliary pushdown stack does not increase its computational power?

Hence the equality PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) is equivalent to DTIME(2^{O(S(n))}) = DSPACE(S(n)); for S(n) = log n this is the well-known open question L = P. No proof of equality or separation is known, so the problem remains open.

An X-factorization of w is a strictly increasing two-way-infinite sequence of integers (i_n)_{n ∈ ℤ} such that, for every n, the block a_{i_n} a_{i_n+1} … a_{i_{n+1}-1} belongs to X. Two X-factorizations of w are called disjoint if their underlying sets of cut-points {i_n : n ∈ ℤ} are disjoint. A bi-infinite word w is periodic if there exists a nonzero integer p such that a_{i+p} = a_i for all i ∈ ℤ, and non-periodic otherwise.

    r(X) ≤ |X| − k + 1 ?

original_question: Does there exist an independent system of three equations in three variables having a non-periodic solution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^+$ the free semigroup of nonempty words over $\Sigma$. Let $\Xi=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ be a set of three unknowns. A (constant-free) word equation in the unknowns $\Xi$ is a pair $(u,v)\in\Xi^+\times\Xi^+$, written $u=v$. A solution is a morphism $h:\Xi^+\to\Sigma^+$ with $h(u)=h(v)$; the solution is called periodic if there exists $w\in\Sigma^+$ such that $h(x_i)\in w^+$ for all $i=1,2,3$, and non-periodic otherwise.

A system $E=\{u_1=v_1,\ldots,u_k=v_k\}$ of word equations is called independent if no proper subsystem of $E$ has the same set of solutions as $E$ (equivalently, $E$ is not equivalent to any of its proper subsystems).

original_question: Let σ: G → Aut(M) be an ergodic action of a compact group G on a Neumann algebra M. Must M necessarily be finite?

The action $\sigma$ is called ergodic if the fixed-point algebra $M^\sigma=\{x\in M:\sigma_g(x)=x\text{ for all }g\in G\}$ equals $\mathbb{C}\,1$. Recall that $M$ is said to be finite if it admits a faithful normal tracial state (equivalently, a separating family of finite normal traces).

paper_title: Open Problems in Stringology
original_question: Fix a pattern string x. In the Boyer-Moore approach, one can imagine a deterministic finite automaton that remembers which parts of x need not be compared again after a mismatch when the pattern is shifted. What is the exact number of states such a Boyer-Moore automaton must have, or at least what are tight upper and lower bounds for that number as a function of |x| and the alphabet?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet of size $\sigma\ge 2$, and let $x\in\Sigma^*$ be a pattern of length $m=|x|$. Consider the following deterministic pattern-matching automaton in the spirit of Boyer–Moore: the automaton scans a text $t\in\Sigma^*$ and, at each step, maintains as its state the maximal information about the alignment of $x$ against $t$ that can be deduced from the comparisons performed so far, namely the set of positions of $x$ already known (from previous comparisons and from previous mismatch shifts) to match or mismatch the corresponding text positions, so that no symbol of $t$ already inspected is ever compared again. Two configurations are identified if they prescribe exactly the same future comparison behavior on every text. Let $S(m,\sigma)$ denote the number of states of the (minimal) such deterministic automaton, taken as the maximum over all patterns $x\in\Sigma^m$.

Determine $S(m,\sigma)$ exactly as a function of $m$ and $\sigma$, or otherwise establish matching (asymptotically tight) upper and lower bounds for $S(m,\sigma)$.
status_search_result: The problem, originally posed by Knuth, remains open. Partial progress exists: research on the size of Boyer–Moore automata has produced experimental and theoretical lower bounds (e.g., a binary family conjectured to give automata of size Ω(m^6)) and conjectured upper bounds ranging from polynomial O(m^7) to exponential O(2^{0.4 m}), but no tight matching bounds or exact formula are known.

paper_title: Some open problems of graph theory.
original_question: Determine the minimum possible value of the largest element x_n among all strictly increasing n-term sequences 0 ≤ x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_n of nonnegative integers for which every difference x_j - x_i with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n is distinct.
self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n \geq 2$, let $\rho(n)$ denote the minimum possible value of $x_n$ taken over all strictly increasing sequences of nonnegative integers
$$0 \le x_1 < x_2 < \cdots < x_n$$
with the property that all $\binom{n}{2}$ differences $x_j - x_i$ (for $1 \le i < j \le n$) are pairwise distinct (equivalently, $\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ is a Sidon set, also called a $B_2$-set). Determine $\rho(n)$ exactly, or determine its precise asymptotic behavior as $n \to \infty$ — in particular, decide whether
$$\rho(n) = n^2 + O(n^{1/2})$$
or otherwise pin down the lower-order term beyond the known bounds
$$n^2 - O(n^{1/2}) \le \rho(n) \le n^2 + O(n^{3/4}).$$
status_search_result: The problem is the classical Sidon / perfect difference set extremal question. It is well known that $\rho(n) = n^2 + O(n^{3/4})$ via the Erdős–Turán and Lindström upper bound, while $\rho(n) \ge n^2 - O(n^{1/2})$ from the trivial counting bound. Closing this gap (equivalently determining the second-order term of the largest Sidon set in $[1,N]$) remains a long-standing open problem in additive combinatorics, with no improvement to the leading constant of the error term known to date.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Given an asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set (M,g,K) and a future trapped surface Sigma, where a closed spacelike 2-surface is future trapped when both future null evolutions are area-non-increasing, must there exist a smooth spherical apparent horizon outside Sigma, meaning a surface with one future null mean curvature equal to zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be a $3$-dimensional asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set: $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold with one Euclidean end, $g$ is a complete Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $M$ playing the role of the second fundamental form of an embedding into a spacetime, satisfying the Einstein constraint equations together with the dominant energy condition.

For a closed two-sided spacelike $2$-surface $\Sigma\subset M$ with outward unit normal $\nu$, let $H$ denote its mean curvature with respect to $\nu$ and let $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ denote the trace of $K$ restricted to $\Sigma$. The future outgoing and ingoing null expansions are
$$\theta^+ = H + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K,\qquad \theta^- = -H + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K.$$
Call $\Sigma$ a future trapped surface if $\theta^+<0$ and $\theta^-<0$ everywhere on $\Sigma$ (both future null evolutions are area‑decreasing). Call a closed surface $\mathcal H\subset M$ an apparent horizon if it is a marginally outer trapped surface, that is, $\theta^+\equiv 0$ on $\mathcal H$.

Question: Given any such $(M,g,K)$ that contains a future trapped surface $\Sigma$, must there exist a smooth apparent horizon $\mathcal H\subset M$ that lies outside $\Sigma$ (i.e. $\Sigma$ is contained in the bounded component of $M\setminus\mathcal H$) and is topologically a sphere?
category_tag: marginally outer trapped surfaces in general relativity
status_search_result: The existence of an outermost marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS), i.e. a smooth apparent horizon, enclosing any given trapped surface in a 3-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set was established by Andersson and Metzger, and extended to dimensions up to 7 by Eichmair using Jang's equation. Combined with the Galloway–Schoen topology theorem, the outermost apparent horizon has spherical topology under the dominant energy condition, so the problem is considered solved in dimension 3.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For apparent horizons in spacelike hypersurfaces, to what extent is the analogy with minimal surfaces valid, and is there a meaningful second-variation or stability theory for the apparent-horizon equations despite the absence of a known functional whose Euler-Lagrange equations are the apparent-horizon equations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface in a $(3+1)$-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime, where $g$ is the induced Riemannian metric on $M$ and $K$ is the second fundamental form of $M$ in the spacetime. For a smooth closed two-sided hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ with outward unit normal $\nu$, let $H$ denote the mean curvature of $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$ and let $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ denote the trace of $K$ restricted to $\Sigma$. The outer null expansion of $\Sigma$ is
$$\theta_+ \;=\; H + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K.$$
Call $\Sigma$ an apparent horizon (a marginally outer trapped surface) when $\theta_+ \equiv 0$ on $\Sigma$. When $K \equiv 0$ this reduces to the minimal surface equation $H=0$ in $(M,g)$.

In the minimal surface case, $\Sigma$ is a critical point of the area functional, and the second variation of area gives a self-adjoint Jacobi operator whose spectrum determines stability. By contrast, when $K \not\equiv 0$, the equation $\theta_+ = 0$ is in general not the Euler--Lagrange equation of any natural functional on hypersurfaces in $(M,g)$.

(a) Determine to what extent the analogy between apparent horizons and minimal surfaces persists at higher order: identify which structural features (e.g. maximum principles, barrier arguments, compactness, regularity, curvature estimates, monotonicity formulas) carry over from minimal surfaces to apparent horizons, and which fail.

(b) In the absence of a variational principle for $\theta_+ = 0$, formulate and justify a meaningful "second-variation" or stability theory for apparent horizons: produce a (necessarily non-self-adjoint) linear operator $L_\Sigma$ on functions on $\Sigma$, obtained by linearizing $\theta_+$ along normal deformations of $\Sigma$, and analyze its spectral properties (existence and reality of a principal eigenvalue, sign criteria for stability, relation to the existence of trapped/untrapped neighborhoods of $\Sigma$, and consequences for the existence and propagation of marginally outer trapped tubes).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Andersson, Mars, and Simon (2007–2008) introduced a stability operator for marginally outer trapped surfaces (MOTS) by linearizing the outer null expansion, established that its principal eigenvalue is real despite the operator being non-self-adjoint, and used this to prove existence of marginally outer trapped tubes; subsequent works (e.g., Andersson–Metzger, Eichmair, Galloway and collaborators) developed regularity, compactness, curvature estimates, and topology results paralleling minimal surface theory. Thus a meaningful stability theory exists, though the analogy with minimal surfaces is incomplete (no variational principle, complex spectrum in general, and remaining open questions on symmetry breaking and instability persist as of recent work).

A complete Riemannian metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called asymptotically flat if, outside a compact set, there exist coordinates $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ in which
$$g_{ij}(x) = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}), \qquad \partial_k g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-2}), \qquad \partial_k\partial_l g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-3}),$$
as $|x|\to\infty$. The metric is called scalar-flat if its scalar curvature $R_g$ vanishes identically. An embedded 2-sphere $\Sigma \subset (\mathbb{R}^3, g)$ is minimal if its mean curvature with respect to $g$ vanishes everywhere, and stable if the second variation of area at $\Sigma$ is nonnegative for all normal variations.

original_question: For a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric g = phi^4 delta with nonnegative scalar curvature, what conditions on the conformal factor phi guarantee that g has no horizon?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\delta$ denote the standard Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let $\phi:\mathbb{R}^3\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth positive function such that the Riemannian metric $g=\phi^4\delta$ is asymptotically flat (i.e., in suitable coordinates at infinity, $\phi\to 1$ with appropriate decay so that $g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}$ and its derivatives decay at the standard rates) and has nonnegative scalar curvature $R_g\ge 0$. Recall that for $g=\phi^4\delta$ the scalar curvature is given by $R_g=-8\phi^{-5}\Delta\phi$, so $R_g\ge 0$ is equivalent to $\Delta\phi\le 0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$. By a horizon of $g$ one means a closed (compact, without boundary), smoothly embedded minimal surface in $(\mathbb{R}^3,g)$.

Determine explicit, sharp conditions on the conformal factor $\phi$ that guarantee that $(\mathbb{R}^3,g)$ contains no horizon. In particular, characterize which superharmonic positive functions $\phi$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, tending to $1$ at infinity, give rise to a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric $g=\phi^4\delta$ with nonnegative scalar curvature and no closed minimal surface.
status_search_result: The question of giving sharp conditions on the conformal factor $\phi$ ensuring that a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric $g=\phi^4\delta$ of nonnegative scalar curvature is horizon-free remains an active research topic. Related work on harmonic conformal classes of asymptotically flat manifolds (e.g., Jauregui's study of invariants and spherically symmetric harmonic rescalings that exclude horizons) addresses special cases, but no general characterization appears established. No definitive resolution was found.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For compact M, determine conditions on conformal data (gamma, A, tau), where gamma is a Riemannian metric, A is a traceless divergence-free symmetric tensor, and tau is a nonconstant mean-curvature function, that ensure solvability of the Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York system for (phi,W) with phi > 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\gamma)$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian $n$-manifold ($n\ge 3$). Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $M$ that is trace-free with respect to $\gamma$ and divergence-free with respect to the Levi-Civita connection of $\gamma$, and let $\tau:M\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth, non-constant function (the prescribed mean curvature). Consider the conformal (Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York) system for an unknown positive function $\phi:M\to(0,\infty)$ and an unknown vector field $W$ on $M$:
$$-a_n\Delta_\gamma\phi + R_\gamma\,\phi \;=\; -\,b_n\,\tau^2\,\phi^{\,N-1} \;+\; |A+\mathcal{L}_\gamma W|_\gamma^{2}\,\phi^{-N-1},$$
$$\operatorname{div}_\gamma(\mathcal{L}_\gamma W) \;=\; \tfrac{n-1}{n}\,\phi^{N}\,d\tau,$$
where $N=\tfrac{2n}{n-2}$, $a_n=\tfrac{4(n-1)}{n-2}$, $b_n=\tfrac{n-1}{n}$, $R_\gamma$ is the scalar curvature of $\gamma$, and $\mathcal{L}_\gamma W$ is the conformal Killing operator $(\mathcal{L}_\gamma W)_{ij}=\nabla_iW_j+\nabla_jW_i-\tfrac{2}{n}(\operatorname{div}W)\gamma_{ij}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the conformal data $(\gamma,A,\tau)$ — in particular without assuming that $\tau$ is constant or near-constant — under which the above coupled system admits a solution $(\phi,W)$ with $\phi>0$.
status_search_result: The full non-CMC solvability question is still open in general. Partial results exist: near-CMC existence (Isenberg–Moncrief and others), and the Holst–Nagy–Tsogtgerel / Maxwell far-from-CMC results (2009) for the positive Yamabe class with small TT-tensor, plus extensions by Dahl–Gicquaud–Humbert and Nguyen. A complete characterization of conditions on $(\gamma,A,\tau)$ ensuring solvability without near-CMC or smallness assumptions has not been obtained, and non-uniqueness/non-existence phenomena have been identified in some regimes.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Which hyperboloidal initial data arise from a spacetime with smooth conformal null infinity, and what class of Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York conformal data constructs such hyperboloidal initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a $4$-dimensional spacetime $(M,g)$. A spacetime is said to admit a smooth conformal null infinity if there exists a manifold with boundary $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ and a smooth function $\Omega\in C^\infty(\widetilde M)$ with $\Omega>0$ on $M$, $\Omega=0$ and $d\Omega\neq 0$ on $\mathscr I:=\partial\widetilde M$, such that $\widetilde g=\Omega^{2}g$ extends smoothly to $\widetilde M$.

A hyperboloidal initial data set is a triple $(\Sigma,h,K)$ where $\Sigma$ is a $3$-manifold diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold with boundary $\overline{\Sigma}$, $h$ is a Riemannian metric and $K$ a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $\Sigma$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(h)-|K|_h^{2}+(\mathrm{tr}_h K)^{2}=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_h K-d(\mathrm{tr}_h K)=0,$$
and such that $\Sigma$ asymptotically approaches a standard hyperboloid in Minkowski spacetime; equivalently, there exists a defining function $\sigma$ for $\partial\overline{\Sigma}$ such that $\sigma^{2}h$ extends to a Riemannian metric on $\overline{\Sigma}$ and $\mathrm{tr}_h K$ tends to a nonzero constant at $\partial\overline{\Sigma}$.

The Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York conformal method parameterises solutions of the constraint equations as follows. One prescribes free conformal data $(\widehat h,\widehat\sigma,\tau)$ on $\Sigma$ consisting of a Riemannian metric $\widehat h$, a transverse-traceless symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor $\widehat\sigma$, and a mean curvature function $\tau$. One then seeks a positive conformal factor $\phi$ and a vector field $W$ solving the coupled Lichnerowicz equation and conformal vector Laplacian equation
$$\Delta_{\widehat h}\phi-\tfrac{1}{8}R(\widehat h)\phi+\tfrac{1}{8}|\widehat\sigma+\mathcal L_{\widehat h}W|^{2}_{\widehat h}\phi^{-7}-\tfrac{1}{12}\tau^{2}\phi^{5}=0,$$
$$\mathrm{div}_{\widehat h}(\mathcal L_{\widehat h}W)=\tfrac{2}{3}\phi^{6}\,d\tau,$$
and recovers $(h,K)=(\phi^{4}\widehat h,\,\phi^{-2}(\widehat\sigma+\mathcal L_{\widehat h}W)+\tfrac{1}{3}\tau\phi^{4}\widehat h)$.

Problems:
(a) Characterise intrinsically which hyperboloidal initial data sets $(\Sigma,h,K)$ arise as the restriction to a spacelike hypersurface of a vacuum spacetime that admits a smooth conformal null infinity.
(b) Identify a class of Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York conformal data $(\widehat h,\widehat\sigma,\tau)$ on $\Sigma$ for which the conformal method produces precisely the hyperboloidal initial data sets described in (a).
status_search_result: The problem of characterising hyperboloidal initial data leading to a smooth conformal null infinity is well-known to be obstructed: Andersson–Chruściel showed that generic asymptotically hyperboloidal data only admit polyhomogeneous (logarithmic) expansions, and only a non-generic subclass yields smooth Scri. Recent work (e.g. 2025 results on hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities) continues to identify subclasses, but a complete intrinsic characterisation of the data and of the corresponding free conformal data in the Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York method remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
context_brief: Connected components of Einstein metric spaces
original_question: Can the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on V = R x M^3 have more than one connected component, and in the asymptotically flat setting with maximal Cauchy surfaces can one establish a compactness or Palais-Smale condition for the ADM mass function?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M^3$ be a smooth, connected $3$-manifold and let $V = \mathbb{R} \times M^3$. Consider the set $\mathcal{E}(V)$ of smooth Lorentzian metrics $g$ on $V$ such that:
(i) $(V,g)$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to $M^3$;
(ii) $g$ satisfies the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$;
(iii) $(V,g)$ is asymptotically flat, in the sense that there exist a maximal (mean curvature zero) Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma \subset V$ on which the induced Riemannian metric is asymptotically flat in the standard sense (one end, suitable decay of the metric to the Euclidean metric and of the second fundamental form).

Equip $\mathcal{E}(V)$ with a natural smooth topology (e.g. the $C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$ topology together with weighted asymptotic norms compatible with the asymptotic flatness condition), and consider the ADM mass functional
$$m_{\mathrm{ADM}} : \mathcal{E}(V) \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$$
defined via the asymptotic flux integral on the maximal Cauchy slice $\Sigma$.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Can $\mathcal{E}(V)$ have more than one connected component?

(b) Within the asymptotically flat, maximal-slice setting described above, does the ADM mass functional $m_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ satisfy a compactness condition of Palais–Smale type, i.e., does every sequence $\{g_n\} \subset \mathcal{E}(V)$ along which $m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(g_n)$ is bounded and the appropriate gradient (with respect to a chosen Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{E}(V)$) tends to zero admit a subsequence converging in $\mathcal{E}(V)$?
status_search_result: No source explicitly resolves whether the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on $\mathbb{R}\times M^3$ has multiple connected components, or whether a Palais–Smale-type compactness holds for the ADM mass on asymptotically flat maximal slices. Related literature confirms global existence of maximal globally hyperbolic developments and partial Palais–Smale results in stationary settings, but the specific structural questions appear unresolved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Find a good local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary metrics, preferably one that is independent of the choice of slicing.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$, and assume that $g$ admits a Killing vector field $\xi$ that is timelike on an open region $U\subset M$ (so $(U,g)$ is a stationary vacuum spacetime). The Kerr family is the two-parameter family of stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat vacuum solutions parametrized by mass $m\ge 0$ and angular momentum $a\in\mathbb{R}$.

Problem: Find a local geometric condition, expressible purely in terms of $g$, $\xi$, and their covariant derivatives on $U$ (and not depending on a choice of spacelike slicing or Cauchy hypersurface), whose validity on $U$ is equivalent to $(U,g)$ being locally isometric to an open subset of a Kerr spacetime. In other words, give a tensorial/scalar local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary vacuum metrics that is independent of any choice of slicing.
status_search_result: Several local characterizations of Kerr exist: Mars's tensorial characterization using a Weyl-type tensor built from the Killing field and the conformal Weyl curvature, invariant curvature-scalar characterizations (e.g. Page–Shoom-style invariants), and a non-negative scalar Kerr-initial-data characterization on hypersurfaces. However, a fully general slicing-independent local characterization of Kerr among arbitrary stationary vacuum metrics remains an active research topic and is regarded as not completely settled.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
context_brief: Singularities of static or stationary vacuum equations
original_question: Give a general description of the types of singularities that can occur in solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, beginning with the possible singularities of their spacelike slices.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the static vacuum Einstein equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold, which, on a spacelike slice $(M^3, g)$ with lapse function $u: M \to (0,\infty)$, take the form
$$ u\,\mathrm{Ric}_g = \nabla^2 u, \qquad \Delta_g u = 0, $$
where $\mathrm{Ric}_g$, $\nabla^2$, and $\Delta_g$ denote the Ricci tensor, Hessian, and Laplace–Beltrami operator of $g$, respectively. More generally, consider the stationary vacuum Einstein equations, whose quotient by the timelike Killing field yields a harmonic map system from a Riemannian 3-manifold into the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$ coupled to an Einstein-type equation on the base.

Provide a general classification and description of the possible types of singularities that can occur in solutions of these equations. In particular, describe:

(a) The possible singularity types of the spacelike slice $(M, g)$ itself (for example: metric degenerations such as curvature blow-up, collapse of injectivity radius, conical singularities, cusps, asymptotically cylindrical ends, or Gromov–Hausdorff limits where the limit space fails to be a smooth manifold).

(b) The possible singularities of the lapse function $u$ (zeros corresponding to horizons, blow-up, or loss of regularity) and how these interact with the geometric singularities of $g$.

(c) For the stationary case, the additional singularities arising from the twist potential and the harmonic map target, including singularities along the axis of rotation and at fixed points of the Killing field.

Determine, in each case, whether the singularity can be removed by a change of coordinates or a smooth extension, and otherwise characterize its asymptotic geometric model.
category_tag: static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations
status_search_result: No comprehensive classification of singularities of solutions to the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations and their spacelike slices appears to be available. Recent works treat partial situations (e.g., space-periodic Kasner-type asymptotics in 5D static vacuum, axisymmetric solitons, behavior of spacelike foliations approaching null surfaces), but a general description remains a guiding open problem in mathematical relativity.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that there is no static spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solution with nonzero electric field.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) system on a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ with gauge group $SU(2)$ and Yang–Mills connection $A$ of curvature $F$. The coupled field equations are
$$R_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac{1}{2}R\,g_{\mu\nu}=8\pi T_{\mu\nu}(F),\qquad D_{\mu}F^{\mu\nu}=0,\qquad D_{\mu}{}^{\!*}F^{\mu\nu}=0,$$
where $T_{\mu\nu}(F)=\mathrm{tr}\bigl(F_{\mu\alpha}F_{\nu}{}^{\alpha}-\tfrac{1}{4}g_{\mu\nu}F_{\alpha\beta}F^{\alpha\beta}\bigr)$.

A solution is called a (asymptotically flat) static spherically symmetric soliton if:
(i) $(M,g)$ admits a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field $\xi$ and an $SO(3)$ action by isometries with two-dimensional spacelike orbits, with respect to which both $g$ and $F$ are invariant;
(ii) the metric on the orbit space is geodesically complete and globally regular (no horizons, no singularities), with the standard asymptotically flat behaviour at spatial infinity;
(iii) the Yang–Mills curvature $F$ has finite total energy.

Writing the connection in the standard spherically symmetric ansatz, $F$ decomposes into a "magnetic" part (transverse to $\xi$) and an "electric" part (mixed with $dt$ in static coordinates adapted to $\xi$).

Prove that any such asymptotically flat static spherically symmetric EYM soliton must have identically vanishing electric component; equivalently, show that there exists no static spherically symmetric, globally regular, asymptotically flat solution of the $SU(2)$ Einstein–Yang–Mills equations with non-zero electric field.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that in the asymptotically flat case, static spherically symmetric SU(2) EYM solitons are typically constructed under the assumption that the electric ("Coulomb") part of the gauge potential vanishes, while genuinely dyonic (electric+magnetic) regular soliton solutions are known to exist in asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetimes. No definitive published proof of non-existence in the asymptotically flat case was located, so the status of the precise conjecture is not clearly resolved by the search.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Find axially symmetric static or stationary Einstein-Yang-Mills solutions that generalize the Kerr-Newman solution.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein-Yang-Mills (EYM) system on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$, coupled to an SU(2) (or more generally a compact non-abelian) gauge connection $A$ with curvature $F = dA + A\wedge A$. The field equations are
$$ \mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g = 8\pi T(F), \qquad D \star F = 0, \qquad D F = 0, $$
where $T(F)_{\mu\nu} = \tfrac{1}{4\pi}\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(F_{\mu\alpha}F_\nu{}^\alpha - \tfrac{1}{4} g_{\mu\nu} F_{\alpha\beta} F^{\alpha\beta}\bigr)$ is the Yang-Mills stress-energy tensor.

Recall that the Kerr-Newman family is the two-parameter family (after fixing mass, angular momentum, and electric charge) of stationary, axially symmetric, asymptotically flat, electrovacuum (i.e., abelian Einstein-Maxwell) black hole solutions, characterized by two commuting Killing vector fields (one timelike at infinity, one with closed orbits) and a regular event horizon.

Problem. Construct, and where possible classify, stationary or static axially symmetric asymptotically flat solutions $(g,A)$ of the non-abelian Einstein-Yang-Mills equations admitting two commuting Killing fields (a stationary one and an axial one) under which the gauge field is appropriately invariant, such that the family genuinely generalizes the Kerr-Newman solution: it should reduce to (or contain) Kerr-Newman in an abelian limit, exhibit a regular event horizon, and possess genuinely non-abelian gauge content (so that the configurations are not gauge-equivalent to embedded abelian Einstein-Maxwell solutions). Provide an existence theory and, ideally, a parametrization or uniqueness statement for such solutions.
status_search_result: Stationary, axially symmetric, asymptotically flat rotating black hole solutions of the SU(2) Einstein-Yang-Mills system with genuinely non-abelian hair have been constructed numerically by Kleihaus and Kunz (and subsequent works), forming sequences indexed by winding and node numbers and limiting to embedded abelian (Kerr-Newman-like) solutions. Thus existence of axially symmetric stationary EYM generalizations of Kerr-Newman is established at the level of numerical/perturbative constructions. However, a complete rigorous existence theory, classification, and uniqueness statement analogous to the Kerr-Newman uniqueness theorems remain open; partial rigidity results show that under restricted circularity assumptions stationary axisymmetric SU(2) EYM fields must be abelian, indicating that the non-abelian solutions are necessarily non-circular and harder to analyze.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
context_brief: No hair for EYM black holes
original_question: Show that every static black-hole solution of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations must be Reissner-Nordstrom, equivalently that static Einstein-Yang-Mills black holes have no Yang-Mills hair.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ with gauge group $SU(2)$ (or, more generally, a compact non-abelian Lie group). Recall that an EYM solution consists of a Lorentzian metric $g$ together with a connection $A$ on a principal bundle whose curvature $F = dA + A \wedge A$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g = 8\pi T(F,g), \qquad d\!\star\! F + [A,\star F] = 0,$$
where $T(F,g)$ is the Yang–Mills stress–energy tensor. A black-hole solution is called static if it admits a Killing field that is timelike outside, and normal to, a non-degenerate event horizon, with the metric and connection invariant under its flow and asymptotically flat.

The Reissner–Nordström family is the family of static, asymptotically flat solutions in which the Yang–Mills connection reduces (modulo gauge transformations) to an abelian connection determined by electric and magnetic charges, and the metric has the explicit Reissner–Nordström form
$$g = -\left(1 - \tfrac{2M}{r} + \tfrac{Q^2}{r^2}\right)dt^2 + \left(1 - \tfrac{2M}{r} + \tfrac{Q^2}{r^2}\right)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2\, d\Omega^2.$$

Prove or disprove: every static, asymptotically flat black-hole solution of the Einstein–Yang–Mills equations is, up to gauge, of Reissner–Nordström form. Equivalently, static EYM black holes carry no genuine Yang–Mills hair.
status_search_result: The conjecture as stated has been disproved: Bartnik and McKinnon (1988) and subsequent work constructed static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat "colored" black-hole solutions to the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations that are not Reissner–Nordström, providing explicit counterexamples to the no-Yang–Mills-hair conjecture. These solutions carry no global Yang–Mills charge yet have non-trivial gauge field outside the horizon, and infinitely many such solutions exist for each horizon radius.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that a solution of the Einstein equations linearized about Minkowski space is close to a non-flat exact solution of the full Einstein equations.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathbb{R}^4, \eta)$ denote Minkowski spacetime, where $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. The vacuum Einstein equations for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a 4-manifold are
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0.$$
Writing $g = \eta + h$ and retaining only terms linear in $h$, one obtains the linearized Einstein equations about Minkowski space, namely
$$\Box \bar h_{\mu\nu} = 0, \qquad \partial^\mu \bar h_{\mu\nu} = 0,$$
where $\bar h_{\mu\nu} = h_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac12 \eta_{\mu\nu}\, \eta^{\alpha\beta} h_{\alpha\beta}$ (after fixing the harmonic/Lorenz gauge).

Equip the space of symmetric $2$-tensor fields on $\mathbb{R}^4$ with a suitable weighted Sobolev norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ such that asymptotically flat data of finite ADM energy lie in $X$.

Prove or disprove the following: for every nontrivial smooth solution $h$ of the linearized vacuum Einstein equations about $\eta$ that decays suitably at spatial infinity, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an exact smooth solution $g$ of the full vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ such that $g$ is not isometric to Minkowski space (i.e., is non-flat) and
$$\|\,g - (\eta + h)\,\|_X < \varepsilon.$$
Equivalently, show that every (nontrivial) linearized vacuum solution near Minkowski space can be approximated arbitrarily well by a genuine non-flat exact vacuum solution of the Einstein equations.
status_search_result: The general question of when a solution of the linearized Einstein equations about Minkowski space can be approximated by (or arises as the linearization of) a genuine non-flat exact vacuum solution is the classical "linearization stability" problem. While linearization stability is known to hold for asymptotically flat backgrounds such as Minkowski (results of Choquet-Bruhat, Fischer–Marsden, Moncrief), the precise formulation asked here — that arbitrary non-flat exact solutions lie arbitrarily close to any linearized solution in a suitable norm — does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature surveyed. Recent work (e.g., on generating exact solutions from linearized approximations via special gauge transformations) addresses related but more restrictive cases. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that very small but finite test bodies move on spacetime geodesics.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations, and let $T^{ab}$ denote a smooth, symmetric, divergence-free stress-energy tensor on $M$ satisfying suitable energy conditions (e.g., the dominant energy condition). Consider a one-parameter family of "test bodies" modeled by stress-energy tensors $T^{ab}_\varepsilon$ (for $\varepsilon > 0$) supported in spatially compact, timelike worldtubes $W_\varepsilon \subset M$ whose spatial diameters and total mass-energies tend to zero as $\varepsilon \to 0$, while remaining strictly positive (i.e., the bodies are small but finite, not idealized point particles). Assume each $T^{ab}_\varepsilon$ is conserved ($\nabla_a T^{ab}_\varepsilon = 0$) and satisfies the dominant energy condition.

Prove that, in an appropriate precise sense to be formulated, the worldtubes $W_\varepsilon$ converge as $\varepsilon \to 0$ to a timelike curve $\gamma$ in $M$ that is a geodesic of the spacetime metric $g$; equivalently, formulate and prove a rigorous theorem stating that very small but finite (extended, non-test-particle-idealized) test bodies in general relativity move on spacetime geodesics, including the back-reaction and finite-size corrections in a controlled way.
status_search_result: Several theorems address this question. The Geroch–Jang theorem (1975) and refinements by Ehlers–Geroch (2004) prove that sufficiently small test bodies satisfying suitable energy conditions follow timelike geodesics, treated via limiting sequences of extended bodies. More recently, gravitational self-force programs (Gralla–Wald, Pound, and others) provide rigorous derivations in the small-mass limit. Thus the problem is partially solved: precise theorems exist under specific hypotheses, but a fully general formulation including all matter models and back-reaction effects continues to be refined.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Devise a numerical or lattice evolution scheme for the Einstein equations that can be proved to preserve the constraint equations, as a step toward proving convergence to a long-time solution.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$. Under a 3+1 decomposition with spatial slices $\Sigma_t$ carrying induced Riemannian metric $\gamma_{ij}$ and second fundamental form $K_{ij}$, the Einstein equations split into:

(i) Evolution equations: a system of PDEs giving $\partial_t \gamma_{ij}$ and $\partial_t K_{ij}$ in terms of $\gamma_{ij}$, $K_{ij}$, lapse $N$, and shift $\beta^i$.

(ii) Constraint equations: the Hamiltonian constraint $R(\gamma) + (\mathrm{tr}_\gamma K)^2 - |K|^2_\gamma = 0$ and the momentum constraint $\nabla^j(K_{ij} - (\mathrm{tr}_\gamma K)\gamma_{ij}) = 0$.

A fundamental property of the continuum system is that if the constraints hold on the initial slice, they are preserved by the evolution.

Problem: Construct a numerical (finite-difference, finite-element, or lattice) discretization of the Einstein evolution equations on a discretization of spacetime such that the discrete analogues of the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints are exactly preserved by the discrete time evolution whenever they are satisfied by the discrete initial data, and prove that solutions of this scheme converge, as the discretization parameter tends to zero, to a long-time smooth solution of the vacuum Einstein equations on a maximal globally hyperbolic development of admissible initial data.
status_search_result: The problem of designing provably constraint-preserving numerical schemes for the Einstein equations with a rigorous long-time convergence proof remains open. Recent progress includes structure-preserving finite-element discretizations of the linearized Einstein equations via Hodge-Dirac/divdiv complexes (2025) and constraint-damping reformulations (Z4/CCZ4) used in practical numerical relativity, but these either treat only linearized models or lack a full mathematical proof of long-time convergence to a solution of the nonlinear vacuum Einstein equations.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Generalize the maximal-surface estimates to show existence of a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface asymptotic to a prescribed cut of future null infinity in an asymptotically flat spacetime, and determine the weakest asymptotic conditions on null infinity under which this holds.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a $(3+1)$-dimensional asymptotically flat Lorentzian spacetime admitting a notion of future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$, on which one may speak of cuts (cross-sections of $\mathscr{I}^+$ diffeomorphic to a 2-sphere). A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is said to be of constant mean curvature (CMC) if its mean curvature $H$ with respect to the future-directed timelike unit normal is constant on $\Sigma$. Such a $\Sigma$ is said to be asymptotic to a given cut $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathscr{I}^+$ if $\Sigma$ extends out to null infinity and its trace at $\mathscr{I}^+$ coincides with $\mathcal{C}$.

Problem. Extending the standard a priori estimates and existence theory for maximal ($H=0$) hypersurfaces to the CMC ($H = \mathrm{const} \neq 0$) setting:

(a) Prove the existence of a CMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$ that is asymptotic to a prescribed cut $\mathcal{C}$ of future null infinity.

(b) Determine the weakest asymptotic conditions on the geometry near $\mathscr{I}^+$ (e.g., decay/regularity of the Bondi data, peeling properties, smoothness of $\mathscr{I}^+$) under which the existence in (a) holds, and show that these conditions are sharp.
status_search_result: Recent work addresses CMC hypersurfaces and foliations in asymptotically flat spacetimes, and there is active research on null hypersurfaces approaching null infinity (e.g., in Bondi–Sachs gauge) and on smoothness of null infinity. However, no source clearly establishes existence of a CMC hypersurface asymptotic to an arbitrary prescribed cut of $\mathscr{I}^+$ under sharp asymptotic conditions, so the problem appears to remain unresolved in full generality.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that a maximal surface in a boost-type domain is necessarily asymptotically flat and coincides with the known maximal slices constructed in that setting.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth $(3+1)$-dimensional Lorentzian manifold and let $\Omega \subset M$ be a boost-type domain, that is, a domain of the form
$$\Omega = \{(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^3 : |t| < \alpha\,|x| + \beta,\ |x|>R\}$$
for some constants $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\beta>0$, $R>0$, on which $g$ is asymptotically Minkowskian (i.e., in the standard coordinates, $g_{\mu\nu}-\eta_{\mu\nu}$ together with appropriate derivatives decays to zero as $|x|\to\infty$ at a suitable rate uniform in the boost cone).

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ is called a maximal surface if it has vanishing mean curvature with respect to $g$. 

Prove (or disprove) the following: every maximal surface $\Sigma$ contained in such a boost-type domain $\Omega$ is necessarily asymptotically flat (in the sense that the induced Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$ approaches the Euclidean metric at infinity with the appropriate decay), and moreover $\Sigma$ must coincide with one of the maximal slices previously constructed in this setting (in particular, $\Sigma$ is unique up to the action of the asymptotic boost/translation symmetries).
status_search_result: Web searches surface classical existence/uniqueness results for maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes (Bartnik; Chruściel–Delay; etc.) and uniqueness theorems for maximal slices in boost-type domains, but none directly confirm a complete resolution of the stated assertion that every maximal surface in a boost-type domain must be asymptotically flat and coincide with the known constructed maximal slices. No definitive solved/open declaration could be located.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that a weak Cauchy surface, defined as a pointwise limit of Cauchy surfaces, in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, i.e., a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold admitting a Cauchy surface (a subset met exactly once by every inextendible timelike curve). Assume $(M,g)$ satisfies suitable energy conditions (for instance the null energy condition $\mathrm{Ric}(k,k)\ge 0$ for every null vector $k$, together with the null genericity condition).

Define a *weak Cauchy surface* in $(M,g)$ to be a subset $S\subset M$ that arises as a pointwise limit of a sequence $(S_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of Cauchy surfaces of $(M,g)$; that is, $S=\{p\in M:\exists\,p_n\in S_n,\ p_n\to p\}$.

Prove that such a weak Cauchy surface $S$ cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic of $(M,g)$.
status_search_result: A direct web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific conjecture about weak Cauchy surfaces (defined as pointwise limits of Cauchy surfaces) being free of inextendible null geodesics under energy conditions. Related work on global hyperbolicity, null distance, and limit causal curves exists, but no source explicitly confirms a proof or disproof of the stated claim.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Prove a singularity theorem assuming the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2}R(g)\,g + \Lambda\,g = T$, where $T$ is the energy-momentum tensor. Recall the following standard conditions:

- (Timelike convergence / strong energy condition) $\mathrm{Ric}(X,X) \ge 0$ for every timelike vector $X$.
- (Dominant energy condition) For every future-directed causal vector $X$, the vector $-T^{\mu}{}_{\nu} X^{\nu}$ is future-directed causal; equivalently, $T(X,Y) \ge 0$ for all future-directed causal $X,Y$, and energy flows along causal directions.

The classical Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems guarantee causal geodesic incompleteness of $(M,g)$ under hypotheses that include the timelike convergence condition together with a suitable causal/initial condition (e.g. existence of a closed trapped surface, a compact Cauchy hypersurface, or a point whose future null cone reconverges).

Problem. Formulate and prove a singularity theorem of Penrose–Hawking type whose curvature/matter hypothesis is the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition. That is, establish that, under appropriate causal and trapping hypotheses together with the dominant energy condition (and possibly the Einstein equations with a specified cosmological constant or matter model), the spacetime $(M,g)$ must be causally geodesically incomplete.
status_search_result: The literature establishes singularity theorems under various energy conditions (null, weak, strong/timelike convergence, and averaged/quantum versions), and recent work derives Hawking-type theorems from worldvolume or quantum energy inequalities. However, there appears to be no general singularity theorem replacing the timelike convergence (strong energy) condition by the dominant energy condition; the DEC alone is generally regarded as too weak to force focusing of timelike geodesics, and the problem of obtaining a genuine DEC-based singularity theorem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Prove a long-time existence theorem for the asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein equations in maximal slicing gauge, strong enough for large data to rule out globally naked singularities and shield formed singularities behind maximal-surface barriers.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ for a Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M,g)$, with Cauchy initial data $(\Sigma_0, h_0, K_0)$ that is asymptotically flat: $\Sigma_0$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ minus possibly finitely many balls, $h_0$ is a Riemannian metric and $K_0$ a symmetric 2-tensor on $\Sigma_0$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(h_0)+(\mathrm{tr}_{h_0}K_0)^2-|K_0|_{h_0}^2=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_{h_0}K_0-d(\mathrm{tr}_{h_0}K_0)=0,$$
and approaching the standard flat data at spatial infinity in a suitably weighted sense. A foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of (a portion of) the maximal Cauchy development by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces is called a maximal slicing if every leaf has vanishing mean curvature, $\mathrm{tr}_{h_t}K_t=0$. The maximal slicing gauge couples this foliation condition to a lapse-shift system: the lapse $N$ solves the elliptic equation
$$\Delta_{h_t}N = N\,|K_t|_{h_t}^2,\qquad N\to 1\ \text{at infinity},$$
and the shift is chosen (e.g. as a minimal-distortion or zero shift) so that the evolution of $h_t,K_t$ given by the ADM equations preserves $\mathrm{tr}_{h_t}K_t=0$.

A globally naked singularity is, informally, a singular event in the maximal Cauchy development whose causal future contains a complete future-directed null geodesic reaching past null infinity; its absence is the content of weak cosmic censorship. A maximal-surface barrier is a smooth maximal hypersurface (or family of such) lying in the Cauchy development whose causal future contains all future singular behavior, so that singularities are "shielded" from infinity by the barrier.

Problem. Establish a long-time existence theorem for the Cauchy problem of the asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein equations evolved in the maximal slicing gauge described above, valid for arbitrarily large initial data, with conclusions strong enough to imply both:
(i) no globally naked singularity forms in the maximal Cauchy development; and
(ii) every singularity that forms is contained in the causal future of a maximal-surface barrier within the foliation.

Specifically, prove existence of a smooth maximal foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in[0,T^*)}$ of a globally hyperbolic region $\mathcal{D}\subset M$ such that either $T^*=\infty$ and $\mathcal{D}$ contains a neighborhood of future null infinity, or else as $t\uparrow T^*$ the leaves $\Sigma_t$ converge to a smooth maximal hypersurface beyond which the geometry degenerates only in the trapped (black-hole) region, in either case ruling out (i) and ensuring (ii).
status_search_result: Weak and strong cosmic censorship for the vacuum Einstein equations remain major open problems for large asymptotically flat data; recent surveys (e.g. Van de Moortel, 2025) describe partial results in symmetry classes and stability/instability theorems near Kerr, but no large-data long-time existence theorem in maximal slicing strong enough to rule out global nakedness and provide maximal-surface shielding has been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Construct an exact purely radiative vacuum spacetime, or prove existence of one, with complete smooth past and future null infinities, regular timelike infinities, and positive mass.
self_contained_problem:
Call a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M,g)$ a purely radiative vacuum spacetime if it satisfies the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ and admits a smooth conformal compactification: there exists a manifold-with-boundary $\widetilde M$ with smooth metric $\widetilde g = \Omega^2 g$ and boundary defining function $\Omega\ge 0$, such that the conformal boundary contains a past null infinity $\mathscr I^-$ and a future null infinity $\mathscr I^+$, both of which are smooth and complete (every null geodesic generator extends to its full affine range), and such that the past timelike infinity $i^-$ and future timelike infinity $i^+$ are regular points of the conformal extension at which $\widetilde g$ is smooth. Require further that the spacetime carries no incoming or outgoing matter and no incoming radiation other than gravitational radiation generated by the geometry itself (i.e., it is genuinely a vacuum solution with the conformal data being purely radiative), and that the ADM/Bondi mass is strictly positive.

Either construct an explicit example of such a purely radiative vacuum spacetime with positive mass, or prove that at least one such spacetime exists.
status_search_result: Existing work (Friedrich's papers on static and radiative spacetimes, and Lübbe's semiglobal stability result) establishes semiglobal existence and stability results for purely radiative vacuum spacetimes, but does not produce a global solution with both past and future null infinities complete, both timelike infinities regular, and positive mass. No explicit exact example with all of these properties simultaneously appears to be known, and the problem is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Are there regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein initial-value problem that guarantee existence but not uniqueness, and is there smooth initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity after which it can be extended nonuniquely while preserving global hyperbolicity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein initial-value problem: an initial data set consists of a smooth Riemannian 3-manifold $(\Sigma, h)$ together with a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $\Sigma$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R_h - |K|_h^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_h K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_h K - d(\mathrm{tr}_h K) = 0,$$
where $R_h$ is the scalar curvature of $h$. A development of $(\Sigma, h, K)$ is a smooth, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M, g)$ solving the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, together with an embedding $\iota : \Sigma \hookrightarrow M$ as a Cauchy hypersurface, such that $\iota^* g = h$ and the second fundamental form of $\iota(\Sigma)$ in $(M, g)$ equals $K$.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Are there regularity conditions on the initial data $(\Sigma, h, K)$ (weaker than those needed for the classical maximal globally hyperbolic development) that guarantee the existence of a development but for which uniqueness (in the appropriate sense, up to isometry) fails?

(b) Does there exist smooth vacuum initial data $(\Sigma, h, K)$ whose vacuum Einstein evolution develops a singularity, beyond which the spacetime can be extended in more than one inequivalent way as a globally hyperbolic vacuum solution?

Searches return well-posedness and low-regularity results but no construction matching the specific scenario asked.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
context_brief: Maximal slices and CMC foliations on R x S3
original_question: Prove that every globally hyperbolic maximally extended solution of the Einstein or Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = R x S^3 contains a maximal hypersurface and both a big bang and a big crunch; equivalently, decide whether any such vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solution fails to admit a constant-mean-curvature foliation, including the Bianchi IX special case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \mathbb{R}\times S^3$ be equipped with a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ such that $(V,g)$ is a globally hyperbolic, maximally extended (i.e., maximal globally hyperbolic) solution of either the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$, or the Einstein–Maxwell equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g)-\tfrac12 R(g)\,g = 8\pi T[F],\qquad dF=0,\quad d\star F=0,$$
where $F$ is a 2-form on $V$ and $T[F]_{\mu\nu}=F_{\mu\alpha}F_\nu{}^\alpha-\tfrac14 g_{\mu\nu}F_{\alpha\beta}F^{\alpha\beta}$.

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subset V$ is called maximal if its mean curvature with respect to the future-directed unit normal vanishes identically. The spacetime $(V,g)$ is said to admit a constant-mean-curvature (CMC) foliation if there exists a smooth foliation of $V$ by closed spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces, each having (spatially) constant mean curvature, with the value of that mean curvature serving as a smooth time function on $V$. A big bang (resp. big crunch) is an incomplete past (resp. future) boundary at which suitable curvature invariants of $g$ blow up.

Prove the following: every such $(V,g)$ contains a maximal hypersurface and possesses both a big bang and a big crunch. Equivalently, decide whether any maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum or Einstein–Maxwell solution on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ can fail to admit a CMC foliation. Treat in particular the spatially homogeneous Bianchi IX case, in which $g$ is invariant under a transitive left action of $SU(2)$ on each $\{t\}\times S^3$.

status_search_result: The existence of CMC foliations and maximal hypersurfaces for maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum/Einstein–Maxwell spacetimes with spatial topology $S^3$, including the Bianchi IX case, is a long-standing open problem in mathematical relativity. Surveys on global dynamics of the Einstein equations (e.g. Rendall) list the existence of CMC slices/foliations on Bianchi IX as unresolved, and recent literature on Bianchi IX (e.g., Brehm 2016, Ringström) addresses BKL/oscillatory behaviour but does not establish the conjecture. No source found announcing a resolution.
