paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
original_question: For every fixed positive integer k, can non-real-representability of matroids of branch-width k be certified using only a polynomial number of rank evaluations?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A matroid $M$ on a finite ground set $E$ is determined by its rank function $r:2^E\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, which is integer-valued, monotone, submodular, and satisfies $0\le r(X)\le|X|$. Access to $M$ is via a rank oracle that, given $X\subseteq E$, returns $r(X)$ in unit time. The matroid $M$ is said to be representable over a field $\mathbb{F}$ (in particular over $\mathbb{R}$) if there exist vectors $\{v_e:e\in E\}$ in some $\mathbb{F}$-vector space such that for every $X\subseteq E$, $r(X)$ equals the dimension of the $\mathbb{F}$-linear span of $\{v_e:e\in X\}$.

The branch-width of $M$ is defined as follows. A branch-decomposition of $M$ is a pair $(T,\mu)$ where $T$ is a cubic tree and $\mu$ is a bijection from $E$ to the set of leaves of $T$. Each edge $e$ of $T$ partitions $E$ into two sets $A_e, B_e$ corresponding to the leaves of the two components of $T-e$, and the width of $e$ is $r(A_e)+r(B_e)-r(E)+1$. The width of $(T,\mu)$ is the maximum width over edges of $T$, and the branch-width of $M$ is the minimum width over all branch-decompositions (with branch-width $1$ if $|E|\le 1$).

A certificate for non-$\mathbb{R}$-representability of $M$ accessed via a rank oracle is a sequence of subsets $X_1,\dots,X_t\subseteq E$ together with the values $r(X_1),\dots,r(X_t)$, such that no matroid on $E$ with this rank data on these sets is representable over $\mathbb{R}$. The length of the certificate is $t$.

Question. Fix a positive integer $k$. Does there exist a polynomial $p_k$ such that every matroid $M$ on $n$ elements with branch-width at most $k$ that is not representable over $\mathbb{R}$ admits a certificate of non-$\mathbb{R}$-representability of length at most $p_k(n)$ using only rank evaluations?
status_search_result: The problem is stated as a conjecture in a survey of open problems on excluding uniform matroids, with the author explicitly indicating no intuition for the answer. Subsequent work has established polynomial-length certificates for non-representability over prime fields, but no result resolves the case of non-representability over $\mathbb{R}$ for matroids of bounded branch-width. The conjecture appears to remain open.

original_question: Can Dowling matroids be recognized in polynomial time, where a Dowling matroid is a matroid M \ V obtained from a framed Dowling matroid M with basis V whose fundamental circuits with respect to V all have size at most 3?
self_contained_problem:
A matroid $M$ on ground set $E$ is a pair $(E,\mathcal{I})$ where $\mathcal{I}\subseteq 2^E$ satisfies the usual independence axioms. For an independent set $V\subseteq E$ that is a basis of $M$ and an element $e\in E\setminus V$, the fundamental circuit of $e$ with respect to $V$ is the unique circuit contained in $V\cup\{e\}$.

Call a matroid $M$ a framed Dowling matroid with joint set $V$ if $V$ is a basis of $M$ and every fundamental circuit of $M$ with respect to $V$ has size at most $3$. Call a matroid $N$ a Dowling matroid if there exists a framed Dowling matroid $M$ with joint set $V$ such that $N = M\setminus V$ (the matroid obtained from $M$ by deleting the elements of $V$).

Assume matroids are presented by an independence oracle (or rank oracle) on $n$ elements. Does there exist an algorithm that, given such a matroid, decides whether it is a Dowling matroid using a number of oracle calls and arithmetic operations bounded by a polynomial in $n$?

context_brief: Polynomial-time recognition of real Dowling matroids
original_question: Can Dowling matroids over the real field R be recognized in polynomial time? Here a matroid is a Dowling matroid over R if it can be extended to an R-representable framed Dowling matroid, equivalently if it has a real representation with at most two nonzero entries in each column.

Setup. Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the real field. A matroid $M$ on a finite ground set $E$ is said to be representable over $\mathbb{R}$ if there exists a matrix $A$ with entries in $\mathbb{R}$, whose columns are indexed by $E$, such that a subset $S\subseteq E$ is independent in $M$ if and only if the corresponding columns of $A$ are linearly independent. 

For a positive integer $n$ and a subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathbb{R}^\times$, the framed Dowling matroid of rank $n$ over $\mathbb{R}$ (with group $\Gamma$) is the matroid represented by the $n\times(n+\binom{n}{2}|\Gamma|)$ real matrix whose columns are: the $n$ standard basis vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ (the "frame"), together with all vectors of the form $e_i-\gamma e_j$ for $1\le i<j\le n$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma$. 

Call a matroid $M$ a Dowling matroid over $\mathbb{R}$ if $M$ can be extended (by adding elements) to a matroid that is isomorphic to a submatroid of some framed Dowling matroid over $\mathbb{R}$; equivalently, $M$ admits a representation over $\mathbb{R}$ by a matrix in which every column has at most two nonzero entries.

Question. The input is a matroid $M$ on $n$ elements, given by an independence oracle (or by an explicit list of bases/independent sets). Does there exist an algorithm running in time polynomial in $n$ that decides whether $M$ is a Dowling matroid over $\mathbb{R}$?

paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
original_question: Let C be a minor-closed class of matroids that does not contain all uniform matroids, and let t be the least integer such that C does not contain all uniform matroids of rank t+1. Must C satisfy one of the following three growth alternatives for simple matroids M in C: tau_t(M) is bounded linearly in the rank r(M); C contains all graphic matroids or all bicircular matroids and tau_t(M) is bounded quadratically in r(M); or C contains all GF(q)-representable matroids for some prime power q and tau_t(M) is bounded by a constant times q^{r(M)}?
self_contained_problem:
For a matroid $M$, let $r(M)$ denote its rank, and for a positive integer $t$, let $\tau_t(M)$ denote the minimum number of rank-$t$ flats of $M$ whose union covers the ground set of $M$. A class $\mathcal{M}$ of matroids is minor-closed if it is closed under taking minors and isomorphism. The uniform matroid $U_{a,b}$ has $b$ elements, every $a$-element subset independent.

Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a minor-closed class of matroids that does not contain all uniform matroids, and let $t$ be the least positive integer such that $\mathcal{M}$ does not contain $U_{t+1,n}$ for every $n \geq t+1$. Prove or disprove: at least one of the following three alternatives must hold.

(i) There exists a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\tau_t(M) \leq c\, r(M)$ for every simple matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}$.

(ii) $\mathcal{M}$ contains either all graphic matroids or all bicircular matroids, and there exists a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\tau_t(M) \leq c\, r(M)^2$ for every simple matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}$.

(iii) There is a prime power $q$ such that $\mathcal{M}$ contains all $\mathrm{GF}(q)$-representable matroids, and there exists a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\tau_t(M) \leq c\, q^{r(M)}$ for every simple matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}$.
status_search_result: The conjecture is a generalization (using the covering invariant $\tau_t$) of the Growth Rate Theorem of Geelen, Kung, and Whittle. While the original Growth Rate Theorem (the case $t=1$, counting elements) is established, the $\tau_t$-trichotomy version is posed as an open conjecture in the matroid-minors program, and current literature (e.g., Nelson's work on exponentially dense matroids and projective geometries) addresses partial cases but does not resolve the full statement.

paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
context_brief: Incompatible bicircular grid minors and duals
original_question: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors B(G_n^+) and B(G_n^+)^* must contain a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here G_n^+ is the graph obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and B(G) denotes the bicircular matroid of a graph G.
self_contained_problem:
Definitions and setup.

(1) For a graph G (allowing loops and parallel edges), the bicircular matroid B(G) is the matroid on edge set E(G) whose independent sets are the edge subsets F ⊆ E(G) such that every connected component of the subgraph (V(G), F) contains at most one cycle (i.e., the pseudoforests of G).

(2) For a positive integer n, let G_n denote the n × n grid graph, and let G_n^+ be the graph obtained from G_n by adding one new vertex (an "apex") and joining it by an edge to every vertex of G_n.

(3) For a matroid M, M^* denotes its dual.

(4) The uniform matroid U_{k,2k} is the matroid on a 2k-element ground set in which the independent sets are exactly the subsets of size at most k.

(5) Two minors N_1 and N_2 of a matroid M are called n-interconnected if, intuitively, they cannot be separated by a low-order matroid separation; precisely, fix the standard notion that minors N_1, N_2 of M are n-interconnected when, for every partition (A, B) of the ground set of M with |A|, |B| ≥ n such that the connectivity λ_M(A) < n, neither N_1 nor N_2 is a minor of both M|A and M|B simultaneously (equivalently, every "small" separation of M fails to display N_1 and N_2 on opposite sides).

Problem. Prove or disprove the following statement:

For every positive integer k, there exists a positive integer n = n(k) such that whenever M is a matroid containing both B(G_n^+) and (B(G_n^+))^* as n-interconnected minors, M must contain U_{k,2k} as a minor.
status_search_result: The problem is stated as Conjecture 9.2 in the survey on excluding a uniform matroid (arXiv:2102.02929, Advances in Combinatorics 2023). No published resolution of this specific conjecture about n-interconnected B(G_n^+) and its dual was found in the search; related results concern unavoidable minors of large 4-connected bicircular matroids but do not settle this conjecture. It appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid

original_question: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors M(G_n^+) and M(G_n^+)^* either contains a U_{k,2k}-minor or contains a minor isomorphic to a rank-k projective geometry over some finite field? Here G_n^+ is obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and M(G) denotes the cycle matroid of G.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Define $G_n^+$ to be the graph obtained from the $n\times n$ grid graph by adding a single new vertex (an apex) and joining it to every vertex of the grid. For a graph $G$, let $M(G)$ denote its cycle matroid, and let $M^*$ denote the dual of a matroid $M$. Recall that $U_{k,2k}$ is the uniform matroid of rank $k$ on $2k$ elements.

Two minors $N_1$ and $N_2$ of a matroid $M$ are said to be $n$-interconnected if, for every partition $(A,B)$ of the ground set of $M$ with $|A|,|B|\ge n$ such that the connectivity of $M$ across $(A,B)$ is less than $n$, both $N_1$ and $N_2$ have all of their elements on the same side of the partition is violated — equivalently, $M$ admits no $(<n)$-separation that separates the elements of either $N_1$ or $N_2$ in a way preventing both minors from being detected together (the precise definition being the standard notion of $n$-interconnectedness for a pair of minors in a matroid: there is no separation of order less than $n$ in $M$ such that each side contains at least $n$ elements and the elements of one of the minors are confined to one side).

Prove or disprove the following: For every positive integer $k$ there exists a positive integer $n$ such that any matroid $M$ which has two $n$-interconnected minors isomorphic to $M(G_n^+)$ and $M(G_n^+)^*$, respectively, must contain either a $U_{k,2k}$-minor or a minor isomorphic to the rank-$k$ projective geometry $\mathrm{PG}(k-1,q)$ over some finite field $\mathrm{GF}(q)$.

original_question: Can one find a structural characterization of the class of round real-representable matroids with no U_{3,6}-minor?
self_contained_problem:
A matroid M is said to be representable over the real numbers (or R-representable) if there exists a matrix with real entries whose columns, indexed by the ground set of M, realize the independence structure of M (i.e., a subset is independent in M iff the corresponding columns are linearly independent over R). context_brief: Structure with a spanning projective-geometry restriction
original_question: Let F be a field over which U_{a,b} is not representable. Can one give a qualitative structure theorem for matroids with no U_{a,b}-minor that have a spanning PG(k,F)-restriction?
self_contained_problem:
Let F be a field, and let a, b be positive integers with a ≤ b such that the uniform matroid U_{a,b} (the matroid on b elements in which the independent sets are exactly the subsets of size at most a) is not representable over F. For an integer k ≥ 0, let PG(k,F) denote the rank-(k+1) projective geometry over F, viewed as a matroid. A matroid M is said to have a spanning PG(k,F)-restriction if PG(k,F) is a restriction of M whose rank equals the rank of M, and M has no U_{a,b}-minor if no minor of M is isomorphic to U_{a,b}.

Provide a qualitative structure theorem describing all matroids M that simultaneously (i) have no U_{a,b}-minor and (ii) contain a spanning PG(k,F)-restriction. That is, give a structural characterization showing in what sense every such matroid is "close to" being representable over F.
status_search_result: A 2016 paper by Geelen and Nelson ("The structure of matroids with a spanning clique or projective geometry," arXiv:1602.05132) provides a qualitative structure theorem for matroids with a spanning PG(n,q)-restriction having no U_{s,2s}-minor and no PG(n,q')-minor for q' > q over finite fields, showing such matroids are "close" to GF(q)-representable. This addresses the finite-field case for specific uniform-minor exclusions, but a fully general qualitative structure theorem covering arbitrary fields F and all (a,b) with U_{a,b} non-representable over F does not appear to be fully resolved.

original_question: Can one give a qualitative structure theorem for matroids with no U_{a,b}-minor that have a spanning M(K_n)-restriction, where M(K_n) is the cycle matroid of the complete graph K_n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $2 \le a \le b-2$, and let $U_{a,b}$ denote the uniform matroid of rank $a$ on $b$ elements (the matroid on a $b$-element ground set whose independent sets are all subsets of size at most $a$). For a positive integer $n$, let $M(K_n)$ denote the cycle matroid of the complete graph $K_n$ on $n$ vertices, whose ground set is the edge set $E(K_n)$ and whose independent sets are the edge sets of forests in $K_n$.

Recall that a matroid $N$ is a minor of a matroid $M$ if $N$ can be obtained from $M$ by a sequence of deletions and contractions, and that $N$ is a restriction of $M$ if $N = M|X$ for some subset $X$ of the ground set of $M$. A restriction $M|X$ is called spanning if the rank of $M|X$ equals the rank of $M$.

Provide a qualitative structure theorem describing all matroids $M$ that
(i) have no $U_{a,b}$-minor, and
(ii) admit a spanning restriction isomorphic to $M(K_n)$ for some $n$.

That is, characterize, up to a controlled set of perturbations or modifications, the class of such matroids in a way analogous to known structural descriptions for minor-closed classes.
status_search_result: Related structural results exist (e.g., descriptions of matroids with a spanning clique or projective geometry restriction by Geelen–Nelson and others, and tangle-based local structure in matroid minor theory by Geelen–Gerards–Whittle), but a definitive qualitative structure theorem for matroids with no $U_{a,b}$-minor that have a spanning $M(K_n)$-restriction does not appear to be explicitly established in the search results. Status remains unclear.

paper_title: Open Problems in Algebraic Statistics
original_question: How can one study the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables by constructing the associated varieties through gluing familiar secant varieties and by using representation theory to describe their defining equations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a directed acyclic graph whose vertex set is partitioned into observed nodes and hidden (latent) nodes, and to each vertex associate a discrete random variable taking finitely many states. The corresponding graphical model is the set of joint probability distributions on the observed variables obtained by marginalizing out the hidden variables in the family of distributions that factor according to $G$. The Zariski closure of this set in the probability simplex (viewed inside an appropriate tensor space) is an algebraic variety $V_G$.

(a) Develop a systematic geometric construction of $V_G$ by realizing it as the result of gluing together (along common coordinate subspaces) classical secant varieties of Segre, Segre–Veronese, or Grassmannian varieties associated with the local structure at each hidden node. Concretely, describe an operation on varieties that mirrors the marginalization-and-factorization operation on graphical models, and prove that iterating this operation on secant varieties of Segre varieties (which correspond to the simplest naive Bayes / hidden-variable models) recovers $V_G$ for arbitrary $G$.

(b) Using the natural action of the product of general linear groups (one factor for each observed variable) on the ambient tensor space, decompose the homogeneous ideal $I(V_G)$ as a representation of this group, and describe a generating set of $I(V_G)$ in terms of irreducible representations (Schur modules / highest-weight vectors). In particular, give explicit, representation-theoretic descriptions of the defining polynomial equations of $V_G$ for general graphs with hidden variables.
category_tag: Algebraic statistics of hidden-variable graphical models
status_search_result: This is posed as a broad general program rather than a single theorem to prove. Partial progress exists: secant varieties of Segre varieties are known to correspond to naive Bayes / latent class models, and representation-theoretic equations have been found in special cases (e.g., results by Landsberg–Manivel, Allman–Rhodes, Garcia–Stillman–Sturmfels, Sullivant and collaborators). However, a unified gluing construction and complete representation-theoretic description of defining ideals for general graphical models with hidden variables remains an active open research direction.

paper_title: Open Problems in Algebraic Statistics
original_question: How should the geometry of maximum likelihood estimation for algebraic statistical models be studied, and how do statistical features of a model relate to geometric properties of the corresponding projective variety?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ be an irreducible complex projective variety such that $V \cap \Delta_n$ is nonempty, where $\Delta_n = \{(p_0:\dots:p_n) : p_i > 0,\ \sum p_i = 1\}$ is the open probability simplex viewed inside $\mathbb{P}^n$. Such a variety, intersected with $\Delta_n$, defines an algebraic statistical model on the sample space $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. Given a vector of observed counts $u = (u_0,\dots,u_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}_{\ge 0}$, the maximum likelihood estimation problem asks for the critical points of the log-likelihood function
$$\ell_u(p) = \sum_{i=0}^n u_i \log p_i - \Big(\sum_i u_i\Big)\log\Big(\sum_i p_i\Big)$$
restricted to the smooth locus of $V$.

Develop a systematic theory of the geometry of maximum likelihood estimation on such projective varieties $V$. Concretely, address the following:

(a) Define and study the maximum likelihood degree $\mathrm{MLdeg}(V)$, the number of complex critical points of $\ell_u$ on $V_{\mathrm{sm}}$ for generic $u$, and express it in terms of intrinsic invariants of $V$ (e.g.\ Euler characteristics of complements of hyperplane sections, Chern–Schwartz–MacPherson classes, or characteristic classes of the pair $(V, V \cap \mathcal{H})$ where $\mathcal{H}$ is the coordinate-plus-sum-hyperplane arrangement).

(b) Determine which geometric properties of $V$ (smoothness, toric structure, determinantal structure, very affineness of $V \setminus \mathcal{H}$, singularities, dual variety, discriminants) correspond to which statistical features of the model (identifiability, existence and uniqueness of the MLE, rationality of the MLE, boundary behavior, model dimension, exponential-family structure).

(c) Provide structural theorems relating $\mathrm{MLdeg}(V)$ and the algebraic complexity of MLE to classical invariants of $V$, and characterize the class of models for which the MLE is a rational function of the data (i.e.\ $\mathrm{MLdeg}(V) = 1$).
category_tag: likelihood geometry of algebraic statistical models
status_search_result: The general program of likelihood geometry has been developed substantially since being posed: the ML degree was characterized topologically (Huh, 2013; Huh–Sturmfels, "Likelihood Geometry", 2014), rational MLE models have been classified for discrete exponential families (Duarte–Marigliano–Sturmfels), Gaussian likelihood geometry of projective varieties has been studied (Améndola et al., 2022), and computations have been carried out for complete quadrics, determinantal varieties, and toric models. However, the overarching program of fully relating statistical features to geometric invariants of arbitrary projective models remains an active area with many open subproblems.

paper_title: Open Problems in Algebraic Statistics
original_question: What is the formula, in terms of m, n, and r, for the maximum likelihood degree of the variety of m×n matrices of rank at most r? In particular, the first interesting unresolved case is m = n = 4 and r = 2, where symbolic solution of the likelihood equations is not currently known.
self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $m, n, r$ with $r \le \min(m,n)$, let $V_{m,n,r} \subset \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$ denote the determinantal variety of $m \times n$ complex matrices of rank at most $r$, cut out by the vanishing of all $(r+1) \times (r+1)$ minors. Given a generic data matrix $U = (u_{ij}) \in \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$ with $u_{++} = \sum_{i,j} u_{ij}$, consider the log-likelihood function
$$
\ell_U(P) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n u_{ij} \log p_{ij} \;-\; u_{++} \log\!\Big(\sum_{i,j} p_{ij}\Big)
$$
viewed as a rational function on $V_{m,n,r}$. The maximum likelihood (ML) degree of $V_{m,n,r}$ is defined as the number of complex critical points of $\ell_U$ on the smooth locus of $V_{m,n,r}$ for generic $U$; this number is independent of the choice of generic $U$.

Find a closed-form formula, as an explicit function of $m, n, r$, for the ML degree of $V_{m,n,r}$. As the first specific instance that is not covered by previously known closed-form expressions, determine (and symbolically certify) the ML degree in the case $m = n = 4$, $r = 2$ by solving the corresponding likelihood equations symbolically.
status_search_result: A general closed-form formula in $m, n, r$ remains unknown. Significant partial progress has been made: Hauenstein, Rodriguez, and Sturmfels computed many ML degrees numerically (including the $4\times 4$ rank-$2$ case using Bertini) and conjectured a closed formula for the $3 \times n$ rank-$2$ case; this conjecture, along with recursive expressions for $m \times n$ rank-$2$ matrices, was subsequently established (Manivel–Michałek and others, including a Euler-characteristic approach by Rodriguez–Wang). Draisma and Rodriguez proved an ML duality between varieties of complementary ranks. No general formula in $m, n, r$ has been published.

paper_title: Open Problems in Algebraic Statistics
original_question: Let Σ be a real symmetric positive-definite 5×5 matrix. For each pair of distinct indices i and j in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and each subset K of {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} excluding i and j, let a_{ij|K} = det(Σ_{{i}∪K,{j}∪K}) be the corresponding almost-principal minor, with row index set {i} ∪ K and column index set {j} ∪ K. Which subsets S of these almost-principal minors occur exactly as the vanishing set {a_{ij|K} : a_{ij|K} = 0} for some real symmetric positive-definite 5×5 matrix Σ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = (\sigma_{ij})$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $5 \times 5$ matrix. For distinct indices $i, j \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ and any subset $K \subseteq \{1,2,3,4,5\} \setminus \{i,j\}$, define the almost-principal minor
$$a_{ij\mid K}(\Sigma) \;=\; \det\bigl(\Sigma_{\{i\}\cup K,\, \{j\}\cup K}\bigr),$$
i.e. the determinant of the submatrix of $\Sigma$ with row index set $\{i\}\cup K$ and column index set $\{j\}\cup K$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the collection of all such symbols $[i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K]$ (with the convention $[i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K] = [j \perp\!\!\!\perp i \mid K]$).

For a real symmetric positive-definite $5\times 5$ matrix $\Sigma$, set
$$Z(\Sigma) \;=\; \{\,[i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K]\in\mathcal{A}\;:\; a_{ij\mid K}(\Sigma)=0\,\}.$$

Classify completely the subsets $S \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ that arise as $Z(\Sigma)$ for some real symmetric positive-definite $5\times 5$ matrix $\Sigma$. Equivalently, determine all representable gaussoids on five elements.
status_search_result: The classification of representable gaussoids is fully known for $n=4$ (629 of 679 gaussoids are realizable). For $n=5$, the corresponding classification has not been completed; the literature on the geometry of gaussoids notes that the relevant compatibility/realizability checks become computationally prohibitive at $n=5$, and recent works on construction methods and selfadhesivity in Gaussian CI structures still treat the $n=5$ realizability question as an unresolved problem.

paper_title: Open Problems in Algebraic Statistics
original_question: For a fixed n, let PD_n be the cone of real positive-definite symmetric n×n matrices, and let SubMod_n be the cone in R^{2^n} with coordinates H_S indexed by all subsets S of {1, 2, ..., n}, defined by the inequalities H_{{i}∪K} + H_{{j}∪K} ≤ H_{{i,j}∪K} + H_K for every subset K of {1, ..., n} and every pair of distinct indices i and j not in K. For Σ in PD_n, define the entropy map H by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I), where Σ_I is the principal minor indexed by I. Since Gaussian conditional independence models are exactly inverse images under H of faces of SubMod_n, characterize the image H(PD_n), determine how H(PD_n) intersects the faces of SubMod_n, and describe the fibers of H.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $n$. Let $\mathrm{PD}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric positive-definite $n\times n$ matrices. Index coordinates of $\mathbb{R}^{2^n}$ by the subsets $S\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, calling the coordinates $H_S$, and define the submodular cone
$$\mathrm{SubMod}_n=\{(H_S)_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}}\in\mathbb{R}^{2^n} : H_{\{i\}\cup K}+H_{\{j\}\cup K}\le H_{\{i,j\}\cup K}+H_K\}$$
for all $K\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ and all distinct $i,j\in\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus K$. Define the entropy map $H:\mathrm{PD}_n\to\mathbb{R}^{2^n}$ by
$$H(\Sigma)_I=-\log\det(\Sigma_I),\qquad I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},$$
where $\Sigma_I$ is the principal submatrix of $\Sigma$ on rows and columns indexed by $I$ (with $\det(\Sigma_\emptyset)=1$). It is known that $H(\mathrm{PD}_n)\subseteq\mathrm{SubMod}_n$, and that Gaussian conditional independence models are precisely the preimages under $H$ of faces of $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$.

(a) Characterize the image $H(\mathrm{PD}_n)$ as a subset of $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$.

(b) Describe how $H(\mathrm{PD}_n)$ intersects each face of $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$.

(c) Describe the fibers of $H$, i.e., for each point $h\in H(\mathrm{PD}_n)$ describe $H^{-1}(h)\subseteq\mathrm{PD}_n$.
category_tag: Algebraic statistics / entropy map of Gaussians
status_search_result: The problem is broadly open. Partial progress exists: the image of the entropy map has been explicitly computed in dimension 3, an analog has been studied over non-archimedean valued fields where the image lies in the supermodular cone, and the tropicalization of the principal-minor map of positive-definite matrices has been identified with the intersection of the affine tropical flag variety with the submodular cone, yielding new algebraic inequalities among principal minors. A full characterization of the image, its intersection with faces, and the fibers of $H$ for general $n$ does not appear in the literature.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: In randomized wait-free consensus for an asynchronous shared-memory system of n processes, where consensus requires agreement, validity, and eventual decision, and where wait-freedom means that every process terminates in finitely many of its own steps regardless of scheduling, what is the optimal expected register-operation complexity under an adaptive adversary that knows the current system state? In particular, can the known O(n^2 log n) expected total-work protocol using atomic read-write registers, or O(n^2) expected total-work protocol using counters, be improved using objects constructible from atomic registers, or can the lower bound be raised to show that quadratic work is necessary?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an asynchronous shared-memory system of $n$ processes that communicate through atomic read/write registers (and possibly other deterministic objects implementable from such registers, e.g., counters). Each process has an input value and must produce an output, subject to:
- Agreement: no two processes decide on different values.
- Validity: any decided value is some process's input.
- Wait-freedom: every nonfaulty process decides after a finite number of its own steps, regardless of how the steps of all processes are interleaved.

Processes may use private randomness. The schedule is chosen by an adaptive adversary that, at each step, observes the entire current state of the system (including the contents of all shared objects and the local state and random choices made so far) and then selects which process takes the next step.

Define the expected total work of a protocol to be the supremum, over all adaptive adversary strategies and all input assignments, of the expected total number of shared-object operations performed by all processes until every process has decided.

Determine the optimal expected total work for randomized wait-free binary consensus against an adaptive adversary in this model. Concretely:
1. Is there a protocol, using only objects implementable from atomic read/write registers, with expected total work $o(n^2 \log n)$ (improving upon the known $O(n^2 \log n)$ register protocol), or $o(n^2)$ when counters are allowed (improving upon the known $O(n^2)$ counter-based protocol)?
2. Or can one prove a matching $\Omega(n^2)$ lower bound on the expected total work, showing that quadratic work is necessary?
status_search_result: Attiya and Censor (STOC 2007, "Tight bounds for asynchronous randomized consensus") gave a protocol achieving expected total work $O(n^2)$ for randomized wait-free consensus against an adaptive adversary in the shared-memory model and proved a matching $\Omega(n^2)$ lower bound, establishing $\Theta(n^2)$ as the optimal expected total work. This closed the previously known polylogarithmic gap and resolved the question.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: In oblivious routing on a graph-modeled multi-hop network, where each newly injected packet chooses a path independently of the path choices of other packets, congestion is the maximum number of selected paths using any edge, and stretch is the ratio between the selected path length and the shortest-path length, for which network classes or structural circumstances can an oblivious routing algorithm simultaneously achieve near-optimal congestion and small, ideally constant, stretch?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-hop communication network modeled as an undirected graph G=(V,E). An oblivious routing algorithm is a (possibly randomized) procedure that, for each source–destination pair (s,t), specifies a path (or distribution over paths) from s to t independently of the choices made for any other source–destination pair. For a given set of packet requests, define:

- congestion C as the maximum, over all edges e∈E, of the number of selected paths using e;
- stretch as the maximum, over all packets, of the ratio between the length of the path selected for that packet and the length of a shortest s–t path in G.

Let C* denote the minimum congestion achievable by any (not necessarily oblivious) routing for the given request set.

Identify graph classes G and structural conditions on G under which there exists an oblivious routing algorithm that, for every request set, simultaneously achieves:
(i) congestion C = O(C*) (or within a polylogarithmic factor of C*), and
(ii) stretch O(1) (ideally a constant independent of |V|).

Beyond known examples (such as d-dimensional meshes and certain geometric/disc networks), determine further network classes — for instance, bounded-growth networks, or networks whose nodes are uniformly distributed in closed polygonal regions — for which both congestion and stretch can be minimized simultaneously by an oblivious routing scheme, and characterize the structural circumstances that make such simultaneous optimization possible.
status_search_result: Results are known for specific network classes (d-dimensional meshes, geometric/hole-free networks) achieving constant stretch with congestion within an O(log n) factor of optimal, and hop-constrained oblivious routing has been studied more recently. However, a general characterization of network classes admitting simultaneously near-optimal congestion and constant stretch remains open, and identifying further such classes (e.g., bounded-growth or wireless-style networks) is still an active question.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: For multi-valued ongoing consensus, where inputs and outputs need not be binary and the required output may be any value lying within the range of the correct input values, which consensus functions should be explored to optimize stability, meaning to minimize output changes over time while preserving the stated validity condition?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an ongoing (long-lived) consensus problem in a distributed system with $n$ processes, where at each time step every process holds an input value drawn from a (not necessarily binary) totally ordered domain $V$. A consensus function is a map
$$f : V^n \times V \to V, \qquad (\mathbf{x}, y_{\text{prev}}) \mapsto y,$$
that, given the current vector of inputs $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ and the previous output $y_{\text{prev}}$, produces a new output $y$. The function must satisfy the range validity condition: for every input vector $\mathbf{x}$ and every previous output $y_{\text{prev}}$,
$$\min_i x_i \;\le\; f(\mathbf{x}, y_{\text{prev}}) \;\le\; \max_i x_i,$$
where the minimum and maximum are taken over the indices $i$ corresponding to correct (non-faulty) processes.

Define the instability of $f$ to be the worst-case number of output changes along any sequence of input vectors $\mathbf{x}^{(0)}, \mathbf{x}^{(1)}, \mathbf{x}^{(2)}, \dots$ in which consecutive vectors differ in at most one coordinate (a geodesic path of input changes), where the output at step $t$ is computed as $y^{(t)} = f(\mathbf{x}^{(t)}, y^{(t-1)})$.

Problem: Identify and characterize consensus functions $f$ that satisfy the range validity condition above and that minimize this instability (i.e., minimize the worst-case number of output changes over time). In particular, determine tight lower and upper bounds on the achievable instability and exhibit explicit families of optimal consensus functions for general (multi-valued) input domains.
status_search_result: Stability of binary and multi-valued consensus functions has been studied (e.g., Davidovitch–Dolev–Rajsbaum on stability of multi-valued continuous consensus, and later work on connected/stabilizing consensus). However, the general question of identifying optimal consensus functions minimizing output changes under range validity for multi-valued ongoing consensus does not appear to be fully resolved; partial bounds are known but a complete characterization remains open.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: For wait-free linearizable register implementations of multi-writer atomic snapshot objects with m components and n processes, what is the optimal time complexity of UPDATE? More specifically, can one prove UPDATE lower bounds stronger than the known Omega(m) bound, or design implementations with UPDATE time better than the known O(n) bound?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a shared-memory asynchronous system with $n$ processes that communicate by reading and writing to atomic registers. An $m$-component multi-writer atomic snapshot object stores a vector $(v_1,\dots,v_m)$ and supports two operations available to every process: $\mathrm{UPDATE}(i,v)$, which sets the $i$-th component to value $v$, and $\mathrm{SCAN}()$, which returns the current vector. An implementation of such a snapshot object from atomic read/write registers is required to be (i) linearizable: every concurrent execution of UPDATE and SCAN operations is equivalent to some sequential execution that respects the real-time order of non-overlapping operations, and (ii) wait-free: every process completes any operation in a finite number of its own steps regardless of the speeds or failures of other processes. The time (step) complexity of an operation is the worst-case number of base-register steps a process performs to complete it.

It is known that any such wait-free linearizable implementation requires $\Omega(m)$ steps in the worst case for an UPDATE operation, and that there exist implementations achieving $O(n)$ steps per UPDATE. Determine the optimal worst-case step complexity of UPDATE for wait-free linearizable implementations of an $m$-component, $n$-process multi-writer atomic snapshot object from atomic registers. In particular:

1. Prove a lower bound on the UPDATE step complexity that is asymptotically stronger than $\Omega(m)$ (for instance, depending nontrivially on $n$), or
2. Construct an implementation whose UPDATE step complexity is asymptotically better than $O(n)$ (for example $o(n)$ when $m$ is small compared to $n$), thereby narrowing or closing the gap between these bounds.
status_search_result: The general problem of the optimal UPDATE step complexity for wait-free linearizable multi-writer atomic snapshot objects from registers appears to remain open. Tight bounds are known only in restricted settings: an $\Omega(m)$ lower bound holds for "partitioned" implementations, and stronger bounds such as $\Omega(\sqrt{mn})$ and $\Omega(mn)$ have been established for space-optimal implementations using only $m$ multi-writer registers. No general lower bound exceeding $\Omega(m)$ or general implementation with UPDATE time below $O(n)$ has been reported.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: Can randomization be used to obtain efficient implementations of multi-writer atomic snapshot objects from registers, potentially beating deterministic lower bounds on snapshot space-time tradeoffs?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the asynchronous shared-memory model in which n processes communicate via atomic read/write registers and may fail by crashing. A multi-writer atomic snapshot object stores a vector of n components and supports two operations: UPDATE(i, v), which sets component i to value v, and SCAN, which returns a vector consisting of (linearizable) values of all n components. An implementation of such an object from base registers is wait-free if every operation by a non-faulty process completes in a finite number of its own steps, and is linearizable with respect to the sequential snapshot specification. Known deterministic lower bounds establish nontrivial space–time tradeoffs: for instance, any implementation using m base registers requires Ω(mn) steps for SCAN in the worst case, and space-optimal implementations require Ω(m^2) steps per SCAN.

Question: Does there exist a randomized wait-free linearizable implementation of a multi-writer atomic snapshot object for n processes from atomic read/write registers whose worst-case (or expected) step complexity for SCAN and UPDATE strictly beats the corresponding deterministic space–time tradeoff lower bounds, for some nontrivial regime of the number m of registers used? In particular, can randomization be exploited to obtain implementations of multi-writer snapshot objects from registers that are asymptotically more efficient than any deterministic implementation subject to the same space constraints?
status_search_result: A randomized wait-free implementation of multi-writer atomic snapshots from registers achieving O(log^3 n) step complexity per operation has been given (Attiya, Censor-Hillel, and others, DISC 2013), an exponential improvement over the linear deterministic lower bounds, demonstrating that randomization can indeed beat deterministic snapshot lower bounds. However, the precise space–time tradeoffs achievable by randomized implementations are not fully resolved, and weaker randomized lower bounds (e.g., Ω(log n / log log n)) leave a gap, so the broader question of optimal randomized space–time tradeoffs remains open.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: For the asynchronous deterministic shared-memory Write-All problem, where p processors must write to t distinct memory locations while an adaptive adversary may introduce dynamic processor failures or delays and work counts all processor steps, can one either prove a work lower bound stronger than Omega(t log t) or design an asynchronous algorithm for the case p = t whose work is asymptotically less than O(t^(1+epsilon)) for every fixed epsilon > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the asynchronous deterministic Write-All problem in a shared-memory model defined as follows. There are $p$ asynchronous processors and a shared memory consisting of $t$ distinct locations, each initialized to $0$. The goal is to ensure that every one of the $t$ memory locations has been written to with the value $1$. An adaptive adversary controls scheduling and may introduce dynamic processor failures (crashes) or arbitrary delays at any time during the execution. The work complexity of an algorithm is the total number of basic shared-memory steps (read/write/compare-and-swap or equivalent primitive operations) taken by all processors, summed across all processors and over the entire execution, in the worst case over adversarial schedules.

It is known that the worst-case work for any deterministic asynchronous Write-All algorithm is $\Omega(t \log t)$, and known algorithms achieve work $O(t^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ when $p = t$.

Resolve at least one of the following:
(a) Prove a work lower bound asymptotically stronger than $\Omega(t \log t)$ for the asynchronous deterministic Write-All problem.
(b) Exhibit a deterministic asynchronous algorithm that, in the case $p = t$, solves Write-All with worst-case work $f(t)$ satisfying $f(t) = o(t^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ (i.e., subpolynomial overhead above $t$).
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a resolution of the work gap for the asynchronous deterministic Write-All problem. The known Ω(t log t) lower bound and algorithms with O(t^{1+ε}) work for p = t remain the standard reference points; subsequent work has focused on related models (message-passing Do-All, randomized variants, at-most-once semantics) rather than closing this specific gap. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: In a synchronous distributed message-passing network of n nodes, where each node can send O(log n) bits to each neighbor per round and has a distinct O(log n)-bit identifier, what is the distributed round complexity of obtaining a good approximation for a general integer linear program? The general ILP setting includes n producing nodes choosing integer variables x_i, m accepting nodes with constraints of the form sum_i a_{j,i} x_i <= b_j for integer coefficients, and an objective to minimize or approximate sum_i c_i x_i, without assuming that the coefficients form a metric.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a synchronous distributed message-passing network modeled by an undirected graph on n nodes. Each node has a distinct identifier of O(log n) bits and may send a (possibly different) message of O(log n) bits to each of its neighbors in every synchronous round (the CONGEST model). 

A general integer linear program is distributed over the network as follows. There are n "producing" nodes, indexed by i, each of which must choose an integer variable x_i ≥ 0. There are m "accepting" nodes, indexed by j, each of which holds a constraint of the form
    Σ_i a_{j,i} x_i ≤ b_j,
where the coefficients a_{j,i} and right-hand sides b_j are nonnegative integers, possibly arbitrarily large, and are not assumed to form any metric. Each producing node i also has a nonnegative integer cost c_i, and the global objective is to minimize (or approximate) Σ_i c_i x_i (analogous formulations apply for maximization). Each producing node i initially knows c_i and the coefficients a_{j,i} associated with it, and each accepting node j initially knows its constraint (the coefficients a_{j,i} and the bound b_j); communication between nodes follows the underlying network graph.

Determine the distributed round complexity, in this model, of computing a good (e.g., constant-factor or (1+ε)-factor) approximation to such a general integer linear program. In particular, is there an algorithm running in a small (ideally constant, or at most polylogarithmic in n) number of rounds that produces a feasible integer assignment whose objective value is within a provable approximation factor of the optimum, for arbitrary nonnegative integer coefficients?
category_tag: distributed approximation of integer linear programs
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on distributed approximation of packing and covering integer linear programs. Ghaffari–Kuhn–Maus (STOC 2017) gave an O(log³ n / ε)-round (1±ε)-approximation in the LOCAL model, and a 2023 PODC paper by Faour, Ghaffari et al. improved this to O(log³(1/ε) log n / ε) rounds for packing and O((log log n + log(1/ε))³ log n / ε) for covering. Matching Ω(log n/ε) lower bounds exist for problems such as vertex cover and dominating set. However, these results are largely in the LOCAL model and concern packing/covering ILPs; the general ILP question (in CONGEST, with arbitrary nonnegative integer coefficients and possibly small/constant round complexity) remains not fully resolved.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: In the k-local distributed algorithm model, where each node can communicate with its neighbors at most k times and therefore can gather only information from its k-neighborhood, is there a deterministic local construction of a maximal independent set in general graphs, and what local complexity can such a construction achieve?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the LOCAL model of distributed computing on a simple undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with $n=|V|$ nodes, where each node has a unique identifier and synchronous communication proceeds in rounds; in each round, every node may exchange a message of arbitrary size with each of its neighbors and perform unbounded local computation. A $k$-local (deterministic) algorithm is one in which every node terminates after at most $k$ rounds, so that its output depends only on the information available in its $k$-hop neighborhood. A maximal independent set (MIS) of $G$ is a set $S \subseteq V$ such that no two vertices of $S$ are adjacent, and every vertex of $V \setminus S$ has a neighbor in $S$.

Question: Does there exist a deterministic distributed algorithm in the LOCAL model that, on every $n$-vertex graph, computes a maximal independent set, and what is the smallest possible local complexity (number of rounds $k$, as a function of $n$ and the maximum degree $\Delta$) achievable by such a deterministic algorithm? In particular, determine the optimal round complexity of deterministic MIS construction in general graphs.
status_search_result: Major progress was achieved by Rozhoň and Ghaffari (STOC 2020), who gave the first polylogarithmic-time deterministic distributed algorithm for network decomposition, yielding a poly(log n)-round deterministic MIS algorithm and resolving Linial's long-standing question about whether deterministic MIS admits a polylogarithmic-round algorithm. Subsequent work (Ghaffari–Grunau, STOC 2023; Faour–Ghaffari et al., 2024–2025) further improved bounds to $O(\log^2\Delta \cdot \log n)$ rounds. However, the exact optimal round complexity of deterministic MIS remains unresolved: there is still a gap between the known upper bounds and the $\Omega(\log n / \log\log n)$ and $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n / \log\log n})$ lower bounds (Kuhn–Moscibroda–Wattenhofer; Balliu et al.). So the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
original_question: Does there exist a language that can be recognized by a deterministic linear bounded automaton using O(n^2) time on inputs of length n, but cannot be generated by any Boolean grammar? Here a Boolean grammar is a formal grammar extending context-free grammars with implicit disjunction, explicit conjunction in rule bodies, and explicit negation.
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a formal grammar generalizing context-free grammars in which each rule has the form
  A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n,
where each αᵢ, βⱼ is a string over (Σ ∪ N) with Σ a terminal alphabet and N a finite set of nonterminals; a string w is generated by such a rule (under a well-founded semantic interpretation, e.g. via the unique solution of the associated language equations) if it can be parsed according to every conjunct αᵢ and according to none of the conjuncts βⱼ. The class of Boolean languages is the family of languages L(G) generated by Boolean grammars G.

A deterministic linear bounded automaton (deterministic LBA) is a deterministic single-tape Turing machine whose work tape is restricted to the cells initially occupied by its input. Its running time on an input is the number of computation steps until acceptance or rejection.

Question: Does there exist a language L ⊆ Σ* such that
  (i) L is decided by some deterministic LBA running in time O(n²) on every input of length n, and
  (ii) L is not equal to L(G) for any Boolean grammar G?

Equivalently, exhibit a language in DTIME(n²) ∩ DSPACE(n) that is provably not generated by any Boolean grammar, or prove that no such language exists.
status_search_result: The problem of separating Boolean grammars from deterministic linear-space / quadratic-time computations remains open. Although the family of Boolean languages is known to lie inside DTIME(n^{2.376}) ∩ DSPACE(n), no specific language in this class has been proved to lie outside the Boolean grammar family, and no general non-representability methods are known. Surveys of the nine Okhotin problems indicate that this lower-bound problem is among those that have not been resolved.

paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
original_question: Are all languages generated by Boolean grammars contained in deterministic time DTIME(n^(3-epsilon)) for some positive epsilon, thereby improving the known cubic-time recognition bound for Boolean grammars?
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, P, S), where Σ is a finite alphabet, N is a finite set of nonterminal symbols disjoint from Σ, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and P is a finite set of rules of the form

    A → α_1 & … & α_m & ¬β_1 & … & ¬β_n,

with m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The language L(G) ⊆ Σ* generated by G is defined as the (unique, when it exists) interpretation of the system of language equations

    A = ⋃_{(A → α_1 & … & ¬β_n) ∈ P} (⋂_i L(α_i)) ∩ (⋂_j (Σ* ∖ L(β_j)))   (A ∈ N),

assuming the system has a strongly unique solution (the standard semantic restriction for Boolean grammars).

The classical recognition algorithm for Boolean grammars, generalizing the Cocke–Kasami–Younger algorithm, decides membership w ∈ L(G) in time O(|w|^3) on a deterministic Turing machine.

Question: Does there exist a real number ε > 0 such that for every Boolean grammar G, the language L(G) belongs to the deterministic time complexity class DTIME(n^{3−ε})?
status_search_result: The problem appears to have been solved affirmatively. Okhotin generalized Valiant's algorithm to Boolean grammars, showing membership can be decided in time O(BMM(n) log n), where BMM(n) is the complexity of n×n Boolean matrix multiplication. Consequently, every Boolean-grammar language lies in DTIME(n^{ω+o(1)}) ⊆ DTIME(n^{3−ε}) for some ε > 0 (e.g., DTIME(n^{2.373})), improving the cubic bound.

paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
original_question: Does every Boolean grammar have an equivalent Boolean grammar in Greibach normal form that generates the same language? For Boolean grammars in this setting, Greibach normal form means that each non-epsilon rule has one leading terminal a shared by all positive and negative conjuncts, with rules of the form A -> a alpha_1 & ... & a alpha_m & not a beta_1 & ... & not a beta_n, where m+n >= 1 and the alpha_i and beta_i are strings over terminals and nonterminals.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, R, S), where Σ is a finite set of terminals, N is a finite set of nonterminals, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and R is a finite set of rules of the form

   A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n,

with A ∈ N, m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The semantics is given by the (assumed unique) solution of the associated system of language equations: each nonterminal A is assigned a language L(A) ⊆ Σ* such that, for every rule above, the intersection of the languages denoted by α_i minus the union of those denoted by β_j is contained in L(A), and L(A) is exactly the union of these contributions over all rules with left-hand side A. The language generated by G is L(G) = L(S).

A Boolean grammar is said to be in Greibach normal form if every rule for a nonterminal generating only nonempty strings has the form

   A → a α₁ & … & a α_m & ¬a β₁ & … & ¬a β_n,

where a ∈ Σ is a single terminal that is the common leading symbol of every positive and every negative conjunct, m + n ≥ 1, and α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)* (the empty word may be handled separately by a rule S → ε if ε ∈ L(G)).

Question. Does every Boolean grammar admit an equivalent Boolean grammar in Greibach normal form generating exactly the same language?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published proof that every Boolean grammar can be converted to Greibach normal form, nor a counterexample. Related work notes that even for the weaker class of conjunctive grammars no Greibach-style normal form is known, and a more elaborate "odd normal form" of Okhotin and Reitwießner is used as a substitute. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
original_question: Does there exist a language that is inherently ambiguous with respect to Boolean grammars? In this context, a language is inherently ambiguous if every Boolean grammar generating it is ambiguous: either more than one rule for a nonterminal can apply to the same string under the positive and negative conjunct conditions, or a conjunct can decompose the same string into component factors in more than one valid way.
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, P, S), where Σ is a finite alphabet of terminal symbols, N is a finite set of nonterminal symbols, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and P is a finite set of rules of the form

  A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n,

with A ∈ N, m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. Each α_i and ¬β_j is called a conjunct. The language L(G) ⊆ Σ* generated by G is defined via a least (or naturally well-founded) solution of the system of language equations associated with the rules, in which a string w ∈ Σ* is generated by A using the rule above if w can be derived from every positive conjunct α_i and from none of the negative conjuncts β_j.

Call a Boolean grammar G unambiguous if the following two conditions hold:
(i) for every nonterminal A ∈ N and every string w ∈ Σ*, at most one rule for A can be applied to w (i.e., w is generated from every positive conjunct and from no negative conjunct of at most one rule for A); and
(ii) for every rule A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n applicable to a string w, and for every positive conjunct α_i = X₁X₂…X_k (with X_j ∈ Σ ∪ N), there exists exactly one factorization w = w₁w₂…w_k such that each w_j is generated by X_j.

A grammar that is not unambiguous is called ambiguous. A language L ⊆ Σ* is said to be inherently ambiguous with respect to Boolean grammars if every Boolean grammar generating L is ambiguous.

Question: Does there exist a language L ⊆ Σ* that is inherently ambiguous with respect to Boolean grammars?
status_search_result: The existence of a language that is inherently ambiguous with respect to Boolean grammars is reported as an open problem in Okhotin's work on unambiguous Boolean grammars, where linear conjunctive languages were shown unambiguous but the general inherent-ambiguity question for Boolean grammars was left open. No subsequent work resolving the question was found.

paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
original_question: Does the hierarchy of Boolean grammars by number of nonterminal symbols collapse? That is, is there a fixed number k > 0 such that every language generated by any Boolean grammar can also be generated by a Boolean grammar with at most k nonterminals?
self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, P, S), where Σ is a finite alphabet of terminals, N is a finite set of nonterminal symbols disjoint from Σ, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and P is a finite set of rules of the form

   A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n,

with m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and each α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The language L(G) ⊆ Σ* generated by G is defined via the (unique, naturally-ordered) solution of the corresponding system of language equations under the standard semantics of Boolean grammars (e.g., the well-founded semantics), so that A ∈ N denotes a language L_G(A) ⊆ Σ*, with the rule above interpreted as requiring membership in every L_G(α_i) and non-membership in every L_G(β_j); set L(G) = L_G(S).

For k ≥ 1, let 𝓑_k denote the class of languages L(G) generated by Boolean grammars G with |N| ≤ k nonterminals, and let 𝓑 = ⋃_{k≥1} 𝓑_k.

Question: Does the nonterminal hierarchy of Boolean grammars collapse? That is, does there exist a fixed integer k > 0 such that 𝓑_k = 𝓑, i.e. every language generated by some Boolean grammar can also be generated by a Boolean grammar using at most k nonterminal symbols?
status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a published resolution of this nonterminal-hierarchy collapse question for Boolean grammars. Related results exist (e.g., one-nonterminal conjunctive grammars over a unary alphabet have been studied), but no source clearly settles whether the full nonterminal hierarchy of Boolean grammars over a general alphabet collapses. Status appears to remain unresolved, but this could not be definitively confirmed.

paper_title: Some open problems in analysis
original_question: Let D be a bounded domain in R^n with n > 1 and smooth connected boundary S. Let L and M be elliptic, second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive Dirichlet operators in D with real-valued coefficients, and let a(x) and b(x) be strictly positive functions that are smooth on the closure of D. If real-valued functions u and v satisfy Lu + a(x)v = 0 in D, -b(x)u + Mv = 0 in D, and u = v = 0 on S, must u = v = 0 throughout D? If the answer is no, can one construct a counterexample without imposing additional assumptions such as L = M or small |b - a|?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $n > 1$, be a bounded domain with smooth connected boundary $S$. Let $L$ and $M$ be elliptic, second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive operators on $D$ with real-valued coefficients, each equipped with the Dirichlet boundary condition on $S$. Let $a, b \in C^\infty(\overline{D})$ be strictly positive functions on $\overline{D}$. Suppose real-valued functions $u, v$ satisfy
$$Lu + a(x) v = 0 \quad \text{in } D, \qquad -b(x) u + M v = 0 \quad \text{in } D, \qquad u = v = 0 \quad \text{on } S.$$
Determine whether these conditions imply $u \equiv v \equiv 0$ in $D$. If the implication fails in general, exhibit a counterexample without assuming $L = M$, without restricting $|b - a|$ to be small, and without imposing any additional structural hypotheses on $L$, $M$, $a$, or $b$ beyond those stated above.
status_search_result: No web evidence was found that resolves this uniqueness question for the coupled selfadjoint elliptic Dirichlet system in the stated generality (no assumption $L=M$, no smallness on $|b-a|$). The status is therefore recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in analysis
original_question: Let L_1 and L_2 be algebraic varieties in complex Euclidean space, for example zero sets of nonconstant polynomials. Let D be a bounded domain in R^n with n > 1, let f be a compactly supported L^2(D) function, and define its Fourier transform F(z) = integral_D f(x) exp(i z dot x) dx. For any fixed positive integer M, can one choose points p_1,...,p_M in L_2 such that the M functions z -> F(z + p_m), restricted to z in L_1, are linearly independent? Equivalently, can the points p_m be chosen so that sum_{m=1}^M c_m F(z + p_m) = 0 for every z in L_1 implies c_m = 0 for every m?
self_contained_problem:
Let n > 1 be an integer and let D be a bounded domain in R^n. Let f be a (nonzero) compactly supported function in L^2(D), and define its Fourier transform on C^n by

   F(z) = ∫_D f(x) exp(i z·x) dx,    z ∈ C^n,

where z·x = z_1 x_1 + ... + z_n x_n. Note that F is an entire function on C^n (of exponential type, by the Paley–Wiener theorem).

Let L_1 and L_2 be algebraic varieties in C^n (for instance, the zero sets of nonconstant polynomials in n complex variables).

Fix an arbitrary positive integer M. Question: can one always choose points p_1, p_2, ..., p_M ∈ L_2 such that the M functions

   z ↦ F(z + p_m),    m = 1, ..., M,

restricted to z ∈ L_1, are linearly independent over C? Equivalently, can the points p_1, ..., p_M ∈ L_2 be chosen so that the relation

   Σ_{m=1}^M c_m F(z + p_m) = 0    for all z ∈ L_1

(with c_m ∈ C) forces c_1 = c_2 = ... = c_M = 0?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this linear-independence question for Fourier translates restricted to algebraic varieties was located. The problem appears to remain open, but no conclusive source confirms the current status, so it is marked unknown.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω be the unit ball in R^3 and let λ1 = π^2 be the first eigenvalue of -Δ on Ω with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. For 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4, does the boundary value problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit a smooth nontrivial solution u not identically zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let $\lambda_1 = \pi^2$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$. Consider the semilinear elliptic boundary value problem with the critical Sobolev exponent
$$-\Delta u = u^5 + \lambda u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega,$$
where $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ is a parameter and the unknown $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function.

Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$, the problem admits a smooth solution $u \not\equiv 0$.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint by Chen, Wei and others titled "On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution" (arXiv:2503.06904) claims a complete resolution of this problem, constructing infinitely many sign-changing, non-radial smooth solutions for the full parameter range, including $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$. The result has been announced but as of May 2026 is still in preprint/peer-review status.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Uniqueness of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
original_question: Let Ω be the unit disk in R^2 and ε > 0. Consider the Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = ε^{-2}u(1 - |u|^2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x) = x on ∂Ω, where u maps Ω into R^2. The radial solution Uε is defined by Uε(x) = x|x|^{-1} fε(|x|), where fε solves the corresponding radial ODE with fε(0)=0 and fε(1)=1. Is Uε the only solution of this boundary value problem?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open unit disk and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Consider the Ginzburg–Landau system for maps $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$,
$$-\Delta u = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2} u\bigl(1 - |u|^2\bigr) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u(x) = x \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega.$$
Identifying $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\mathbb{C}$, define the radial solution $U_\varepsilon(x) = \frac{x}{|x|} f_\varepsilon(|x|)$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ is the unique solution of the radial ODE
$$-f''(r) - \frac{1}{r} f'(r) + \frac{1}{r^2} f(r) = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2} f(r)\bigl(1 - f(r)^2\bigr), \quad r \in (0,1),$$
with $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$. Determine whether, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $U_\varepsilon$ is the only solution of the above boundary value problem.
status_search_result: The question of whether the radial solution $U_\varepsilon$ is the unique solution to the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet problem on the unit disk with boundary data $x$ is a long-standing open problem originally posed by Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein. Partial results are known: uniqueness has been established for small $\varepsilon$ (small domain regime) and for $\varepsilon$ sufficiently large, but the full problem for all $\varepsilon > 0$ remains open as of recent surveys by Brezis.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Global minimality of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
original_question: For the disk Ginzburg-Landau energy Eε(u) = (1/2)∫Ω |∇u|^2 + (1/(4ε^2))∫Ω (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on H^1_g(Ω; R^2), where g(x)=x on ∂Ω, is the radial solution Uε a minimizer of Eε for every ε > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disk, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be the identity map $g(x) = x$. Define
$$H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) : u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}.$$
For $\varepsilon > 0$, consider the Ginzburg–Landau energy
$$E_\varepsilon(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + \tfrac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2\,dx, \qquad u \in H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2).$$
It is known that there exists a unique radially symmetric critical point $U_\varepsilon$ of $E_\varepsilon$ in $H^1_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ of the form $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\, x/|x|$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ satisfies $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$.

Question: Is $U_\varepsilon$ a global minimizer of $E_\varepsilon$ on $H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$?
status_search_result: The radial solution $U_\varepsilon$ is known to be a local minimizer for every $\varepsilon>0$ (Mironescu 1996; Lieb–Loss). Global minimality is established in regimes where the energy is convex (large $\varepsilon$, e.g. $\varepsilon \geq 1/\sqrt{\lambda_1}$) and in the small-$\varepsilon$ asymptotic regime, but for the intermediate range global minimality of $U_\varepsilon$ remains an open problem.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Consider smooth maps u: R^2 → R^2 ≃ C satisfying the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation -Δu = u(1 - |u|^2) on R^2 and the condition |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞. The degree at infinity deg(u,∞) is then defined, and for each integer q there is a distinguished radial-equivariant solution Vq(r,θ)=e^{iqθ}gq(r), with V0 ≡ 1 and deg(Vq,∞)=q. Must every such solution u be equal, up to multiplication by a complex unit and translation in R^2, to Vq with q = deg(u,∞)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $u: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \cong \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth solution of the Ginzburg–Landau equation
$$-\Delta u = u\bigl(1 - |u|^2\bigr) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,$$
satisfying the condition at infinity
$$|u(x)| \to 1 \quad \text{as } |x| \to \infty.$$
Under these assumptions, the topological degree at infinity, $\deg(u, \infty) \in \mathbb{Z}$, is well defined. For each $q \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a distinguished radially equivariant solution of the form
$$V_q(r,\theta) = e^{i q \theta} g_q(r),$$
where $(r,\theta)$ are polar coordinates on $\mathbb{R}^2$, $V_0 \equiv 1$, $g_q: [0,\infty) \to [0,1]$ is smooth with $g_q(0)=0$ for $q\neq 0$ and $g_q(r) \to 1$ as $r\to\infty$, and $\deg(V_q, \infty) = q$.

Question: Must every such solution $u$ coincide with $V_q$ up to multiplication by a complex unit and translation? That is, setting $q := \deg(u,\infty)$, do there necessarily exist $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha|=1$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$$u(x) = \alpha\, V_q(x - x_0) \quad \text{for all } x \in \mathbb{R}^2?$$
status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing open question (going back to Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein and reiterated in subsequent work of Brezis, Mironescu, and others). Partial results are known: under additional assumptions such as local minimality or finite energy, uniqueness up to symmetry has been established (Mironescu in dimension 2, extended by Millot–Pisante and Pisante in higher dimensions). Without such restrictions, the full classification of entire solutions on $\mathbb{R}^2$ for arbitrary degree $q$ is not resolved as of recent literature.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Additional harmonic maps from the disk to S^2
original_question: Let Ω be the unit disk in R^2, let 0 < R < 1, and prescribe the boundary map g(x,y)=(Rx,Ry,√(1-R^2)) from ∂Ω into S^2. For harmonic maps u: Ω → S^2 solving -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω with u=g on ∂Ω, two explicit solutions u and ū are known and are the unique minimizers in the relevant degree classes E0 and E_{-1}. Are there any other solutions of this harmonic-map boundary value problem besides those two explicit solutions?
self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² be the open unit disk, and let S² ⊂ ℝ³ be the standard unit sphere. Fix a parameter R with 0 < R < 1, and define the boundary map g : ∂Ω → S² by
   g(x, y) = (Rx, Ry, √(1 − R²))    for (x, y) ∈ ∂Ω.
Consider the Dirichlet boundary value problem for harmonic maps from Ω into S²: find u = (u₁, u₂, u₃) : Ω → S² with u ∈ H¹(Ω; S²) satisfying
   −Δu_i = u_i |∇u|²    in Ω  (i = 1, 2, 3),
   u = g    on ∂Ω.
Two explicit solutions are known:
 (i) the map u that minimizes the Dirichlet energy among maps of degree 0 (class E₀);
 (ii) the map ū obtained from u by a suitable inversion, which minimizes the Dirichlet energy among maps of degree −1 (class E₋₁);
and u, ū are the unique minimizers in their respective topological classes.

Question: Does the above boundary value problem admit any harmonic-map solution other than u and ū?
status_search_result: A web search returned no result establishing that the question of whether there exist solutions to this Dirichlet problem beyond the two explicit Brezis–Coron solutions has been resolved. Related works (Brezis–Coron, Jost, and subsequent literature) discuss existence of at least two solutions and properties of minimizers, but do not appear to settle the uniqueness-up-to-the-two-explicit-maps question for this specific boundary datum.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Energy minimization among continuous harmonic-map competitors
original_question: In the degree-zero boundary setting for harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2, consider the infimum of the Dirichlet energy E(u)=∫Ω |∇u|^2 over maps u in H^1_g(Ω;S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball. Is this infimum achieved by some continuous map?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the open unit ball and let $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the unit sphere. For a map $u : \Omega \to S^2$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega; S^2) = \{u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e.}\}$, define the Dirichlet energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2 \, dx.$$
Fix a smooth boundary datum $g \in C^\infty(\partial\Omega; S^2)$ satisfying the topological condition $\deg(g) = 0$, and let
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{u \in H^1(\Omega; S^2) : u|_{\partial\Omega} = g\}.$$
Consider the class of admissible competitors that are continuous up to the boundary,
$$\mathcal{A} = H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2),$$
which is nonempty since $\deg(g) = 0$. Decide whether the infimum
$$I(g) := \inf\{E(u) : u \in \mathcal{A}\}$$
is attained, i.e., whether there exists $u_* \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2)$ with $E(u_*) = I(g)$.
status_search_result: The question of whether the infimum of the Dirichlet energy among continuous H^1 maps from B^3 to S^2 with prescribed degree-zero boundary data is attained is a long-standing open problem associated with Hardt–Lin and discussed in the framework of relaxed energies of Bethuel–Brezis–Coron. No published resolution was located; the problem continues to appear in surveys of variational problems for harmonic maps.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 with degree-zero boundary data, define the relaxed energy R on H^1_g(Ω;S^2) through weak H^1 limits of continuous maps. Are the minimizers of this relaxed energy continuous on the closed ball, or is at least one relaxed-energy minimizer continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g:\partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth boundary datum of topological degree zero. Define
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)|=1 \text{ a.e.}, \; u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \},$$
equipped with the Dirichlet energy $E(u) = \tfrac12 \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx$. It is known (Bethuel) that the subset
$$\mathcal{R}_g = \overline{\{ u \in C^0(\overline{\Omega}; S^2) \cap H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)\}}^{\,H^1\text{-strong}}$$
is a strict subset of $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$, and that smooth maps are not dense. For $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$, define the relaxed energy
$$R(u) = \inf\Bigl\{ \liminf_{n\to\infty} E(u_n) : u_n \in C^0(\overline{\Omega};S^2)\cap H^1_g(\Omega;S^2),\; u_n \rightharpoonup u \text{ weakly in } H^1\Bigr\}.$$
Equivalently, $R(u) = E(u) + 4\pi L(u)$, where $L(u)$ is the length of a minimal connection associated with the singularities of $u$ (Bethuel–Brezis–Coron).

Question: Is every minimizer of $R$ over $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$? If not in general, does there always exist at least one minimizer of $R$ that is continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$?
status_search_result: The continuity of minimizers of the Bethuel–Brezis–Coron relaxed energy for maps from $B^3$ to $S^2$ remains an open problem. Partial regularity results are known: Bethuel–Brezis–Coron and Giaquinta–Modica–Souček showed that minimizers of the relaxed energy are smooth outside a closed singular set, and later refinements show smoothness off a finite set, but full continuity (or existence of one continuous minimizer) for general degree-zero boundary data has not been established.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), 1 < p ≤ 2, does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| is bounded by c(p-1) times the double integral over S^1×S^1 of |f(x)-f(y)|^p/|x-y|^2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. For $1<p<\infty$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb C$ such that
$$\|f\|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p:=\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy<\infty.$$
Every such $f$ admits a well-defined topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb Z$ (defined, e.g., via approximation by smooth maps or via the distributional Jacobian).

Determine whether there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for every $p\in(1,2]$ and every $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$,
$$|\deg f|\le c\,(p-1)\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy.$$
category_tag: Fractional Sobolev spaces and topological degree
status_search_result: A 2017 refinement (arXiv:1710.02994) sharpens the Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen degree estimate for maps $S^d\to S^d$ when $d\ge 2$, but explicitly notes that the corresponding question for $d=1$ (i.e., the $S^1\to S^1$ case asked here) remains open. No subsequent resolution was located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For f in C(S^1;S^1) and δ>0, let Iδ(f) be the double integral of |x-y|^{-2} over pairs (x,y) in S^1×S^1 such that |f(x)-f(y)| ≥ δ. Does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| ≤ c δ Iδ(f) for every continuous f:S^1→S^1 and every δ ≤ √3?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle, and let $C(S^1;S^1)$ be the space of continuous maps from $S^1$ to itself. For $f\in C(S^1;S^1)$, let $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote its topological degree. For $\delta>0$, define
$$I_\delta(f):=\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{\mathbf{1}_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|\ge \delta\}}}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy,$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean distance in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $dx, dy$ are the arc-length measures on $S^1$.

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$ such that
$$|\deg f|\;\le\; c\,\delta\,I_\delta(f)$$
holds for every $f\in C(S^1;S^1)$ and every $\delta\in(0,\sqrt{3}]$?
